# Apple Photos on iPhone — Complete Feature Atlas

**Date:** 2026-07-14
**Status:** Reference document. This is the bar we must clear, and the API surface we must build on.
**Purpose:** So that an implementing agent never has to re-research Apple Photos. Every feature, every toggle, every limit, every trap.

## How this document was produced, and how far to trust it

**My training data predates the current release of iOS and cannot be trusted for any Apple fact.** Every claim here was researched from the live web in July 2026, then handed to an **independent adversarial fact-checker instructed to refute it by default.**

That pass was not ceremonial. Across the corpus it returned **393 CONFIRMED, 194 CORRECTED, 25 UNVERIFIED, and 14 REFUTED** verdicts — roughly a third of first-pass claims needed correction. It caught a **fabricated Apple quotation** and a **fabricated GitHub issue number**. Where a verdict corrected a claim, **the corrected fact is what appears below**; the original does not.

**Confidence markers used throughout:**
- Unmarked claims are **sourced and confirmed**.
- **`⚠️ Trap:`** marks something that will actively mislead an implementer — an API that looks usable but is not, a feature that looks shipping but is beta, a name that looks real but is fabricated.
- Claims marked **unverified** could not be sourced either way. **Do not build on them without checking.**
- Anything requiring a physical-device audit to confirm is called out as such rather than guessed at.

## Version baseline

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Current shipping** | **iOS / iPadOS 26.5.2** |
| In beta | iOS 26.6 (expected ~late July 2026) |
| Announced, not shipping | **iOS 27** — announced at WWDC on 2026-06-08, public beta 2026-07-13, GM expected **~September 2026** |

> **⚠️ iOS 27 is not shippable.** Any iOS 27 feature below is explicitly marked. Do not build a product on it, and do not let an "available in iOS 27" API read as available today.

**Recent history that matters:** Apple substantially redesigned Photos in **iOS 18** (tab bar removed, unified scroll) to significant user backlash, and then **partially reversed it in iOS 26** (Library/Collections tabs restored, Liquid Glass). An implementer who learned Photos before 2025 has a stale mental model. The IA below is the current one.

## The one-paragraph summary

Apple Photos is **excellent at presence and craft** — it is already on the phone, it scrolls instantly over 100k photos, and it works on a plane — and **structurally weak at the decision layer**. It gives users **no way to correct its face recognition on iPhone** (the confirm flow was removed around iOS 17 and never returned; you cannot even draw a face box), **no cross-age handling** (users report "losing entire grandchildren"), **no un-merge**, **no confidence surfacing**, and **no export of the people graph it builds about your family**. And it gives third-party developers **nothing at all** about people: PhotoKit exposes zero person identities, zero face bounding boxes, and no way to enumerate the People album.

That combination — a walled people-graph that is simultaneously *bad* and *inescapable* — is the opening.

---
## 1. Information Architecture & Navigation

Apple Photos on iPhone is, as of the current shipping release (**iOS 26.5.2**), a three-destination app: a floating Liquid Glass tab bar at the bottom holding **`Library`** (bottom-left), **`Collections`**, and a system **`Search`** tab (bottom-right). Everything else in the app — albums, people, memories, trips, media types, the map — is a *row inside Collections* or a *mode inside a toolbar menu*, not a top-level destination. The single most important thing an implementer must know: **this structure is only ~10 months old.** iOS 18 (Sept 2024) deleted the tab bar entirely and replaced it with one unified scrolling view; the backlash was severe enough that Apple restored tabs in iOS 26 (Sept 2025), and Craig Federighi said so from the WWDC 2025 stage: *"Many of you missed using tabs in the Photos app."* The second most important thing: Apple Photos has **three visually distinct toolbar buttons** that an implementer will be tempted to collapse into one "…" overflow menu. Doing so misrepresents the entire navigation model (see §1.3).

### 1.1 Version ground truth and the IA timeline

Verified 2026-07-14. The IA you must match **today** is iOS 26's. iOS 27 is an *additive delta*, not a restructure.

| Release | Date | IA impact |
|---|---|---|
| iOS 18.0 | Sept 2024 | **Tab bar deleted.** Four tabs (`Library` / `For You` / `Albums` / `Search`) replaced by one unified scroll view. Everything below the grid becomes a "Collection." |
| iOS 18.1 | Oct 2024 | No IA change. Natural-language Photos search, Clean Up, memory-movie-from-description, 4K60 scrubbing fix. |
| iOS 18.2 | Dec 2024 | No IA change. Frame-by-frame video scrubbing; a `Loop Videos` toggle; **swipe right to go back** inside Collections; clearable `Recently Viewed` / `Recently Shared` history; `Favorites` appears in both Pinned Collections *and* Utilities; album sorting (alphabetically / by date created / manual). |
| **iOS 26.0** | **Sept 2025** | **Tab bar restored** as `Library` / `Collections` + `Search`. Three Collections layout sizes. Event recognition. This is the current IA. |
| iOS 26.1 → 26.5.2 | Oct 2025 – Jun 2026 | **Zero** Photos IA changes. (Full shipped chain per Apple's "About iOS 26 Updates," support.apple.com/en-us/123075: 26 → 26.0.1 → 26.1 → 26.2 → 26.2.1 → 26.3 → 26.3.1 → 26.4 → 26.4.1 → 26.4.2 → 26.5 → 26.5.1 → **26.5.2**, released ~June 29, 2026, security-only.) |
| iOS 26.6 | **beta 5** (build `23G5065a`, seeded July 13, 2026) | Expected ~late July 2026. |
| iOS 27 | **dev beta 3** (`24A5380h`, July 6, 2026); **public beta 1** (July 13, 2026) | Announced WWDC 2026 (keynote June 8–9, 2026). Ships fall 2026. **Does not change the tab structure.** See §1.16. |

⚠️ **Trap:** A widely repeated claim says iOS 18.2 restored a tab bar or "tab-like structure." **It did not.** No source describes a tab bar in any iOS 18.x build. The tab bar returned *only* in iOS 26. If you are benchmarking against "the iOS 18 Photos app," you are benchmarking a tabless single-scroll app that no longer exists.

⚠️ **Trap:** Apple announced a **Carousel view** at WWDC 2024 ("*A new carousel view presents highlights that update each day and feature favorite people, pets, places, and more*" — Apple Newsroom, June 10, 2024). It was **cut in iOS 18 developer beta 5** (early August 2024) after beta-tester complaints that it "complicated quick access to frequently used elements," and **never shipped in any public build.** Apple's own Sept 2024 release-day iOS 18 press release makes no mention of it. Treat any "Photos Carousel" claim about shipping iOS as **false**. Concretely: if your team was planning swipe-through-highlights as a *primary navigation gesture*, Apple already ran that experiment in public and abandoned it.

### 1.2 The tab bar (iOS 26 restoration)

Apple's iOS 26 release notes, verbatim: *"Separate tabs for Library and Collections offers easier navigation, and you can access Search in every view."* Apple's iOS 26 feature PDF calls it **"Updated tab design"**: *"Photos features separate tabs for the Library and Collections views, along with quick access to Search, so you can easily navigate to what you're looking for."* Apple's iPhone User Guide instructs: *"Make sure the Library tab is selected in the bottom-left corner."* Apple's own screenshot alt-text describes the bottom bar as *"the Library, Collections, and Search buttons."*

This is **not** a restoration of the pre-iOS 18 four-tab bar. `For You` is **gone permanently**. `Albums` is **not a tab** — it is a row inside `Collections` (confirmed by Apple's own Albums guide page: *"Tap Collections. Tap Albums"*). It is a partial climb-down, and users who wanted the Albums tab back still do not have it.

**Behavior.** It is the standard iOS 26 Liquid Glass *floating* tab bar: translucent (photos show through), hovering above content, and it **auto-hides / morphs on scroll**. In the `Library` tab, scrolling causes the tab bar to give way to a Liquid Glass segmented control for **`Years` / `Months` / `All`** — which occupy the **bottom** edge of the screen, with the `Search` button persisting in the bottom-right. Apple's screenshot alt-text is explicit: *"At the bottom of the screen, from left to right, are buttons to view the library by Years, Months, and All buttons. In the bottom-right corner is the Search button."*

⚠️ **Trap:** Every intuition says `Years | Months | All` is a **top** segmented control. It is not — it lives at the **bottom**, sharing the bottom edge with the tab bar via a scroll-driven morph. Build it at the top and your app will feel structurally wrong to anyone coming from Photos.

*Unverified:* whether Photos also applies the generic iOS 26 "minimize tab bar on scroll" behavior in the `Collections` tab (only the Library morph is confirmed by a source).

### 1.3 ⚠️ THE THREE TOOLBAR CONTROLS — the highest-risk misreading in the whole IA

Apple Photos does **not** have a single "…" overflow menu. It has **three separate, non-interchangeable toolbar controls**, and which one you tap depends on *where you are*. Secondary write-ups routinely flatten all three into "the ellipsis menu"; that is wrong and will produce a broken navigation model.

| Control | Apple's name | Where it appears | What it contains |
|---|---|---|---|
| Slider-style icon (asset `IL_SortandFilter.png`) | **the Sort and Filter button** | `Library` tab; inside an album; inside a memory; the `Groups` View Options | `View Options`, `Filter`, `Sort by Recently Added` / `Sort by Date Captured`, **`Show Map` (in Library)** |
| Layout icon | **the Layout and Reorder button** | Top of the `Collections` tab | Three layout-size icon buttons, `Collapse All`, `Reorder`, library scope picker |
| "…" | **the More button** | Photo detail; the `Albums` screen; inside an *open* collection | Album sort/filter/view-format; per-photo actions; **`Show Map` (inside a collection)** |

The clearest illustration: **`Show Map` lives under the Sort and Filter button in `Library`, but under the More button inside a collection.** Same feature, two different controls, depending on context.

Additional stateful detail: inside an album, **when a filter is active the Sort and Filter button is replaced by a different icon**; tapping it and choosing **`Remove Filter`** clears the filter. That icon swap is a real implementation requirement, not decoration.

### 1.4 `Library` tab — the grid

The pure chronological grid of everything. Apple: *"Browse the library in the Photos app to view your entire collection of photos and videos."* Navigation: *"Swipe down to browse photos, then tap Years or Months to go to a specific time in your library."*

**Three scopes**, exact labels: **`Years`**, **`Months`**, **`All`**.

- `Years` and `Months` are **curated**, not complete. Apple, verbatim: *"Years and Months views are curated to show your best shots, and visual clutter like similar photos, screenshots, whiteboards, and receipts aren't shown. To see every photo and video, tap All."*
- `All` is the exhaustive grid.
- **Pinch to zoom** works on the grid: *"While you're viewing the library, pinch the screen to zoom in or out."*

The `Years`/`Months`/`All` concept dates to iOS 13; in iOS 18 it lived inside the unified view; in iOS 26 it is bound to the Library tab.

#### 1.4.1 `View Options` (via the **Sort and Filter button** → `View Options`)

Exact Apple labels:

| Label | Effect |
|---|---|
| `Zoom In` | Enlarge thumbnails |
| `Zoom Out` | Reduce thumbnails, see more at once |
| `Aspect Ratio Grid` | Show each thumbnail in the dimension it was captured in |
| `Square Photo Grid` | Return to square thumbnails |
| `Screenshots` | **Hides** screenshots |
| `Shared Library Badge` | Hide the badge on iCloud Shared Photo Library thumbnails |
| `Shared with You` | Hide photos/videos shared with you in Messages |
| `From My Mac` | Hide photos/videos manually added from your Mac |

⚠️ **Trap (documentation bug):** Apple's own live guide page prints **"Aspect Ration Grid"** — a typo. The shipping UI label is **`Aspect Ratio Grid`**. Do not copy Apple's string verbatim from the docs. (Apple's page also lists `Shared Library Badge` **twice**, with two slightly different descriptions.)

⚠️ **Trap (verb polarity):** These toggles *hide*. Tapping `Screenshots` **removes** screenshots from the grid. Many users read the label as "show screenshots" and get the opposite result.

#### 1.4.2 Sort and Filter (via the **Sort and Filter button**)

**Sort — exactly two options**, verbatim from Apple:
- **`Sort by Recently Added`** — *"Photos and videos you added most recently appear at the bottom of the library."*
- **`Sort by Date Captured`** — *"Photos and videos are sorted by the date they were taken, instead of the date they were added to the library."*

**Filter.** Apple documents: **`Favorites`**, **`Edited`**, **`Photos`**, **`Videos`**, **`Not in an Album`**. Filters are **combinable** — Apple, verbatim: *"You can apply multiple filters at the same time. For example, tap Photos and Edited to see only photos you've edited."* **`All Items`** clears all filters and returns the full library.

⚠️ **Trap:** A "Screenshots" *filter* is **unverified** — Apple names only Videos, Favorites, Not in an Album, Photos, and Edited. `Screenshots` exists as a **hide toggle** under `View Options` and as a **Media Types** collection, but there is no documented Screenshots entry in the Filter list. Do not assume parity.

### 1.5 `Collections` tab — structure and section inventory

A vertical stack of section headings, each with a horizontally-swipeable row of tiles. Apple, verbatim: *"Under each collection heading, swipe left or right to see different collections. Or tap the heading to see all the collections in that category."* Tapping the heading is a real navigation action, not decoration.

**All eleven section names are confirmed to exist in iOS 26:**

| Section | Notes |
|---|---|
| `Pinned` | Heading carries an **`Edit`** button. Apple's marketing name: "Pinned Collections." |
| `Recent Days` | Day-clustered; `Saved Today` appears below it |
| `People & Pets` | **Named `People` when no pets are detected in the library.** Contains a nested `Groups` row. |
| `Memories` | Contains a `Favorites` sub-collection (Favorite Memories) |
| `Trips` | Location-clustered |
| `Featured Photos` | |
| `Wallpaper Suggestions` | A real, wired destination with its own Apple guide page |
| `Albums` | User albums + folders. **Not a tab.** |
| `Shared Albums` | |
| `Media Types` | Reorderable; larger, more distinct buttons in iOS 26 |
| `Utilities` | Reorderable; larger, more distinct buttons in iOS 26 |

⚠️ **Trap (hard-coded string):** The collection is labeled **`People`**, not `People & Pets`, when no pets appear in the user's library. Apple: *"the People & Pets collection (or the People collection if no pets appear)."* A hard-coded "People & Pets" string is wrong for a large fraction of users.

⚠️ **Trap (default order):** **Do not assume `Pinned` is row 1.** Apple's prose says Pinned is *"at the top of the screen"*, but Apple's **own iOS 26 guide screenshot alt-text** reads: *"On the screen from top to bottom are the following Collections: Memories, Pinned, Albums, and Recent Days"* — **Memories is above Pinned.** AppleInsider's iOS 26 walkthrough gives the default order as **Memories, Pinned, Albums, People & Pets, Featured Photos, Shared Albums, Recent Days, Trips, Media Types, Utilities, Wallpaper Suggestions**. Apple's own documentation is internally inconsistent. The section **names** are sourced; the factory **order** is **not reliably sourced** — verify on a device before writing any spec that depends on it. (It is user-reorderable anyway, so "default order" is only a starting state.)

Apple's iOS 18 press release describes the generation model: *"New collections like Recent Days, People & Pets, and Trips automatically keep the library organized with on-device intelligence."*

### 1.6 `Pinned` Collections — pin, unpin, reorder

The user-curated row. Apple, verbatim: *"You can choose which collections and albums appear below the Pinned heading at the top of the screen. Pin the collections and albums you view most often, so they're easy to find."*

| Action | Exact flow |
|---|---|
| Enter edit mode | `Collections` → tap **`Edit`** (to the right of the `Pinned` heading) |
| Pin | *"Tap the suggested collection you want to add, or scroll down and tap **`Any Collection or Album`** to see more options."* Unpinned items show an **Add badge**. |
| Unpin (in edit mode) | Tap the **Remove badge**, then tap **`Delete`** |
| Reorder | *"Touch and hold a pinned collection, then drag it to a new position."* |
| Exit | The **Close** button |
| Shortcut (pin) | Touch and hold a collection anywhere → **`Pin`** |
| Shortcut (unpin) | Touch and hold → **`Unpin`** |

**Pinnable object types:** albums, media types, utilities, memories, and individual people/pets. **Default pins shipped by Apple:** `Recently Saved` and `Favorites` (the latter added to Pinned in iOS 18.2). Pinning syncs with iCloud Photos.

Discovery is genuinely poor here: the `Edit` button and the touch-and-hold → `Pin` gesture are both invisible affordances, and `Any Collection or Album` is buried below a suggestion list. Many users never find pinning at all — which is precisely why the auto-generated clutter feels unmanageable to them.

### 1.7 Collections display options (via the **Layout and Reorder button**)

Apple: *"Collections can be viewed with larger or smaller image tiles, or without any images at all. You can also change the order collections appear on the screen."* Apple's iOS 26 feature PDF, verbatim: *"you can now adjust the size—choose from **larger tiles**, a **denser layout**, or an option that **emphasizes the top row**."*

| Item in the menu | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **the Large Grid button** | **Icon, not text** | Enlarges the collection tiles |
| **the Small Grid button** | **Icon, not text** | Reduces the collection tiles / denser layout |
| **the Mixed Grid button** | **Icon, not text** | The default display; emphasizes the top row |
| `Collapse All` | Genuine text label | Hides all collection tiles |
| `Reorder` | Genuine text label | Enters drag-to-reorder mode |
| `Both Libraries` / `Personal Library` / `Shared Library` | Genuine text labels | Library scope picker (see §1.7.1) |

⚠️ **Trap:** The three layout sizes are **icon buttons**. Secondary sources (and Apple's own *action descriptions* in the guide — "Enlarge the size of the collection tiles", "Reduce the size of the collection tiles", "Show the default display") read like menu labels. **They are not.** An implementer copying those strings would ship UI text that does not exist anywhere in Photos.

**Per-collection collapse** uses **the Forward button** (a chevron) on the section heading: *"If you want to hide the image tiles for a single collection, tap [the chevron]. Tap [it again] to stop hiding them."* **When collapsed, only the collection's name shows — no thumbnail preview.** The row still occupies vertical space.

**`Reorder` has two entry points:** (a) the Layout and Reorder button, or (b) *"Scroll to the bottom of the screen, tap **`Reorder`**, then drag a collection into a new position. Tap **`Done`**."*

#### 1.7.1 Library scope: `Both Libraries` / `Personal Library` / `Shared Library`

If the user is in an **iCloud Shared Photo Library** (iOS 16.1+), the Layout and Reorder menu offers exactly three scope options, exactly those labels: *"Choose which library to include in collections (if you're part of an iCloud Shared Photo Library): Tap Both Libraries, Personal Library, or Shared Library."* Related but separate: the `Shared Library Badge` View Option (§1.4.1) and Search scoping via typing **"Shared by"** and tapping a participant.

⚠️ **Trap (naming collision):** **iCloud Shared Photo Library**, **Shared Albums**, and **Shared with You** are **three distinct sharing systems** living in the same app with near-identical names. Users cannot tell them apart, and neither will your spec if you are careless. The scope picker being buried in a menu is the #1 cause of "my photo disappeared" confusion — it is simply in the other library scope.

### 1.8 The intelligent collections

These are Apple's differentiation. **None of them is exposed by PhotoKit** (see §1.17).

#### `Recent Days` (and `Saved Today`)
Apple: *"Tap Collections, then scroll down to Recent Days. Swipe left or right to quickly move between days, or tap Recent Days to view all. Tap a day to open the collection."* Opening a day shows a **curated summary, not everything**: *"When you open a day in Recent Days, you see a summary of the best photos from the day. To see all the photos you took that day, tap **`Show All`**."* A related collection **`Saved Today`** sits below Recent Days: *"To see photos you saved today, tap Collections, then tap the Saved Today collection below Recent Days."* (In iOS 18 beta 5, Apple folded the separate "Recently Saved" concept into Recent Days.)

#### `People & Pets` (and `Groups`) — the most under-inventoried surface
On-device face and pet recognition plus **co-occurrence clustering**: *"The Photos app recognizes groups of people and pets who often appear together in pictures and videos, and sorts them into group collections."* Flow: `Collections` → `People & Pets` → *"Swipe the collections below Groups to browse, or tap Groups to view them all."*

| Action | Exact flow |
|---|---|
| Create a group | Tap **`+`** to the right of `Groups` → **`Create New Group`** → select people/pets → optionally rename → **`Create`** |
| Edit a group | Touch and hold a group → **`Edit Name and People`**, **`Add People & Pets`**, **`Delete Group`** |
| Reorder groups | Touch and drag inside the Groups screen |
| Group view option | **Sort and Filter button** → `View Options` → **`Other People`** (show pictures of this group with additional people present) |
| Sort people/pets | **`Sort`** → **`Sort by Name`** (alphabetical) or **`Sort by Custom Order`** (touch and hold a key photo, drag) |
| Favorite a person/pet | Touch and hold their key photo → **`Favorite`**. **Favorited people sort to the front of the collection.** |
| Add unrecognized faces | **`Add People`** button at the bottom of the collection — surfaces additional unrecognized faces for naming. *This is the primary recall-improvement affordance.* |
| Hide / de-feature (collection level) | Touch and hold a key photo → **`Hide [name]`**, **`Don't Feature [name]`** |
| De-feature (photo level) | On a photo: **More button** → **`Don't Feature a Person`** → **`Feature This Person Less`** / **`Never Feature This Person`** → **`Confirm`** |
| Repair a misidentification | On a photo, tap the face → **`This is Not [name]`** → **`Rename This Person`** / **`Rename This Pet`** |
| Face menu (photo detail) | **`All Photos`**, **`Make Key Photo`**, **`Edit Name and Photos`**, **`Don't Feature This Person`** |
| Reset everything | `Collections` → **account avatar (top-right)** → **`Reset People & Pets Suggestions`** |

Note the **two distinct de-featuring levers** (collection-level `Don't Feature [name]` vs photo-level `Don't Feature a Person`) — they are different flows in different places, and this duplication is itself a usability defect worth exploiting.

#### `Memories` (and Favorite Memories)
Apple: *"The Memories collection in the Photos app includes personalized collections of photos and videos that feature a significant person, pet, place, activity, or event from your photo library."* Flow: *"Swipe left under Memories to scroll through a selection of your memories, or tap Memories to view them all."*

Inside a memory: **Sort and Filter button** (filter/sort), **`Show All`**, an in-memory **Search** button, the **More button** (share / delete / **`Show Map`**), **`Select`** (for individual sharing), and **Play** (the memory movie).

Favoriting: *"Touch and hold a memory, then tap **`Add to Favorite Memories`**"*; view them at `Collections` → `Memories` → **`Favorites`** (iOS 26).

**iOS 26 event-named memories:** memories are named after the *specific* concert or sports game you attended (see §1.14).

Suppression is scattered: account avatar → turn off **`Show Featured Content`** and/or **`Show Holiday Events`**.

#### `Trips`
Apple: *"In the Photos app, you can quickly find photos and videos from your trips grouped into collections, based on location data from the photos."* Flow: *"Tap Collections, scroll down to Trips, then tap the trip collection you want to view. Tap a year at the top of the screen to help you find older trips."* The year row includes an **`All`** chip, selected by default. Spatio-temporal clustering of geotagged assets (away-from-home location + contiguous date range). **Only assets with embedded GPS participate** — users with Location Services off get no Trips at all. **There is no way to create, rename, merge, or split a Trip.**

#### `Featured Photos` and `Wallpaper Suggestions`
Both are real Collections sections generated on-device. `Wallpaper Suggestions` has its own Apple guide page ("Get wallpaper suggestions in Photos on iPhone") and is a fully wired destination. Both are suppressible only by turning off `Show Featured Content` — not removable from the Collections list (§1.9 trap).

### 1.9 `Media Types` and `Utilities`

Both are rows in Collections, both open to a full screen, and **both are reorderable with the same flow**: *"Tap **`Edit`**, touch and hold the collection you want to move, then drag it to a new position. To undo your changes, tap **`Reset`**."* Then `Done`. In iOS 26 both rows got *"larger, more distinct buttons that make it clearer you can swipe or tap to get to more options."*

**`Media Types`.** Apple: *"you can find collections of photos and videos organized by media type. For example, browse all your Portrait mode photos or time-lapse videos in one place."* Individual media types can be pinned: *"To quickly locate your favorite media type, add it to the Pinned collection."*

⚠️ **Trap:** **Apple publishes no canonical list of Media Types membership.** The plausible mapping is 1:1 onto PhotoKit's smart-album subtypes (§1.17) — but that is an *inference*, not documentation, and the specific claim that Spatial and Screen Recordings are "newer additions" is **unverified**. Enumerate on a real device before shipping a parity claim.

**`Utilities`.** Apple: *"you can revisit photos you recently edited, saved, viewed, or shared, or find photos based on their content—like **documents**, **receipts**, **handwriting**, **illustrations**, and **QR codes**."*

Known members (high-confidence but **Apple never publishes a canonical list** — enumerate on-device):

| Member | Backing |
|---|---|
| `Recently Saved`, `Recently Viewed`, `Recently Shared`, `Recently Edited` | Activity history (Recently Viewed / Recently Shared became clearable in iOS 18.2) |
| `Imports`, `Duplicates`, `Hidden`, `Recently Deleted`, `Favorites` | System smart albums |
| `Recovered` | Special: *"If a photo or video wasn't saved properly and couldn't be added to your library, you may find a copy of it in Recovered"* → **`Permanently Delete`** or **`Restore to Library`**. **Deletion here is irreversible** (Apple warns explicitly). |
| `Documents`, `Receipts`, `Handwriting`, `Illustrations`, `QR Codes` | **On-device semantic content classification** |

**Privacy lock.** Apple: *"Some Utilities collections, like **Hidden** and **Recently Deleted**, are locked by default for your privacy."* Open with **`View Album`** + Face ID / Touch ID / passcode. Disable at **Settings → `Apps` → `Photos`** → turn off **`Use Face ID`** / **`Use Touch ID`** / **`Use Passcode`**. `Recently Deleted` retains items for **30 days**. A separate, **stronger** control also exists: **`Show Hidden Album`** (Settings → Apps → Photos) removes the Hidden collection *from Photos entirely* — Apple: *"You can add an extra layer of privacy by removing it from view."* Recently Deleted also supports **`Select` → More button → `Recover` / `Delete`**.

### 1.10 `Albums` — a row inside Collections, not a tab

This is the most-missed casualty of the iOS 18 redesign, and **iOS 26 did not fix it.** Albums is still a row you must scroll to inside `Collections`.

The `Albums` screen carries a **`Personal` / `Shared` / `Activity` segmented control** below the title bar (Apple's screenshot alt-text: *"Below that are buttons to view albums by Personal, Shared, or Activity"*) — an entire second-level navigation layer, and where shared-album Activity actually surfaces.

| Action | Exact flow (uses **the More button** — genuinely "…" here) |
|---|---|
| New album | `Collections` → `Albums` → **`+`** → **`New Album`** → name → add photos → choose a key photo → **`Create`** |
| New folder | **`+`** → **`New Folder`** → name → add albums → **`Create`** |
| Remove album from folder | Touch and hold → **`Remove from Folder`** |
| Sort albums | **More button** → choose a sort option. *"If you choose **`Sort by Custom Order`**, touch and hold an album, then drag it to a new position."* (Sorting added in iOS 18.2: alphabetically / by date created / manual.) |
| Filter | **More button** → **`Filter`** → show only albums or only folders |
| View format | **More button** → **`List View`** or **`Key Photo`** |
| Rename | Touch and hold → **`Edit Title and Photos`** |
| Delete | Touch and hold → **`Delete Album`** (**photos remain in the library**) |
| Share from an open album | **`Select All`** is available |

`Shared Albums` is its own separate Collections row.

⚠️ **Trap:** The `Albums` screen is the *one place* where the "…" More button reading is correct. This is exactly why the three-control distinction (§1.3) matters — Photos really does have all three, and they are **not** interchangeable.

### 1.11 `Search` tab

In iOS 26 Search moved from a top-bar button to a dedicated tab at the **bottom-right**. Apple: *"you can access Search in every view."* Guide: *"Tap [the Search button] in the bottom-right corner… You can search in the Library or Collections tab, or within a specific album or collection."* It follows the system **`UISearchTab`** pattern (a tab subclass representing the system search tab, which expands into a search field on selection).

On entry you get **suggestion chips**: *"you see suggestions of dates, people, and locations."*

**Documented query types:**

| Type | Example |
|---|---|
| Date | A month or a year |
| Place | A city or state |
| Business names | POI names |
| Category | `beach`, `sunset` |
| Events | Sports games, concerts |
| Person | Anyone identified in `People & Pets` |
| Text (OCR) | An email address or a phone number |
| Caption | User-written captions |

**Media-type narrowing:** *"You can narrow your search by including a media type in the search field, such as Video or Portrait."*
**Results view:** *"Swipe up to browse the complete search results, or tap **`Collections`** to view collections that include your search query."*
**Shared-library scoping:** type **"Shared by"** then tap a suggested name.
**Video results (iOS 26):** *"Search results for a video display a matching frame"* as the thumbnail.

**Apple Intelligence layer.** Adds natural-language query understanding and searching *within* video clips for key moments. **Device gate: iPhone 15 Pro and later** — plus the iPhone 16 line and iPhone 16e. **Language gate: English plus 15 others** (Danish, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Chinese Simplified, Chinese Traditional, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese) = **16 total**. Most of the installed base is still on keyword search.

### 1.12 `Show Map` — **there is no `Places` tab**

There is **no top-level Places/Map destination** in the current IA. Map is a *mode*, reached three ways:

| Context | Exact path |
|---|---|
| Library | *"Tap Library, tap [the **Sort and Filter** button], then tap **`Show Map`**"* |
| Inside a collection (a trip, a recent day, a memory) | *"Tap [the **More** button], then tap **`Show Map`**"* |
| Per photo | Open a photo, swipe up **or** tap the **Info** button, tap the map / address link → **`Show Nearby Photos`** expands to the surrounding area |

**Only assets with embedded GPS appear.** Apple, verbatim: *"Only pictures and videos that have embedded location information (GPS data) are included."* Pre-iOS 18 this was a visible **`Places`** album; it has been demoted to a hidden menu item, and users report they can no longer find map browsing at all.

⚠️ **Trap:** `Show Map` is under **two different controls depending on where you are** (Sort and Filter in Library; More inside a collection). This is the clearest single proof that flattening Photos' toolbar into one overflow menu is wrong.

### 1.13 Account / avatar menu (top-right of `Collections`) — the app's de facto settings

Tap your account avatar in the top-right corner of the **Collections** tab. Contents, all confirmed verbatim:

| Toggle | Apple's description |
|---|---|
| **`Show Featured Content`** | *"Turn off Show Featured Content to prevent Photos from automatically generating featured photos and memories"* |
| **`Show Holiday Events`** | *"prevent Photos from creating memories and featured content about holidays"* |
| **`Auto-Play Motion and Loop Videos`** | *"By default, videos and Live Photos automatically play when you tap Collections. To turn autoplay off, tap your account in the top-right corner, then turn off Auto-Play Motion and Loop Videos."* (This toggle was labeled just **`Loop Videos`** when it debuted in iOS 18.2; renamed by iOS 26.) |
| **`Reset People & Pets Suggestions`** | Resets face/pet suggestion state |

⚠️ **Trap (split-brain settings):** Photos preferences live in **two places**. The avatar menu holds the four above. **Settings → `Apps` → `Photos`** holds the Face ID / Touch ID / passcode lock for Hidden & Recently Deleted, the `Show Hidden Album` toggle, and (in iOS 27 beta) `Sync Immediately`. Apple's own user guide has to repeat "tap your account in the top-right corner" three separate times because nobody finds it.

### 1.14 Event details panel (concerts, sports) — iOS 26

Apple's iOS 26 feature PDF, verbatim: *"View details of events, like concerts, sports, and more, right in the **Info panel** in Photos, then listen to top songs from the artist or their tour, see the final score, or browse upcoming events."* Apple's iOS 26 release notes: *"Recognition for events like concerts and sports lets you see the details of an event and access related content."*

**UI behavior:** a photo with a recognized event shows a **ticket button in place of the usual info button**. Tapping it opens the events panel — for music: set list, artist, venue, related playlists, upcoming concert dates; for sports: scoreboard, venue, upcoming games. Memories in the Collections tab are then **named after the specific concert or game**.

⚠️ **Trap:** The ticket button **replaces** the info button, which surprises users looking for EXIF. There is also **no way to correct a misidentified event**, and the feature is region- and catalog-limited.

### 1.15 History: the iOS 18 unified single-view redesign (what iOS 26 replaced)

Worth knowing because it is the reference case study in how *not* to structure a photo app, and because half the internet's "Photos IA" writing still describes it.

iOS 18 removed the four-tab bar and replaced it with **one scrolling `UICollectionView` surface**: grid on top, everything else below as a "Collection." Apple's release-day framing: *"The biggest-ever update to Photos… The beautiful, simplified layout puts the library into a **unified yet familiar view**… New collections like Recent Days, People & Pets, and Trips automatically keep the library organized with on-device intelligence… Users can personalize their experience with a **customizable layout**… and **pin favorite collections**."*

The iOS 18 section set: Recent Days, Albums, People and Pets, Memories, Trips, Shared Albums, Pinned Collections, Featured Photos, Media Types, Utilities, Wallpaper Suggestions.

**Documented complaints** (MacRumors, "Two Months Later, Users Still Divided," Nov 21, 2024): cluttered interface making specific photos hard to find; **redundant auto-generated albums and collections**; photos/videos no longer defaulting to full-screen viewing; **removal of the Library and Albums tabs**; **AI-organization overemphasis at the expense of simple manual organization**. Some users refused to update to iOS 18. An entire genre of "how to fix / revert the iOS 18 Photos app" articles exists (Macworld, TechRadar, Cult of Mac, Pocket-lint, OSXDaily).

#### 1.15.1 ⚠️ THE REGRESSION: iOS 26 **removed** the ability to hide/exclude collections

This is the single clearest product opening in the entire IA.

**iOS 18** had a **`Customize & Reorder`** sheet at the very bottom of the unified view. Each collection had a **checkmark you could deselect to remove it from view entirely**, plus a three-bar drag handle to reorder; you exited with an **X** in the top right. MacRumors' verbatim iOS 18 flow: *"Open the Photos app. Scroll all the way down to the bottom of the main view. Tap the Customize and Reorder option… deselect the checkmark next to a collection to remove it from view, and tap and hold the three bars next to a collection, then drag to rearrange its position."*

**iOS 26 deleted that sheet.** The bottom button is now just **`Reorder`**. MacRumors, verbatim: *"You can still grab and drag to reorder, but **there is no longer an option to exclude certain types of collections**."* Collapsing is the partial substitute: *"When collapsed, you'll only see the name of the collection rather than a thumbnail preview of what it includes."* **A collapsed collection still occupies a titled row.** Apple's current guide contains no hide/exclude affordance anywhere. **Still absent in iOS 27 beta 3 / public beta 1.**

The workaround chain (Settings → Apps → Photos → turn off `Show Featured Content`; then collapse each row one by one) is multi-step, non-obvious, and **incomplete** — those toggles suppress *generation*, not the section chrome. Users cannot get a clean grid-only Photos app. MacObserver's guide on the topic concludes plainly that automatic grouping **cannot be fully turned off** in iOS 26.

### 1.16 iOS 27 (fall 2026, currently BETA — do not ship against this today)

**Status: developer beta 3 (`24A5380h`, July 6, 2026); public beta 1 seeded July 13, 2026 (identical build). Ships fall 2026. NOT shippable today.**

**iOS 27 does not restructure the IA.** `Library` / `Collections` / `Search` persist unchanged. IA-relevant additions:

| Addition | Detail |
|---|---|
| Two new `Utilities` collections | **`Captured by Me`** — *"all of the images that you've taken from the Camera app on your current or past iPhone"*. **`Identity Documents`** — aggregates pictures of passports, licenses, and similar documents. |
| **`Show Selected`** | New view in `Library` showing all currently-checked photos, so you can bulk-edit metadata |
| **Star ratings (1–5) and keywords** | On photos and videos, **with filter-by-rating**. Apple's first genuinely metadata-driven organization. |
| **`Start Slideshow`** | From **any** album or collection (previously Memories-only). Tap the icon in the upper right → `Start Slideshow`. Customizable transitions, slide duration, background music; **saveable as a video**. |
| **`Create Shared Album`** | A dedicated option in any album menu |
| Shared Albums overhaul | Filterable by photos or videos; settable to **expire after 30 days**; upload links + granular permissions; activity log; emoji reactions; **full-resolution media**; **Windows/Android participation** |
| **`Sync Immediately`** | Settings → Photos |
| Performance | Collections tab renders faster; Photos search rebuilt — Apple: *"In Spotlight, Photos, and Mail, the search experience has been rebuilt"* (to be *"more stable and efficient"*). Search also improves people/pet photo selection in Top Results. |

**Device gates:** the performance/organization features run on iPhone 11 and later; the AI editing tools (Clean Up / Extend / Reframe) require Apple Intelligence (iPhone 15 Pro and later, plus the iPhone 16 line / 16e).

⚠️ **Trap (unsourced number):** A widely circulated "**~70% faster**" figure is attached to new Camera captures appearing in Photos. Apple's WWDC 2026 newsroom copy says photos *load* up to 70% faster; MacRumors says only that captures load *"quicker."* **The specific "new Camera captures appear 70% faster" claim is unverified.** Do not quote it.

⚠️ **Trap (strategic, unresolved):** **It is unknown whether iOS 27's star ratings and keywords are exposed to third parties via PhotoKit.** No Apple developer documentation or release note confirms it either way. This is strategically decisive — see §1.17.

### 1.17 What a third-party app can and cannot do

The PhotoKit surface is far narrower than the Photos UI. **Every one of Apple's *differentiated* collections is proprietary.** That is simultaneously Apple's moat and your opening.

`PHAssetCollectionSubtype` — the complete case list, fetched from Apple's docs 2026-07-14:
`albumRegular`, `albumSyncedEvent`, `albumSyncedFaces`, `albumSyncedAlbum`, `albumImported`, `albumMyPhotoStream`, `albumCloudShared`, `smartAlbumAllHidden`, `smartAlbumAnimated`, `smartAlbumBursts`, `smartAlbumCinematic`, `smartAlbumDepthEffect`, `smartAlbumFavorites`, `smartAlbumGeneric`, `smartAlbumLivePhotos`, `smartAlbumLongExposures`, `smartAlbumPanoramas`, `smartAlbumRAW`, `smartAlbumRecentlyAdded`, `smartAlbumScreenshots`, `smartAlbumSelfPortraits`, `smartAlbumSlomoVideos`, `smartAlbumTimelapses`, `smartAlbumUnableToUpload`, `smartAlbumUserLibrary`, `smartAlbumVideos`, `smartAlbumScreenRecordings`, `smartAlbumSpatial`.

**There is NO subtype for** Memories, Trips, People & Pets, Groups, Recent Days, Featured Photos, Wallpaper Suggestions, Pinned, or any content-aware Utility (Receipts, Documents, Handwriting, Illustrations, QR Codes).

| Capability | Available to 3rd parties? | Mechanism / why not |
|---|---|---|
| Liquid Glass tab bar, floating + minimize-on-scroll, search tab | **Yes — free** | Stock UIKit/SwiftUI. `UITabBarController` + `UITab` + **`UISearchTab`** (`automaticallyActivatesSearch`), or SwiftUI `TabView` + `Tab(role: .search)`. **Recompiling with the iOS 26 SDK gives you the Liquid Glass bar and the scroll-minimize morph for free.** Ref: WWDC25 session 284, "Build a UIKit app with the new design." |
| Chronological grid, `Years`/`Months`/`All` scopes, pinch-to-zoom | **Yes** | `PHAsset.creationDate` + `PHFetchOptions` sort descriptors. Zoomable grid layout is trivial. |
| **Curation** behind `Years`/`Months` (best-shot pick, similar-photo suppression, screenshot/receipt/whiteboard filtering) | **No** | No public API. You must build your own aesthetic scorer + junk classifier (Vision + your own models). **This is a real differentiation surface.** |
| `View Options` toggles (Zoom, Aspect Ratio Grid / Square Photo Grid, hide Screenshots / Shared with You / From My Mac / Shared Library Badge) | **Yes** | `PHAssetMediaSubtype.photoScreenshot`; `PHAsset.sourceType` (`.typeUserLibrary` / `.typeCloudShared` / `.typeiTunesSynced`) covers "From My Mac"; Shared-with-You assets via the Shared with You framework / PHAsset source flags; aspect-vs-square is pure layout (`PHAsset.pixelWidth`/`pixelHeight`). |
| Sort + Filter (Recently Added / Date Captured; Favorites, Edited, Photos, Videos, Not in an Album; combinable) | **Yes** | `PHFetchOptions` predicates + sort descriptors. `Not in an Album` requires diffing the user library against the union of `PHAssetCollection` memberships — cheap but O(albums); Apple gets it for free. |
| **`Media Types` row** | **Yes — 1:1, and it is the ONLY Collections row that is** | `PHAssetCollection.fetchAssetCollections(with: .smartAlbum, subtype: …)` over the smart-album subtypes above. |
| **User albums + folders + shared albums (read AND write)** | **Yes — fully** | `PHAssetCollection` (`albumRegular`), `PHCollectionList` (folders), `albumCloudShared`. Create/modify via `PHPhotoLibrary` change requests with **full library authorization**. **You can mirror or two-way-sync the user's real Apple album tree — the single strongest "companion app" wedge in the whole API.** |
| Hidden, Recently Added, Favorites, Imports, Unable to Upload (Utilities subset) | **Yes** | `smartAlbumAllHidden`, `smartAlbumRecentlyAdded`, `smartAlbumFavorites`, `albumImported`, `smartAlbumUnableToUpload`. |
| **`Recently Deleted`** | **No** | Not fetchable by third parties at all. |
| Duplicates, Recovered, Recently Viewed, Recently Shared, Recently Edited | **No** | No API. Rebuildable (perceptual hashing for duplicates; your own activity log for the rest). |
| Semantic Utilities: `Documents`, `Receipts`, `Handwriting`, `Illustrations`, `QR Codes` | **No** | No API. Rebuildable with Vision (`VNRecognizeTextRequest`, document detection, `VNDetectBarcodesRequest` for QR) + a small classifier. |
| **`People & Pets` / `Groups`** | **NO — the single biggest "rebuild from scratch" item** | **`PHPerson` is not public.** No subtype for People, Pets, or Groups. ⚠️ **Trap:** `albumSyncedFaces` **looks** like the answer and is not — it only covers legacy iTunes-synced Faces albums from a Mac, never the on-device recognized people. You must run your own face/pet detection + embedding + clustering (Vision, or a custom model). Co-occurrence grouping is easy *once you have identities*. |
| **`Memories`** (incl. memory movies) | **No** | **`PHMemory` is not a public API.** No subtype. You must generate your own themed compilations — *and license your own soundtrack music*, a legal problem Apple sidesteps via Apple Music integration. |
| **`Trips`** | **No — but easily rebuildable** | Not exposed as a collection, but `PHAsset.location` gives you `CLLocation`; DBSCAN / temporal clustering over (lat, lon, date) reproduces Trips well. Reverse-geocode names with `CLGeocoder`/MapKit. **One of the easiest Apple collections to beat** — Apple offers *zero* trip editing. |
| `Recent Days` grouping | **Partly** | Day grouping is trivial (`PHAsset.creationDate`). The *"summary of the best photos from the day"* curation is not exposed. |
| **`Pinned` Collections** (read or write the user's pins) | **No** | No PhotoKit API. Implement your own pinning model — and beat Apple by allowing pinned **saved searches, faces, date ranges, and folders**, not just Apple's fixed object set. |
| Photos **Search** (as an index/API) | **No** | Not exposed as a search API. PhotoKit gives you assets + metadata; **you must build the index yourself** (Vision `VNRecognizeTextRequest`, `VNGenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest`, face/pet detection, Core ML, CLIP-style embeddings). ⚠️ **Trap:** Apple indexes continuously with **system privileges**; a third-party app must index under **app-lifecycle/background-execution constraints**. This asymmetry is the hardest engineering problem in building a Photos competitor — plan for it before you plan anything else. |
| Map browsing | **Yes** | `PHAsset.location` + MapKit clustering. |
| Event details (concerts / sports panel) | **No** | Not exposed. Rebuildable in principle (geo + time → ticketing/sports/music APIs) but requires **third-party data licensing** (Ticketmaster / Songkick / setlist.fm / sports feeds). Apple has a structural advantage via Apple Music. |
| Collections layout state, collapse, reorder, avatar-menu prefs | **Yes (n/a)** | Pure app view-state. Apple's version is *less* capable than iOS 18's — see §1.18. |
| **iOS 27 star ratings + keywords via PhotoKit** | **UNKNOWN — strategically decisive** | No Apple developer doc or release note confirms exposure either way. **Action: check the iOS 27 PhotoKit release notes and any WWDC 2026 Photos/PhotoKit session on a beta SDK.** If exposed → a shared metadata substrate exists for the first time and companion-app strategy changes materially. If **not** exposed → Apple has just built a metadata lock-in moat, and you should ship ratings/keywords/tags **immediately** with XMP-sidecar import/export as the interop story. |

### 1.18 Where Apple is weak — our opening

- **You cannot hide a Collections section. Period.** iOS 18's `Customize & Reorder` checkboxes are gone; iOS 26 offers only `Reorder` + collapse, and a collapsed section still occupies a titled row. Apple's `Show Featured Content` / `Show Holiday Events` toggles suppress *generation*, not *chrome*. **Ship a first-class "what appears in my app" control: per-section show/hide, plus a genuine "grid only, no AI sections" mode.** MacObserver's own conclusion: automatic grouping **cannot be fully turned off**. Search volume for "stop iOS 26 from automatically organizing your photos" quantifies the demand.
- **Albums is 3+ taps away.** Losing the dedicated `Albums` tab is the **#1 named complaint** of the iOS 18 redesign and **iOS 26 did not fix it** — Albums remains a row you scroll to inside Collections, vs **1 tap pre-iOS 18**. The workaround (pin it) is undiscoverable. **Putting user albums one tap away is instant differentiation for the manual-organizer segment.**
- **Redundant, un-deletable auto-generated sections.** The loudest complaint about the whole redesign. MacRumors' two-months-later piece cites *"confusion from redundant auto-generated albums and collections"* and *"overemphasis on AI features at the expense of simple organization."* Eleven sections; most users want three.
- **Memories resurfaces painful content, and the mitigations are scattered across three UI locations.** Ex-partners, deceased relatives, hospital photos. The levers are: photo-level `Don't Feature a Person` → `Feature This Person Less` / `Never Feature This Person`; collection-level `Hide [name]` / `Don't Feature [name]`; avatar-menu `Show Featured Content` / `Show Holiday Events`. **This is the most emotionally severe complaint in the entire app and Apple handles it badly. A single, clear, respectful "what should I resurface?" control wins on trust alone.**
- **The three toolbar controls are undiscoverable.** Sort and Filter, Layout and Reorder, and More are three different buttons in three different places, and `Show Map` lives under two of them depending on context. Surface density / aspect / exclusion / sort as **persistent first-class chips**, not two-levels-deep menus.
- **Map is a hidden menu item, not a destination.** Pre-iOS 18 it was a visible `Places` album; now it is buried under a toolbar menu. **A dedicated, always-available Map tab is a straightforward win.**
- **No manual control over Trips at all.** You cannot create, rename, merge, or split a Trip, and GPS-less photos are silently excluded. **Let users name/merge/split trips and merge across devices.**
- **Search is weak and Apple knows it.** Apple rebuilt search for iOS 27 (*"In Spotlight, Photos, and Mail, the search experience has been rebuilt"*) and specifically improved people/pet photo selection in Top Results — an implicit admission that ranking was poor. Meanwhile **Apple Intelligence NL search is gated to iPhone 15 Pro+/16-series and 16 languages**, leaving most of the installed base on literal keyword search.
- **The `Recently Added` vs `Date Captured` sort distinction confuses users constantly** — imported/AirDropped photos land at "today" by default.
- **The filter set is shallow:** no filter by camera, lens, ISO, location radius, or person. No ratings and no keywords until iOS 27 — meaning **there is a window, closing this fall, to ship ratings/keywords/tags first.**
- **Duplicates is famously unfindable** (large search volume for "Duplicates folder missing in Photos") and the merge flow is slow on large libraries. `Utilities` as a whole is a grab-bag with no organizing logic — `Handwriting` sits next to `Recently Deleted` next to `Favorites`, three taps and a scroll from app launch.
- **No way to correct Apple's classifications.** A misfiled receipt, a misidentified concert, a mis-clustered pet: Apple offers no repair path except for people (`This is Not [name]`). **Correctability is a cheap, high-trust differentiator.**
- **Settings are split-brain** — the avatar menu holds four toggles, Settings → Apps → Photos holds the biometric lock, `Show Hidden Album`, and (iOS 27) `Sync Immediately`. Motion-sensitive users in particular cannot find the autoplay kill-switch.
- **`Identity Documents` (iOS 27 beta) is a trust liability Apple is voluntarily taking on** — silently aggregating passports and driver's licenses into a browsable collection. **A privacy-forward competitor should treat this as opt-in, locked, and strictly on-device — and say so loudly.**
## 2. Library & Grid Browsing

The Library is Photos' primary surface: an infinite, date-ordered grid of every asset in the user's photo library, plus the zoom hierarchy, sort/filter controls, multi-select, and the full-screen detail viewer you reach by tapping a thumbnail. In iOS 26 it is one of exactly two tabs (`Library` and `Collections`) in a restored bottom tab bar, after iOS 18 deleted the tab bar entirely and turned Photos into a single long scroll view — a change that produced the loudest Photos backlash in the app's history. **The single most important thing an implementer must know: the classic four-level Years/Months/Days/All pyramid is gone. iOS 26 has only three levels — `Years`, `Months`, `All` — and Apple explicitly states that Years and Months are *curated*, hiding "similar photos, screenshots, whiteboards, and receipts." Only `All` shows the complete library.** Everything a competitor builds in this domain sits downstream of that fact: users do not trust a grid that silently omits their photos.

### 2.1 Top-level structure: the tab bar and where Library sits

iOS 26 restored a bottom tab bar with two items: `Library` (bottom-left) and `Collections`. A `Search` button is separate and also at the bottom — it was relocated from the top in iOS 26. Apple's exact instruction is `"Make sure the Library tab is selected in the bottom-left corner."` When you scroll the Library grid, the tab bar morphs into a navigation bar that exposes the `Months` and `Years` options, with controls to return to the tab bar or launch Search.

| Release | Photos top-level IA |
|---|---|
| iOS 17 and earlier | 4-tab bar: `Library`, `For You`, `Albums`, `Search`; Library had 4 zoom levels (Years / Months / Days / All Photos) |
| iOS 18.x | **No tab bar at all.** One continuous scroll view: grid on top, collections carousels below. `Days` level removed. |
| iOS 26 (current, 26.5.2) | 2-tab Liquid Glass tab bar: `Library` \| `Collections`, plus a separate bottom `Search` button. Three levels: `Years` \| `Months` \| `All`. |

⚠️ **Trap:** Do not model the iOS 18 single-scroll IA. Apple itself reversed it. The removal drew sustained press and community hostility (Pocket-lint: the redesign is "a disaster"; an Apple Community thread titled "I despise the iOS 18 Photos App"), and a paid third-party app — Photon Library, $5, Sept 2024 — shipped specifically to "bring back the feel of the old iOS Photos app." The lesson for a competitor is behavioral, not visual: **ship a conventional, persistent tab bar and never take it away.**

The `Collections` tab (the other half of the IA, and the destination for everything the Library grid does not hold) contains, per Apple and press: `Recent Days` (top of the tab in iOS 26), `Saved Today`, `Memories`, `Featured Photos`, `People & Pets`, `Trips`, `Pinned`, `Albums`, `Shared Albums`, `Media Types`, and `Utilities`. Apple's Collections page opens with `"curated collections such as Memories, Favorites, People & Pets, and more."` Two whole browsing axes live here and are covered in their own atlas sections: **Places / map-based browsing** (Apple has a dedicated page, "Browse photos and videos by location on iPhone") and **Trips** ("Find your travel photos and videos"). Both are first-class ways users navigate a library and neither is reachable from the Library grid.

### 2.2 Library levels: `Years` / `Months` / `All` (the `Days` level is dead)

You reveal the level control by **swiping/pulling down on the photo grid** — it is *not* a persistent segmented control. Apple, verbatim:

> "Swipe down on the photo library grid, then tap one of the following: **Years:** Quickly locate a specific year in your photo library. **Months:** View collections of photos that you took throughout a month, organized by significant events—like a family outing, social occasion, birthday party, or trip."

And the disclaimer that defines the whole surface:

> "**Years and Months views are curated to show your best shots, and visual clutter like similar photos, screenshots, whiteboards, and receipts aren't shown. To see every photo and video, tap All.**"

`Months` clusters by "significant events" — on-device spatiotemporal + content clustering. `Years` and `Months` both apply an on-device aesthetic/curation score to pick "best shots" and actively suppress screenshots, near-duplicates, whiteboards, and receipts. Apple exposes **no API and no user control** over this scoring. The `Days` level from iOS 13–17 was cut in the iOS 18 redesign and did not return; its replacement is the `Recent Days` *collection* on the Collections tab (§2.9).

⚠️ **Trap:** `Years` and `Months` are lossy views. A large fraction of "my photos are missing!" support traffic is users looking at a curated level. If you replicate the hierarchy, either (a) show a persistent, honest indicator of how many assets are being suppressed at the current level, or (b) default to complete and make curation opt-in. Apple does neither.

⚠️ **Trap:** The Years/Months control being hidden behind a pull-down gesture is undiscoverable. MacRumors flagged the analogous iOS 18 filter button: it "was hidden unless you started scrolling... which could be confusing."

### 2.3 Grid density: pinch-to-zoom and `View Options` → `Zoom In` / `Zoom Out`

Two mechanisms change thumbnail density.

- **Gesture.** Apple: `"Tip: While you're viewing the library, pinch the screen to zoom in or out."`
- **Menu.** Tap the More (ellipsis) button → `View Options` →
  - `"Enlarge the size of the photo and video thumbnails: Tap Zoom In."`
  - `"Reduce the size of the photo and video thumbnails, to see more at the same time: Tap Zoom Out."`

`Zoom In` and `Zoom Out` are **repeatable menu items, not a slider**.

**How many discrete densities exist is UNVERIFIED.** Apple documents only the two repeatable actions and the pinch gesture and never states a count. No primary source gives one. Do not assume a number; verify on a device. There is also no way to jump directly to a specific density, and no documented "remember my zoom per collection / across launches" behavior.

### 2.4 `Aspect Ratio Grid` vs `Square Photo Grid`

Also under More → `View Options`. Apple's published text, verbatim (typo and all):

> "View each photo or video thumbnail in the dimension it was captured in: Tap **Aspect Ration Grid**. To return to square thumbnails, tap **Square Photo Grid**."

⚠️ **Trap — Apple's own documentation has a typo.** A byte-level grep of Apple's raw HTML for the "Browse your photo library on iPhone" page finds the string `Aspect Ration` exactly once, and **no** correctly-spelled `Aspect Ratio Grid` anywhere on the page. The real in-app string is almost certainly `Aspect Ratio Grid`, but **no source confirms the on-screen label**. Verify on device before using either spelling in UI copy, localization strings, or a test fixture.

Two commonly-repeated sub-claims are **inferences, not documented facts**: (a) that Square is the default (only implied by Apple's "To return to square thumbnails"); (b) that the menu shows whichever mode you are *not* currently in (Apple never says this). Treat both as unverified.

Square mode center-crops thumbnails to 1:1; Aspect Ratio mode renders each thumbnail at its native aspect (a masonry/mosaic grid). Apple offers no in-between (e.g. 4:3-normalized) mode. The setting is buried two levels deep and most users never find it.

### 2.5 `View Options` content-hiding toggles (persistent) — vs `Filter` (temporary)

Apple draws a crucial distinction that an implementer must preserve: **View Options are durable de-cluttering; Filters are a temporary narrowing.** The View Options toggles, per Apple:

| Apple's instruction | Toggle label |
|---|---|
| "Hide screenshots" | `Screenshots` |
| "Hide photos and videos shared with you in Messages" | `Shared with You` |
| "Hide photos and videos you manually added from your Mac" | `From My Mac` |
| "Hide the shared library badge on thumbnails" / "Hide the thumbnail badge on items in your iCloud Shared Photo Library" | `Shared Library Badge` |

Defaults, per Apple: `"By default, screenshots, photos and videos synced from your Mac, and photos and videos shared with you in the Messages app automatically appear in your photo library. You can hide these items to reduce clutter... To stop hiding them, tap the option again."`

⚠️ **Trap:** Apple's own documentation lists `Shared Library Badge` **twice**, under two different descriptions. It is **one toggle**, not two. Do not build two.

There are only **four** exclusions. Notably there is no "hide receipts/documents" toggle even though Photos *knows* what a receipt is (it maintains a Receipts collection under Utilities).

### 2.6 Library sort: `Sort by Recently Added` / `Sort by Date Captured`

The Library sort menu (More button; Apple's iOS 26 page is titled "Sort and filter the photo library on iPhone") has **exactly two options**:

> "**Sort by Recently Added:** Photos and videos you added most recently appear at the bottom of the library. **Sort by Date Captured:** Photos and videos are sorted by the date they were taken, instead of the date they were added to the library."

⚠️ **Trap — direction is inverted relative to almost every other gallery app.** Newest items land at the **bottom**. There is **no newest-first/oldest-first toggle for the Library** — that framing exists only inside albums (§2.7). "The Library opens scrolled to the bottom" is true in practice but is an **inference, not an Apple-documented fact**; Apple never states it. Apple also never states the direction for `Sort by Date Captured` — ascending is inferred. Verify on device.

Semantics: `Date Captured` = EXIF/creation date. `Recently Added` = the date the asset entered the library, which diverges for imports, AirDrops, Messages saves, and scanned old photos (a scanned 1970s print has an old capture date but a today added-date). Apple names `Sort by Recently Added` as its own recommended route to find items you just imported or saved.

### 2.7 `Filter` — Library filters vs album filters and sorts

**Library filter menu** (More → `Filter`). Apple: `"You can apply filters to your photo library to display only particular items—such as Videos, Favorites, or Not in an Album—and temporarily hide everything else."` Filters **combine**: `"Tip: You can apply multiple filters at the same time. For example, tap Photos and Edited to see only photos you've edited."` To clear: `"To remove the filters and return to the full library, tap All Items."`

Labels Apple names: `Photos`, `Videos`, `Favorites`, `Edited`, `Not in an Album`, `All Items` (reset).

⚠️ **Trap:** Apple names these **by example only** ("such as..."), never as an exhaustive menu. The list is confirmed-but-possibly-incomplete — there may be additional items. Verify on device before treating it as a spec.

`Not in an Album` is a genuinely beloved filter for library-cleanup workflows and has no PhotoKit equivalent (see §2.16).

**Album filter and sort** — a *different* vocabulary, and this is where true newest/oldest sorting lives. Apple: `"You can filter an album to show only photos, only videos, or photos and videos you marked as favorites. You can also sort photos and videos in an album by newest to oldest, oldest to newest, or in a custom order."` And: `"If you choose Sort by Custom Order, touch and hold the photo or video thumbnail, then drag it into a new position."` To clear: `"tap the icon that replaced [the More button] at the bottom of the screen, then tap Remove Filter"` — an active filter visibly changes the toolbar icon.

⚠️ **Trap — label attribution.** Apple's page prints **only** the label `Sort by Custom Order`. It *paraphrases* the other two ("newest to oldest, oldest to newest") and never prints the strings `Sort by Oldest First` / `Sort by Newest First`. Those two labels are corroborated only by press (iDownloadBlog, MacRumors). Two further commonly-repeated claims are **UNVERIFIED with no source either way**: that Shared Albums offer `Sort by Date Added` and lack custom order; and that albums have a `Select All` button that the main Library lacks.

### 2.8 Scrolling and scrubbers

Two distinct scrubbers exist; do not conflate them.

1. **Viewer filmstrip scrubber — DOCUMENTED.** In the full-screen viewer: `"swipe the thumbnails below the photo to quickly jump forward or back."` A horizontal thumbnail strip beneath the photo, synchronized with the paged viewer.
2. **Grid fast-scroll scrubber — UNVERIFIED.** Apple's Photos documentation never mentions a drag-to-fast-scroll scroll indicator on the library grid. What *is* documented is user pain: Apple Community ("How do you scroll fast to the end of a big library?") and MacRumors Forums threads report that rapid scrolling to the end of a large library broke or changed with iOS 18. Whether iOS 26's grid indicator is grabbable, and whether it shows a date bubble, **could not be sourced**. Verify on device; do not spec it from memory.

There is **no jump-to-date affordance in the grid**. To reach a distant point in time you must pull down to `Years`/`Months` or use Search. Per Luke Wroblewski's UX analysis of the redesign, scrolling-to-find-an-image is the *dominant* Photos use case — which makes this the highest-value, lowest-effort gap in the whole domain.

### 2.9 Motion autoplay: `Auto-Play Motion` and `Loop Videos`

Apple: `"By default, videos and Live Photos automatically play when you tap Collections. To turn autoplay off, tap your account in the top-right corner, then turn off Auto-Play Motion and Loop Videos."`

| Control | Effect | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Auto-Play Motion` | Live Photos / short videos begin playing as you scroll, without tapping | Reachable in-app (account button, top-right) **and** at `Settings` → `Apps` → `Photos` |
| `Loop Videos` | A video restarts automatically when it reaches the end | Added as a user-controllable toggle in **iOS 18.2** after complaints. On by default. |

⚠️ **Trap — scope.** Apple's documentation scopes autoplay specifically to the **Collections** tab. It does **not** claim the plain Library grid autoplays motion. Secondary sources describe the Settings toggle more broadly. The exact autoplay scope in the Library grid is **UNVERIFIED** — check on device before building a "match Apple" behavior. Autoplay is also a well-known irritant (there is a whole genre of "how to stop videos looping in the Photos app" articles) and it burns battery on long scrolling sessions.

### 2.10 `Recent Days` — where the `Days` level went

Apple: `"You can find the photos and videos you took on a particular day in the Recent Days collection. Tap Collections, then scroll down to Recent Days. Swipe left or right to quickly move between days, or tap Recent Days to view all. Tap a day to open the collection."`

The curation behavior is the important part: `"When you open a day in Recent Days, you see a summary of the best photos from the day. To see all the photos you took that day, tap Show All."` A day opens **curated by default**, with `Show All` as the escape hatch. In iOS 26, `Recent Days` sits at the **top** of the Collections tab; `Saved Today` appears below it.

⚠️ **Trap:** `Recent Days` is only *recent*. It is **not** a day-by-day browse of your entire history the way the old `Days` tab was. Users have also reported it failing to populate at all. Combined with curate-by-default, this is a second major source of "my photos are missing" belief.

### 2.11 Recency collections: `Recently Saved`, `Recently Viewed`, `Recently Shared`, `Saved Today`

Apple: `"You can find all the photos and videos you've saved from other apps—like Messages, Safari, and Mail—in the Recently Saved collection. Photos and videos that were sent to you using AirDrop also appear here."` Access: `"Tap Collections, then tap the Recently Saved collection below Pinned."` Tip: `"You can also find the Recently Saved collection below Utilities along with the Recently Viewed and Recently Shared collections."` And: `"To see photos you saved today, tap Collections, then tap the Saved Today collection below Recent Days."` Apple names `Sort by Recently Added` (§2.6) as an equivalent path.

These answer "where did the photo I just saved go?" — an extremely common question — yet they live several scrolls down in Collections → Utilities and most users never find them.

### 2.12 `Utilities` and `Media Types` collections

**Utilities** (Collections → scroll down → `Utilities`). Apple: `"you can revisit photos you recently edited, saved, viewed, or shared, or find photos based on their content—like documents, receipts, handwriting, illustrations, and QR codes."` It is also where the locked stuff lives: `"Some Utilities collections, like Hidden and Recently Deleted, are locked by default for your privacy."` `Duplicates` and `Recovered` are Utilities collections too. Reorderable: `"Tap Edit, touch and hold the collection you want to move, then drag it to a new position. To undo your changes, tap Reset."`

⚠️ **Trap:** `Imports` is frequently listed as a Utilities collection. It is **not named on any Apple page** — treat as unsourced and verify on device. (Apple does have a separate "Import and export photos and videos on iPhone" page; the import *surface* is real, its status as a Utilities collection is not established.)

The content collections (receipts, documents, handwriting, illustrations, QR codes) are powered by on-device Vision/scene classification. Classification accuracy is uneven and **there is no way to correct a misclassification or add your own category**.

**Media Types** (Collections → scroll down → `Media Types`). Apple: `"browse all your Portrait mode photos or time-lapse videos in one place."` Reorderable identically (`Edit` → drag → `Reset`), and pinnable. iOS 26 gave the Media Types and Utilities rows "larger, more distinct buttons that make it clearer you can swipe or tap to get to more options."

⚠️ **Trap:** Apple names **only** "Portrait mode" and "time-lapse" as examples and **never enumerates** the Media Types list. Any 11-item enumeration you see (Bursts / Live Photos / Panoramas / Screenshots / Slo-mo / Time-lapse / Portrait / RAW / Screen Recordings / Spatial / Cinematic) is **unverified** — it reads authoritative and is not. The *PhotoKit* enum (§2.16) *is* authoritative and is a separate, sourced artifact; do not conflate the API enum with the shipped UI list.

### 2.13 Collections customization

Collections → More button at top. Apple documents:

| Action | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| Enlarge / reduce collection tiles | `"Enlarge the size of the collection tiles"` / `"Reduce the size of the collection tiles"` / `"Show the default display"` — three tile-size display modes |
| Hide all tiles | `"Hide the collection tiles: Tap Collapse All."` (iOS 26 also allows collapsing an individual collection to name-only) |
| Reorder | `"Reorder collections: Tap Reorder, touch and drag a collection into a new position..."` **Second path Apple also documents:** `"Scroll to the bottom of the screen, tap Reorder."` |
| Pin | `"Tap Edit (to the right of the Pinned heading)... Pin a collection: Tap the suggested collection you want to add, or scroll down and tap Any Collection or Album to see more options."` Shortcut: `"touch and hold it, then tap Pin"` / `"Unpin"` |
| Library scope (iCloud Shared Photo Library members) | `"Choose which library to include in collections: Tap Both Libraries, Personal Library, or Shared Library."` Also reachable as `Library View Options` from the **profile button** in the upper-right; thumbnails carry Shared Library / Personal Library badge icons. |

**iOS 26 regression:** MacRumors notes that in iOS 26 `"there is no longer an option to exclude certain types of collections"` — you can collapse but not remove. This drew immediate complaints. Keeping true exclusion is an obvious free win.

Separately, Apple documents an entirely distinct content-suppression surface — **"Hide people, memories, and holidays in Photos on iPhone"** — which changes what appears while browsing and is *not* the same as View Options hiding or the Hidden album. An implementer needs all three concepts.

### 2.14 Multi-select

Apple's own words: `"Tap Select, then tap multiple photos or slide your finger across multiple photos to select more than one."` iOS 26 made the `Select` button larger and always visible at the top of the Library.

**Confirmed bulk affordances:**

| Surface | Bulk control |
|---|---|
| `Duplicates` | `Select All` (`"tap Select, tap Select on each set or tap Select All, then tap Merge"`) |
| `Recently Deleted` | `Recover All` and `Delete All` |
| Main Library | *(see trap below)* |

⚠️ **Trap:** "There is no `Select All` in the main Library" is a near-universal belief and is consistent with Apple documenting `Select All` only for Duplicates and with an entire cottage industry of "how to select all photos on iPhone" articles — **but no source states it outright.** It is an argument from silence. Verify on device.

⚠️ **Trap:** The elaborate power-user gesture (touch the first photo, slide horizontally across a row, then without lifting slide down to sweep whole rows, holding at the bottom edge to auto-scroll) and the system-wide two-finger drag-to-select gesture are **press-sourced only, not documented by Apple**. Treat as behavior to verify, not as spec.

iOS 27 beta partially acknowledges the multi-select problem with a new `Show Selected` view (§2.18).

### 2.15 Detail viewer and the info panel

**Viewer.** Apple: `"Tap a photo to view it in full screen. Swipe left or right on the photo to keep browsing, or swipe the thumbnails below the photo to quickly jump forward or back. Tap [X] to close the photo and return to the library or collection. Tip: To focus on the photo you're viewing, tap it to hide the controls onscreen. Tap it again to show the controls."` Video: `"Tap a video to play it. As the video plays, you can pause the video, or drag the white bar to go forward or back in the video."` (Pinch-to-zoom and double-tap-to-zoom *within* an individual photo are heavily-used gestures that Apple's browsing pages do not document; assume they exist and verify.)

This part of Photos is well-liked. It is the baseline you must **match**, not beat.

**Spatial Scenes (iOS 26, new).** Apple's viewer tip: `"Tap [icon], then move your iPhone in your hand to view the photo with a 3D effect (available on iPhone 12 or later)."` Per MacRumors it is a **hexagon icon in the upper right**; the in-app control is reportedly named `Spatial Scene`. It "separates the subject from the background, introducing slight motion when you move your phone back and forth," and **"works with all photos, even those that have been in your Photo Library for years."** It runs on **iPhone 12 and later and does NOT require Apple Intelligence** — unusually permissive for a 2025/26 Apple AI feature. The effect can also be applied to the Lock Screen wallpaper. It is per-photo and manual: no default-on mode, no batch/gallery mode.

**Info panel.** Apple: `"Tap the photo or video whose metadata you want to see, then swipe up or tap [the info button]."` Close with `"Swipe down or tap [X]"`. Apple's exact field list, in order:

1. **People and pets** identified in the photo
2. A **caption field** to describe the photo or video, and make it easier to find in Search
3. Items detected by **Visual Look Up**
4. **Event information** for photos and videos taken at concerts or sporting events
5. **What device captured** the photo or video
6. **The date and time** the photo or video was taken (tap `Adjust` to edit)
7. **Camera metadata such as lens, shutter speed, file size, and more**
8. **Where** the photo or video was taken (tap the link to view the location in Maps; tap `Adjust` to edit the location; tap `Add a location` to enter one)
9. **Who shared** the photo or video with you, if it was shared
10. **What albums** the photo is in (tap to open the album)

There is **no raw/complete EXIF dump** — Apple curates which fields it shows. No histogram. No custom metadata fields (until iOS 27's Keywords).

**Adjust Date & Time / Adjust Location.** Apple: `"Tap Adjust Date & Time or Adjust Location. For date and time changes, use the calendar and clock to update, then tap Adjust. For location changes, enter where the photo was taken in the text field, then tap the location when it appears under Map Locations."` **Batch:** `"To change the date, time, or location of a batch of photos, tap Select, tap the thumbnails you want to change, then follow the steps above."` **Revert:** `"To revert a photo or video to its original date, time, or location, tap [info], tap Adjust Date & Time or Adjust Location, then tap Revert."` The edit is a non-destructive metadata override — the original is retained, which is why Revert works.

⚠️ **Trap — the canonical use case is unserved.** Batch date adjustment sets an **absolute** date. There is **no "shift all by +3 hours"** relative/timezone-correction affordance, which is *the* archetypal need (a trip's photos shot with the camera on the wrong timezone). Cheap, high-value differentiator.

**Caption.** A free-text per-asset caption entered in the info panel, indexed by Photos Search: `"A caption field to describe the photo or video, and make it easier to find in Search."` Captions are hidden behind a swipe-up, most users don't know they exist, there is no bulk captioning, and they are not surfaced in the grid. *(The frequently-repeated claim that captions travel with the file when shared is **UNVERIFIED** — it could not be located on any Apple page. Do not rely on it.)*

### 2.16 Live Photos, bursts, `Duplicates`, `Hidden`, `Recently Deleted`, `Recovered`

**Live Photos.** Playback: `"To play the Live Photo, tap the photo thumbnail... then touch and hold the screen."` Effects — open a Live Photo, tap `Live` in the **top-left corner**, then choose:

| Label | Apple's description |
|---|---|
| `Live` | "Applies the Live video playback feature." |
| `Loop` | "Repeats the action in a continuous looping video." |
| `Bounce` | "Rewinds the action backward and forward." |
| `Long Exposure` | "Simulates a DSLR-like long exposure effect by blurring motion." |
| `Live Off` | "Turns off the Live video playback feature or applied effect." |
| `Portrait` | "Applies the Portrait effect." |
| `Portrait off` | "Turns off the Portrait effect." |

Edit tools (Edit → Live Photos): `"Set a key photo: Move the white frame on the frame viewer, tap Make Key Photo, then tap Done."` / `"Trim a Live Photo: Drag either end of the frame viewer."` / `"Make a still photo: Tap the Live button at the top of the screen to turn off the Live feature."` / `"Mute a Live Photo: Tap [speaker] at the top of the screen."` Export: share → `Save as Video`.
