⚠️ **Trap (Apple-documented gotcha):** `"Live Photos taken on an iPhone 15 model or later with a portrait effect lose the portrait effect if you change the key photo."` *(The separate claim that Live Photos are unavailable when ProRAW or HEIF Max is on is **UNVERIFIED**.)* Batch-converting Live Photos to stills — a top storage-saving request — is not offered.

**Bursts.** A burst appears as a single stacked thumbnail. Apple: `"To select the photos you want to keep, tap the Burst thumbnail, then tap Burst (number)."` / `"Gray dots below the thumbnails mark the suggested photos to keep."` / `"Tap the circle in the lower-right corner of each photo you want to save as an individual photo, then tap Done."` / `"To delete the entire Burst, tap the thumbnail, then tap [trash]."` Capture: swipe the Shutter button left, or `Settings` → `Camera` → `Use Volume Up for Burst`. Bursts are browsable at Collections → `Media Types` → `Bursts`.

⚠️ **Trap — do not ship the iPhone burst-keep labels.** The strings `Keep Only X Favorites` and `Keep Everything` appear **nowhere in Apple's iPhone burst documentation** — they are press-sourced only (Gadget Hacks, iPhone Life, MacRumors). The verbatim pair `Keep Only Selection` / `Keep Everything` is from the **Mac** Photos guide, a different platform with a different label set; the Mac semantics are `"Keep Only Selection — the selected photos appear individually... and unselected photos are placed in Recently Deleted. The burst no longer appears... Keep Everything — the selected photos appear individually, and the photo burst remains unchanged."` Do not conflate the two platforms' labels.

**Duplicates.** Collections → `Utilities` → `Duplicates`. `"Tap Merge to combine a set of duplicates, then tap Merge [number] Items."` Bulk: `"To merge multiple sets or all duplicates, tap Select, tap Select on each set or tap Select All, then tap Merge. Tap Merge [Number] Items to confirm."` Merge semantics, verbatim: `"When you merge duplicate photos, your phone combines the highest image quality and relevant data to keep one photo in your library. The other duplicate photos move to your Recently Deleted album."` So it is a **genuine merge** (best pixels + union of relevant data), not a delete — and reversible for 30 days via Recently Deleted. Visibility: `"If you don't have any duplicate photos or videos in your library, the Duplicates collection doesn't appear."` Timing: `"the duplicates detection process happens automatically and may take some time."` Available since **iOS 16 / iPadOS 16.1**.

Apple's **matching criteria are entirely undocumented** — exact-hash vs perceptual vs EXIF-assisted is not disclosed, nor is why it is so slow to populate.

**Hidden.** `"When you hide photos and videos, they move to the Hidden album, so they don't appear anywhere else in Photos, like the Library, other albums, or even the Photos widget on your Home Screen."` Hide: viewer → More → `Hide` (or touch-and-hold a thumbnail → `Hide`), then confirm; multi via Select → More → `Hide`. Find/unhide: Collections → scroll down → `Hidden` under `Utilities` → `View Album` → unlock with **Face ID / Touch ID** → More → `Unhide`. Locked by default since **iOS 16 / iPadOS 16.1 / macOS Ventura**. To remove the lock: `Settings` → `Apps` → `Photos` → turn off `Use Face ID` / `Use Touch ID` / `Use Passcode` — **this unlocks Hidden *and* Recently Deleted**. To conceal it entirely: turn off `Show Hidden Album`. Hiding syncs across iCloud devices. Platform quirk: visible by default on iPhone/iPad, **off by default on Mac** (View → Show Hidden Photo Album).

*Vocabulary note:* iOS 26's guide now says "the Hidden **collection**" and "the Recently Deleted **collection**", but the button is still `View Album` and the setting is still `Show Hidden Album`. Copy Apple's iOS 26 vocabulary ("collection") in prose; copy the literal strings in UI.

⚠️ **Trap:** Hidden is **not a vault**. It is a fixed, discoverable location behind a biometric gate — not encrypted storage. Users routinely believe otherwise.

**Recently Deleted.** `"Deleted photos and videos are kept in the Recently Deleted collection for 30 days before being permanently removed from all devices."` Access: Collections → `Utilities` → `Recently Deleted` → `View Album` → biometric/passcode unlock. Recover: `"Tap Select, then select the photo or video that you want to keep. Tap [More], then tap Recover. If you want to recover all... tap Recover All. Tap Recover to confirm."` Permanent delete: `"Tap [More], then tap Delete or Delete All. Tap Delete from All Devices or Delete Photos I Added to confirm. When you delete a photo or video from this album, you can't get it back."` The two confirm labels reflect iCloud Shared Library ownership: `"Only the person who added the photo or video to the Shared Library can permanently delete or recover it from the Recently Deleted folder."` Items merged away by Duplicates, and unselected burst frames, land here.

*(Minor inconsistency: Apple's newer standalone recover article omits `Recover All` and documents only per-item Recover; the label survives in support article 104967, updated March 2026.)*

⚠️ **Trap:** Users constantly report "I deleted photos but storage didn't go down" — because it doesn't, for 30 days. Surface this.

**`Recovered` — the collection almost nobody knows about.** A *separate* safety net from Recently Deleted. Apple: `"If a photo or video wasn't saved properly and couldn't be added to your library, you may find a copy of it in Recovered."` Access: Collections → `Utilities` → `Recovered` → tap an item → `Permanently Delete` or `Restore to Library`. Apple's hard warning: `"Important: When you delete a recovered photo or video, it's deleted permanently. You can't recover photos that you deleted from the Recovered collection in Utilities."` Apple explicitly cross-references it: `"If the photos or videos you're looking for don't appear in the Recently Deleted collection, they may be in the Recovered collection."` It is a quarantine for orphaned/partially-written assets (crashed writes, interrupted imports, third-party save failures), with **no notification** when items land in it and **no 30-day grace** on deletion.

⚠️ **Trap for *your* app:** **Assets your own app fails to save properly can end up in `Recovered`.** Robust save-completion handling is a correctness issue, not just a UX one.

### 2.17 Liquid Glass (iOS 26 visual treatment)

Photos is a flagship Liquid Glass app. Per MacRumors: the two-button tab bar "uses **translucency to show the photos that are behind it**, and when it expands into the larger navigation bar that has options for months and years, it remains clear... The tab bar, the search button, the select button, and other buttons... have the same translucency, and use the more rounded look." Chrome contracts and expands contextually as you scroll the grid.

Known complaints: legibility of translucent chrome over busy photos (a general iOS 26 grievance), and the moving-target problem — chrome that resizes on scroll makes controls feel unstable. **Strategic call for a competitor:** mimicking Liquid Glass feels native but leaves you permanently a step behind Apple's tuning. Photo apps are one of the few categories where a bold, opinionated visual identity is rewarded, because the content is the hero either way.

### 2.18 iOS 27 (BETA — NOT SHIPPABLE TODAY)

⚠️ **These features are in beta and are NOT available on the current shipping OS (iOS 26.5.2).** iOS 27 was announced at WWDC 2026; developer beta 3 (build 24A5380h) shipped 2026-07-06 and public beta 1 on 2026-07-13; general release is expected ~September 2026. All labels and behavior below come from dated tech press covering betas — **not** from Apple's shipped documentation — and may change.

Press consensus (9to5Mac): iOS 27 "doesn't contain any big changes to the design of the Photos app." But several changes land squarely in library browsing:

| Feature (beta) | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Star ratings + filter by rating** | Add **one-to-five star ratings** to photos and videos, **and filter the library by rating**. This is the single most consequential iOS 27 browsing change — a ratings filter is a core library primitive. |
| `Keywords` | Add keywords to a photo by scrolling up near the bottom of it. **Captions still exist** — keywords are additive, not a replacement. |
| `Captured by Me` | New `Utilities` collection containing only images you actually took with the Camera app (on current or past iPhones) — excludes screenshots and images saved from others. |
| `Identity Documents` | New `Utilities` collection surfacing passports, driver's licenses, and similar. |
| `Show Selected` | Displays all the photos you have currently checked, so you can review the selection and modify metadata on it. |
| Video frame extraction | Extract individual frames from a video as photos (changes what lands in the library). |
| Performance | The Collections tab renders faster; new Camera captures load into the library faster. |
| Search | Returns "more pleasing photos of people and pets in Top Results." |
| Slideshows | Creatable from **any** album or image collection (previously Memories only), with custom transitions/duration, saveable as video. |
| Shared Albums overhaul | Filter by photos/videos, 30-day expiry, upload links, activity log, emoji reactions, full-resolution items, Android/Windows contributors. |

**Read these as Apple's own bug report.** `Show Selected` is a tacit admission that multi-select in a huge grid is unmanageable. `Keywords` + star ratings admit that captions alone were insufficient for organization. `Captured by Me` admits the library is polluted by screenshots and saved images. **All of them are validated demand you can serve today, on iOS 26, before Apple ships.**

### 2.19 What a third-party app can and cannot do

The access model first, because it gates everything: since iOS 14, photo-library authorization is three-state (`denied` / `limited` / `authorized`). In `PHAuthorizationStatus.limited` the user hand-picks which assets your app may see, and this is a prominent, easy choice in the system prompt. `PHPickerViewController` / SwiftUI `PhotosPicker` runs **out of process, requires no photo-library permission at all**, and returns only what the user explicitly picks.

⚠️ **Trap — a claim you will encounter and must not build on:** it is sometimes asserted that PHPicker is a route by which a user can hand your app a **Hidden** asset. **No source supports this** (no Apple documentation, no WWDC session). Apple's own docs say hidden photos "don't appear anywhere else in Photos," and nothing indicates the picker is an exception. Treat as unverified-leaning-false. Do not design a feature around it.

| Capability | Available to 3rd parties? | Mechanism / why not |
|---|---|---|
| Full-library grid, pinch-zoom, density steps | **Yes** | Pure `UICollectionView`/SwiftUI. Use `PHCachingImageManager` with target sizes tracking the density step or you'll thrash memory on fast pinches. Requires **full** (not limited) authorization. |
| Aspect-ratio / mosaic grid | **Yes** | `PHAsset.pixelWidth` / `pixelHeight` give native aspect **without loading image data** — compute masonry layout cheaply up front. |
| Sort by capture date **and** by added date | **Yes** | `PHAsset.creationDate`, `PHAsset.modificationDate`, and — the one people miss — **`PHAsset.addedDate`** ("The date and time this asset was added to the photo library"). Drive with `PHFetchOptions.sortDescriptors`. You can also offer the ascending/descending toggle Apple withholds from the Library. |
| Filters: Photos / Videos / Favorites / Edited | **Yes** | `PHFetchOptions.predicate` on `mediaType`, `isFavorite`, `hasAdjustments` ("indicates whether the asset contains adjustment data"), `mediaSubtypes`. |
| Filter: `Not in an Album` | **Yes, but you compute it** | No predicate exists. Fetch all album memberships and take the set difference yourself. |
| Hide Screenshots / From My Mac / Shared with You | **Yes** | `PHAssetMediaSubtype.photoScreenshot`; `PHFetchOptions.includeAssetSourceTypes` with `PHAssetSourceType` (`.typeUserLibrary`, `.typeCloudShared`, `.typeiTunesSynced`). You can offer far more granular exclusions than Apple's four. |
| Media-type smart albums | **Yes — the one curation area Apple hands you outright** | `PHAssetCollectionSubtype`: `smartAlbumBursts`, `smartAlbumLivePhotos`, `smartAlbumPanoramas`, `smartAlbumScreenshots`, `smartAlbumScreenRecordings`, `smartAlbumSlomoVideos`, `smartAlbumTimelapses`, `smartAlbumDepthEffect` (Portrait), `smartAlbumSelfPortraits`, `smartAlbumLongExposures`, `smartAlbumAnimated`, `smartAlbumCinematic`, `smartAlbumRAW`, `smartAlbumSpatial`, `smartAlbumVideos`, `smartAlbumFavorites`, `smartAlbumRecentlyAdded`, `smartAlbumUserLibrary`, `smartAlbumGeneric`, `smartAlbumUnableToUpload`, `smartAlbumAllHidden`. Or filter `PHAsset.mediaSubtypes` directly. |
| Live Photo playback + identification | **Yes, well supported** | `PHLivePhotoView` (`.hint` / `.full` playback styles); `PHAsset.mediaSubtypes.contains(.photoLive)`; `PHAsset.playbackStyle` (`.livePhoto`, `.video`, `.videoLooping`, `.imageAnimated`, `.image`); `PHCachingImageManager.requestLivePhoto(...)`; `PHLivePhotoEditingContext` + `PHLivePhotoFrame` for editing; `PHAsset.playbackVariation`. Loop/Bounce/Long-Exposure *rendering* and key-photo setting you implement yourself over the video track. Watch battery/thermals when autoplaying many tiles. |
| Burst stacks + Apple's suggested keepers | **Yes — one of PhotoKit's best-covered areas** | `PHAsset.burstIdentifier`, `PHAsset.representsBurst`, **`PHAsset.burstSelectionTypes`** (`PHAssetBurstSelectionType` — includes the autoPick/userPick bits, i.e. **you can read Apple's own suggested-keeper flags, the "gray dots"**), `PHAsset.fetchAssets(withBurstIdentifier:options:)`, `PHFetchOptions.includeAllBurstAssets`, `smartAlbumBursts`. |
| Edit date / time / location (incl. batch) | **Yes** | `PHAssetChangeRequest(for:)` exposes settable `creationDate`, `location`, `isFavorite`, `isHidden`; wrap in `PHPhotoLibrary.shared().performChanges`. Batch = a loop inside one change block. ⚠️ **Trap:** your write **overwrites**; PhotoKit gives you no Revert. Store the original yourself if you want Apple's `Revert`. |
| Full EXIF (lens, shutter speed, ISO, aperture, file size) | **Yes, but not for free** | `PHAsset` does **not** carry EXIF. You must pull image data (`PHImageManager.requestImageDataAndOrientation` or `PHAssetResource`) and read `CGImageSourceCopyPropertiesAtIndex` (`kCGImagePropertyExifDictionary` / TIFF / GPS). |
| Caption (Apple's caption field) | **NO — read or write** | `PHAsset` has no public caption/title property; `PHAssetChangeRequest` has no caption setter. You can write IPTC/XMP description on export and keep your own store keyed by `localIdentifier`, but you **cannot round-trip into Apple's caption field**. Real interop wall. Expect iOS 27 `Keywords` and star ratings to have the same problem. |
| People & Pets identification | **NO** | No public faces/persons API. (`albumSyncedFaces` covers only legacy iPhoto syncs.) Rebuild with Vision. |
| Visual Look Up results | **NO** | Not exposed. Approximate with the Vision framework. |
| Years / Months "best shots" curation; `Recent Days` "best photos" summary; "significant events" clustering | **NO** | PhotoKit ships **no** aesthetic-score, best-shot, or event-clustering API. The `PHAssetCollectionSubtype` enum contains no such collection. **This is the deepest moat in the domain — and, because Apple's curation is opaque and uncorrectable, the biggest opening.** |
| `Duplicates` collection / duplicate detection | **NO** | No subtype, no API. Build your own (perceptual hash + burst/Live-sibling awareness + EXIF/size heuristics). |
| `Recovered` collection | **NO** | No subtype. |
| Utilities content collections (Receipts, Documents, Handwriting, Illustrations, QR Codes) | **Not via PhotoKit — but fully rebuildable** | No `PHAssetCollectionSubtype` cases. Rebuild on-device with **Vision**: `VNClassifyImageRequest`, `VNRecognizeTextRequest`, `VNDetectDocumentSegmentationRequest`, `VNDetectBarcodesRequest` (QR). Very achievable parity item, and you can go further (warranties, boarding passes, medical, IDs). |
| `Recently Viewed` / `Recently Shared` (system library) | **NO** | Photos tracks view and share events internally and exposes nothing. You can only track events inside *your own* app. |
| `Recently Saved` | **Partially** | `PHAssetCollectionSubtype.smartAlbumRecentlyAdded` exists; combine with `PHAsset.sourceType` and `addedDate`. |
| **Hidden assets** | **NO — the hardest wall in PhotoKit** | `PHFetchOptions.includeHiddenAssets` exists and `PHAsset.isHidden` is readable/writable — **and it is a trap.** Per Apple staff on the developer forums: *"Beginning with iOS 16, users can require authentication to view the hidden album, and the user setting is true by default. When true, the system doesn't return hidden assets even if the includeHiddenAssets fetch option is true... there is no API that would allow your app to receive these assets through PhotoKit."* **You cannot build a Hidden-album browser over the system library.** Options: implement your own vault (import copies into app-private encrypted storage and delete originals — heavy, risky), or accept the gap. **Decide this early; it materially shapes the product.** |
| **Recently Deleted assets** | **NO — completely inaccessible** | Per Apple's developer forums: *"There is no API by which your app can fetch Recently Deleted assets."* There is no `smartAlbumRecentlyDeleted` case. Your app **can** delete (`PHAssetChangeRequest.deleteAssets(_:)`, which prompts the user and routes items to Recently Deleted) but can never list, recover, or purge them. **Implication: you cannot ship "undo my delete" or "empty the trash" over the system library.** Build your own soft-delete layer and tell users plainly that Apple's 30-day trash is a *separate* thing. |
| Spatial Scenes (3D depth from any 2D photo) | **Partially** | You can *identify* spatial assets (`smartAlbumSpatial`, spatial `mediaSubtypes`). Apple's generative depth-synthesis model is **not** exposed. Approximate with a monocular depth model (Core ML / Vision) + a gyro-driven parallax shader — very achievable and visually striking. |
| Liquid Glass chrome | **Yes** | iOS 26 SDK materials; or approximate with `UIVisualEffectView` / `.ultraThinMaterial`. |
| `PHAsset.rating` / `PHAsset.extendedMetadata` | **UNVERIFIED** | Both appear in the PhotoKit docs JSON (`PHAsset.Rating`; `PHFetchOptions.prefetchAssetExtendedMetadata`) with empty/thin abstracts, and neither is surfaced anywhere in the iPhone Photos UI. Availability, semantics, and minimum OS version are **unconfirmed**. If `rating` is a real public star-rating property it would be a notable, underused surface — and would front-run iOS 27's star ratings. **Investigate before relying on it.** |

**Non-negotiable engineering requirements for any full-library browser:**
- `PHPhotoLibraryChangeObserver` + `PHChange` are **mandatory** for keeping the grid in sync. Get this right early or you ship a stale, buggy grid.
- `PHCachingImageManager`, used aggressively, or scrolling performance is unacceptable at 50k+ assets.
- A genuinely usable **Limited-access mode** — not a dead end — because a large fraction of users will choose it.
- Earn the full-access prompt with a clear value proposition *before* you ask; expect meaningful drop-off.

### 2.20 Where Apple is weak — our opening

- **No fast-scrub / jump-to-date in the grid.** There is no date-labelled scroll rail, no jump-to-date, and (per Apple Community and MacRumors Forums threads) rapid scrolling to the end of a large library broke or regressed with iOS 18 and users still complain. Scrolling-to-find-an-image is, per Luke Wroblewski's analysis, the **dominant** Photos use case. A scrubber with a floating year/month bubble plus jump-to-date is the **highest-value, lowest-effort win in the entire domain.**
- **Curation is opaque, uncorrectable, and silently lossy.** `Years`, `Months`, and each `Recent Days` day open *curated by default*, hiding "similar photos, screenshots, whiteboards, and receipts." Users conclude photos are missing. **Invert the default: complete by default, curation opt-in, with an always-visible "N hidden by curation — show" affordance.** Apple offers no way to see or correct the score.
- **Library sort is two options with no direction control**, and newest lands at the **bottom** — inverted vs. essentially every other gallery app. Apple gives no newest-first-at-top option for the Library at all. `PHAsset.addedDate` + `sortDescriptors` means you can ship both Apple modes *plus* the direction toggle Apple withholds, in an afternoon.
- **No `Select All` in the Library** (widely believed, consistent with all documentation, unverified only in the narrow sense that Apple never says it out loud). Selecting thousands of photos requires an exhausting drag; an entire genre of "how to select all photos on iPhone" articles exists because of it. iOS 27's beta `Show Selected` is Apple conceding the point. **Ship: Select All in the library, range-select (tap first + tap last), select-by-day/month header, invert selection, a persistent selection tray.** Apple has none of these in the Library.
- **`Duplicates` is the single biggest wedge.** Complaints: takes days-to-weeks to populate on large libraries (or never does); catches only near-exact duplicates and misses obvious visual near-dupes; users cannot see *why* two items matched or choose which copy survives; no way to force a re-scan; merging thousands of sets is slow and stalls. Multiple long-running Apple Community threads. Apple's matching criteria are undocumented. **A fast, explainable, user-tunable dedupe — with similar-photo cleanup, not just exact duplicates — is the strongest single feature available here.**
- **Burst triage is a hidden chore.** Many users have hundreds of unreviewed bursts silently eating storage; Apple never nags. And you can **read Apple's own suggested-keeper flags** via `PHAsset.burstSelectionTypes`. A one-tap burst-cleanup flow is a large, cheap storage win.
- **Batch date adjustment has no relative shift.** No "+3 hours" / timezone correction — the archetypal need — only absolute dates.
- **No relative/date-range/camera/lens/filetype/size/location filters** in the Library filter menu, and filters are **temporary** — they cannot be saved as a persistent smart view, so cleanup workflows reset constantly.
- **Only four content-hiding toggles**, and none for receipts or documents — even though Photos *has* a Receipts collection. Users repeatedly ask for screenshot-free libraries.
- **iOS 26 regression: you can no longer exclude collection types** from the Collections tab ("I'm surprised they eliminated the option to exclude certain types of Collections... there are some I'd still rather exclude just to reduce clutter"). You can only collapse. Keep true exclusion.
- **Utilities and Media Types are buried** behind a long Collections scroll; `Receipts`, `Documents`, `QR Codes`, and especially `Recovered` are effectively undiscovered. `Recovered` is the answer to a distressing class of "my photos vanished" tickets, has **no notification** when items land in it, and deleting from it is **instantly irreversible**. **Proactively surfacing orphaned/unsaved media would look like magic.**
- **`Hidden` is not a vault** — just a fixed location behind a biometric gate — yet users believe it is secure. A real, encrypted, plausibly-deniable vault is an obvious product.
- **Deleting doesn't free space for 30 days**, which is a constant source of "I deleted photos but storage didn't go down" confusion Apple never explains at the point of deletion.
- **No custom order and no `Select All` in the Library** even though albums have both; the Library/album sort vocabularies are inconsistent and users find the split arbitrary. Unify them.
- **Privacy is the strategic wedge.** Users are increasingly wary of granting full library access, and *all* of Apple's own intelligence (duplicates, classification, faces, curation) is already on-device. An explicit, verifiable **on-device-only** guarantee is a defensible pitch that costs you nothing and directly earns the full-access prompt.
## 3. Search

Search in Apple Photos is a single search field (reached from the search button in the **bottom-right corner** of the Photos app in iOS 26) sitting on top of an on-device "Photos knowledge graph" that Apple builds by re-analyzing every asset in the library — scene tags, face/pet clusters, OCR'd text, places, events — plus one server-assisted landmark lookup. Baseline search works on **every iPhone running iOS 26** with no Apple Intelligence required; the natural-language/semantic layer on top requires Apple Intelligence hardware (iPhone 15 Pro / 16 / 17 families).

**The single most important thing an implementer must know:** PhotoKit exposes essentially **none** of this index. Apple gives third-party apps the *pixels* and a thin sliver of EXIF-ish metadata, and keeps 100% of the derived intelligence — no people, no pets, no scene tags, no OCR text, no landmarks, no events, and (through iOS 26) not even the user's own captions. Any competing photo-search app must rebuild the entire index itself from `PHAsset` pixels. The upside is total ownership; the cost is that you pay for the analysis Apple already did.

Current shipping OS is **iOS 26.5.2** (released 29 Jun 2026). iOS 26.6 is in beta. **iOS 27** was announced at WWDC 2026 (Apple PR dated 8 Jun 2026), reached public beta 13 Jul 2026, and ships "this fall" — everything labeled iOS 27 below is **beta, not shippable today**.

---

### 3.1 The search surface — entry points and result chrome

Tapping the search button surfaces **suggestions of dates, people, and locations** before you type anything. After you run a query, Apple's guide says: *"Swipe up to browse the complete search results, or tap Collections to view collections that include your search query."* So results have two planes — a flat asset grid and a `Collections` toggle that shows matching collections.

| Surface | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Main search field | Photos → search button, bottom-right corner (iOS 26) | Pre-populated with date / people / location suggestions |
| Scoped album search | `Collections` → `Albums` → [album] → search button → *"enter the person, object, or place you're looking for"* → tap search | Documented on the **Albums** page, not the Search page |
| Scoped tab search | Apple: *"You can search in the Library or Collections tab, or within a specific album or collection."* | One-liner; no further grammar documented |
| Spotlight (system-wide) | Swipe-down Spotlight | Finds *"images in your photo library"* and *"even text in your photos using Live Text"* |

**Result-list chrome** (verbatim labels): `See All`, `Select`, `Sort by Recently Added`, `Sort by Date Captured`, `Filter` → `Favorites` / `Edited`.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Apple documents that `See All` / `Select` / `Sort` / `Filter` chrome **only** under the heading *"Search for specific photos and videos with Apple Intelligence"* on the Apple-Intelligence-in-Photos page. It is **not documented for non-Apple-Intelligence search results anywhere**. Do not assume the same chrome exists (or is spec'd) for baseline search.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** There are **three distinct sort/filter surfaces** in Photos and they are easy to conflate: search-result sort/filter (above), *"Sort and filter the photo library on iPhone"* (library-level), and *"Filter and sort photos and videos in albums on iPhone"* (album-level). They are separate Apple documentation pages with separate chrome. Do not design one control and assume it covers all three.

---

### 3.2 What Photos indexes — the eight searchable dimensions

Apple's iPhone User Guide enumerates exactly what you can type into the search field. This list is verbatim and is the authoritative spec of the searchable surface:

| # | Dimension | Apple's exact phrasing | Requires Apple Intelligence? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Date | `Date (month or year)` | No |
| 2 | Place | `Place (city or state)` | No |
| 3 | Business names | `Business names (museums, for example)` | No |
| 4 | Category | `Category (beach or sunset, for example)` | No |
| 5 | Events | `Events (sports games or concerts, for example)` | No |
| 6 | Person / pet | A person identified in the `People & Pets` collection | No |
| 7 | Text | `Text (an email address or phone number, for example)` — i.e. Live Text OCR | No |
| 8 | Caption | `Caption` | No |

Plus two non-enumerated narrowing inputs:

- **Media type tokens.** Apple's tip, verbatim: *"You can narrow your search by including a media type in the search field, such as Video or Portrait."*
- **`Shared by`** — only if you participate in an iCloud Shared Photo Library (see §3.10).

**How the index is produced.** Apple's ML research describes the **Apple Neural Scene Analyzer (ANSA)**: a multi-task on-device network whose heads produce (a) scene tags from a **fixed taxonomy image tagger**, (b) **image-language embeddings**, (c) utility classifiers for receipts / documents / repair references, (d) low-quality-image detection, (e) a dedup embedding. Apple states scene tags from ANSA "are ingested in the Photos knowledge graph" and that visual content search is surfaced "through the Photos app and Spotlight." ANSA runs all heads in **< 9.7 ms on iPhone 13** using **~24.6 MB**. Apple explicitly cites detecting "food, mountains, beaches, birthdays, pets, or hikes" and using image-language embeddings to catch "human-object interactions like people seated around a table."

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The size of Apple's scene/category taxonomy is **not published**. The widely-repeated "4,000+ scenes" figure could not be sourced to any current Apple page. Treat any specific class count as **unverified folklore** — do not put a number in a deck or a spec.

---

### 3.3 Combining terms, and the search grammar Apple never documented

Multi-term narrowing empirically works — type a person's name, accept the suggestion, then add a place and a year — and it is described extensively by the tech press. But:

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Apple's documentation **nowhere** describes "tokens," AND-semantics, or multi-term combination. The **only** narrowing mechanism Apple documents is the media-type tip quoted above. The commonly-cited example query "Jeff L. Carlson in Italy in 2022" is **not Apple's** — it traces to third-party tech writing (and "Jeff Carlson" is a tech author's own name used as a sample person). The claim that this behavior "dates back to iOS 12" is likewise press, not Apple. An implementer should **not** treat "tokens that AND together" as documented, guaranteed, or stable Apple behavior — but should note it as the *de facto* interaction model users have learned.

What is definitively absent from the grammar, in shipping iOS 26:

- No **OR**, no **NOT**/exclusion.
- No **date ranges**, no `before:` / `after:`, no numeric comparisons.
- No **`in:album`** operator (album scoping exists but is a three-tap navigation, not a query operator).
- No **saved searches**.
- No **camera / lens / EXIF** search (no "shot on 77mm", no "ISO > 3200").
- No **user-defined keywords** on iPhone — the keyword UI exists only in Photos for Mac (until iOS 27, see §3.8).

---

### 3.4 People & Pets, and Groups

Apple, verbatim: *"The Photos app sorts photos and videos of people, dogs, and cats in the People & Pets collection (or the People collection if no pets appear)."* Named people and pets become searchable inputs. The collection is kept in sync across devices: *"When you use iCloud Photos, People & Pets is kept up to date on all your devices."*

**Exact UI vocabulary** (all verbatim-confirmed):

| Action | Label / path |
|---|---|
| Name someone | Photo info panel → `Edit Name and Photos` → `Name This Person` / `Name This Pet` |
| Browse | `Collections` → `People & Pets` |
| Surface more faces | `Add People` |
| Prioritize | `Favorite` / `Unfavorite` |
| Ordering | `Sort by Name` / `Sort by Custom Order` |
| Fix a misidentification | `This is Not [name]` → `Rename This Person` / `Rename This Pet` |
| Suppress | `Hide [name]` / `Don't Feature [name]` |

**Groups** — Apple, verbatim: *"The Photos app recognizes groups of people and pets who often appear together in pictures and videos, and sorts them into group collections."* Path: `Collections` → `People & Pets` → `Groups`. Labels: `Create New Group`, `Edit Name and People`, `Add People & Pets`, `Delete Group`, drag-to-reorder, and `View Options` → `Other People` (widens the group).

**How it works (Apple's own description).** On-device: face **and upper-body** detection → separate embedding networks → a novel **incremental agglomerative clustering** in two passes (a conservative face+torso clustering, then hierarchical agglomerative clustering on face embeddings only). Apple: *"end-to-end process runs entirely locally, on the user's device."* Pet (dog/cat) recognition arrived in **iOS 17**.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The clustering description comes from a **2021 Apple ML Research post**. It is Apple's own statement but it is not a current-OS spec — the algorithm may have changed. Cite it as prior art, not as a description of what iOS 26 does today.

Known pain: recognition **stalls if the device is never left charging + idle** (see §3.14); users routinely report the People collection never populating. Merging/splitting clusters is fiddly, no confidence is surfaced, there is no bulk correction, no cross-library merge, and **no way to export the person↔asset mapping** — the names a user painstakingly assigns are trapped in Apple's library.

---

### 3.5 Places, Trips, business names, and metadata repair

Search accepts `Place (city or state)` and `Business names (museums, for example)`. Apple derives these primarily from EXIF GPS + reverse geocoding to POIs, plus on-device signals like Home/Work from Contacts or Maps.

**Trips.** A location-derived collection: *"photos and videos from your trips grouped into collections, based on location data from the photos."* Path: `Collections` → `Trips`. Verbatim navigation hint: *"Tap a year at the top of the screen to help you find older trips."*

**The info panel's location row**, verbatim: *"Where the photo or video was taken (tap the link to view the location in Maps; tap Adjust to edit the location; tap 'Add a location' to enter a location)."*

**Metadata repair as a retrieval lever** — an underrated surface. Apple documents `Adjust Date & Time` and `Adjust Location` (both with `Revert`), **and batch editing via `Select`**. This lets users fix the very date/location metadata that date-search and place-search depend on. A competitor that makes metadata repair a first-class, bulk, undoable operation directly improves its own retrieval quality.

Pain: Trips are **location-only**, so any photo with stripped GPS (screenshots, AirDropped images, most imported scans, anything from a privacy-scrubbing pipeline) never joins a trip. Business-name matching is inconsistent.

---

### 3.6 Enhanced Visual Search — the one part of Photos search that is not local

Apple, verbatim: *"Enhanced Visual Search lets you search your photo library for landmarks or points of interest in photos or videos — making it easier to find what you're looking for, even if those photos and videos don't have any saved geolocation information. Just search in the Photos app or via Spotlight for a landmark, like the Golden Gate Bridge or the Arc de Triomphe."*

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Toggle (iPhone) | `Settings` ▸ `Apps` ▸ `Photos` ▸ `Enhanced Visual Search` |
| Toggle (Mac) | `Photos` ▸ `Settings` ▸ `General` |
| Introduced | "Starting in iOS 18, iPadOS 18, and macOS Sequoia" — present in iOS 26 |
| Apple Intelligence required? | **No** — it predates 18.1 and Apple lists no AI requirement |
| Region availability | *"Enhanced Visual Search isn't available in all countries or regions."* Apple does **not** publish the list of excluded regions |
| Apple support doc | Published 15 Sep 2025 |
| Default state | **ON by default** |

**Mechanism** (the most relevant prior art in the whole atlas for anyone doing server-assisted matching without seeing user photos): an on-device model decides whether a photo likely contains a landmark, then produces a *"low-fidelity mathematical representation"* (an embedding) of the candidate region. **The embedding — not the image — is encrypted and sent to Apple** and matched against a global landmark index "too big to fit on your device." The privacy stack is three-layer:

1. **Homomorphic encryption** — Apple's server matches against the index **without decrypting** the query.
2. **Differential privacy** — the device sends **fake decoy requests** alongside the real one.
3. **OHTTP relay** — a third-party network relay strips the device's IP so Apple never sees it.

Decryption keys never leave the device; requests aren't stored and aren't linked to the Apple Account.

> ⚠️ **Trap (strategic, not technical):** Enhanced Visual Search was **turned on by default with no opt-in prompt**, and was discovered by developers in Dec 2024 / Jan 2025 (Jeff Johnson; The Register; 9to5Mac), producing a real backlash about Apple silently sending photo-derived data off-device. Many users still don't know the toggle exists. If you are building a strictly-local competitor, this is the single cleanest wedge: **"we are 100% on-device, no exceptions"** is a claim Apple Photos structurally cannot make.

---

### 3.7 Live Text (OCR) — text in photos is indexed and searchable

Apple, verbatim: *"Live Text recognizes text within your photos, videos, and images you find online."* In Photos, tap the Live Text button to select text, then: `Copy Text`, `Select All`, `Look Up`, `Translate`, `Search the web`, `Share` — plus quick actions (call a number, open a site, convert currency, get directions).

Critically, recognized text **feeds Photos search** (dimension #7, `Text`) and **feeds Spotlight**.

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Toggle | `Settings` ▸ `General` ▸ `Language & Region` ▸ `Live Text` |
| Apple Intelligence required? | **No** |
| **Hardware floor** | **iPhone XS, iPhone XR, and later** |
| Region caveat | *"Live Text isn't available in all regions or languages."* |

**Language coverage (46 locales, verbatim from Apple's iOS Feature Availability page):** Cantonese (China mainland), Cantonese (Hong Kong), Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Czech, Danish, Dutch, English (AU/CA/IN/IE/MY/NZ/PH/SA/SG/ZA/AE/UK/US), French (BE/CA/FR/LU/CH), German, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Malay, Norwegian (Nynorsk + Bokmål), Polish, Portuguese (BR/PT), Romanian, Russian, Spanish (LatAm/MX/ES/US), Swedish, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Vietnamese.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** "No Apple Intelligence required" is **not** the same as "works everywhere." Live Text (and Visual Look Up) still have a hardware gate of **iPhone XS / XR and later**. An implementer targeting older hardware, or writing marketing copy that says "works on every iPhone," will be wrong.

---

### 3.8 Captions — and iOS 27's keywords and star ratings

**Captions (shipping, iOS 26).** The photo info panel contains, verbatim: *"A caption field to describe the photo or video, and make it easier to find in Search."* `Caption` is a first-class search dimension and syncs via iCloud Photos. Feature exists since iOS 14.

Captions are **manual**, and therefore in practice **almost always empty**. Nobody built caption-based workflows because, until iOS 27, no third-party app could read or write them (see §3.17).

**iOS 27 (BETA — not shippable today):** Apple adds **user-facing keywords and 1–5 star ratings** to photos and videos in the Photos app, **and the ability to filter by rating**. This is arguably the single biggest new retrieval primitive in the Photos search domain in years — it finally gives iPhone users the manual-tagging vocabulary that Photos for Mac has had all along. *(Source: MacRumors iOS 27 Photos guide, corroborated by the `PHAsset.rating` / `PHAssetChangeRequest.addKeyword(_:)` symbols in the iOS 27 beta SDK.)*

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Do not attempt to scrape captions out of the file's metadata. The caption is **not written into IPTC until the user exports the file** — `CGImageSource` metadata scraping will not find it, and `iptcDict` does not contain it. Apple DTS told developers on the forums flatly: *"there is no API to retrieve this."* (Forum chatter claims at least one App Store app reads captions pre-iOS 27 — this could **not be verified** and may indicate a private/undocumented route. Do not rely on it.)

---

### 3.9 Categories, Utilities, and Media Types

**Category** is Apple's word for scene/object classification (`Category (beach or sunset, for example)`). No Apple Intelligence required. The taxonomy is a **closed, undocumented, fixed** vocabulary: users cannot see it, cannot extend it, and cannot add their own keywords on iPhone (until iOS 27). Queries that *sound* obvious — "Rome monuments" — fall outside it and return **nothing**.

**Utilities** (`Collections` ▸ `Utilities`), verbatim: *"you can revisit photos you recently edited, saved, viewed, or shared, or find photos based on their content—like documents, receipts, handwriting, illustrations, and QR codes."* Also contains `Recovered`, plus `Hidden` and `Recently Deleted`, which are **locked by default**. The Utilities list is reorderable via `Edit` / `Reset`. ANSA has "dedicated classifiers" for receipts, documents and repair references.

**iOS 27 (BETA)** adds **two new Utilities collections**: `Captured by Me` (all images taken with the Camera app on your current or past iPhone) and `Identity Documents` (passports, licenses, and similar). Both are new content-based retrieval categories.

**Media Types** (`Collections` ▸ `Media Types`) groups Portrait, Time-lapse, etc. — Apple's page is *"Locate photos and videos by media type on iPhone."*

> ⚠️ **Trap:** `Edit` / `Reset` reordering is documented for **Utilities** specifically. The claim that the **Media Types** list is reorderable/pinnable is **unverified** — do not spec it as Apple parity.

---

### 3.10 Events, and "Shared by" participant search

**Events.** Search accepts `Events (sports games or concerts, for example)`, and the photo info panel shows *"Event information for photos and videos taken at concerts or sporting events."* Apple is joining photo timestamp + location against an events knowledge base. Coverage is undocumented: it works for some venues/events and silently not for others.

**Shared by.** Verbatim gating: *"If you're a participant in an iCloud Shared Photo Library, you can also search by the person who added the photo or video to the library."* Apple's section heading is `Search by shared library participant`, and the documented step is literally: *"Tap, then enter 'Shared by.'"* followed by *"Tap a suggested name."*

---

### 3.11 Apple Intelligence — natural-language search, video key moments, memory movies

Two Apple labels for the same thing: the support-page section heading is **`Search with Apple Intelligence`**; the Apple Intelligence feature list calls it **`Natural language search in Photos`**.

Apple, verbatim: *"Apple Intelligence makes it even easier to find a specific photo or a key moment in a video—just describe what you want to find."* Apple's own marquee example queries: **"Maya skateboarding in a tie-dye shirt"** and **"Sadie cartwheeling on the grass."**

Note the *shape* of those examples — `<named person> doing <action> in <clothing>`. Semantic matching over on-device embeddings is **joined with the named-people index**. **Face identity is the backbone of Apple's best search queries.** Any competitor without a face recognizer cannot reproduce the demo.

**Three Apple Intelligence search features:**

| Feature | Apple's description |
|---|---|
| Natural language search | Describe what you want; results support `See All` / `Select` / `Sort by Recently Added` / `Sort by Date Captured` / `Filter` (`Favorites`, `Edited`) |
| Video key-moment search | *"You can also search video clips for key moments."* Returns a **position within a video**, not just the video |
| Memory movie from a prompt | *"You can create a custom memory movie of a story you want to see, right in Photos. Just type a description, and Apple Intelligence finds the best photos and videos, crafts a storyline with unique chapters and a narrative arc, and sets it to music."* Path: `Photos` ▸ `Collections` ▸ `Memories` ▸ `Create` ▸ enter a description ▸ `Done`. Apple's feature-list label: `Create a memory movie in Photos` |

**Gating (all verbatim from Apple's "How to get Apple Intelligence" support article, last updated 07 Jul 2026):**

| Requirement | Value |
|---|---|
| Devices | *"iPhone 15 Pro models, and iPhone 16 models or later"* (i.e. iPhone 15 Pro / 15 Pro Max, iPhone 16 family, iPhone 17 family) |
| OS | *"iOS 18.1 or later"* — shipped since iOS 18.1; present in iOS 26.x |
| Storage | *"7 GB of storage on device"* |
| Language | *"Device language and Siri language set to the same supported language"* |
| Toggle | `Settings` ▸ `Apple Intelligence & Siri` |
| Languages (16) | English, Danish, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese |
| Regions | *"With iOS 26.1 … available in most regions around the world."* EU supported from iOS 18.4+ |
| **Excluded** | **NOT available** for devices purchased in China mainland, nor for users in China mainland with a China-mainland Apple Account |
| Maturity | Apple still labels Apple Intelligence **"available in beta"** |

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The Apple Intelligence device gate excludes a very large installed base — **iPhone 14 and older, iPhone 15 / 15 Plus, and every iPhone SE get nothing**. If your competing app's semantic search runs on those devices, that is not a marginal feature difference; it is a categorically different addressable market.

---

### 3.12 Visual Look Up and visual intelligence (search-adjacent)

**Visual Look Up** — identify what is *inside* a photo. Apple, verbatim: *"With Visual Look Up, you can identify and learn about architectural landmarks, popular statues, famous art, plants, pets, books, and more that appear in photos and images. Visual Look Up can also identify food and suggest related recipes."*

- **Affordance:** open a photo full-screen; *"If the Info button displays a symbol with stars,"* Visual Look Up is available. Tap the starred Info button, then tap `Look Up` at the top of the photo information.
- Works in Photos, Safari, and Quick Look. Related capability: `Lift a subject from the photo background`.
- The info panel has a documented row: **`Items detected by Visual Look Up`**.
- **No Apple Intelligence required** — but the **iPhone XS / XR hardware floor** applies (same as Live Text).
- **Languages: only six.** English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Spanish. *"Visual Look Up isn't available in all regions or languages."*

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Visual Look Up results are a **web/knowledge card, not searchable structured tags**. Visual Look Up findings do **not** become search tokens (except where they overlap Enhanced Visual Search landmarks). Users assume "Photos knows this is a Golden Retriever, so I can search for Golden Retriever" — that inference is wrong.

**visual intelligence** (Apple lowercases the feature name) — camera + on-screen visual search. Requires Apple Intelligence.

| Entry point | Trigger |
|---|---|
| Physical world | Click-and-hold **Camera Control** (iPhone 16/17 with Camera Control). *"On iPhone 17e, iPhone 16e, iPhone 15 Pro, and iPhone 15 Pro Max"* use the Action button, a Lock Screen control, or Control Center |
| On-screen | *"Quickly press and release the side button and the volume up button at the same time"* to take a screenshot, then use the visual intelligence tools at the bottom |

Capabilities: business info in front of you (`Schedule` / `Order` / `Menu` / `Reserve`); identify plants and animals; interact with text (`Summarize` / `Translate` / `Read Aloud`, plus call/email/website actions); `Add to Calendar` → `Create Event` from a poster or flyer; search for visually similar images; swipe to highlight a specific item and search just that; and **`Ask`** (asks **ChatGPT** about what's on screen). Apple's Apple-Intelligence feature list phrasing includes *"Search Google and across supported apps."* Place-identification languages: Chinese, Dutch, Danish, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Vietnamese.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** visual intelligence's `Ask` button does **not** search your library — it searches the web, and it **routes the content to ChatGPT (OpenAI)**. Apple's only conversational visual answer today is **outsourced**. Do not model it as "Apple has an AI that can answer questions about your photos."

---

### 3.13 Conversational photo queries — there is **no** "Ask Photos" in Apple Photos

**As of shipping iOS 26.5.2, there is no Apple feature that lets you hold a conversation with your photo library.** There is no Apple analogue of Google Photos' "Ask Photos." The nearest shipping thing is visual intelligence's `Ask` → which goes to ChatGPT, about a screenshot or camera view, **not your library**.

**iOS 27 (BETA — dev testing from 8 Jun 2026 per Apple's PR; public beta 13 Jul 2026; ships fall 2026)** is where this changes. Apple's actual sentence about the new Siri AI, verbatim: *"It can draw on personal context understanding to search across messages, emails, photos, and more."*

Apple's own examples of photo-relevant queries:
- *"Search for a photo from years ago"* (apple.com/os/ios)
- Newsroom caption: *"a search of photos from the previous weekend, with subject matter and specific people called out in the search"*

**Mechanism:** Siri AI taps the **rebuilt Spotlight index**, which Apple says works "entirely on device"; harder requests escalate to **Private Cloud Compute**, where "their personal data is not stored nor made accessible to Apple or anyone else."

**Siri AI gating (iOS 27 beta, verbatim from Apple's PR):** iPhone 16 models or later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, iPad mini (A17 Pro), iPad models with M1 or later, MacBook Neo (A18 Pro), Mac with M1 or later, Apple Vision Pro. **English first** — *"Siri AI will be available as a beta later this year for users with a supported device set to English."* EU carve-out: available on Mac and Vision Pro, but *"not be available initially in the EU in iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS."* China: *"will not be available in China while Apple works through regulatory requirements."* Later language expansion is planned to Danish, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Vietnamese, Chinese (Simplified/Traditional), Japanese, Korean.

**Also iOS 27 beta:** a standalone **Siri app** with iCloud-synced conversation history; **`Siri mode in Camera`** — Apple, verbatim: *"Siri mode and Visual Intelligence let you search, ask questions, and take action based on what's around you with just a tap"* (a brand-new search entry point from the camera viewfinder).

> ⚠️ **Trap — three widely-circulated claims that are wrong or unverified:**
> - The phrasing *"gather photos from a recent trip"* is **not Apple's wording** and could not be sourced to Apple. Do not quote it.
> - The Siri app's **`Search or Ask` field label is UNVERIFIED** — it appears only in leak coverage, in no Apple source. Do not hand this label to an implementer.
> - An **`Ask Siri` entry in the Photos long-press context menu** (iOS 27 developer beta 2, single image, on-screen awareness + personal context) is corroborated **only by tech press**, not by Apple docs. Mark it beta-press-sourced.
> - **Apple Watch device lists are inconsistent in Apple's own materials** (Newsroom says Series 9+; the support article says Series 6 and later, all Ultra, SE 2+ when paired). Irrelevant to Photos, but do not quote a watch list confidently.

---

### 3.14 When the index is built — the operational fact that decides everything

Photos analysis is **deliberately deferred to charging + idle**. Apple's People-recognition research states the clustering algorithm *"runs periodically, typically overnight during device charging."* Apple's Photos & Privacy legal page states, verbatim: *"This on-device analysis includes scene classification, people and pets identification, photo quality analysis, and audio classification."*

| Claim | Sourcing status |
|---|---|
| Analysis runs while **charging + idle** | **Sourced** (Apple ML Research) |
| Device must also be **locked** | **Strongly supported but secondary** — comes from the in-app People-collection hint and secondary press (MacObserver et al.), not a verbatim Apple page |
| Full analysis takes **hours to days** after an OS update / migration / large import | **Operational folklore** — Apple Support Communities, not Apple docs. (iOS 27's multi-day `Indexing in Progress` reports independently corroborate the direction.) |

Apple Intelligence models themselves must also be **downloaded** on first enable: *"For the fastest model download experience, keep your device connected to Wi-Fi and power while models are downloading."*

**This is the single most important operational fact for anyone building a competitor**, because of the asymmetry in §3.17: Apple's Photos daemon gets **unbounded overnight NPU time**; your app gets `BGProcessingTaskRequest`, granted opportunistically and stingily. Design implication: make indexing **incremental, resumable, cheap-first** (thumbnail-resolution embeddings before full-resolution passes), and **surface progress honestly**. Users routinely believe Apple's face recognition and search are "broken" when they are simply **starved** — the device was never left locked + plugged in long enough, and Apple gives almost no progress UI. An app that shows an explicit index-progress meter and offers "index now, I'll wait" **wins on perceived reliability even at equal model quality.**

---

### 3.15 Spotlight integration

Apple, verbatim: *"On iPhone, you can search for apps and contacts, content in apps like Mail and Messages, and even text in your photos using Live Text… and find and open webpages, apps, and images in your photo library."* Enhanced Visual Search landmark results also surface *"in the Photos app or via Spotlight."* Per-app visibility toggle: `Settings` ▸ `Search` ▸ `Show App in Search`.

For a third party, Spotlight cuts exactly one way — see §3.17.

### 3.16 iOS 27 (BETA) — the rebuilt search index

Apple Newsroom, verbatim: *"In Spotlight, Photos, and Mail, the search experience has been rebuilt to make it more stable and efficient to help users find exactly what they are looking for. And in Mail, a completely new ranking system surfaces even more relevant results in **Top Hits**."*

Apple effectively conceded that search was broken. At WWDC 2026, **Stacey Ford, VP of OS Program Management**: *"We've all had that moment where you search for something you know is there, but it just won't show up."*

| iOS 27 search change | Status |
|---|---|
| Rebuilt Spotlight/Photos/Mail search index; existing content reindexed | Beta |
| `Indexing in Progress` state visible to users after updating | Beta, widely reported |
| User-facing **keywords** and **1–5 star ratings**, with **filter by rating** | Beta |
| New Utilities collections: `Captured by Me`, `Identity Documents` | Beta |
| `Siri mode` in Camera | Beta |
| Siri AI personal-context search across photos | Beta, English-first |
| Mail `Top Hits` ranking system | Beta |

> ⚠️ **Trap — two commonly-misquoted iOS 27 claims:**
> - The phrases *"rearchitected to be more stable, efficient, and comprehensive, covering both old and new content"* and new content indexed *"almost immediately"* do **not** appear in Apple's Newsroom PR. They are **MacRumors' rendering** of Apple's briefing. Attribute accordingly.
> - The **"70% faster"** figure is **not** about general library loading. Apple's iOS 27 page says ***new*** *photos load in your Photos library up to 70% faster* — it is about **newly captured** photos appearing. Apple's footnote scopes it to testing on an iPhone 15 with a **50,000-asset library**, "taking additional individual photos with Camera app." Stating it as "photos load up to 70% faster" **overclaims**.

Whether the rebuild actually fixes semantic search is **unknown** — it is beta software and Apple has over-promised on search before. This is both **a window and a risk**: if Apple's fall-2026 Photos search is genuinely good, a pure "better search" pitch weakens. Differentiate on the axes Apple **structurally cannot move** (see §3.18).

---

### 3.17 What a third-party app can and cannot do

**The one-line answer:** Apple gives you the **pixels** and a thin sliver of EXIF-ish metadata, and keeps **100% of the derived intelligence**.

#### Reading the library

`PHFetchOptions.predicate` supports **only these `PHAsset` keys** (Apple's supported-predicate-keys table):

```
SELF, localIdentifier, creationDate, modificationDate, mediaType,
mediaSubtypes, duration, pixelWidth, pixelHeight, isFavorite,
isHidden, burstIdentifier
```

> ⚠️ **Trap:** **Location is not in that list.** You can *read* `PHAsset.location` (a `CLLocation` with lat/long/altitude/speed) but you **cannot** `NSPredicate`-filter on it — you must fetch and filter in memory, which is O(library) on every geo query. *(Verification note: Apple's predicate doc says predicates must use "the properties … listed in the table," but the fact-checker could not render that table to positively confirm location's exclusion. Treat as **very likely true but unproven** — validate empirically before architecting around it.)*

#### The capability table

| Capability | Available to 3rd parties? | Mechanism / why not |
|---|---|---|
| Issue a text query against the Photos search index | **No** | No API of any kind. The index is not readable and not queryable. |
| Let the *user* search Apple's index inside your app | **Yes — indirectly** | `PHPickerViewController` / SwiftUI `PhotosPicker` embeds **Apple's own search bar** (`PHPickerCapabilities.search`). It runs **out-of-process**, needs **no photo-library permission**, and returns only what the user picks. You never see the index — only the chosen assets. *This is the only supported way to "use" Apple's search.* |
| People / face identity | **No** | No `PHPerson`, no `PHFace` (both **absent** from the Photos framework symbol list). No People smart-album subtype. No person predicate key. |
| Face **recognition** via Vision | **No** | ⚠️ **Trap:** Vision has `DetectFaceRectanglesRequest`, `DetectFaceLandmarksRequest`, `DetectFaceCaptureQualityRequest` — **detection, landmarks, and quality only**. There is **no public face-embedding / faceprint / identity API of any kind**. This looks like a face API. It is not a recognition API. |
| Pet identity | **No** | Same as above. `RecognizeAnimalsRequest` classifies *cat vs dog* — it does **not** tell you *which* dog. |
| Scene / category tags from Apple's taxonomy | **No** | Not exposed. Closest: Vision `ClassifyImageRequest` (iOS 18+) returns `ClassificationObservation`s over Apple's own image-classification taxonomy — a **different, enumerable** taxonomy you can index yourself. |
| Apple's already-computed OCR text | **No** | You must **re-OCR every asset yourself** with `RecognizeTextRequest`. |
| Live Text **UI and OCR**, from scratch | **Yes — at full parity** | VisionKit `ImageAnalyzer` + `ImageAnalysisInteraction` with `AnalysisTypes` `.text` / `.machineReadableCode` / `.visualLookUp` gives you literally Apple's Live Text UI plus `interaction.text` / `.selectedText`. This is the **one Apple capability a third party gets at parity**. |
| Visual Look Up | **Yes** | `ImageAnalyzer.AnalysisTypes.visualLookUp`; `ImageAnalysisInteraction.subjects` / `subject(at:)` / `highlightedSubjects` / `image(for:)` for a background-removed subject cutout. Vision's `GenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest` gives the mask directly. |
| Enhanced Visual Search / landmark results | **No** | No API to submit an embedding to Apple's landmark index, and **no on-device landmark classifier in Vision**. |
| Memories / Trips / Utilities collections | **No** | The full `PHAssetCollectionSubtype` enumeration contains **no** People/Pets/Places/Memories/Trips/Utilities subtype. |
| Media-type smart albums | **Yes — partially** | `PHAssetCollectionSubtype` **does** expose: `smartAlbumPanoramas`, `smartAlbumVideos`, `smartAlbumSlomoVideos`, `smartAlbumTimelapses`, `smartAlbumBursts`, `smartAlbumScreenshots`, `smartAlbumSelfPortraits`, `smartAlbumLivePhotos`, `smartAlbumDepthEffect`, `smartAlbumLongExposures`, `smartAlbumAnimated`, `smartAlbumCinematic`, `smartAlbumRAW`, `smartAlbumSpatial`, `smartAlbumScreenRecordings`, `smartAlbumFavorites`, `smartAlbumRecentlyAdded`, `smartAlbumAllHidden`, `smartAlbumUnableToUpload`, `smartAlbumUserLibrary`, `smartAlbumGeneric`. ⚠️ **Trap:** this list *looks* comprehensive; the content-based Utilities categories (Documents/Receipts/Handwriting/Illustrations/QR Codes) have **no subtype**. |
| Event (concert / sports) metadata | **No** | Apple joins timestamp+location against an internal events knowledge base. You'd need your own events source (or Calendar / ticket-email signals). |
| "Shared by" participant as a search key | **No** | `PHAsset.sourceType`, `PHFetchOptions.includeAssetSourceTypes`, and the shared-library APIs on `PHPhotoLibrary` surface library *membership* — but "who added it" is **not a queryable attribute**. |
| Read/write **captions, keywords, ratings** | **iOS 26: No. iOS 27: Yes (BETA)** | Through iOS 26 there is **no API** (Apple DTS, verbatim: *"there is no API to retrieve this"*). **iOS 27 beta** adds READ via `PHAsset.extendedMetadata` → `PHAssetExtendedMetadata` (`caption`, `keywords`, `originalFileName`), prefetchable via `PHFetchOptions.prefetchAssetExtendedMetadata`; plus `PHAsset.rating` / `PHAsset.Rating`. WRITE via `PHAssetChangeRequest.caption`, `.rating`, `.addKeyword(_:)`, `.removeKeyword(_:)`. ⚠️ **Trap:** **all of these are marked Beta in Apple's own docs. Do not ship against them before iOS 27 GA — they can change or be pulled.** |
| Filter on location | **No (predicate)** / **Yes (in memory)** | See the trap above. |
| Write location back | **Yes** | `PHAssetChangeRequest.location`. |
| Background indexing parity with Apple's overnight daemon | **No** | ⚠️ **Trap — a real structural disadvantage.** Your options are `BGProcessingTaskRequest` (`requiresExternalPower`, `requiresNetworkConnectivity`), which the system grants **opportunistically and stingily**, or foreground processing. Apple's Photos daemon gets unbounded overnight NPU time. You do not. |
| Get original bytes for your own analysis | **Yes** | `PHAssetResource` + `PHAssetResourceManager`. Thumbnails at scale: `PHImageManager` / `PHCachingImageManager`. |
| Detect library changes while your app was not running | **Yes** | `PHPhotoLibraryPersistentChangesObserver`. Incremental indexing anchor: `PHAsset.addedDate` (new and public in **iOS 26**) — this is what "Recently Added" sorts on. |
| Query the system Photos index from Spotlight APIs | **No** | You **cannot** query the system's index. |
| Push *your* photo entities into system Spotlight | **Yes** | Core Spotlight `CSSearchableItem` / `CSSearchableIndex` — your app's photos become findable system-wide, on the same surface Apple Photos occupies. ⚠️ **Trap:** iOS 27's `CoreSpotlightSource` explicitly *"retrieves data from the app's Spotlight index"* — **your** index, **not the system's**. It is not a backdoor into Apple's. |
| Be a destination for visual intelligence's app search | **Unverified** | Apple's phrasing is *"Search Google and across supported apps"*, apparently via App Intents. **Whether this is open to arbitrary third parties or is a curated partner list is not clearly documented.** Verify before planning integration. You certainly **cannot** invoke visual intelligence programmatically or read its results. |

#### Authorization tiers (the practical access model)

| Tier | API | Permission prompt? | What you get |
|---|---|---|---|
| Picker | `PHPickerViewController` / SwiftUI `PhotosPicker` | **None** | Out-of-process; user picks; you receive only the picks. Includes Apple's own search bar. |
| Full Access | `PHPhotoLibrary.requestAuthorization(for: .readWrite)` | Yes | Apple's privacy page, verbatim: *"you may choose to Allow Full Access, which **grants the third-party app access to your photos and videos, including your hidden photos even if the album is locked**"* |
| Limited Access | same, user selects a subset; expand with `PHPhotoLibrary.presentLimitedLibraryPicker` | Yes | A user-chosen subset |
| Add-only | `.addOnly` | Yes | Write only |

Settings path: `Settings` ▸ `Privacy & Security` ▸ `Photos`. Apple: *"Access to photos includes associated metadata, such as location and depth information."*

`PHPickerCapabilities` (iOS 17+) options, settable via `PHPickerConfiguration.disabledCapabilities`: `.search` (*"A capability that corresponds to the search bar"*), `.collectionNavigation` (the Albums tab), `.selectionActions`, `.stagingArea`, `.sensitivityAnalysisIntervention`.

> ⚠️ **Trap (label mismatch):** Apple's **privacy page** calls the middle tier **"Limit Access"**; the **Settings UI and the API** call it **"Limited."** Use "Limited" in code and UI copy.

> ⚠️ **Trap (trust):** Full Access is a scary prompt and grants **more than users expect** — hidden and locked photos included. An app that does meaningful work under **Limited Access**, or that indexes under an explicit, revocable, on-device-only contract, has a genuine trust advantage over apps that demand Full Access on first launch.

#### The replication toolkit — what you build your own index with

Every symbol below was verified present in Apple's framework symbol indexes. **No hallucinated API names.**

| Framework | Symbols | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Vision (iOS 18+ Swift API) | `RecognizeTextRequest` | OCR → your text index |
| | `RecognizeDocumentsRequest` (iOS 26) | Structured docs / tables |
| | `DetectBarcodesRequest` | QR codes |
| | `ClassifyImageRequest` | Scene/object taxonomy (enumerate its identifiers to build a scene index) |
| | `RecognizeAnimalsRequest` | Cats/dogs (species, **not** identity) |
| | `GenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest` | Embeddings → similarity + dedup |
| | `GenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest`, `GeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest` | Subject lift |
| | `GenerateAttentionBasedSaliencyImageRequest` | Smart crop / curation |
| | `CalculateImageAestheticsScoresRequest` | Quality — Apple's own "photo quality analysis" analogue |
| | `DetectLensSmudgeRequest`, `DetectHumanBodyPoseRequest` | Quality gating; pose/action signals |
| | `CoreMLRequest` | Bring your own model |
| | `VideoProcessor` | Frame pipelines → **per-timestamp** video index |
| VisionKit | `ImageAnalyzer` + `ImageAnalysisInteraction` (`.text`, `.machineReadableCode`, `.visualLookUp`) | Apple's actual Live Text + Visual Look Up + subject-lift UI, in your app, in a few lines |
| Foundation Models | iOS 26: on-device LLM, guided generation (`@Generable`), tool calling, Private Cloud Compute. Vision ships `BarcodeReaderTool` / `OCRTool` as Foundation-Models tools | Reasoning / chaptering / summarization over your index |
| Foundation Models (**iOS 27 BETA**) | **Image attachments**: `Attachment` / `ImageAttachmentContent` / `ImageReference` | Multimodal prompting over photos |
| Core Spotlight (**iOS 27 BETA**) | `SpotlightSearchTool` + `CoreSpotlightSource` + `SpotlightSearchTool.GuidanceProfile` (`textMatch`, **`similarityMatch`** = semantic, `numericMatch`, `dates`, `people`, `contentType`) + `ContentDomain.visualMedia` (*"Photos, videos, and other visual content"*) | **On-device semantic + keyword retrieval over YOUR OWN index, wired directly into a `LanguageModelSession`.** Confirmed by WWDC26 session 246 ("LLM search using Core Spotlight"). Also: the new index-delegate method `searchableItems(forIdentifiers:)` rehydrates the full `CSSearchableItem` so the model can see metadata the compact search index cannot return; plus custom `PipelineStage`s |

**The strategic read on that last row:** Foundation Models (with image attachments) + `SpotlightSearchTool`/`CoreSpotlightSource` with `GuidanceProfile.similarityMatch` is **the first Apple-sanctioned stack for building a private, on-device conversational photo agent** — RAG over *your* index, not Apple's. It is the single most important API finding in this domain. It is **iOS 27 beta**; you cannot ship it today, but you should architect toward it.

**And the one hole Apple never fills:** **face identity.** Vision gives detection, landmarks, and capture quality — and no recognition embedding, ever. Face recognition is simultaneously (a) the capability Apple's public SDK **structurally refuses to provide**, and (b) the backbone of Apple's own best search queries ("Maya skateboarding in a tie-dye shirt"). A third party that ships its own detector + embedder + clusterer is not adding a feature; it is crossing the moat.

---

### 3.18 Where Apple is weak — our opening

**1. Semantic search does not actually work well, and Apple has publicly admitted it.**
- Apple Support Communities reports that Apple-Intelligence queries such as *"Photos from my most recent trip to Germany"* or *"Rome monuments"* **"draw a complete blank"**, and that in practice only keyword/title matching — *"which the old search function also used"* — seems to work. *(Note: the thread could not be fetched directly (HTTP 429); the exact wording of individual user posts is second-hand, though the direction of the complaint is well-corroborated by press.)*
- iOS 26.x shipped **search regressions**: users reporting "Apple Intelligence Required" even with Apple Intelligence enabled; Photos/Spotlight search broken after 26.4 and only partially fixed in 26.5.
- Apple's own VP of OS Program Management, **Stacey Ford**, at WWDC 2026: *"We've all had that moment where you search for something you know is there, but it just won't show up."* Apple is now on its second-or-third "we fixed search" cycle; MacRumors commenters were openly skeptical.

**2. Structural exclusions Apple cannot fix without abandoning its own gating.** These are the axes to compete on, because Apple *cannot move them*:
- **Hardware.** Semantic search requires iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 16+. **Every iPhone 14 and older, iPhone 15 / 15 Plus, and every iPhone SE gets nothing.** Live Text and Visual Look Up have their own floor (iPhone XS/XR+).
- **Language.** Apple Intelligence search: **16 languages**. Visual Look Up: **6 languages** (English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Spanish). The world has 100+.
- **Geography.** Apple Intelligence is **unavailable in China mainland** (device *and* account). Enhanced Visual Search "isn't available in all countries or regions" (list unpublished). iOS 27's Siri AI has an **EU carve-out** for iOS/iPadOS/watchOS and is **blocked in China** pending regulatory clearance, and launches **English-first**.

**3. The Enhanced Visual Search trust wound.** It sends photo-derived embeddings **off-device**, and it was **turned on by default with no opt-in prompt** — discovered by developers in Dec 2024/Jan 2025 (Jeff Johnson / The Register / 9to5Mac) and never fully lived down. Many users still don't know the toggle exists. **A strictly-local competitor can make an unqualified "100% on-device, no exceptions" claim that Apple Photos structurally cannot.**

**4. The search grammar is impoverished and undocumented.** No OR, no NOT, no date ranges, no `before:`/`after:`, no saved searches, no `in:album` operator, no camera/lens/EXIF search. The **category taxonomy is closed and unpublished**, so users cannot learn the vocabulary — a query that sounds obvious ("Rome monuments") falls outside it and silently returns nothing. Album-scoped search is buried **three taps deep** and is not reachable from the main search field.

**5. Everything the user manually invests is trapped.** Named people, cluster corrections, captions, and (in iOS 27) keywords and ratings **cannot be exported**. There is **no** person↔asset mapping export. This is pure vendor lock-in — and an opening for an app whose explicit pitch is an **exportable, cross-platform, portable index**. (Counter-risk: it is also a **cold-start problem for us** — users will not re-tag 400 people. Ingest must be near-free.)

**6. The indexing experience is opaque and starves silently.** Analysis only runs while **charging + idle**, Apple gives **almost no progress UI**, and users therefore conclude that face recognition and search are "broken" when they are merely **unfed**. An honest index-progress meter plus an explicit **"index now, I'll wait"** affordance wins on *perceived* reliability at equal model quality.

**7. Coverage gaps in the retrieval primitives themselves.**
- **Trips are location-only** — any asset with stripped GPS (screenshots, AirDrops, scans, privacy-scrubbed imports) can **never** join a trip.
- **Visual Look Up findings are not searchable.** Photos will tell you it's a Golden Retriever, then refuse to let you search "Golden Retriever." Findings become a knowledge card, not a search token.
- **Event coverage is undocumented** — it silently works for some venues and not others.
- **Groups cannot express exclusion** — you cannot ask for "photos of A and B but *not* C."
- **Video key-moment search offers no timestamp list** — you cannot get a jump-list of matching moments. **Intra-video moment retrieval is a genuinely differentiating feature that almost no competitor ships.**

**8. Apple's own conversational answer is outsourced.** visual intelligence's `Ask` routes to **ChatGPT (OpenAI)** and searches the **web**, not your library. There is **no shipping Apple "Ask Photos."** Apple's own version arrives in **iOS 27** — unreleased, **English-first**, **Apple-Intelligence-hardware-only**, **EU/China gated**, and arriving after a two-year credibility hit on the "more personal Siri" promise. **A shipping, local, all-languages, all-devices conversational photo search has a wide-open window through at least late 2026.**

> ⚠️ **Trap — the honest counter-argument.** iOS 27's rebuilt index may genuinely land in fall 2026. If it does, a pure "our search is better" pitch weakens fast. Do not bet the product on Apple staying bad at search. Bet it on the axes Apple **structurally cannot move**: older devices, all languages, China/EU availability, **no server hop under any circumstances**, an **exportable index**, and **face identity** — the one capability Apple's public SDK refuses to give anyone, including itself, on any device Apple has chosen not to bless.
## 4. People & Pets

`People & Pets` is Apple Photos' face- and pet-recognition surface: an on-device pipeline that detects faces and upper bodies, embeds and clusters them into identities, and exposes those identities as a browsable collection where the user can name, merge, favorite, hide, and suppress them. It is reached at `Photos` > `Collections` > `People & Pets` on iOS 26, and it is the substrate for person-name search, Memories curation, and the Photos widget.

**The single most important thing an implementer must know:** none of it is available to third parties. PhotoKit exposes no person entity, no face rectangle, no People album, and no person filter — confirmed twice on the record by Apple engineers and independently by dumping PhotoKit's complete 1,024-symbol index (exactly two symbols match person/face/people/identity, and both are dead iPhoto-sync vestiges). Detection is free via Vision; **identity is yours to build**. That is a cost, and it is also a moat: nobody else can touch Apple's people graph either — including Apple's own users, who cannot export it.

### 4.1 The API answer: PhotoKit has no people surface

This is definitive and should anchor the entire architecture. A third-party iOS app **cannot**: read the names Apple assigned to people or pets; enumerate the People & Pets collection or its members; read the face bounding boxes Apple detected; read pet identities; or determine which `PHAsset`s contain a given person. This holds regardless of whether the user grants Full Access or Limited Access.

| Evidence | Detail |
|---|---|
| Apple Frameworks Engineer "Jordan", Developer Forums thread 126711 (Jun 2020) | "No, there is not an API to access people data in PhotoKit as of now." |
| Apple DTS Engineer, Developer Forums thread 722050 (accepted answer) | "There is no api to access the People album, please file a feature request using Feedback Assistant." |
| PhotoKit symbol index dump (1,024 symbols) | Exactly **two** symbols match person/people/face/identity: `PHAssetCollectionSubtype.albumSyncedFaces` and `PHCollectionListSubtype.smartFolderFaces`. Both are iPhoto-sync vestiges (see 4.2). No `PHPerson`, no `PHFace`, no person fetch option, no person predicate, no People smart-album subtype. |
| `PHPickerFilter` full case list | `bursts`, `cinematicVideos`, `depthEffectPhotos`, `images`, `livePhotos`, `panoramas`, `screenRecordings`, `screenshots`, `slomoVideos`, `timelapseVideos`, `videos`, `spatialMedia`, plus combinators `any(of:)` / `all(of:)` / `not(_:)` / `playbackStyle(_:)`. **No person, no people, no faces case.** |

A widely-cited community claim (forum user `bwebster`, thread 126711, June 2020) states: "Apple actually goes to specific lengths to prevent accessing face/person information using PhotoKit. Even using private APIs, access to that info is denied to third party apps."

> ⚠️ **Trap:** That quote is from a **community member, not an Apple engineer**, and it dates to June 2020. Treat it as credible hearsay about private-API blocking, **not** as stated Apple policy. Do not cite it as Apple's position. The claim that a Feedback Assistant feature request has been "open since Dec 2022" is **unverified** — the 2022 forum threads that surface are about Shared Albums, not people.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Do not write "nothing in iOS 27 changes any of this." iOS 27 (beta) adds `PHPickerConfiguration.searchText` — see 4.11. It still reads no identity, but it is a new person-adjacent surface and the flat statement will be wrong.

### 4.2 The two PhotoKit traps

Both of these look like the People album to an engineer scanning enum cases. Neither is.

| Symbol | Apple's own abstract | Reality | Availability |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PHAssetCollectionSubtype.albumSyncedFaces` | "A Faces group synced to the device from iPhoto." | A Faces album pushed onto the device by iTunes photo-sync from iPhoto/Aperture on a Mac. A long-dead workflow. Never reflected on-device Photos recognition. **Empty on any modern device.** | iOS 8.0 / iPadOS 8.0 / Mac Catalyst 13.1 / macOS 10.11 / tvOS 10.0 / visionOS 1.0 |
| `PHCollectionListSubtype.smartFolderFaces` | "The collection list is a smart folder containing one or more Faces synced from iPhoto." | Same vestige, one level up in the hierarchy. Will snare an engineer scanning **collection-list** subtypes rather than album subtypes. | iOS 8.0+ |

> ⚠️ **Trap:** These two are the *only* face/person symbols in PhotoKit's entire surface. Finding them and concluding "People is reachable" is the single most likely way to burn a sprint. Flag both in your own codebase comments.
