For completeness, the full `PHAssetCollectionSubtype` **smart-album** case list — note the absence of any People or Pets case: `AllHidden`, `Animated`, `Bursts`, `Cinematic`, `DepthEffect`, `Favorites`, `Generic`, `LivePhotos`, `LongExposures`, `Panoramas`, `RAW`, `RecentlyAdded`, `Screenshots`, `SelfPortraits`, `SlomoVideos`, `Timelapses`, `UnableToUpload`, `UserLibrary`, `Videos`, `ScreenRecordings`, `Spatial`.

### 4.3 What Vision *does* give you (detection, quality, humans, animals)

Vision is the compensating primitive. It runs on the Apple Neural Engine, on every supported iPhone, with **no Apple Intelligence requirement and no device gating**.

Vision's `Facial analysis` topic section contains **exactly three requests**, verified by dumping the framework's topic index. None of them is recognition.

| Request (Swift-native) | Returns / abstract | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `DetectFaceRectanglesRequest` | "A request that finds faces within an image." → `FaceObservation` | `boundingBox` (via `BoundingBoxProviding`), plus `roll`, `pitch`, `yaw` |
| `DetectFaceLandmarksRequest` | "…finds facial features like eyes and mouth." → `FaceObservation.Landmarks2D` | Accepts `inputFaceObservations` to chain off a prior detection |
| `DetectFaceCaptureQualityRequest` | "…produces a floating-point number that represents the capture quality of a face." | **Also** accepts `inputFaceObservations`. `captureQuality` is a property on `FaceObservation` itself |

`FaceObservation` exposes `landmarks` (`Landmarks2D`), `pitch`, `roll`, `yaw`, `captureQuality`, `boundingBox`. Coordinates are normalized (`NormalizedRect` / `NormalizedPoint`, with an explicit `CoordinateOrigin`). Requests are **revisioned** (`supportedRevisions`) — pin the revision so accuracy benchmarks stay reproducible across OS updates.

Legacy Objective-C/Swift equivalents (`VNDetectFaceRectanglesRequest`, `VNDetectFaceLandmarksRequest`, `VNDetectFaceCaptureQualityRequest`, `VNFaceObservation`) go back to iOS 11. The Swift-native API is **iOS 18.0+ / iPadOS 18.0+ / macOS 15.0+ / tvOS 18.0+ / visionOS 2.0+**.

**Person / human requests** (the same primitives Apple uses internally):

| Request | Abstract / output | Availability |
|---|---|---|
| `DetectHumanRectanglesRequest` | "…finds rectangular regions that contain people." Has an `upperBodyOnly` toggle → `HumanObservation` (exposes `isUpperBodyOnly`) | iOS 18.0+ (Swift) |
| `GeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest` | "…produces a mask of individual people it finds in the input image." → `InstanceMaskObservation` | iOS 18.0+ (Swift) |
| `GeneratePersonSegmentationRequest` | Person matte | iOS 18.0+ (Swift) |
| `DetectHumanBodyPoseRequest` | Body pose | iOS 18.0+ (Swift) |
| `DetectHumanBodyPose3DRequest` | 3D body pose | **iOS 18.0+ for the Swift-native request.** The *legacy* `VNDetectHumanBodyPose3DRequest` is iOS 17.0+ / macOS 14.0+ |
| `DetectHumanHandPoseRequest` | Hand pose | iOS 18.0+ (Swift) |

> ⚠️ **Trap:** `DetectHumanBodyPose3DRequest` (Swift) is **iOS 18.0+, not iOS 17+**. Setting a deployment target of iOS 17 and expecting the Swift API will not compile. Only the `VN`-prefixed legacy class is iOS 17.

> The claim that Apple replaced the hand-pose model in iOS 26 with a smaller/faster one (still 21 joints) is **unverified** — it could not be sourced from Apple docs or a WWDC page. Do not repeat it as fact.

The strategic point about `upperBodyOnly`: Apple's own ML paper (4.4) says Photos clusters using **both** face and upper-body embeddings, using clothing as a same-day cue. Apple ships you the identical upper-body detection primitive it uses internally, so you can replicate torso-assisted association for occluded or back-turned subjects.

**Animals:**

| Symbol | Fact |
|---|---|
| `RecognizeAnimalsRequest.Animal` | Exactly **two** cases: `.cat` and `.dog`. Nothing else. (iOS 18.0+; `VNRecognizeAnimalsRequest` earlier) |
| `RecognizeAnimalsRequest` | "Configuring a request" → `supportedAnimals`, `Animal`. "Understanding the result" → `RecognizedObjectObservation` (bounding box + labels + confidence) |
| `DetectAnimalBodyPoseRequest` | Present in Vision's "Pose analysis" section |

Vision **recognizes a cat/dog as an object class** — it does not tell you *which* cat. Individual pet identity is no more available to third parties than human identity is. The exact `.cat`/`.dog` correspondence with Apple Photos' own pet support is strong circumstantial evidence that Photos' pet feature is this same model, though Apple never states that.

**The embedding nuance that matters most:**

> ⚠️ **Trap (the inverse kind — a capability people wrongly say is absent):** It is true that Vision ships **no face embedding, no faceprint, and no recognition request at any privilege level**. It is **false** that Apple ships zero embedding capability. Vision has `GenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest` → `FeaturePrintObservation`: a general-purpose on-device image embedding with a built-in **distance function** and a `cropAndScaleAction`. Run against a face rectangle from `DetectFaceRectanglesRequest`, it is the closest Apple-supplied embedding primitive available to a third party. It is not a face-tuned embedder and you will almost certainly beat it with your own — but do not tell an implementer "Apple gives you nothing." Also useful for quality gating: `CalculateImageAestheticsScoresRequest` and `DetectLensSmudgeRequest`.

`DetectFaceCaptureQualityRequest` is quietly the most valuable request for a competitor: it is exactly the signal needed for key-face selection and for weighting which crops feed your embedder.

### 4.4 Apple's actual recognition pipeline (from Apple's own ML paper)

Apple published the architecture ("Recognizing People in Photos Through Private On-Device Machine Learning", Apple ML Research). It is unusually candid and is a free benchmark spec. Every element below is verbatim-confirmed against the paper.

**Detection.** A single deep neural network "takes a full image as input, and outputs bounding boxes for the detected faces and upper bodies." Upper body is used because faces are frequently occluded or turned away, and because clothing gives "constant characteristics — like clothing — within a specific context."

**Embedding.** Separate networks extract a face embedding and a torso/upper-body embedding. The face embedding is trained with an **additive-margin cosine objective on the unit hypersphere** (margin-mining softmax: angular margin + hard-example weighting), with synthetic mask augmentation for masked faces. Face-embedding generation is **<4 ms end-to-end on the Apple Neural Engine, ~8× faster than the equivalent GPU model**. Fairness: trained on paid crowd-sourced, globally representative data across age/gender/ethnicity.

**Confidence / OOD gating.** A fine-tuned **embedding-confidence branch**, trained on random / non-face / out-of-domain crops, filters false-positive and unrepresentable detections out of the gallery.

**Clustering — two passes.** This is the part most summaries omit, and it is precisely where the vulnerability lives:

1. **Pass 1 (conservative, high-precision, greedy).** Produces many small clusters; each cluster is a running average of its member embeddings. Merges from this pass are effectively permanent. The distance function switches between face-only, a face + upper-body linear combination, and upper-body-only depending on what is available: `D_ij = min(F_ij, α·F_ij + β·T_ij)`, where `F` is face distance and `T` is torso distance. **Upper-body embeddings are only ever compared within the same "moment"** — a metadata grouping by time and location — because clothing is a same-day signal.
2. **Pass 2 (recall growth).** Hierarchical agglomerative clustering (HAC) using **face embeddings only**, with median inter-member distance linkage and random sampling, to grow clusters *across* moment boundaries and "increase recall significantly."

**Identity assignment** to a named cluster is **not** nearest-neighbor. Apple uses sparse coding: minimize `||y − D·x||²₂ + λ||x||₁` and assign to the cluster with maximum total sparse-code "energy."

**Scheduling.** Clustering "runs periodically, typically overnight during device charging." Everything runs locally on the user's device.

**What the paper does not contain** — and this is the whole wedge: no age-invariant loss, no age-conditioned matching, no cross-age linking pass, no explicit calibration or threshold-tuning story, no continuous on-device adaptation, and no user-correction feedback loop. The clothing/torso cue is architecturally **within-event**: it helps at a party and does nothing across five years.

### 4.5 The collection: navigation, labels, and structure

The album is titled **`People & Pets`** — but is labeled just **`People`** if no dogs or cats have been identified yet. Apple, verbatim: "The Photos app sorts photos and videos of people, dogs, and cats in the People & Pets collection (or the People collection if no pets appear)."

Navigation (Apple's exact wording): "Open Photos, then tap `Collections`. Swipe up, then tap `People & Pets`." Each person/pet is represented by a **key photo** (Apple's own term; also referred to as a "face thumbnail").

> The specific list of sibling collections (`Recent Days`, `Pinned`, `Memories`, `Trips`, `Albums`, `Featured Photos`) is **unverified** — Apple's own Collections page says only "curated collections such as Memories, Favorites, People & Pets, and more." More importantly: the Collections tab is **user-reorderable and collapsible** (tap the `...` at the top of Collections → `Reorder` / `Collapse All`; collections can also be resized or individually hidden). People & Pets' prominence is user-controlled, not fixed — relevant if you reason about discoverability.

Named people and pets are also findable from the **Search** tab by typing their name (see 4.9).

### 4.6 The full iOS correction and curation surface

This is every lever iOS 26 gives a user over the people graph. It is roughly **twelve** levers — do not repeat the common claim that iOS gives "exactly three." The precise, defensible criticism is not that the levers are few; it is that **none of them surfaces or steers confidence**.

| Action | Exact iOS 26 path and labels |
|---|---|
| **Name a person/pet (primary entry point)** | Open a photo/video, swipe up for details (or tap the `Info` button). People/pets appear as circles in the **bottom-left**. "A question mark appears next to those you haven't named." Tap the one with the question mark → `Edit Name and Photos` → `Name This Person` or `Name This Pet` → enter name → `Done`. If the person is already recognized elsewhere, tap `Merge Photos` instead. |
| **Contacts-suggested names** | "If the person is listed in your contacts, you can tap their name below `Results`." Apple: "Photos suggests names from your Contacts." The section label is literally `Results`. This is how most names actually get entered. |
| **Reach faces not in the collection** | "If the person or pet you want to name doesn't appear, tap `Add People` at the bottom of the People & Pets collection to see more faces." |
| **Merge duplicate people/pets** | (A) `People & Pets` → `Edit` → select the people to merge → `More` button → `Merge` → `Merge Photos` to confirm. (B) Inline while naming: tap `Merge Photos`. Apple acknowledges the need: "Sometimes the same person is identified in more than one group within People & Pets." |
| **Remove a misidentified photo** | "In the People & Pets collection, tap the person or pet. Tap `Select`, then tap each photo that isn't of the person or pet. Tap the `More` button, then tap `This is Not [This Person]`." Inline variant: swipe up on a photo → tap the person's circle bottom-left → `This is Not [name]` → `Rename This Person` / `Rename This Pet`. |
| **Fix an incorrect name** | `Collections` → `People & Pets` → tap the misidentified person/pet → tap the button at the top of the screen → "Tap the incorrect name at the top of the menu, tap the name again, enter the correct name" → `Done`. (User Guide section title: `Fix incorrect names`.) |
| **Favorite / Unfavorite** | Touch and hold the key photo → `Favorite`; reverse with `Unfavorite`. Bulk: `Edit` → tap each person → `Favorite` button at the bottom. Apple: "Mark the People that you access the most as a Favorite so that it's easier to find them." Favorites sort ahead of non-favorites (corroborated by `osxphotos`, which documents `PersonInfo.sort_order` as "favorite persons are sorted before non-favorite persons"). |
| **Sort the collection** | `People & Pets` → `Sort` → `Sort by Name` (alphabetical) or `Sort by Custom Order` (then touch and hold a key photo and drag it to a new position). |
| **Change the key photo** | (A) Touch and hold the key photo → `Edit Name and Photos` → tap the photo icon in the bottom-right of the current key photo → select from the grid. (B) Open the person → `Sort and Filter` button → `View Options` → `Faces` → touch and hold the photo → `Make Key Photo`. |
| **Hide a person/pet** | `People & Pets` → touch and hold the person/pet's key photo → `Hide [name]`. (Distinct from the Hidden **album** under `Albums` > `Utilities` > `Hidden`, which hides *assets*, not people.) |
| **Suppress from Memories/Featured/widget** | See 4.7. |
| **Groups** | See 4.8. |

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Popular write-ups (and the researcher who first compiled this) describe hidden people collecting in a **collapsible section at the bottom of the album with a `Show less` control**, and an **`Unhide`** label. **None of that is verifiable.** Apple's iOS docs document `Hide [name]` and do not describe unhiding at all. Do not ship `Show less` or `Unhide` as real iOS labels. (macOS *is* documented: Control-click → `Hide this Person` → confirm with `Hide from People & Pets Album`.)

### 4.7 `Don't Feature` — Memories / Featured / widget suppression

This is the feature people mean when they say "stop showing me my ex." Two entry points, both verbatim-confirmed:

- **(A) From the collection:** touch and hold a thumbnail → `Don't Feature [Name]` → choose `Feature This Person Less` or `Never Feature This Person` → tap `Confirm`.
- **(B) From a photo:** tap the `More` button → `Don't Feature a Person` → (if multiple people) tap the person, tap `Next` → same two options → `Confirm`.

Apple states the scope precisely: "This adjusts the way the Photos app curates your Memories, Featured photos, and the photos that you see in the Photos widget — so you see less photos of these people or pets."

**The undo has two different labels in two different Apple documents, and both are real:**

| Reset path | Source | Scope (apparent) |
|---|---|---|
| `Collections` → tap your account (top-right) → `Reset People & Pets Suggestions` | iOS 26 iPhone User Guide | Global |
| Touch and hold a thumbnail → `Reset [Name] Feature Settings` → tap it again to confirm | Apple Support article 108795 (published Jan 16, 2026) | Per-person |

Related global toggles live in the same account sheet: `Show Featured Content` ("Turn off Show Featured Content to prevent Photos from automatically generating featured photos and memories") and `Show Holiday Events`.

> ⚠️ **Trap (behavioral, and exploitable):** Apple's own warning — "If you choose to feature someone less, you have to reset their Memories settings in order to see that person again in People & Pets." **Feature-less has a side effect on the album itself, not just on Memories.** A user who suppresses someone from their widget can lose them from People & Pets and will not connect the two actions.

The control is bluntly binary — "less" vs "never" — with no per-context granularity (e.g. "never in widgets but fine in search").

### 4.8 Groups

A genuinely good Apple feature that is easy to overlook. Apple: "The Photos app recognizes groups of people and pets who often appear together in pictures and videos, and sorts them into group collections." Found at `Collections` → `People & Pets` → `Groups`. Groups are both **auto-generated by co-occurrence mining** and **manually creatable** from any combination of people and pets.

| Operation | Exact labels |
|---|---|
| Create | "To the right of `Groups`, tap `+`, then tap `Create New Group`" → select people/pets → name it → `Create` |
| Edit | Touch and hold → `Edit Name and People` → rename; remove a member via the `x` "at the top-left corner of their picture"; `Add People & Pets`; change the group photo via "the photo icon in the bottom-right corner" |
| Delete | Touch and hold → `Delete Group` |
| Reorder | "Tap `Groups`. Touch and hold a group, then drag it to a new position." |
| See the group *with others present* | `...` → `View Options` → `Other People` |
| Share | `...` → `Share` |

Groups is Apple's de-facto answer to hierarchy in the People album. It is weaker than folders, but it is not nothing, and any competitive comparison that says "Apple has no grouping" will be corrected.

### 4.9 Search over people and pets

**Person-name search does NOT require Apple Intelligence.** Apple's baseline "Search for photos and videos on iPhone" page lists **"A person identified in the People & Pets collection"** as a plain supported query type, alongside Date, Place, Business names, Category, Events, Text, and Caption.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Do not build a competitive claim on "Apple gates person search behind Apple Intelligence." It is false and you will be publicly corrected. What Apple Intelligence adds is **compositional natural-language queries** — e.g. "Maya skateboarding in a tie-dye shirt", "Sadie cartwheeling on the grass" (both verbatim from Apple's iOS 26 guide) — not person search itself. ("Dad smiling" / "Snowy sleeping" circulate widely but come from Apple's Oct 2024 newsroom / press coverage, not the iOS 26 guide.)

Apple Intelligence search results support `See All`, `Select`, `Sort by Recently Added` / `Sort by Date Captured`, and `Filter` ("tap `Filter`, then tap an option—like `Favorites` or `Edited`"). Memory movies can be generated from a typed description: `Collections` → `Memories` → `Create`. Apple's guide explicitly cross-links naming: "For more information on naming people and pets in photos, see Find and name people and pets in Photos."

**Apple Intelligence gating** (this part *is* a real limitation): not available on all iPhone models, languages, or regions. Beta language list (16 entries as published): English, Danish, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese.

**A separate people-keyed search axis Apple ships and most people miss:** search by **iCloud Shared Photo Library participant** — type `Shared by`, then tap a suggested name. It is entirely independent of People & Pets recognition.

### 4.10 Pets, indexing, iCloud sync, and privacy

**Pets: dogs and cats only, iOS 17+.** Apple, verbatim: "in iOS 17, iPadOS 17, and later, the Photos app can recognize dogs and cats, too." Pets get the full people affordance set — `Name This Pet`, key photos, Favorite, Hide, `Don't Feature`, Merge, and inclusion in Groups. No other species appears anywhere in Apple's docs. Birds, horses, rabbits, reptiles, and livestock are simply invisible to Apple Photos.

**Indexing requirements — an under-appreciated UX constraint you can beat outright.** Apple, from support article 105081 ("If you can't find pets in the People & Pets album in Photos"): *"Your iPhone or iPad must be locked and connected to power during the detection process. Photos on your Mac can detect these photos as long as you aren't using the app. Depending on what tasks are running in the background and the size of your photo library, this process could happen quickly or take up to a few days to complete."* While it runs, a **`Finding People...`** message appears in the album, and the album stays labeled `People` until pet detection completes.

> ⚠️ **Trap (scope):** Apple states the locked + on-power requirement **only in the context of pet detection**. Generalizing it to "all of Photos' background analysis" is an *inference*, not something Apple wrote. It is a plausible inference — Apple's ML paper independently says clustering "runs periodically, typically overnight during device charging" — but cite the **paper**, not Apple Support, for the general claim.

**iCloud sync.** Confirmed in three Apple primary sources:
- Support 108795: "when you have iCloud Photos turned on, the people you favorite or name stay up to date across your Apple devices."
- iOS 26 User Guide: "When you use iCloud Photos, People & Pets is kept up to date on all your devices."
- Photos & Privacy legal page (updated 2025-12-12): "When you add a name to a person in the People & Pets Album, their name and face will appear in Photos across all your iCloud-enabled devices."

Requires iCloud Photos ON. Apple does not publish the sync payload format, and says **nothing** about whether the *embeddings/faceprints* sync or are re-derived per device — treat that as unknown.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The widely-repeated claim that face signatures sync through a Keychain-like end-to-end-encrypted channel Apple cannot read traces to a **Macworld article, not an Apple primary source**. Do not repeat it as an Apple guarantee. What Apple actually documents: Photos in iCloud is E2EE **only** under Advanced Data Protection (iOS 16.2+); under standard data protection it is encrypted in transit and at rest, but **Apple holds the keys**.

**Privacy posture — and the framing mistake to avoid.** Apple's legal page: "Photos uses on-device machine learning… This on-device analysis includes scene classification, people and pets identification, photo quality analysis, and audio classification." And: "Apple does not access your photos or videos, and does not use them for research and development." Photos additionally fuses on-device signals: "which photos you have edited or shared to other people, people you frequently communicate with in Messages, relationships set in Contacts, Home and Work locations set in Contacts or Maps, **locations where you take photos**, and important dates in Calendar and Contacts."

> ⚠️ **Trap:** **"Apple Photos is fully on-device" is false**, and marketing against it will get you publicly corrected. The same legal page documents **Enhanced Visual Search**: "Your device privately matches places in your photos to a global index Apple maintains on our servers. We apply homomorphic encryption and differential privacy, and use an OHTTP relay that hides IP address." It is **on by default**, toggled at `Settings` > `Apps` > `Photos` (Mac: `Photos` > `Settings` > `General`). It covers **landmarks/POIs, not people** — so people/pets identification genuinely *is* on-device. **Scope every privacy claim to people/pets identification specifically.**

### 4.11 iOS 27 (beta, ships fall 2026) — read the signal

⚠️ **Nothing in this subsection is shippable today.** iOS 27 was announced at WWDC 2026 (keynote 2026-06-08), is in developer beta, and ships fall 2026. Labels and behavior can still change. Current shipping OS is **iOS 26.5.2** (iOS 26.6 in beta).

Verbatim from Apple's own iOS 27 keynote feature list:
- "Search returns more pleasing photos of people and pets in Photos" (Top Results)
- "Choose a specific pet in Photo Shuffle"
- "Option to include photos of yourself in Photo Shuffle"

> ⚠️ **Trap:** "iOS 27 improves people and pets **recognition**" is an **over-read** of the press coverage. What Apple actually says is about **search-result selection** — "better pictures of people and pets in your results." That is ranking/thumbnail quality, **not recognition or clustering accuracy**. Nothing in the iOS 27 beta materials claims an improved recognition engine.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Photo Shuffle is not a new people surface. Lock Screen Photo Shuffle has had a `People` category for years: `Settings` > `Wallpaper` > `Add New Wallpaper` > `Photo Shuffle` → choose categories (`People` / `Nature` / `Cities`) or an album, with shuffle frequency `On Tap` / `On Lock` / `Hourly` / `Daily`, plus `Select Photos Manually`. iOS 27 only **adds** individual pet selection and self-inclusion.

**The one iOS 27 change that actually touches this product area:** `PHPickerConfiguration.searchText` (type `PHPickerSearchText`; iOS / iPadOS / Mac Catalyst / macOS / visionOS **27.0**). It **pre-seeds the system Photos picker's search field with arbitrary app-supplied text**. Since Apple's baseline Photos search accepts "a person identified in the People & Pets collection" as a query, an iOS 27 app can present the system picker **already scoped to a named person's photos — with no entitlement, no private API, and no Apple Intelligence**. The app still cannot *read* the name or *enumerate* the assets (the user must tap), but the blanket statement "a third-party app has no way to surface a specific person's photos" stops being true in iOS 27. Related new symbols: `PHPickerCapabilities.search`, `PHPickerConfiguration.update.searchText`.

Adjacent iOS 27 Photos changes worth tracking competitively (all beta): `Add keywords to photos and videos in Photos`; **1–5 star ratings**; search by additional metadata; `Captured by Me` collection; `Identity Documents` collection; a `Selection view` / `Show Selected` bulk-metadata editing surface; generative editing (`Clean Up` with Fast / High Quality / Auto, `Extend`, `Reframe`); a slideshow maker; save a video frame as a photo; "new photos load in your Photos library up to **70% faster**" (Apple's own scoping of the figure) and faster Collections-tab rendering.

**Read the signal:** Apple is not fixing the correction loop, not adding manual face boxes, not restoring the bulk confirm flow, and not addressing cross-age. It is polishing ranking and wallpaper selection. **Every gap in 4.13 survives into iOS 27.** Separately, keywords + star ratings are the first user-writable metadata surface Photos has shipped in years — Apple conceding that users want manual metadata control, which is the same instinct that says they want manual control over people.

### 4.12 macOS divergence (matters for a migration/parity story)

macOS Photos has capabilities iOS does not, and different vocabulary for the ones it shares. If you build a desktop helper or a parity table, use the right label per platform.

| Capability | macOS | iOS 26 |
|---|---|---|
| **Draw a face box manually** | **Yes.** "Click `Info` in the toolbar. Click `+`, drag the circle to position it over the person or pet if necessary, click the `Name` field and type a name, then press Return." And: "You can click `+` multiple times to name multiple people or pets in a photo or video." | **No. No equivalent affordance exists anywhere.** Confirmed by full-text read of the iOS 26 User Guide. |
| **Bulk candidate review ("Is this X?")** | **Yes**, and the current label is **`Review More Photos`**: `Collections` (sidebar) → `People & Pets` → double-click a person → `More` button → `Review More Photos` → click `Yes` or `No` per suggestion → `Done`. | **Removed.** Absent from the entire iOS 26 User Guide and from support article 108795. |
| Undo a manual box / remove a face | Control-click the circle over the person or pet → `This is Not [name]` | n/a |
| Show inline name labels | `View` > `Show Face Names` / `View` > `Hide Face Names` | Not available |
| Merge | Select the people/pets → Control-click → **`Merge [number] People`** | `Merge` → `Merge Photos` |
| Hide | Control-click → `Hide this Person` → `Hide from People & Pets Album` | `Hide [name]` |
| Rename | Control-click → `Rename` | Tap the button at the top → edit the name |
| Make key photo | Control-click a photo → `Make Key Photo` | Touch and hold → `Make Key Photo` |
| Name a person | `Name this Person` (lowercase "this") | `Name This Person` |
| Detection scheduling | Runs "as long as you aren't using the app" | Requires device **locked and connected to power** |

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The commonly-repeated macOS detail "resize the circle via the white handle" is **not** in Apple's current macOS guide. Apple documents **positioning** (drag), not resizing. Mark as unverified.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The old iOS bulk-review flow is widely called `Confirm Additional Photos`, and is said to live "below Places" on a person's page. **That navigation is stale.** The live macOS label is `Review More Photos`, reached from the `More` button. The claim that the iOS "Is This [X]?" Yes/No popup disappeared at iOS 17 / 17.0.2 is **user-reported (Apple Community), not Apple-documented** — the *absence* in iOS 26 is confirmed; the *removal date* is secondary-sourced.

### 4.13 The one real interop path: the macOS Photos SQLite DB

On **macOS only**, the Photos library database exposes `ZPERSON` and `ZDETECTEDFACE`. The open-source **`osxphotos`** library reads them — every detail below was verified against `osxphotos` source, including the ones that sound too good to be true.

| `osxphotos` object | Fields |
|---|---|
| `PersonInfo` | `name`, `display_name`, `uuid`, `keyphoto`, `facecount`, `photos`, `face_info` (sorted by quality score), `favorite` (Photos 5+), `sort_order` (Photos 5+; "favorite persons are sorted before non-favorite persons"), **`feature_less`** — "Returns True if person has been marked as 'Feature This Person Less' in Photos… Photos 8+ only" (implemented as `SELECT ZTYPE FROM ZUSERFEEDBACK WHERE ZPERSON = ?`) |
| `FaceInfo` | `uuid`, `name`, `asset_uuid`, `person_info`, `photo`, `center`, `size_pixels`, `face_rect()`, `roll_pitch_yaw()` (radians), `roll`, `pitch`, `yaw`, `quality`, **`mwg_rs_area`** (Metadata Working Group Region Area), **`mpri_reg_rect`** (Microsoft Photo Region Rectangle) |

Even Apple's **feature-suppression flag** is readable on macOS. Face regions can be emitted in two standard, portable formats (MWG-RS and Microsoft Photo Region). Forensics researchers have documented that `ZDETECTEDFACE` also carries columns for eye/mouth positions and attribute estimates (age, hair color, baldness, facial hair, glasses); there is also a `ZFACECROP` table.

Caveats: the schema is **private and undocumented**; `osxphotos` itself gates on `photos_version` because schema changes across Photos releases have broken tools before; the tables are **empty until the OS finishes its background analysis pass**; and this is **impossible on iOS** — the DB is sandboxed and unreachable.

**Strategically, this is a one-time desktop-assisted import path, not an API.** The user runs a Mac helper once, you ingest their names + MWG-RS face rectangles, and their Apple people graph lands in your app pre-populated. That converts Apple's biggest lock-in into your onboarding funnel — and no iOS-only competitor can offer it.

### 4.14 Face regions in image metadata — a hypothesis worth an hour, not a roadmap item

This circulates as fact, and if true it means Apple's own face boxes ride along **inside file metadata a third-party app can read**, without PhotoKit.

**What is now corroborated by two independent sources:**
1. Apple Developer Forums thread 126711 (user `protosphere`, Jun 2020, verbatim): "Apple seems to be saving the face tag as EXIF, under prefix IIO. Where you can find x,y w, h, type, confidence level and face id which is a number. However the name of the person isn't stored. I assume, face id gets matched for a name in Photos app db."
2. An independent EXIF analysis (Harley Turan) documents that iOS writes into image metadata "the faces detected within an image (including the x & y position, the width & height, and the yaw & roll angles for each face)", and "it includes the `FaceID` property for each detected face, which seems to be a sequential integer relating to the face's ID within the 'People' tab." The underlying fields are **MWG Regions with Apple extensions**: `RegionExtensionsAngleInfoRoll`, `RegionExtensionsAngleInfoYaw`, `RegionExtensionsFaceID` — i.e. the standard, portable, third-party-readable XMP `mwg-rs` schema, the same schema `osxphotos` emits.
3. Apple's privacy page supports the reachability premise: for the Photo Picker, "Access to photos includes associated metadata."

**What is still genuinely unverified, and what you must test before betting on it:** whether these face regions are present in the **asset bytes a third-party app actually receives** via `PHPicker` / `PHAssetResource` on a **current** iOS build, for assets that were (a) captured on-device, (b) synced from iCloud, and (c) imported.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Do not put this on the roadmap until someone runs `exiftool` on a picker-delivered file from an iOS 26 device (and dumps the full `CGImageProperties` dictionary from `requestImageDataAndOrientation` across HEIC/JPEG, iPhone-captured vs imported). **Even in the best case it yields boxes and an opaque numeric ID — never Apple's person names** — so it does not change the strategic conclusion that you must own the identity layer.

### 4.15 Existence proof: Ente Photos ships a full competing stack on iOS today

Ente (open-source, E2EE) does precisely what you need to do, in the App Store, on iOS, right now. Their published pipeline, verbatim-confirmed from their own ML page:

| Stage | What Ente uses |
|---|---|
| Detection | **YOLO5Face** — "the leading architecture for object detection repurposed for faces. We're using the small [variant]" |
| Filtering | Non-Max Suppression |
| Alignment | Custom similarity-transform geometric alignment |
| Embedding | **MobileFaceNet** — "results in a unique embedding for each face" |
| Quality metrics | "We also record certain metrics on each face, such as the blurriness of the face and the positioning." |
| Clustering | Custom **"linear incremental clustering"** — "Linear clustering refers to the fact that clustering happens in a chronological order, while incremental implies that new clustering rounds on new information yield the same result as one clustering round on all data together." |
| Sync | "Each client pulls any existing indexes from Ente's server before indexing locally." Indexes are stored locally, then encrypted and stored server-side. **Cluster corrections sync, so a user only makes them once.** |
| Practical hint | Ente recommends **initial indexing on desktop**, then letting results sync to mobile: "After that, the mobile app should be enough to keep up with any new photos taken." They also document device-load safeguards for older hardware. |

This confirms the viable shape end to end: `PHAsset` image data → your detector → your aligner → your embedder → your clusterer → your synced, correctable people graph. **The App Store permits it and the platform supports it.** Their "correct once, syncs everywhere" property is exactly what Apple fails at.

### 4.16 What a third-party app can and cannot do

| Capability | Available to 3rd parties? | Mechanism / why not |
|---|---|---|
| Read Apple's person/pet **names** | **NO** | No symbol exists in PhotoKit. Apple engineers on the record; 1,024-symbol index dump confirms. |
| Enumerate the **People & Pets** collection | **NO** | No `PHAssetCollectionSubtype` case. Apple DTS: "There is no api to access the People album." |
| Read Apple's **face bounding boxes** via PhotoKit | **NO** | No face-region type in PhotoKit. |
| Read Apple's **pet identities** | **NO** | Same. |
| Know which `PHAsset`s contain a given person | **NO** | No person fetch option, no person predicate. |
| Filter the system **picker** by person | **NO** (today) | `PHPickerFilter` has no person/people/faces case. |
| **Pre-seed the system picker's search field** with a person's name | **iOS 27 beta only** | `PHPickerConfiguration.searchText` / `PHPickerSearchText` (iOS 27.0). Baseline Photos search accepts "a person identified in the People & Pets collection", so the picker can open scoped to a named person — **no entitlement, no Apple Intelligence**. Returns no identity data; the user must tap. **Not shippable until fall 2026.** |
| Filter **Shortcuts** `Find Photos` by person | **No documented route** | Apple's "Add filter parameters" page documents only Album, Width, etc.; every "person" hit on it is "personal automation." ⚠️ Apple gives *examples*, not an exhaustive enumeration — this is a documented-absence argument, not a proven negative. Do not architect around a Shortcuts bridge. |
| Face **detection** (bounding box, roll/pitch/yaw) | **YES** | Vision `DetectFaceRectanglesRequest` → `FaceObservation`. Free, ANE-accelerated, no gating. |
| Face **landmarks** | **YES** | Vision `DetectFaceLandmarksRequest` → `FaceObservation.Landmarks2D`; chains via `inputFaceObservations`. |
| Per-face **capture-quality score** | **YES** | Vision `DetectFaceCaptureQualityRequest`; `captureQuality` on `FaceObservation`. Ideal for key-face selection and crop weighting. |
| **Upper-body / person** detection | **YES** | `DetectHumanRectanglesRequest` with `upperBodyOnly` → `HumanObservation`. Same primitive Apple uses internally. |
| Person **instance masks / segmentation** | **YES** | `GeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest`, `GeneratePersonSegmentationRequest`. |
| Body / hand / 3D pose | **YES** | `DetectHumanBodyPoseRequest`, `DetectHumanHandPoseRequest`, `DetectHumanBodyPose3DRequest` (Swift: **iOS 18+**; legacy `VN…`: iOS 17+). |
| **Cat/dog** detection | **YES** | Vision `RecognizeAnimalsRequest`; `Animal` enum = `.cat`, `.dog` only. |
| **Individual pet identity** ("which cat") | **NO from Apple** | Not exposed at any tier. Build it yourself. |
| **Face embedding / faceprint / recognition** | **NO face-specific API** | Vision's `Facial analysis` section contains exactly 3 requests, none of them recognition. **But** `GenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest` → `FeaturePrintObservation` is a general on-device image embedding with a distance function; run over a face crop it is the nearest Apple-supplied embedding primitive. Not face-tuned. |
| Image aesthetics / smudge quality gating | **YES** | `CalculateImageAestheticsScoresRequest`, `DetectLensSmudgeRequest`. |
| Build a **full competing recognition stack** on iOS | **YES — shipping precedent** | Ente Photos: YOLO5Face → similarity-transform alignment → MobileFaceNet → linear incremental clustering, all on-device, E2EE index sync, in the App Store. |
| **Draw a face box manually** in your own app | **YES** | You control your own detection layer. Apple's iPhone users actively ask for this and cannot get it. |
| Read Apple's person names + face rects **on macOS** | **YES, unsupported** | Photos SQLite DB (`ZPERSON`, `ZDETECTEDFACE`) via `osxphotos`; emits MWG-RS and Microsoft Photo Region rectangles. Private schema, breaks across versions, **impossible on iOS**. Viable as a one-time desktop-assisted import. |
| Read face rects from **image metadata** (MWG Regions + Apple extensions) | **UNVERIFIED — test, don't plan** | Two independent sources describe `RegionExtensionsFaceID` / `…AngleInfoRoll` / `…AngleInfoYaw` in XMP `mwg-rs`. Unverified whether they survive into picker-delivered bytes on current iOS. Yields boxes + an opaque ID, **never names**. |
| Run indexing in the background with honest progress | **YES** | `BGProcessingTask` + Vision + your own embedder. Apple shows only an opaque `Finding People...` with no counts, no ETA, and a multi-day tail. |

### 4.17 Where Apple is weak — our opening

**Sourcing discipline first:** the most emotionally quotable complaints about Apple's people recognition ("losing entire grandchildren…", "barely usable at ~1,000 named people") are **unattributable** — a fact-checker could not source them to any indexed origin. **Do not put those quotes or that number in a deck, a pitch, or a marketing page.** The wedge below stands entirely on Apple's own documentation and Apple's own published architecture, which is stronger anyway.

- **iOS has no bulk correction loop, and macOS does.** The candidate-review flow (`Review More Photos` on Mac: Yes/No per suggestion, `Done` to stop) has no iOS equivalent — confirmed by full-text read of the iOS 26 User Guide and support article 108795. iPhone users have **no proactive, high-throughput way to supply labeled hard positives/negatives**, which is exactly the signal that would most improve a clustering system. A fast, swipe-based, batched confirm/deny queue is a feature iPhone users *used to have* and lost.

- **You cannot assert "there is a face HERE" on iPhone. At all.** iOS naming is strictly a *selection* over Apple's own detections — the question-mark circles and the `Add People` sheet. If Apple's detector missed a face (profile, occlusion, small in frame, motion blur, odd lighting), that face appears **nowhere** and the user has literally no recourse. macOS has the affordance (`Info` → `+` → drag a circle → type a name → Return); iOS has none. Confirmed by exhaustive absence in Apple's own iOS docs.

- **Nothing surfaces confidence.** iOS ships ~12 curation levers (name, merge, `This is Not [This Person]`, rename, `Add People`, favorite, hide, `Don't Feature`, reset, key photo, sort, groups) and **not one of them** lets a user see *why* two clusters joined, see *how confident* a match is, un-merge a bad merge, retrain, or adjust a threshold. Confirmed by exhaustive reading of Apple's iOS 26 People/Pets guide and article 108795: **there is no un-merge, no confidence display, no threshold control, and no explanation of a merge decision anywhere on iOS.** A visible, tunable, reversible decision layer is a product Apple has structurally chosen not to build.

- **Cross-age failure is architectural, and Apple never claims otherwise.** Build this argument on Apple's own paper, not on user quotes: the first clustering pass is deliberately conservative/high-precision and its merges are permanent; cluster centroids are running averages of embeddings; the upper-body/clothing cue is **only compared within a single "moment" (time+location)**; the second pass is face-embeddings-only HAC with median-distance linkage. There is **no age-invariant loss, no age-conditioned matching, no cross-age linking pass, and no continuous adaptation** anywhere in the published architecture, and Apple never claims cross-age robustness. Note honestly that Apple Community reports show **sibling/lookalike conflation is at least as dominant a failure as cross-age fragmentation** — so ship a benchmark that measures both.

- **Bad merges are unrecoverable and self-reinforcing.** There is no documented un-merge on iOS. Once two people's faces are pooled, the cluster centroid is poisoned and future matching compounds the error. Non-destructive, undoable merges with a visible provenance trail is a cheap, high-trust win.

- **Feature-less has a hidden album side effect.** Apple's own warning: "If you choose to feature someone less, you have to reset their Memories settings in order to see that person again in People & Pets." Suppressing someone from your widget can silently remove them from the album, and the reset is all-or-nothing (`Reset People & Pets Suggestions`) or requires finding the per-person `Reset [Name] Feature Settings`. The control is binary — "less" vs "never" — with no per-context granularity.

- **Organization is thin.** Confirmed from Apple's own docs: the **only** organizational primitives for People & Pets are `Sort by Name`, `Sort by Custom Order`, Favorite (floats to top), Hide, and Groups. No folders, no nesting, no tags, no relationship modeling, no search-within-people, no filter-by-letter, no way to triage one-off strangers out of the grid. (Be fair: **Groups is auto-populated and is Apple's de-facto hierarchy answer** — weaker than folders, not nothing.) Apple publishes **no maximum number of people** anywhere.

- **Indexing is opaque and slow.** "Locked and connected to power"; "could happen quickly or take up to a few days"; a bare `Finding People...` string with **no progress, no counts, no ETA**. Users cannot tell whether it is broken or merely slow — which is the #1 support-complaint pattern. A third-party app can run Vision + its own embedder under `BGProcessingTask` and show honest, granular progress. Apple ships an entire troubleshooting article ("If you can't find pets in the People & Pets album") because this fails so often.

- **Pets are cats and dogs only.** Birds, horses, rabbits, reptiles, and livestock are entirely unsupported, and **individual pet identity** (which of your two tabbies) is not offered to third parties at all. Broader species support plus per-individual pet identity is uncontested space.

- **Apple Intelligence search is hard-gated.** Compositional natural-language people search requires Apple Intelligence — not available on all iPhone models, languages, or regions (16-language beta list). A competitor whose conversational people search works on **every** iPhone, in **every** language, is strictly more available. *(But scope the claim correctly: plain person-name search is **not** AI-gated. See 4.9.)*

- **Your people graph is not portable.** Years of manual naming and merging are locked in with no export on iOS. The only escape is an unsupported macOS SQLite read. **"Your people, portable" is a message Apple structurally cannot counter** — and via a Mac helper reading `ZPERSON`/`ZDETECTEDFACE` and emitting MWG-RS rectangles, it doubles as an onboarding funnel that imports their existing Apple people graph on day one.

- **iOS 27 fixes none of it.** Apple's own keynote list for iOS 27 delivers better *search result ranking* for people/pets, pet selection in Photo Shuffle, and self-inclusion in Photo Shuffle. No correction loop, no manual face boxes, no restored confirm flow, no cross-age work, no recognition-engine claim. Every gap above survives into fall 2026.
## 5. Memories, Memory Movies & Featured Photos

Memories is Apple's on-device auto-curation system: a private knowledge graph (built from face/pet recognition, Apple Neural Scene Analyzer scene tags, location, and time) selects "a significant person, pet, place, activity, or event" from the library and turns it into a titled collection plus an auto-edited, music-scored **memory movie**. Featured Photos is the same curation stack expressed as a rotating "best photos" feed, and it is the default source for the Home Screen Photos widget and Lock Screen Photo Shuffle. **The single most important fact for an implementer: none of this is exposed to third parties. There is no `PHMemory` type, no memories case in `PHAssetCollectionSubtype`, no curation-score symbol anywhere in PhotoKit.** That is not a handicap — it means a competitor is not "behind on data," it is on a level field, and Apple has separately shipped the two primitives (Vision image aesthetics + utility filtering) that it says it uses to build Memories itself.

Version baseline for everything below: **iOS 26** (current shipping point release **iOS 26.5.2**; iOS 26.6 in developer beta). iOS 27 is in developer *and* public beta (public beta 1: 2026-07-13), ships fall 2026 — iOS 27 items are marked and are **not shippable today**.

### 5.1 Where these surfaces live in iOS 26 (navigation context)

iOS 18 removed the Photos tab bar entirely and **eliminated the `For You` tab**. iOS 26 restored a tab bar: `Library` and `Collections` buttons, plus a separate `Search` button at the bottom. (Strictly it is a two-button switcher plus Search, not three co-equal tabs — matters for UI parity.)

The `Collections` tab contains, top to bottom: `Recent Days`, then dedicated views for `People & Pets`, `Pinned`, `Memories`, `Trips`, `Albums`, `Featured Photos`, plus `Media Types` and `Utilities` sections, and — below the fold — `Wallpaper Suggestions`. Collections can be collapsed (name only, no thumbnail) and reordered; a quick-access control at the top lets you collapse all, show all, reorder, or choose a different view.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Almost all documentation and press older than ~2024 describes Memories/Featured Photos as living in a **`For You` tab**. That tab does not exist. If your research surfaces "For You," the source is stale.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** iOS 18 let you *exclude* collection types from the Collections tab. **iOS 26 removed that option** — you can only collapse, not exclude.

Also new in iOS 26 and adjacent to this domain: **Spatial Scenes** (2D→3D depth effect; iPhone 12 or later; **no Apple Intelligence required**) and an event-details sheet (swipe up on a concert/sports photo for venue, score, tour dates). Liquid Glass styling throughout.

### 5.2 Memories — the collection

Apple's definition, verbatim: *"The Memories collection in the Photos app includes personalized collections of photos and videos that feature a significant person, pet, place, activity, or event from your photo library."*

Path: `Photos` → `Collections` → the `Memories` row (swipe left to scroll a selection) or tap `Memories` to see them all.

Apple's exact control vocabulary inside a memory (from *View your memories in Photos on iPhone*, iOS 26 guide):

| Action | Control (Apple's name) |
|---|---|
| Filter and sort the memory's contents | `the Sort and Filter button` |
| See every item in the memory | `Show All` |
| Search within the memory | `the Search button` |
| Share / Delete the memory, show its location on a map | `the More button` (the ellipsis) |
| Share only some items | `Select` → `the Share button` |
| Play the memory movie | `the Play button` — bottom-right corner of the memory's cover tile |
| Favorite a memory | touch and hold → `Add to Favorite Memories` |

Favorited memories live at `Collections` → `Memories` → `Favorites`.

**How it works (Apple's own account, from Apple ML Research).** 100% on-device. Photos "learn[s] from identity information to build a private, on-device knowledge graph that identifies interesting patterns in a user's library, such as important groups of people, frequent places, past trips, events, the last time a user took an image of a certain person," and "the knowledge graph powers the beloved Memories feature in Photos, which creates engaging video vignettes centered around different themes in a user's library." Face/person recognition "runs entirely locally, on the user's device." Scene understanding comes from **Apple Neural Scene Analyzer (ANSA)**: "The scene tags from ANSA are ingested in the Photos knowledge graph, which is the foundation of personalized experiences." Asset selection uses **"utility content filtering, image tagging and image aesthetics to pick the highest-quality images."** Key-photo choice is additionally informed by a differentially-private, crowd-learned "iconic scenes" model.

*(The often-repeated claim that Memories dates to iOS 10 is unverified trivia — no Apple source found. Do not make it load-bearing.)*

### 5.3 What triggers a memory (types)

Apple never publishes an exhaustive taxonomy. The **documented** trigger surface is exactly the five nouns in Apple's definition — a significant **person**, **pet**, **place**, **activity**, or **event** — plus two strong structural signals:

1. **Holiday memories are a distinct class.** Apple ships a `Show Holiday Events` toggle whose off-state "prevent[s] Photos from creating memories and featured content about holidays." Apple scopes this to *"holiday events in your home country or region"* — a locale dependency you must model.
2. **Day-, place-, and person-anchored memories are the three primary generators.** The `Feature Less` menu offers exactly three axes: `Feature This Day Less`, `Feature This Place Less`, `Feature a Person Less`. Apple would not ship those three suppression verbs if those were not the three anchors.

`Trips` is a separate sibling collection in the iOS 26 Collections tab, so trip-shaped groupings are broken out of Memories in the IA.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Widely-circulated details about memory *titles* — patterns like `<Place> - Over the Years`, `<Month Year> Trip`, `Memories Across Borders`, and the existence of "On This Day"-style memories — are **anecdotal, not Apple-documented**. They are plausible and useful as design inspiration, but do not ship them in a spec as if Apple published them.

### 5.4 Memory movie playback — and the real control set

Apple: *"View each memory in your Memories collection as a movie that's set to music."* No Apple Intelligence required; works on every iPhone that runs iOS 26.

**This is the highest-value vocabulary correction in the whole domain.** Apple's own figure caption enumerates the entire playback UI:

> "At the bottom of the screen are the **Memory Mixes** and **Browse** buttons. At the top of the screen are the **Back**, **Mute**, and **More** buttons."

There are **five controls, total**. Every editing verb hangs off one of three of them:

| Control | Position | What it opens |
|---|---|---|
| `Memory Mixes` | bottom | Swipe through Memory mixes; nested inside it: `the Filters button` (Memory looks) and `the Music button` |
| `Browse` | bottom | The reorder grid (touch-and-hold, drag) |
| `More` | top | `Manage Photos`, `Short`/`Medium`/`Long`, `Share`, `AirPlay`, `Loop` |
| `Mute` | top | Mutes playback audio (does **not** remove music from the movie) |
| `Back` | top | Exit |

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Nearly every third-party how-to (and the first-pass research this atlas is built on) invents an **"edit button," a "length button," a "music button," a "looks button," or a top-of-screen "share button"** in the playback UI. **None of these exist in iOS 26.** If your parity spec names any of them, it is wrong. Music and Filters are *inside* `Memory Mixes`; length, Manage Photos, Share, AirPlay and Loop are *inside* `More`; reorder is *inside* `Browse`.

Playback gestures (Apple's exact wording):

| Gesture | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Pause | Tap the screen, then tap pause |
| Scrub | *"Swipe left or right. Or tap the screen, then slide the frames at the bottom of the screen left or right."* |
| Mute | Tap the screen, then tap `Mute` |
| Close | Tap the screen, then tap close / `Back` |

The auto-edit is a montage whose cuts are beat-aligned to the chosen soundtrack, opening on a title card carrying the memory's title + subtitle.

### 5.5 Every album is implicitly a memory movie (the DIY path)

Apple, verbatim: *"All the collections and albums you have in the Photos app can be viewed as memory movies."* And the create-from-scratch instruction, verbatim: *"To create a memory movie from scratch, create a photo album, then follow the steps above to watch it as a memory movie."* Apple's page intro adds that every collection/album "can also be viewed as a memory movie that you can watch as created, **or edit to make more personal**" — i.e. the DIY movie gets the full Memory Mixes / Filters / Music / Manage Photos / length control set.

Path: `Photos` → `Collections` → select any collection or album → tap the play button. **No Apple Intelligence required.**

This is the single most under-reported fact in the domain. It means the *entire* memory-movie engine is available to any user, on any iPhone, seeded with an arbitrary asset list — and it means the input to the engine is nothing more exotic than an ordered set of assets. It is therefore the easiest Apple behavior to match, and Apple's discoverability for it is near zero: most users have no idea an album can be played as a movie.

### 5.6 Personalizing a memory movie

All paths start: play the memory → tap the screen.

#### Memory mixes
Apple's definition, verbatim: *"Memory mixes are curated combinations of different songs, pacing, and styles that change the look and feel of a memory movie."* Note Apple's capitalization split: the **control** is `the Memory Mixes button` (title case), the **content noun** in prose is "Memory mixes" (lowercase *mixes*).

Steps: play → tap screen → tap `the Memory Mixes button` → **swipe left** to view different Memory mixes → tap the screen to apply one. Swiping cycles *paired bundles* (song + tonally-matched photographic look + pacing), not independent axes. Dates to iOS 15. A wider song pool is available with an Apple Music subscription.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The frequently-cited detail that the Memory mix icon "looks like a musical note with stars" and sits in the **lower-left** is third-party (iPhone Life) and **unverified**. Apple describes neither the glyph nor a left/right position — only "at the bottom of the screen."

#### Memory looks — but the button is called `Filters`
Apple: *"Use Memory looks to apply consistent color and style adjustments to all the photos in a memory movie."*

**Correct iOS 26 path:** play → tap screen → tap `the Memory Mixes button` → tap **`the Filters button`** → tap a look → tap `Done`.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** There is **no "Looks button"** in iOS 26. `Memory looks` is Apple's *prose noun for the content*; the *control* is labeled **`Filters`**, and it is nested one level down inside the Memory Mixes surface. Ship "Filters" as the control label.

Mechanically these are **adaptive per-asset grades, not flat LUTs** — a look "analyz[es] each photo and video, and appl[ies] the correct amount of contrast and color adjustment for a consistent look," so a mixed-exposure library still reads as one graded piece. *The often-quoted count of **12 looks** is sourced only to iOS-15-era secondary coverage (MacRumors); Apple publishes no count. Treat as unverified — measure on device.* Users cannot create or import a custom look.

#### Music (memory soundtracks + Apple Music)
Apple: *"You can change a memory movie's music by choosing from memory soundtracks or suggested songs in Apple Music. Apple Music subscribers can also access their Apple Music library and view suggested songs based on musical preferences or the content of the memory."*

**Correct iOS 26 path:** play → tap screen → tap `the Memory Mixes button` → tap **`the Music button`** → tap a song → tap `Done`. There is **no top-level music button**; it lives inside Memory Mixes. Apple Music subscribers additionally get `the Search button` to search the full Apple Music catalog.

The built-in soundtrack library is organized by **mood**. Corroborated mood buckets: **Dreamy, Sentimental, Gentle, Chill, Uplifting, Happy, Epic**, plus a bottom **`Special`** bucket of context-locked cues that Photos only auto-selects in specific situations (e.g. a *Happy Birthday* cue for birthdays).

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Some sources list additional moods **"Neutral," "Club," and "Extreme."** No source supports these — treat them as **unverified / possibly fabricated**. Likewise, the claim that *changing the music mood also changes the title-screen font and the transitions* is **unverified**: Apple attributes pacing/style changes to **Memory mixes**, not to the music picker.

#### Manage Photos (add / remove / search) — via `More`
**Correct path:** play → tap screen → tap **`the More button`** → tap `Manage Photos` → then:

| Sub-action | Apple's verbatim instruction |
|---|---|
| Add | *"Tap All, scroll through your library, select the photos you want to add"* |
| Remove | *"Deselect a photo to remove it from the memory"* |
| Search | *"Tap All, tap the Search button, then type the name of a person, place, or date"* |

Each action ends with `the Done button`; you exit via `the Back button`.

#### Reorder — via `Browse` (a *different* button)
**Correct path:** play → tap screen → tap **`the Browse button`** → *"Touch and hold a photo, then drag it to a new position in the grid."*

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Manage Photos and Reorder look like siblings but hang off **two different controls** (`More` vs `Browse`). Getting this wrong is the most common error in the secondary literature.

#### Length: `Short` / `Medium` / `Long` — via `More`
Apple, verbatim: *"Depending on the number of photos in a memory movie, you can change its length to short, medium, or long. Your choice automatically adjusts the number of photos included."*

**Correct path:** *"Tap the screen as the memory plays, tap the More button, then tap Short, Medium, or Long."* Same `More` menu as Manage Photos — **there is no "length button."**

The key insight: **this is a curation-aggressiveness control, not a duration slider.** Picking `Long` admits *more photos* (lowering the quality bar), it does not hold the same photos on screen longer. Options only appear if the memory has enough photos. **Apple publishes no wall-clock durations for Short/Medium/Long anywhere — measure them on device.**

### 5.7 Title, subtitle, and key photo

Apple: *"You can edit the title or subtitle of a memory and change the key photo that appears with the title of the memory."*

> ⚠️ **Trap:** This is edited from the **memory VIEW, not from playback**. Path: `Collections` → `Memories` → **tap a memory to view the collection** → tap `the More button` → tap the current title → edit the title/subtitle fields. Change the key photo: *"Tap the photo icon in the bottom-right corner of the current key photo, then select a new photo in the photo grid"* → `Done`.

Titles and subtitles are generated from knowledge-graph facts (place names, date span, event type) plus ANSA scene tags — ANSA's tags feed "selecting cover photos, generating video titles." Key-photo selection is influenced by the differentially-private "iconic scenes" model. Subtitles are typically the date range.

Quality is poor and this is well documented. Tom's Guide: a movie of a **living** child spanning 2016–2021 was titled `2016 - 2021`, "making it sound like the sort of In Memoriam video you'd see at the Oscars." A Germany-only movie was titled "Memories Across Borders."

### 5.8 `Create a memory movie` with Apple Intelligence

> ⚠️ **Trap — naming:** Apple's official name is exactly **`Create a memory movie`**. It is the section heading in *Use Apple Intelligence in Photos on iPhone* and a verbatim bullet ("Create a memory movie in Photos") in Apple's official Apple Intelligence feature list (support.apple.com/121115). The press term **"Memory Maker" is NOT an Apple name** — it is a MacRumors coinage. Do not use it in product copy, specs, or App Store text.

Apple: *"You can create a custom memory movie of a story you want to see, right in Photos. Just type a description, and Apple Intelligence finds the best photos and videos, crafts a storyline with unique chapters and a narrative arc, and sets it to music."* Apple Newsroom (2024-10-28): "Apple Intelligence will pick out the best photos and videos based on a user's description, craft a storyline with chapters based on themes identified from the photos, and arrange them into a movie with its own narrative arc."

**Exact steps (verbatim):** `Photos` → *"Tap Collections, tap Memories, then tap Create. Enter a description of the movie you want to create from your library, then tap Done."* Prompts may use locations, names of anyone identified in Photos (**including named pets**), times of year, and special occasions. The output is then editable with the same Memory mixes / Filters / Music / Manage Photos / Short-Medium-Long / title controls as any other memory movie.

**Failure state:** when the prompt is too narrow, Photos returns **`Try Another Description`** and prompts the user to "add details to your description or choose a new person, place or event from your library." *(This UI string is corroborated by Tom's Guide, not by Apple documentation — treat as third-party-sourced copy.)*

#### Requirements — the gate that defines the market

| Requirement | Value (verbatim from Apple where quoted) |
|---|---|
| Apple Intelligence | **Required** |
| iPhone | *"iPhone 15 Pro models, and iPhone 16 models or later"* — i.e. 15 Pro / 15 Pro Max, 16 / 16 Plus / 16 Pro / 16 Pro Max / 16e, iPhone 17 / 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max / 17e, iPhone Air |
| iPad | *"iPad mini (A17 Pro), and iPad models with M1 and later"* |
| Mac | *"Mac computers with Apple silicon"* |
| OS | **iOS 18.1 or later** (currently iOS 26.x) |
| Free storage | **~7 GB** |
| Language | *"Device language and Siri language set to the same supported language"* |
| Supported languages (16) | English, Danish, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese |
| EU | Available with **iOS 18.4** / iPadOS 18.4 or later |
| China mainland | *"will not currently work for supported devices purchased in China mainland"* |
| Enablement | Settings → `Apple Intelligence & Siri` |

**Internals are undocumented.** Apple says "chapters" and "narrative arc" but publishes **no** chapter count, no chapter-boundary logic, no statement of whether the model runs on-device or on Private Cloud Compute, and **no prompt-length limit**. Treat all of that as unknown.

#### It does not work well — documented failures
Tom's Guide revisited it six months after launch (2025-04-26): *"I don't think Memory Movies has gotten any smarter since iOS 18.1. The process of creating videos with your own prompts still involves a lot of trial-and-error… More damning is that final test where the Memory Movie-generated video isn't appreciably better than the one that Photos produces all by itself."* Specific reproducible failures:

| Prompt | Failure |
|---|---|
| "Oktoberfest music" | Produced "electronica you'd hear in a discotheque"; a retry produced "a decidedly Latin beat" |
| Germany **and** Czechia | Returned German photos only |
| Contained the place name "Prague" | **Rejected outright** — Apple Intelligence asked for a different search term |
| Date-bounded (Aug 2016 – Jun 2017) | Hard-failed into `Try Another Description` |
| Three Disneyland trips | Returned a 3-image movie from a single 2019 Disney Paris visit |
| "…with her school bag" | Semantic constraint silently dropped |
| "flowers grouped by color" | Broke on multi-color subjects |

Reviewer letter grades across five prompts: **D, A, (mixed), C-, D.**

### 5.9 Natural language search (the same query brain, adjacent surface)

Apple: *"Apple Intelligence makes it even easier to find a specific photo or a key moment in a video—just describe what you want to find."* Apple's own example prompts: **"Maya skateboarding in a tie-dye shirt"** and **"Sadie cartwheeling on the grass."** Officially listed as `Natural language search in Photos` in the Apple Intelligence feature list. It localizes moments **inside videos**, not just photos.

Result controls: `See All`; `Select` (to share or add to an album); `Sort by Recently Added` / `Sort by Date Captured`; `Filter` → e.g. `Favorites`, `Edited`. Sort and Filter are both under `the Sort and Filter button`.

Same Apple Intelligence gate as §5.8 (iPhone 15 Pro / 16+, iOS 18.1+).

*Design inference, not Apple fact: the same query-understanding layer plausibly feeds `Create a memory movie` — the "Prague" rejection and date-range hard-fail are the same brittleness in both surfaces. Apple does not state this.*

iOS 27 (**beta, unreleased**) reportedly improves Top Results to return "more appealing photos of people and pets" and allows search by additional metadata.

### 5.10 Featured Photos

An algorithmically-curated, rotating set of "best" images. In iOS 26 it is a **named collection in the `Collections` tab** and the **default source for the Home Screen Photos widget and Lock Screen Photo Shuffle** (Apple's Photo Shuffle steps name a literal `Use Featured Photos` button).

Same curation stack as Memories. Per Apple ML Research, images "containing receipts, documents, and repair references" are explicitly excluded from *"Memories, Sharing, and Featured Photos"* by utility-content classifiers; selection uses "utility content filtering, image tagging and image aesthetics." Community reporting (unverified) says Featured Photos deliberately skews toward photos you have **not looked at recently** — recency-of-view as a *negative* signal, to manufacture rediscovery.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The menu item **`Remove from Featured Photos`** appears all over the web. Every source describing it **predates the iOS 18 redesign and describes it living in the `For You` view**, which no longer exists. It is **unverified for iOS 26** and iOS 26 coverage (MacObserver) suggests per-photo removal may be gone entirely. Do not write product copy or a competitive claim that asserts it exists today. The only controls Apple *documents* for iOS 26 are the global `Show Featured Content` toggle and the per-person `Don't Feature a Person` flow.

### 5.11 The entire user-control surface: negative curation + kill switches

This is Apple's **complete** curation-control vocabulary. It is worth copying verbatim because it is the language users already know — and note that **every single control is negative**.

| # | Path | Controls |
|---|---|---|
| A | `Collections` → `Memories` → **touch and hold** a memory → `Feature Less` | then one of: `Feature This Day Less`, `Feature This Place Less`, `Feature a Person Less` |
| B | Open a photo → ellipsis → `Don't Feature a Person` → *(if multiple people: tap the person, then `Next`)* | `Feature This Person Less` or `Never Feature This Person` → tap `Confirm` |
| C | `Photos` → `Collections` → **tap your account in the top-right corner** | `Reset Suggested Memories` (undoes Feature Less choices) · `Reset People & Pets Suggestions` (undoes person suppression) |
| D | `Collections` → `Memories` → **touch and hold** a memory | also offers `Add to Favorite Memories`, `Share Photos`, `Delete` |
| E | `Photos` → `Collections` → **account (top-right)** | `Show Featured Content` (off = "prevent Photos from automatically generating featured photos and memories") · `Show Holiday Events` (off = "prevent Photos from creating memories and featured content about holidays") |
| F | `Photos` → `Collections` → account → `Shared Library` | `Shared Library Suggestions` on/off — the kill switch for the "For Your Shared Library" surface |

**Blast radius of `Show Featured Content`, in Apple's own words:** the settings page intro says these controls govern "your memories, featured photos, **and the Photos widget**." So turning it off to stop unwanted memories *also* kills Featured Photos *and* drains the Home Screen Photos widget's default source.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** `Show Featured Content` **disables the generation pipeline, not just the display**. And it is **all-or-nothing**: you cannot keep Memories and kill Featured Photos, or vice versa. One switch governs both plus the widget.

Holiday suppression is scoped to **"holiday events in your home country or region"** — so mixed-faith / multicultural / expatriate households still get irrelevant holiday memories. Model locale explicitly if you clone this.

### 5.12 Sharing a memory — and the export hole

Two distinct paths:

**(1) Share the MOVIE.** *"As the memory plays, tap the More button at the top of the screen, then do any of the following:"*
- *"Share a memory using AirDrop, Messages, or Mail: Tap `Share`, then choose a sharing option."*
- *"Play on a nearby device using AirPlay: Tap `AirPlay`, then choose an available device."*
- Apple's own tip: *"Before you tap AirPlay, tap `Loop`, so the memory automatically plays again."* — `Loop` is a real, named control, and it lives in the same `More` menu.

**(2) Share the COLLECTION (stills, not the movie).** `Collections` → `Memories` → touch and hold a memory → `Share Photos`. Or open the memory → `Select` → pick items → share.

> ⚠️ **Trap — there is no export path.** Apple documents **no way to save a memory movie as a video file** in iOS 26. Sharing is AirDrop / Messages / Mail / AirPlay only. Contrast: **Live Photos** *do* have `Save as Video`, and iOS 27's new slideshow maker *does* add one-tap save-as-video. The absence for memory movies is real and is one of the sharpest product gaps in the domain.

> ⚠️ **Trap — Apple Music DRM.** Memory movies scored with an Apple Music track **cannot be exported/shared with their music**, because the track is DRM-protected. Apple Community threads ("Memory Video - Export Failed", "when saving Memory to video, the music…") document the failure, and iPhone Life states plainly that "certain Memory Mix soundtrack songs won't be shareable when you share your Memory Mix with your friends and family." **This wall applies to you too** — MusicKit lets you *play* Apple Music for a subscriber, but you cannot mux Apple Music audio into a rendered video file. A competitor that licenses a royalty-free/production-music bed can ship something Apple structurally cannot: a shareable, exportable movie that still has its music.

### 5.13 Downstream consumers of the curation feed

#### Photos widget (Home Screen / Lock Screen / Today View)
Shows **Featured Photos by default** and rotates on a system timer. Apple explicitly names "the Photos widget" as one of the three surfaces governed by `Show Featured Content` and per-person suppression. Third-party sources (not Apple) report that `Edit Widget` lets you swap the source to a specific **Album** (an option Apple added in iOS 17), and that **you cannot choose which individual photo appears** at a given moment.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The exact iOS 26 add-widget gesture sequence and the widget's size list are **unverified** for iOS 26 — the commonly-quoted "touch and hold Home Screen → Edit → Add Widget → choose size → Add Widget → Done" flow resembles the iOS 14-era flow and iOS 26's Home Screen edit flow differs. Verify on device before designing parity.

You cannot pick the photo, cannot exclude one photo without perturbing the underlying curation, and cannot set the rotation interval. An entire App Store category of third-party "Photo Widget" apps exists purely to fix this — **validated demand**.

#### Lock Screen Photo Shuffle
A wallpaper type that rotates photos on the Lock Screen. Apple's verbatim setup flow (from *Change your iPhone wallpaper*, current for iOS 26):

`Settings` → `Wallpaper` → `Add New Wallpaper` → *"Select `Photo Shuffle` from the top row of options"* → *"Choose one or more categories like People, Nature, or Cities, or choose an existing album"* → *"Choose a shuffle frequency (`On Tap`, `On Lock`, `Hourly`, or `Daily`)"* → *"Tap the `Use Album` button or `Use Featured Photos` button when done (the button text depends on your Photo Shuffle)."*

Apple also documents a **second configuration mode most write-ups miss: `Select Photos Manually`** — pick your own collection of images → checkmark → tap the ellipsis to set shuffle frequency → `Add`.

To change it later from the Lock Screen editor: *"If you chose Photo Shuffle, tap the photo thumbnail to change the photo selection or change the shuffle frequency by tapping the More button."*

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Apple names only **People, Nature, or Cities** as categories. **`Pets` as a Photo Shuffle category is third-party-sourced** (iMore, Gadget Hacks) — it appears to be real but is not Apple-documented. Relatedly, the claim that **iOS 27 adds a pet-specific Photo Shuffle option is unsupported and probably false** — Pets has been a shuffle category since the iOS 16/17 era, so "new in iOS 27" is doubly wrong. **Do not put it in a competitive-gap analysis.**

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The per-photo exclusion control **`Don't Feature Photo`** (customize screen → ellipsis) is **unverified** — no source confirms it for iOS 26. Macworld (2022) described it and noted such choices are effectively irreversible.

Adjacent, same wallpaper surface: **Spatial Scene wallpaper** — `Settings` → `Wallpaper` → `Add New Wallpaper` → `Photos` → scroll the top bar to the **Spatial Scene** tab → "Generating Spatial Scene" → `Add`. iPhone 12 or later, iOS 26.

#### Wallpaper Suggestions (inside Photos)
Apple: *"You can get wallpaper suggestions for your Lock Screen or Home Screen that stylize photos of your favorite people and pets."* Path: `Photos` → `Collections` → **swipe up** → tap a suggested wallpaper (below the `Wallpaper Suggestions` heading).

Implementation detail from Apple's figure caption: each suggestion is an **"automatically generated combination of photos, filter effects, and clock face fonts"** shown in a grid. **A suggestion bundles image + filter + clock font — it is not merely a photo.** Material if you clone it.

The surface is hidden below the fold of the Collections tab; most users never find it.

### 5.14 Sharing Suggestions → `For Your Shared Library`

Apple's definition: *"Sharing suggestions recommends photos you might want to add to your iCloud Shared Photo Library, such as photos you took when participants of the shared library were nearby, or photos of people you indicated interest in during the setup process. iPhone sends a notification to review sharing suggestions."*

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Path to the surface | *"tap `Collections`, tap your account in the top-right corner, then tap `For Your Shared Library`."* |
| Kill switch | `Collections` → account → `Shared Library` → **`Shared Library Suggestions`** on/off |
| Auto-contribution settings | `Collections` → account → `Shared Library` → `Sharing from Camera`: **`Share Automatically`** (adds photos taken when participants are nearby — requires Bluetooth on and participants signed in) and **`Share When At Home`** |
| Broaden suggestions | Tap `Add People` and pick a person who **need not be a shared-library member** |
| Requirements | iCloud Shared Photo Library needs iOS 16.1+ and iCloud Photos; **up to 6 participants** |
| Mechanism | Bluetooth/proximity detection of participants at capture time + on-device face recognition against nominated people + geofenced "at home" detection |

> ⚠️ **Trap — a feature that died.** The **old** For-You-era "Sharing Suggestions" (Photos suggesting you *send an event's photos to the people detected in them*, via Messages) **vanished with the `For You` tab in iOS 18** and has no replacement. No Apple documentation for a standalone, non-Shared-Library sharing-suggestion surface exists for iOS 26. If you find a source describing it, that source is stale. (Apple has never published a removal statement — this is inference from absence, but a well-grounded one.)

### 5.15 Slideshow — the iOS 18 regression Apple is only now reversing

**iOS 26 (current, shipping):** the classic themed Slideshow is **gone**. Apple's entire slideshow documentation now reads: *"In the Photos app, you can create a slideshow to view a selection of photos and videos that you choose from your photo library. Slideshows are automatically formatted and set to music."*

Steps: `Photos` → `Select` → tap each photo → tap **`the More button`** → tap **`Play as Slideshow`**. Apple then redirects *all* customization to the memory-movie editor: *"To change the slideshow music, theme, and more, see Personalize your memories."*

**In other words: in iOS 26, a slideshow IS a memory movie.** Same forced music, same forced Ken Burns motion, same three-control editor.

What users lost in iOS 18 and still do not have on iOS 26:
- Slideshow **themes** (Ken Burns, Origami, etc.)
- Running a slideshow **without music at all**
- Turning **off** the forced Ken Burns pan/zoom
- **Per-slide timing**

Apple Community thread titles tell the story: *"Why did Photos update remove slideshow options?"*, *"Where did slideshow themes go in Photos?"*, *"ipados 18 has slideshow disappeared?"* Representative user framing: Apple "removed the standard Slideshow and replaced it with an inferior memory maker that has none of the functionality of the original," leaving "absolutely no creative control."

**iOS 27 (BETA — public beta 1 landed 2026-07-13, ships fall 2026 — NOT shippable today):** restores real slideshows — buildable from **any** selection of photos/videos (not just an album), with customizable **transition style**, **slide duration** (for the whole slideshow *and* for individual photos), **background music**, and **save/export the result as a video in one tap**.
