> ⚠️ **Trap:** The iOS 27 slideshow details come from press (MacRumors, 9to5Mac), **not Apple documentation** — Apple has not published the iOS 27 user guide. **The exact UI labels for transition style / slide duration / background music are NOT confirmed and must not be treated as final vocabulary.**

This is a **two-year-old open wound that a competitor can fill TODAY on the ~entire installed base of iOS 26 devices** — and Apple's own iOS 27 reversal is an admission the complaint was valid.

### 5.16 Live Photo effects (the one partially-open door)

Apple's exact menu, from the `Live` control in the **top-left corner** of an open Live Photo, with Apple's own one-line definitions:

| Option | Apple's definition |
|---|---|
| `Live` | "Applies the Live video playback feature." |
| `Loop` | "Repeats the action in a continuous looping video." |
| `Bounce` | "Rewinds the action backward and forward." |
| `Long Exposure` | "Simulates a DSLR-like long exposure effect by blurring motion." |
| `Live Off` | "Turns off the Live video playback feature or applied effect." |
| `Portrait` | "Applies the Portrait effect." |
| `Portrait off` | "Turns off the Portrait effect." |

**Editor** (open Live Photo → `Edit` → the `Live` tab; the editor's bottom tab set is `Live` · `Adjust` · `Filters` · `Crop`):
- Set a key photo: *"Move the white frame on the frame viewer, tap `Make Key Photo`, then tap `Done`."*
- Trim: *"Drag either end of the frame viewer."*
- Make a still photo: tap `Live` at the top to turn off the Live feature.
- Mute a Live Photo.

**Export:** open the Live Photo → tap `the More button` in the top-right → **`Save as Video`**.

> ⚠️ **Trap (Apple documents this one itself):** *"Live Photos taken on an iPhone 15 model or later with a portrait effect lose the portrait effect if you change the key photo."*

The effect set has been frozen at three (Loop / Bounce / Long Exposure) since **iOS 11**. No speed control, no exposure-time control on Long Exposure, no GIF export, no stabilization/alignment control (which is why handheld Long Exposure is poor).

### 5.17 Memories notifications

Photos fires a local notification when the on-device curation job (which runs on charge/idle) produces a new memory. It can be disabled **without** killing all Photos notifications:

`Settings` → `Notifications` → `Photos` → `Customize Notifications` → toggle off **`Memories`**.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** This menu path is **third-party-sourced** (macReports, Gadget Hacks) — Apple does not document it on any page. Verify on device.

The nuclear option remains `Photos` → `Collections` → account → `Show Featured Content` off, which stops *generation* entirely.

This notification is the exact moment an unwanted memory (an ex, a deceased relative) ambushes a user, and the opt-out is buried under a submenu most users don't know exists. Multiple Apple Community threads exist purely to explain how to stop "New Photos Memory" alerts.

### 5.18 There is no "Recap" / "Year in Review"

**Apple ships no officially-named, annually-scheduled Recap or Year-in-Review feature in Photos on iPhone.** No Apple Support page, no Newsroom item, no developer doc. This is a finding worth stating loudly because it is exactly the kind of feature it is tempting to *assume* exists — Apple Music has `Replay`; **Photos has no equivalent**. Google Photos, by contrast, *does* ship a documented, named **Recap**.

What actually exists: auto-generated memories with year-spanning titles and date-range subtitles; users typing a year description into `Create a memory movie` (press coverage at the 2024 year-end framed Apple Intelligence memory-movie creation as the way to "revisit your highlights of 2024"); and Apple Community threads titled *"Missing: Photos Year in Review Slideshow"*, *"Year in review slide show"*, *"iPhotos Year in Review"* asking where it went.

> ⚠️ **Trap on the trap:** absence of documentation is not proof that no year-titled memory is ever auto-generated. Assert only the defensible claim: **"not a documented, named feature."** (Note also that the only sources claiming Apple *does* have one are AI-generated content farms.)

### 5.19 What a third-party app can and cannot do

Verified against Apple's live API index (PhotoKit/Photos symbol index and the full `PHAssetCollectionSubtype` case list enumerated from Apple's docs JSON, 2026-07-14).

| Capability | Available to 3rd parties? | Mechanism / why not |
|---|---|---|
| Read Apple's **Memories** | **No** | No `PHMemory` type. `PHAssetCollectionSubtype`'s **30 cases contain no memories case**. Nothing in the Photos framework symbol index exposes curation. |
| Read **Featured Photos** | **No** | No `featured` case in `PHAssetCollectionSubtype`; no symbol anywhere. |
| Read Apple's **curation/aesthetics scores** for an asset | **No** | Not surfaced on `PHAsset`. |
| Read/render an Apple **memory movie**, Memory mix, or Memory look | **No** | No API. Not even Apple exposes a memory-movie verb via App Intents (see below). |
| Historical **Moments** API (`PHAssetCollectionType.moment`, moment lists) | **No — removed** | ⚠️ **Trap:** this is the first place an implementer will look for Apple's curation. It was removed years ago and is **absent from the current enum**. It is *gone*, not merely undocumented. |
| Set the **Lock Screen wallpaper** / install a Photo Shuffle | **No** | No API exists. **A genuine Apple moat.** Nearest legal substitute: a Lock Screen **widget** (WidgetKit accessory families) plus a user-installed Shortcuts automation. |
| Score image quality the way Apple does | **YES** | **Vision** `CalculateImageAestheticsScoresRequest` → `ImageAestheticsScoresObservation` (iOS 18+): `overallScore` in **[-1, 1]** ("Multiple factors get analyzed to determine image quality such as blur and exposure") and **`isUtility`** ("true for photos that are well taken, but have non-memorable content" — screenshots, receipts). **This is literally Apple's own stated two-signal recipe** — "utility content filtering, image tagging and image aesthetics" — shipped as public API. |
| Face / person / pet detection, scene classification, saliency (attention + objectness), subject lifting | **YES** | Vision. `VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest` for subject lift. |
| Semantic image embeddings for search / clustering | **YES** | `VNGenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest`, or bundle your own CLIP/SigLIP. |
| Full library access, asset metadata, Live Photos | **YES** | PhotoKit. `PHLivePhoto`, `PHLivePhotoView`, `PHLivePhotoEditingContext`. |
| Read Apple's own effect smart albums | **YES** | `PHAssetCollectionSubtype`: `smartAlbumLivePhotos`, `smartAlbumLongExposures`, `smartAlbumAnimated` (the Loop/Bounce bucket), `smartAlbumBursts`, `smartAlbumFavorites`, `smartAlbumScreenshots`, `smartAlbumDepthEffect`, `smartAlbumCinematic`, `smartAlbumSpatial`, `smartAlbumRAW`, plus `smartAlbumPanoramas`, `smartAlbumTimelapses`, `smartAlbumSlomoVideos`, `smartAlbumSelfPortraits`, `smartAlbumScreenRecordings`, `smartAlbumRecentlyAdded`, `smartAlbumAllHidden`, `smartAlbumUnableToUpload`, `smartAlbumGeneric`, `smartAlbumUserLibrary`, `smartAlbumVideos`. |
| iCloud Shared Photo Library membership per asset | **YES (read)** | PhotoKit has a "Shared photo library" topic group; the **suggestion engine** is not exposed. |
| On-device LLM for prompt → storyline / chapters / titles | **YES — but gated** | **Foundation Models framework** (iOS 26+). ⚠️ **Trap:** it is a myth that this lets you outflank Apple's hardware gate. Foundation Models runs **only on Apple-Intelligence-capable devices with Apple Intelligence enabled — iPhone 15 Pro / iPhone 16 or later, the EXACT same gate as Apple's `Create a memory movie`.** You can *match* the gate, not beat it. **Plan a non-LLM fallback for pre-15-Pro hardware.** |
| Render an auto-edited movie | **YES** | AVFoundation — `AVMutableComposition` + `AVVideoComposition`. Bring your own beat detection. |
| Adaptive per-asset color grading (clone "Memory looks") | **YES** | Core Image + per-asset histogram/exposure analysis; gate correction strength on the Vision aesthetics score. |
| Play real Apple Music tracks | **YES (for subscribers)** | **MusicKit** (MusicKit for Swift / `ApplicationMusicPlayer`); catalog search + recommendations let you rebuild the "suggested songs" UX. |
| **Mux Apple Music audio into an exported video file** | **No** | DRM. ⚠️ **Trap:** MusicKit playback ≠ export rights. **Apple hits this same wall itself** (§5.12). Licensed royalty-free/production music is the only way to ship a shareable, music-bearing export. |
| Be driven by Siri / Apple Intelligence / Shortcuts as a photo app | **YES** | **App Intents** — the Photos assistant-schema domain is public. Full `AssistantSchemas.PhotosIntent` case list: `search`, `createAlbum`, `updateAlbum`, `deleteAlbum`, `addAssetsToAlbum`, `removeAssetsFromAlbum`, `createAssets`, `updateAsset`, `duplicateAssets`, `deleteAssets`, `openAsset`, `openAlbum`, `cleanupPhoto`, `crop`, `straighten`, `setRotation`, `setFilter`, `setExposure`, `setSaturation`, `setWarmth`, `setDepth`, `toggleDepth`, `toggleSuggestedEdits`, `copyEdits`, `pasteEdits`, `updateRecognizedPerson`, `postToSharedAlbum`. |
| A memory-movie **App Intent** schema | **No — for anyone** | ⚠️ **Trap / sharpest insight in the domain:** there is **no memory-movie schema**. Apple did not open that verb to third parties *or to itself* via App Intents. Memory movies are unreachable from Siri and Shortcuts entirely. |
| A genuinely configurable photo widget | **YES** | **WidgetKit** is fully open — per-photo pinning, custom rotation interval, multiple albums, people filters. The App Store's crowded "Photo Widget" category is proof of demand. |
| Local notifications for your own memories | **YES** | UserNotifications. Fully replicable, and improvable (batching, good-time delivery, opt-in scoping, never notify about a suppressed person). |

**Bottom line:** the walled garden is the *data*, not the *capability*. Apple hands out the aesthetics scorer, the face/pet/scene models, the embeddings, the renderer, the music player, the assistant surface, and the widget runtime. A competitor must build its own curation graph from `PHAsset` metadata (`creationDate`, location, `isFavorite`, `mediaSubtypes`, burst identifiers) + Vision + its own clustering — and can then legitimately claim it does everything Apple does, with the controls Apple refuses to ship. A third party can also pull in **EventKit** and **Contacts** signals, which is roughly the only structural advantage Apple's graph has (it sees Calendar/Contacts natively).

### 5.20 Where Apple is weak — our opening

Ranked roughly by size of the wedge.

- **There is no positive curation. At all.** Apple's *entire* control surface is negative: `Feature This Day Less`, `Feature This Place Less`, `Feature a Person Less`, `Feature This Person Less`, `Never Feature This Person`, `Show Featured Content` off, `Show Holiday Events` off. **You cannot say "always build memories from these people," "build a memory from this album," "pin this memory," or "schedule a memory."** This is the clearest product gap in the domain and it has existed for a decade.

- **Emotional safety is reactive only.** Users must *discover* `Never Feature This Person` themselves, **after** being ambushed by a memory of an ex or a deceased relative — typically via a push notification. There is no proactive "sensitive person" setup during onboarding. XDA published a how-to titled "How to stop Photos from surfacing memories of exes and deceased people" *because Apple ships no answer*. A competitor that asks once, up front, "is there anyone you don't want to see?" wins trust Apple cannot buy back.

- **The iOS 18 slideshow regression is a two-year-old open wound, live on iOS 26 today.** Themes, music-off, Ken-Burns-off, and per-slide timing all disappeared; Apple's docs now literally redirect slideshow customization to the memory-movie editor. Apple only restores real slideshows in **iOS 27 (beta, ships fall 2026)** — a tacit admission the complaint was valid. **You can ship the fix now, on the entire iOS 26 installed base.**

- **No export path for memory movies.** Apple documents AirDrop/Messages/Mail/AirPlay only — **no "save as video."** Combine with the Apple Music DRM wall (a memory movie scored with Apple Music *cannot* carry its music into a share) and Apple is structurally incapable of shipping a shareable, music-bearing movie. Licensing a production-music bed makes this a feature Apple cannot copy without renegotiating the music industry.

- **Repetition is the #1 complaint and is a decade old.** Apple Community thread *"Repetitive 'Memories'"* reports the same handful of photos resurfacing **10–20 times, sometimes with identical captions**. Related: memories built from downloaded wallpapers and screenshots rather than personal photos; culturally wrong memories (an Easter memory generated for a Jewish family); holiday suppression scoped only to the "home country or region."

- **Apple Intelligence's `Create a memory movie` does not work well, and is gated to iPhone 15 Pro / 16+.** Six months post-launch Tom's Guide concluded the AI movie "isn't appreciably better than the one that Photos produces all by itself," with hard failures on place names ("Prague" rejected), multi-country prompts, date ranges (hard-fail into `Try Another Description`), and semantic constraints (silently dropped). Grades across five prompts: **D, A, mixed, C-, D.** *Caveat: Foundation Models carries the same hardware gate, so you cannot out-flank Apple on device coverage with an on-device LLM — you must ship a non-LLM curation fallback for pre-15-Pro phones, which then covers a market Apple's AI feature cannot reach at all.*

- **Auto-titles are tone-deaf.** A movie of a *living* child spanning 2016–2021 got titled `2016 - 2021`, reading as an In Memoriam reel. Titles are template-y knowledge-graph fills. An on-device LLM (or a server model, or a decent template library) beats them trivially — and titling is the first thing a user sees.

- **The memory-movie editor has no timeline.** You can reorder in a grid, but you **cannot set per-photo duration, cannot choose which segment of a video clip plays, and cannot add text**. `Short`/`Medium`/`Long` is a curation-aggressiveness preset, not a duration control — and `Long` actively dilutes quality by admitting weaker shots. Apple publishes no wall-clock durations for any of the three.

- **Editing is buried.** Everything hangs off three unlabeled icons that only appear *while the movie is playing*: `Memory Mixes` (→ Filters, Music), `Browse` (→ reorder), `More` (→ Manage Photos, length, Share/AirPlay/Loop). Discoverability is dismal, and Apple's own kill switches are hidden inside an **account sheet inside a tab**, not in Settings where users look.

- **Memory mixes bundle song + look together.** If you like the look but not the song you must go re-edit music separately. No independent axes.

- **The Photos widget is rigid.** You cannot pick the photo, cannot exclude a photo without perturbing the curation, cannot set the rotation interval — and turning off `Show Featured Content` to stop unwanted memories **guts the widget too**. The App Store's crowded "Photo Widget" category is validated demand for exactly this fix, and **WidgetKit is fully open to you**.

- **No year-in-review.** Apple ships nothing. Google Photos ships a named `Recap`; Spotify Wrapped trained the expectation. Apple Community threads asking where Apple's went have gone unanswered for years. A scheduled year/month recap with a **shareable vertical-video export** is an obvious, un-taken slot — and Apple's DRM problem means Apple cannot easily take it even if it wanted to.

- **Live Photo effects have been frozen since iOS 11.** Three effects (Loop / Bounce / Long Exposure), no speed control, no exposure-time control, no GIF export, no stabilization. **And PhotoKit gives you the raw material** (`PHLivePhoto`, `PHLivePhotoEditingContext`, plus the `smartAlbumLivePhotos` / `smartAlbumLongExposures` / `smartAlbumAnimated` smart albums). Better long exposure, variable shutter, motion trails, speed ramps, GIF export — all buildable today.

- **The old For-You "Sharing Suggestions" (send this event's photos to the people in them) simply vanished in iOS 18** with no replacement. And Apple's surviving suggestion surface is locked to iCloud Shared Photo Library — **max 6 participants**, Apple-ecosystem-only, requires Bluetooth and everyone signed in, and fails silently. A competitor doing proximity + face-match suggestions itself is bound by none of those.

- **Two full Photos redesigns in two years.** The iOS 18 redesign is one of the best-documented UX failures in recent Apple history (the swipeable carousel was pulled mid-beta; iMore reported the backlash forced a rethink; iOS 26 restored the tab bar). The trust cost is real, and stability is a positioning asset.

---
## 6. Albums, Shared Libraries & Organization

This is Apple Photos' manual-organization layer: user-created albums, folders that contain albums, the system-generated collections (`Media Types`, `Utilities`), the pinned-shortcut row, and the two entirely different sharing mechanisms Apple confusingly ships side by side (`Shared Albums`, a 2048px-downscaled copy-based photo stream from the iOS 6 era; and `iCloud Shared Photo Library`, a full-fidelity second library with move semantics). The single most important structural fact: **albums are references, not containers** — a photo can live in many albums, deleting an album never deletes its photos, and there is no "move between albums" primitive. The single most important *implementer* fact: **under limited photo library access, PhotoKit cannot create or fetch user albums at all** — every album feature you build is hard-gated behind the user granting full library access.

Version baseline for this section: iOS 26.5.2 shipping (26.5.1 on iPhone 17 series / iPhone Air; iOS 26.6 in developer beta). iOS 27 is **prerelease** (developer beta 1 June 8 2026, public beta 1 July 13 2026, ships ~fall 2026) and every iOS 27 item below is marked as such.

---

### 6.1 Information architecture: where albums live in iOS 26

iOS 26 replaced iOS 18's single scrolling view with a **two-tab model**: a `Library` tab and a `Collections` tab, plus a `Search` tab. Every album and organization surface now lives under `Collections`. Apple's how-to steps universally begin: "Tap Collections, then tap Albums."

Sections that appear inside the `Collections` tab:

| Section | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Recent Days` | Auto-grouped recent activity |
| `Memories` | Curated slideshows (see Memories section of this atlas) |
| `Pinned` | User-curated shortcut row (§6.9) |
| `People & Pets` | Face/pet recognition groupings |
| `Trips` | Auto-grouped travel |
| `Albums` | User albums + folders (§6.2, §6.5) |
| `Shared Albums` | Legacy iCloud Photo Sharing (§6.11) |
| `Media Types` | System auto-collections by media kind (§6.7) |
| `Utilities` | Imports, Duplicates, Hidden, Recently Deleted, (conditionally) Recovered (§6.8) |
| `Featured Photos` | Curated highlights |

Inside the `Albums` screen there is a **segmented control** with buttons to view albums by `Personal`, `Shared`, or `Activity`. This is the actual top-level IA of the Albums screen — `Shared` and `Activity` are not merely steps buried inside other flows.

⚠️ **Trap: the iOS 18 → iOS 26 navigation churn.** Any tutorial, blog post, or model memory predating ~mid-2025 describes an `Albums` *tab*. That tab does not exist in iOS 26. If your onboarding copy says "go to the Albums tab," it is wrong for every currently shipping iPhone.

---

### 6.2 User albums — create, rename, delete, share

**Create** (iOS 26, Apple's exact steps):
1. Tap `Collections`.
2. Tap `Albums`, then tap the Add button (**+**).
3. Tap `New Album`, "then name the album, add photos, and choose a key photo to represent the album."
4. Tap `Create`.

Note that **key-photo selection is offered at creation time** on iOS.

| Operation | Exact iOS 26 flow | Apple's note |
|---|---|---|
| Rename | Touch and hold the album → `Edit Title and Photos` → enter new name → `Done` | The affordance is *not* labeled "Rename" |
| Delete | Touch and hold the album → `Delete Album` | "When you delete an album, the photos and videos within it remain in your photo library and any other albums they were added to." |
| Share contents | Open album → `Select` → tap items, "or tap Select All to share everything in the album" → Share button → `AirDrop`, `Messages`, or `Mail` | — |

**Storage/sync model:** albums are stored in the Photos SQLite library and synced by iCloud Photos. Apple: "If you use iCloud Photos, albums are stored in iCloud. They're up to date and accessible on devices where you're signed in to the same Apple Account."

**Reference semantics (macOS guide, applies to the same library model):** "You can place photos in more than one album." There is no "move photo from album A to album B" on iOS — the user must `Add to Album` (B), then `Remove from Album` (A), as two separate menu journeys.

**Undocumented limits:** Apple does not publish any maximum number of user albums, maximum number of folders, or maximum folder nesting depth. No source could be found. Treat as unbounded but verify on-device before relying on it.

---

### 6.3 Album contents — add, remove, filter, sort, custom order

| Task | Exact flow |
|---|---|
| Add from inside the album | Open album → tap the Add button "after the last photo in the album's photo grid" → select → `Done`. Apple tip: "Tap [the Search button] to find photos from a specific time or place" while picking. |
| Add a single photo | Open the photo → More button (**…**) → `Add to Album` → pick album |
| **Bulk add from the library** | `Select` → tap items → **the Share button** → `Add to Album` → tap the album |
| Remove one | Touch and hold the photo → `Remove from Album` |
| Remove several | `Select` → items → More button → `Remove from Album` |
| Search within an album | Open album → Search button → "enter the person, object, or place you're looking for" |

⚠️ **Trap (corrected from a common error): bulk-add uses the SHARE button, not the More button.** Apple's verbatim text: "Tap Select, then tap the items you want to add. Tap [the Share button], tap Add to Album, then tap the album you want to add the items to." Single-item add *does* use More. The two paths use different buttons for the same logical action — an implementer copying "the real vocabulary" will get this wrong if they generalize from one flow.

**Filter an album's contents:** open the album → tap the **`Sort and Filter` button** → `Filter` → choose an option. Confirmed options: "only photos, only videos, or photos and videos you marked as favorites." To clear: "tap the icon that replaced [the Sort and Filter button] at the bottom of the screen, then tap `Remove Filter`."

**Sort an album's contents:** `Sort and Filter` button → choose a sort option. Confirmed options: newest to oldest, oldest to newest, and `Sort by Custom Order`. With custom order: "touch and hold the photo or video thumbnail, then drag it into a new position."

⚠️ **Trap: this control is the `Sort and Filter` button, not the More button.** Apple's iPhone User Guide names it explicitly. Same for the library-level control (§6.10). The Albums-*list* control (§6.5) genuinely *is* the More button. Three nearby surfaces, two different button identities.

Filters are **transient and per-album**. There is no saved-filter concept — that would be a Smart Album, which iOS does not have.

---

### 6.4 Key photo (album cover)

On iOS the key photo is chosen **at album creation**: "name the album, add photos, and choose a key photo to represent the album." The key photo is the image shown above the album name in the Albums list.

On macOS, changing it later is explicit and documented: "To set an album's key photo—the photo that represents the album in the Photos window—double-click the album to open it, select a photo, then choose `Image` > `Make Key Photo`."

⚠️ **Trap: post-hoc "Make Key Photo" on iOS is UNVERIFIED.** Multiple tech-press sources (iDownloadBlog 2021, iPhoneLife, MakeUseOf, AppleToolBox) describe an in-album touch-and-hold → `Make Key Photo` gesture on iPhone, but **none are iOS 26-era and Apple's iOS 26 User Guide does not document it** — the guide documents only creation-time key-photo choice and a touch-and-hold → `Edit Title and Photos` sheet. Do not ship this as a documented Apple flow; verify on-device.

Also documented by press: the key photo **cannot** be changed for the `Recents` or `Favorites` collections at all.

**Third-party access: none.** PhotoKit exposes no key-photo/cover property and no change request for it on `PHAssetCollection`. A third-party app cannot read or set the Photos-app key photo (it can obviously pick its own cover for its own UI).

---

### 6.5 Folders (containers for albums)

Apple: "You can create folders to organize your albums. After you create a folder, it appears in the Albums collection."

- **Create:** `Collections` → `Albums` → **+** → `New Folder` → name the folder and add albums to it → `Create`.
- **Remove an album from a folder:** "tap the folder to open it, touch and hold an album, then tap `Remove from Folder`."

A folder is a `PHCollectionList` — a collection that contains other collections. Folders can nest (a collection list can contain other collection lists).

**Albums-list controls (this one really is the More button):** Apple verbatim — "Tap Albums, tap [the More button], then choose a sort option. If you choose `Sort by Custom Order`, touch and hold an album, then drag it to a new position. To show only albums or only folders, tap [the More button], tap `Filter`, then choose an option. To change the format of the albums list, tap [the More button], then select `List View` or `Key Photo`."

⚠️ **Trap: Apple never enumerates the non-custom album sort options.** The guide says "choose a sort option" and names only `Sort by Custom Order`. The full option set (by title? by date?) is undocumented — verify on-device.

**Limitations:** folders contain only albums and other folders — you cannot place a loose photo in a folder. There is no drag-an-album-into-a-folder gesture from the albums grid; you must go through the `New Folder` sheet or `Remove from Folder`. (macOS has a separate documented "Group albums in folders" feature; the cross-platform folder model is not fully symmetric.)

---

### 6.6 Smart Albums — **they do not exist on iOS**

This is settled by an Apple primary source, from the **macOS** Photos guide: *"Note: Smart Albums that you create on your Mac don't appear in Photos on your iPhone or iPad."*

There is no rule-builder, no criteria engine, and no user-defined Smart Album anywhere in Photos on iPhone or iPad as of iOS 26. Every album on iOS is hand-curated.

On macOS, Smart Albums are real and rich: `File` > `New Smart Album`, then build conditions from three pop-ups — a category pop-up ("Photo, by default"), a relationship pop-up ("is," by default, with is/is not), and a criteria pop-up ("favorite," by default) — with add/remove condition buttons and a `Match` pop-up offering `any` / `all`. Edit later via Control-click the Smart Album in the sidebar → `Edit Smart Album`. **None of this syncs to, or is creatable on, iOS.** macOS-only album features also include `Make Key Photo`, `Duplicate Album`, and merging albums by dragging one onto another.

⚠️ **Trap — the biggest terminology trap in the whole domain: PhotoKit's "smart albums" are NOT macOS Smart Albums.** `PHAssetCollectionType.smartAlbum` and its ~21 `PHAssetCollectionSubtype` cases *do* exist on iOS, but they are the **fixed, system-defined** Media-Types/Utilities collections (Videos, Selfies, Bursts, Screenshots, Hidden…). They are not user-definable, accept no rules, and share nothing with macOS Smart Albums but the word. An engineer who reads `smartAlbum` in the PhotoKit docs and concludes "iOS has smart albums, we can create them" will lose days.

The exact count is **21**: Apple's `PHAssetCollectionSubtype` page lists 19 under "Smart Album Types" — `smartAlbumAllHidden`, `smartAlbumAnimated`, `smartAlbumBursts`, `smartAlbumCinematic`, `smartAlbumDepthEffect`, `smartAlbumFavorites`, `smartAlbumGeneric`, `smartAlbumLivePhotos`, `smartAlbumLongExposures`, `smartAlbumPanoramas`, `smartAlbumRAW`, `smartAlbumRecentlyAdded`, `smartAlbumScreenshots`, `smartAlbumSelfPortraits`, `smartAlbumSlomoVideos`, `smartAlbumTimelapses`, `smartAlbumUnableToUpload`, `smartAlbumUserLibrary`, `smartAlbumVideos` — plus `smartAlbumScreenRecordings` and `smartAlbumSpatial`, listed separately as newer enumeration cases.

⚠️ **Trap: `smartAlbumDepthEffect` is Apple's API name for what the UI calls "Portrait."** There is no `smartAlbumPortrait`.

**Nothing in the iOS 27 beta indicates iOS gains user Smart Albums** — though iOS 27 does add keywords and star ratings (§6.13), which are exactly the metadata primitives a rules engine would consume. (That Apple is building toward an iOS rules engine is *speculation*, not fact.)

**Third-party angle:** you *can* build your own rule engine on PhotoKit. `PHFetchOptions` accepts an `NSPredicate` (with limits — Photos does **not** support `NSPredicate(block:)` or the generic initializer), and `PHAsset` exposes `mediaType`, `mediaSubtypes`, `isFavorite`, `creationDate`, `location`, `pixelWidth`/`pixelHeight`, `burstIdentifier`, etc. But you cannot create a persistent album that the *Photos app itself* treats as smart — you would re-materialize a regular album on each evaluation, or keep the rule inside your own app.

---

### 6.7 Media Types collections

`Collections` → scroll down → `Media Types` → tap a type. These are system-generated, fixed collections. The user cannot define them and cannot hand-remove a photo from one. Apple (macOS guide, same model): "You can't delete individual photos from a Smart Album or from the collections created for you, such as Videos or Bursts. The photos are added to these collections automatically based on the search criteria of the collection."

**Reorder (confirmed verbatim):** "Tap `Edit`, touch and hold the collection you want to move, then drag it to a new position. To undo your changes, tap `Reset`." (This affordance did not exist before iOS 26.)

⚠️ **Trap: Apple never publishes the Media Types UI list, and the PhotoKit subtype enum is NOT that list.** The iOS guide only *exemplifies* it ("Tap a collection like Videos or Selfies"; "browse all your Portrait mode photos or time-lapse videos in one place"). Do not hand a PhotoKit enum dump to a designer as the UI spec — `smartAlbumFavorites` is a top-level Pinned collection; `smartAlbumAllHidden` and Recently Deleted live under `Utilities`, not Media Types; and `smartAlbumRecentlyAdded`, `smartAlbumUnableToUpload`, `smartAlbumGeneric`, `smartAlbumUserLibrary` are not user-facing Media Types entries at all. The plausible UI set (Videos, Selfies, Live Photos, Portrait, Panoramas, Time-lapse, Slo-mo, Bursts, Screenshots, Screen Recordings, Animated/GIFs, RAW, Cinematic, Spatial, Long Exposure) is **reconstructed from PhotoKit + press, not sourced from Apple.** Verify on-device against a library containing every media type.

⚠️ **Trap: "collections only appear if you have matching content" is only EXPLICITLY documented by Apple for `Duplicates` and `Recovered`.** Generalizing that rule to every media type is *unverified*. It is probably true — no two users see the same list — but do not state it as an Apple fact.

Content prerequisites where they are known: Spatial requires spatial capture (iPhone 15 Pro and later, or Vision Pro content); Cinematic requires Cinematic-mode capture.

---

### 6.8 Utilities collections

`Collections` → scroll down → `Utilities`. Apple verbatim: "Tap Collections, then scroll down to Utilities. Tap a collection like `Recently Deleted` or `Hidden`, or tap `Utilities` to see more."

iOS 26 contents: `Imports`, `Duplicates`, `Hidden`, `Recently Deleted`, and (conditionally) `Recovered`. Note iOS 26.1 reshuffled Utilities ordering — `Recently Deleted`'s default position moved near the top — so do not hard-code positions.

#### `Duplicates` and Merge
Apple: "The Photos app identifies duplicate photos and videos in your photo library in the Duplicates collection." Merge: "Tap `Merge` to combine a set of duplicates, then tap `Merge [number] Items`." Merging keeps the highest quality and relevant data, saving space. **"If you don't have any duplicate photos or videos in your library, the Duplicates collection doesn't appear."** Feature has existed since iOS 16.

Apple documents **no** matching criteria and **no** thresholds — it is a black box with no tuning, no manual pairing, and no control over which copy survives a merge.

#### `Hidden`
Path: `Collections` → `Utilities` → tap the `Hidden` collection (below Utilities) → `View Album` → unlock your iPhone (Face ID / Touch ID / passcode).
- Hide: open the photo → More button → `Hide`. Apple: "Hidden photos are moved to the Hidden collection. You can't view them anywhere else." Hidden assets are excluded from Library, Memories, Search, and widgets.
- Unhide (Apple documents only a **single-item** flow): "Tap the photo or video you want to stop hiding. Tap [the More button], then tap `Unhide`." A Select-based bulk unhide is *not documented* on that page.
- Two independent settings, both at `Settings` > `Apps` > `Photos`: (1) the lock — `Use Face ID` / `Use Touch ID` / `Use Passcode`, **on by default since iOS 16**; turning it off makes Hidden and Recently Deleted open without auth. (2) visibility — `Show Hidden Album`; turn off to remove the Hidden collection from the Photos app entirely (available since iOS 14).
- With iCloud Photos, hiding on one device hides on all.

⚠️ **Trap: locked Hidden media is silently omitted from export.** Apple, on the import/export page: "Photos and videos in the Hidden album won't be transferred if the album is locked. To unlock the Hidden album, go to Settings > Apps > Photos, then turn off Use Face ID, Use Touch ID, or Use Passcode." Any migration/export/backup feature you build will silently drop hidden media unless you surface this to the user.

Hidden is **not real privacy**: it is a locked view within the same library, still counted in storage, still synced to iCloud, recoverable by anyone with the device passcode.

#### `Recently Deleted`
Path: `Collections` → `Utilities` → `Recently Deleted` → `View Album` → unlock. Apple: **"Deleted photos and videos are kept in the Recently Deleted collection for 30 days before being permanently removed from all devices."** Flow: `Select` → items → More button → `Recover` or `Delete`. "Recently Deleted and Hidden collections are locked by default."

The 30-day tombstone syncs across all devices on the same Apple Account with iCloud Photos.

⚠️ **Trap (an earlier claim REFUTED): there is no verified "only the contributor can delete from Recently Deleted" rule for Shared Libraries.** That sentence could not be found in Apple's iOS 26 guide or the iCloud Shared Photo Library articles. What Apple *does* document is different: "You receive notifications if content you added to the shared library is deleted… If content you added is deleted, you can move it from Recently Deleted back to your personal library within 30 days." Ship the documented rule, not the invented one.

#### `Recovered`
Path: `Collections` → `Utilities` → `Recovered`, unlocked with Face ID / Touch ID / Optic ID. Apple: "This album displays images and videos that are on your device but not currently part of your library. Photos or videos can become lost due to several reasons, including a database corruption issue, photos taken in a camera app that did not save correctly to the Photos library, **or third-party apps that are given access to manage your photo library**."

Per-item actions: `Permanently Delete` or `Restore to Library`.

Two sharp edges, both verbatim from Apple:
1. "When you delete a photo or video from the Recovered album, it does not appear in your Recently Deleted album. **It is deleted immediately and the action cannot be undone.**"
2. "The Recovered album only appears if your iPhone, iPad, Mac, or Vision Pro finds photos or videos that are on your device but not part of your Library."

Availability: iOS 18 / iPadOS 18 / macOS Sequoia 15.1 / visionOS 2.4 and later — so present in iOS 26.

⚠️ **Trap, and it is aimed directly at us:** Apple explicitly names *"third-party apps that are given access to manage your photo library"* as a cause of orphaned assets. A competing app that writes to the library and mishandles asset lifecycle will land its users in the `Recovered` album — and Apple's own support page will tell them a third-party app did it. Asset-lifecycle correctness is a reputational requirement, not just a bug class. (When the `Recovered` album appeared abruptly on the iOS 18 upgrade, surfacing long-forgotten photos, it produced a well-publicized privacy scare.)

#### `Imports`
`Collections` → `Utilities` → `Imports` — items brought in from a camera, SD card, external drive, or another iOS device.
- **Import:** connect via Lightning/USB-C adapter or card reader → Photos → `Import` → `Import All`, or select items → `Import` → `Import Selected` → choose an import destination.
- **Export:** select items → Share button → `Export Unmodified Original` → tap your storage device (below `Locations`) → `Save`.

⚠️ **Trap: `Export Unmodified Original` exports the ORIGINAL, not what you see.** Apple: "For photos and videos that have been edited, the unmodified original version will be exported." There is no first-class way to export the *edited rendition* to external storage from this flow. This surprises users constantly.

---

### 6.9 Pinned Collections

A user-curated row of shortcuts under a `Pinned` heading at the top of the `Collections` tab. This is one of the headline iOS 26 Photos navigation additions — and it exists precisely because the iOS 18 redesign buried everything.

Apple verbatim: **"By default, Pinned Collections includes `Favorites`, `Recently Saved`, `Map`, `Videos`, and `Screenshots`."**

| Action | Flow |
|---|---|
| Open the editor | `Collections` → tap `Pinned`, then tap `Edit` (support article), **or** tap `Edit` to the right of the `Pinned` heading (user guide) — both entry points are real |
| Pin | Tap a suggested collection, "or scroll down and tap `Any Collection or Album` to see more options" |
| Remove | Tap the remove button, then `Delete` |
| Reorder | Touch and hold, then drag |
| Quick pin/unpin | "To quickly add a collection to Pinned, touch and hold it, then tap `Pin`. To remove a collection from Pinned, touch and hold it, then tap `Unpin`." |

Glyph semantics in the picker (verbatim): "Collections with [the Remove button] next to them are currently in your pinned collections. Collections with [the Add button] next to them are not yet pinned."

Apple explicitly notes you can pin "any collection from your library, such as `Recently Deleted`, `Selfies`, `Receipts`, or your favorite custom albums." **The presence of `Receipts` is significant**: Apple's search-derived semantic categories are addressable as pinnable collections. That category browser is its own documented feature ("Find receipts, QR codes, recently edited photos, and more on iPhone"), and `Recently Saved` likewise has its own guide page.

Pinning is purely a navigation layer — it creates nothing and duplicates nothing.

**Third-party access: none.** Pinned Collections is Photos-app UI state with no PhotoKit representation. You cannot read what the user pinned, and you cannot pin anything.

---

### 6.10 Collections-tab layout, and library-level sort / filter / View Options

#### Collections tab: layout, reorder, collapse
Tap the **`Layout and Reorder` button** at the top of `Collections`. Its options are icon buttons — `Large Grid`, `Small Grid`, `Mixed Grid` — plus `Collapse All` (hide the collection tiles, showing names only) and `Reorder` (touch and drag a collection into a new position, then `Done`). `Reorder` is also reachable by scrolling to the bottom of the Collections tab.

- **Hide a single collection's image tiles:** "If you want to hide the image tiles for a single collection, tap [the Forward button]. Tap [the Forward button] to stop hiding them." ⚠️ **Trap: this is the Forward button, NOT a touch-and-hold gesture** — a widely repeated error.
- **Autoplay:** "By default, videos and Live Photos automatically play when you tap Collections. To turn autoplay off, tap your account in the top-right corner, then turn off `Auto-Play Motion and Loop Videos`."
- **Library scope selector** also lives here: `Both Libraries`, `Personal Library`, or `Shared Library` (see §6.14).

⚠️ **Trap: Apple's own docs disagree on this control's name.** The iPhone User Guide calls it the **`Layout and Reorder` button**; Apple support article 118229 calls the *same* control **"the More button"** for iOS 26. Both labels are in Apple's documentation. An implementer copying "the real vocabulary" will find two real vocabularies.

**Regression worth knowing:** iOS 18 let you *exclude* collection types from the Collections view entirely. iOS 26 removed that — per MacRumors, "You can still grab and drag to reorder, but there is no longer an option to exclude certain types of collections."

#### Library tab: sort, filter, View Options
All three hang off the **`Sort and Filter` button** (again: *not* the More button).

| Control | Options (Apple verbatim where quoted) |
|---|---|
| **Sort** | `Sort by Recently Added` — "Photos and videos you added most recently appear at the bottom of the library." • `Sort by Date Captured` — by capture date rather than add date |
| **Filter** | `Sort and Filter` → `Filter`. "display only particular items—such as `Videos`, `Favorites`, or **`Not in an Album`**". Also `Photos`, `Edited`. "You can apply multiple filters at the same time. For example, tap Photos and Edited to see only photos you've edited." Clear via `All Items`. |
| **View Options** | `Sort and Filter` → `View Options`. "Tap `Screenshots`, `From My Mac`, or `Shared with You` to hide these items in your library." (Persistent exclusions, unlike transient filters.) |

**`Not in an Album` is the single most useful organization primitive Apple ships** — and it is a transient filter buried three levels deep in a sheet, with no count badge, no persistent inbox, and no workflow attached. See §6.18.

---

### 6.11 Shared Albums (legacy iCloud Photo Sharing)

A **copy-based** photo stream dating to the iOS 6 era. Apple: "Shared Albums upload a copy of your data. Downloaded content may not contain the same information as the original." Shared-album content does **not** reference your library assets and is invisible to your own library organization.

**Enable:** `Settings` > `[your name]` > `iCloud` > `Photos` > turn on `Shared Albums`.

**Create — two documented paths:**
1. `Collections` → `Albums` → `Shared` → **+** → `Add Photos` / "Type a name in the `Shared Album Name` text field" / `Add Participants` → `Create`.
2. (Support article 108314) "In iOS 26 or later, tap `Collections`, then scroll down to `Shared Albums`… Tap `Shared Albums`. In iOS 26 or later tap [the Add button]. In iOS 18 and visionOS, tap `Create`."

**Push library items into a shared album (a distinct, documented path):** "From your Library or from within an album, tap `Select`… Tap [the Share button], then tap `Add to Shared Album`. Choose the album… Tap `Post`."

**Join:** tap the invite notification and `Accept`, or `Collections` → `Albums` → `Activity` → Accept.
**View:** `Collections` → `Shared Albums`. "Tap `Activity` to view updates to your shared albums, such as new photos and comments."
**Rename** (creator only): open album → More → tap the current album name → rename.
**Leave/delete:** More → "tap `Delete Shared Album` if you created the album, or tap `Unsubscribe` if you're a subscriber."

⚠️ **Trap (REFUTED claim): "Deleting a shared album permanently deletes all of its photos" is NOT an Apple sentence** — it could not be found in the iOS 26 guide. What Apple actually says leans the opposite way: "Photos that you saved or downloaded from a shared album to your photo library stay in your library even if the shared album is deleted, or the person who created the album stops sharing it." Do not put the scarier, unsourced warning in your UI copy.

#### Participants, permissions, Public Website
All of these live under: open the shared album → More button → **tap the album name**. (A non-obvious tap target.)

| Control | Exact label / behavior |
|---|---|
| Invite | `Add Participants` → name/email/phone |
| Remove | Tap the name → `Remove Subscriber` |
| Resend | Tap the name → `Resend Invitation` |
| Posting permission | `Participants Can Add Photos` toggle — turn off to make yourself the only poster. **Labeled `Subscribers Can Post` in iOS 17 and earlier.** |
| Notifications | `Notifications` toggle — stops alerts when subscribers like, comment, or add |
| Public link | Turn on `Public Website`, then tap `Share Link` to distribute an iCloud URL |

⚠️ **Trap: `Public Website` is an unauthenticated URL with no password and no expiry** (pre-iOS 27). Apple's own blunt warning: **"When Public Website is turned on, anyone with the URL can access the album."**

**Content rights (verbatim):** "Creators of a shared album can delete any photos, videos, or comments in the album. Participants can delete anything that they personally added."
- Delete a single item: "Tap a photo or video, tap **[the Delete button]**, then tap `Delete from Shared Album`." ⚠️ **This is the Delete (trash) button, not More** — and Apple's own two pages disagree on the confirmation label: the User Guide says `Delete from Shared Album`, support article 108314 renders it as `Delete Photo`.
- Delete a comment: "touch and hold it, then tap `Delete`."
- Save to your own library: "Tap `Share`, swipe up on the share menu, then tap `Save Image` or `Save Video`."

---

### 6.12 Shared Album hard limits and fidelity loss (exact numbers)

Every number below is verbatim-confirmed against Apple's "Shared Album limits" page (support.apple.com/en-us/108916).

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Max photos+videos from one contributor across ALL shared albums, per **hour** | **1,000** |
| Same, per **day** | **10,000** |
| Max shared albums an owner can **share** | **200** |
| Max shared albums a user can **subscribe to** | **200** |
| Max **subscribers per shared album** | **100** |
| Max combined photos+videos from all contributors in **one** shared album | **5,000** |
| Max comments per photo/video (a comment = a like or a text entry) | **200** |
| Max characters per comment | **1,024** |
| Max invites an owner may send per day | **200** |
| Sharing Suggestions | limited to **5,000 items**, max share size **1 GB** |
| GIF size | **≤ 100 MB** |

⚠️ **Trap: the "100 albums" figure that circulates widely is wrong.** The album caps are **200 owned / 200 subscribed**. **100 is the max *subscribers per album*.**

**Fidelity (verbatim):**
- "When shared, photos are reduced to **2048 pixels on the long edge**, except panoramic photos, which can be up to **5400 pixels wide**."
- "Videos can be up to **fifteen minutes** in length and are delivered at up to **720p** resolution."

**Formats:** images — HEIF, JPEG, RAW, PNG, GIF, TIFF. Video — HEVC, MP4, QuickTime, H.264, MPEG-4.

⚠️ **Trap: "Shared Albums have no Live Photo support" is FALSE.** Apple explicitly supports the special formats **slo-mo, time-lapse, Live Photos, and Memory videos**. What Shared Albums genuinely do **not** support: **"Shared Albums do not support spatial photo or video."** The real fidelity complaint is the 2048px/720p downscale, not format exclusion.

**Storage (iOS 26 and earlier):** "The photos and videos in your Shared Albums are kept in iCloud, but they **don't count against your iCloud storage limit**." (This appears to invert in iOS 27 — see §6.13.)

**Platform gaps:** you cannot upload HEIF, HEVC or RAW to Shared Albums on a **Windows PC**; TIFF is not supported on **iCloud.com**; you cannot upload RAW on iCloud.com. Also: "Not all features are available in all countries or regions."

**If you are only READING shared albums:** expect 2048px-max images, not originals.

---

### 6.13 iOS 27 — Shared Albums overhaul, keywords, star ratings ⚠️ **PRERELEASE / NOT SHIPPABLE TODAY**

iOS 27 is in **public beta as of July 13 2026** and ships ~fall 2026. Nothing here is available on a shipping iPhone. All of it may change or be pulled.

**Apple Newsroom, WWDC 2026 (verbatim):** "iCloud Shared Albums add **full-resolution sharing**, support for more file types, **emoji reactions**, updated activity feeds with the ability to see **activity per album**, and new **temporary albums** that allow users to collaborate on short-term projects **without taking up space in their iCloud**. **Anyone, including users without an Apple device, can join and contribute photos to albums on the web**, making preserving group memories easier than ever."

apple.com/os/ios adds: "It's easier for friends and family on Android or Windows to join and contribute their own photos on iCloud.com. Shared Albums also adds support for full-resolution sharing and new ways to filter and react to photos and invite others to share an album."

Press-sourced detail (MacRumors 2026-06-08/11, 9to5Mac 2026-06-16, iDownloadBlog 2026-07-06) — **press, not Apple primary**:
- Shared Albums can be **filtered by photos or videos**
- A dedicated `Create Shared Album` option appears in any album's menu
- You can create an **upload link with permission controls**
- Albums can be set to **expire after 30 days** (the "temporary albums")
- **Per-album recent activity log**
- **React with any emoji** (six presets plus a plus button for more)
- Easier saving out of shared albums

**iOS 27 also adds keywords and star ratings** (press-sourced, no Apple primary located): an `Add Keywords` option that appears when you scroll up on a photo, near the existing caption field, plus **1-to-5 star ratings** with the ability to **filter by rating**. Treat the exact UI wording as press-sourced/prerelease.

⚠️ **Trap: the iCloud storage rule appears to INVERT in iOS 27, and Apple has not said so outright.** Apple's own framing — temporary albums let you collaborate "without taking up space in their iCloud" — strongly implies that permanent full-resolution shared albums **now DO consume the owner's iCloud quota**, reversing the longstanding "don't count against your iCloud storage limit" rule. Tech press (Ubergizmo, June 2026) states this outright. But Apple's live support page 108916 still says the opposite for iOS 26, and **no explicit Apple sentence confirming the reversal was found**. Treat the inversion as highly likely but **not Apple-confirmed** — and if you are modeling Apple's sharing economics competitively, model both branches.

⚠️ **STRATEGIC TRAP — read this before you plan a sharing product.** iOS 27 removes the two biggest Apple weaknesses a competing sharing product would have targeted: **the 2048px downscale** and **Apple-only participation**. A differentiation thesis built on "we share at full resolution" or "we let Android users join" has roughly a three-month shelf life. Differentiate on **organization and intelligence**, not on sharing fidelity.

**Third-party API in iOS 27: UNVERIFIED.** No evidence was found that PhotoKit gains shared-album write access, or any keyword/rating write API, in iOS 27. **Assume shared albums remain read-only to third parties, and assume no keyword/rating API, until proven otherwise** against the iOS 27 PhotoKit release notes.

---

### 6.14 iCloud Shared Photo Library

A **separate, second library** — not an album, and a completely different mechanism from Shared Albums. Available since iOS 16.1; current in iOS 26.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Participants | "A shared library can include **up to six participants including the organizer**; you can belong to **one shared library at a time**." |
| Requires | iCloud Photos on: `Settings` > `[your name]` > `iCloud` > `Photos` > `Sync this iPhone`. **"You don't need Family Sharing turned on to set up a shared library."** |
| Minimum OS | **iOS 16.1 / iPadOS 16.1 / macOS 13 or later.** "Photos and videos added to a shared library won't be available on devices with earlier versions." |
| Under-13 users | Can only join/create with Family Sharing members. "Age varies by country or region." |
| Fidelity | Full-fidelity originals. **Content MOVES** out of the personal library — it is not copied and not downscaled. |
| Storage | **"All content added to a shared library counts toward the iCloud storage space of the library organizer."** Participants get access free. |
| Rights | All participants can add, edit, and delete everything. |

**Setup:** `Photos` → `Collections` → tap your account (top-right) → `Shared Library` → follow the onscreen steps. (Also at `Settings` > `Apps` > `Photos` > `Shared Library`.) Add participants later: `Collections` → account → `Manage` → `Add Participants`.

**Rules-based auto-add at setup:** the setup flow offers `All My Photos and Videos`, `Choose by People or Date` (face recognition on selected people, and/or a start date), or `Choose Manually`. ⚠️ **These three exact labels are sourced from Apple's Photos guide for *Mac*, not the iOS guide** — the iOS guide only says "follow the onscreen instructions." They are almost certainly identical on iOS, but the iOS primary source does not confirm them.

⚠️ **Trap: `All My Photos and Videos` silently excludes three classes.** Choosing it does **NOT** move **screenshots, screen recordings, or hidden items** into the Shared Library. Anyone reimplementing bulk migration will be surprised.

#### Moving content, library switching, Camera

| Feature | Exact behavior |
|---|---|
| Move | Select photo(s) → More button → `Move to Shared Library` (or `Move to Personal Library` to bring it back). Apple: "After content is moved to the shared library, it's no longer in your personal library." |
| Suggestions | `Collections` → account → `For Your Shared Library` shows candidate content. Toggle: `Shared Library Suggestions`. (An "Add People" control extending suggestions to non-members is *unverified* — no Apple source found for that label.) |
| Library switching (iOS 26) | Library tab → the **`Sort and Filter` button**; or `Collections` → the More button (per support article 118229) → choose `Both Libraries`, `Personal Library`, or `Shared Library` |
| Badge | Shared items carry a Shared Library badge in the thumbnail's top-right corner. Turn off via `Shared Library Indicator`. |
| Camera | After setup, a `Shared Library` button appears at the top of Camera to switch capture destination. **Default is the personal library.** `Settings` > `Apps` > `Photos` > `Shared Library` > `Sharing from Camera` offers `Share Automatically` (auto-adds when **Bluetooth** detects shared-library participants nearby — requires participants signed in and Bluetooth on) and `Share Manually`, plus a separate `Share When At Home` toggle. |
| Deletion | `Deletion Notifications` toggle. "If content you added is deleted, you can move it from Recently Deleted back to your personal library within 30 days." |

**Cross-surface contamination (architecturally important):** "Content in a shared library is also added to **everyone's memories, featured photos, and the Photos widget**." Shared-library content is injected into derived curation surfaces, not just the grid.

⚠️ **Trap: silent sync-halt when the organizer runs out of iCloud storage.** "If the library creator runs out of iCloud storage, you can no longer add content to the Shared Library. **Changes such as edits, favorites, and metadata adjustments no longer sync.**" A full organizer quota silently stops metadata sync for every participant.

#### Leaving and deleting — the 7-day rule
`Collections` → account → `Manage` → `Delete Shared Library` (organizer) or `Leave Shared Library` (participant).

Verbatim: **"When a shared library is deleted, participants who have been members of the shared library for more than 7 days can copy everything from the shared library into their own libraries. Participants who have been members for less than 7 days can copy only the content they contributed."** And: "When you leave a shared library, you can copy everything from the shared library into your own library, or just the content you contributed."

The 7-day tenure gate exists to stop a bad actor joining, grabbing everything, and leaving. But the consequence is nasty and poorly signposted: on the organizer's departure, members past 7 days automatically receive **everything** — potentially tens of thousands of assets dumped into their personal library, blowing up their iCloud quota.

---

### 6.15 Favorites, Duplicate, and Copy

**Favorites** is a system collection (heart), pinned by default in Pinned Collections, and doubles as a filter in both the library filter sheet ("Videos, Favorites, or Not in an Album") and per-album filters ("photos and videos you marked as favorites"). It is a **boolean flag on the asset**, not an album membership. PhotoKit: `PHAssetCollectionSubtype.smartAlbumFavorites`.

**`Favorites` is the ENTIRETY of Apple's cross-app-writable tagging vocabulary on iOS.** No colors, no labels, no stars (until iOS 27 — and even then API support is unconfirmed). If a competing app needs exactly one piece of state that round-trips into Apple Photos, this is it: `PHAsset.isFavorite` (read) / `PHAssetChangeRequest.isFavorite` (write).

**`Duplicate` (single asset):** open a photo/video → More button → `Duplicate`. "A duplicate copy appears next to the original in your library." Bulk copy: `Select` → thumbnails → More button → `Copy`.

⚠️ **Trap: naming collision.** `Duplicate` (More menu) deliberately **creates** a second asset. `Duplicates` (Utilities) **finds and merges** accidental ones. They are unrelated features with near-identical names, and the former directly feeds the latter's problem. Users duplicate to preserve an original before destructive edits — a workaround for the fact that Photos' non-destructive editing is *single-branch*: you cannot keep two edit variants of one asset.

---

### 6.16 What a third-party app can and cannot do

**The gating fact first.** Apple's PhotoKit documentation, verbatim, on running under `PHAuthorizationStatus.limited`:

> **"You can't create or fetch user albums.** If your app requires this functionality, you'll need to update its behavior and user interface appropriately when your app's authorization status is [limited]."

Limited access has been the default many users choose since iOS 14, and it **applies retroactively to already-shipped apps**: "The limited Photos library affects all apps that use PhotoKit in iOS 14, including those already published to the App Store." Under `.limited`, the entire album/collection layer is dark. Every album feature you build is gated behind convincing users to grant **full** library access.

⚠️ **Trap: `authorizationStatus()` and `requestAuthorization(_:)` LIE about limited access.** Apple: "The [`authorizationStatus()`] and [`requestAuthorization(_:)`] methods aren't compatible with the limited library and **return [authorized] when the user authorizes your app for limited access only**." You **must** use the `PHAccessLevel`-taking variants (`authorizationStatus(for:)`, `requestAuthorization(for:handler:)`). Code that uses the legacy methods will believe it has full access, then throw or silently fail on album operations.

⚠️ **Trap: `PHAssetCreationRequest` auto-enrolls its output.** "The system automatically adds assets that your app creates with a [`PHAssetCreationRequest`] to the user's limited library selection."

⚠️ **Trap: `PHPickerViewController` needs no permission at all — and gives you no album access.** It is the right tool if you only need to pick images. It is the wrong tool if you are building an organizer.

⚠️ **Trap: missing `Info.plist` keys CRASH the app.** `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription` for read/write (`NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription` if add-only). Apps linked on/after iOS 10 crash without it.

**Mandatory discipline for all writes** (verbatim from Apple):
> "Before creating a change request, use the [`canPerform(_:)`] method to verify that the collection allows the edit operation you're requesting. **If you attempt to perform an unsupported edit operation, Photos throws an exception.**"
> "If you create or use a change request object outside a photo library change block, **Photos raises an Objective-C exception**."

`PHCollectionEditOperation` exposes `.delete`, `.rename`, `.addContent`, `.removeContent`, `.deleteContent`, `.createContent`, `.rearrangeContent`.

⚠️ **Trap: Apple does not publish a per-subtype write-permission table.** The rule "`canPerform(.addContent)` returns false for `albumCloudShared` and for system smart albums" is inferred from Apple's general contract plus long-standing developer practice — **not** from an explicit Apple enumeration. Always call `canPerform(_:)`; never assume.

| Capability | Available to 3rd parties? | Mechanism / why not |
|---|---|---|
| Create a user album | **Yes — full access only** | `PHAssetCollectionChangeRequest.creationRequestForAssetCollection(withTitle:)` in a change block; use `placeholderForCreatedAssetCollection` to get the identifier. Resulting subtype: `PHAssetCollectionSubtype.albumRegular`. **Blocked under `.limited`.** |
| Rename / delete a user album | **Yes — full access only** | `PHAssetCollectionChangeRequest.title`; `deleteAssetCollections(_:)`. Guard with `canPerform(.rename)` / `.delete`. |
| Add / remove / insert / move / replace assets in an album | **Yes — full access only** | `addAssets(_:)`, `removeAssets(_:)`, `removeAssets(at:)`, `insertAssets(_:at:)`, `moveAssets(at:to:)`, `replaceAssets(at:withAssets:)`. A genuinely ordered-collection API — positional insert and reorder, not just append. |
| Read/write an album's **custom order** | **Yes (read + write)** | Assets fetched from an `albumRegular` collection come back in the user's order; write with `moveAssets(at:to:)` / `insertAssets(_:at:)`. |
| Create / rename / delete **folders**, manage children | **Yes — full access only** | `PHCollectionListChangeRequest.creationRequestForCollectionList(withTitle:)`, `deleteCollectionLists(_:)`, `title`; `addChildCollections(_:)`, `insertChildCollections(_:at:)`, `removeChildCollections(_:)`, `removeChildCollections(at:)`, `moveChildCollections(at:to:)`, `replaceChildCollections(at:withChildCollections:)`. Fetch via `PHCollectionList.fetchCollectionLists(with:subtype:options:)` and `PHCollection.fetchTopLevelUserCollections(with:)`. |
| Reorder top-level collections | **Yes** | `PHCollectionListChangeRequest.init(forTopLevelCollectionListUserCollections:)` + `moveChildCollections(at:to:)` |
| **Read** system Media Types / smart albums | **Yes** | `PHAssetCollection.fetchAssetCollections(with: .smartAlbum, subtype: <case>, options:)` returns the same collections the Photos app shows. **You get Apple's classification for free** — one of the most useful PhotoKit surfaces for a competitor. Also `PHAsset.mediaSubtypes` (`PHAssetMediaSubtype`) to classify yourself. |
| **Write** to system smart albums (Media Types) | **No** | Cannot add, remove, create, rename, or delete. `canPerform(_:)` reports unsupported; Photos throws if you try. |
| **Read** Shared Albums | **Yes, with a gotcha** | `PHAssetCollectionSubtype.albumCloudShared` ("An iCloud Shared Photo Stream"). ⚠️ **Trap: shared-album assets are EXCLUDED from default fetches.** You must set `PHFetchOptions.includeAssetSourceTypes` to include `.typeCloudShared`. A classic silent-empty-result bug. Expect 2048px images, not originals. |
| **Write** to Shared Albums (create, invite, post, comment, react) | **No** | Those collections do not vend write edit-operations. Not expected to change in iOS 27 (unverified). |
| Read/set the **key photo** (album cover) | **No** | No property, no change request on `PHAssetCollection`. |
| Read/set **Pinned Collections** | **No** | Photos-app UI state, no PhotoKit representation. |
| Read/set collection **order, collapse, grid size** | **No** | Photos-app UI state. |
| Read/set **filter/sort UI state** (library or per-album) | **No** | Reproducible independently, but not readable. `PHFetchOptions` supports `sortDescriptors` (`creationDate` vs `modificationDate`) and `NSPredicate` on `PHAsset` properties. |
| Reproduce **`Not in an Album`** | **Yes, but compute it yourself** | No direct predicate. Diff all assets against the union of album memberships. |
| Enumerate / recover / purge **Recently Deleted** | **No** | No PhotoKit API at all. `PHAssetChangeRequest.deleteAssets(_:)` *sends* assets there (with a system confirmation prompt each time) — that is the full extent of access. |
| Read Apple's **Duplicates** set or invoke **Merge** | **No** | No API. You must ship your own perceptual/hash duplicate detection over `PHAsset`. |
| Read the **Recovered** album | **No** | No API. |
| Read **Hidden** | **Nominally yes, practically no** | `PHAssetCollectionSubtype.smartAlbumAllHidden` is fetchable, but a **locked** Hidden album yields no assets (developers infer lock state from an empty fetch). Locked is the **default** since iOS 16. Treat Hidden as effectively unavailable. |
| Read **Imports** | **Yes** | `PHAssetCollectionSubtype.albumImported` ("An album imported from a camera or external storage"). |
| Read **My Photo Stream** | **Yes (read only)** | `PHAssetCollectionSubtype.albumMyPhotoStream`. Other non-smart subtypes: `albumRegular`, `albumSyncedEvent`, `albumSyncedFaces`, `albumSyncedAlbum`. |
| Manage **iCloud Shared Photo Library** (create/join/leave/move assets, read the badge, set Camera destination) | **No** | No dedicated public PhotoKit API. `PHFetchOptions.includeAssetSourceTypes` predates it and targets shared *streams* (`albumCloudShared`) and iTunes-synced content. **You cannot reliably distinguish shared-library membership** — a significant blind spot for any app whose users are on a Shared Library. |
| Write **keywords** or **star ratings** (iOS 27) | **Unverified — assume NO** | PhotoKit historically exposes no keyword/rating write API on iOS (macOS Photos has keywords). Whether iOS 27 opens a surface is **unknown**. Check the iOS 27 PhotoKit release notes before planning around it. |
| Write **`isFavorite`** | **Yes — fully** | `PHAsset.isFavorite` (read) / `PHAssetChangeRequest.isFavorite` (write). **The only user-facing organizational metadata a third party can freely write.** |
| Duplicate an asset | **Yes, but no one-call API** | Fetch the original's image data, write a new asset with `PHAssetCreationRequest`. |
| Build transient, in-memory collections for your own UI | **Yes** | `PHAssetCollection.transientAssetCollection(with:title:)`, `PHCollectionList.transientCollectionList(...)` — invisible to the Photos app. |
| Observe library changes | **Yes** | `PHPhotoLibraryChangeObserver`. Also use it to track limited-selection changes. |
| Suppress the once-per-launch limited-access prompt | **Yes** | `PHPhotoLibraryPreventAutomaticLimitedAccessAlert` in `Info.plist`; present the picker yourself with `presentLimitedLibraryPicker(from:)` (iOS 15+ has a callback variant returning the new local identifiers). |

**Design consequence:** an organization-centric app **must** detect `.limited` and either degrade gracefully (no album features at all) or run a well-argued upsell to full access. This is not a polish item; it is the shape of your entire onboarding funnel.

---

### 6.17 Where Apple is weak — our opening

- **No Smart Albums on iOS. At all.** This is the single largest structural gap in Apple Photos organization on iPhone. Apple's own primary docs admit Mac-created Smart Albums *silently vanish* on iPhone — a long-running, heavily-upvoted complaint on Apple's own discussion forums (e.g. threads 252116471, 252470117). Every album on iPhone is hand-curated. **A real, syncing, rule-based album engine on iPhone is the clearest wedge in this entire atlas.** ⚠️ But note the counter-risk: iOS 27 adds keywords and 1–5 star ratings — exactly the metadata a rules engine consumes. Apple may be building toward it. Move fast, and do not bet solely on "we have tags, Apple doesn't."
- **No "move between albums."** Two separate long-press/menu journeys (`Add to Album` in B, then `Remove from Album` in A) to accomplish one obvious operation. Trivial for us to fix.
- **`Not in an Album` is Apple's best organization primitive and it is buried three levels deep.** It is a *transient filter* inside a sheet — no persistent "unfiled" inbox, no count badge, no triage workflow, no way to act on it in bulk. This is a free, high-value feature for us: an unfiled-photo inbox with a count, computed by diffing all assets against the union of album memberships.
- **Duplicates is a black box that frequently doesn't work.** No tuning, no threshold, no manual pairing, no choice of which copy survives a merge. Widely reported: the `Duplicates` collection fails to appear or stays empty for days on large libraries after an upgrade or restore; detection is conservative and misses near-duplicates (burst-adjacent, re-saved, re-compressed copies). And Apple ships **no API** for it — so third-party cleaners already own this category. Our angle: aggressive perceptual detection with user-visible thresholds and explicit keep-this-one control.
- **Deleting doesn't free space for 30 days, and no third party can fix that.** `Recently Deleted` has no PhotoKit API — you cannot enumerate, recover, or purge it. Any "you freed 4 GB!" claim in a cleaner app is deferred by up to 30 days. This is a well-known source of user rage; be the app that explains it honestly and links the user into the trash.
- **Album cover changes are undocumented on iOS.** Apple documents key-photo selection only at creation. The post-hoc gesture is press-folklore. Covers for `Recents` and `Favorites` cannot be changed at all.
- **`Public Website` is a privacy footgun.** All-or-nothing, no password, no expiry (pre-iOS 27), "anyone with the URL can access the album."
- **iCloud Shared Photo Library is structurally fragile.** Exactly **one** shared library per person, ever. **Six** people, maximum. All-or-nothing **move** semantics — content leaves your personal library, which is why Apple maintains a support article titled "If you're missing photos or videos in the Photos app." The organizer bears **100%** of the storage cost, and when their quota fills, *everyone's* edits, favorites, and metadata **silently stop syncing**. The organizer leaving can dump the entire shared library into every member's personal library (the 7-day rule), blowing up their quotas.
- **Bluetooth-proximity auto-sharing from Camera (`Share Automatically`) is a privacy surprise** for many users — photos silently route to a shared library when a participant is physically nearby.
- **Apple's own UI vocabulary is inconsistent, and it costs users.** The same Collections control is the `Layout and Reorder` button in the iPhone User Guide and "the More button" in support article 118229. Shared-album single-item delete confirms as `Delete from Shared Album` in the guide and `Delete Photo` in article 108314. Bulk-add-to-album uses the **Share** button while single-add uses **More**. Rename is hidden behind `Edit Title and Photos`. A coherent, consistent verb set is a real, if unglamorous, differentiator.
- **iOS 26 regressed Collections customization:** iOS 18 let users *exclude* collection types entirely; iOS 26 only allows reorder and collapse. `Pinned` exists specifically as Apple's remedy for its own iOS 18 navigation regression.
- **Autoplay motion is on by default** in Collections (`Auto-Play Motion and Loop Videos`) — a persistent battery and attention complaint.
- **No first-class export of the EDITED rendition.** `Export Unmodified Original` does what it says; users expect their edits. And locked Hidden media is **silently omitted** from export with no warning at export time.
- **Non-destructive editing is single-branch.** You cannot keep two edit variants of one asset — users duplicate assets as a workaround, which feeds the duplicates problem Apple then fails to detect.
- **⚠️ The sharing wedge is closing.** iOS 27's full-resolution sharing and non-Apple web contribution neutralize the two classic third-party-sharing pitches by ~fall 2026. **Do not build the strategy there.** Build it on organization, rules, dedup, and unfiled-photo triage — where Apple ships nothing and exposes no API to anyone else either.
## 7. The Complete Editing Toolset

Apple Photos' editor is a **single-recipe, non-destructive, parameter-driven** editor — not a layer stack. You tap `Edit` in the top-right of an open asset, work in a bottom toolbar whose contents change depending on the asset type *and* the device model, and tap `Done`. Photos then stores the **original**, a **current (rendered) version**, and **exactly one opaque adjustment recipe** describing the most recent edit — and iCloud Photos syncs all three, which is what lets a user revert or resume an edit on a different device. The single most important thing an implementer must internalize: **there is no edit history and no layer list.** One recipe per asset, most-recent-edit-wins, and the recipe is app-private — so the moment a user touches Apple's editor on an asset your app edited, your recipe is destroyed and replaced with Apple's, and your layered work becomes an unrecoverable flattened pixel buffer.

Version baseline for this section: everything is **shipping iOS 26** (current public build iOS 26.5.2; iOS 26.6 in beta) unless explicitly marked **iOS 27 beta** (developer beta since 2026-06-08, public beta 2026-07-13, ships fall 2026).

---

### 7.1 Edit mode: entry, chrome, and the conditional bottom toolbar

Open a photo or video → tap `Edit` (top right). Top bar during editing: `Cancel` (top-left), `Done` (top-right), plus `Undo` and `Redo` buttons at the top of the screen. A `More` (…) button holds `Copy Edits`, `Paste Edits`, `Appearance`, and third-party editing extensions. Tapping `Cancel` on a dirty session prompts **`Discard Changes`**. Edits are staged in-session and committed on `Done`; Undo/Redo walk multiple steps *within the session only*.

**The bottom toolbar is conditional.** These permutations are all real — each is drawn from Apple's own iOS 26 User Guide screenshot alt-text, spread across several different pages (edit, crop, Live Photos, video, Portrait):

| Toolbar | Context (as documented) |
|---|---|
| `Styles`, `Portrait`, `Adjust`, `Crop`, `Clean Up` | Still photo, Photographic-Styles-capable iPhone with Styles on, portrait data present |
| `Portrait`, `Adjust`, `Filters`, `Crop`, `Clean Up` | Still photo with portrait data, no Styles |
| `Styles`, `Adjust`, `Crop`, `Clean Up` | Still photo, Styles, no portrait data |
| `Adjust`, `Filters`, `Crop`, `Clean Up` | Plain still photo |
| `Style`, `Portrait`, `Adjust`, `Filters`, `Crop`, `Clean Up` | **Six items — `Style` AND `Filters` coexisting** (Portrait page alt-text) |
| `Live`, `Adjust`, `Filters`, `Crop` | Live Photo — **no Clean Up** |
| `Video`, `Audio Mix`, `Adjust`, `Filters`, `Crop` | Video — **no Clean Up** |

⚠️ **Trap: do not implement a hard Styles-vs-Filters mutual exclusion.** Apple's Filters page says *"On iPhone 16 models or later, use Photographic Styles instead of filters to give your photos a customized look. Filter effects are available on these models if you haven't turned on Photographic Styles."* That reads like a swap, and secondary coverage treats it as one — but Apple's own iOS 26 Portrait-page alt-text shows a six-item toolbar containing **both** `Style` and `Filters`. Apple is *steering* users, not enforcing exclusivity. Verify on-device before you build an either/or toolbar.

⚠️ **Trap: Clean Up is photo-only.** It is absent from both the Live Photo and the video toolbars. Adjust, Filters and Crop all work on stills, Live Photos and video — the AI eraser does not.

**Two distinct compare gestures.** Apple documents both, and an implementer needs both:
1. **Tap the image** — *"You can tap the photo or video to compare the edited version to the original."*
2. **Tap the control button** — in `Adjust`: *"The outline around each button indicates the level of change for that setting. Tap the button to compare the edited version to the original."* In `Crop`: *"Tap the button to switch between the edited photo or video and the original."*

### 7.2 `Adjust` — the 16-item slider strip

Tap `Adjust`, then swipe left/right under the photo through a horizontal strip of controls; tap one and drag the slider for precise values. Apple's verbatim mechanic: *"Swipe left under the photo to view the settings you can adjust—for example, Exposure, Brilliance, or Highlights. Tap a setting, then drag the slider to make precise adjustments."* Each control's button carries a ring/outline whose fill *"indicates the level of change for that setting."*

The strip, in order — 1 auto + 15 sliders:

| # | Control | Apple's semantics (from Apple's Photos guide, same engine) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Auto` (accessibility label: **Enhance**) | Analyzes the image and applies "the correct mix of adjustments"; itself a slider, not a toggle |
| 2 | `Exposure` | |
| 3 | `Brilliance` | *"makes it look richer and more vibrant, brightening dark areas, pulling in highlights, and adding contrast to reveal hidden detail… color neutral (no saturation is applied)"* |
| 4 | `Highlights` | |
| 5 | `Shadows` | |
| 6 | `Contrast` | |
| 7 | `Brightness` | |
| 8 | `Black Point` | *"sets the point at which the darkest parts of the image become completely black without any detail"* |
| 9 | `Saturation` | |
| 10 | `Vibrance` | *"adjusts the color contrast and separation between similar colors"* |
| 11 | `Warmth` | |
| 12 | `Tint` | |
| 13 | `Sharpness` | |
| 14 | `Definition` | adjusts contrast to improve clarity of detail |
| 15 | `Noise Reduction` | |
| 16 | `Vignette` | |

The same strip applies to **stills, Live Photos, and video**.

⚠️ **Trap: the ORDER is not Apple-sourced.** Apple's iPhone User Guide never enumerates the strip — it only names "Exposure, Brilliance, or Highlights" as examples, and confirms Brilliance via alt-text. The 16-item sequence above was independently reproduced by two sources that agree exactly (including the counterintuitive Contrast-before-Brightness), and the verifier reproduced it a third time. One outlier source (TapSmart) gives a different internal order and claims 17 sliders. Confidence in the *set* is high; confidence in the *order* is ~85%. **Device-verify before building UI against it.**

⚠️ **Trap: `AUTO` vs `Enhance`.** Apple's screenshot alt-text calls the magic-wand control *"the Enhance button"* (that is the accessibility label); the visible on-screen string in the strip is reported as `AUTO`. No Apple page shows the visible string — treat `AUTO` as likely-correct but unverified.

**Auto / Enhance in detail.** Apple's tip: *"Tap [the Enhance button] to automatically enhance the light and color."* It is a slider — you dial the strength of the auto-correction up and down. Applying it populates several of the underlying sliders, but Photos never shows you *which* ones it moved. Works on photos and video.

### 7.3 `Filters`
