Tap `Filters`, swipe the thumbnail row, tap one, then drag the slider to adjust intensity. Apple: *"Tap [the Filters button] to apply filter effects such as Vivid or Dramatic. To remove a filter that was applied when you took the photo, tap Original."* Filters set in the **Camera** app carry into Photos and can be changed or removed there — non-destructively.

**The 10-item roster (9 looks + Original):** `Original`, `Vivid`, `Vivid Warm`, `Vivid Cool`, `Dramatic`, `Dramatic Warm`, `Dramatic Cool`, `Mono`, `Silvertone`, `Noir`. Each has a single intensity slider.

*Sourcing note:* Apple never enumerates all ten. Apple names `Vivid`, `Dramatic` and `Original` in prose, and Apple's own alt-text names `Dramatic Warm` (*"Dramatic Warm is selected and there is a slider to adjust the intensity of the filter"*). The full ten-name roster comes from secondary sources — treat the four Apple-attested names as certain and the rest as high-confidence-secondary.

Filters apply to **video and Live Photos** as well as stills. There are no user-created filters, no importable LUTs, and no per-filter parameter editing beyond the one intensity slider.

### 7.4 Photographic Styles — two generations, and they behave completely differently

This is the single hardest thing in the editing surface to get right, because Apple ships **two separate model lists** for what looks like one feature.

#### Latest generation (post-capture re-editable) — the interactive pad

`Edit` → `Styles` → swipe left/right through the style choices below the image, **or** tap the **Styles Chooser** to open a 2-D **pad**. Apple, verbatim: *"drag your finger on the square to simultaneously adjust the tone and color. Drag your finger left or right on the slider below to adjust the intensity level."* And: *"As you make adjustments, the values for tone, color, and intensity are shown at the top of the screen. Tap [Reset] to reset these values."* So: X/Y pad (color × tone) + a separate intensity slider + a numeric readout of **tone, color, intensity** + a `Reset` button.

The defining property: on these models the style is **fully re-editable and removable after capture** — the first time Apple has allowed that. This is not a global LUT; Apple says styles *"intelligently adjust specific colors in different parts of your photos"*, i.e. the capture pipeline preserves per-region/semantic data so the style can be recomputed later.

**Models that support latest generation Photographic Styles** (Apple's exact aside list): iPhone 16, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max, iPhone 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, iPhone Air.

⚠️ **Trap: iPhone 16e and iPhone 17e are NOT on that list**, even though they *are* on the general Photographic Styles list. If you gate features by "chip generation" or "16 and later", you will be wrong. Use Apple's per-feature aside pages.

⚠️ **Trap: hard HEIF requirement, invisible until it bites.** Apple, verbatim: *"To edit Photographic Styles in the Photos app, Camera needs to capture photos with High Efficiency image capture. To turn on High Efficiency, go to Settings > Camera > Formats, then tap High Efficiency."* A user who set `Most Compatible` (JPEG) silently loses post-capture Style editing entirely, with no explanation in the UI.

*Style names — **UNVERIFIED**.* Widely reported as five skin-tone/undertone styles (Cool Rose, Neutral, Rose Gold, Gold, Amber) plus ten mood styles (Standard, Vibrant, Natural, Luminous, Dramatic, Quiet, Cozy, Ethereal, Muted Black and White, Stark Black and White). Only `Dramatic` is corroborated by Apple's own alt-text; the rest appear on no reachable Apple page. **Treat the roster as unsourced and device-verify.**

#### Previous generation (capture-time only, irreversible)

On the older models the style is chosen in **Camera** and tuned with **`Tone`** and **`Warmth`** sliders at capture time — Apple: *"Drag the Tone and Warmth sliders to control how strongly the style affects your photos."* The presets are Standard plus Rich Contrast, Vibrant, Warm, Cool. The style is **baked into the capture pipeline and cannot be edited or removed in Photos afterward.** Reset/remove for future captures only: `Settings` > `Camera` > `Photographic Styles` > `Use Standard`.

**Models that support Photographic Styles** (Apple's exact aside list, both generations combined): iPhone SE (3rd generation), iPhone 13 mini, 13, 13 Pro, 13 Pro Max, iPhone 14, 14 Plus, 14 Pro, 14 Pro Max, iPhone 15, 15 Plus, 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, iPhone 16, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max, **iPhone 16e**, iPhone 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, iPhone Air, **iPhone 17e**.

⚠️ **Trap for the user, opportunity for us:** a user who shot 2,000 photos in `Vibrant` on an iPhone 14 **cannot undo it, ever.** The style is in the pixels. A de-styling / neutralizing tool is a concrete, sizeable opening — though doing it well is genuinely hard.

Styles are **stills-only**. No video.

### 7.5 `Crop` — aspect ratio, rotate, flip, and geometry

All verbatim Apple:

| Operation | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Manual crop | *"Drag the rectangle corners to enclose the area you want to keep in the image, or pinch open or closed."* |
| Aspect lock | *"When you drag a corner, the crop tool keeps the original aspect ratio of the photo. To change the aspect ratio, tap the lock at the top-right corner of the photo to unlock the aspect ratio."* **Aspect is preserved by default** — this surprises people. |
| Preset ratios | Tap the **`Aspect Ratio Freeform`** button, *"then choose an option such as Square, Wallpaper, 9:16, or 5:7."* |
| Rotate | *"Tap [Rotate] to rotate the image 90 degrees."* |
| Flip | *"Tap [Flip] to flip the image horizontally."* |
| Viewer shortcut | *"To quickly crop a photo while you're viewing it, pinch the photo to zoom in. When the photo appears as you want it cropped, tap Crop in the top-right corner of the screen."* |

Crop, rotate, flip and the geometry sliders **all work on video** as well as stills.

⚠️ **Trap: the full aspect-ratio list is unsourced.** Apple names only four presets and says *"choose an option such as…"*, implying more. The commonly-cited full set (Original, Freeform, Square, Wallpaper, 9:16, 8:10, 5:7, 3:4, 3:5, 2:3, 16:9, plus a portrait/landscape orientation toggle) is **not** Apple-sourced. Device-verify.

**Geometry sliders.** Inside the crop tool: *"Swipe left under the photo to view editing options. Tap the effect you want to edit, then drag the slider to make precise adjustments."* Apple's alt-text calls these *"a slider to adjust the geometry enhancements"*, and *"The level of adjustment you make is displayed by the slider"* (a slider readout, not a separate numeric field). The three controls are widely reported as **Straighten** (rotation), **Vertical** (vertical keystone) and **Horizontal** (horizontal keystone) — ⚠️ **but Apple's iPhone page never names them.** Very likely correct; not Apple-sourced.

⚠️ **Trap: there is no documented `Auto` button inside the Crop tool.** The researcher's "Auto auto-straighten / level-correct" claim is **UNVERIFIED** — it appears nowhere in Apple's iOS 26 crop documentation, and the sources describing it are ambiguous between Mac Photos and older iOS versions (there is even an Apple Community thread titled *"14.3 photo editing - auto straighten gone"*). **Do not build against it.**

### 7.6 `Markup` — the annotation layer

`Edit` → `Markup` → `Add`. Apple: *"Tap [Edit], then tap [Markup]. Tap [Add] to add text, shapes, and more."* / *"Tap [the Add Annotations button] to add stickers, captions, text, shapes, or even your signature."*

**The iOS 26 iPhone Markup palette, exhaustively** (from Apple's alt-text, left to right): **`Pen`, `Mono line`, `Marker`, `Eraser`, `Lasso`, `Ruler`, `Pencil`** — followed by the **`Color Picker`** button and the **`Add`** button.

⚠️ **Trap: there is no Reed pen in iPhone Photos Markup.** The Reed pen (calligraphy pen with stroke-angle presets) is an **iPadOS 26 / Apple Pencil** feature. It does not appear in the iOS 26 iPhone Markup palette. Building it into an iPhone-parity feature list means building a phantom.

⚠️ **Trap: `Mono line` is a real, distinct tool** that most secondary write-ups omit entirely. Also note Apple's own vocabulary is inconsistent: the iOS 26 User Guide says **`Marker`**; an older Apple KB says "highlighter". Use `Marker`.

| Sub-feature | Detail |
|---|---|
| Eraser modes | Two, and they are semantically different: *"Tap the eraser tool again, then choose Pixel Eraser or Object Eraser."* Object-erase removes a whole stroke as an object; pixel-erase is raster. |
| Color picker modes | Three: *"tap Grid, Spectrum, or Sliders."* |
| Redo | **Shake the device to Redo.** |
| Loupe / magnifier | An **`Add` menu item** (`Add Loupe`), not a palette tool: *"Drag the loupe around, use the blue dot to adjust the size, and the green dot to increase or decrease the magnification level."* (Claims that its outline thickness and color are adjustable are unsourced.) |
| Shape snapping | Draw a shape in one stroke and pause, and it snaps. Apple's exact roster: *"straight lines, arrows, arcs, continuous lines with 90-degree turns, squares, circles, rectangles, triangles, pentagons, chat bubbles, hearts, stars, and clouds."* |
| Text | Font, size, justification, style, color. |
| Shapes | Border color, border width, fill color, opacity. *"Use the green dots to adjust the arrow's curve and the speech bubble's appearance."* |
| `Description` | Adds a custom image description that **VoiceOver reads** — an accessibility feature, from the `Add` menu. |

Markup content is **flattened into the rendered edit** on `Done`. It is part of the revertible stack (`Revert to Original` removes it), but individual annotations are **not re-editable objects** once you commit and reopen.

### 7.7 `Clean Up` — Apple Intelligence object removal (shipping, iOS 26)

`Edit` → `Clean Up`. Apple, verbatim: *"After you tap Clean Up, some items may be highlighted automatically so you can quickly tap to remove them."* / *"Tap, brush, or circle what you want to remove. Use two fingers to pinch to zoom or pan the image."* On-device generative inpainting. Removals go onto the non-destructive stack and are undoable and revertible.

⚠️ **Apple's own most damning line, verbatim from its docs:** *"If you brush over a person's face, the face may become blurred with a pixelated effect."* Apple ships a warning that its AI eraser mangles faces.

**Provenance:** photos edited with Clean Up get **`Modified with Clean Up` written into the EXIF `Credits` field** (since iOS 18.1) — visible by swiping up to the Info panel. The label survives iMessage and AirDrop but is stripped by most third-party/social apps.

**Device gating** (Apple's dedicated requirements KB, word for word):

| Requirement | Value |
|---|---|
| iPhone | **iPhone 16 models, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max** — nothing below 15 Pro |
| Other | Any iPad with A17 Pro or M1 and later; Mac with M1 or later |
| Minimum OS | iOS 18.1 / iPadOS 18.1 / macOS Sequoia 15.1 |
| EU | Historically required iOS 18.4+ |
| China mainland | Does not work on devices purchased in China mainland; and does not work for devices bought elsewhere if you are **in** China mainland **and** your Apple Account region is China mainland |
| Languages (Apple Intelligence beta list) | English, Danish, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Vietnamese, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Japanese, Korean |
| Apple's caveat | *"Clean Up is not available in all languages or regions."* |

⚠️ **Staleness trap:** as of **iOS 26.1**, Apple now says Apple Intelligence *"features are available in most regions around the world"*. The EU iOS 18.4 carve-out is **historical, not a current restriction**. Don't ship a geo-gate based on the 18.x-era docs.

**Documented failure modes** (Apple docs + Apple Community threads): faces pixelate rather than disappear; it works on background clutter but fails at simple retouching (a blemish, a pimple); **it does not work on RAW/ProRAW files** — on Mac it *replaced* the old `Retouch` tool, which did work on RAW and on faces, and users are vocally angry about the regression; results degrade badly near frame edges where it lacks context on one side; and the device/region/language matrix generates a steady stream of "Clean Up not visible / not working" confusion.

### 7.8 iOS 27 BETA — the new generative editing layer (Clean Up v2, Extend, Reframe) ⚠️ NOT SHIPPING

**Do not build against this as if it ships today.** iOS 27 entered developer beta 2026-06-08, public beta 2026-07-13, and ships fall 2026. Three tools, all quotes verbatim from Apple Newsroom (June 2026):

1. **Clean Up (upgraded)** — *"the popular Clean Up tool gets a major upgrade, so users can remove distractions with better quality and more realistic infill, even when the scene is complex."* It reconstructs backgrounds generatively rather than patching small simple areas.
2. **Extend** (outpainting) — *"users can expand their images to give their subjects more breathing room… straighten a crooked horizon without cropping out anything important, or adjust the aspect ratio, and Extend will fill in the missing pieces."* iOS 27 also uses Extend automatically to expand Lock Screen wallpapers that don't fit the display.
3. **Spatial Reframing** (UI label reported as `Reframe`) — *"Spatial Reframing builds on Apple's deep understanding of spatial models thanks to Apple Vision Pro, so users can touch and drag a photo and preview in real time how the perspective shifts — as if they'd repositioned the camera in the original scene. Using powerful image models, Spatial Reframing will only generate new content where the perspective has been shifted, ensuring the reframed photo stays consistent with the original scene."*

**CRITICAL PROVENANCE CHANGE:** *"Photos adjusted with Apple Intelligence will automatically include a hidden **SynthID** watermark to identify those that have been edited with AI."* This is in addition to, and distinct from, the existing visible `Modified with Clean Up` EXIF Credits string. *(Scope is inference: Apple does not state whether SynthID covers only AI edits or all edits. Read as AI-edits-only — unverified.)*

**iOS 27 Apple Intelligence device list** (Apple's, exact): iPhone 16 models or later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, iPad mini (A17 Pro), iPad models with M1 or later, **MacBook Neo (A18 Pro)**, Mac models with M1 or later, Apple Vision Pro, Apple Watch Series 9 or later.

⚠️ **Traps in this whole block:**
- The **`Tools` entry point** (three-sliders icon → Apple Intelligence icon labeled `Tools`) is **UNVERIFIED beta UI** from hands-on press, not Apple documentation. It can change before fall.
- Of the three Clean Up removal options, **only `High Quality` is corroborated**. `Fast` and `Auto` as literal UI labels are **UNVERIFIED**; press describes it as: the user can manually select High Quality, or it triggers automatically for complex edits.
- **Where these models run is unknown.** Apple explicitly says the new *Image Playground* photorealistic model runs on **Private Cloud Compute**. Apple does **not** state the on-device/PCC split for Photos' Clean Up v2 / Extend / Reframe. A "High Quality vs Fast" toggle suggests a hybrid, but this is not sourced — and it matters enormously for a privacy-positioned competitor. Test it on the beta.
- Reframe likely depends on **capture-time spatial/depth data** and will therefore degrade or be unavailable on imported photos, screenshots, and older captures. Unconfirmed but strongly implied.

### 7.9 Live Photo editing

`Edit` → `Live`. Toolbar: `Live`, `Adjust`, `Filters`, `Crop`. Four operations, all verbatim:

| Operation | Apple's instruction |
|---|---|
| Set a key photo | *"Move the white frame on the frame viewer, tap Make Key Photo, then tap Done."* |
| Trim | *"Drag either end of the frame viewer to choose the frames the Live Photo plays."* |
| Make a still | *"Tap the Live button at the top of the screen to turn off the Live feature. The Live Photo becomes a still of its key photo."* |
| Mute | *"Tap [the Mute button] at the top of the screen. Tap it again to unmute."* |

Separately, from the **viewer** (not the editor), tap `Live` in the **top-left corner** to choose an effect: `Live` (normal), `Loop` (*"Repeats the action in a continuous looping video"*), `Bounce` (*"Rewinds the action backward and forward"*), `Long Exposure` (*"Simulates a DSLR-like long exposure effect by blurring motion"*), `Live Off`, and — when applicable — `Portrait` / `Portrait off`. `More` (…) → **`Save as Video`** converts a Live Photo into a shareable video file.

⚠️ **Trap: two destructive/exclusive interactions Apple states outright.**
- *"Live Photos taken on an iPhone 15 model or later with a portrait effect **lose the portrait effect if you change the key photo**."* Changing the key frame silently destroys the portrait rendering.
- *"When the portrait effect is applied to a Live Photo taken in Photo mode, **the Live Photo effects aren't available**."* Portrait **or** liveness — not both.

### 7.10 Video editing — trim, speed, slo-mo ramp, Audio Mix

Toolbar: `Video`, `Audio Mix`, `Adjust`, `Filters`, `Crop`. **The full 16-item Adjust strip, all Filters, and Crop/rotate/flip/geometry all work on video.**

**Trim:** *"Drag either end of the frame viewer below the video to adjust the start and stop times, then tap Done"*, then choose **`Save Video`** (overwrite in place) or **`Save Video as New Clip`** (keeps both).

⚠️ **Trap — the hole in the non-destructive guarantee.** Apple, verbatim: **_"A video saved as a new clip can't be reverted to the original."_** Save-as-New-Clip permanently breaks the revert path. If you copy Apple's non-destructive model wholesale, you will copy this bug too. The photo-side counterpart is the `Duplicate` command — Photos has no "keep both versions" story for stills inside the edit stack itself.

**Playback speed:** `Edit` → `Video` → the **`Playback Speed`** button → pick a speed. Apple: *"The playback options available depend on the format of the video you captured. The larger the format you capture, the more options are available"* — high-frame-rate captures yield more slow-down options.

**Slo-mo ramp:** for videos shot in Slo-mo mode, *"Drag the black vertical bars beneath the frame viewer to set where the video is played in slow motion"* — the slow section's in/out points are set **independently of the trim**.

**`Audio Mix`** — four modes with Apple's exact descriptions, plus *"Drag the slider below the mix options to increase or decrease the effect and background noise levels."*

| Mode | Apple's description |
|---|---|
| `Standard` | *"Play the original audio you recorded"* |
| `In-Frame` | *"Reduce sounds and voices from sources not visible in the video frame"* |
| `Studio` | *"Reduce background sounds and reverb, to make it sound more like you're recording in a professional studio"* |
| `Cinematic` | *"Put all the voices onto a front-facing track and leave environmental noises in surround, like the audio in movies"* |

Audio Mix requires the video to have been recorded with **Spatial Audio** on a supporting model (capture options: Spatial Audio, Studio, Mono). **Models that record Spatial Audio** (Apple's aside): iPhone 16, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max, **iPhone 16e**, 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, iPhone Air, iPhone 17e.

⚠️ **Trap: the "e" models are NOT uniformly excluded.** iPhone 16e is *excluded* from latest-gen Photographic Styles and from portrait-capture-in-Photo-mode, but *included* in Spatial Audio / Audio Mix. Any device-gating table must be **per-feature**, never tiered by "e = lesser".

Missing entirely from Photos' video editor: multi-segment cutting, splitting, reordering, joining clips (that's iMovie's job), audio ducking/keyframes, music tracks, titles, transitions, scopes/waveform, and any export bitrate/codec control.

### 7.11 Portrait mode editing

`Edit` → `Portrait`. Five capabilities:

1. **Depth Control (the f-stop slider).** *"Drag the Depth Control slider at the bottom of the screen to increase or decrease the background blur effect. **A black dot marks the original depth value for the photo**."* (Apple's alt-text calls the same control *"the Depth Adjustment setting"* — both labels exist in Apple's docs.)
2. **Portrait Lighting.** Tap the Lighting button at the top; *"Touch [the Portrait Lighting control], then slide your finger left or right to choose a lighting effect"*, then *"Drag the slider below the lighting effects left or right to adjust the intensity."* Six effects, Apple's exact descriptions:

   | Effect | Apple's description |
   |---|---|
   | `Natural Light` | *"The face is in sharp focus against a blurred background"* |
   | `Studio Light` | *"The face is brightly lit, and the photo has an overall clean look"* |
   | `Contour Light` | *"The face has dramatic shadows with highlights and lowlights"* |
   | `Stage Light` | *"The face is spotlit against a deep black background"* |
   | `Stage Light Mono` | *"like Stage Light, but the photo is in classic black and white"* |
   | `High-Key Light Mono` | *"creates a grayscale subject on a white background"* |

3. **Change the focus point.** *"Tap a new subject or focus point in the photo… the background blur automatically adjusts so the new subject appears sharp and in focus."* Available on **iPhone 13 or later**. ⚠️ Apple's own caveat: *"Make sure that the new subject isn't blurred or too far in the distance"* — i.e. focus-point retargeting frequently just fails.
4. **Apply portrait AFTER capture to a Photo-mode shot.** *"photos with a person, dog, or cat taken in Photo mode can become portraits in the Photos app."* Select `Portrait` at the bottom, tap `Portrait` at the top to turn the effect on, then use the Lighting Intensity / Depth buttons. Works because iPhone 15 and later capture depth for every Photo-mode frame containing a person/dog/cat.
5. **Remove the portrait effect** — from the **viewer**: *"Tap Portrait in the top-left corner of the screen, then tap Portrait Off."*

**Models that support portrait capture in Photo mode** (Apple's exact aside): iPhone 15, 15 Plus, 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, iPhone 16, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max, iPhone 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, iPhone Air, iPhone 17e. ⚠️ **iPhone 16e is absent.**

### 7.12 Cinematic mode video editing — and the one place Apple hands you parity

`Edit` → the Cinematic controls. Turn the effect off/on: *"Tap Cinematic at the top of the screen, then tap Done."*

**Focus retiming — the key feature.** *"White dots under the frame viewer indicate where Camera automatically changed the focus while recording. Yellow dots indicate where the focus was manually changed."* Workflow: scrub the white vertical bar to the moment, then *"Tap a subject, outlined in yellow, to change the focus; double-tap to set automatic focus tracking on the subject."* A yellow dot appears marking the new focus change. *"You can also touch and hold the screen to lock the focus at a specific distance from the camera."* Delete a manual rack: tap the yellow dot, then tap Delete. A **`Manual Tracking`** button toggles between automatic focus tracking and your manually-selected focus points.

**Depth of field:** tap the `Depth Control` button at the top → drag the slider below the video. Fully revertible.

**Export with depth intact:** `Share` → `Options` → turn on **`All Photos Data`** → AirDrop to a Mac (**macOS 13+**) to edit in Photos / Final Cut Pro / iMovie / Motion with depth and focus metadata preserved. ⚠️ Note `Share` → **`Export Unmodified Original`** to external storage always exports the **original**, never the edit.

⚠️ **Trap: "iPhone 13 and later" is WRONG.** Apple's **Models that support Cinematic mode** aside lists exactly: iPhone 13 mini, 13, 13 Pro, 13 Pro Max, 14, 14 Plus, 14 Pro, 14 Pro Max, 15, 15 Plus, 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, 16, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max, 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max. **iPhone Air, iPhone 16e, and iPhone 17e are ALL ABSENT** — three current shipping models that the "13 and later" shorthand would wrongly include.

### 7.13 `Copy Edits` / `Paste Edits` (batch edit propagation)

Quietly the most sophisticated thing in the app. Open an edited photo/video → `More` (…) → **`Copy Edits`** → *"Review and turn off any edits you don't want to copy, then tap Copy"* (a checklist sheet of the individual adjustments — you can selectively exclude any of them). Then: *"Tap Select, then tap the thumbnails of the photos you want to paste the edits onto, or open a single photo or video. Tap [More], then tap Paste Edits."* Works on a batch in one action, on photos and videos.

**The load-bearing detail, verbatim:** *"Photos automatically adjusts the white balance and exposure of the edited photos to create a better match and make the photos look even more similar."* This is **not a dumb parameter copy** — Photos re-normalizes exposure and white balance per target image. Match this or your paste will look wrong on half the batch.

What's missing: no named/saveable presets, no preset library, no import/export of looks. You can only copy from one existing photo.

### 7.14 Undo, Redo, compare, Revert to Original

**During editing:** *"As you edit a photo or video, tap [Undo] and [Redo] at the top of the screen to undo and redo multiple edit steps."* Tap the photo/video (or the individual control button) to compare against the original.

**After saving — two documented revert paths, both real:**
- (a) Open the edited photo/video → `More` (…) → **`Revert to Original`**.
- (b) Open it → `Edit` → `Revert` → confirm **`Revert to Original`**.

Revert is **all-or-nothing**. There is no partial revert of a single adjustment after `Done`, and no version snapshots. And ⚠️ *"A video saved as a new clip can't be reverted to the original."*

**iCloud sync semantics:** Apple repeats on every editing page that *"any edits you make to your photos and videos are saved across all your devices."* Because the original + recipe + current render are all synced, *"a user can revert or resume edits made on a different device."* That cross-device resume/revert is a direct architectural consequence of the storage model below — you get it only if you replicate the model.

### 7.15 The non-destructive edit stack — exactly how Photos stores it

This is the architectural heart, and the corpus's original description of it was **wrong in a way that would have burned an implementer**. Here is the corrected model.

**What Photos stores, per asset** (Apple's actual PhotoKit wording): *"For each asset, Photos stores **the original version**, the **current version** (which includes the most recent adjustments), and the **set of adjustments** that were applied to the original version to create the current version."*

⚠️ **Trap:** it is **original + adjustments + current render** — NOT "previous + current". The widely-repeated "previous and current version" phrasing appears nowhere in Apple's docs and is a third-party blog invention. The distinction is load-bearing: an *original* is what makes Revert-to-Original possible; a *previous* version would imply a one-step undo history, **which Photos does not store.**

**`PHAdjustmentData`** is *"an application-defined **recipe**"* with three fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `formatIdentifier` | Reverse-DNS string identifying whose format it is (Apple's own edits use an Apple identifier) |
| `formatVersion` | Version of that format |
| `data` | Opaque blob — the recipe itself |

**THE CRITICAL RULE, verbatim:** *"For each asset, Photos stores only **one** [PHAdjustmentData] object, representing the **most recent edit** made to the asset's content."* No multi-app edit chain. No layer list. One recipe, one original, one flattened current render.

**The handoff protocol** when an app or extension opens an asset for editing. Photos asks your code *"can you interpret this adjustment data?"* via `canHandle(_:)` / `PHContentEditingInputRequestOptions`:

| Answer | For a **photo** | For a **video** |
|---|---|---|
| **Yes** | Photos hands you the **original** + the adjustment data. You reconstruct the edit from the recipe; the user can alter or revert it. | Same. |
| **No** | Photos hands you the **current version** — *"the rendered output of all past edits, so your app can further edit the asset but cannot alter or revert the most recent edit."* | ⚠️ **Photos does not store a current version of video assets.** Apple: *"If your extension can't read a video asset's adjustment data, it must work with the **original** version of the video, **overwriting past edits**."* |

⚠️ **Trap — the video asymmetry is inverted from how it is usually described, and it is destructive.** For a photo, an incompatible extension gets a safe flattened render. For a **video**, there is no flattened render to hand it — so the incompatible extension gets the *original* and **silently destroys every prior edit** on commit. Design around this explicitly.

On commit you supply a `PHContentEditingOutput` carrying your rendered result plus your own new `PHAdjustmentData`, posted via a `PHAssetChangeRequest` inside `performChanges`. Each `performChanges` prompts the user for permission to modify the library.

**The two consequences you must design around:**
1. Because Photos keeps only the **most recent** recipe, and because the recipe is app-private, **the moment a user touches Apple's Photos editor on an asset your app edited, your recipe is destroyed and replaced.** Your layered edit becomes an unrecoverable flattened pixel buffer. Conversely, you can never read Apple's recipe.
2. Therefore: **keep your own sidecar/edit database** keyed by `localIdentifier` + a content hash, and treat `PHAdjustmentData` as a best-effort interop channel, never your source of truth.

### 7.16 Third-party Photo Editing Extensions — the sanctioned way in

**User flow (iPhone):** Photos → tap a photo → `Edit` → tap the **`More` (…)** button → select an app from the menu → edit with the extension's tools → `Done`. Apple: *"You can apply edits from multiple apps and extensions to one photo, or use any combination of apps and extensions plus the editing tools built into Photos."*

**Managing them:** `Edit` → `More` (…) → *"swipe to the left until you see the More button, and then tap it"* → in the list of apps with Photos extensions, tap `Edit`, tap the Insert (+) button to add an app to favorites, and touch-and-hold the Reorder button to drag them into order.

**Discovery:** users find them in the App Store by searching *"Photos extension"* — Apple's own advice. *(The claim that Apple maintains an App Store editorial story titled "Edit Images Faster With Photo Extensions" is **unverified**.)*

**The contract:** your extension's principal view controller adopts **`PHContentEditingController`**. Its five members are the entire API surface:

| Member | Role |
|---|---|
| `canHandle(_:)` | Can you resume the existing adjustment data? (Determines which version Photos hands you — see 7.15.) |
| `startContentEditing(with:placeholderImage:)` | You receive a `PHContentEditingInput`. For a Live Photo you get `livePhotoEditingInput` and build a `PHLivePhotoEditingContext`. |
| `finishContentEditing(completionHandler:)` | Hand back a `PHContentEditingOutput` carrying your rendered result + your new `PHAdjustmentData`. |
| `shouldShowCancelConfirmation` | Whether to confirm on cancel. |
| `cancelContentEditing()` | Teardown. |

Works for photos, videos **and** Live Photos.

⚠️ **Trap: "chainable" does not mean "layered."** Apple says you can stack edits from multiple apps — but each commit **overwrites the single stored recipe**. A non-compatible extension downstream of yours gets the flattened current version (or, for video, the original) and cannot alter or revert your work.

### 7.17 RAW / Apple ProRAW behavior in Photos

Photos edits an Apple ProRAW / RAW capture with the **same full 15-slider consumer Adjust set** it gives a JPEG. Apple: *"ProRAW combines the information of a standard RAW format along with iPhone image processing, which gives you more flexibility when editing the exposure, color, and white balance."* Applying any adjustment renders and saves a JPEG/HEIF as the **current version** while retaining the RAW **original** — so `Revert to Original` returns you to the RAW.

Availability: Apple ProRAW is Pro models, iPhone 12 Pro and later, iOS 14.3+.

⚠️ **Trap: Photos DOES show a RAW badge.** The claim "Photos does not show a visible RAW badge" is **misleading**. There is no RAW label on the **grid thumbnail**, but Photos **does display a `RAW` badge at the top of the image in the detail view.** Don't design a "we alone surface RAW" pitch on a false premise.

⚠️ **Clean Up does not work on RAW files** — a loudly-voiced regression, because on Mac the tool Clean Up replaced (`Retouch`) *did* work on RAW **and** on faces.

Photos offers **no RAW-specific controls at all**: no highlight recovery, no per-channel white balance, no lens correction, no demosaic control.

### 7.18 Edit-mode `Appearance` (light/dark canvas) — new in iOS 26

`Edit` → `More` (…) → **`Appearance`**. Apple: *"By default, the background of Edit mode matches the light or dark appearance of your iPhone. You can change the background color of Edit mode—for example, set it to always appear dark if you prefer to edit photos against a dark background."*

| Option | Apple's string |
|---|---|
| `System` | *"Match Edit mode to the light or dark appearance of your iPhone"* |
| `Dark` | *"Make Edit mode always appear dark"* |
| `Light` | *"Make Edit mode always appear light"* |

Small, but telling: Apple is conceding that the surrounding canvas biases perceived tone. Copy it.

### 7.19 Adjacent features that set editing expectations

**iOS 26 — Spatial Scenes.** A hexagonal button in the **top-right of the photo viewer** converts any 2D photo into a 3D "spatial scene" that parallaxes as you move the iPhone. Runs monocular depth estimation on the **Neural Engine**, on-device, on **any** photo — including photos taken years ago and photos shot on another camera altogether. Usable as Lock Screen wallpaper and in the Photos widget.

⚠️ **Important and easy to miss: Spatial Scenes does NOT require Apple Intelligence.** It runs on **iPhone 12 and later** — a vastly wider gate than the Clean Up / Extend / Reframe tools sitting next to it in the same viewer. Do not lump it in with the AI tools when building your device matrix.

**iOS 27 beta (fall 2026), all NOT SHIPPING:**
- **`Save Video Frame as Photo`** — frame grab from a video, from the `More` (…) menu. Photos has lacked this for the app's entire life.
- **Keywords and 1–5 star ratings** on photos and videos, filterable by rating. ⚠️ **Star ratings are OFF by default** — they must be enabled at `Settings` > `Photos` > `View Options` > **`Show Rating Controls`**.
- **Selection View** — review/modify metadata (e.g. location) for multiple images at once.
- **Slideshows** from any album/collection/selection, with transition styles, slide durations and background music; saveable and shareable.

### 7.20 Device-gating matrix — build this per-feature, never tiered

⚠️ **Trap: there is no clean device tier.** Apple's model lists differ per feature, and the "e" models are excluded from some advanced features and included in others. Gate off Apple's per-feature aside pages, not chip generation.

| Feature | iPhone 16e | iPhone 17e | iPhone Air | Floor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Photographic Styles (any) | ✅ included | ✅ included | ✅ | iPhone SE (3rd gen) / 13 |
| **Latest-gen** Photographic Styles (2-D pad, post-capture editable) | ❌ **excluded** | ❌ **excluded** | ✅ | iPhone 16 |
| Portrait capture in Photo mode (apply portrait after the fact) | ❌ **excluded** | ✅ included | ✅ | iPhone 15 |
| Spatial Audio → `Audio Mix` | ✅ **included** | ✅ | ✅ | iPhone 16 |
| Cinematic mode | ❌ **excluded** | ❌ **excluded** | ❌ **excluded** | iPhone 13 mini |
| `Clean Up` (Apple Intelligence) | ✅ (16 models) | ✅ | ✅ | iPhone 15 Pro |
| Portrait focus-point change | — | — | — | iPhone 13 |
| Spatial Scenes | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | **iPhone 12** (no AI gate) |
| Apple ProRAW | ❌ (Pro only) | ❌ | ❌ | iPhone 12 **Pro** |

### 7.21 What a third-party app can and cannot do

| Capability | Available to 3rd parties? | Mechanism / why not |
|---|---|---|
| Build the whole 16-item Adjust strip | ✅ Yes | Core Image near-equivalents: `CIExposureAdjust`, `CIHighlightShadowAdjust`, `CIVibrance`, `CIColorControls`, `CITemperatureAndTint`, `CISharpenLuminance`, `CIUnsharpMask`, `CINoiseReduction`, `CIVignette`. |
| **Read the parameters of an edit made in Apple's Photos app** | ❌ **No** | `PHAdjustmentData` is an opaque, app-private blob under Apple's own `formatIdentifier`. If you don't recognize it, Photos hands you the flattened current version and you can no longer alter or revert that edit. |
| Read/replicate Apple's Auto-Enhance recipe | ❌ No | No API exposes it. Build your own (histogram/scene analysis or a small on-device model). |
| Ship Apple's Vivid / Dramatic / Silvertone filter looks | ❌ No | Not exposed. Core Image ships an *older, different* generation (`CIPhotoEffectChrome/Fade/Instant/Mono/Noir/Process/Tonal/Transfer`) — **these are not the same looks.** Ship your own LUTs. |
| Capture in, read, alter, or remove a **Photographic Style** | ❌ **No — hard moat** | No public API. A third-party camera cannot capture in a Style; a third-party editor cannot read, alter, or remove a Style on an Apple-Camera photo. |
| Crop / rotate / flip / straighten / perspective | ✅ Yes | Trivially replicable; Core Image perspective transforms + Vision `VNDetectHorizonRequest` for auto-level. |
| Markup drawing substrate | ✅ Mostly | PencilKit (`PKCanvasView` / `PKToolPicker`) gives you the drawing tools. You build the sticker / text / shape / loupe layer yourself. |
| **Clean Up** (Apple's inpainting model) | ❌ **No public API whatsoever** | No PhotoKit, Vision, or Image Playground entry point to Apple's inpainting model. Ship your own — which is exactly why this is beatable. `VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest` gives you subject/instance masks to build on. |
| iOS 27 `Extend` / `Reframe` / Clean Up v2 | ❌ No announced API | Not exposed. `ImagePlayground.framework` exists (one view modifier, no API keys) but that is image **generation**, not editing a user's photo. |
| Full **Live Photo** editor incl. per-frame filtering and mute | ✅ **Yes — fully public and powerful** | `PHLivePhotoEditingContext`: `frameProcessor` (a block Photos calls for every frame of both video and still, handing you a `CIImage`), `audioVolume`, `fullSizeImage`, `duration`, `photoTime` (key-photo offset), `orientation`, `saveLivePhoto(to:options:)`, `prepareLivePhotoForPlayback(withTargetSize:)`. |
| Loop / Bounce / Long Exposure effects | ⚠️ Not exposed, but trivially reimplementable | Loop = concat; Bounce = concat + reverse; Long Exposure = frame averaging. |
| Video trim / speed / crop / filters | ✅ Yes | AVFoundation + Core Image. |
| **`Audio Mix`** (In-Frame / Studio / Cinematic) | ❌ **No** | No API gives a third-party app the multi-mic Spatial Audio stems needed for source separation. A real Apple-only capability on iPhone 16+. |
| Read depth / disparity + portrait mattes; build your own bokeh and relighting | ✅ Yes | `AVDepthData` + PhotoKit auxiliary images (semantic segmentation mattes for skin/hair/teeth/glasses). Vision person-segmentation and foreground-instance-mask requests substitute on non-depth photos. |
| Toggle **Apple's** portrait effect on/off; apply **Apple's** Portrait Lighting looks; change Apple's depth-derived focus subject | ❌ No | Not exposed. You can build equivalents, not drive Apple's. |
| **Cinematic focus retiming — read, delete, add, retime Apple's focus decisions, re-render bokeh** | ✅ **YES — Apple hands you full parity** | The public **`Cinematic` framework** (iOS 17, 2023): `CNScript` (*"a collection of focus decisions, focus transitions, detections, and detection tracks associated with a movie captured in Cinematic mode and methods to change them"*), `CNDecision` (*"a decision to focus on a particular detection, or group of detections, at a particular time"*), `decisions(in:)`, plus a bokeh renderer. |
| **Capture** Cinematic video from a third-party camera | ✅ Yes (new in iOS 26) | Cinematic Video API: `isCinematicVideoCaptureEnabled = true` on `AVCaptureDeviceInput`, producing *"Cinematic video with disparity data, metadata, and the original video, allowing for non-destructive editing."* |
| Copy/Paste Edits across a batch | ✅ Yes, in your own format | Fully replicable — but you can never copy edits made in Apple's Photos into your app (opaque recipe). |
| Non-destructive stack with revert | ✅ Yes | Write `PHAdjustmentData`; Photos preserves the original and the user can revert. ⚠️ See the video asymmetry in 7.15. |
| Insert your editor into Photos' main toolbar | ❌ No | Photo Editing Extensions live only behind `Edit` → `More` (…) — a discovery graveyard. |
| Deep RAW controls | ✅ **Yes, and better than Apple's** | `CIRAWFilter`: demosaic, per-channel WB, `boost` / `boostShadowAmount`, local tone map, lens/chromatic-aberration correction, sensor-native highlight recovery. Photos exposes **none** of this. |
| Generate Spatial Scenes | ❌ Not exposed | But monocular depth → layered parallax is buildable with Vision / Core ML depth models. |
| Write star ratings / keywords into Photos | ❌ **No** | PhotoKit has no writable rating or keyword field for third parties. Apple is adding these in **iOS 27 as a first-party-only capability** — so your app's own tagging **will not sync into Photos**. Plan for that. |

⚠️ **Trap: extensions run hosted, constrained.** A Photo Editing Extension runs inside the Photos app's process budget — memory- and time-constrained. Heavy ML inpainting is risky there. This is why serious editors ship a **full standalone app AND a thin extension**.

### 7.22 Where Apple is weak — our opening

- **No edit history, no layers, no versions.** Photos stores exactly **one** `PHAdjustmentData` recipe per asset, "representing the most recent edit". `Revert` is all-or-nothing. There is no partial revert of a single adjustment after `Done`, no version snapshots, and **no way for the user to even see what edits were applied** — the Info panel shows no adjustment readout. A real multi-step, re-editable, layered history is a straightforward and honest differentiator.
- **`Clean Up` is genuinely bad, and Apple says so.** Its own documentation warns: *"If you brush over a person's face, the face may become blurred with a pixelated effect."* It fails at simple retouching (blemishes), degrades near frame edges, **does not work on RAW at all**, and is device-gated to iPhone 15 Pro and up. On Mac it *replaced* `Retouch`, which handled both RAW and faces — a regression users are loudly angry about. There is **no API**, so nobody can be "the Clean Up for everyone else" — you must ship your own inpainting model, and the bar is low.
- **RAW is treated as a JPEG.** Photos hands a ProRAW file the same 15 consumer sliders it gives a snapshot: no highlight recovery, no per-channel white balance, no lens correction, no demosaic control. `CIRAWFilter` exposes all of it to third parties. **This is the clearest quality gap in the entire editor.** A pro-leaning competitor wins here by default.
- **Photographic Styles are a one-way door on ~4 years of iPhones.** iPhone SE 3 / 13 / 14 / 15 / 16e / 17e users had their style baked into the pixels at capture with no post-hoc removal. A de-styling / neutralizing tool addresses a real, large, aggrieved population.
- **No presets, no LUTs, no shareable looks.** `Copy Edits` / `Paste Edits` is clever (it even re-normalizes white balance and exposure per target) but you can only copy from *an existing photo*. There are no named presets, no preset library, no import/export, no way to carry a look across a shoot or share it with another person.
- **The Adjust engine has no professional controls at all.** No layers, no masks, no local/selective adjustments, no curves, no HSL-per-color, no white-balance eyedropper, no histogram, no numeric value entry.
- **`Save Video as New Clip` permanently breaks revert** — Apple's own words. The non-destructive guarantee has an explicit, undocumented-in-the-UI hole.
- **Photo Editing Extensions are a discovery graveyard.** Buried behind `Edit` → `More` (…) → swipe → `More`. Users overwhelmingly do not know they exist, and Apple's own discovery advice is "search the App Store for *Photos extension*".
- **Video editing is a stub.** One trim range. No splitting, no multi-segment cutting, no reordering, no joining, no audio ducking or keyframes, no music, no titles, no transitions, no scopes, no bitrate/codec control. Apple's answer is "use iMovie."
- **Confusing conditional UI.** The toolbar changes shape by asset type and device; Apple steers iPhone 16+ users away from `Filters` toward `Styles` (which are **stills-only**), frustrating people who want filters on video. Users on Apple Community report persistent "Clean Up not visible / not working" confusion caused purely by the device × region × language matrix.
- **AI provenance is about to become table stakes.** iOS 27 will embed a **hidden SynthID watermark** in every Apple-Intelligence-edited photo, on top of the existing visible `Modified with Clean Up` EXIF Credits string. Decide deliberately whether to match that standard: **matching it is a trust differentiator; not matching it will eventually read as a red flag.**
- **Features Photos has lacked for its entire life** and is only adding in iOS 27 beta: star ratings, keywords, and saving a video frame as a photo. Any competing app that already ships them should say so loudly — and any that doesn't is about to be behind.
## 8. Capture Formats & Media Types

This section covers every media format the iPhone Camera can produce, how each one is physically stored inside the Photos library, and exactly what is destroyed when a third-party app reads it naively. It spans the `Settings > Camera > Formats` pane, the capture modes (Portrait, Cinematic, Spatial, Pano, Slo-mo, Time-lapse, Night, Action, Dual Capture), and the PhotoKit data model that represents them.

The single most important thing an implementer must know: **a `PHAsset` is not a file.** It is a bag of `PHAssetResource` objects — `photo`, `video`, `pairedVideo`, `fullSizePhoto`, `fullSizeVideo`, `fullSizePairedVideo`, `alternatePhoto`, `photoProxy`, `adjustmentData`, `adjustmentBasePhoto`, `adjustmentBaseVideo`, `adjustmentBasePairedVideo`, `audio` — plus metadata. `PHImageManager.requestImage` and any `UIImage` round-trip silently destroy: the Live Photo MOV pairing, the ProRAW DNG (you get a rendered JPEG), Portrait depth/disparity maps and mattes, the entire Cinematic disparity + focus-decision layer, the MV-HEVC second eye on spatial media, burst grouping, HDR gain maps, animated-GIF frames beyond the first, the RAW half of a RAW+JPEG pair, and the non-destructive `adjustmentData` that makes `Revert` work.

Everything below is written against **iOS 26** (current shipping build iOS 26.5.2; iOS 26.6 in developer beta). iOS 27 is in beta with GA expected ~September 2026; its announced Photos work is generative editing and organization, and **no iOS 27 change to any capture-format contract has been announced** — but one PhotoKit symbol (`PHAsset.originalResourceChoice`) is iOS 27-beta-only and is called out as a trap below.

---

### 8.1 The structural model: resources, not files

Correct ingestion means enumerating `PHAssetResource.assetResources(for: asset)` and handling every resource, not asking for "the image."

| Resource type | Apple's verbatim abstract | Present when |
|---|---|---|
| `.photo` | "Provides the original photo data for its asset." | Always, for photos |
| `.video` | "Provides the original video data for its asset." | Always, for videos |
| `.audio` | "Provides the original audio data for its asset." | Audio assets |
| `.alternatePhoto` | "Provides photo data that isn't the primary form of its asset." | RAW+JPEG imports from external cameras |
| `.fullSizePhoto` | "Provides a modified version of the original photo asset." | Photo has been edited |
| `.fullSizeVideo` | "Provides a modified version of the original video asset." | Video has been edited |
| `.adjustmentData` | "Provides data for use in reconstructing recent edits to its asset." | Asset has been edited |
| `.adjustmentBasePhoto` | "Provides an unaltered version of its photo asset for use in reconstructing recent edits." | Edited photo |
| `.adjustmentBaseVideo` | "Provides an unaltered version of its video asset." | Edited video |
| `.pairedVideo` | "Provides the original video data component of a Live Photo asset." | Live Photo |
| `.fullSizePairedVideo` | "Provides the current video data component of a Live Photo asset." | Edited Live Photo |
| `.adjustmentBasePairedVideo` | "Provides an unaltered version of the video data for a Live Photo asset for use in reconstructing recent edits." | Edited Live Photo |
| `.photoProxy` (iOS 17+) | Deferred-processing proxy (see 8.16) | Freshly captured 24/48 MP with deferred delivery |

Each `PHAssetResource` also exposes `originalFilename`, `uniformTypeIdentifier`, `contentType`, `pixelWidth`, `pixelHeight`, `assetLocalIdentifier`.

**Golden rule for ingestion:** never use `PHImageManager.requestImageDataAndOrientation` alone. Always call `PHAssetResource.assetResources(for:)` and enumerate. Read bytes with `PHAssetResourceManager.requestData(for:options:dataReceivedHandler:completionHandler:)` with `isNetworkAccessAllowed = true` — otherwise iCloud-optimized assets fail silently. Before creating a multi-resource asset, validate with `PHAssetCreationRequest.supportsAssetResourceTypes(_:)`.

⚠️ **Trap: `PHAsset.originalResourceChoice` is iOS 27 BETA ONLY.** It looks like the obvious way to ask which resource (RAW vs. compressed) is the editing base for a RAW+JPEG asset. Apple's docs mark it **iOS 27.0 beta / iPadOS 27.0 beta / macOS 27.0 beta / visionOS 27.0 beta**. It does not exist in any shipping OS as of 2026-07-14 (current shipping = iOS 26.5.2). Do not ship against it. Its abstract, for future reference: "The original resource used as the basis for rendering this asset's derivatives… only meaningful for assets that have a RAW alternate, such as RAW+JPEG assets, where it indicates whether the RAW or the compressed resource serves as the unadjusted base. For all other assets the value is compressed." (`PHAssetCreationRequest` gains a matching property in the same beta.)

---

### 8.2 `Settings > Camera > Formats` — the master pane

This is the single pane that decides what bytes the Camera writes. Section headers and options, verbatim:

**Section: `Camera Capture`**

| Option | Photos become | Videos become |
|---|---|---|
| `High Efficiency` | HEIF (`.HEIC`) | HEVC (H.265) |
| `Most Compatible` | JPEG | H.264 |

Apple's wording: "All new photos and videos will now use JPEG or H.264 format. To return to using the space-saving HEIF and HEVC formats, choose High Efficiency."

The setting **only appears on devices that can capture HEIF/HEVC**. Apple's exact device list: iPhone 7 or iPhone 7 Plus or later; iPad (6th generation) or later; iPad Air (3rd generation) or later; iPad mini (5th generation) or later; iPad Pro (10.5-inch), iPad Pro (11-inch), and iPad Pro 12.9-inch (2nd generation) or later; Apple Vision Pro.

⚠️ **Trap: `Most Compatible` does far less than users think.** It affects **only new captures by Apple's Camera app**. It does not convert existing library assets, does not bind third-party camera apps (which pick their own codec via `AVCapturePhotoSettings`), and does not affect screenshots. The Apple Community is full of "I chose Most Compatible and my photos are still HEIC" threads for exactly this reason.

**Section: `Photo Capture`**
- `Apple ProRAW` (older label) or `ProRAW & Resolution Control` (newer label — depends on model). See 8.4.
- `ProRAW Format`: `12 MP`, `48 MP`, or `HEIF 48 MP`.
- `Photo Mode`: `12 MP` or `24 MP` (default for the Main/Fusion camera).
- `Resolution Control`: turn on to reach 48 MP.

**Section: `Video Capture`**
- `Apple ProRes` (requires iOS 15.1 or later). See 8.6.
- `ProRes Encoding`: `HDR`, `SDR`, or `Log`.

---

### 8.3 Still images: HEIF/HEIC, JPEG, and the resolution ladder

A HEIC file is a **container** (ISO/IEC 23008-12) whose images are HEVC-coded. It can hold multiple image items plus **auxiliary images**: depth/disparity maps, portrait effects matte, semantic segmentation mattes, and an HDR gain map, plus a thumbnail. This is why HEIC→JPEG conversion is lossy in ways that have nothing to do with pixel quality — the auxiliary images simply vanish.

Apple's maker-note dictionary (`kCGImagePropertyMakerAppleDictionary`) carries Apple-specific keys inside the still, including **key `17` = the Live Photo asset identifier UUID** (see 8.7).

**Resolution control.** `Settings > Camera > Formats > Photo Mode` → `12 MP` or `24 MP`. To reach 48 MP: `Settings > Camera > Formats`, turn on `Resolution Control` or `ProRAW & Resolution Control` (label depends on model). The Camera app then shows a format control at the top of the screen. Apple, verbatim: "If you choose **HEIF Max** or **RAW Max**, you get up to 48 MP. The resolution changes if you use zoom or switch to Night mode or Flash when you take a picture. **RAW 12** offers up to 12 MP and standard **HEIF** offers up to 24 MP."

The in-Camera format control has four states on Pro models: `HEIF` / `HEIF Max` / `RAW 12` / `RAW Max`. `RAW Max` is **Pro-models only**. Note the interaction gesture differs by doc generation: the older support article says *touch and hold* the resolution setting at the top of the screen; the current iOS 26 iPhone User Guide phrases it as "tap the control at the top of the screen to turn the format you want to use on and off." Support both.

⚠️ **Trap: "HEIF Max on iPhone 14 and later" is wrong.** Apple's marketing prose says "On iPhone 14 and later models with iOS 17, you can choose your format and resolution in the Camera app, but RAW Max is only available on iPhone Pro models." This is loose. **iPhone 14 and iPhone 14 Plus ship a 12 MP Main camera and physically cannot produce 24 MP or 48 MP output.** In practice the non-Pro 24/48 MP resolution control exists only on 48 MP-Fusion base models: iPhone 15 / 15 Plus and later, iPhone 16e, iPhone 17 / iPhone Air — plus the Pro line from iPhone 14 Pro. Do not gate your UI on "iPhone 14 or later."

⚠️ **Trap: the silent 48 MP → 12 MP fallback.** Only the Main camera at 1× produces 48 MP. Ultra Wide, Telephoto, Night mode, flash, and macro all fall back to 12 MP — with no warning. Users believe they shot 48 MP and did not. **Read `PHAsset.pixelWidth`/`pixelHeight` and label the real resolution**, not the setting.

**APIs.** Read via `PHAssetResource` (`.photo`) → `PHAssetResourceManager.requestData`, or `PHContentEditingInput.fullSizeImageURL`. Decode with ImageIO (`CGImageSource`), which exposes the primary-image index, per-index properties, auxiliary data via `CGImageSourceCopyAuxiliaryDataInfoAtIndex`, and `kCGImagePropertyGroups`. Write HEIC with `CGImageDestinationCreateWithURL(…, UTType.heic, …)`. Third-party capture: `AVCapturePhotoOutput` + `AVCapturePhotoSettings(format:)` with `.hevc`; request 24/48 MP directly via `AVCapturePhotoOutput.maxPhotoDimensions` / `AVCaptureDevice.Format.supportedMaxPhotoDimensions`.

---

### 8.4 Apple ProRAW (linear DNG)

**Availability:** iPhone 12 Pro and later **Pro models**, iOS 14.3+. 48 MP ProRAW: iPhone 14 Pro and later Pro.

**Enable:** `Settings > Camera > Formats` → turn on `Apple ProRAW` or `ProRAW & Resolution Control` under the `Photo Capture` header. In Camera: "Depending on your settings, tap either `JPEG` or `HEIC` at the top of the screen, then tap `RAW`." The badge is literally the word `RAW`. Persist across launches via `Settings > Camera > Preserve Settings > ProRAW & Resolution Control`.

**`ProRAW Format`** (`Settings > Camera > Formats`): `12 MP`, `48 MP`, or `HEIF 48 MP`. Apple names the exact model list for this option: iPhone 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max, 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, 14 Pro, 14 Pro Max.

**File format:** standard **DNG** (Adobe Digital Negative), extension `.dng`, UTI `com.adobe.raw-image`. Apple ProRAW is a **linear** DNG — demosaiced, computationally-fused linear scene data with full RAW adjustment latitude for exposure/white balance/color. It is *not* a raw Bayer dump. Apple: "ProRAW uses the industry standard digital negative (DNG) file format, so you can open ProRAW files with apps that are compatible with DNG files" — but warns that an app which doesn't understand ProRAW "might look different than expected when opened."

| Fact | Value (Apple, verbatim) |
|---|---|
| File size @ 12 MP | ~25 MB |
| File size @ 48 MP | ~75 MB |
| Relative size | "ProRAW files are 10 to 12 times larger than HEIF or JPEG files." |
| 48 MP restriction | "Only photos that you take with the main camera at 1x can be saved 48 MP. Ultra Wide, Telephoto, Night mode, flash, and macro photos can only be saved at 12 MP." |
| Mutually exclusive with | "You can't use ProRAW with Live Photos, in Portrait mode, or when shooting video." |
| Compatible with | "capture images in ProRAW format using any of its cameras, including when also using the Smart HDR, Deep Fusion, or Night mode features." |

⚠️ **Trap: an EDITED ProRAW shares as JPEG.** Apple states it plainly — once you edit a ProRAW in Photos, "you can also share the edited version, which has the **.jpg** file extension when shared." And: "The Mail app automatically converts the ProRAW file to a smaller JPG file." Apple's own documented workaround to get the untouched DNG back out is an absurd dance: **Share → Duplicate → Edit → `Revert` → then AirDrop.** To get *both* the DNG and the edited JPG: AirDrop with `Share > Options > All Photos Data` on and "Save to Downloads" on the Mac; or import via Image Capture / the Windows Photos app over USB; or on Mac Photos, `File > Export > Export Unmodified Original`.

**APIs.** Capture: `AVCapturePhotoOutput.isAppleProRAWSupported` / `.isAppleProRAWEnabled`; `AVCapturePhotoOutput.isAppleProRAWPixelFormat(_:)` vs. `isBayerRAWPixelFormat(_:)` distinguishes linear ProRAW from plain Bayer RAW; `availableRawPhotoPixelFormatTypes`; `rawFileType` (`.dng`); `AVCapturePhotoSettings(rawPixelFormatType:processedFormat:)` for RAW+JPEG/HEIC pairs; `rawEmbeddedThumbnailPhotoFormat`. Read: `PHAssetResource` of type `.photo` with `uniformTypeIdentifier == "com.adobe.raw-image"`; decode with ImageIO or Core Image's `CIRAWFilter` (which exposes exposure/temperature/tint/boost/sharpness knobs).

---

### 8.5 Video: HEVC/H.264, HDR (Dolby Vision), frame rates, PAL

Under `High Efficiency`, video records as **HEVC** in a QuickTime `.MOV`; under `Most Compatible`, **H.264**. Audio is AAC unless Spatial Audio is in play (8.11). Apple's compatibility warning, verbatim: "On some older devices, support for HEVC is affected by the resolution and frame rate (fps) of the video. Resolutions of 1080p or lower and frame rates of 60 fps or lower are more broadly compatible with older devices."

**In-Camera format matrix.** Tap the resolution/fps values in the corner of the Camera screen: formats `HD`, `4K`, `HD (PAL)`, `4K (PAL)`; frame rates `24`, `25`, `30`, `60`, or `120` fps. Additional formats are enabled in `Settings > Camera > Record Video`.

⚠️ **Trap: PAL is not a toggle.** PAL is not a standalone switch in `Record Video`; it appears as the *formats* `HD (PAL)` and `4K (PAL)`. Apple describes PAL as "a television video format used in many countries and regions in Europe, Africa, Asia, and South America."

**`Settings > Camera > Record Video` contains, verbatim:**

| Setting | Apple's description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `HDR Video` (labeled `HDR Video` or `HDR` depending on model) | "iPhone records video in HDR and shares HDR videos with devices using iOS 13.4, iPadOS 13.4, macOS 10.15.4, or later; other devices receive an SDR version of the same video." Apple describes it as **Dolby Vision** HDR. | — |
| `Auto FPS` | "apply Auto FPS to only 30-fps video, to both 30- and 60-fps video, or turn it off" | — |
| `Auto Low Light FPS` (some models, in place of Auto FPS) | "automatically reducing the frame rate to 24 fps" | — |
| `Lock Camera` | "prevents switching between cameras while recording video." | **Off** |
| `Enhanced Stabilization` | "zooms in slightly to provide improved stabilization while recording in Video mode or Cinematic mode." | **On** |
| `Lock White Balance` | — | — |
| `Action Mode Lower Light` | see 8.12 | — |

⚠️ **Trap: HDR video silently tone-maps on share.** "Other devices receive an SDR version of the same video" means the shared derivative is tone-mapped. This is the root cause of the extremely common "my iPhone video looks washed out / blown out after uploading" complaint. Detect Dolby Vision (via `AVAsset` track format descriptions → transfer function / color primaries) and offer an explicit preserve-vs-tone-map choice.

**APIs.** Read: `PHAsset` (mediaType `.video`) → `PHAssetResource` `.video` (true original bytes) and `.fullSizeVideo` (edited render). `PHImageManager.requestAVAsset(forVideo:)` / `requestExportSession` return the **edited** render — use `PHAssetResourceManager` on `.video` for the original. Capture: `AVCaptureDevice.activeFormat` + `isVideoHDREnabled`; `AVCaptureDevice.Format.isVideoHDRSupported`. `Enhanced Stabilization` maps to `AVCaptureConnection.preferredVideoStabilizationMode` (`.cinematicExtended` / `.cinematicExtendedEnhanced`).

---

### 8.6 Apple ProRes, Apple Log / Log 2, ProRes RAW, genlock, open gate

**Enable:** `Settings > Camera > Formats` → turn on `Apple ProRes` under the `Video Capture` header. **Requires iOS 15.1 or later.** Then in Camera, select Video mode, tap the resolution/fps values in the corner and tap a ProRes option.

**`ProRes Encoding`** (`Settings > Camera > Formats`): `HDR`, `SDR`, or `Log`. Apple, verbatim: "iPhone 15 Pro models, iPhone 14 Pro models, and iPhone 13 Pro models support ProRes recording … in high dynamic range (HDR), in standard dynamic range (SDR), or in Log encoding. **iPhone 17 Pro models and iPhone 16 Pro models support ProRes recording in either HDR or in Log encoding**" — i.e. **iPhone 16 Pro and 17 Pro dropped SDR ProRes.** Apple Log is therefore a *first-party stock Camera format*, not something that requires Final Cut Camera.

**Capability matrix (Apple, verbatim):**

| Configuration | Limit |
|---|---|
| ProRes baseline | "ProRes is available for recording up to **4K at 30 fps**." |
| iPhone 15 Pro / 15 Pro Max | "can record **4K at 60 fps** when connected to a compatible external storage device." |
| iPhone 16 Pro / 16 Pro Max / 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max | "can record **4K at 120 fps** when connected to a compatible external storage device." |
| 128 GB models | "recording to internal storage is only available at **1080p at 30 fps**." Apple's capacity table gives **128 GB = 1080p HD 30/25 fps for ALL ProRes models** (broader than the 15 Pro / 16 Pro-only phrasing). |
| External drive for 4K60 | ≥ 220 MB/s sustained, ≤ 4.5 W draw |
| External drive for 4K120 | ≥ 440 MB/s sustained, ≤ 4.5 W draw |
| Cameras | "ProRes is available on all cameras, including the front camera." |
| Mode exclusions | "**ProRes isn't supported in Cinematic, Time-lapse, or Slo-Mo mode.**" |

**iPhone 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max only, via Final Cut Camera 2.0:** ProRes RAW ("you can record videos in **ProRes RAW** using applications such as **Final Cut Camera**"), **Apple Log 2** ("giving users the ability to record in an even wider color gamut in **ProRes or HEVC**"; the `Log 2 LUT` is applied in Final Cut Pro), **genlock** (sync to an external reference signal), **timecode** (`Time of Day`, `Record Run`, or external), and **open gate** recording ("uses the full camera sensor to capture a wider field of view at resolutions greater than DCI 4K"). ProRes video up to 4K60 is supported on the new 200 mm Telephoto on iPhone 17 Pro.

**Availability of ProRes overall:** iPhone 13 Pro and later Pro models.

⚠️ **Trap: third-party ProRes RAW *capture* is unverified.** Apple Newsroom explicitly states "**Genlock API support is available to third parties** and is already being used with the new Blackmagic Design Camera ProDock." It makes **no equivalent statement about ProRes RAW capture**. Whether a public AVFoundation path exists for third-party ProRes RAW capture (vs. Final Cut Camera being privileged) is **unverified** — do not plan a product around it without confirming against an Apple developer doc or WWDC session.

*(Also unverified: the claim that Final Cut Camera 2.0 requires iPhone Xs+ / iOS 18.6+. No first-party statement found.)*

⚠️ **Trap: any non-passthrough export destroys ProRes and Log.** A ProRes or Log MOV appears in PhotoKit as an ordinary video asset. Any `AVAssetExportSession` preset that is not `AVAssetExportPresetPassthrough` will re-encode ProRes to H.264/HEVC and annihilate the log latitude and the RAW data. Always use passthrough, or copy the `.video` `PHAssetResource` bytes directly.

**APIs.** `AVCaptureMovieFileOutput` with `AVVideoCodecType.proRes422`, `.proRes422HQ`, `.proRes422LT`, `.proRes422Proxy`, `.proRes4444`.

---

### 8.7 Live Photos

Apple: "With Live Photos, your iPhone records what happens **1.5 seconds before and after** you take a picture" (≈3 s total).

**On disk it is TWO resources:** a still (HEIC or JPEG) and a QuickTime `.MOV` with video + audio.

**⚠️ Trap: pairing is by UUID in metadata, not by filename.**
- **Still:** `kCGImagePropertyMakerAppleDictionary` key **`17`** = an asset-identifier UUID string.
- **MOV:** top-level QuickTime metadata **`com.apple.quicktime.content.identifier`** (constant `AVMetadataQuickTimeMetadataKeyContentIdentifier`) = the **same** UUID.
- The MOV additionally carries a per-frame timed-metadata track marking the still-frame time (`com.apple.quicktime.still-image-time`), which expresses the key-photo offset. *(This key is well-established in the tooling literature but is not documented in a fetchable Apple developer reference — treat as high-confidence-but-community-sourced.)*

Strip either identifier and you have two unrelated files forever. Write both files with matching UUIDs or Photos ingests them as a dead still plus an orphan video.

**Camera UI (iOS 26).** Tap the camera-controls button, then the Live Photos button. ⚠️ **Trap: the toggle is THREE-state on iOS 26, not binary.** Apple: "Tap `Live`. Tap again to switch between **`Live Off`, `Live On`, and `Live Auto`**." A slash through the button means the feature is off. To always show the button: `Settings > Camera > Indicators > Live Photo`.

**Persistence.** The current iOS 26 iPhone User Guide says `Settings > Camera > Preserve Settings > Live Photo` **is on by default**. An older Apple support article still says "The Camera app turns Live Photos on again automatically" unless you enable that switch. These two Apple docs conflict; **ship the User Guide behavior.**

**Hard exclusion (Apple, verbatim):** "**Live Photos aren't available when ProRAW or HEIF Max is turned on.**" Your capture UI must model this mutual exclusion.

*Device floor (iPhone 6s and later, iPad 5th gen+, etc.) is historically accurate but is **not stated in any current Apple article** — treat as unverified; do not present it as sourced.*

**Effects and the key photo.** From the `Live` control in the **top-left corner** of the photo in Photos, the current iOS 26 User Guide lists **seven** options: `Live`, `Loop`, `Bounce`, `Long Exposure`, `Live Off`, `Portrait`, `Portrait off`. (The commonly-cited three-item list — Loop / Bounce / Long Exposure — comes from an older support article and is incomplete for current iOS.)

Key photo: `Edit` → `Live` button → drag the white frame → `Make Key Photo` → `Done`.

⚠️ **Trap (Apple's own words):** "**Live Photos taken on an iPhone 15 model or later with a portrait effect lose the portrait effect if you change the key photo.**"

**Other post-capture operations:** Trim a Live Photo (drag either end of the frame viewer), Mute a Live Photo, `Make a still photo`, and the share-menu `Save as Video`.

**Playback variation.** `PHAsset.playbackVariation` (`PHAsset.PlaybackVariation`, iOS 11.0+) enumerates exactly: `.none`, `.autoloop` (Loop), `.mirror` (Bounce), `.longExposure` (Long Exposure). `PHAsset.playbackStyle` (iOS 11.0+) then reports `.livePhoto` vs. `.imageAnimated` vs. `.videoLooping` vs. `.image` — a viewer should switch on this.

⚠️ **Trap: there is no public API to *set* a playback variation.** You can read it, and you can replicate the effect yourself via `PHLivePhotoEditingContext`, but you cannot ask Photos to mark an asset as Loop/Bounce/Long Exposure. A viewer that ignores `playbackVariation` renders a Loop/Bounce/Long-Exposure asset as a plain Live Photo — visibly wrong. Long Exposure in particular *replaces the displayed still* with a synthesized frame while the original remains recoverable via `Revert`, so a naive export of a Long Exposure gives you the **original still**, not the long-exposure image the user thinks they saved.

**Documented losses (Apple's own):** "If you share via **Mail**, the Live Photo is sent as a still image." / "If you edit your Live Photo in a **third-party app**, you might lose any Live Photo effects that you've applied."

**APIs.**
- Read: `PHAsset.mediaSubtypes ∋ .photoLive`; `PHImageManager.requestLivePhoto(for:…)` → `PHLivePhoto`, displayed in `PHLivePhotoView`. For raw bytes: `PHAssetResource.assetResources(for:)` yields `.photo` + `.pairedVideo` (originals); if edited, also `.fullSizePhoto` + `.fullSizePairedVideo` (current) and `.adjustmentBasePhoto` / `.adjustmentBasePairedVideo` + `.adjustmentData`.
- Construct from your own files: `PHLivePhoto.request(withResourceFileURLs:placeholderImage:targetSize:contentMode:resultHandler:)`.
- Write to library: `PHAssetCreationRequest.forAsset()` then `addResource(with: .photo, fileURL:)` **and** `addResource(with: .pairedVideo, fileURL:)`.
- Edit: `PHLivePhotoEditingContext` (`frameProcessor` per-frame `CIImage`, `audioVolume`, `photoTime`, `prepareLivePhotoForPlayback`, `saveLivePhoto(to:)`).
- Capture: `AVCapturePhotoOutput.isLivePhotoCaptureEnabled` / `.isLivePhotoCaptureSupported` / `.isLivePhotoCaptureSuspended`; `AVCapturePhotoSettings.livePhotoMovieFileURL` / `.livePhotoMovieMetadata` / `.livePhotoVideoCodecType`; `isLivePhotoAutoTrimmingEnabled` trims excessive movement.
- Picker: `PHPickerFilter.livePhotos`. Web: Apple's **LivePhotosKit JS**.

---

### 8.8 Portrait mode — depth, disparity, and mattes

Portrait applies a depth-of-field effect. In Photos the user can change the **f-stop** and the **Portrait Lighting** effect after the fact, and `Revert`. Night mode can be combined with Portrait on supported models. Apple, verbatim: "**Apple ProRAW isn't supported in Portrait mode.**"

**Storage.** The depth information is an **auxiliary image inside the HEIC/JPEG container** — not a separate file. The rendered blur is baked into the displayed image, but the **unblurred original + depth remain**, which is exactly why f-stop stays re-editable.

| Auxiliary payload | ImageIO key | AVFoundation type |
|---|---|---|
| Depth / disparity map | `kCGImageAuxiliaryDataTypeDepth` / `kCGImageAuxiliaryDataTypeDisparity` | `AVDepthData` |
| Portrait effects matte | `kCGImageAuxiliaryDataTypePortraitEffectsMatte` | `AVPortraitEffectsMatte` |
| Semantic segmentation mattes (hair, skin, teeth, glasses) | — | `AVSemanticSegmentationMatte` |

⚠️ **Trap: re-encoding a Portrait HEIC drops ALL auxiliary images.** A `UIImage` → JPEG round-trip, or most generic image pipelines, yields a permanently-baked blur with no depth, no f-stop editing, no Portrait Lighting, and no `Revert`. Apple's user-level preservation path is AirDrop with `Share > Options > All Photos Data`.

⚠️ **Trap: `embedsDepthDataInPhoto` is a separate flag from `isDepthDataDeliveryEnabled`.** If `embedsDepthDataInPhoto` is `false`, depth is delivered to your capture delegate but **is not written into the file**. Same pattern for `embedsPortraitEffectsMatteInPhoto` and `embedsSemanticSegmentationMattesInPhoto`.

**APIs.** Identify: `PHAsset.mediaSubtypes ∋ .photoDepthEffect` ("The asset is a photo captured with the Camera app's Portrait mode depth effect"); picker filter `PHPickerFilter.depthEffectPhotos`. Read depth: `PHContentEditingInput.fullSizeImageURL` → `CGImageSource` → `CGImageSourceCopyAuxiliaryDataInfoAtIndex(…, kCGImageAuxiliaryDataTypeDisparity)` → `AVDepthData(fromDictionaryRepresentation:)`. Capture: `AVCapturePhotoOutput.isDepthDataDeliverySupported`/`Enabled`, `AVCapturePhotoSettings.isDepthDataDeliveryEnabled`, `embedsDepthDataInPhoto`, `isDepthDataFiltered`, `isPortraitEffectsMatteDeliveryEnabled` + `embedsPortraitEffectsMatteInPhoto`, `enabledSemanticSegmentationMatteTypes` + `embedsSemanticSegmentationMattesInPhoto`.

*Version annotations (depth data iOS 11+, portrait effects matte iOS 12+, semantic segmentation mattes iOS 13+) are consistent with AVFoundation history but were not independently re-verified — check at runtime.*

*Unverified: the widely-reported claim that recent iPhones (15/16 era) capture depth in **normal Photo mode** for eligible subjects, letting a plain photo be converted to a Portrait afterward. No Apple support page states this. **Feature-detect** by checking for a disparity auxiliary image on assets that lack `.photoDepthEffect`.*

---

### 8.9 Cinematic mode

**Capture.** Camera → swipe **left** to `Cinematic` mode. Apple: "Cinematic mode applies a depth-of-field effect that keeps the subject of your video sharp while creating a beautifully blurred foreground and background."

Focus UI, verbatim: "A **yellow frame** on the screen indicates the person in focus; a **gray frame** indicates a person is detected, but not in focus. Tap the gray box to change the focus; tap again to lock the focus on that person." / "**Touch and hold** the screen to lock the focus at a single distance." Tap anywhere to set a focus point if no person is detected. Pre-record controls: tap the controls chevron then `Aperture` or `Exposure`; the Camera Control can also adjust depth-of-field. On iPhone 15 Pro, 16 Pro and 17 Pro models, "tap 2 to zoom in."

**Resolution.** `Settings > Camera > Record Cinematic`: default **1080p HD @ 30 fps**; switchable to **4K @ 24 fps** or **4K @ 30 fps**.

**Editing in Photos.** `Edit` → `Cinematic`: change focus points, toggle between automatic focus tracking and manual focus points, drag a slider to adjust depth of field, then `Revert`. In the editor, **white dots = automatic focus changes; yellow dots = manual focus changes.**

**Storage — this is the important part.** The recorded MOV is **not** a baked-blur video. Apple (WWDC25): the movie file "contains the **disparity data, metadata, and the original video** that enables non-destructive editing." The focus decisions live in a **`CNScript`** — "a collection of focus decisions, focus transitions, detections, and detection tracks associated with a movie captured in Cinematic mode." Rendering the bokeh is a separate step (`CNRenderingSession` / Metal).

**Availability split — memorize this:**

| Capability | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Capture in Apple's Camera app | iPhone 13 and later |
| Third-party **playback/edit** | **iOS 17+** (Cinematic framework) |
| Third-party **capture** | **iOS 26+** (new in 2025 — the year Cinematic capture opened to apps like Kino / Filmic Pro) |
| Editing iOS-16+ Cinematic videos on Mac | macOS 13+ |

⚠️ **Trap: naive export of a Cinematic video is catastrophic.** A standard `AVAssetExportSession` yields either a flat video with **no bokeh at all** (you exported the original track) or **permanently baked bokeh with no re-focus**. Either way the disparity track and the `CNScript` are gone and "the blur can't be changed anymore" forever. Apple's user-level preservation path: AirDrop with `Share > Options > All Photos Data` on — Apple describes this as transferring "Cinematic mode videos—with **depth and focus metadata**."

**Cinematic framework (iOS 17+) — full symbol inventory:** `CNAssetInfo` (Cinematic-specific tracks), `CNScript` (+ `CNScriptChanges`, `CNScriptFrame`), `CNDecision` (a focus decision at a time), `CNDetection` / `CNDetectionTrack` / `CNCustomDetectionTrack` / `CNFixedDetectionTrack`, `CNDetectionType` (face, torso, cat, dog…), `CNObjectTracker`, `CNBoundsPrediction`, `CNRenderingSession` + `CNRenderingSessionAttributes` + `CNRenderingSessionFrameAttributes`, `CNCompositionInfo`, and **`CNImageRenderingSession`** + `CNImageRenderingSessionConfiguration` (renders a shallow-depth-of-field effect onto **still images** — directly relevant to building a Portrait-equivalent pipeline).

**Cinematic capture API (iOS 26, new):**
- `AVCaptureDeviceInput.isCinematicVideoCaptureEnabled = true` (+ `isCinematicVideoCaptureSupported`)
- Format gating: `AVCaptureDevice.Format.isCinematicVideoCaptureSupported`, `videoFrameRateRangeForCinematicVideo`, `videoMin/MaxZoomFactorForCinematicVideo`
- Bokeh strength: `AVCaptureDeviceInput.simulatedAperture` (f-stops; `minSimulatedAperture` / `maxSimulatedAperture` / `defaultSimulatedAperture` on the format)
- Metadata: `AVCaptureMetadataOutput` with `requiredMetadataObjectTypesForCinematicVideoCapture` — **an exception is thrown if your `metadataObjectTypes` differ**
- Manual focus: `setCinematicVideoTrackingFocus(detectedObjectID:focusMode:)`, `setCinematicVideoTrackingFocus(at point:focusMode:)` (creates a salient-object metadata object), `setCinematicVideoFixedFocus(at:focusMode:)`
- `CinematicVideoFocusMode` = `.none` / `.strong` (solid yellow rect, keeps tracking) / `.weak` (dashed rect, the algorithm may rack away)
- Supported formats: **Dual Wide (rear) and TrueDepth (front), 1080p and 4K, 30 fps**, 420v/420f for SDR/EDR or x420 for 10-bit HDR
- Recommended stabilization: `.cinematicExtendedEnhanced`

**Identify:** `PHAsset.mediaSubtypes ∋ .videoCinematic` (iOS 15.0+); picker filter `PHPickerFilter.cinematicVideos`.

---

### 8.10 Spatial photos, spatial video, and Spatial Scenes

**Capture UI.** Camera → swipe **right** to `Spatial` mode → rotate to landscape → tap the Shutter button. Apple's framing guidance, verbatim: "Keep your iPhone steady and level. Frame your subjects **3 to 8 feet** from the camera. Use lighting that is even and bright." Spatial media syncs via iCloud Photos and "you can also view and share spatial photos and videos just like regular photos and videos on any of your other Apple devices" — they unfold into 3D on Apple Vision Pro.

#### Spatial photos — exact structure

Apple (ImageIO docs): "A **spatial photo** is a multi-image **HEIC** file containing a left-eye image and a right-eye image, a **stereo pair group**, plus **spatial metadata**." Both images must have identical pixel dimensions.

Per-image properties dictionary:
- `kCGImagePropertyGroups` = `{ kCGImagePropertyGroupIndex: 0, kCGImagePropertyGroupType: kCGImagePropertyGroupTypeStereoPair, kCGImagePropertyGroupImageIsLeftImage / kCGImagePropertyGroupImageIsRightImage: true, kCGImagePropertyGroupImageDisparityAdjustment: <Int> }`
- `kCGImagePropertyHEIFDictionary` = `{ kIIOMetadata_CameraExtrinsicsKey: { kIIOCameraExtrinsics_Position: [x,y,z] in metres, kIIOCameraExtrinsics_Rotation: identity 3×3 }, kIIOMetadata_CameraModelKey: { kIIOCameraModel_Intrinsics: 3×3 matrix, kIIOCameraModel_ModelType: kIIOCameraModelType_SimplifiedPinhole } }`
- `kCGImagePropertyHasAlpha: false`
