**Three mandatory spatial properties:** **horizontal field of view** (must be identical for both cameras), **baseline** (interaxial distance; human average 64 mm; **iPhone 15 Pro spatial video baseline = 19.2 mm**), and **projection** (always **rectilinear**).

**Horizontal disparity adjustment** (a.k.a. convergence adjustment): a signed fraction of image width encoded as an integer in **[−10000, +10000]** (value × 1e4). Apple's recommended default is +2% (i.e. `Int(0.02 × 1e4) = 200`). Positive pushes content farther away; **each image shifts by HALF the adjustment.**

Destination: `CGImageDestinationCreateWithURL(url, UTType.heic, 2, [kCGImagePropertyPrimaryImage: 0])`. Left/right identification is **by the group flags, NOT by image order**; the primary-image index picks what non-stereo platforms show.

⚠️ **Trap: stereo ≠ spatial.** If the mandatory spatial metadata is absent, the file is merely *stereo*. visionOS will not offer the Immersive presentation or the comfort treatments. Write the metadata or you built a worse file.

#### Spatial video — exact structure

Apple: "A **spatial video** is a QuickTime movie with a stereo **MV-HEVC** video track, plus **spatial metadata**." MV-HEVC (multiview HEVC) carries both eyes in one track — a base layer plus a second layer encoding only the inter-view difference, so a 2D-only decoder simply plays the base layer.

Capture uses the Main (1×) + Ultra Wide cameras simultaneously; the higher-quality Wide image is the "hero eye" (Final Cut Pro's term). Same three mandatory camera properties as spatial photos, plus the disparity adjustment — and per Apple these **must be constant for the entire duration**: "Don't write spatial metadata to a stereo video if the baseline, horizontal field of view, or recommended disparity adjustment of your stereo video varies over time." Non-rectilinear content (equirectangular / fisheye) must **not** be tagged spatial.

| Fact | Value (Apple, verbatim) |
|---|---|
| Resolution | "Spatial videos are captured in **1080p at 30 frames per second in standard dynamic range**." |
| Size | "A minute of spatial video is approximately **130 MB**." |
| Shipping | "With **iOS 17.2**, iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max users can now record spatial videos." |

*Apple has not published a spec page enumerating spatial-video resolutions for iPhone 16/17-class hardware, which may differ from the 15 Pro figures above.*

**Availability:** Capture in Camera app — iPhone 15 Pro / 15 Pro Max (iOS 17.2+) and later; also Apple Vision Pro. **Third-party spatial video capture — iOS 18+**, iPhone 15 Pro-class hardware.

**APIs.** Identify: `PHAsset.mediaSubtypes ∋ .spatialMedia`; `PHPickerFilter.spatialMedia`. Capture (iOS 18+): `AVCaptureMovieFileOutput.isSpatialVideoCaptureSupported` / **`isSpatialVideoCaptureEnabled = true`**, gated by `AVCaptureDevice.Format.isSpatialVideoCaptureSupported`; pair with `preferredVideoStabilizationMode = .cinematicExtendedEnhanced`. Apple abstracts away "the complexity of synchronization, camera calibration, encoding, and metadata writing" — you get a fully-formed spatial MOV out of the movie file output. Read/write: AVFoundation MV-HEVC support (`AVAssetWriter` with tagged buffers / `AVAssetReader` multiview APIs, iOS 17.2+). Apple ships a sample for the photo side: **SpatialPhotoConverter**.

⚠️ **Trap: `.spatialMedia` carries a back-dated availability annotation.** Apple documents `PHAssetMediaSubtype.spatialMedia` as **iOS 16.0+ / visionOS 1.0+**, even though spatial capture shipped in iOS 17.2 on iPhone 15 Pro. **Feature-detect at runtime; do not trust the annotation.**

⚠️ **Trap: spatial photo *capture* has no dedicated third-party flag.** Unlike spatial *video* (`isSpatialVideoCaptureEnabled`), there is no documented AVFoundation switch for third-party spatial *photo* capture. You must synthesize a spatial photo from any stereo pair using the ImageIO recipe above.

⚠️ **Trap: naive export flattens spatial media permanently.** Extracting "the image" from a spatial HEIC gives you **one eye**; the second view, the stereo group, the extrinsics/intrinsics and the disparity adjustment are gone. A stock video transcode collapses MV-HEVC to single-view HEVC/H.264. **Even passthrough copying can drop the spatial metadata if the container is rewritten.**

#### Spatial Scenes (iOS 26) — a VIEW state, not a capture format

iOS 26's Photos app can turn an ordinary 2D photo into a 3D "spatial scene" that parallaxes as you tilt the phone. This is **generative depth estimation / novel-view synthesis performed on-device from a single image** — an effect applied at view time, not a new stored stereo file, which is why it works on decades-old photos.

Apple's first-party vocabulary (support article "View spatial scenes in Apple Vision Pro", published 2025-09-22): the control is the **`spatial scenes button`**, located "in the top-right corner of the photo." Apple states: "Viewing spatial scenes on iPhone requires **iOS 26 or later**. Viewing them on iPad requires iPadOS 26 or later." Spatial scenes also appear in Safari (spatial browsing) and the Spatial Gallery app. Apple confirms the render-state framing: "You can share any photo to another Apple Vision Pro, iPhone, or iPad to **re-create the same spatial scene on that device**."

*Unverified (press-sourced only): the "iPhone 12 and later" device floor, the claim that it does not require Apple Intelligence, and the Lock Screen wallpaper effect.*

⚠️ **Trap: no public API.** There is no confirmed public API for a third-party app to generate Spatial Scenes as of iOS 26. Parity requires your own monocular depth model + parallax renderer — which is entirely buildable, and arguably the most copyable of Apple's spatial features.

---

### 8.11 Audio: Spatial Audio, Stereo, Mono, Wind Noise Reduction, Audio Mix

Apple, verbatim: "On **iPhone 16 models or later**, your camera records in **Spatial Audio** by default. To change recording settings, go to `Settings > Camera > Record Sound`, then tap `Spatial Audio`, `Stereo`, or `Mono`." Apple's per-option definition of Spatial Audio: "Audio playback is immersive from all directions on supported playback devices." **"Earlier iPhone models record in Stereo."** On older models the control is a plain toggle: `Settings > Camera > Record Stereo Sound`.

**`Wind Noise Reduction`** — Apple: "On **iPhone 16 or later**, when you record video with either Spatial Audio or Stereo, wind noise is automatically reduced. To change this setting, turn off `Wind Noise Reduction`."

**Format.** Spatial Audio capture is **first-order ambisonics (FOA)**. Third-party capture path: set `multichannelAudioMode` to first-order ambisonics on the `AVCaptureDeviceInput` / audio connection.

**`Audio Mix`** is the whole payoff of capturing Spatial Audio: post-capture audio editing in Photos with modes **Standard / In-Frame / Studio / Cinematic**. It is backed by the Cinematic framework: `CNAssetSpatialAudioInfo`, `CNSpatialAudioContentType`, `CNSpatialAudioRenderingStyle` (see Apple's "Editing Spatial Audio with an audio mix" guide).

⚠️ **Trap: a stock export collapses ambisonics to stereo.** Transcoding a Spatial-Audio MOV through any standard `AVAssetExportSession` preset destroys the ambisonic track — and with it, the user's ability to ever use `Audio Mix` on that clip again. Users lose it on export and have no idea why.

---

### 8.12 The capture modes: Burst, Slo-mo, Time-lapse, Pano, Night, Action, QuickTake, Dual Capture, Macro

#### Bursts
"Swipe the Shutter button to the **left** to begin taking photos in rapid succession. Lift your finger to stop." Or hold Volume Up if `Settings > Camera > Use Volume Up for Burst` is on. Apple explicitly notes: "**You can take Burst photos with the rear and front-facing cameras.**"

Review: tap the burst thumbnail, then tap `Burst (number)`. "**Gray dots** below the thumbnails mark the **suggested** photos to keep." "Tap the circle in the lower-right corner of each photo you want to save as an individual photo, then tap `Done`." Deleting the thumbnail deletes the entire burst.

**Storage:** a burst is **N separate `PHAsset`s** sharing a `burstIdentifier` string. One is flagged `representsBurst == true` (the stack cover). Each asset carries `burstSelectionTypes` (`PHAssetBurstSelectionType`) — a bitmask of `autoPick` (the system's gray-dot "suggested" photos) and/or `userPick`.

⚠️ **Trap: `includeAllBurstAssets`.** `PHAsset.fetchAssets(withBurstIdentifier:options:)` requires `PHFetchOptions` with **`includeAllBurstAssets = true`** or you only ever see the representative — a library ingests one photo per burst and **silently loses the other 39**. The opposite failure is equally common: ingesting all of them without reading `burstIdentifier` floods the grid with 40 near-identical frames and discards the stacking plus the system's suggested picks. Picker filter: `PHPickerFilter.bursts`.

#### Slo-mo
Camera → swipe to `Slo-mo`. Apple: "Slo-mo is set to record at **1080 HD at 240 fps** from the back camera and **1080 HD at 120 fps** from the front camera. To change the back camera to 120 fps, go to `Settings > Camera > Record Slo-mo`." You can tap the Shutter button to take a still while recording. On **iPhone 16 Pro models and iPhone 17 Pro models** you can also record slow motion from **Video mode**: "Tap the format and resolution values in the corner of the screen, then select **`120 FPS`**."

Post-hoc editing: "**Slide the vertical bars below the frame viewer** to define the section you want to play back in slow motion."

**Storage:** the file is a full-rate (120/240 fps) video. The slow-motion **ramp** (which segment plays slow) is stored as an **edit, in `adjustmentData`** — not baked into the media. That is precisely why the ramp is re-editable and revertable.

⚠️ **Trap: two opposite slo-mo export failures, both extremely common.**
1. Copy the `.video` `PHAssetResource` → you get the **original 240 fps clip with no ramp** (most players show it at normal speed).
2. Use `requestExportSession` / `requestAVAsset` with default (current-version) options → you get the **rendered ramp baked in** and lose all ability to re-edit.

To be faithful you need `.video` + `.adjustmentData` (+ `.fullSizeVideo` for the current render). "My slo-mo exported as a normal-speed video" is one of the single most-reported iPhone export bugs across third-party apps and cloud services.

Identify: `PHAsset.mediaSubtypes ∋ .videoHighFrameRate`; `PHPickerFilter.slomoVideos`.

#### Time-lapse
Camera → `Time-lapse` mode → Record to start/stop. "Capture footage at selected intervals to create a time-lapse video." Apple's tip: "On **iPhone 12 or later**, use a tripod to capture time-lapse videos with more detail and brightness when recording in low-light situations" (Night-mode time-lapse on supported models).

Frames are captured at an adaptive interval which is halved as recording lengthens, so the output stays roughly 20–40 s regardless of duration. **The time compression is BAKED IN** — unlike slo-mo, nothing is recoverable and nothing extra needs preserving. This is the least lossy of the special formats.

Identify: `.videoTimelapse`; `PHPickerFilter.timelapseVideos`. There is **no public API to capture a time-lapse** — you'd build your own interval capture.

#### Panoramas
Camera → swipe **left** to `Pano` mode → Shutter → "Pan slowly in the direction of the arrow, keeping it on the center line" → Shutter again to finish. "Tap the arrow to pan in the opposite direction. To pan vertically, rotate iPhone to landscape orientation. You can reverse the direction of a vertical pan, too."

A single stitched, very-wide-aspect HEIC/JPEG. No auxiliary data. Apple's subtype description: "a **large-format panorama** photo."

⚠️ **Trap: unbounded aspect ratios.** Extreme dimensions (e.g. 20000 × 3000) break naive thumbnailers, memory-map assumptions and grid layouts. **Treat `pixelWidth`/`pixelHeight` as unbounded.** Identify: `.photoPanorama`; `PHPickerFilter.panoramas`.

#### Night mode
Auto-engages in low light; the Night mode indicator shows the capture duration. "If **crosshairs** appear in the frame, your iPhone has detected movement—align them to help you reduce motion and improve the image quality." "To cancel a Night capture in progress, tap the `Stop` button." **Manual exposure:** tap the controls chevron → `Night Mode` → choose an exposure option; "Your selection is saved for your next Night mode photo." (Also `Preserve Settings > Night Mode`.)

On supported models: Night mode **selfies**, Night mode **time-lapse**, and Night mode with **Portrait mode**. Availability: iPhone 11 and later (rear).

Output is an ordinary HEIC/JPEG (or a ProRAW DNG — **Night mode does work with ProRAW, but only at 12 MP**). Multi-frame fusion is baked in; no separate resource. **Nothing is lost on export** — but note it silently forces ProRAW / HEIF Max down to 12 MP. There is **no `PHAssetMediaSubtype` for Night mode** and **no public "Night mode" capture API**; `AVCapturePhotoSettings.photoQualityPrioritization = .quality` plus the system's automatic low-light fusion is the closest third-party equivalent.

#### Action mode
"On supported models, **Action mode** provides improved stabilization while recording in Video mode." Tap the Action-mode button; tap again to turn off. Pin the button via `Settings > Camera > Indicators > Action Mode`. Also `Preserve Settings > Action Mode`. Apple: "Action mode works best in bright light. If you want to use Action mode in lower light, go to `Settings > Camera`, tap `Record Video`, then turn on **`Action Mode Lower Light`**."

⚠️ **Hard limit, Apple's own words: "Action mode has a maximum capture resolution of 2.8K."** Users do not realize this. Availability: iPhone 14 and later.

Heavy sensor-crop + gyro-driven electronic stabilization applied **at capture** and baked into the file. **No separate resource, no metadata sidecar, nothing to preserve.** There is **no `PHAssetMediaSubtype` for Action mode** — an Action-mode video is indistinguishable from a normal video in PhotoKit except by its 2.8K-class dimensions. Closest third-party analogue: `AVCaptureConnection.preferredVideoStabilizationMode = .cinematicExtendedEnhanced`.

#### QuickTake (video in Photo mode)
Touch and hold the Shutter button to record; **slide right to lock**; you can take stills while recording. On supported models, click-and-hold the Camera Control to "record videos in full resolution."

#### Dual Capture (NEW, shipping today)
**iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, and iPhone Air.** Camera → Video mode → controls → **`Dual Capture`** records the **front and rear cameras simultaneously**. This is a new capture format shipping in the current OS.

#### Macro / Auto Macro
⚠️ **Trap: the Ultra Wide silently takes over.** At close focus distances the camera switches to the Ultra Wide sensor automatically, **changing which sensor produced the file** (and therefore its resolution ceiling and characteristics). Controlled by Auto Macro switching and `Settings > Camera > Preserve Settings > Macro Control`.

---

### 8.13 Screenshots and screen recordings

⚠️ **Trap: "screenshots are PNG" is now WRONG.** iOS 26 added `Settings > General > Screen Capture` with a format choice. Apple, verbatim:

| Setting | Screenshots | Screen recordings |
|---|---|---|
| `SDR` — "This option captures less brightness and color." | **PNG** | **HEVC (H.265)** |
| `HDR` — "This option captures more brightness and color. It requires an HDR display to show the full quality." | **HEIC** | **HEVC (H.265) in an HDR container** |

Apple's caveat: "On standard displays, HDR screenshots appear in SDR format, and HDR recordings play back with slightly reduced quality."

The same `Screen Capture` pane also holds `Automatic Visual Look Up` (auto-identify objects in screenshots), `CarPlay Screenshots`, and `Full-Screen Previews`.

macOS equivalent (confirmed by Apple's HEIF article): "On supported Mac computers with **macOS Tahoe 26** or later, if the `Capture Format` setting in the Screenshot app is set to HDR, screenshots are captured in HEIF format and screen recordings are captured in HEVC format."

**Identify:** `PHAsset.mediaSubtypes ∋ .photoScreenshot` (photos) and `.videoScreenRecording` (videos, iOS 13.0+). Picker filters: `PHPickerFilter.screenshots`, `PHPickerFilter.screenRecordings`.

⚠️ **Trap: Apple's own docs are wrong here.** The documentation page for `PHAssetMediaSubtype.videoScreenRecording` carries an incorrect abstract — "The media subtype is a photo animation such as a GIF, animated PNGs, etc." — which actually belongs to `.photoAnimation`. It is a doc copy bug. **Trust the symbol names, not the abstracts**, especially if you scrape Apple's docs.

---

### 8.14 GIFs and animated images

Animated GIFs and animated PNGs imported into or saved to Photos are stored as **image assets** with `PHAssetMediaSubtype.photoAnimation` (iOS 11.0+ / visionOS 1.0+). `PHAsset.playbackStyle` returns **`.imageAnimated`** (iOS 11.0+).

⚠️ **Trap: `requestImage` returns a SINGLE FRAME.** To keep the animation you must pull the `.photo` `PHAssetResource` bytes (the GIF/APNG file) and decode all frames with ImageIO (`CGImageSourceGetCount` + per-frame `kCGImagePropertyGIFDelayTime`). Almost every naive importer turns GIFs into stills.

There is **no `PHPickerFilter` case for animated images** — use `PHPickerFilter.playbackStyle(.imageAnimated)`.

---

### 8.15 Photographic Styles

A capture-time color/tone pipeline, with a new generation on **iPhone 16 models** (iOS 18+). `Settings > Camera > Photographic Styles`; the UI offers `Get Started` and `Reset to Standard`. Also persisted via `Settings > Camera > Preserve Settings > Photographic Style`.

**This is format-critical:** on **iPhone 16 and later**, a Photographic Style is **adjustable and removable AFTER capture** in Photos — i.e. it is a **reversible latent adjustment on the HEIF**, not a baked filter. An ingestion tool that flattens the rendered pixels destroys the user's ability to change or remove the style.

*Unverified: the exact storage mechanism (whether the style rides in `adjustmentData` or a proprietary sidecar) is not documented in a source we could verify, and neither is the behavior on pre-iPhone-16 models. **Verify on-device before relying on it** — it materially affects ingestion fidelity on iPhone 16/17.*

---

### 8.16 Deferred Photo Processing (`photoProxy`) — the asset that changes under you

When shooting 24 MP / 48 MP with `autoDeferredPhotoDeliveryEnabled`, the capture pipeline returns a **lightly-processed proxy immediately** and finishes the real processing later, in the background, inside Photos.

Apple's abstract for `AVCaptureDeferredPhotoProxy` (iOS 17.0+): "A lightly-processed photo with data that the system may use to process and fetch a higher-resolution asset at a later time… This object represents intermediate data that the system can render into a final image and ingested into the user's photo library using the PhotoKit framework. **The intermediate data aren't accessible by the calling process.**"

It lands in the library as a `PHAssetResourceType.photoProxy` resource (iOS 17.0+), later replaced/augmented by the real `.photo`.

⚠️ **Trap: freshly-captured assets are NOT immutable.** If you ingest an asset immediately after capture, you may be reading the **proxy** — and the asset's bytes, quality and pixel dimensions **can change later** when the system finishes processing. A correct importer registers a `PHPhotoLibraryChangeObserver` and **re-reads assets whose resources change**, rather than assuming the first read is final.

⚠️ **Trap (known bug, Apple Developer Forums thread 766714): creating an asset with `.photoProxy` can cause LOCATION DATA TO BE PURGED** after the asset refreshes. Switching to `.photo` avoids it.

**Capture path:** delegate callback `photoOutput(_:didFinishCapturingDeferredPhotoProxy:error:)` → save via `PHAssetCreationRequest.addResource(with: .photoProxy, data: deferredPhotoProxy.fileDataRepresentation(), options:)`.

---

### 8.17 Edits, `adjustmentData`, and metadata overrides

**Every Photos edit is non-destructive.** Photos keeps the unmodified original plus a description of the edit, which is why `Revert` always works — and why an edited asset has **more resources** than an unedited one (see the table in 8.1).

On `PHAsset`: `hasAdjustments`, `adjustmentTimestamp`, `adjustmentFormatIdentifier`, `adjustmentsState`. `PHAdjustmentData` = "A description of the edits made to an asset's photo, video, or Live Photo content, which allows your app to reconstruct or revert the effects of prior editing sessions."

**Edit round-trip API:** `PHAsset.requestContentEditingInput` → `PHContentEditingInput` (`fullSizeImageURL`, `fullSizeImageOrientation`, `avAsset`/`audiovisualAsset`, `livePhoto`, `adjustmentData`, `playbackStyle`, `mediaSubtypes`) → produce a `PHContentEditingOutput` with your own `PHAdjustmentData(formatIdentifier:formatVersion:data:)` → `PHAssetChangeRequest.contentEditingOutput`. If you write `adjustmentData`, Photos hands it **back** to you next time (via `PHContentEditingInputRequestOptions.canHandleAdjustmentData`) so the user can re-edit — this is how Apple's own filters and third-party Photo Editing Extensions stay non-destructive.

⚠️ **Trap: you need BOTH halves.** Exporting only `.fullSizePhoto` throws away `Revert`. Exporting only `.photo` throws away the user's edits. Faithful export = original + edited render + `adjustmentData`. Note also that when exporting to an external storage device from iOS Photos, "For photos and videos that have been edited, **the unmodified original version will be exported**."

#### `Adjust Date & Time` and `Adjust Location`

Flow: open the photo/video → tap the **info** button (ⓘ) → tap `Adjust Date & Time` or `Adjust Location`. Apple: "For date and time changes, use the calendar and clock to update, then tap `Adjust`. For location changes, enter where the photo was taken in the text field, then tap the location when it appears under **`Map Locations`**."

**Batch:** "To change the date, time, or location of a batch of photos, tap `Select`, tap the thumbnails you want to change, then follow the steps above."
**Revert:** tap ⓘ → `Adjust Date & Time` or `Adjust Location` → `Revert`.

The info panel also exposes: people and pets; a **caption** field ("to describe the photo or video, and make it easier to find in Search"); Visual Look Up items; event information for concerts or sporting events; **what device captured it**; camera metadata (lens, shutter speed, file size); location (tap to open in Maps; "Add a location" if none); who shared it; and which albums it's in.

Separately, Apple's Personal Safety Guide documents the Share sheet's `Options > Location` toggle, which strips location when sharing.

*Unverified: the "iOS 15+" availability floor for Adjust Date & Time / Adjust Location.*

⚠️ **Trap: THE THREE-CLOCK PROBLEM.** An importer faces three disagreeing timestamps:
1. `PHAsset.creationDate` — user-adjustable, authoritative for sorting, and **written into exported files**.
2. `PHAsset.addedDate` — "The date and time this asset was added to the photo library (from the device that was used to add this asset)" — **distinct from `creationDate`**.
3. The file's own EXIF `DateTimeOriginal` — may disagree with both.

Use `creationDate` for user-facing sort, but **expose the EXIF when they differ** — Apple does not.

⚠️ **Trap: there is NO public PhotoKit API to read the ORIGINAL (pre-adjustment) date or location** once the user has adjusted it, nor to perform Apple's `Revert` on a metadata adjustment. To recover the original you must parse EXIF/GPS out of the `.photo` resource's raw bytes yourself and compare. Write side: `PHAssetChangeRequest.creationDate` / `.location` / `.isFavorite` / `.isHidden` inside `performChanges`.

---

### 8.18 RAW+JPEG from external cameras (`alternatePhoto`)

When a photo is imported from an external camera as a RAW+JPEG pair, Photos stores it as **ONE asset with TWO photo resources**. Apple's verbatim abstract for `.alternatePhoto` (iOS 8.0+ / macOS 10.11+ / visionOS 1.0+): "Provides photo data that isn't the primary form of its asset. For example, a photo asset imported from an external camera may contain both a **JPEG file (the primary form of the asset)** and a **RAW file (the alternate photo)**."

⚠️ **Trap: `requestImage` / `requestImageDataAndOrientation` return only the PRIMARY (the JPEG).** The RAW is invisible to those APIs and is **silently dropped by nearly every third-party importer**. Photographers who pull Canon/Nikon/Sony RAW+JPEG into Photos and then into a third-party app routinely lose the RAW without a single warning.

**Do this instead:** enumerate `PHAssetResource.assetResources(for:)` and look for **both** `.photo` and `.alternatePhoto`; check each resource's `uniformTypeIdentifier` (e.g. `com.adobe.raw-image`, `com.canon.cr3-raw-image`, `com.nikon.nef-raw-image`, `com.sony.arw-raw-image`). Write: `PHAssetCreationRequest.addResource(with: .photo, …)` + `addResource(with: .alternatePhoto, …)`.

⚠️ **Trap:** the natural companion — `PHAsset.originalResourceChoice`, which says whether the RAW or the compressed resource is the unadjusted editing base — **is iOS 27 beta only** and unusable today. See 8.1.

---

### 8.19 Android Motion Photos — Apple does not convert them

Android Motion Photos (Google/Samsung) are a **JPEG or HEIC with an MP4 embedded inside it** plus a Google XMP block (`GCamera:MicroVideo`, or a `Container`/`Item` directory in newer "Motion Photo v1" files).

**Apple Photos does not automatically convert these into Live Photos.** They import as ordinary still images and the embedded video is inert. Every Android switcher loses motion on every motion photo, permanently and silently.

*Evidence quality, stated honestly: there is **no first-party Apple documentation** of this — it is a negative, and Apple does not document a feature it does not implement. Support rests on Apple Community threads plus the existence of an entire third-party conversion ecosystem (MotionPhotoMuxer, MotionPhoto2, Pinwheel on macOS, Motion2Live on iOS). Treat as an empirically-observed behavior to verify on-device, not as an Apple-sourced fact.*

**The two formats solve the same problem oppositely:**
- **Google:** embeds the MP4 **inside** the JPEG (one file; offset recorded in XMP).
- **Apple:** keeps **two files linked by a UUID** (MakerApple key `17` ↔ `com.apple.quicktime.content.identifier`).

**Conversion is fully specified and entirely implementable:** extract the embedded MP4 → generate a UUID → write it into the still's MakerApple dictionary **and** into the MOV's QuickTime metadata → create a `PHAsset` via `PHAssetCreationRequest` with `.photo` + `.pairedVideo` resources. The reverse (Live Photo → Motion Photo) is equally implementable — but note **Google has shipped/announced a Live Photos → Android transfer tool**, so the reverse direction is being commoditized. **The Android → Apple direction is the underserved one.**

---

### 8.20 Reference enumerations

**`PHAssetMediaSubtype`** (an OptionSet — an asset can carry SEVERAL):

| Case | Availability | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `.photoPanorama` | — | Large-format panorama |
| `.photoHDR` | — | HDR photo |
| `.photoScreenshot` | — | Screenshot |
| `.photoLive` | iOS 9.1 | Live Photo |
| `.photoDepthEffect` | iOS 10.2 | Portrait-mode depth effect |
| `.photoAnimation` | iOS 11.0 | GIF / animated PNG |
| `.videoStreamed` | — | Streamed video |
| `.videoHighFrameRate` | — | Slo-mo |
| `.videoTimelapse` | — | Time-lapse |
| `.videoCinematic` | iOS 15.0 | Cinematic mode |
| `.videoScreenRecording` | iOS 13.0 | Screen recording (⚠️ doc abstract is wrong) |
| `.spatialMedia` | iOS 16.0 **(back-dated; spatial shipped iOS 17.2 — runtime-check)** | Spatial photo or video |

Plus `PHAssetMediaSubtypeNone`.

**`PHAsset.PlaybackStyle`** (iOS 11.0+): `.unsupported`, `.image`, `.imageAnimated`, `.livePhoto`, `.video`, `.videoLooping`.
**`PHAsset.PlaybackVariation`** (iOS 11.0+): `.none`, `.autoloop`, `.mirror`, `.longExposure`.
**`PHAssetSourceType`**: how the asset entered the library (device camera / cloud shared / iTunes sync).
**`PHPickerFilter`**: `images`, `videos`, `livePhotos`, `depthEffectPhotos`, `bursts`, `panoramas`, `screenshots`, `screenRecordings`, `slomoVideos`, `timelapseVideos`, `cinematicVideos`, `spatialMedia`, `playbackStyle(_:)`, plus combinators `all(of:)` / `any(of:)` / `not(_:)`.

**`Settings > Camera > Preserve Settings` — full inventory:** `Camera Mode`, `Photographic Style`, `Creative Controls`, `Depth Control`, `Macro Control`, `Exposure Adjustment`, `Night Mode`, `Portrait Zoom`, `Action Mode`, `ProRAW & Resolution Control`, `Apple ProRes`, `Live Photo`.

**Other `Settings > Camera` toggles that materially change the captured file** (frequently overlooked): `View Outside the Frame`, `Prioritize Faster Shooting`, `Lens Correction`, `Scene Detection` (iPhone 12), `Lens Cleaning Hints`, `Save Captures to Photo Library`, and `Smart HDR` (iPhone 11 / SE 2nd gen / iPhone 12 expose a manual HDR toggle). Also **`Customize the Main camera lens`** — the default focal-length choice (e.g. 24 / 28 / 35 mm) changes what the Main/Fusion camera actually writes.

---

### 8.21 The lossless export escape hatches (exact Apple labels)

These are the paths Apple tells users to use. They are obscure, manual, and one-asset-at-a-time. **Automating them is the entire product opportunity.**

| # | Path | What it preserves | Caveat |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Settings > Apps > Photos > Keep Originals` | Defeats the USB-import transcode to JPEG/H.264 | On iOS 18+ the setting lives under `Settings > Apps > Photos`, **not** the old top-level Photos pane. Sibling option is labeled `Automatic` (*high-confidence but not first-party-documented*). |
| 2 | **iCloud Photos** | "the media is preserved in its original format, resolution, and frame rate" | Requires iCloud |
| 3 | AirDrop with `Share > Options > All Photos Data` ON, then "Save to Downloads" on the Mac | The **only** consumer path that moves depth, Cinematic focus metadata, the ProRAW DNG **and** the edited JPG, and the edits together | Manual, per-share |
| 4 | `Duplicate` → `Edit` → `Revert` → AirDrop | Extracts an untouched ProRAW original from an edited asset | Apple's own recommended dance. Absurd. |
| 5 | Mac Photos: `File > Export > Export Unmodified Original` | The original bytes | ⚠️ **DROPS the user's edits** |
| — | Import via **Image Capture** (Mac) or the **Windows Photos** app over USB | Apple's recommended way to get **both** the ProRAW DNG and the edited JPG | Requires `Keep Originals` |

**Lossy by design — do not route through these:** `Mail` (converts ProRAW → JPG; sends a Live Photo as a still image), `Messages`/AirDrop to a non-HEVC-capable device (auto-converts to "a more compatible format, such as JPEG or H.264"), and any third-party re-encode.

⚠️ **Trap for a desktop companion app:** if you ingest over USB and the user has `Automatic` set, **the phone downconverts before you ever see the bytes** — and you get blamed. This is the #1 cause of "my ProRAW/HEIC turned into a JPEG" bug reports filed against innocent third-party importers. Either tell the user to set `Keep Originals`, or **detect the transcode** (the delivered file is JPEG while the asset's `uniformTypeIdentifier` says HEIC) and warn. On-device, PhotoKit is unaffected by this setting.

---

### 8.22 What a third-party app can and cannot do

| Capability | Available to 3rd parties? | Mechanism / why not |
|---|---|---|
| Read every resource of an asset losslessly | **Yes** | `PHAssetResource.assetResources(for:)` + `PHAssetResourceManager.requestData` with `isNetworkAccessAllowed = true` |
| Capture HEIF/HEVC or JPEG/H.264 | **Yes** — and **not bound by the user's `Formats` setting** | `AVCapturePhotoOutput` + `AVCapturePhotoSettings(format:)`; your app picks its own codec |
| Capture 24 MP / 48 MP | **Yes** | `AVCapturePhotoOutput.maxPhotoDimensions`, `AVCaptureDevice.Format.supportedMaxPhotoDimensions` |
| Capture Apple ProRAW (linear DNG) | **Yes** | `isAppleProRAWSupported`/`Enabled`; `isAppleProRAWPixelFormat(_:)` vs `isBayerRAWPixelFormat(_:)`; `rawFileType = .dng` |
| Capture ProRes video | **Yes** | `AVVideoCodecType.proRes422` / `.proRes422HQ` / `.proRes422LT` / `.proRes422Proxy` / `.proRes4444` |
| Capture **ProRes RAW** (iPhone 17 Pro) | **UNVERIFIED** | Apple Newsroom says only "using applications such as Final Cut Camera." No public AVFoundation path confirmed. **Do not plan around it.** |
| **Genlock** to an external reference | **Yes** | Apple Newsroom (2025-09-09): "Genlock API support is available to third parties" — already used by the Blackmagic Design Camera ProDock |
| Capture Live Photos | **Yes** | `AVCapturePhotoOutput.isLivePhotoCaptureEnabled` + `AVCapturePhotoSettings.livePhotoMovieFileURL`; `isLivePhotoAutoTrimmingEnabled` |
| Write a real Live Photo into the library | **Yes** | `PHAssetCreationRequest` + `.photo` **and** `.pairedVideo` resources — **both files must already carry the matching UUID** (MakerApple key `17` / `com.apple.quicktime.content.identifier`) or Photos ingests a dead still + orphan video |
| **Set** a Live Photo playback variation (Loop / Bounce / Long Exposure) | **No** | Read-only (`PHAsset.playbackVariation`). You can replicate the effect with `PHLivePhotoEditingContext`, but you cannot ask Photos to mark the asset |
| Capture depth / portrait matte / semantic mattes | **Yes** | `isDepthDataDeliveryEnabled` + **`embedsDepthDataInPhoto`** (separate flag!), `isPortraitEffectsMatteDeliveryEnabled` + `embedsPortraitEffectsMatteInPhoto`, `enabledSemanticSegmentationMatteTypes` + `embedsSemanticSegmentationMattesInPhoto` |
| **Play/edit** Cinematic video | **Yes, iOS 17+** | Cinematic framework: `CNAssetInfo`, `CNScript`, `CNDecision`, `CNRenderingSession` |
| **Capture** Cinematic video | **Yes, but only iOS 26+** | `AVCaptureDeviceInput.isCinematicVideoCaptureEnabled`. Before iOS 26 this was **impossible** for third parties. Dual Wide (rear) / TrueDepth (front), 1080p & 4K @ 30 fps only |
| Render shallow depth-of-field onto a **still** | **Yes** | `CNImageRenderingSession` + `CNImageRenderingSessionConfiguration` (Cinematic framework) |
| **Capture** spatial video | **Yes, iOS 18+** | `AVCaptureMovieFileOutput.isSpatialVideoCaptureEnabled`, gated by `AVCaptureDevice.Format.isSpatialVideoCaptureSupported`. Apple handles synchronization, calibration, encoding and metadata for you |
| **Capture** spatial *photos* | **No dedicated API** | No documented AVFoundation flag equivalent to `isSpatialVideoCaptureEnabled`. Synthesize from any stereo pair via the ImageIO recipe (8.10) |
| Read/write spatial HEIC and MV-HEVC | **Yes** | ImageIO (`kCGImagePropertyGroups` / stereo pair group) and AVFoundation MV-HEVC (`AVAssetWriter` tagged buffers, iOS 17.2+) |
| Generate **Spatial Scenes** (2D → 3D) | **No public API confirmed** | Build your own monocular depth model + parallax renderer |
| Capture first-order-ambisonic **Spatial Audio** | **Yes** | `AVCaptureDeviceInput.multichannelAudioMode = .firstOrderAmbisonics` |
| Read/edit Spatial Audio mixes | **Yes** | Cinematic framework: `CNAssetSpatialAudioInfo`, `CNSpatialAudioContentType`, `CNSpatialAudioRenderingStyle` |
| Capture a **Night mode** photo | **No** | No public API. Closest: `photoQualityPrioritization = .quality` + the system's automatic low-light fusion |
| Capture **Action mode** | **No** | No public API. Closest: `preferredVideoStabilizationMode = .cinematicExtendedEnhanced` |
| Capture a **Time-lapse** | **No** | No public API. Build your own interval capture |
| Detect that a video was shot in Night / Action mode | **No** | **No `PHAssetMediaSubtype` exists for either.** Action-mode video is only inferable from its 2.8K-class dimensions; Night mode only from EXIF/maker-note forensics |
| Preserve edits + originals + `Revert` | **Yes** | `.photo` + `.fullSizePhoto` + `.adjustmentData` (+ `.adjustmentBase*`) |
| Write your own re-editable adjustments | **Yes** | `PHAdjustmentData(formatIdentifier:formatVersion:data:)` → `PHContentEditingOutput`; Photos hands it back via `canHandleAdjustmentData` |
| Read the **original** (pre-adjustment) date / location | **No** | No PhotoKit API, and no way to invoke Apple's metadata `Revert`. You must parse EXIF/GPS from the `.photo` resource bytes yourself |
| Know which resource is the RAW base of a RAW+JPEG asset | **Not today** | `PHAsset.originalResourceChoice` is **iOS 27 BETA only** |
| Convert Android Motion Photos → Live Photos | **Yes — and Apple never will** | Fully specified: extract the embedded MP4, mint a UUID, write it to MakerApple key `17` + `com.apple.quicktime.content.identifier`, create with `.photo` + `.pairedVideo` |

---

### 8.23 Where Apple is weak — our opening

- **Every "lossless" path is manual, obscure, and one-asset-at-a-time.** Apple documents the five fidelity-preserving escape hatches across **five different support articles**, and the flagship one (`Share > Options > All Photos Data`) is a per-share toggle buried two levels into a sheet. **Nothing on the market does bulk, manifest-driven, full-fidelity export** that preserves every `PHAssetResource`, the Live Photo UUID pairing, the burst grouping, the stereo pair group, the `CNScript`, and the `adjustmentData` — and can restore all of it back into a Photos library. This is the whole ballgame.

- **Apple's own ProRAW workaround is `Duplicate → Edit → Revert → AirDrop`.** That is Apple's *documented* instruction for retrieving an unmodified DNG from an asset the user edited. Any tool that simply always keeps the DNG and stores edits as a sidecar is strictly, obviously better.

- **Silent resolution downgrades users never see.** 48 MP collapses to 12 MP the moment you zoom, use Night mode, use flash, use macro, or leave the 1× Main camera — invisibly. Action mode silently caps at **2.8K**. Auto Macro silently swaps the Ultra Wide sensor in. **An importer that reads `pixelWidth`/`pixelHeight` and labels the *real* resolution is more honest than Apple's own UI.**

- **`Most Compatible` doesn't do what its name says.** It affects only new Camera-app captures. Existing assets, third-party camera apps and screenshots are untouched — which is why Apple Community is full of "I chose Most Compatible and I still get HEIC."

- **The USB transcode is under-communicated to the point of being a trap.** `Settings > Apps > Photos > Keep Originals` is the one toggle standing between a user and having their ProRAW/HEIC silently downconverted on import — and third-party importers get blamed for it. Surfacing "your phone is currently downconverting on import — here's the one toggle" is a cheap, very high-trust win.

- **Batch date adjustment has no relative shift.** Apple's batch `Adjust Date & Time` applies the **same** date to every selected photo — there is no "shift by N hours," no timezone correction, no EXIF/filename reconciliation. This is a well-known top user request. It's also trivially implementable.

- **Apple exposes no way to recover the original date/location after an adjustment**, and no API to invoke its own `Revert` — so a competitor that shows "EXIF says X, Photos says Y" is showing users something Apple structurally cannot.

- **Bursts are a double-sided failure everywhere.** Fetch without `includeAllBurstAssets` and you lose 39 of 40 frames; fetch without reading `burstIdentifier` and you flood the grid and lose the system's `autoPick` suggestions. Preserving the stack, the representative, and the suggested picks — and letting the user promote picks — is a concrete differentiator that essentially nobody ships.

- **Slo-mo is the most-reported iPhone export bug in the world.** "My slo-mo isn't slow anymore" happens because the ramp lives in `adjustmentData`, not in the pixels, and both obvious export routes are wrong in opposite ways.

- **Panoramas render as unusable slivers** in nearly every third-party grid. A full-bleed row + horizontal-scrub viewer is an easy, immediately visible win.

- **GIFs flatten to a single frame** in almost every naive importer, because `requestImage` returns one frame. Fixing this costs an afternoon.

- **Android Motion Photos are a permanent, silent, total loss for every switcher** — and there is **no first-party Apple path, and almost certainly never will be**. The conversion is fully specified (see 8.19) and there is an entire ecosystem of hobbyist tools proving demand. **This is the single highest-leverage feature a competing photo app could ship.** Note the reverse direction (Live Photo → Android) is being commoditized by Google; the Android → Apple direction is the underserved one.

- **Spatial media is invisible outside Apple's walls.** Spatial photos and videos silently flatten in almost every third-party app and every non-Apple cloud service, and users have **no way to tell which of their photos are spatial**. A grid that badges spatial assets and preserves both eyes on export is a clear, defensible differentiator.

- **Spatial Scenes has no public API — but it is the most copyable feature Apple ships.** It is on-device monocular depth estimation plus a parallax renderer. Reproducing it is a well-understood ML problem, and Apple's own version has documented reliability problems (it works poorly on photos without a clear foreground subject).

- **Photographic Styles fidelity is undocumented.** On iPhone 16+ the style is a reversible post-capture adjustment, not a baked filter — but Apple never explains this, and no third-party ingestion tool preserves it. *(Verify the exact storage mechanism on-device before relying on it.)*

- **Storage panic is real and unaddressed.** 75 MB per 48 MP ProRAW shot; ProRes on a 128 GB device is hard-capped at 1080p30; 130 MB per minute of spatial video. Apple offers no per-format budgeting, no "which formats are eating my storage" view, and no smart archival tier.

- **HDR video tone-maps silently on share** ("other devices receive an SDR version"), producing the extremely common washed-out/blown-out complaint. An app that detects Dolby Vision and offers an explicit preserve-vs-tone-map choice is differentiated on a problem Apple has chosen not to explain.

- **Apple's own documentation is wrong in places** (the `.videoScreenRecording` abstract; the back-dated `.spatialMedia` availability; "HEIF Max on iPhone 14" marketing prose that contradicts the 12 MP hardware). If you scrape Apple's docs to build your capability matrix, you will inherit their bugs.
## 9. Apple Intelligence in Photos

"Apple Intelligence" is Apple's brand for its on-device + private-server AI stack, and inside the Photos app it is far thinner than the marketing implies: as of the current shipping OS (**iOS 26.5.2**, July 2026) it amounts to exactly **three** features — `Clean Up`, natural language search, and `Create a memory movie` — all hard-gated to iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 16-or-later, 16 languages, and unavailable in mainland China. **None of the three is exposed to third-party apps in any form.** The single most important thing an implementer must know: the flagship capability everyone assumes exists — conversational, personal-context Siri that answers "show me photos of Maya at the beach last summer" from your library — **does not ship on any iPhone today**, has slipped roughly two years, and is announced only as an English-only *beta* later in 2026. That is an open field.

⚠️ **Trap (version):** `apple.com/apple-intelligence` and `apple.com/os/ios` have **already been updated to iOS 27 marketing content** (Siri AI, Spatial Reframing, Extend, photorealistic Image Playground). A researcher who lands on those pages today will mistake fall-2026 features for shipping ones. The authoritative *shipping* list is Apple Support doc **HT121115, "How to get Apple Intelligence," Published Date: July 07, 2026**, which still frames everything as "With iOS 26, iPadOS 26, and macOS Tahoe 26 and later."

---

### 9.1 Version ground truth

| State | Version | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Shipping** | iOS 26.5.x (26.5.1 released 2026-06-01; **26.5.2** current) | No Photos AI feature changed in any 26.5.x point release. Do not quote 26.5.2's exact release date — it could not be pinned to a primary Apple source. |
| **Beta** | iOS 26.6 (dev beta 5 seeded 2026-07-13; public release expected ~late July 2026) | Maintenance/bug-fix. **No new Photos AI features.** 9to5Mac reads the beta as *preparing the Spotlight index that Siri AI will use in iOS 27* — that is 9to5Mac's inference, **not an Apple statement**. |
| **Announced, not shipping** | iOS 27 (WWDC26 keynote 2026-06-08/09; ships fall 2026; currently developer beta) | Confirmed at API level, not from marketing: Apple's docs JSON marks `Attachment`, `PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel` and the custom-LLM-provider protocol as `introducedAt: 27.0, beta: true`, and marks `ImageCreator` as `deprecatedAt: 27.0`. |

### 9.2 The complete shipping feature list (iOS 26.5)

**Inside Photos, Apple Intelligence-gated — exactly three:**

| Feature | Apple's exact name | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Generative object removal | `Clean Up` | Photos → open photo → edit control → `Clean Up` |
| Semantic free-text search | "Natural language search in Photos" | Photos → `Search` |
| Text-to-highlight-reel | "Create a memory movie in Photos" | Photos → `Collections` → `Memories` → `Create` |

**Adjacent, *not* Apple Intelligence-gated (works on every iPhone):** Enhanced Visual Search (§9.6).

**Adjacent, Apple Intelligence-gated, outside Photos:** Visual Intelligence, Image Playground, Genmoji, `Image Wand` (Notes; HT121115 lists it as "Image Wand (iOS and iPadOS only)"), Writing Tools, "Intelligent actions in Shortcuts" + "Use Apple Intelligence models in Shortcuts", ChatGPT integration.

**Announced but NOT shipping:** personal-context Siri / photo search by voice (§9.9); Spatial Reframing, `Extend`, larger-object Clean Up (§9.11).

### 9.3 The Apple Intelligence gate (identical for all three Photos features)

| Requirement | Value |
|---|---|
| **iPhone models** | iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, and **iPhone 16 models or later** — i.e. 16, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max, 16e, 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, iPhone Air, 17e |
| **Other devices** | iPad with A17 Pro or M1 and later; Mac with M1 or later; Apple Vision Pro (visionOS 26); Apple Watch Series 6 and later / all Ultra / SE 2 and later **when paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone nearby** |
| **Minimum OS** | iOS 18.1 (feature floor); the three Photos features are listed under iOS 26 in HT121115 |
| **Free storage** | **7 GB** |
| **Language rule** | **Device language must equal Siri language**, and both must be one of the 16 supported languages |
| **16 supported languages** | English, Danish, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Vietnamese, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Japanese, Korean |
| **Toggle** | Settings → `Apple Intelligence & Siri` |
| **EU** | Supported since iOS 18.4 |
| **China mainland** | **Not available.** Not for devices purchased there, and not for devices purchased elsewhere if the user is in China mainland AND their Apple Account country/region is China mainland. |

⚠️ **Trap (contradictory Apple docs):** Apple's dedicated `Clean Up` requirements doc **HT121429 has a stale Published Date of April 14, 2025** and still enumerates only *"iPhone 16 models, iPhone 15 Pro, and iPhone 15 Pro Max."* It has never been revised to name iPhone 17 / iPhone Air / iPhone 17e, which **are** Apple-Intelligence-capable per the current HT121115 ("iPhone 15 Pro models, and iPhone 16 models or later"). The two Apple docs are literally inconsistent. Read HT121429 as "iPhone 16 models **or later**." Do not build a device allowlist from HT121429.

⚠️ **Trap (silent degradation):** On an unsupported iPhone, or in mainland China, the user simply gets *worse search* with **no explanation and no error**. Nothing in the UI tells them the semantic index is absent. Any competitor should treat "explain why AI is off" as a free win.

---

### 9.4 `Clean Up` — generative object removal

Generative inpainting inside the Photos editor. Apple's iPhone User Guide vocabulary, verbatim:

> "Open a photo, tap [edit], then tap **Clean Up**."
> "After you tap Clean Up, some items may be highlighted automatically so you can quickly tap to remove them."
> "**Tap, brush, or circle** what you want to remove."
> "Use **two fingers to pinch to zoom or pan** the image."
> "**If you brush over a person's face, the face may become blurred with a pixelated effect.**"
> "When you're finished, tap **Done**."
> "Clean Up is not available in all languages or regions."

The face behavior is a deliberate guardrail, not a bug: Apple **refuses clean generative removal of faces** and degrades to pixelation.

**On-device?** Clean Up works offline and is gated on the local Apple Intelligence model download, which is strong evidence it runs on-device — but **Apple has never stated this**. Mark as *inferred, not sourced*. (Contrast with iOS 27's *enhanced* Clean Up, which Apple **does** now place on a server model — see §9.10.)

⚠️ **Trap (provenance metadata — do NOT build on this):** It is widely repeated that Clean Up stamps the EXIF **Credits** field with `Modified with Clean Up`, surviving iMessage/AirDrop but lost via WhatsApp. **There is no Apple documentation for this anywhere.** The sole source is a single iDownloadBlog hands-on from **2024-08-29 testing iOS 18.1 beta 3** — two years and two major OS versions stale. Nothing verifies iOS 26 still writes the tag, still uses the Credits field, or preserves it across transports. Treat as *plausible, press-sourced, unverified on iOS 26*. Separately: **do not claim Apple emits C2PA / Content Credentials on Clean Up edits** — no source establishes that either way.

**Documented weaknesses (sourced):** (1) Fill/reconstruction quality rates **behind Google's Magic Eraser / Magic Editor** in head-to-head reviews, because Google "factors in the surroundings of the object being removed" and Apple's fill is less context-aware. (2) Non-deterministic — accuracy "isn't always consistent," results "varied each time" on the same image. (3) The face-pixelation guardrail means it cannot do the thing many users actually want (remove a photobomber). (4) Hard device gate excludes iPhone 15 / 15 Plus and every base model before 16, and excludes mainland China entirely. (5) Reviewers **do** credit Apple's *selection* ergonomics (one-pass auto-highlight vs. Google's piecemeal selection) — so Apple's edge here is UX, not model quality. **Beat the fill, keep the selection ergonomics.**

### 9.5 Natural language search in Photos

Free-text semantic search over the library, "including a key moment in a video." Apple's own guide: *"Apple Intelligence makes it even easier to find a specific photo or a key moment in a video—just describe what you want to find."*

Apple's chosen example queries (use these as your baseline test set — they are Apple's *best case*):
- `Maya skateboarding in a tie-dye shirt`
- `Sadie cartwheeling on the grass`

Result-view affordances, Apple's exact labels: `See All` · `Select` (then share or add to album) · `Sort by Recently Added` / `Sort by Date Captured` · `Filter` → e.g. `Favorites`, `Edited`.

**Person/pet names resolve only via the Photos People & Pets naming graph** — "Maya" matches nothing unless the user has named her there. Apple's guide makes the dependency explicit.

**How it works:** an on-device semantic index combining a vision-language embedding with the named People & Pets graph. Apple publishes no architecture. *Inferred:* it appears to work offline and is gated on the local model download, but no Apple source states on-device vs Private Cloud Compute. Also ships on **visionOS 26**.

**Documented failure modes — this is Apple's weakest link and the best wedge:**

| Failure | Evidence |
|---|---|
| **Time-of-day / lighting terms return nothing** | Searches for someone "at night," and the variants "at sunset," "after dark," "in the evening," all came up blank (BGR) |
| **Compositional color+object queries fail** | `yellow car` returned **no cars at all**, while plain `car` returned yellow cars at the top (Tom's Guide) — a textbook attribute-binding failure indicating a weak, bag-of-concepts retrieval model |
| **Text visible in the image isn't reliably searchable** | A photo captioned "gym tag" returned nothing for that query (BGR) |
| **Indexing stalls** | Long-standing user reports of Photos "endlessly analyzing the library," leaving search and dependent features "extremely limited or unusable" (Apple Community thread 255823627) |

BGR's verdict: the feature "still needs a lot of work."

### 9.6 `Create a memory movie in Photos`

Text-to-memory-movie. Apple's description, verbatim: *"Just type a description, and Apple Intelligence finds the best photos and videos, crafts a storyline with unique chapters and a narrative arc, and sets it to music."*

Exact navigation (real vocabulary an implementer needs): Photos → tap `Collections` → tap `Memories` → tap `Create` → *"Enter a description of the movie you want to create from your library"* → tap `Done`.

Note the information architecture: **it is buried under Collections → Memories, not under any top-level "AI" surface.** Also ships on visionOS 26.

**How it works:** an LLM generates a chaptered storyline / narrative arc from the prompt; the semantic index selects matching assets; the system scores and orders clips and picks a soundtrack. *Inferred, not sourced:* whether the storyline step runs on-device or routes to Private Cloud Compute — Apple has not said.

⚠️ **Trap (don't fabricate a complaint corpus):** There is **essentially no substantive body of specific complaints about memory-movie quality**. Its low mindshare is itself the signal. Treat "users hate memory movies" as **UNVERIFIED**. What *is* sourced: memory movies depend entirely on the retrieval layer of §9.5, and that layer demonstrably fails on time-of-day, color+object binding, and in-image text. A storyline is only as good as its asset retrieval, so Apple's retrieval weaknesses propagate here by construction.

### 9.7 Enhanced Visual Search — the one Photos AI feature on *every* iPhone

Easy to miss and structurally different from everything above. Enhanced Visual Search lets you search your library for **landmarks and points of interest** — Apple's examples: *"the Golden Gate Bridge or the Arc de Triomphe"* — and returns every photo/video in which that landmark is visible, **even if the media has no geolocation metadata**. Searchable from the Photos app **and from Spotlight**.

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| **Toggle (iPhone/iPad)** | `Settings` → `Apps` → `Photos` → `Enhanced Visual Search` |
| **Toggle (Mac)** | `Photos` → `Settings` → `General` → `Enhanced Visual Search` |
| **Minimum OS** | iOS 18 / iPadOS 18 / macOS Sequoia |
| **Device gate** | **NONE.** Runs on **all** iPhones. No A17 Pro requirement, no 15 Pro requirement, no Apple Intelligence toggle. |
| **Region** | "Enhanced Visual Search isn't available in all countries or regions." |
| **Default state** | Widely reported as **on by default** — but note this is **press-sourced (the Jan 2025 Jeff Johnson controversy), not stated in Apple's doc**. |
| **Apple doc** | support.apple.com/en-us/122033, published 2025-09-15 |

⚠️ **Trap (this is NOT a local feature):** Despite living behind a Photos toggle, **Enhanced Visual Search sends data to Apple's servers.** Apple's own doc: an on-device model produces *"a low-fidelity mathematical representation… called an embedding. This embedding — not image data — is encrypted and sent to Apple servers, where it's compared against a global list of landmarks and places that's too big to fit on your device."* Anyone who characterizes it as on-device is wrong, and for a privacy-positioned product this is the single most important fact about it.

**The privacy architecture (worth stealing wholesale):**
1. On-device ML model decides whether a photo likely contains a landmark.
2. It computes a **low-fidelity embedding** of the region of interest — pixels never leave the device.
3. The embedding is encrypted with **homomorphic encryption**; Apple matches it against the global index **without decrypting it**. Decryption keys never leave the device.
4. **Differential privacy:** the device sends **fake decoy requests** alongside the real one, so the server cannot tell which is genuine.
5. An **OHTTP relay run by a third party** strips the IP address before the request reaches Apple.
6. Apple states the request is not stored, not linked to the Apple Account, and not used to improve the global index.

**The lesson, precisely stated:** the technology was genuinely privacy-preserving and it **still cost Apple trust** — purely because it was **opt-out rather than opt-in and undisclosed at setup**. When researchers noticed in Jan 2025, Forbes ran it as Apple's *"secretive new update surprises users,"* a wave of how-to-disable articles followed (Pocket-lint: *"I disabled Apple's Enhanced Visual Search and you might want to as well"*), and Macworld and 9to5Mac had to publish defenses explaining Apple isn't spying. If our app does *any* server-assisted photo analysis: make it **opt-IN**, disclose it in onboarding, explain it in one sentence a human can read.

### 9.8 Visual Intelligence (camera + onscreen)

Two distinct surfaces, both shipping.

**(A) Camera surface** — click-and-hold the **Camera Control**:

| Capability | Apple's labels |
|---|---|
| Business/restaurant lookup | `Schedule`, `Order`, `Menu`, `Reserve` |
| Identify plants and animals | — |
| Interact with text | `Summarize`, `Translate`, `Read Aloud`, plus tap-to-call / email / create-event |
| Visual web search | "Search Google and across supported apps" |
| Poster/flyer → event | `Add to Calendar` → `Create Event` |

**(B) Onscreen surface (new in iOS 26)** — press the normal screenshot chord (side + volume up); visual-intelligence tools appear at the bottom of the screenshot: search the web for similar items; **"Swipe your finger on a specific item to highlight it and search for that particular item"**; `Ask ChatGPT`; `Add to Calendar`; tap through to a relevant website; `Summarize`; `Read Aloud`; tap an identified plant/animal. Then delete or save the screenshot.

**Invocation matrix** — Apple names the exception models exactly:

| Models | How Visual Intelligence is invoked |
|---|---|
| iPhone 16 / 17 series with Camera Control | Click-and-hold the **Camera Control** |
| **iPhone 17e, iPhone 16e, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max** (no Camera Control) | Customize the **Action button**, add a **visual intelligence control to the Lock Screen**, or open **Control Center** |
| All Apple Intelligence iPhones | Onscreen surface via screenshot chord (it's a button chord, not Camera Control) |

**Language carve-out:** the **place-identification-by-camera** language list is *narrower* than the general 16: Chinese, Dutch, Danish, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Vietnamese — **no Korean.**

**How it works:** hybrid. On-device detection/classification and OCR; **visual web search is delegated to a search provider** (Apple explicitly warns: *"Subject to your search provider's terms of use and data privacy policies"*); the conversational layer is delegated to **ChatGPT** via the optional extension.

⚠️ **Trap (Visual Intelligence does NOT search your library):** Apple's Visual Intelligence searches the **web** and **third-party apps**. It does **not** search the user's own photo library. That gap is precisely what the Visual Intelligence *framework* lets a third-party app fill (§9.13) — and it is the strongest distribution hook available to a competing photo app.

**Weaknesses:** fragmented invocation (three different gestures for one feature; Apple's own docs need a table); the reasoning layer is outsourced to ChatGPT, so it is region-gated to ChatGPT availability, requires a separate opt-in extension, and consumes ChatGPT tokens; search-result quality is bounded by the third-party search provider.

### 9.9 Image Playground, Genmoji, Image Wand, Writing Tools

These are Apple Intelligence surfaces *adjacent* to Photos — none of them lives inside the Photos editor, but all of them touch photo content.

**Image Playground** (separate app + system sheet). Shipping iOS 26 styles: `Animation`, `Illustration`, `Sketch`, plus **five ChatGPT-powered styles** new in iOS 26 — `Anime`, `Oil Painting`, `Print`, `Vector`, `Watercolor` — plus an **`Any Style`** free-text mode (e.g. "Van Gogh," "photorealism"). Can start from a text description or an existing photo; output lands in the photo library. Apple's own styles run on-device; **the five new styles and Any Style route to ChatGPT**, which is why they consume ChatGPT tokens.

Documented reception: the most-mocked Apple Intelligence feature at launch — quality reported as "incredibly poor" and "terrible," the canonical example being **a hand with six fingers**; **cartoon-only aesthetic** while every competitor did photorealism; repetitive/uninspired results; **strict content filters** and **inaccurate likenesses** of people. TechCrunch's framing of the iOS 26 fix: Apple is *"salvaging Image Playground with a boost from ChatGPT"* — i.e. **the good styles are ChatGPT's, not Apple's**, and per press reports they "require ChatGPT tokens, which in practice means you're limited to one or two images unless you pay for a ChatGPT subscription" (the one-or-two figure is **press-sourced, not Apple**).

**Genmoji.** User-generated emoji from a text description, and — since iOS 18.2 — **from a photo of a person in your library**, producing a Genmoji that resembles them. This is a **direct consumer of the People & Pets graph**: Apple's source is explicitly "a person identified in your Photos library." Exact UI labels for the person-seeded flow: `Choose a Person`, `Choose Other Photo`, `Customize Appearance` (hairstyle, facial hair, eyewear options). Genmoji are inserted inline in text as adaptive image glyphs, behave like characters, and are usable as stickers. iOS 26 added ChatGPT-backed styles here too. **There is no Genmoji surface inside the Photos editor.** Better received than Image Playground, but documented complaints are **strict content filters (refusals)** and **inaccurate likenesses** of real people.

**Image Wand.** Listed on HT121115 as a shipping iOS 26 feature — "Image Wand (iOS and iPadOS only)" — a first-party sketch-to-image surface in Notes. In iOS 27 it is re-listed as "Transform rough sketches into images in virtually any style right in Notes."

**Writing Tools.** Proofreading; rewriting with the three tone labels `Friendly`, `Professional`, `Concise`; a freeform **`Describe your change`** affordance (e.g. "Make this more enthusiastic"); summarization; list and table generation; and since iOS 18.2, generative composition (`Compose`) with optional ChatGPT hand-off. Relevance to a photo app: captions, album descriptions, shared-album notes, memory-movie titles. On-device for proofread/rewrite/summarize; Compose can route to ChatGPT.

⚠️ **Trap (Apple's own summarization visibly hallucinates):** The nearest adjacent Apple Intelligence text feature — **notification summaries** — mangled headlines badly enough that Apple **pulled/disabled them for news apps** after BBC complaints. Do not imitate Apple's on-device summarization quality uncritically.

### 9.10 On-device vs Private Cloud Compute — Apple now publishes the mapping

⚠️ **Trap (a widely-repeated claim that is now FALSE):** It used to be true that "Apple does not publish a per-feature on-device/PCC table." **As of WWDC26 that is no longer true.** Apple's own ML Research site names a family of **five third-generation Apple Foundation Models, "custom-built in collaboration with Google,"** and assigns each to a tier:

| Model | Tier | What it powers |
|---|---|---|
| **AFM 3 Core** | On-device | Next-gen ~3B dense model |
| **AFM 3 Core Advanced** | On-device, **tiered** | 20B **sparse** model (activates 1–4B params per request), stored in flash/NAND using Instruction-Following Pruning with per-prompt routing; natively multimodal; powers expressive voices + higher-accuracy dictation. Apple states it is **"unlocked by and optimized for our most capable Apple silicon systems"** — i.e. **Apple confirms top-tier on-device AI does NOT run on every Apple-Intelligence device.** |
| **AFM 3 Cloud** | Private Cloud Compute | Server workhorse |
| **ADM 3 Cloud** | Private Cloud Compute | **Diffusion model "for image generation and editing, which unlocks advanced photo-editing tools, the all-new Image Playground, and more."** |
| **AFM 3 Cloud Pro** | Private Cloud Compute | Agentic tool use, complex reasoning |

Two consequences an implementer must internalize:

1. **Apple's flagship iOS 27 photo-editing AI is SERVER-SIDE and METERED.** Apple's WWDC26 newsroom: *"Some Apple Intelligence features, including image generation, have daily usage limits because they rely on powerful server models. Increased access is available with most iCloud+ subscription plans."* Apple's best photo AI is **partly paywalled behind iCloud+**.
2. **"PCC runs on Apple silicon" is now materially outdated.** Apple: *"For AFM 3 Cloud Pro, we worked with Google and NVIDIA to extend Private Cloud Compute to NVIDIA GPUs in Google Cloud, while maintaining the same guarantees to protect our users' privacy."* Apple and Google issued a **joint statement**: *"the next generation of Apple Foundation Models will be based on Google's Gemini models and cloud technology."*

Apple's three stated PCC guarantees (still quoted correctly from apple.com/apple-intelligence): "Your data is never stored," "Used only for your requests," and a "verifiable privacy promise" (independently inspectable server images).

**What remains genuinely undisclosed:** whether **today's shipping** Clean Up, natural language search, and memory-movie storyline generation run wholly on-device or touch PCC. They *behave* as on-device (offline-capable, gated on the local model download) but **Apple has never said so**. If this distinction is load-bearing for privacy marketing, it needs **empirical verification** — airplane-mode testing plus network capture on a real device — not more searching.

**ChatGPT features go to OpenAI, not PCC.** Apple's docs are explicit that this is a third-party service subject to OpenAI's terms — this is the visible seam in Apple's privacy narrative. *"Integration with ChatGPT is available only in regions where ChatGPT app and service is available. Refer to Open AI for ChatGPT availability."*

### 9.11 Siri's photo capabilities — the headline gap (NOT SHIPPING)

The promised behavior — ask Siri "show me photos of Maya at the beach last summer," have Siri use personal context across Messages/Mail/Photos, act on on-screen content, and chain in-app actions (Apple's own 2024 example: *"Make this photo black and white and send it to my wife"*) — **is not available on any shipping iPhone as of 2026-07-14.**

HT121115, **republished July 7, 2026**, still closes the iOS 26 feature list with the verbatim sentence:

> **"More personal Siri features are still in development and will be available in future software updates."**

What Siri **can** do today, verbatim from HT121115: *"Siri enhancements, like product knowledge, more resilient request handling, more natural voice, and the ability to type to Siri"* — plus ChatGPT hand-off. **That is all.** No photo search by voice.

**Slippage history:** promised WWDC24 (June 2024) → delayed March 2025 → "this fall" 2025 → "spring 2026" → now announced as **"Siri AI"** at WWDC26. Apple's own words for the delay: it *"did not converge in the way, quality-wise, that we needed it to."* The delay drew **false-advertising lawsuits** and forced Apple to **withdraw an ad campaign**. This is not a quality complaint; it is a **non-delivery** complaint, roughly two years running.

**What Siri AI is announced to do** (Apple Newsroom, WWDC26, verbatim): *"It can draw on personal context understanding to search across messages, emails, photos, and more… A dedicated Siri app allows users to revisit a past conversation or kick off a new one — all in one place — and uses iCloud to privately sync conversational history."* Underpinned by a **Spotlight semantic index of app content** populated via App Intents entity schemas.

⚠️ **Trap (the ship date is much softer than "iOS 27, fall 2026"):** Apple does **not** say Siri AI lands with iOS 27 GA. Apple Newsroom: *"Siri AI will be available as a **BETA** later this year for users with a supported device set to **ENGLISH**, and Apple will quickly expand support for more languages."* The apple.com/apple-intelligence banner reads *"Siri AI coming in English later this year."* So at consumer launch it is **(a) a beta, (b) English-only, (c) decoupled from the iOS 27.0 GA date.** It is not yet even in developer testing on watchOS (*"Siri AI will be available for developer testing in a future watchOS 27 beta"*).

**Regional carve-outs — note the carve-IN that is usually dropped:**
- *"Siri AI will not be available initially in the EU in **iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS**."*
- **BUT:** *"**Mac and Apple Vision Pro users in the EU WILL be able to access Siri AI** when set to a supported language."*
- *"Siri AI and the other new Apple Intelligence features **will not be available in China** while Apple works through regulatory requirements."* (Apple-confirmed verbatim.)

**Hardware tiering:** Apple now **confirms** the top on-device model is hardware-gated (AFM 3 Core Advanced "unlocked by and optimized for our most capable Apple silicon systems"). The specific chip name **"A19 Pro" remains press-sourced (TechCrunch/AppleInsider), not Apple-confirmed.** Likewise, the claim that Siri AI is built on a **Google Gemini-derived model** is now supported by the official Apple–Google joint statement (§9.10), though Apple's newsroom release itself does not name Google.

### 9.12 iOS 27 Photos AI (ANNOUNCED — do NOT treat as shipping)

Apple's Photos editor gains three Apple Intelligence tools in iOS 27, per apple.com and the WWDC26 newsroom (all verbatim):

| Tool | Apple's words |
|---|---|
| **Spatial Reframing** | *"Reframe a photo after it's been taken with Spatial Reframing."* / *"Move the viewpoint, adjust the angle, or zoom in as if you were repositioning the camera in the moment."* / Newsroom: *"enables users to improve the composition of a photo after it's been taken."* This is **novel-view synthesis, not cropping.** |
| **`Extend`** | *"Expand your shots with the Extend tool."* — generative outpainting beyond the original frame. |
| **`Clean Up` (enhanced)** | *"Remove even larger objects with the enhanced Clean Up tool."* |

Also in iOS 27, in-domain and easy to miss:
- **Image Playground rebuilt** on a new generative model running on **Private Cloud Compute**, with native **photorealistic** generation and natural-language + touch refinement: *"Create unique, high-quality images in just about any style, including photorealistic. Modify and transform your images with just a description or using touch."*
- **Photos search itself is being rebuilt:** *"In Spotlight, Photos, and Mail, the search experience has been rebuilt to make it more stable and efficient."* Plus *"photos load up to 70 percent faster after being taken"* and *"iCloud Shared Albums introduce cross-platform photo sharing with full-resolution support."*
- **Visual Intelligence expands:** "Siri mode in Camera"; Visual Intelligence comes to Mac (screenshot-based), iPad (*"tap the item with your finger or circle it with Apple Pencil"*), and Apple Vision Pro (*"simply look at something"*); new smart actions (split the bill, nutritional info on a dish, import a card to Apple Wallet).
- **Home app AI video search:** *"describing what happened in a selection of HomeKit Secure Video footage before you watch, and using AI to search for a clip based on what happened."* — Apple shipping **semantic search over video of people in your home**, gated behind **iCloud+**.
- **Shortcuts:** adds "Describe a shortcut" (natural-language shortcut authoring).

**iOS 27 device list, quoted verbatim from Apple:** *"iPhone 16 models or later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, iPad mini (A17 Pro), iPad models with M1 or later, MacBook Neo (A18 Pro), Mac with M1 or later, Apple Vision Pro, Apple Watch Series 9 or later…"* (MacBook Neo (A18 Pro) is a real shipping Mac, not a typo.) Same 16 languages at announcement.

⚠️ **Trap (a fall-2026 expiry date on "better Clean Up"):** Apple is moving up-market into generative photo editing — outpainting, view synthesis, larger-object removal — in roughly three months. **Any product whose only differentiator is "better Clean Up" is dead by fall 2026.** The defensible ground is the layer Apple is *not* building for iPhone: retrieval, library-scale reasoning, a conversational agent over your own photos, and the devices/regions Apple excludes. There is **no announced API** for Spatial Reframing, Extend, or the enhanced Clean Up — expect them to remain first-party-only, consistent with Apple's unbroken pattern of shipping **zero generative photo-editing APIs**.

---

### 9.13 What a third-party app can and cannot do

**The one-sentence asymmetry to internalize: Apple gives third parties excellent image ANALYSIS and SEGMENTATION, and ZERO image GENERATION / INPAINTING outside the Image Playground sheet.**

| Capability | Available to 3rd parties? | Mechanism / why not |
|---|---|---|
| **Clean Up / generative inpainting / generative fill** | **NO** | No public API anywhere in the SDK. PhotoKit gives asset access and edit round-tripping (`PHContentEditingInput` / `PHContentEditingOutput`, adjustment data) but no Apple inpainting model. **You get the MASK, never the FILL.** Bring your own inpainting model (Core ML / MLX / Core AI). This is the largest capability gap you must fill yourself — and the largest moat, since Apple will not hand it to anyone. |
| **Object selection / masking (the *selection* half of Clean Up)** | **YES** | **Vision**: `GenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest` (subject lift), saliency requests. **iOS 27 beta:** `GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest` — *"A request that generates a segmentation mask from points, a rectangle, or a scribble"* — tap-to-segment with add/remove-point refinement. Effectively hands developers Clean Up's selection UX. |
| **Natural-language / semantic photo search** | **NO** | Apple exposes **no semantic-photo-search API and no embeddings API**. PhotoKit (`PHAsset`, `PHAssetCollection`, `PHFetchOptions`) gives predicate queries over metadata only — date, location, media type, favorite, burst, album membership, limited face/person data. There is **no access to Apple's semantic index**. WWDC26 session 237 confirms: *"No explicit embeddings API," "No dedicated semantic search API."* |
| **Text→image retrieval (CLIP-style)** | **NO (must build)** | Vision's `GenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest` gives **image↔image** similarity only. It is **NOT a joint text-image embedding** and cannot do text→image retrieval. You must ship your own vision-language model (CLIP/SigLIP-class) via Core ML / MLX / Core AI and build your own index. |
| **Memory movies / storylines / auto-highlight reels** | **NO** | No memory-movie API, no storyline API, no auto-highlight API. No PhotoKit or App Intents surface lets a third party create, read, or trigger a Memory. Photos' own Memories are **not exposed as a readable collection type**. You must build the whole pipeline: prompt → retrieval → shot selection → pacing → music. |
| **Enhanced Visual Search (landmark index)** | **NO** app-level API — **BUT the architecture is replicable** | No API for the feature. However Apple **open-sourced its homomorphic-encryption work** (`swift-homomorphic-encryption`) and the Private Information Retrieval pattern, and **OHTTP relays are available to apps**. The pattern — on-device embedding → encrypted server-side ANN lookup against a large index → OHTTP → DP decoys — is a credible way to offer big-index visual lookup without a scary privacy story. **Steal this wholesale.** |
| **On-device LLM** | **YES — free, offline, no API key, no entitlement** | **Foundation Models framework**, shipping since **iOS 26.0** (also iPadOS/macOS/visionOS 26.0; watchOS 27.0 beta). `SystemLanguageModel.default` = the same **~3B-parameter** on-device model that powers Apple Intelligence. Guided generation via `@Generable` (schema-constrained decoding — the framework *guarantees* valid instances of your Swift type, not prompt-and-pray); tool calling via the `Tool` protocol; streaming; `Instructions` / `Prompt` / `Transcript` / `GenerationOptions`; a `contentTagging` use case (topics, actions, objects, emotions); `Guardrails` on input and output. |
| **Multimodal / image input to the on-device LLM** | **iOS 27 beta only** | `Attachment` — `Attachment(image)` inside a `Prompt`, with `.label("image-0")` to disambiguate when comparing multiple images. Gives on-device **vision**-language reasoning: captioning, scene understanding, text extraction. Plus **image-based tool calling** with Apple-supplied Vision tools the model can invoke on-device (`BarcodeReaderTool`, an OCR tool covering 30+ languages) and custom Vision-backed tools. |
| **Private Cloud Compute inference** | **iOS 27 beta only — but the commercial terms are unusually good** | `PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel()` is a **one-line swap** on `LanguageModelSession`: **32K-token context**, stronger reasoning, **no API keys, no auth, no server to run, no per-token bill to you.** Cost is borne by the **user's daily request quota tied to their iCloud+ subscription**; read `quotaUsage` / `isLimitReached` and Apple provides system UI to prompt an iCloud+ upgrade. Requires the `com.apple.developer.private-cloud-compute` entitlement. Per the WWDC26 guide, **Small Business Program apps (<2M first-time downloads) get PCC API costs free.** |
| **Bring-your-own LLM behind Apple's API** | **iOS 27 beta only** | A public **`LanguageModel` / `LanguageModelExecutor` provider protocol** lets you run *any* model — Claude, Gemini, a self-hosted fine-tune, a local open-weights model — behind the same Foundation Models API surface, plus `DynamicProfile` for hot-swapping models/tools/instructions at runtime (WWDC26 session 339). Clean architecture: **on-device by default, cloud on opt-in.** |
| **Image generation (Image Playground)** | **YES today — but being CLOSED** | See the trap below. |
| **Genmoji generation** | **NO — render/store only** | No API to programmatically generate a Genmoji. You **receive** them from the text-input system as **`NSAdaptiveImageGlyph`** (iOS 18.0+). Free if you use `UITextView`/`NSTextView` on TextKit 2. Persist via `imageContent`; reconstruct via `init(imageContent:)`; `contentIdentifier` and `contentDescription` (alt text) available. The closest generation path is the `.emoji` `ImagePlaygroundStyle` via the sheet. |
| **Writing Tools** | **YES — nearly free** | If your text views are `UITextView` / `NSTextView` / `WKWebView` **running on TextKit 2**, Writing Tools appears **automatically with zero code**. Tune with `writingToolsBehavior` on `UITextInputTraits` (`.complete`, `.limited`, `.none`).
