Custom text engines adopt **`UIWritingToolsCoordinator`** (public since iOS 18.2); custom text views get the callout-bar entry point via `UITextInteraction`. **Action item: make every caption/description field TextKit 2 so we inherit this for free.** |
| **Appear inside Apple's own visual-search results** | **YES — and this is a distribution channel, not just an API** | **Visual Intelligence framework** (iOS 26.0, non-beta; macOS 27.0 beta). Implement an App Intents `IntentValueQuery` whose input is a **`SemanticContentDescriptor`** — carrying `pixelBuffer` (the captured scene: screenshot, photo, or photo/video stream) and `labels` (Visual Intelligence's own classification). Match against your content, return `AppEntity` results; Apple renders them in the visual-search sheet using your entity's `DisplayRepresentation` (title, subtitle, image); tapping deep-links into your app. Apple advises **returning ~100 results max** for latency. **Consequence: a photo app can register to answer "find this in my library" from Apple's own camera/screenshot UI — the user points their camera at a friend or a place and OUR app surfaces their matching photos, inside Apple's own surface.** (WWDC26 session 297.) |
| **Plug into Siri / Spotlight semantic search** | **YES — indirectly, and the plumbing ships TODAY** | You cannot call Siri's photo brain. But **App Intents** is how you plug into it: define **App Entities** and adopt **entity schemas** so your content enters the **Spotlight semantic index**; define **intent schemas** so natural-language actions work without hard-coded phrases; and use the WWDC26 **View Annotations API** to map on-screen views to entities so Siri can discuss what the user is looking at *inside your app*. Sessions: 240 (App Schemas), 343, 345, 246 (LLM search using Core Spotlight), AppIntentsTesting (295). **Strategic read: because Apple's own Siri cannot search photos today, and App Intents lets a third-party app answer photo queries from Spotlight/Siri, a competing photo app that ships great App Intents coverage NOW can be the thing that answers "show me photos of…" on iPhone before Apple's own Photos app can — and it stays plugged in when Siri AI lands.** |
| **General image understanding (unrestricted)** | **YES — no AI gate at all** | **Vision framework**: image classification; **saliency** (attention-based and objectness-based, for smart cropping); **feature prints** (image↔image similarity); object detection/tracking; contour detection; text detection + **OCR**; **face detection / face tracking / face landmarks / face capture quality**; human body detection; **body pose**; hand pose; animal recognition (cats/dogs); barcode detection; rectangle/horizon detection; optical flow; **person segmentation**; document detection; foreground-instance masking. **Entirely on-device, all iPhones, no Apple Intelligence dependency, no region gate, no language gate — works in mainland China.** Vision as a whole now also supports watchOS (WWDC26 session 237). |
| **Ship your own models on-device** | **YES** | **Core AI** (new, WWDC26 session 324) — Apple describes it as *"the inference framework powering on-device Apple Intelligence. And now, it's available for you to use."* Full lifecycle: Python libraries for converting/authoring/optimizing models; a modern **Swift** API for plug-and-play inference *and* advanced low-latency/low-memory use; a Core AI **models repository** with ready-to-run examples; Instruments profiling; model specialization/caching; **Xcode ahead-of-time model compilation**; inference across CPU/GPU/Neural Engine. Sessions 324–326. Plus **Core ML** and **MLX**. Pair with the new **Evaluations framework** (sessions 298/299/335) for prompt/model regression testing. |
| **No-code access to the same on-device model** | **YES** | HT121115 lists **both** "Intelligent actions in Shortcuts" **and** "Use Apple Intelligence models in Shortcuts" as shipping iOS 26 features — a no-Swift path to the same model, useful for automation and rapid prototyping. |
| **Proxy ChatGPT through Apple** | **NO** | Apple does not proxy ChatGPT for third-party apps. Integrate an external LLM yourself (and from iOS 27, front it with the Foundation Models `LanguageModel` provider protocol so it shares one API surface with the on-device model). |

#### Traps in the developer APIs

⚠️ **Trap: `ImageCreator` is being killed.** Today (iOS 18.1–26.x) the **ImagePlayground framework** offers two paths: (1) the **system sheet** — `.imagePlaygroundSheet(isPresented:concepts:sourceImage:onCompletion:onCancellation:)` in SwiftUI, or `ImagePlaygroundViewController` in UIKit/AppKit; and (2) **`ImageCreator`** — a **headless, programmatic** generator (`images(for:style:limit:)` returning an AsyncSequence, with `availableStyles`), meaning your app could generate images with **no Apple UI**. Available `ImagePlaygroundStyle` values: `.animation`, `.illustration`, `.sketch`, `.emoji`, `.any`, `.all`, `.externalProvider` (the ChatGPT-backed styles). **Apple's documentation marks `ImageCreator` as `deprecatedAt: 27.0`, with the message "Use ImagePlaygroundViewController or imagePlaygroundSheet."** In iOS 27, headless generation goes away and **all** image generation must go through Apple's system sheet (stated rationale, session 375: "greater image quality, built-in privacy, and a consistent user experience"), and generation moves to PCC. **Do not architect any feature that depends on silently generating images with Apple's model.** You will get Apple's UI, Apple's branding, Apple's content filters, Apple's PCC round-trip, and Apple's daily quota — or you bring your own model. (No entitlement is required to present the sheet. Framework floors: ImagePlayground iOS 18.1 / iPadOS 18.1 / macOS 15.1 / visionOS 2.4; `ImagePlaygroundStyle` iOS 18.4 / macOS 15.4 / visionOS 2.4.)

⚠️ **Trap: `@Environment(\.supportsImageGeneration)` DOES NOT EXIST.** This symbol is frequently cited and is **hallucinated** — `developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/environmentvalues/supportsimagegeneration` returns **HTTP 404**. The real environment value is **`supportsImagePlayground`**, and it is **not new in iOS 27** — it has existed since iOS 18.1 / iPadOS 18.1 / macOS 15.1 / visionOS 2.4. Correct usage: `@Environment(\.supportsImagePlayground) private var supportsImagePlayground` — *"A Boolean value that indicates whether image generation is available on the current device."* (The companion claim that "in iOS 27 the user must have image generation enabled in Settings" is **UNVERIFIED** — no Apple source found.) This is exactly the class of error that must not reach an implementer: it looks like a plausible keypath and fails.

⚠️ **Trap: the `SystemLanguageModel` availability enum has THREE cases, not two.** `SystemLanguageModel.availability` returns `.available` or `.unavailable(reason)`, and `UnavailableReason` has **`.deviceNotEligible`, `.modelNotReady`, AND `.appleIntelligenceNotEnabled`**. The third is the one that fires **most often in the field** — eligible hardware, but the user simply never turned Apple Intelligence on in Settings. Omitting it means a non-exhaustive switch and silent mishandling of the most common failure mode.

⚠️ **Trap: the 4,096-token context window is the binding constraint on the on-device LLM.** `SystemLanguageModel` has a **4,096-token context window** shared across system instructions, *all* prior turns, *every* tool call and its output, and the new prompt. Overflow raises `GenerationError.exceededContextWindowSize`. iOS 26.4 added `contextSize` on `SystemLanguageModel`, a `tokenCount(for:)` method, and a `usage` property on sessions/responses (total, cache-read, reasoning tokens) — **but the 4,096 ceiling itself did not move.** Apple ships a technote specifically on this: **TN3193**. Developers report features that work in a two-line demo and break in production because "when a chat quotes back rows of data, it fills the window faster than expected." **Do not build chat-over-your-whole-library on the on-device model** without aggressive retrieval + summarization, or a PCC (32K) fallback on iOS 27. And note: **per-image LLM captioning of a 50k-photo library with a ~3B model is a batch-indexing problem, not a query-time one.**

⚠️ **Trap: three model versions are already in the wild.** Apple retrains `SystemLanguageModel` in OS updates; there are currently **three versions** (26.0–26.3, 26.4, and 27.0), and prompt behavior shifts between them. Apple publishes guidance on versioning your prompts. **Plan for prompt regression testing from day one** (Evaluations framework, sessions 298/299/335). There is also an **`fm` CLI** and a **Foundation Models Python SDK**, the framework reportedly runs on **Linux**, and Apple has said the framework is **going open source** — so you can prototype and evaluate prompts off-device.

⚠️ **Trap: `Guardrails` will refuse things.** Foundation Models flags sensitive content on **both input and output**. For a photo app touching people and bodies, that matters — plan for refusals as a normal code path.

⚠️ **Trap: preserve `NSAdaptiveImageGlyph` or you will silently destroy users' Genmoji.** Apple's guidance is explicit and this is a common bug: *"Typically, you receive new NSAdaptiveImageGlyph objects only from the text-input system"* — and **if your app filters attributed-string attributes, you MUST preserve the `adaptiveImageGlyph` attribute (`NSAdaptiveImageGlyphAttributeName`).**

⚠️ **Trap: Apple's word is `scribble`, not "lasso."** `GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest` (iOS 27.0 / iPadOS 27.0 / macOS 27.0 / tvOS 27.0 / visionOS 27.0, **all beta; NOT on watchOS**) generates *"a segmentation mask from points, a rectangle, or a scribble."* Searching Apple's docs for "lasso" finds nothing.

⚠️ **Trap: `GenerateObjectnessBasedSaliencyImageRequest` is NOT new in iOS 27.** It has shipped since **iOS 18.0 / macOS 15.0 / tvOS 18.0 / visionOS 2.0 (non-beta)**. The only thing new in 27 is **watchOS 27.0 (beta)** support. Do not chase a beta SDK for a request you can ship today.

⚠️ **Trap: Foundation Models will be DARK in mainland China** and on every non-Apple-Intelligence device. Availability follows Apple Intelligence availability exactly. Any feature built on it **must degrade gracefully** — which is a strong argument for making Vision + your own Core ML/Core AI models the *baseline* path and Foundation Models the *enhancement* path.

⚠️ **Trap: PCC pricing above the Small Business threshold is undocumented.** The WWDC26 guide states apps under **2M first-time downloads** get PCC API costs free. **What apps above that threshold pay is not documented anywhere.** If a business model assumes free PCC at scale, that assumption is **unfunded**.

---

### 9.14 Where Apple is weak — our opening

**Retrieval is the soft underbelly.** Apple's natural-language search fails on three axes that are trivially testable and that we can beat with a competent CLIP/SigLIP-class model:
- **Temporal/lighting reasoning:** "at night," "at sunset," "after dark," "in the evening" **all return blank** (BGR).
- **Attribute binding:** `yellow car` returns **no cars at all**, while plain `car` returns yellow cars at the top (Tom's Guide). This is a bag-of-concepts retrieval model, not a compositional one.
- **OCR-in-image:** text visible in a photo is not reliably searchable — a photo captioned "gym tag" returned nothing (BGR).
- **Everything downstream inherits these failures.** Memory movies are only as good as their asset retrieval; Apple's retrieval weakness propagates into its own flagship generative Photos feature.

**Indexing is opaque and fragile.** Long-standing user reports of Photos *"endlessly analyzing the library,"* leaving search "extremely limited or unusable" (Apple Community thread 255823627), with no visible progress, no resumability, and no diagnosis. **Transparent, resumable indexing with visible progress is a free differentiator.**

**The conversational agent is a two-year no-show — and the window is closing.** Apple advertised personal-context Siri in June 2024, marketed the iPhone 16 around it, pulled it, took **false-advertising lawsuits**, **withdrew an ad campaign**, and publicly conceded it *"did not converge in the way, quality-wise, that we needed it to."* Users have been primed to want exactly this and repeatedly disappointed. **But:** when Siri AI arrives it becomes a default. Our window to establish the habit is roughly **now through October 2026** — and even then, Apple's launch is a **beta, English-only, not in the EU on iOS/iPadOS/watchOS, and not in China at all.**

**Coverage is a structural, self-inflicted gap Apple has chosen not to close.** Vision + Core ML/Core AI are **unrestricted** — no A17 Pro gate, no region gate, no language gate. A competitor building on that stack ships the same features to **every iPhone, including iPhone 14 and below, and including mainland China**, where Apple's own Photos app is AI-dead. Apple has structurally opted out of competing for those users.

**Apple's best photo AI is metered and paywalled.** Apple's WWDC26 newsroom, verbatim: *"Some Apple Intelligence features, including image generation, have daily usage limits because they rely on powerful server models. Increased access is available with most iCloud+ subscription plans."* And Image Playground's *good* styles (Anime, Oil Painting, Print, Vector, Watercolor, Any Style) route to **ChatGPT** and consume **ChatGPT tokens** — press reports converge on "one or two images unless you pay for a ChatGPT subscription." **Apple's headline generative quality is not free, is not unlimited, and is not even Apple's.** A local-first competitor can credibly say "we do this on your device, unlimited, and we never call OpenAI" — a claim **Apple itself cannot make** for these features.

**The privacy narrative has a visible seam, and Apple has already been burned in this exact domain.** Enhanced Visual Search was mathematically airtight — homomorphic encryption, differential-privacy decoys, OHTTP relay — and it **still** cost Apple trust, purely because it was **opt-out and undisclosed** (Forbes: Apple's *"secretive new update surprises users"*). Meanwhile Apple's iOS 27 flagship photo editing runs on **server** diffusion (ADM 3 Cloud) and PCC has been **extended to NVIDIA GPUs in Google Cloud**, with Apple and Google jointly stating that *"the next generation of Apple Foundation Models will be based on Google's Gemini models and cloud technology."* **A per-feature, plain-language badge — `on device` / `private cloud` / `third-party cloud` — with everything non-local opt-IN, is something Apple structurally does not offer and increasingly cannot.**

**Image generation quality has been ~18 months behind the field — and even Apple doesn't trust it.** Image Playground launched to "incredibly poor"/"terrible" reviews (the canonical example: a hand with **six fingers**), was locked to cartoon aesthetics, produced inaccurate likenesses, and was only made tolerable by outsourcing its best styles to ChatGPT. TechCrunch's framing: Apple is *"salvaging Image Playground with a boost from ChatGPT."*

**Apple's own summarization visibly hallucinates.** Notification summaries mangled headlines badly enough that Apple **pulled them for news apps** after BBC complaints. Any AI text Apple ships in a photo context should be assumed to have the same failure profile.

**Fragmented invocation.** Visual Intelligence has **three different entry gestures** depending on model (Camera Control / Action button / Lock Screen / Control Center) plus a screenshot chord — Apple's own docs need a table to explain it. And Visual Intelligence **doesn't search your own library at all** — a gap Apple leaves wide open and hands us the framework to fill.

**Where Apple is genuinely strong — don't fight it head-on:** Clean Up's *selection* ergonomics (one-pass auto-highlight) are better than Google's; PCC's developer commercial terms are genuinely excellent (no keys, no bill, iCloud+-metered); the Visual Intelligence framework is a real distribution channel; and Foundation Models gives us a free, offline, guaranteed-schema LLM. **Take all four. Fight on retrieval, coverage, transparency, and the agent.**
## 10. iCloud Photos, Sync & Storage

iCloud Photos is a **bidirectional sync of one library**, not a backup. Every device signed into the same Apple Account sees the same library; a deletion on one device is a deletion everywhere (Apple's own support page carries the heading "Photos delete from all of your devices"). The single most important fact for an implementer: **`Optimize iPhone Storage` is ON BY DEFAULT**, which means a `PHAsset` can exist on device with full metadata but *no full-resolution local resource* — every PhotoKit image/video/resource request will silently hand you a degraded proxy (or nothing at all) unless you explicitly set `isNetworkAccessAllowed = true`, whose default is `false`. The second most important fact: since **iOS 26.1** Apple ships `PHBackgroundResourceUploadExtension`, the first sanctioned way for a third-party app to have the *system* upload photo-library resources to its own server while the app is suspended — this is the entire ballgame for a competing photo sync.

### 10.1 The sync model — what iCloud Photos actually is

A single library synced bidirectionally across all devices signed into the same Apple Account. Apple (support 108782): *"iCloud Photos keeps every photo and video you take in iCloud, so you can access your library from any device, anytime — just open the Photos app. Changes you make on one device change on your other devices too."* Edits are non-destructive and the unadjusted original is retained server-side: *"iCloud stores your original photos and videos, so you can revert any changes you made, any time."* This is exactly what `PHImageRequestOptionsVersion.original` / `.unadjusted` expose.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Settings path (iOS 26) | `Settings` > `[your name]` > `iCloud` > `Photos` > `Sync this iPhone` |
| Prior label | `iCloud Photos` (iOS 15 and earlier) — Apple 105061: *"Turn on Sync this iPhone. In iOS 15 or earlier, tap to turn on iCloud Photos."* Generic Apple copy also uses `Sync this device` |
| Minimum OS (Apple-stated, verbatim) | iOS 8.3, iPadOS 13.1, macOS 10.10.3, or iCloud for Windows 7.x or later |
| Supported file types | HEIF, JPEG, RAW, PNG, GIF, TIFF, HEVC, MP4 — plus slo-mo, time-lapse, 4K video, Live Photos |
| Latency SLA | **None published.** Apple: *"Depending on your internet speed, the time it takes to see your photos and videos across your devices and iCloud.com can vary."* |
| Library size cap | **None published.** Apple 105061: *"as long as you have enough space in iCloud, you can store as many photos and videos as you want."* Practical bound = your storage plan (max 12 TB) |

**What syncs:** originals at full resolution; edits; albums and organization; Favorites; Hidden; **face information** (see below).

**What does not sync (or is recomputed per-device):** face *recognition inference* itself is on-device ML (apple.com/privacy/features: *"Face recognition and scene and object detection… happen on device instead of in the cloud"*). Memories are generated on-device.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** It is commonly repeated that "only the *name* you attach to a face syncs." That is wrong. Apple 108770 states plainly: *"When you use iCloud Photos, your photos, videos, **and face information** automatically sync to iCloud."* The Photos & Privacy legal page adds: *"When you add a name to a person in the People & Pets Album, their name **and face** will appear in Photos across all your iCloud-enabled devices."* The ML inference runs on-device; face information — not merely a label string — is synced. (What *format* that face data takes — confirmations, embeddings, crops — is **unverified**; the "mathematical signature" story comes from forums, not Apple.)

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Do not tell an implementer "captions and keywords sync on iPhone today." **Keyword tagging on iPhone is a new iOS 27 capability** (previously Mac-only). Captions/keywords only become readable from PhotoKit in iOS 27 via `PHAssetExtendedMetadata` (see §10.17).

> ⚠️ **Trap (unverified):** "Memories do not sync" is *widely* asserted and is consistent with Apple saying Memories are generated by on-device ML — but **Apple has never stated it**, and no primary source confirms it. Treat as **unverified**; do not build product logic on it.

**China mainland:** iCloud is operated by GCBD (Guizhou-Cloud Big Data) under a separate legal and operational regime. Apple links "Learn how iCloud operates in China mainland" directly from the iCloud Photos setup page. This materially changes the trust model.

### 10.2 Storage modes: `Optimize iPhone Storage` vs `Download and Keep Originals`

Two mutually exclusive modes at `Settings` > `[your name]` > `iCloud` > `Photos`. Mac equivalents (Photos > Settings > iCloud tab): `Download Originals to this Mac` / `Optimize Mac Storage`.

| Mode | Behavior (Apple, verbatim) |
|---|---|
| `Optimize iPhone Storage` | **ON BY DEFAULT.** *"Optimize iPhone Storage is turned on by default, but you can turn it off."* *"all your full-resolution photos and videos are stored in iCloud in their original formats, with storage-saving versions kept on your iPhone."* |
| `Download and Keep Originals` | Full-resolution kept on device **and** in iCloud. |

Eviction is demand-driven and LRU-ish, not eager: *"Your library also optimizes when you need space, starting with photos and videos you access least, and you can download originals over Wi-Fi or cellular."*

> ⚠️ **Trap:** **Apple does not publish the proxy resolution or file size.** It says only "space-saving versions" / "storage-saving versions." Every specific figure you will find ("sized to your screen resolution," "50–90% smaller," specific pixel dimensions) is from blogs, not Apple. Do not put a number in a spec. The only thing you can rely on is the API contract in §10.3.

### 10.3 Fetching cloud-only originals from PhotoKit (the core implementer contract)

When an asset has been optimized away, the `PHAsset` still exists with full metadata but has no full-res local resource. This is the #1 thing an implementer must handle.

**`PHImageRequestOptions`** (iOS 8.0+) surface:

| Property | Notes |
|---|---|
| `isNetworkAccessAllowed` | **Bool, default `false`.** Apple: *"If NO (the default), and the image is not on the local device, the `PHImageResultIsInCloudKey` value in the result handler's info dictionary indicates that the image is not available unless you enable network access."* |
| `progressHandler` | `PHAssetImageProgressHandler` — called periodically during the iCloud download with a 0.0–1.0 `Double`, an error, a stop pointer, and an info dict. This is how you build a download progress bar. |
| `deliveryMode` | `.opportunistic` = *"automatically provides one or more results in order to balance image quality and responsiveness"* — **your result handler is called MULTIPLE times** (degraded first, then final). `.highQualityFormat` = *"only the highest-quality image available, regardless of how much time it takes."* `.fastFormat` = *"only a fast-loading image, possibly sacrificing image quality."* With `isSynchronous = true`, `deliveryMode` is forced to `.highQualityFormat`. |
| `version` | `.current` (edits applied) / `.unadjusted` / `.original` (*"the original, highest-fidelity version"*) |
| `resizeMode`, `normalizedCropRect` | Standard |
| `preferHDR`, `targetHDRHeadroom`, `allowSecondaryDegradedImage` | *"Request HDR image data if available (such as PQ/HLG formats)."* |

> ⚠️ **Trap:** `preferHDR`, `targetHDRHeadroom`, and `allowSecondaryDegradedImage` are **NOT new** — they are **iOS 17.0 / iPadOS 17.0 / macOS 14.0 / tvOS 17.0 / visionOS 1.0**. They have shipped for ~3 years. Do not gate them behind an iOS 26/27 availability check.

**Result info dictionary keys:** `PHImageResultIsInCloudKey`, `PHImageResultIsDegradedKey`, `PHImageResultRequestIDKey`, `PHImageCancelledKey`, `PHImageErrorKey`.

`PHImageResultIsInCloudKey` — Apple: *"If true, no image was provided, because the asset data must be downloaded from iCloud. To download the data, submit another request, and specify true for the `isNetworkAccessAllowed` option."*

> ⚠️ **Trap:** A `nil` image with `PHImageResultIsInCloudKey == true` is **not an error** — it is the documented signal to re-request with network access. Apps that treat it as failure ship the classic "my photos are blurry / can't export originals" bug.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** There is **no public API to ask whether an asset is local** without issuing a request (no public `isCloudPlaceholder`). The sanctioned pattern is a probe request with `isNetworkAccessAllowed = false`, then inspect `PHImageResultIsInCloudKey`. It is awkward and there is no alternative.

`isNetworkAccessAllowed` exists identically on `PHVideoRequestOptions`, `PHLivePhotoRequestOptions`, `PHAssetResourceRequestOptions`, and `PHContentEditingInputRequestOptions` — all default `false`.

**Error codes** (`PHPhotosError.Code`, iOS 13.0+): `.networkAccessRequired` (*"the request for an asset resource fails because it requires network access"*), `.networkError`, `.missingResource`, `.notEnoughSpace`, `.userCancelled`, `.limitExceeded`, `.requestNotSupportedForAsset`. `PHAsset` also exposes `isSyncFailureHidden` — *"A Boolean value that indicates whether the user hides the sync failure message"* (a per-asset UI flag, not a sync-status API).

**Byte-exact originals:** do **not** use `PHImageManager` (it re-encodes/renders). Use `PHAssetResource.assetResources(for:)` + `PHAssetResourceManager.default().requestData(for:options:dataReceivedHandler:completionHandler:)` or `.writeData(for:toFile:options:completionHandler:)` (iOS 9.0+), with `PHAssetResourceRequestOptions.isNetworkAccessAllowed = true` and its own `progressHandler`. `PHAssetResource` exposes `type` (`PHAssetResourceType`), `uniformTypeIdentifier`, `originalFilename`, `pixelWidth`/`pixelHeight`, and `dataSize` (*"nil if unavailable — may not be available until resource download/processing is complete"*).

> ⚠️ **Trap:** **One `PHAsset` can have MULTIPLE resources.** Apple: *"A photo asset can contain both JPEG and RAW files"*; *"A Live Photo asset contains both still photo and video resources"*; *"An edited asset contains resources representing asset content before and after the edit, as well as a resource corresponding to the `PHAdjustmentData`."* Enumerate `PHAssetResourceType` and pick deliberately (`.photo` vs `.fullSizePhoto` vs `.pairedVideo` vs `.adjustmentData`) or you will silently export the wrong bytes.

### 10.4 Background Resource Upload Extension — the competitive unlock (iOS 26.1+)

Shipped in **iOS 26.1**. For the first time, a third-party app can register a system extension the OS wakes to upload photo-library resources to the app's own server **in the background, while the app is suspended or the device is locked**. Apple: *"The system manages uploads on your app's behalf, processing them in the background even when people switch to other apps or lock their devices. The system calls your extension to process uploads when conditions allow, scheduling work based on factors such as network availability, power state, and device activity."* Widely read as an EU DMA/antitrust-driven concession; press named Google Photos, Dropbox, OneDrive, WhatsApp, Telegram, and Immich as beneficiaries.

**Setup contract**

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| Extension point identifier | **`com.apple.photos.background-upload`** — set under `EXAppExtensionAttributes` > `EXExtensionPointIdentifier` |
| Info.plist (top-level) | **`BackgroundUploadURLBase`** (String, e.g. `https://api.example.com`) — *"The system requires this key for network access validation"*, i.e. the OS pins where your extension may talk |
| Extension target template | Generic Extension |
| Host-app enable call | `try PHPhotoLibrary.shared().setUploadJobExtensionEnabled(true)`; read back `uploadJobExtensionEnabled` |
| Authorization | **Full library access required.** Apple: *"Your app must have full library access before enabling the extension. Call `requestAuthorization(for:handler:)` with the `.readWrite` access level and verify the status is `.authorized`."* |
| Housekeeping | Apple tells you to disable the extension when the user signs out or turns off cloud sync in your app |

> ⚠️ **Trap:** **Not available in the Simulator.** Physical device only.

**Job model.** Jobs are `PHAssetResourceUploadJob` objects created inside a `PHPhotoLibrary.performChanges` block via `PHAssetResourceUploadJobChangeRequest.creationRequestForJob(destination: URLRequest, resource: PHAssetResource)`. The `destination` `URLRequest` carries your endpoint, auth headers, and metadata headers. **Each `PHAssetResource` needs its own job.**

| Concept | Detail |
|---|---|
| Lifecycle | `.registered` → `.pending` → `.succeeded` / `.failed` / `.cancelled` |
| Fetch | `PHAssetResourceUploadJob.fetchJobs(action:options:)` with `Action` = `.process` / `.acknowledge` / `.retry` |
| Quota | `PHAssetResourceUploadJob.jobLimit` caps in-flight jobs; exceeding it throws `PHPhotosError.limitExceeded` from `performChanges`. Recover by `acknowledge()`-ing completed jobs and returning `.processing` |
| Retry | `retry(destination:)` accepts `nil` (reuse original request) or a fresh `URLRequest` (e.g. refreshed auth token). **A job may only be retried once.** |
| Cancel | `cancel()` works only in `.registered` or `.pending`; cancelled jobs are auto-acknowledged |
| Introspection | `.destination`, `.error` (standard `NSURLErrorDomain` codes), `.responseHeaderFields` (your server's response headers, normalized to lowercase — Apple's sample reads back `x-server-resource-id`), `.type` |
| Extension entry points | `processJobs() async -> PHBackgroundResourceUploadProcessingResult` (`.completed` / `.processing` / `.failure`) and `willTerminate()` |
| Canonical loop | retry failed jobs → acknowledge completed jobs → create new jobs |
| Map job → resource | `PHAssetResource.assetResource(forUploadJob:)` |

> ⚠️ **Trap:** `PHAssetResourceUploadJob.resource` is **DEPRECATED**. Use `PHAssetResource.assetResource(forUploadJob:)`.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** `jobLimit`'s numeric value is **not published in Apple's docs**. Read it at runtime; never hard-code it.

**Resumable uploads — the server-side contract you cannot skip.** The system implements the IETF draft resumable-uploads protocol and **your server must implement it too**:

1. The system sends an **HTTP `OPTIONS`** preflight to your upload endpoint (the capability check is cached).
2. Your server replies **`200 OK` with an `Upload-Limit` header** (max upload size in bytes) to opt in — or **`501 Not Implemented`** to decline.
3. Per upload, your server **MUST** emit an **HTTP `104` (Upload Resumption Supported)** informational response carrying a `Location:` header **before** the final response (e.g. `201`). Apple: *"The 104 informational response serves as the authoritative signal that the server supports resumable uploads. If an upload is interrupted after the client receives this response, the system automatically resumes the transfer from where it stopped."*

Apple: *"Your API must include both the OPTIONS preflight check and the 104 informational response."*

> ⚠️ **Trap:** If your server does not emit `104`, **uploads restart from zero on every interruption.** Many HTTP stacks, CDNs, and load balancers cannot emit 1xx informational responses at all. Validate this end-to-end before committing to an architecture — it is the most common way a background-upload integration fails.

**Availability and the three-code-path problem**

| Symbol | Availability |
|---|---|
| `PHBackgroundResourceUploadExtension` | **iOS/iPadOS 26.1+ — iOS/iPadOS ONLY (no macOS at all). DEPRECATED as of iOS 27.0** ("Adopt `PHBackgroundResourceUploadJobExtension` instead") |
| `PHBackgroundResourceUploadJobExtension` (async) | iOS 27.0 / iPadOS 27.0 / macOS 27.0 / Mac Catalyst 27.0 — **beta, unreleased.** Apple: *"In macOS and Mac Catalyst, `PHBackgroundResourceUploadJobExtension` is the only available protocol."* |
| `PHAssetResourceUploadJob`, `PHAssetResourceUploadJobChangeRequest` | iOS/iPadOS 26.1; macOS/Mac Catalyst 27.0 (beta) |

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The 26.1 protocol was deprecated **one minor cycle after introduction**. If you ship today you must support **both** protocols, and the API is visibly still settling. Additionally, Apple Developer Forums carry open threads reporting the system **not triggering uploads on iOS 26.2** despite correctly configured jobs ("PhotoKit Background Upload Extension not working on iOS 26.2", "Background Upload Extension Bug on iOS 26.2"). **Real-world reliability is genuinely unknown.** Prototype and measure actual wake frequency and throughput on a physical device across a week before betting a product on it.

### 10.5 Download-only jobs (iOS 26.4+) — system-mediated iCloud fetch

`PHAssetResourceUploadJobChangeRequest.creationRequestForDownloadJob(resource:)` makes the system pull a cloud-only asset resource down from iCloud to local storage **without uploading it anywhere**. Apple: *"This method registers a job that requests an asset resource be downloaded from iCloud to the device without uploading it to a remote server."*

`PHAssetResourceUploadJob.Type` has two cases:
- **`.downloadOnly`** — *"A download job type (will download the resource from iCloud if required)"*
- **`.upload`** — *"An upload job type (will download the resource from iCloud if required, then upload)"*

Because `.upload` already downloads implicitly, **you do not need to pre-materialize optimized-away originals before enqueuing an upload job.** Download-only jobs share the same `.registered → .pending → .succeeded/.failed` lifecycle and count against `jobLimit`. Check `job.type` when acknowledging to distinguish them.

| Symbol | Availability |
|---|---|
| `creationRequestForDownloadJob(resource:)` | **iOS 26.4 / iPadOS 26.4 / Mac Catalyst 26.4**; macOS 27.0 (beta) |
| `PHAssetResourceUploadJob.Type` enum | iOS/iPadOS 26.4; **Mac Catalyst 27.0 (beta)** |

> ⚠️ **Trap:** A download-only job is **NOT a durable local pin.** Apple explicitly warns: *"The system may subsequently purge the downloaded resource due to system conditions"* / *"due to disk space constraints. After a download-only job succeeds, process the resource promptly or create an upload job to send it to your server."*

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Download-only jobs are a **26.4+** capability while the parent extension is **26.1+** — a narrower window than the extension itself. And there is **no documented way to observe download progress** for these jobs (unlike `PHAssetResourceRequestOptions.progressHandler`).

### 10.6 Change tracking and cross-device asset identity

**Change tracking**

| API | Availability | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `PHPhotoLibraryChangeObserver` → `photoLibraryDidChange(_:)` | iOS 8.0+ | Diff the `PHChange` against your `PHFetchResult`s. **Only fires while your process is alive.** |
| `PHPhotoLibrary.fetchPersistentChanges(since:)` + `PHPersistentChangeToken` | iOS 16.0 / macOS 13.0 | The background/extension path; used explicitly in Apple's background-upload sample |
| `PHPhotoLibraryPersistentChangesObserver` → `photoLibraryPersistentChangesDidUpdate(_:)` | **iOS 27.0 / iPadOS 27.0 / Mac Catalyst 27.0 / macOS 27.0 / tvOS 27.0 / visionOS 27.0 — beta, unreleased** | Push-style observer for persistent changes |

> ⚠️ **Trap:** `fetchPersistentChanges(since:)` throws `PHPhotosError.persistentChangeTokenExpired` — *"the library state is older than the available history of persistent changes."* Apple's prescribed handling inside the upload extension: *"the system has pruned history past your saved token; discard the saved token, return `.processing`, and re-sync on the next invocation."* **Apple never documents the history retention window.** Design for expiry from day one — a full re-scan of a 100k-asset library is expensive and *will* happen. (`.persistentChangeDetailsUnavailable` also exists.)

**`PHCloudIdentifier`** (iOS 15.0 / iPadOS 15.0 / Mac Catalyst 15.0 / macOS 10.13 / tvOS 15.0 / visionOS 1.0) is the **only** public way to refer to an iCloud-Photos asset across devices. Apple: *"A local identifier is valid for referring to objects only in the context of a local device… Because a cloud identifier is universal, you can use it on any iCloud-synced device."* Batch-convert with `PHPhotoLibrary.localIdentifierMappings(for:)` / `cloudIdentifierMappings(for:)`.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** `PHCloudIdentifier.stringValue`, `init(stringValue:)`, and `.notFound` are all **DEPRECATED**. For persistence you must use **`archivalStringValue` / `init?(archivalStringValue:)`**. Code written against the obvious-looking `stringValue` targets a deprecated API.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Mapping is *"an expensive operation, so perform lookups sparingly"* — batch it. It fails **per-identifier** with `PHPhotosError.identifierNotFound` (asset missing/deleted on this device) or `.multipleIdentifiersFound` (one cloud ID matching several local assets, surfaced via `PHLocalIdentifiersErrorKey`; Apple's own sample says *"Prompt the user to resolve"*). That ambiguity exists in Apple's own sync engine and is a documented source of duplicate-photo confusion.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** A cloud identifier **only exists if iCloud Photos is on.** For a non-iCloud library you are stuck with `localIdentifier`, so your schema must carry **both**.

### 10.7 Photo library authorization levels

`PHAccessLevel` (iOS 14.0 / macOS 11.0): `.addOnly`, `.readWrite`.
`PHAuthorizationStatus` (iOS 8.0): `.notDetermined`, `.restricted`, `.denied`, `.authorized`, **`.limited`**.

Since iOS 14 the user can grant **limited** access ("Select Photos…"), sharing only a hand-picked subset. Apple's caveats for `.limited`: *"The system automatically adds assets that your app creates with a `PHAssetCreationRequest` to the user's limited library selection"* and **"You can't create or fetch user albums."**

User-facing choice per Apple Legal: **`Allow Full Access`** vs **`Limit Access`** — and Apple advertises that Allow Full Access *"grants the third-party app access to your photos and videos, **including your hidden photos even if the album is locked**."*

Info.plist: `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription` (read/write), `NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription` (add-only). *"Attempting to access the Photos library without a valid usage description causes your app to crash."*

> ⚠️ **Trap:** **A competing sync app cannot function on `.limited` access.** Background upload requires `.authorized` (full). Your onboarding must earn the scariest permission tier — the same tier Apple's own privacy page advertises as including hidden and locked photos. Also handle the user *downgrading* you to `.limited` later via `Settings` > `Privacy & Security` > `Photos`, and suppress the automatic once-per-lifecycle limited-library picker so you can present it deliberately.

### 10.8 Encryption: Standard vs Advanced Data Protection

**iCloud Photos is NOT end-to-end encrypted by default.** Apple's own encryption table (support 102651) reads literally:

| Data category | Standard data protection | Key storage | Advanced Data Protection | Key storage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Photos | In transit & on server | **Apple** | End-to-end | **Trusted devices** |

**Advanced Data Protection** (`Settings` > `[your name]` > `iCloud` > `Advanced Data Protection` > `Turn on Advanced Data Protection`) is opt-in and *"the number of data categories that use end-to-end encryption rises to 25 and includes your iCloud Backup, Photos, Notes, and more"* (from 15). Internally, Photos is a CloudKit "available-after-authentication" service whose service keys normally live in Apple-datacenter HSMs; enabling ADP deletes those keys from the HSMs and retains them only on trusted devices. Turning ADP **off** re-uploads both the pre-ADP and post-ADP service keys back to Apple's HSMs.

**Requirements:** iOS/iPadOS 16.2, macOS 13.1, tvOS 16.2, watchOS 9.2, iCloud for Windows 14.1 or later — **on every device signed into the account**; 2FA; a device passcode; and at least one recovery contact **or** a 28-character recovery key. **Managed Apple Accounts and child accounts are not eligible.**

> ⚠️ **Trap:** **Even WITH ADP on, this Photos metadata stays under Apple-held keys** (Apple's exact list): *"The raw byte checksum of the photo or video; Whether an item has been marked as a favorite, hidden, or marked as deleted; When the item was originally created on the device; When the item was originally imported and modified; How many times an item has been viewed."* Apple justifies the checksums as convergent encryption for de-duplication: *"checksums of file and photo data are used to help Apple de-duplicate and optimize the user's iCloud and device storage."* Anyone claiming "Photos is E2E under ADP" without this caveat is overstating the guarantee.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** **ADP is unavailable to new users in the United Kingdom** since **Feb 21, 2025**, following a UK government demand (Apple has a dedicated support page: support.apple.com/en-us/122234). This is decision-grade for any product making E2E claims to UK users. (The vaguer "may not be available in all countries or regions" line is *not* on Apple's current ADP page.)

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Turning on ADP **disables iCloud.com web access by default**: *"When you turn on Advanced Data Protection, access to your iCloud data on the web at iCloud.com is disabled… If you turn on web access again, you can use one of your trusted devices to approve temporary access to your data on the web"* — which *"allows the web browser that you're using and Apple to have temporary access to data-specific encryption keys provided by your device."*

**Sharing asymmetry:**
- **iCloud Shared Photo Library DOES stay E2E under ADP** — *"as long as ALL participants have Advanced Data Protection enabled."*
- **Shared Albums NEVER support ADP.** Apple 108756: *"iWork collaboration, the Shared Albums feature in Photos, and sharing content with 'anyone with the link,' don't support Advanced Data Protection. This means the shared content is not end-to-end encrypted even when Advanced Data Protection is enabled."* Rationale (Platform Security guide): *"the feature permits albums to be publicly shared on the web."*
- For any sharing operation, *"a title and representative thumbnail may be stored by Apple with standard data protection to show a preview."*

### 10.9 iCloud storage tiers and pricing

5 GB free with every Apple Account. Paid tiers are branded **iCloud+**. US monthly pricing (Apple support 108047, published April 6, 2026):

| Tier | US/mo | CAD | MXN | BRL | HomeKit Secure Video cameras |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 GB | Free | — | — | — | — |
| 50 GB | $0.99 | 1.29 | 17 | 5.90 | 1 |
| 200 GB | $2.99 | 3.99 | 49 | 19.90 | up to 5 |
| 2 TB | $9.99 | 12.99 | 179 | 66.90 | unlimited |
| 6 TB | $29.99 | 39.99 | 499 | 199.90 | unlimited |
| 12 TB | $59.99 | 79.99 | 999 | 399.90 | unlimited |

The 6 TB and 12 TB tiers are **real** (stale training data frequently hallucinates them away). All paid tiers include iCloud Private Relay, Hide My Email, Custom Email Domain, and Family Sharing with up to five other members. Also bundled in Apple One. iOS 27 (beta) adds: *"Most iCloud+ subscription plans offer higher daily usage limits for Apple Intelligence features, including image generation."*

**The 5 GB free tier has not increased since 2011** and is the canonical Apple grievance — it cannot hold even one iPhone backup plus a photo library. "iCloud storage is full" is a documented sync-pause reason (§10.12).

### 10.10 iCloud Shared Photo Library

A **second** library, co-owned by up to **6 people total** (creator + 5), living alongside the Personal Library in the same Photos app. **A user can join only ONE Shared Library.** Requires iOS 16.1 / iPadOS 16.1 / macOS Ventura or later **with iCloud Photos on**. Under-13s can only join/create with Family Sharing members.

| Semantic | Detail (Apple 118229) |
|---|---|
| Contribution model | **Move, not copy**: *"When you contribute photos and videos to iCloud Shared Photo Library, they move out of your Personal Library and into the Shared Library."* |
| Storage accounting | *"The library creator… provides iCloud storage for all of the content. Everyone else gets access to the Shared Library content without it counting towards their iCloud storage."* |
| Permissions | All participants can add, edit, **and delete** content |
| Deletion asymmetry | *"When a participant deletes a photo or video from the Shared Library, it moves to Recently Deleted. Only the **contributor** of that photo or video can delete it from Recently Deleted."* |
| Storage-full contagion | *"If the library creator runs out of iCloud storage, you can no longer add content to the Shared Library. Changes such as edits, favorites, and metadata adjustments no longer sync."* Surfaces to participants as **`Move Photos to Personal Library to Continue Syncing`** |
| Creator deletes the library | Participants in it **>7 days** get **everything** copied into their Personal Library; participants in it **<7 days** get only what they themselves contributed |
| Participant leaves | Chooses "everything" or "just what I contributed" |
| Camera integration | `Settings` > `Apps` > `Photos` > `Shared Library` > `Sharing from Camera`, with `Share Automatically` (Bluetooth proximity to participants' devices), `Share Manually`, `Share When At Home`. A Shared Library toggle button appears in the Camera app |
| Library view switching (iOS 26) | Photos > Library > Sort and Filter button, **or** Collections > More button > `Personal Library` / `Shared Library` / `Both Libraries`. A per-photo **Shared Library Indicator** badge can be toggled off |
| Old-OS visibility | *"If you use a device with an earlier version of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, or iCloud for Windows, you can't see content moved to the Shared Library"* (iCloud.com can) |

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The **creator's full iCloud account can pause a participant's Personal Library sync.** This is a cross-account failure mode with no analogue anywhere else in iOS.

### 10.11 Shared Albums (a completely different feature) — and the iOS 27 overhaul

The older, lossy, web-shareable album feature. **Completely separate from iCloud Shared Photo Library.** Do not conflate them.

**Hard limits (Apple support 108916, page dated Feb 27, 2025):**

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Shared albums an owner can share | **200** |
| Shared albums a user can subscribe to | **200** |
| Subscribers per album | **100** |
| Combined photos + videos per album | **5,000** |
| Comments per item (a like counts as a comment) | **200** |
| Characters per comment | **1,024** |
| Invites per day | **200** |
| Rate limit per contributor across all shared albums | **1,000/hour** and **10,000/day** |

**Fidelity (iOS 26 and earlier):** *"When shared, photos are reduced to 2048 pixels on the long edge, except panoramic photos, which can be up to 5400 pixels wide."* Videos: up to **15 minutes**, delivered at up to **720p**. GIFs ≤ 100 MB. **Spatial photo/video not supported.** Formats: HEIF, JPEG, RAW, PNG, GIF, TIFF; HEVC, MP4, QuickTime, H.264, MPEG-4. Windows PCs cannot upload HEIF/HEVC/RAW to Shared Albums; iCloud.com cannot take TIFF or RAW.

Related toggles: `Public Website` (publishes an album to an open URL) and `Participants Can Add Photos` (iOS 18+) / `Subscribers Can Post` (iOS 17 and earlier).

**iOS 27 (developer beta, ships fall 2026 — NOT shippable today)** overhauls Shared Albums: full-resolution photo and video sharing; support for more file types; **`React with any emoji`**; updated activity feeds with per-album activity; **`Expire your Shared Albums`** — new **30-day temporary albums** *"that allow users to collaborate on short-term projects without taking up space in their iCloud"*; additional participant permissions; and *"Anyone, including users without an Apple device, can join and contribute photos to albums on the web"* — i.e. Android and Windows participation via iCloud.com.

> ⚠️ **Trap (the storage flip):** "Shared Album content does not count against your iCloud storage" is true for **legacy (pre-iOS 27) shared albums only**. In **iOS 27, upgraded Shared Albums DO consume the owner's iCloud storage** — Apple's in-app disclaimer reads *"the owner of the shared album will provide iCloud storage for any new items added to this shared album."* Additionally, creating a *permanent* shared album in iOS 27 requires iCloud Photos to be on, while 30-day *temporary* albums do not. Shipping "Shared Albums are free storage" as a durable fact is exactly the kind of error that reaches production.

> ⚠️ **Trap (unverified):** Apple has **not republished the limits table for iOS 27**. Whether the 200/200/100/5,000 caps and the 15-min/720p video caps change alongside the full-resolution overhaul is **unknown**. Likewise, whether iOS 27's more-central web/cross-platform sharing preserves the ADP exclusion is **unverified** — the exclusion almost certainly persists (Apple's stated rationale is precisely public web sharing) but no iOS 27-era Apple statement re-confirms it. Verify before making any privacy claim.

### 10.12 Sync-status vocabulary, pause reasons, and the `Unable to Upload` album

This is the failure vocabulary your users will compare you against. Source: Apple support 101559, *"If your iCloud Photos aren't syncing or syncing with iCloud is paused"* — **published June 18, 2026** (current).

**Status surface (iOS 26):** Photos app > `Collections` > profile/account button, top-right corner. (iOS 17 and earlier: Library tab > All Photos > scroll to bottom.) Tapping the account shows details; *"The last time your iPhone synced with iCloud appears below the account profile."*

| Indicator | Meaning (Apple's wording) |
|---|---|
| **Yellow badge** | "iCloud syncing is paused." |
| **Yellow warning icon** | "Your iCloud storage is almost full." |
| **Red exclamation mark** | "Your iCloud storage is full." |
| **Blue badge** | "You have notifications from a shared library or shared album." |
| **Partially filled blue circle** around your account icon | "Photos are actively uploading to iCloud." |
| **Partially filled gray outline** around your account icon | "Uploads are paused." |

**Documented pause reasons (exact strings):**

| Status string | Cause |
|---|---|
| `Low Data Mode` / `Low Power Mode` | "syncing paused to reduce network data usage or save battery" |
| `Optimizing Battery Power` / `Optimizing System Performance` / `Poor Network Connection` | "syncing paused to improve power, performance, and network connection. To force syncing, tap **`Sync Now`**." |
| `Low Battery` | "syncing paused because your battery charge is below **20 percent**. To resume syncing, charge your device." |
| `[Device] Needs to Cool Down` | "syncing paused to protect your device from overheating." |
| iCloud storage is full | "syncing paused because you exceeded your iCloud storage limit." |
| `Move Photos to Personal Library to Continue Syncing` | "syncing paused because a Shared Library owner has hit their storage limit." |

**Manual pause:** Photos > Collections > profile button > **`Pause`** (iOS 26; iOS 18: profile button > Pause; iOS 17 and earlier: Library > All Photos > scroll down > Pause). Apple: *"You can see the status and pause the upload for **one day**. Depending on your library status, pause might not be available."*

**The `Unable to Upload` album.** When iCloud Photos cannot upload an item, Photos creates a system album literally named **`Unable to Upload`** and drops the item there. Apple's documented remedy: *"Check if you have an album named Unable to Upload. **Edit each photo** or video, then check to see if the photo or video uploads to iCloud. Or upload items in the Unable to Upload folder to iCloud again from your iPhone or iPad, or reimport items in the Unable to Upload folder to iCloud from your Mac."* Apple attributes these failures largely to **unsupported file types** (supported set: HEIF, JPEG, RAW, PNG, GIF, TIFF, HEVC, MP4, slo-mo, time-lapse, 4K, Live Photos).

> ⚠️ **Trap:** `Unable to Upload` is a **quarantine/retry bucket, not a permanent-failure bucket** — Apple documents a recovery path. Design your equivalent as a retryable queue with a stated reason, not a graveyard. But note that Apple's *actual official fix* is "edit the photo and hope," which is an admission that the sync engine has states it cannot self-heal, and **no API tells you why an item failed**.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The album is fetchable as a `PHAssetCollection` but there is **no `PHAssetCollectionSubtype` constant for it** — you would have to match on `localizedTitle`, which is fragile and locale-dependent.

**Apple's latency guidance is literally "wait":** *"Connect your device to power and to Wi-Fi, then let the device sync uninterrupted overnight"* and *"Depending on the size of your library and your Wi-Fi speed, you may need to wait overnight for your device to finish syncing. Some larger-sized files may take longer to upload or sync."* **No SLA is published anywhere.**

### 10.13 iCloud Backup vs iCloud Photos; deletion and turn-off semantics

They are **different systems and photos are in exactly one of them.** Apple 108770: *"iCloud helps keep your data safe in two main ways: syncing and backing up… Any data on your device that isn't regularly synced is stored in your iCloud Backup."* And verbatim: *"If you haven't turned on iCloud Photos, iCloud Backup may include photos and videos in your Photos or Camera Roll, as well as face information from the People & Pets album. When you use iCloud Photos, your photos, videos, and face information automatically sync to iCloud so they aren't included in your daily backup."* Corroborated on the Photos side: *"They're not duplicated in your iCloud backup, so keep backup copies of your library."*

**Therefore: iCloud Photos ON ⇒ photos are SYNCED, not BACKED UP. There is no second copy.** Deleting a photo deletes it from the only copy Apple holds, modulo the 30-day window.

Also: *"If you turn off iCloud Backup for a device, any backups stored in iCloud are kept for **180 days** before being deleted."* Apple Watch backups ride inside the iPhone backup.

**Deletion:** *"When you delete photos and videos on one device, they're deleted everywhere that you use iCloud Photos. If you delete something accidentally, you can recover it in the `Recently Deleted` folder for **30 days**. After that, it's deleted permanently and you can't get it back."*

**Turning it off — two very different flavors:**

| Flavor | Path | Semantics |
|---|---|---|
| Turn off on **one device** | `Settings` > `[name]` > `iCloud` > `Photos` > deselect `Sync this iPhone` | Prompted with **`Download Photos & Videos`** (pull full-res copies down first) or **`Remove from iPhone`**. Apple warns: *"If you choose not to download a copy of your photos and videos, **optimized photos are not the original resolution**."* Afterward, "new changes like uploads of new photos, edits, and deletions no longer sync to that device." Mac equivalents: `Sync this Mac` / `Download` / `Remove from Mac` |
| Turn off **everywhere and delete from iCloud** | `Settings` > `[name]` > `iCloud` > `Storage` > `iCloud Photos` > **`Turn Off and Delete Photos`** (iOS 17 and earlier: `Turn Off & Delete from iCloud`) | *"Photos and videos stored in iCloud are deleted **30 days** after you stop using the service. If you change your mind before then, you can select **`Undo Delete`**."* Mac: `Turn Off and Delete from iCloud`, then `Recover iCloud Photos`. You must delete a Shared Photo Library you own first |

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Choosing `Remove from iPhone` when you were on `Optimize iPhone Storage` leaves the user with **only degraded proxies**. This is the classic, documented data-loss trap and it is the single most consequential misunderstanding in the Apple ecosystem.

### 10.14 iCloud.com, export, and import

**iCloud.com/photos** is a full web client: Library, Memories, Albums, upload, download, share, hide, favorite, slideshow, title/caption/metadata editing, Shared Photo Library, shared albums with likes/comments, iCloud Links, delete and recover. **Web-only Apple Accounts do not get Photos on iCloud.com** (Apple 102447 enumerates web-only access as iCloud Drive, Pages, Numbers, Keynote, Contacts, Notes, and Shared Albums with 1 GB free storage — Photos is not on the list).

**Download from iCloud.com** (Apple 111762): select up to **1,000 items at a time**, then More > `More Download Options`:

| Option | Apple's description |
|---|---|
| `Unmodified Originals` | "format as captured or imported" |
| `Highest Resolution` | "best quality for your device; typically HEIC or H.265" |
| `Most Compatible` | "JPEG or MP4/H.264" |

**Export from iPhone:** Photos > Library > Select > Share button > **`Export Unmodified Originals`**, then choose a Files destination.

**`Allow Search` on iCloud.com (new in iOS 26.4).** Apple 126463: *"In iOS 26.4 or later, you can use your trusted Apple devices to provide search results for iCloud Drive and iCloud Photos on iCloud.com."* Photos suggestions are limited to **dates, people, and locations**; searches are encrypted and use on-device processing; the device shows a notification **up to once per day** and keeps a **28-day search report** you can download or delete. **Cannot be enabled at all on a Managed Apple Account or a phone-number Apple Account.** (The settings path `Settings` > `[your name]` > `iCloud` > `iCloud.com` > `Allow Search` and its default-off state are sourced to 9to5Mac, not an Apple page — **re-verify before shipping copy that references it**.)

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The researcher-level claim that Mac/PC import-export offers "three distinct paths, each with different fidelity guarantees" is **unverified** as stated. Apple documents distinct mechanisms — Photos app / Image Capture import over USB, iCloud for Windows with its own Photos pane, and iCloud.com download — but publishes **no comparative fidelity guarantee** across them. Do not architect a migration story around one. The mechanism you *should* use in-app is `PHAssetResourceManager.writeData(for:toFile:options:)` with `isNetworkAccessAllowed = true`, which is the byte-exact equivalent of `Export Unmodified Originals`.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** **There is no public iCloud Photos web/REST API.** Apple has never shipped one, and CloudKit Web Services does not expose the user's Photos container. Every third-party "iCloud photo downloader" is reverse-engineering a private endpoint. **A competing sync cannot legitimately read iCloud Photos server-side — you must go through PhotoKit on-device.** This is the hardest constraint in the entire domain.

### 10.15 What is computed on-device (People & Pets, Memories, Enhanced Visual Search)

**People & Pets.** Face recognition inference is on-device ML. Album path: Photos > `Collections` > swipe up > **`People & Pets`** (or just `People` if no dogs or cats are identified). Apple 108795: *"The Photos app organizes the images of the people, dogs, and cats in the People & Pets collection"*; pets (dogs and cats) recognized *"in iOS 17, iPadOS 17, and later."* Apple: *"when you have iCloud Photos turned on, the people you favorite or name stay up to date across your Apple devices."* As established in §10.1, **face information — not just names — syncs.** (The often-cited "iOS 11+ for face sync" floor has **no Apple source**; treat as **unverified**.)

**Memories.** Generated on-device from on-device signals. Apple Legal (Photos & Privacy, dated 2025-12-12) lists the inputs: *"on-device information, such as which photos you have edited or shared to other people, people you frequently communicate with in Messages, relationships set in Contacts, Home and Work locations set in Contacts or Maps, locations where you take photos, and important dates in Calendar and Contacts."* Whether Memories **sync as objects is UNVERIFIED** — Apple never says either way.

**Enhanced Visual Search** (iOS 18+, macOS Sequoia+, **ON by default** — which drew a real backlash). This is the **one** Photos feature that talks to Apple's servers about photo content.

- **Scope is narrow:** *"Enhanced Visual Search allows you to search your photo library for **landmarks** within your photos or videos."* Landmarks and points of interest **only** — not photo content generally.
- **What leaves the device:** *"a low-fidelity mathematical representation… called an **embedding**"* — *"This embedding — not image data — is encrypted and sent to Apple servers."*
- **Three stacked protections:** **homomorphic encryption**; **differential privacy** (the device sends fake requests alongside the real one); and an **OHTTP relay** (a third-party anonymization network that hides the IP address).
- **Toggle:** `Settings` > `Apps` > `Photos`. On Mac: Photos > Settings > General.
- *"Enhanced Visual Search isn't available in all countries or regions."*

### 10.16 Offline behavior and library scale

**Offline (inference, not Apple-documented).** Apple publishes no dedicated offline doc and **nowhere guarantees** "the local library remains fully browsable offline." What *is* documented: `Optimize iPhone Storage` keeps "storage-saving versions" on device, so browsing generally works; opening an evicted original fails with a degraded image plus `PHImageResultIsInCloudKey`, or `PHPhotosError.networkAccessRequired` / `.networkError` from `PHAssetResourceManager`; new captures/edits queue locally with a pause reason such as `Poor Network Connection`; deletions queue and propagate on reconnect. Under `Download and Keep Originals`, offline is a non-event except that new items still won't upload. **Mark this as inference.**

**Scale.** Design for 100k–500k assets. `PHFetchResult` is lazy and batched, so fetches are cheap; the expensive parts are `PHCachingImageManager` preheating, per-asset resource enumeration, and `PHCloudIdentifier` mapping (explicitly "expensive" — batch it). Folklore limits (~1,000,000 items, 10,000 albums) trace to Aperture-migration guidance from the macOS Photos era and are **not** current Apple statements.

### 10.17 iOS 27 (developer beta, ships fall 2026 — NOT shippable today)

iOS 27 was announced at WWDC 2026 (June 9, 2026); Beta 3 shipped July 6, 2026 (build 24A5380h); public release "this fall." Everything here is **beta/unreleased**.

| Change | Detail |
|---|---|
| `PHBackgroundResourceUploadJobExtension` | Async replacement for the deprecated 26.1 `PHBackgroundResourceUploadExtension`; the **only** protocol on macOS/Mac Catalyst |
| `PHAssetExtendedMetadata` | **`caption`, `keywords`, `originalFileName`** — read via `PHAsset.extendedMetadata`, or prefetch with `PHFetchOptions.prefetchAssetExtendedMetadata` to avoid N+1 fetches. Captions and keywords were previously **not readable** from `PHAsset` at all |
| `PHPhotoLibraryPersistentChangesObserver` | Push-style persistent-change observer |
| Upload-job stack on desktop | Extends to macOS 27 / Mac Catalyst 27 |
| Photos app | Shared Albums overhaul (§10.11); keyword tagging **on iPhone** (previously Mac-only); new `Captured by Me` and `Identity Documents` collections; slideshow maker; extracting video frames as photos; Apple Intelligence editing (Spatial Reframing, `Extend`, upgraded `Clean Up`) |
| iCloud+ | *"Most iCloud+ subscription plans offer higher daily usage limits for Apple Intelligence features, including image generation."* |

**Performance claim, precisely stated:** Apple's *"up to 70% faster"* number refers to **new captures loading in the Photos library immediately after you take them** (Apple's testing on iPhone 15). App launches up to 30% faster; AirDrop up to 80% faster.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** *"Up to 70% faster"* is **capture-to-library render latency, NOT bulk-import/ingest throughput for large libraries.** An implementer benchmarking "library ingest" against this number is chasing a claim Apple never made.

### 10.18 What a third-party app can and cannot do

| Capability | Available to 3rd parties? | Mechanism / why not |
|---|---|---|
| Read the synced library (assets, albums, favorites, hidden, dates, location, `hasAdjustments`, `mediaSubtypes`, `sourceType`, `playbackStyle`) | **Yes** | PhotoKit: `PHAsset`, `PHAssetCollection`, `PHFetchResult`. You read the *synced result*; you cannot join the sync itself |
| Fetch a cloud-only original on demand | **Yes** | `PHImageRequestOptions` / `PHAssetResourceRequestOptions` with `isNetworkAccessAllowed = true` + `progressHandler` |
| Get byte-exact originals (RAW, Live Photo pair, pre-edit resource, `PHAdjustmentData`) | **Yes** | `PHAssetResource.assetResources(for:)` + `PHAssetResourceManager.requestData` / `.writeData` |
| **Background upload of library resources to your own server while suspended/locked** | **Yes — iOS 26.1+** | `PHBackgroundResourceUploadExtension` (26.1, deprecated at 27.0) / `PHBackgroundResourceUploadJobExtension` (27.0 beta). Requires full library access, `setUploadJobExtensionEnabled(true)`, extension point `com.apple.photos.background-upload`, `BackgroundUploadURLBase`, **and a server implementing OPTIONS/`Upload-Limit`/HTTP 104**. Not in Simulator |
| Make the system pre-download a cloud-only resource | **Yes — iOS 26.4+** | `PHAssetResourceUploadJobChangeRequest.creationRequestForDownloadJob(resource:)`. Result may be purged by the system — not a durable pin |
| Track library changes in background | **Yes** | `PHPhotoLibrary.fetchPersistentChanges(since:)` (iOS 16+); must handle `persistentChangeTokenExpired` with a full re-scan |
| Stable cross-device asset identity | **Yes** | `PHCloudIdentifier` + `archivalStringValue`. **Only exists when iCloud Photos is on** — carry `localIdentifier` too |
| Ask "is iCloud Photos syncing / paused / how many items pending?" | **No** | **PhotoKit exposes no sync-status API at all.** `PHAsset.isSyncFailureHidden` is the closest thing and is only a per-asset UI flag |
| Know *why* an item failed to upload | **No** | No API. The `Unable to Upload` album is fetchable as a `PHAssetCollection` but has **no `PHAssetCollectionSubtype` constant** — you must string-match `localizedTitle`, which is locale-dependent and fragile |
| Read or restore `Recently Deleted` | **No** | The Recently Deleted collection is **not accessible via PhotoKit**. You cannot see or rescue trashed assets |
| Read People / faces / face rectangles / Apple's clustering | **No** | **No public `PHPerson`**, no face rects, no identity clusters, no access to the `People & Pets` album. You must run your own detection (Vision) and your own clustering + naming, from scratch, on pixels you fetch yourself. You can neither read nor write Apple's People names |
| Read Memories, Featured Photos, Sharing Suggestions, scene classification, the Enhanced Visual Search index | **No** | None are exposed by PhotoKit. Rebuild with Vision / Core ML |
| Tell whether an asset lives in the Personal vs Shared Photo Library | **No (real gap)** | `PHAssetSourceType` has only `typeUserLibrary`, `typeCloudShared` (= iCloud **Shared Album**), `typeiTunesSynced`. **There is no source type for Shared Photo Library membership.** A competing app cannot faithfully mirror the Personal/Shared split |
| Read captions / keywords | **Not until iOS 27 (beta)** | `PHAssetExtendedMetadata` (`caption`, `keywords`, `originalFileName`). Unavailable on iOS 26.x |
| Read iCloud Photos server-side (REST/web) | **No** | **No public iCloud Photos web/REST API exists.** CloudKit Web Services does not expose the Photos container. Everything must go through PhotoKit on-device |
| Create or fetch user albums under `.limited` access | **No** | Apple: *"You can't create or fetch user albums"* under limited library access |
| Run background upload under `.limited` access | **No** | Requires `.authorized` (full) library access, explicitly |
| Influence ADP / encryption | **N/A** | ADP is transparent to PhotoKit — a trusted device sees decrypted assets either way |
| Know the proxy resolution used by `Optimize iPhone Storage` | **No** | Apple does not publish it. Only the API contract (`PHImageResultIsDegradedKey` / `PHImageResultIsInCloudKey`) is reliable |
| Know `jobLimit`'s value, or the persistent-change history retention window | **No** | Neither is published. Read `jobLimit` at runtime; design for token expiry without knowing the window |

### 10.19 Where Apple is weak — our opening

- **No sync visibility, at all.** There is no per-item state, no error, no queue, no throughput, no ETA — for users *or* for developers (there is no sync-status API). Apple's entire status vocabulary is six icons and eight pause strings (§10.12), and its official guidance for a slow sync is *"let the device sync uninterrupted overnight."* Field reports (MacRumors, Apple Community — **directional, not Apple-acknowledged**) describe `Syncing N items…` hanging indefinitely with, in users' words, no way to find out which files are stuck; the community workaround is to binary-search by building albums and lightly editing photos to nudge them through. **A real, honest, per-item sync dashboard with a working retry is a first-class differentiator that Apple simply does not offer.**
- **`Unable to Upload`'s official fix is "edit the photo and hope."** That is literally Apple's documented remedy. There is no reason code, no API, and users discover the album years later holding photos that were never backed up. Honest per-item error reporting with a *reason* and a *retry* is a strong "we do it better" story.
- **iCloud Photos is not a backup — and Apple says so** (*"They're not duplicated in your iCloud backup, so keep backup copies of your library"*). Deletions propagate globally; the only safety net is a silent 30-day `Recently Deleted` window that PhotoKit cannot even read. A third-party app using `PHBackgroundResourceUploadExtension` is the **first** thing that can be a genuine independent second copy without the user leaving the Photos app.
- **Not E2E by default, and E2E with holes.** Standard data protection means **Apple holds the keys**. ADP is opt-in, has a total recovery burden (*"Apple can't help recover the user's end-to-end encrypted iCloud data"*), disables iCloud.com by default, excludes Managed and child accounts, and is **unavailable to new UK users since Feb 21, 2025**. Even with ADP on, Apple retains keys to photo/video **byte checksums**, **favorite/hidden/deleted flags**, **creation/import/modification dates**, and **view counts**. And **Shared Albums are never E2E**. A competitor that is E2E by default with no metadata carve-outs has a genuine, citable differentiator.
- **5 GB free, unchanged since 2011.** It cannot hold one iPhone backup plus a photo library. `iCloud storage is full` is a documented sync-pause reason, and Apple built a whole in-OS remediation flow because users hit the wall constantly. Pricing anchor: 200 GB at **$2.99/mo** is where most families sit.
- **No offline pinning anywhere in Photos.** With `Optimize iPhone Storage` on by default and eviction driven by an opaque LRU, there is **no "make this album available offline" control**. Users board a plane and discover their library is proxies. This is a glaring, easily-beaten omission.
- **No user control over which photos stay local**, and no way to see what is local vs cloud-only. Apple doesn't even publish the proxy resolution.
- **Shared Photo Library's model confuses people by design.** It is a **move, not a copy** — Apple's own troubleshooting page leads with *"When you move photos to your Shared Library, you no longer see them in your Personal Library"* because users think photos vanished. The **creator pays for everything**; if the creator's account fills, **participants' Personal Library sync pauses** (`Move Photos to Personal Library to Continue Syncing`) — a cross-account failure with no analogue elsewhere in iOS. Only **one** Shared Library per person. The <7-day/>7-day exit rule is undiscoverable.
- **Shared Albums were 2048px for a decade.** Photos downscaled to 2048px on the long edge, video capped at **15 minutes / 720p**, no spatial media — the #1 complaint about the feature for ten years. iOS 27 finally fixes it (full-resolution, cross-platform web contribution), but that is **unreleased**, and the fix flips shared albums into consuming the owner's iCloud storage.
- **People & Pets is inconsistent across devices and offers zero recourse.** Faces are widely reported as the last thing to sync, with different devices showing different face counts and different clusterings for the same library — a long-running, never-fixed inconsistency. Apple offers **no visibility, no forced re-scan, and no conflict resolution**. And because PhotoKit exposes **no People API at all**, this is simultaneously the biggest gap and the biggest opportunity in the domain: whoever builds trustworthy, inspectable, correctable people-clustering owns a surface Apple has locked shut and left broken.
- **Memories are non-portable.** They are recomputed on-device from device-local signals and cannot be exported, shared as objects, or carried to another platform. A competitor with portable, exportable, user-owned memories has a defensible attack surface.
- **Enhanced Visual Search shipped ON by default** and phones home (an embedding, over an OHTTP relay, homomorphically encrypted) about landmarks in your photos. The cryptography is genuinely strong; the *default* drew real backlash anyway. Default-off, with an explicit opt-in, is free trust.
- **Bulk export from the web is capped at 1,000 items per selection.** For a 50k library that is a multi-day chore, and there is **no first-party "export my whole library to a folder" button on iOS at all** — `Export Unmodified Originals` is buried in the share sheet and most users never find it.
## 11. System Integration & Sharing Surfaces

Apple Photos' real moat is not the app — it is the roughly thirty system surfaces the library is wired into: the Share Sheet, AirDrop, Messages/`Shared with You`, widgets, the Lock Screen wallpaper, StandBy, Journal suggestions, the Apple TV screen saver, Live Text/Visual Look Up/Visual Intelligence, Spotlight, Continuity Camera, and Siri. The single most important thing an implementer must know is that **Apple has quietly opened almost all of them**. Since iOS 26.1 a third-party app can back up the user's library in the background with the system scheduling the uploads (PhotoKit Background Resource Upload extension); since iOS 18 it can be driven by Siri/Apple Intelligence through the App Intents `.photos` schema domain; since iOS 16/17 it can reproduce Live Text, Visual Look Up and subject lifting pixel-for-pixel via VisionKit and Vision. The walls that remain are few but absolute: **no Lock Screen wallpaper API, no StandBy photos-view extension point, no tvOS screen saver extension point, no AirDrop-only API, and no way to post to an iCloud Shared Album programmatically.**

Baseline for everything below: **current shipping OS is iOS 26.5.2** (released 2026-06-29); **iOS 26.6 is in developer beta**; **iOS 27 was announced at WWDC on 2026-06-08, is in developer and public beta, and ships fall 2026**. Every iOS 27 item in this section is explicitly marked as unreleased.

### 11.1 The Share Sheet — the entry point

The system activity view Photos invokes from its Share button. Apple's iOS 26 iPhone User Guide documents exactly three entry points, verbatim:

| Entry point | Apple's wording |
|---|---|
| Single item | "Share a single photo or video: Open the photo or video, tap [Share]…" |
| Multi-select | "Share multiple photos or videos: While viewing a screen with multiple thumbnails, tap `Select`…" |
| Whole collection | "Share all the photos in a collection: While viewing a collection—like a collection from `Recent Days`, `Memories`, or `Trips`—tap [More], tap `Share`…" |

Apple also documents an attachment-size caveat: *"The size limit of attachments is determined by your service provider. For devices or services that don't support Live Photos, a Live Photo is shared as a still photo."*

⚠️ **Trap:** The commonly-cited enumeration of the Photos activity row (`Copy`, `Save to Files`, `Add to Album`, `Print`, `Assign to Contact`, `Duplicate`, `Hide`, `Save as Video`) is **not enumerated anywhere in Apple's documentation**. The individual labels are plausible, but the list as a whole is *unverified* — do not treat it as a spec. Enumerate it on a real iOS 26 device before copying it.

**Developer mechanism.** `UIActivityViewController` (iOS 6+; visually restyled under Liquid Glass in iOS 26). Content passes as activity items / `NSItemProvider`. Tuning knobs: `excludedActivityTypes`, `excludedActivitySectionTypes` (`UIActivitySectionTypes`), and `allowsProminentActivity` to elevate one activity. Three ways to *appear in* someone else's share sheet:

1. **Share Extension** — `NSExtensionPointIdentifier = com.apple.share-services`, with an `NSExtensionActivationRule` declaring supported types: `NSExtensionActivationSupportsImageWithMaxCount`, `...MovieWithMaxCount`, `...FileWithMaxCount`, `...Text`, `...WebURLWithMaxCount`, `...WebPageWithMaxCount`, `...AttachmentsWithMinCount`/`MaxCount`, plus `NSExtensionActivationUsesStrictMatching` and a raw-predicate escape hatch (default `TRUEPREDICATE` always shows). Ship it inside your app bundle; no extra registration.
2. **Action Extension** — for in-place transforms.
3. **`UIActivity` subclass** — app-local custom services; override `activityType`, `activityTitle`, `activityImage`, `canPerform(withActivityItems:)`, `prepare(withActivityItems:)`, `activityCategory`, then `perform()` or `activityViewController`.

**Share-sheet conversation suggestions (the top avatar row).** *Unverified as a documented Apple feature:* the row exists in practice, but no Apple support guide, developer doc or newsroom post describes, names, or version-dates it. Do **not** hand an implementer an "iOS 13+" availability number for it. What *is* documentable is the developer-facing hook: apps and their share extensions donate an `INSendMessageIntent` on every message send (populating recipients, `speakableGroupName`, `conversationIdentifier`) and add `INSendMessageIntent` to `IntentsSupported` in the share extension's `Info.plist`. ⚠️ **Trap:** WWDC 2026 formally deprecated SiriKit in favour of App Intents (2–3 year migration window). Verify the donation path still exists in the iOS 27 SDK before building on it.

### 11.2 The `Options` panel — metadata, format, iCloud Link

Reached by tapping `Options` in the Photos share sheet, under the heading **"Adjust the information you share about a photo or video."** This is the best-sourced surface in the whole section — every string below is verbatim from the current iOS 26 iPhone User Guide.

| Control | Apple's exact copy |
|---|---|
| `Location` | "Turn off location data: Turn off `Location`." |
| File format | "Tap `Automatic` for the best file format for the destination, tap `Current` to prevent a file format conversion, or tap `Most Compatible` and files may convert to JPEG or MOV." |
| `iCloud Link` | "Turn on `iCloud Link` to share a URL to view or download the photos or videos. iCloud links are available for **30 days**." |
| `All Photos Data` | "Turn on `All Photos Data` to share the original file with edit history and metadata; the recipient can view and modify the current version (**available with AirDrop and iCloud links only**)." |
| Warning | "Sharing a photo or video includes sharing its associated metadata, such as date and time, location, device, and captions." |
