A third-party app can strip or keep EXIF and do its own format conversion, but `iCloud Link` and `All Photos Data` (edit-history-preserving transfer) are Apple-private. The nearest equivalents are your own share links plus exporting `PHAssetResource` originals together with `PHAdjustmentData`.

### 11.3 AirDrop (and NameDrop)

Peer-to-peer encrypted transfer over Wi-Fi + Bluetooth, range 30 ft / 10 m. Apple: *"Most items are saved in the app that they're sent from. For example, if someone uses AirDrop to send you a photo from the Photos app, it's saved in the Photos app on your device."* Transfers between devices signed into the same Apple Account auto-accept.

| Fact | Status |
|---|---|
| Discovery states: `Receiving Off` / `Contacts Only` / `Everyone for 10 Minutes` | Confirmed. Control Center surfaces only `Contacts Only` and `Everyone for 10 Minutes`; `Everyone for 10 Minutes` auto-reverts. |
| `Settings` > `General` > `AirDrop` > `Use Cellular Data` toggle | Confirmed |
| Proximity-initiated transfer by bringing two iPhones together (iOS 17+) | **Corrected — contact-gated.** Apple's wording is *"If you're within close range of someone in your contacts…"*, i.e. not any two iPhones. Shares its mechanism with NameDrop. |
| iOS 26.2 one-time AirDrop codes | Confirmed labels: recipient taps `Get AirDrop Code`; *"You can continue to share and receive items using AirDrop with that person for 30 days without needing to use another AirDrop code."* |
| Code is "6 digits" | **Unsourced.** Apple never states a digit count. |
| Managing known contacts | **Corrected.** Apple's documented path is the **Contacts app** → find the sender in your `Other Known` list → `Forget This Person`. The `Settings` > `General` > `AirDrop` > `Manage Known AirDrop Contacts` path appears **only in press coverage** of the 26.2 beta. |
| iOS 27: "AirDrop transfers are up to 80 percent faster" | Confirmed — **unreleased (fall 2026)**. Source is apple.com/os/ios (not Apple Newsroom). |

⚠️ **Trap:** **There is no public AirDrop-only API.** To SEND, present a `UIActivityViewController` — AirDrop is a built-in activity, and you can set `excludedActivityTypes` to leave essentially AirDrop alone. To RECEIVE, declare `CFBundleDocumentTypes` / `LSItemContentTypes` UTIs and handle the file in `application(_:open:options:)` / the scene delegate. You **cannot** enumerate nearby AirDrop peers or drive the transfer UI yourself.

### 11.4 Messages integration and `Shared with You`

Photos texted to you are auto-saved to your library and surfaced in a `Shared with You` shelf inside Photos. Apple, verbatim from the Photos guide: *"Photos and videos shared with you in the Messages app are automatically saved in your photo library. To turn off this feature, go to `Settings` > `Apps` > `Messages` > `Shared with You`, then turn off `Photos`."*

| Control | Path |
|---|---|
| Per-thread | In the conversation, tap `Info`, then turn off `Show in Shared with You` |
| Master switch | `Settings` > `Apps` > `Messages` > `Shared with You` > **`Automatic Sharing`** (separate from the per-app switches) |
| Per-app | `Settings` > `Apps` > `Messages` > `Shared with You` > choose apps |
| Supported first-party apps | `Music`, `Apple TV`, `News`, `Photos`, `Podcasts`, `Safari` |

**Developer mechanism:** the **SharedWithYou** framework (iOS 16+). `SWHighlightCenter` (priority-ordered list of links the system elects to surface — set a delegate, read `highlights`, use `highlightCollectionTitle`), `SWHighlight` (model object), `SWAttributionView` (system-rendered sender name/avatar chip linking back to the Messages thread; `highlightMenu`, `supplementalMenu`, `menuTitleForHideAction`). For collaboration: `SWCollaborationView` plus SharedWithYouCore.

⚠️ **Trap:** SharedWithYou surfaces **universal links to your content**, not raw images. A competing photo app gets a `Shared with You` shelf for *its own* shared albums/links — it does **not** get a feed of arbitrary images someone texted the user. You cannot replicate Photos' auto-save-from-Messages behaviour.

⚠️ **Trap (unverified claim):** The assertion that Photos ships an **iMessage app-drawer extension** is *not documented by Apple* and should not be stated as fact. The sticker half **is** well-supported: a lifted photo subject can be saved via `Add Sticker` and reused "in photos, email, text messages, and more" (Apple guide pages: "Make stickers from your photos", "Send stickers"). Third parties can build the equivalent with `MSMessagesAppViewController` (Messages framework) and sticker packs.

### 11.5 SharePlay — ⚠️ the biggest trap in this section

⚠️ **Trap: SharePlay in Photos is an Apple Vision Pro / visionOS feature, NOT an iPhone one.** The widely-repeated flow ("during a FaceTime call, open Photos, pick a photo, tap SharePlay so everyone sees it; scrubbing syncs") appears in the **Apple Vision Pro User Guide** under "View photos and videos together during a FaceTime call," and Apple explicitly gates it: *"You can look at photos and videos from the Photos app during a FaceTime call with other friends and family members **who have Apple Vision Pro**."* The iPhone User Guide's SharePlay page ("Use SharePlay to watch, listen, and play together in FaceTime on iPhone") covers video, music, Game Center multiplayer and live sports — **it contains no Photos section at all**. Any "iOS 15.1+" availability figure for Photos SharePlay is fabricated. On iPhone the rough equivalent is **FaceTime screen sharing**, a different mechanism. Do not build "parity with Photos SharePlay on iPhone" — there is nothing to reach parity with.

The *capability*, however, is fully replicable and is an opening: **Group Activities** (iOS 15+) lets any app do synchronised co-viewing. Adopt `GroupActivity`, use `GroupSession` to sync, `GroupActivitySharingController` to promote from your UI, `GroupSessionMessenger` for custom messages, and `GroupSessionJournal` for file/data transfer. Apple even ships a sample titled *"Creating a collaborative photo gallery with SharePlay."* Entitlement: `com.apple.developer.group-session`. On Vision Pro, Apple's version works with spatial Personas for panoramas and spatial videos.

### 11.6 iCloud Shared Albums and iCloud Shared Photo Library

These are **two distinct first-party sharing subsystems** and conflating them is a common error.

**iCloud Shared Albums.** Invite people who can add their own photos, videos and comments. Historically: downscaled (lossy), effectively Apple-only, a 5,000-photo limit, buried comments, and unreliable enough that "If Shared Albums aren't working" is a standing Apple support article.

**iCloud Shared Photo Library.** A *second, co-owned library* that **up to five other people** can contribute to and edit, with camera-level `Share Automatically` rules, participant-based auto-inclusion, and a Library/Personal toggle in the Photos and Camera UI. Apple ships dedicated guide pages: "Set up or join an iCloud Shared Photo Library," "Add content to an iCloud Shared Photo Library," "Use iCloud Shared Photo Library on iPhone." For a competing photo app this is arguably the most important sharing surface in the whole domain.

**iOS 27 (unreleased, fall 2026) — Apple closes its own biggest sharing weakness.** Apple's copy on apple.com/os/ios: *"It's easier for friends and family on Android or Windows to join and contribute their own photos **on iCloud.com**."* and *"Shared Albums also adds support for full-resolution sharing and new ways to filter and react to photos."*

⚠️ **Trap:** "Android support" is **web participation via iCloud.com**, not a native Android/Windows Photos client, and reporting indicates Android/Windows participants **still need an Apple Account**. Do not model it as a real cross-platform client.

⚠️ **Trap (unverified, verify at GA):** press reporting on the iOS 27 betas indicates the upgraded full-resolution Shared Albums are **no longer exempt from iCloud storage limits** — historically Shared Album content did not count against the user's quota; full-res content apparently now does. Material cost consequence for anyone modelling a competing sharing feature.

**Strategic read:** a competitor whose entire pitch is "we're the cross-platform, full-resolution shared album" has roughly one release cycle before that argument weakens. Differentiate on **permissions, ownership, export, and genuinely native non-Apple clients** instead.

⚠️ **Trap:** There is **no public API to create or post to an iCloud Shared Album**. PhotoKit can *read* assets in shared albums the user already belongs to (via `PHAssetCollection`), but that is all. Note the wrinkle: the App Intents `.photos` domain **does** define a `postToSharedAlbum` schema — that means **your app can expose *its own* shared-album posting to Siri**, not that you can post to Apple's.

### 11.7 The living-room surfaces: Apple TV, AirPlay, HomePod

**Apple TV screen saver.** Verbatim from the Apple TV User Guide: *"Go to the Photos app on Apple TV 4K. Navigate to `Shared Albums` or `Albums` at the top of the screen. Select a shared album from the Shared Albums category or an album from the Albums category, then select `Set as Screen Saver` and confirm."* Curation lives in `Settings` > `Screen Saver`:

| Setting | Options |
|---|---|
| `Current Selection` | `Aerials`, `Memories & Slideshows`, `Portraits`, `Snoopy` |
| `Memories & Slideshows` > `Memories` | `All Memories` or `Favorites` |
| `Memories & Slideshows` > `Albums` | `Favorites`, `Activity`, or one of the shared albums |
| `Portraits` | Set which types of portraits (`People`, `Pets`, `Nature`, `Cities`) to use, and how often to change the portrait |

`Portraits` is a **separate, photo-library-sourced screen saver type** that draws on People/Pets recognition — directly relevant to any face-recognition-adjacent product. *(The claimed first-launch prompt to "sync all iCloud photos or Shared Albums only" is unverified.)*

**AirPlay from Photos.** Documented and often forgotten: *"Show photos on Apple TV 4K or an AirPlay 2-enabled smart TV: Go to the Photos app, tap a photo, then tap [Share]. Swipe up, tap [AirPlay], then choose your Apple TV 4K…"* It is a share-sheet activity, so a third-party app gets it for free by using `UIActivityViewController`.

⚠️ **Trap:** **tvOS has no third-party screen saver extension point.** Aerials and photo screen savers are Apple-only; no public API supplies screen saver imagery. The nearest hook is `TVTopShelfContentProvider` (TVServices), which fills the Top Shelf strip on the tvOS Home Screen when your app icon is focused — a real but much weaker surface. A competitor's realistic play is a tvOS app with its own full-screen slideshow mode, which will **not** survive as a system screen saver.

**HomePod: not a surface.** No shipping HomePod or HomePod mini has a display; the touch surface shows only a waveform. There is no Apple Photos "HomePod frame" and nothing to replicate. The TV is the living-room photo surface.

### 11.8 Widgets: Home Screen, Lock Screen, StandBy, Always-On

**Photos Home Screen widget.** Two configurations — the widget gallery's type selector reads `Featured` / `Album` (the widget's display name is `Featured Photos`); the `Album` option was added in iOS 17. Sizes: small, medium, large (plus extra-large on iPad). Edited via touch-and-hold > `Edit Widget`.

Suppression controls are confirmed verbatim in Apple's guide page "Hide people, memories, and holidays in Photos on iPhone," which explicitly states they affect *"your memories, featured photos, and the Photos widget"*:

| Goal | Path |
|---|---|
| Kill featured photos + memories app-wide and in the widget | `Collections` > account button > turn off `Show Featured Content` |
| Suppress holidays | Same screen > turn off `Show Holiday Events` |
| Suppress a person | Photo > `More` > `Don't Feature a Person` > `Feature This Person Less` **or** `Never Feature This Person` |
| Undo all person suppression | `Collections` > account button > `Reset People & Pets Suggestions` |

*Unverified:* no Apple-authored page enumerates the full iOS 26 Photos widget variant list. A "People" or "Pets" **widget** is **not** Apple-sourced. `People`, `Nature`, `Cities` are confirmed as **Photo Shuffle (Lock Screen wallpaper) categories** — do not conflate the two.

**Developer mechanism:** WidgetKit. Families `systemSmall` / `systemMedium` / `systemLarge` / `systemExtraLarge` / `systemExtraLargePortrait`. Configure via `AppIntentConfiguration`. Widget extensions run in a **tightly memory-limited process** — render pre-downscaled thumbnails, never full-res `PHAsset`s, and drive updates with a `TimelineProvider` or APNs push. *(The commonly cited ~30 MB widget memory cap is **not officially documented** by Apple; treat the constraint as qualitative.)* iOS 27 (unreleased) adds further widget customization through App Intents plus "dynamic styling."

**Lock Screen accessory widgets — not a photo surface.** Confirmed from Apple's `WidgetRenderingMode` docs (iOS 16+): *"The system can modify the appearance of accessory family widgets. For example, it renders widgets on the Lock Screen on iPhone using the **vibrant** mode…"* Modes: `fullColor` / `accented` / `vibrant`. Families: `accessoryCircular`, `accessoryRectangular`, `accessoryInline` (`accessoryCorner` is watchOS).

⚠️ **Trap:** Because Lock Screen accessory widgets always render `vibrant` (desaturated, translucent), **you cannot put a full-colour photo on the Lock Screen via a widget.** The only photo path to the Lock Screen is the wallpaper — which has no public API.

**StandBy.** Apple: *"You can use StandBy to turn your iPhone into a bedside clock, a photo frame, a display for viewing widgets or Live Activities in full screen, and more."* Enable at `Settings` > `StandBy`. Charge the phone on its side, stationary, press the side button. *"Swipe left or right to switch between widgets, photos, and clocks."* Night Mode tints the screen red in low light. *"In each location where you charge iPhone with MagSafe, StandBy remembers your preferred view… you can have it set up for family photos in the kitchen or an alarm clock at your bedside."* Display timeout: `Settings` > `StandBy` > `Display` > `Automatically` / `After 20 Seconds` / `Never`. Availability iOS 17+.

⚠️ **Trap:** You can appear in StandBy's **widget** view but you **cannot create a StandBy photos view**. Per WWDC23 "Bring widgets to new places," the only widget family available in iPhone StandBy is **`systemSmall`**, and such widgets appear automatically in the StandBy gallery if you already ship a `systemSmall` Home Screen widget (use `containerBackgroundRemovable(false)` and let `widgetContentMargins` shrink for edge-to-edge). The photos pane of StandBy is a system view with **no extension point** — this is an inference from the absence of any such API, not an affirmative Apple denial, but a strong one.

**Always-On display.** iPhone 14 Pro and later. Apple: *"With the Always-On display (on supported models), StandBy stays on to show useful information… For all other iPhone models, it's easy to activate StandBy any time by either tapping the screen, gently nudging the table your iPhone is on, or using Siri."* The dimmed Lock Screen (and therefore its photo wallpaper) stays visible. **No photo surface for third parties** — Always-On renders the Lock Screen, and Lock Screen accessory widgets render `vibrant`.

### 11.9 Lock Screen wallpaper: Photos, Photo Shuffle, Spatial Scene

The single richest photo surface on the device, and the single hardest wall.

**Apple's exact information architecture** (corrected — this is frequently described wrong): `Settings` > `Wallpaper` > `Add New Wallpaper` (or touch-and-hold the Lock Screen > `+`). Then: *"Tap `Photos` or `Photo Shuffle` to choose your own photo. You can also select a wallpaper from categories like `Weather & Astronomy`, `Emoji`, or `Color`."*

⚠️ **Trap:** `Spatial Scene` is **not** a sibling tab of `Photos` / `Photo Shuffle` in the wallpaper gallery. It is a category tab **inside the Photos picker**. Apple: *"Tap `Photos`. **Scroll to the right in the top bar and tap the `Spatial Scene` tab**."*

| Feature | Apple's exact behaviour | Availability |
|---|---|---|
| `Photo Shuffle` | "Choose one or more categories like `People`, `Nature`, or `Cities`, or choose an existing album. Choose a shuffle frequency (`On Tap`, `On Lock`, `Hourly`, or `Daily`). Tap the `Use Album` button or `Use Featured Photos` button when done." Manual mode: "From the Photo Shuffle screen, tap `Select Photos Manually`," pick images, then "tap the ellipsis button to choose a shuffle frequency." | iOS 16+ |
| `Depth Effect` | On-device subject segmentation composites the subject in front of the clock. Silently disables itself when the clock would be occluded. | iOS 16+ |
| `Spatial Scene` | Generative 2D→3D depth synthesis, rendered with parallax on device motion. "A `Generating Spatial Scene` message appears and disappears once the 3D effect is ready." Eligibility: "Eligible photos typically feature high-quality lighting, a clear separation between the subject and background, or a landscape orientation." "With either, **only your Lock Screen will display the 3D effect**." | iOS 26, **iPhone 12 or later** |
| Adaptive clock | iOS 26: the time "fluidly adapts to the available space in an image." User Guide: "On iPhone 12 and later, you can try a spatial scene for a 3D effect and try options where the time dynamically adapts to your photo wallpaper and notifications." | iOS 26 |
| Other controls | Clock font/transparency, colour-filter `styles`, `Add Widgets`, Live Photo slow-motion on wake, then `Set as Wallpaper Pair` or `Customize Home Screen`. | iOS 16+ |

⚠️ **Trap — the hardest wall in the section:** **There is no public API to read, set, or register a Lock Screen wallpaper, and no way to contribute a wallpaper "category" or a Photo Shuffle source.** (Inferred from the absence of any documented API rather than an affirmative Apple statement, but nothing contradicts it.) The only legitimate approximations: (1) generate the parallax/depth-composited image yourself with Vision subject masks plus a depth map, and let the user save it and set it manually; (2) do the same effect in-app. Note the *subject-aware framing itself is fully replicable* — `VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest` gives you the same foreground mask Apple uses for Depth Effect (see 11.11).

iOS 27 (unreleased) adds a wallpaper extension that uses Apple Intelligence to expand a photo to fill the Lock Screen.

### 11.10 Journal photo suggestions — the gated API

Journal proposes `Moments` assembled from recent life events — places visited, photos taken, songs played, workouts — generated **on device** ("data used for suggestions is private and stored on your iPhone"); entries are end-to-end encrypted in iCloud.

| Setting | Path / options |
|---|---|
| Per-category suggestion sources | `Settings` > `Privacy & Security` > `Journaling Suggestions` |
| Write without suggestions | `Settings` > `Apps` > `Journal` > turn off `Show Suggested Moments` |
| `Add Entry Title` | `Always` / `Only for Moments` / `Never` |
| `Always Use Moment Date` | toggle |
| `Add Current Location` | toggle |
| `Save to Photos` | Saves photos/videos taken inside Journal to the Photos library |
| Notifications | `Settings` > `Notifications` > `Journaling Suggestions` |

**Developer mechanism:** the **JournalingSuggestions** framework (iOS 17.2+; also iPadOS 26.0) gives you *the same system picker*: `JournalingSuggestionsPicker` in SwiftUI, returning `JournalingSuggestion` / `JournalingSuggestionAsset`, with `JournalingSuggestionsConfiguration` and notification-driven presentation via `JournalingSuggestionPresentationToken`. You do **not** request photo permission — the user's selection in the system picker *is* the consent.

⚠️ **Trap:** *"For the picker to appear, your app needs a special entitlement in your app's code signature"* — **`com.apple.developer.journal.allow`**, which requires Apple's approval. This is the single most privileged Photos-adjacent API and the entitlement is a real gatekeeping bottleneck for a competitor. Plan for a "we may never get this" branch.

### 11.11 On-image intelligence: Live Text, Visual Look Up, subject lift, Visual Intelligence

All four of Apple's marquee on-image features are available to third parties — three of them *pixel-identical*, one of them as a search-results provider.

**Live Text.** Apple: *"Live Text recognizes text within your photos, videos, and images you find online."* Enable at `Settings` > `General` > `Language & Region` > `Live Text`. Usage: *"Open a photo or pause a video that contains text. Tap [Live Text button], then touch and hold the selected text. Use the grab points to select specific text."* Menu labels, verbatim: `Copy Text` / `Select All` / `Look Up` / `Translate` / `Search the web` / `Share`. Quick actions: *"you can tap a quick action at the bottom of the screen to do things like make a phone call, get directions, translate languages, convert currencies, and more."* Works in *"Safari, Photos, Camera, Quick Look, and more."* iOS 15+ (iPhone XS/XR or later); video Live Text iOS 16+. Region/language gated.

**Visual Look Up.** Apple: *"With Visual Look Up, you can identify and learn about architectural landmarks, popular statues, famous art, plants, pets, books, and more that appear in photos and images. Visual Look Up can also identify food and suggest related recipes."* UI: *"If the `Info` button displays a symbol with stars, Visual Look Up is available. Tap the starred `Info` button, then tap `Look Up` at the top of the photo information…"* iOS 15+; region/language gated. ⚠️ **Trap:** the per-version category expansion often quoted (iOS 16 birds/insects; iOS 17 laundry-care symbols and car-dashboard symbols) is **press-sourced only** — Apple's current guide says only "and more." Do not put "laundry symbols" in a spec citing Apple.

**Lift subject from background.** Apple, verbatim: *"You can isolate the subject of a photo or video frame from its background, then copy or share it in other documents and apps. You can use this feature in Photos, Safari, Quick Look, and more. Open a photo in full screen, **or pause a video on any frame**. Touch and hold the subject. When an outline appears around the subject, do one of the following: Continue to touch the subject, then with another finger, open a document in another app and drag the subject into the document. / Tap `Copy` or `Copy Subject`… / Tap `Look Up`… / Tap `Add Sticker`, then save the sticker to use in photos, email, text messages, and more. / Tap `Share`…"* The page is titled "Lift a subject from the photo **or video** background." Subject lift iOS 16+; `Add Sticker` (Live Stickers) iOS 17+.

**Visual Intelligence.** The Apple Intelligence-era successor surface. Invocation (corrected — the usual list is incomplete): **click and hold** the Camera Control (Apple's verb is "click and hold," not "long press"); on iPhone 17e, iPhone 16e, iPhone 15 Pro and 15 Pro Max, *"you can access visual intelligence by customizing the Action button **or Lock Screen**, or opening Control Center."* In iOS 26 it extends to the screen: take a screenshot (*"Quickly press and release the side button and the volume up button at the same time"*) and Visual Intelligence options appear. Apple Newsroom, verbatim: visual intelligence *"extends to a user's iPhone screen so they can search and take action on anything they're viewing across apps"*; users can *"ask ChatGPT questions about what they're looking at onscreen… as well as search Google, Etsy, or other supported apps to find similar images and products"*; and *"Visual intelligence also recognizes when a user is looking at an event and suggests adding it to their calendar, repopulating key details like date, time, and location."* Onscreen actions include `Ask`, `Search`, `Summarize`, `Read Aloud`, `Add to Calendar`, plus save/delete-screenshot controls; in-world modes cover businesses (`Schedule` / `Order` / `Menu` / `Reserve`) and plant/animal ID. iOS 26 added on-device identification of art, books, landmarks, natural landmarks and sculptures. iOS 27 (unreleased) adds "Siri mode in Camera — start a visual search right from your viewfinder," plus expanded bill splitting / nutrition insights and visionOS support.

⚠️ **Trap:** **"Highlight to Search" is not an Apple label.** The gesture is real — Apple describes it without naming it: *"Swipe your finger on a specific item to highlight it and search for that particular item."* The name comes from press coverage. Do not ship a menu label Apple does not ship.

*Device gating (verify against Apple's "iOS and iPadOS Feature Availability" page):* Visual Intelligence requires Apple Intelligence-capable iPhones; Apple's own copy names iPhone 17e, iPhone 16e, iPhone 15 Pro and 15 Pro Max for the Action-button/Lock-Screen invocation path. The full current device list for iOS 26.5 was not independently confirmed.

**The developer APIs — this is where the section pays for itself.**

| Apple feature | Third-party API | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Live Text (still) | **VisionKit**: create an `ImageAnalyzer` (check `ImageAnalyzer.isSupported`, `supportedTextRecognitionLanguages`), call `analyze(_:configuration:)` with `AnalysisTypes` of `.text` / `.machineReadableCode` / `.visualLookUp`; attach an `ImageAnalysisInteraction` to your `UIImageView` via `addInteraction(_:)`, set `analysis`, set `preferredInteractionTypes` to `.textSelection` / `.dataDetectors` / `.automatic` / `.automaticTextOnly`. | You get **Apple's exact selection UI, callout menu and quick actions**. Read state via `text`, `selectedText`, `selectedAttributedText`, `hasText(at:)`, `hasDataDetector(at:)`, `selectedRanges`, `resetTextSelection()`, `liveTextButtonVisible`, `setSupplementaryInterfaceHidden(_:animated:)`. Non-`UIImageView` hosts must implement `contentsRect(for:)` on `ImageAnalysisInteractionDelegate`. macOS equivalent: `ImageAnalysisOverlayView`. |
| Live Text (live camera) | `DataScannerViewController` (VisionKit, iOS 16+) — `startScanning()`, `recognizedItems`, `dataScanner(_:didTapOn:)`, `capturePhoto()`, `regionOfInterest`, `zoom`. | Requires `NSCameraUsageDescription`. |
| Visual Look Up | Add `.visualLookUp` to `ImageAnalyzer.AnalysisTypes` **and** to `ImageAnalysisInteraction.preferredInteractionTypes`. The framework "adds a button in the bottom corner of the view that people can click or tap for more information about the recognized subjects." | ⚠️ **Trap:** you get Apple's Look Up sheet for free, but you **cannot** customise the knowledge results, add categories, or read the recognized class programmatically. For that you build your own classifier. |
| Subject lift (system UI) | `ImageAnalysisInteraction` with `.imageSubject` in `preferredInteractionTypes`. Exposes `subjects` (`Set<Subject>`), `subject(at:)`, `image(for:)` (returns the cut-out `UIImage`), `highlightedSubjects`, and a `SubjectUnavailable` error. | Apple's exact glow-outline and long-press behaviour. Drag-out is standard UIKit drag & drop (`UIDragInteraction`). |
| Subject lift (custom pipeline) | **Vision `VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest`** — "A request that generates an instance mask of noticeable objects to separate from the background." iOS 17.0 / iPadOS 17.0 / Mac Catalyst 17.0 / macOS 14.0 / tvOS 17.0 / visionOS 1.0. Results are `VNInstanceMaskObservation` (`allInstances`, `instanceMask`, `generateMask(forInstances:)`, `generateMaskedImage(ofInstances:from:croppedToInstancesExtent:)`, `generateScaledMaskForImage(forInstances:from:)`). Swift-6 replacement: the **struct** `GenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest` (iOS 18.0 / iPadOS 18.0 / macOS 15.0 / tvOS 18.0 / visionOS 2.0 / watchOS 27.0), producing `InstanceMaskObservation`, with `perform(on:orientation:)` overloads and a `Revision` enum. | Use Vision when you need HDR preservation, very large images, or **multiple instances**; use VisionKit when you want Apple's exact interaction. Apple's own Photos UI only lifts **one** subject at a time — Vision will return many. That is a free product advantage. |
| Visual Intelligence results | **VisualIntelligence** framework (iOS 26.0+, iPadOS 26.0+, macOS 27.0). Implement an App Intents `IntentValueQuery` taking a `SemanticContentDescriptor` (exposes `pixelBuffer` and `labels` for the captured scene/screenshot); match against your library; return `AppEntity` results with a good `DisplayRepresentation` (title, subtitle, image). Tapping a result fires your `OpenIntent`. | ⚠️ **Trap:** Apple states *"Your app can't contain more than one `IntentValueQuery` that takes a `SemanticContentDescriptor`"* — use the `@UnionValue` macro to return multiple entity types. Limit results (~100) and offer a "More results" button backed by an intent conforming to the `semanticContentSearch` schema. **This is how Etsy appears in visual search — a photo app can return "photos in YOUR library that look like this."** |

### 11.12 Files, Spotlight, Siri and Shortcuts

**Photos in Files — an open goal.** Apple is explicit: *"While you can save photos to iCloud Drive (or another cloud service) in the Files app, your photo library is stored in the Photos app."* The library is **not browsable in Files**. The only bridges are the `Save to Files` share-sheet activity (exports a copy), importing from Files back into Photos, and direct import/export to an external USB storage device (Apple guide: "Import and export photos and videos on iPhone"). Apple also ships a dedicated "Print photos" page for AirPrint.

⚠️ **Opening, not a trap:** a third-party photo library **can** appear inside Files as a first-class, browsable provider by shipping a **File Provider extension** (FileProvider framework), with optional in-place document access via `LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace`. **Apple's own Photos does not do this.** A library that is navigable in Files, drag-and-droppable into any app, and mountable in macOS Finder has a structural advantage Apple has chosen not to take.

**Photos in Spotlight.** Confirmed verbatim from "Search with Spotlight on iPhone" (iOS 26): Spotlight lets you *"find and open webpages, apps, and images in your photo library, across your system, and on the web,"* and it searches *"even text in your photos using Live Text."* Also confirmed: *"When you search for an app, app shortcuts for your most likely next action appear within the Top Hit. (For example, a shortcut to the `Favorites` album appears when you search for Photos.)"*

⚠️ **Trap:** Three widely-repeated Spotlight "facts" are **refuted or unsourced**: (a) the natural-language example *"photos of [Name] at [location]"* does **not** appear in the current guide; (b) the five-toggle per-app control list (`Show App in Search`, `Show Content in Search`, `Show on Home Screen`, `Suggest App`, `Suggest Notifications`) is **not** what Apple documents — the current guide documents exactly **one** control: *"Go to `Settings` > `Search`. Scroll down, tap an app, then turn `Show App in Search` on or off."*; (c) `Show More` / `Search in App` result pagination is undocumented. Do not ship these as spec.

**Getting *your* photos into Spotlight — three layers:**

1. **Core Spotlight** — index `CSSearchableItem` / `CSSearchableItemAttributeSet` (with `thumbnailData`, `CSPerson`, custom attributes) into `CSSearchableIndex`; indexes stay **on-device and private**. Use `CSIndexExtensionRequestHandler` / `CSImportExtension` to re-index on demand.
2. **App Intents `IndexedEntity`** — conform your photo `AppEntity` to `IndexedEntity` and donate it. Apple's own sample "Integrating your photo app with Apple Intelligence" does exactly this: *"By conforming app entities to `IndexedEntity` and donating them to a Spotlight index, the sample app enables people to search for its content in Spotlight and enable semantic search results."*
3. **iOS 27 (unreleased)** — entity schemas *"contribute your app's content to the Spotlight semantic index, so Siri can surface it with attribution back to your app,"* with a dedicated WWDC26 session "LLM search using Core Spotlight."

Net: **a third-party photo app can be searched semantically from Spotlight.** Apple Photos' own Spotlight results are shallow.

**App Intents `.photos` schema domain — the most important integration surface for a competing photo app, and almost nobody has adopted it.** Apple: *"The `.photos` domain defines app schemas that provide a structured representation for common photo and video actions and content. Apply schemas in the `.photos` domain to make your app's photo and video functionality available to Apple Intelligence and Siri… a person can edit a photo on different apps that support the `editAsset` schema with the same phrases."*

Full enumerated action list (all 26 verified against Apple's live docs):

`addAssetsToAlbum`, `cleanupPhoto`, `copyEdits`, `createAlbum`, `createAssets`, `crop`, `deleteAlbum`, `deleteAssets`, `duplicateAssets`, `editAsset`, `openAlbum`, `openAsset`, `pasteEdits`, `postToSharedAlbum`, `removeAssetsFromAlbum`, `setDepth`, `setExposure`, `setFilter`, `setRotation`, `setSaturation`, `setWarmth`, `straighten`, `toggleDepth`, `toggleSuggestedEdits`, `updateAlbum`, `updateAsset`, `updateRecognizedPerson`

Content/parameter types: `album`, `asset`, `recognizedPerson`. Static enums: `albumType`, `assetType`, `filterType`, `rotationDirection`. Apple: *"Most schemas in this domain operate on assets that are already in your app's library. The exception is `createAssets`, which adds new assets from an external source."*

⚠️ **Trap (will break your code): the protocol namespace everyone quotes is deprecated.** `AssistantSchemas.*` — the **entire namespace**, including `AssistantSchemas.PhotosIntent` / `PhotosEntity` / `PhotosEnum` — is marked **deprecated** in Apple's current docs. The live types are **`AppSchema.PhotosIntent` / `AppSchema.PhotosEntity` / `AppSchema.PhotosEnum`** (under `AppSchema`, iOS 18.0+). The macros are **`@AppIntent(schema:)` / `@AppEntity(schema:)` / `@AppEnum(schema:)`**, *not* `@AssistantIntent(schema:)`. Apple's doc collection is retitled "App schema domains." This was renamed for WWDC26 ("Build intelligent Siri experiences with App Schemas").

⚠️ **Trap (deprecated schemas):** `openAsset` is **deprecated** — Apple: "Use `.system.open` instead." `search` in the `.photos` domain is **deprecated** — Apple: "Use `.system.search` instead."

⚠️ **Trap (build-target error, and the most consequential correction here): every schema in the `.photos` domain is iOS 18.0+ — shippable today — EXCEPT `editAsset`, which alone is iOS 27.0+.** The widely-repeated advice to "treat the full editing schema set as an iOS 26→27 target" is **backwards**. `crop`, `straighten`, `setFilter`, `setExposure`, `setSaturation`, `setWarmth`, `setRotation`, `setDepth`, `toggleDepth`, `cleanupPhoto`, `copyEdits`, `pasteEdits`, `toggleSuggestedEdits`, `createAssets`, `duplicateAssets`, `postToSharedAlbum`, `updateRecognizedPerson` — all verified iOS 18.0+. Only Apple's *sample project* ("Integrating your photo app with Apple Intelligence") requires iOS 27.0 / Xcode 27.0. **You can ship Siri-controllable photo editing right now.**

Also adopt: `Transferable` on your entities (so the system can hand your photos to other apps), `NSUserActivity` annotation of the on-screen entity so "rotate this photo" resolves to what's visible, and `OpenIntent`. **iOS 27 (unreleased) additions relevant to photos:** `EntityCollection<PhotoEntity>` (pass identifiers, not resolved entities — Apple's example is literally `TagPhotosIntent`), `SyncableEntity` (stable cross-device IDs — Apple's example is `PhotoEntity`), `LongRunningIntent` + `CancellableIntent` with progress (Apple's example is `UploadPhotoIntent`, and WWDC26 notes `LongRunningIntent` supports **background GPU access** for photo processing / on-device inference), `RelevantEntities`, `ValueRepresentation`, `ExecutionTargets`, `@UnionValue`, and the View Annotations API.

**SiriKit is deprecated as of WWDC 2026; App Intents is now the only path.** Apple Photos' own Siri support is weak. This is a **use-it-or-lose-it window** in which a competitor can be *more Siri-controllable than Photos itself*.

### 11.13 The library APIs: picker, background upload, editing extension

**`PHPickerViewController`** — the system picker, rendered **out of process**, with **no permission prompt at all**, because the user's selection *is* the grant. Availability: iOS 14.0+ / iPadOS 14.0+ / Mac Catalyst 14.0+ / **macOS 13.0+** / visionOS 1.0+ (SwiftUI: `PhotosPicker`). Apple's stated benefits: deferred image loading and recovery UI; reliable handling of large/complex assets like RAW and panoramic images; user-selectable assets `UIImagePickerController` can't reach; a Live-Photos-only filter; `PHLivePhoto` objects **without** library access; and **"stricter validations against invalid inputs."** Constraints, verbatim: *"you can't subclass `PHPickerViewController`. Its view hierarchy belongs to the system,"* and *"In iOS 17 and later, the picker controller ignores touch events while its opacity is anything other than fully opaque."*

**Full PhotoKit** (`PHPhotoLibrary`, fetching, change requests, `PHPhotoLibraryChangeObserver`, persistent change tokens) requires explicit authorization: `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription` (read/write) or `NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription` (add-only). ⚠️ **Trap:** a missing usage-description key **crashes the app**. Since iOS 14 users can grant a **limited** library (`PHAuthorizationStatus.limited`); handle it properly — re-prompt with `PHPhotoLibrary.presentLimitedLibraryPicker(from:)`, and suppress the periodic system `Select More Photos` alert with the `PHPhotoLibraryPreventAutomaticLimitedAccessAlert` Info.plist key if you present your own. `PHAccessLevel` / `PHAuthorizationStatus` govern the grant.

*Design decision for the team:* a lightweight companion app should use `PHPicker` (zero prompts, best conversion). A full library replacement needs `.readWrite` full access — which is required anyway for the Background Upload extension — and must degrade gracefully when a large share of users pick `Select Photos…`.

**PhotoKit Background Resource Upload extension — the single biggest unlock for a competing photo app.** Apple: *"PhotoKit's Background Resource Upload extension enables apps to deliver seamless cloud backup experiences. The system manages uploads on your app's behalf, processing them in the background even when people switch to other apps or lock their devices. The system calls your extension to process uploads when conditions allow, scheduling work based on factors such as network availability, power state, and device activity."*

| Element | Detail |
|---|---|
| Extension point | `com.apple.photos.background-upload` (set `EXExtensionPointIdentifier` inside `EXAppExtensionAttributes`) |
| Required Info.plist key | **`BackgroundUploadURLBase`** (String, e.g. `https://api.example.com`) — "The system requires this key for network access validation." |
| Host-app prerequisite | **Full** library access (`requestAuthorization(for: .readWrite) == .authorized`), then call `PHPhotoLibrary.shared().setUploadJobExtensionEnabled(true)`; check `uploadJobExtensionEnabled` |
| Runtime flow | System invokes `processJobs()`; you `fetchJobs(action:options:)` with retry / acknowledge / process actions; create jobs inside `performChanges` blocks (one job per `PHAssetResource`, each with a destination `URLRequest` carrying your auth headers); return `.processing` / `.failure` |
| Job states | `registered`, `pending`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled` |
| Error handling | `limitExceeded` (inflight job cap — acknowledge completed jobs to free capacity); `persistentChangeTokenExpired` from `fetchPersistentChanges(since:)` (discard token, re-sync); `responseHeaderFields` (lowercased); `error` (NSURLErrorDomain codes) |
| Download without upload | `creationRequestForDownloadJob(resource:)` fetches an iCloud resource locally **without** uploading (`type == .downloadOnly`) |
| Cleanup | `willTerminate()` |
| Resumable uploads | Supported, per the draft resumable-uploads protocol |
| Availability | `PHBackgroundResourceUploadExtension` — **iOS 26.1 / iPadOS 26.1** (shipping today). `PHBackgroundResourceUploadJobExtension` (async, exposing `processJobs()` and `willTerminate()`) — **iOS 27.0 / iPadOS 27.0 / Mac Catalyst 27.0 / macOS 27.0 (unreleased)** |

⚠️ **Trap (precision):** it is often said that "`PHBackgroundResourceUploadExtension` is deprecated in iOS 27." Apple does **not** flag the protocol symbol itself as deprecated — it deprecates its **members**: `process()` carries "Adopt `PHBackgroundResourceUploadJobExtension` instead," and `notifyTermination()` is likewise deprecated. Net advice is unchanged (plan for both; new code targets the Job extension), but the literal claim is wrong.

⚠️ **Trap:** **the extension does not work in the Simulator**, and developers report behaviour differences between iOS 26.1 and 26.2. Budget device-only testing.

**Why this matters:** before iOS 26.1, third-party backup apps (Google Photos, Immich, Dropbox) could only upload while foregrounded or during unreliable background-refresh windows. That was Apple's single biggest structural advantage over every rival, and **it is now largely gone.** Immich and others are already building on it.

**Photo Editing Extension — your app *inside* Apple Photos.** Apple: *"You can incorporate your app's features directly into the Photos app in iOS or macOS by building an app extension. A photo-editing app extension can enable people to edit media, apply your app's filter effects, build slideshows, books, or custom content, such as a collage, right in Photos app using code that you supply."* And: *"Include the app extension in your app bundle and the system installs it in Photos at the same time someone installs your app."* Adopt `PHContentEditingController` (`canHandle(_:)`, `startContentEditing(with:placeholderImage:)`, `finishContentEditing(completionHandler:)`, `cancelContentEditing()`, `shouldShowCancelConfirmation`) plus `PHContentEditingInput`, `PHContentEditingOutput`, and `PHAdjustmentData` — the last of which makes your edits **non-destructive and re-editable later by your extension**. Availability: iOS 8.0+, iPadOS 8.0+, Mac Catalyst, macOS 10.11+, visionOS 1.0+. A rare **inbound** hook — instead of pulling users out of Photos, you inject into it. Badly underused. Memory- and time-constrained.

### 11.14 The other devices: Mac, Watch, Vision Pro, car

**Continuity Camera (iPhone as a capture device for the Mac).** On the Mac, **Control-click where you want to insert** (Apple: *"Control-click where you want to insert the sketch or photo"*; *"You may need to click `Insert from iPhone or iPad` before seeing the options"*), then `Take Photo` or `Scan Documents`. The Camera app opens on the phone; tap the Shutter, then `Use Photo`. For scans, drag the corners then `Keep Scan`. Requirements, verbatim: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on; *"signed in to the same Apple Account on both devices"*; *"within 30 feet (10 meters)"* (plus a VPN local-networking caveat). Apple documents two siblings on the same page: **Continuity Sketch** (draw on iPhone → appears on Mac) and **Continuity Markup** (mark up a Mac file using iPhone).

*Third-party API:* essentially free **on macOS** — AppKit responder-chain support means `NSTextView` and standard document apps get the "Insert from iPhone" menu automatically; a Mac app can adopt NSServices/responder methods (`importFromDevice:`) to receive the image. On iOS there is **no** third-party API to *be* the capture target for another device — it is a system Continuity service.

**Apple Watch.** watchOS ships a Photos app that syncs a chosen album or memories, plus a **Photos watch face** and a **photo complication**. A real cross-device integration target for a photo product; frequently forgotten.

**Apple Vision Pro / spatial.** Photos on visionOS shows the library, memories, panoramas, spatial photos and spatial videos, all syncing via iCloud Photos. visionOS 2 added creating spatial photos **from existing 2D library photos** via ML — Apple Newsroom: users *"can revisit past memories by creating spatial photos directly from their library in the Photos app, using advanced machine learning to transform a 2D image into a beautiful spatial photo."* Apple also ships a separate, Apple-curated **Spatial Gallery** app (no third-party submission path). iOS 26 brought the same idea to iPhone as **Spatial Scenes** (hexagon button in the image viewer; iPhone 12+). *(The claim of a dedicated `Panoramas` **tab** in the visionOS Photos tab bar is unverified — panoramas are certainly first-class there, but the tab-bar label was not confirmed.)*

*Third-party API:* PARTIAL. PhotoKit is available on visionOS 1.0+ and Vision/VisionKit largely are too, so a third-party visionOS photo app can read the library and display spatial media. But ⚠️ **Trap: Apple's 2D→3D spatial-photo generation is not exposed as a public API.** You would build your own monocular depth + novel-view synthesis.

**iOS 27 Photos additions (unreleased, fall 2026), per apple.com/os/ios:** `Spatial Reframing` (*"Reframe a photo after it's been taken with Spatial Reframing"*), an **`Extend` tool** (*"Expand your shots with the Extend tool"*), an enhanced Clean Up that can *"remove even larger objects,"* a wallpaper extension that uses Apple Intelligence to expand a photo to fill the Lock Screen, and *"new photos load in your Photos library up to 70% faster."* Apple's page carries the standard "Features are subject to change" disclaimer.

**CarPlay — out of scope.** There is **no Photos app on CarPlay and no photo app category.** Apple's CarPlay developer documentation limits third-party CarPlay apps to entitlement-gated, driving-safe categories: audio, communication/messaging, driving task, EV charging, fueling, navigation, parking, and quick food ordering. Photos is deliberately absent for driver-distraction reasons. iOS 26 did bring widgets and Live Activities to CarPlay (Apple Newsroom: *"With widgets and Live Activities, users can stay in the loop without losing focus on the road"*), so the only conceivable surface is a CarPlay widget — and whether a photo-content widget would pass App Review for CarPlay is doubtful. *(Whether the Photos widget itself can appear in CarPlay in iOS 26 is unverified.)* **Treat CarPlay as out of scope.**

### 11.15 Context: the iOS 26 Photos app shape

After the widely disliked iOS 18 single-scroll redesign (which removed tabs), **iOS 26 restored a tab bar**. Apple Newsroom: *"The Photos app is updated to feature separate tabs for `Library` and `Collections` views."* Search moved to the bottom. Liquid Glass translucency throughout; a hexagon button in the top-right of the image viewer produces a `Spatial Scene`. Craig Federighi on stage at WWDC: *"Many of you missed using tabs in the Photos app."*

`Collections` contains `Recent Days`, `People & Pets`, `Pinned`, `Memories`, `Trips`, `Albums`, `Featured Photos` — reorderable, collapsible (names-only), with multiple thumbnail sizes. *(This exact sub-section inventory is high-confidence but is not enumerated as a single verbatim list by Apple — verify on device.)* The iOS 18 → iOS 26 reversal is itself the strongest available evidence that **Photos' navigation is a contested, winnable axis.**

### 11.x What a third-party app can and cannot do

| Capability | Available to 3rd parties? | Mechanism / why not |
|---|---|---|
| Appear in the system Share Sheet | **Yes** | Share Extension (`com.apple.share-services`) with `NSExtensionActivationRule`; Action Extension; `UIActivity` subclass |
| Present a share sheet with AirDrop | **Yes** | `UIActivityViewController`; exclude other activities via `excludedActivityTypes` |
| Enumerate AirDrop peers / drive the transfer UI | **No** | No public AirDrop-only API exists. Send via `UIActivityViewController`; receive via `CFBundleDocumentTypes` / `LSItemContentTypes` + `application(_:open:options:)` |
| Generate an "iCloud Link" or transfer `All Photos Data` (edit history) | **No** | Apple-private. Build your own share links; export `PHAssetResource` originals + `PHAdjustmentData` yourself |
| Occupy the share sheet's top conversation-suggestion row | **Yes** (mechanism documented; the row itself is undocumented) | Donate `INSendMessageIntent` on every send; add it to `IntentsSupported` in the share extension's Info.plist. ⚠️ SiriKit deprecated at WWDC26 — verify in the iOS 27 SDK |
| Get a `Shared with You` shelf | **Yes** — but only for **your own links** | SharedWithYou framework (iOS 16+): `SWHighlightCenter`, `SWHighlight`, `SWAttributionView`, `SWCollaborationView`. It surfaces universal links to *your* content, **not** raw texted images |
| Auto-save images from Messages into your app | **No** | Apple-private behaviour of Photos |
| Ship an iMessage app / sticker pack | **Yes** | `MSMessagesAppViewController` (Messages framework); sticker packs |
| Synchronised co-viewing over FaceTime (SharePlay) | **Yes, fully** | Group Activities (iOS 15+): `GroupActivity`, `GroupSession`, `GroupActivitySharingController`, `GroupSessionMessenger`, `GroupSessionJournal`. Entitlement `com.apple.developer.group-session`. Apple sample: "Creating a collaborative photo gallery with SharePlay". ⚠️ Note Apple Photos itself has **no** SharePlay on iPhone — this is a *gap*, not parity |
| Create or post to an **iCloud** Shared Album | **No** | No public API. PhotoKit can only *read* shared albums the user already belongs to (`PHAssetCollection`). (`postToSharedAlbum` in App Intents exposes **your** app's sharing to Siri, not Apple's) |
| Ship a Home Screen widget of photos | **Yes** | WidgetKit; `systemSmall`…`systemExtraLargePortrait`; `AppIntentConfiguration`; `TimelineProvider`. Memory-constrained — use downscaled thumbnails |
| Put a full-colour photo on the **Lock Screen** via a widget | **No** | Lock Screen accessory widgets always render in `vibrant` mode (`WidgetRenderingMode`). Hard wall |
| Set / read / register a **Lock Screen wallpaper**, or add a Photo Shuffle source | **No** | No public API of any kind. Hardest wall in the section. Workaround: generate the depth-composited image yourself and let the user set it manually |
| Appear in **StandBy** | **Partial** | Widget view only, and only `systemSmall` (WWDC23). The StandBy **photos pane is a system view with no extension point** |
| Influence the **Always-On** dimmed display | **No** | It renders the Lock Screen; accessory widgets are `vibrant` |
| Be a **tvOS screen saver** | **No** | No screen saver extension point exists. Nearest hook: `TVTopShelfContentProvider` (Top Shelf strip). Fallback: your own full-screen slideshow inside a tvOS app |
| AirPlay photos to Apple TV / AirPlay 2 TV | **Yes** | Standard share-sheet AirPlay activity |
| HomePod photo frame | **n/a** | No HomePod has a display. Not a surface |
| Use Apple's **Journal suggestions** picker | **Yes, but gated** | JournalingSuggestions (iOS 17.2+): `JournalingSuggestionsPicker`, `JournalingSuggestion`, `JournalingSuggestionAsset`. **Requires the `com.apple.developer.journal.allow` entitlement — Apple approval required** |
| Reproduce **Live Text** exactly | **Yes, verbatim and free** | VisionKit `ImageAnalyzer` + `ImageAnalysisInteraction` (`.textSelection`, `.dataDetectors`). Live camera: `DataScannerViewController` |
| Reproduce **Visual Look Up** | **Partial** | `.visualLookUp` in `AnalysisTypes` + `preferredInteractionTypes` gives you Apple's sheet — but you **cannot** customise results, add categories, or read the recognized class programmatically |
| Reproduce **subject lift** | **Yes, two ways** | (1) VisionKit `.imageSubject` → Apple's exact glow UI + `image(for:)` cut-out. (2) Vision `VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest` (iOS 17+) / `GenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest` (iOS 18+) → **multiple** instances, HDR-safe, very large images |
| Appear in **Visual Intelligence** results | **Yes** | VisualIntelligence framework (iOS 26+): App Intents `IntentValueQuery` taking a `SemanticContentDescriptor` (`pixelBuffer`, `labels`) → `AppEntity` results → `OpenIntent`. **Max one such query per app**; use `@UnionValue` for multiple types |
| Be **browsable in the Files app** | **Yes — and Apple Photos is not** | File Provider extension (FileProvider framework) + `LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace`. Structural advantage Apple has declined to take |
| Be **searchable in Spotlight**, semantically | **Yes** | Core Spotlight (`CSSearchableItem`, `CSSearchableIndex`, `CSImportExtension`) **and** App Intents `IndexedEntity` donation. iOS 27 (unreleased): entity schemas feed the Spotlight semantic index with attribution |
| Be **Siri / Apple Intelligence controllable** | **Yes — and this is the strategic one** | App Intents `.photos` schema domain: 26 actions, `album`/`asset`/`recognizedPerson` entities, 4 enums. Use `AppSchema.*` + `@AppIntent(schema:)`. **All schemas iOS 18.0+ except `editAsset` (iOS 27.0+)** |
| **Background cloud backup** of the user's library | **Yes, since iOS 26.1** | PhotoKit Background Resource Upload extension (`com.apple.photos.background-upload` + `BackgroundUploadURLBase`). System schedules uploads on network/power/activity. **Requires full `.readWrite` authorization.** No Simulator support |
| Put your editor **inside Apple Photos** | **Yes** | Photo Editing Extension: `PHContentEditingController` + `PHContentEditingInput`/`Output` + `PHAdjustmentData` (non-destructive, re-editable). iOS 8.0+ |
| Read the library with **no permission prompt** | **Yes** | `PHPickerViewController` / `PhotosPicker` — out-of-process; the user's selection *is* the grant |
| Generate a **spatial (2D→3D) photo** the way Apple does | **No** | Apple's ML pipeline is not exposed. Build your own monocular depth + novel-view synthesis |
| Ship a **CarPlay** photo experience | **No** | No photo app category; CarPlay entitlements cover audio, communication/messaging, driving task, EV charging, fueling, navigation, parking, quick food ordering |

### 11.y Where Apple is weak — our opening

- **No SharePlay in Photos on iPhone at all.** It is a Vision Pro-only feature. Group Activities (iOS 15+) is fully public, including `GroupSessionJournal` for media transfer, and Apple even ships a "collaborative photo gallery with SharePlay" sample. Shipping synchronised co-viewing on iPhone is **feature superiority, not parity**.
- **The photo library is invisible to the filesystem.** Apple states outright that "your photo library is stored in the Photos app," and the only bridges are `Save to Files`, import-from-Files, and external-USB import/export. A competitor that ships a **File Provider extension** is browsable in Files, drag-and-droppable into any app, and mountable in macOS Finder. Apple has chosen not to do this for a decade.
- **Background backup was Apple's structural moat and it is gone.** Users complained for ten years that third-party backup "stops when you close the app." Since **iOS 26.1** the system schedules third-party uploads based on network, power and device activity. Immich is already building on it. This is table stakes now — but almost nobody has shipped it.
- **The `.photos` App Intents domain is essentially unadopted, and it is shippable today.** 26 schemas — including `cleanupPhoto`, `updateRecognizedPerson`, `crop`, `setFilter`, `postToSharedAlbum` — have been available since **iOS 18**, not iOS 27. Apple Photos' own Siri support is weak. SiriKit is dead as of WWDC26. A competitor can be **more voice-controllable than Photos itself**, right now.
- **Spotlight photo results are shallow, and semantic indexing is open.** Apple documents Spotlight finding "images in your photo library" and text via Live Text — but natural-language photo queries mostly fail. `IndexedEntity` donation puts *your* photos into Spotlight's semantic index, and Apple's own sample says so explicitly.
- **Featured Photos surfaces content users actively don't want.** Apple's only remedies are blunt: `Never Feature This Person`, `Show Featured Content` off, `Show Holiday Events` off. There is no "only these 40 photos," and the widget cannot show Live Photos or video.
- **Subject lift is artificially limited to one subject.** Apple's own UI lifts one subject at a time; `VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest` returns `allInstances` — many. Batch lift, multi-subject cut-out, and organised sticker management are all trivially available and absent from Photos.
- **Visual Look Up has no path back into your own library.** You can identify a plant, but you cannot then search "all photos of monstera." Visual Intelligence has the same gap — and the **VisualIntelligence framework explicitly lets a third-party app return "photos in YOUR library that look like this"** as a search result. Apple has not done this for the user's own library.
- **StandBy's photo frame is uncurated.** It inherits Featured/Memories with no album picker of its own and no way to pin a single photo; Night Mode's red tint ruins photos. An in-app "frame mode" for a plugged-in phone is unblocked.
- **Shared Albums were lossy, Apple-only, and capped at 5,000 photos**, with "If Shared Albums aren't working" as a standing support article. ⚠️ But iOS 27 (fall 2026) fixes the two headline complaints — full-resolution sharing and Android/Windows participation (via iCloud.com, still requiring an Apple Account). **A "cross-platform full-res shared album" pitch has roughly one release cycle of life left.** Differentiate on permissions, ownership, export, and genuinely native non-Apple clients — and watch the reported (unconfirmed) change that full-res Shared Album content now counts against iCloud storage quota, which is a cost lever Apple is handing you.
- **The Photos navigation is a proven, contested axis.** Apple removed tabs in iOS 18, took a year of public backlash, and restored `Library` / `Collections` tabs in iOS 26 — with Federighi conceding on stage, "Many of you missed using tabs in the Photos app." Navigation is winnable.
- **The Journal entitlement is a bottleneck, not a wall — but plan for rejection.** `com.apple.developer.journal.allow` requires Apple's approval. Build the "we never get it" branch: your own on-device moment-suggestion engine over your own library, which needs no entitlement at all.
## 12. PhotoKit — The Third-Party Developer Surface

PhotoKit is the only sanctioned way a third-party iOS app touches the system photo library. It is the framework behind everything a non-Apple photo app can do: enumerate assets, fetch pixels, stream original file bytes, write back a narrow set of user-owned fields, observe changes, and (new in iOS 26.1) hand resources to the system for background upload to your own server. **The single most important thing to know: PhotoKit hands you raw pixels + structural/file metadata + write-back for user-owned fields, and gives you literally nothing from Apple's intelligence layer.** There is no `PHPerson`, no People/Pets album subtype, no Memories type, no face descriptor anywhere in Vision, and no scene/object/OCR/person key in the fetch predicate grammar. Apple DTS on the developer forums (thread 126711): *"No, there is not an API to access people data in PhotoKit as of now,"* with a follow-up noting Apple *"goes to specific lengths to prevent accessing face/person information using PhotoKit. Even using private APIs, access to that info is denied to third party apps."* That is still true on iOS 26.5.2 shipping and unchanged in the iOS 27 beta SDK.

Version baseline for everything below: **iOS 26 is the shipping floor** (26.5.2 current; 26.6 in developer beta). **iOS 27 was announced at WWDC 2026 and ships ~September 2026** — every symbol marked `iOS 27 BETA` in this section carries Apple's own beta flag in its DocC metadata and can change or be withdrawn. Nothing marked BETA may be a launch dependency.

⚠️ **Trap (framework namespace):** Apple's canonical doc namespace is `/documentation/photos/`; the older `/photokit/` paths 301-redirect to it. PhotosUI symbols (`PHPickerViewController`, `PHLivePhotoView`, `PHContentEditingController`) live under `/documentation/photosui/`. Two frameworks, one mental model.

---

### 12.1 Authorization — `PHAuthorizationStatus`, `PHAccessLevel`, and the Info.plist keys

Five statuses, two access levels. Both are stable, both are iOS 14-era or older.

| Symbol | Cases / values | Available since |
|---|---|---|
| `PHAuthorizationStatus` | `.notDetermined`, `.restricted`, `.denied`, `.authorized`, `.limited` | iOS 8.0 (`.limited` added iOS 14.0) |
| `PHAccessLevel` | `.addOnly`, `.readWrite` | iOS 14.0 |
| `PHPhotoLibrary.authorizationStatus(for:)` | takes a `PHAccessLevel` | iOS 14.0 |
| `PHPhotoLibrary.requestAuthorization(for:handler:)` | takes a `PHAccessLevel` | iOS 14.0 |
| `PHPhotoLibrary.authorizationStatus()` | no argument | iOS 8.0, **DEPRECATED iOS 14.0** |
| `PHPhotoLibrary.requestAuthorization(_:)` | no argument | iOS 8.0, **DEPRECATED iOS 14.0** |

⚠️ **Trap (the single most common PhotoKit bug in the wild):** the deprecated no-argument variants are **not limited-library-aware**. Apple's docs: *"The [`authorizationStatus()`] and [`requestAuthorization(_:)`] methods aren't compatible with the limited library and return [`.authorized`] when the user authorizes your app for limited access only."* An app using them believes it has the whole library, fetches, gets a near-empty result, and blames the user. **Always use the `(for:)` variants. Treat `.limited` as a first-class app state, not an error.**

The permission prompt fires automatically and asynchronously on the first PhotoKit call that needs it. Apple advises *against* making PhotoKit calls at app launch, so the prompt lands on a deliberate user action rather than in the middle of onboarding.

**Info.plist keys (crash-on-missing):**

| Key | Required when | Since |
|---|---|---|
| `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription` | any read or read/write access | iOS 6.0 |
| `NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription` | app only adds to the library (`.addOnly`) | iOS 11.0 |
| `PHPhotoLibraryPreventAutomaticLimitedAccessAlert` (Boolean `YES`) | suppressing the limited-library nag (see 12.2) | iOS 14.0 |

Apple: *"Attempting to access the Photos library without a valid usage description causes your app to crash."* Purpose strings are surfaced verbatim in the system alert and are localizable via `InfoPlist.strings`. App Review guideline **5.1.1** rejections for vague purpose strings are extremely common; Apple actively pushes apps toward `PHPickerViewController` and scrutinizes full-library requests. A photo browsing/management/backup app qualifies, but the purpose string should name the on-device, no-upload nature of processing to preempt reviewer friction.

---

### 12.2 The Limited Photo Library (`.limited`) — the landmine under every album-based app

Since iOS 14 the permission sheet offers a subset option alongside full access and denial. Apple's own documentation calls the option `Select Photos…`; note that Apple's article text dates from iOS 14 and the modern iOS 26 sheet wording differs somewhat (e.g. `Limit Access…` / `Allow Full Access`) — treat `Select Photos` as the *documented* label, not necessarily today's on-screen string.

Under `.limited`, the system maintains a per-app allowlist of `PHAsset` `localIdentifier`s and transparently filters every fetch to that set. Most APIs behave identically. **Two documented exceptions matter enormously:**

1. *"The system automatically adds assets that your app creates with a `PHAssetCreationRequest` to the user's limited library selection."*
2. **"You can't create or fetch user albums."** Apple continues: *"If your app requires this functionality, you'll need to update its behavior and user interface appropriately when your app's authorization status is `.limited`."*

⚠️ **Trap:** an Albums tab built on `PHAssetCollection` fetches renders **blank** under `.limited` — it does not error, it just returns nothing. Apple warns bluntly: *"The limited Photos library affects all apps that use PhotoKit in iOS 14, including those already published to the App Store."* The Albums surface must either hide itself or show an explicit upgrade-access affordance when `status == .limited`.

**Managing the selection.** `PHPhotoLibrary.shared().presentLimitedLibraryPicker(from:)` (iOS 14.0+) and `presentLimitedLibraryPicker(from:completionHandler:)` (iOS 15.0+, hands back an array of **newly** selected local identifiers). By default *"the system automatically prompts the user to update their limited-library selection once per app life cycle. This automatic presentation isn't the preferred user experience for most apps. Instead, apps need to suppress the automatic prompt and present it programmatically."* Suppress with `PHPhotoLibraryPreventAutomaticLimitedAccessAlert = YES`, then present it yourself from an explicit affordance (e.g. a `Manage Selected Photos…` row in Settings plus an inline banner).

⚠️ **Trap:** Apple states of the completion-handler variant: *"This method only works when the user enables limited-library mode."* Calling it under `.authorized` does not vend identifiers. It is not a general "user changed selection" signal — selection changes also arrive through the normal `PHPhotoLibraryChangeObserver`, which is the correct listener.

---

### 12.3 `PHPickerViewController` — zero-permission picking, and why it cannot be your architecture

The out-of-process picker (iOS 14.0+, SwiftUI equivalent `PhotosPicker`) that replaced `UIImagePickerController`. Apple: *"Because the system manages its life cycle in a separate process, it's private by default. The user doesn't need to explicitly authorize your app to select photos."* It supports search, multi-select, and zoom natively.

`PHPickerConfiguration` knobs: `filter` (`PHPickerFilter`), `selectionLimit`, `selection` (`.default` / `.ordered` / `.continuous` / `.continuousAndOrdered`), `preferredAssetRepresentationMode`, `preselectedAssetIdentifiers`, `mode` (`.default` grid / `.compact` linear, iOS 17.0+), `disabledCapabilities` (iOS 17.0+), `edgesWithoutContentMargins`. Controller methods: `updatePicker(using:)`, `deselectAssets(withIdentifiers:)`, `moveAsset(withIdentifier:afterAssetWithIdentifier:)`, `scrollToInitialPosition()`, `zoomIn()`, `zoomOut()`. Results arrive as `PHPickerResult { assetIdentifier: String?, itemProvider: NSItemProvider }`.

`PHPickerCapabilities` (iOS 17.0+) — exactly five cases, all real: `.collectionNavigation`, `.selectionActions`, `.search`, `.stagingArea`, `.sensitivityAnalysisIntervention`. That last one makes the **system picker itself blur nudity** — free import-flow safety with **no entitlement at all**.

⚠️ **Trap (nil assetIdentifier):** `PHPickerResult.assetIdentifier` is **always `nil`** unless you construct the configuration as `PHPickerConfiguration(photoLibrary: PHPhotoLibrary.shared())` — and *that* variant does require library authorization, defeating the zero-permission property.

⚠️ **Trap (picker ≠ library access):** picking through `PHPicker` does **not** extend the limited-library selection. A picked asset is still not fetchable as a `PHAsset` afterwards. You get files via `NSItemProvider`, not a live library: no change observation, no favorites, no albums, no incremental sync. The picker is correct for "import a few photos" and architecturally useless for a library-manager or backup product.

**iOS 27 BETA additions to `PHPickerConfiguration`** (iOS/iPadOS/Mac Catalyst/macOS/visionOS 27.0; no tvOS):

| Property | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `searchText` | `PHPickerSearchText?` (default `nil`) | Pre-populates the picker's search field |
| `metadataOptions` | `PHPickerMetadataOptions` (default `[]`) | OptionSet; exactly two members: `.removeLocation`, `.removeCaptions` |

⚠️ **Trap (will not compile):** `searchText` is **not** a `String`. It is `PHPickerSearchText?`, an Optional wrapper struct constructed via `init(_:)`. You must write `config.searchText = PHPickerSearchText("beach")`. Assigning a bare `String` fails to compile.

`searchText` is strategically the closest thing to third-party access to Apple's semantic index that has ever existed: you seed the system picker's own search — backed by Apple's private semantic/scene index — with a query on the user's behalf, with **zero permission**, and the user confirms the selection. It is still a picker: user-confirmed, foreground, never a silent background search. Worth a spike as a "search Apple's brain" fallback. Both properties are BETA and cannot ship before ~Sept 2026.

---

### 12.4 The data model and the hard ceiling on what you can query

**`PHAsset` — the exhaustive exposed surface.** `mediaType` (`PHAssetMediaType`), `mediaSubtypes` (`PHAssetMediaSubtype`), `contentType` (`UTType`), `creationDate`, `modificationDate`, `addedDate`, `duration`, `pixelWidth`, `pixelHeight`, `location` (`CLLocation` — coordinate, altitude, speed, course, timestamp), `sourceType` (`PHAssetSourceType`: `.typeUserLibrary` / `.typeCloudShared` / `.typeiTunesSynced`), `isFavorite`, `isHidden`, `hasAdjustments`, `adjustmentFormatIdentifier`, `adjustmentTimestamp`, `adjustmentsState` (iOS 18.0+), `burstIdentifier`, `burstSelectionTypes`, `representsBurst`, `playbackStyle`, `playbackVariation`, `localIdentifier` (from `PHObject`), plus deprecated `isSyncFailureHidden`. iOS 27 BETA adds **readable** `rating` (`PHAsset.Rating`) and `originalResourceChoice`.

Fetch class methods: `fetchAssets(in:options:)`, `fetchAssets(with:options:)`, `fetchAssets(withLocalIdentifiers:options:)`, `fetchAssets(with:mediaType:options:)`, `fetchAssets(withBurstIdentifier:options:)`, `fetchKeyAssets(in:options:)`. Editing preflight: `canPerform(_ editOperation: PHAssetEditOperation)`, `requestContentEditingInput(with:completionHandler:)`.

`PHAssetMediaSubtype` cases: `photoPanorama`, `photoHDR`, `photoScreenshot`, `photoLive`, `photoDepthEffect`, `photoAnimation`, `videoStreamed`, `videoHighFrameRate`, `videoTimelapse`, `videoCinematic`, `videoScreenRecording`, `spatialMedia` (iOS 18.0+).

⚠️ **Trap (`addedDate` is brand new):** `PHAsset.addedDate` — *"date this asset was added to the photo library from the device used to add it"* — is **iOS 26.0+ / iPadOS 26.0 / macOS 26.0 / tvOS 26.0 / visionOS 26.0**, NOT a long-standing iOS 8-era property. Any deployment target below iOS 26 must `#available`-guard it or it will not build. If your minimum target is below iOS 26, the "when did this enter the library" axis simply does not exist and must be reconstructed another way (e.g. EXIF corroboration).

**What is conspicuously ABSENT from `PHAsset`:** no camera make/model, no ISO/aperture/focal length, **no EXIF at all**, no scene labels, no persons, no `isSyncedToCloud` flag. EXIF requires loading the actual resource bytes (12.6). Whether an asset's data is cloud-only is discoverable only at request time via the result-handler info dict key `PHImageResultIsInCloudKey` — there is no cheap precomputed "is local" flag. (Partial escape hatch shipped in iOS 26.1: download-only upload jobs — see 12.10.)

**`PHFetchOptions`.** Properties: `predicate` (`NSPredicate`), `sortDescriptors`, `fetchLimit`, `includeHiddenAssets`, `includeAllBurstAssets`, `includeAssetSourceTypes` (`PHAssetSourceType` OptionSet), `wantsIncrementalChangeDetails`, plus `prefetchAssetExtendedMetadata` (iOS 27 BETA).

Apple: *"Photos supports only a restricted set of keys for the `predicate` and `sortDescriptors` properties."* The **complete** supported key list for `PHAsset` — this is the definitive ceiling, byte-for-byte from Apple's own table:

`SELF`, `localIdentifier`, `creationDate`, `modificationDate`, `mediaType`, `mediaSubtypes`, `duration`, `pixelWidth`, `pixelHeight`, `isFavorite`, `isHidden`, `burstIdentifier`

Twelve structural keys. **No scene, object, text, face, person, keyword, or caption key exists.** Unsupported keypaths raise at *fetch time*, not compile time.

⚠️ **Trap:** teams routinely predicate on unsupported keys and ship a runtime crash. And because in-memory filtering of a full-library fetch is the only way to do anything clever, **incremental indexing with persistent change tokens (12.9) is non-negotiable** — a 100k-photo library cannot be re-enumerated on every launch.

**`PHAssetCollection` / `PHCollectionList`.** `PHAssetCollectionType` is exactly `.album`, `.smartAlbum`, `.moment` (**deprecated** — the old date/location grouping is gone; you must do your own event clustering). Properties: `assetCollectionType`, `assetCollectionSubtype`, `estimatedAssetCount`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `approximateLocation`, `localizedLocationNames`, `localizedTitle`. Fetches: `fetchAssetCollections(with:subtype:options:)`, `fetchAssetCollections(withLocalIdentifiers:options:)`, `fetchAssetCollectionsContaining(_:with:options:)`, `transientAssetCollection(...)`.

**Verified `PHAssetCollectionSubtype` cases** (a widely-circulated list of these is wrong; the following names are the ones that exist in public API):

| User albums | Smart albums |
|---|---|
| `albumRegular` | `smartAlbumGeneric`, `smartAlbumPanoramas`, `smartAlbumVideos`, `smartAlbumFavorites` |
| `albumSyncedEvent` | `smartAlbumTimelapses`, `smartAlbumAllHidden`, `smartAlbumRecentlyAdded`, `smartAlbumBursts` |
| `albumSyncedFaces` *(legacy iTunes-synced — NOT the People album)* | `smartAlbumSlomoVideos`, `smartAlbumUserLibrary`, `smartAlbumSelfPortraits`, `smartAlbumScreenshots` |
| `albumSyncedAlbum` | `smartAlbumDepthEffect`, `smartAlbumLivePhotos`, `smartAlbumAnimated`, `smartAlbumLongExposures` |
| `albumImported` | `smartAlbumRAW`, `smartAlbumCinematic`, `smartAlbumSpatial` (iOS 18.0+) |
| `albumMyPhotoStream` | `smartAlbumUnableToUpload`, `smartAlbumScreenRecordings` |
| `albumCloudShared` | wildcard: `.any` (how you actually fetch across all subtypes) |

⚠️ **Trap (names that do not compile):** `albumCloudSharedPhoto` and `smartAlbumSlowmo` are **wrong** — the real cases are `albumCloudShared` and `smartAlbumSlomoVideos`. And `smartAlbumUnfiltered`, `smartAlbumVisibleHidden`, `smartAlbumRecentlyDeleted`, `smartAlbumCloudSharedAlbum` are **not public PhotoKit API at all** (they 404 on developer.apple.com and are absent from the enum's case list) — they exist only as undocumented raw values. Do not reference them expecting them to build against the public SDK.

⚠️ **Trap (the defining absence):** there is **no `.smartAlbumPeople`**, no `.smartAlbumPets`, and no memory type or subtype anywhere in the enum. Apple's People & Pets album and Memories are simply not in the API. Confirmed on iOS 26 shipping and in the iOS 27 beta. No `PHPerson` type exists; no `PHMemory` type exists.

`smartAlbumUserLibrary` (Recents / all photos) is the workhorse and the one most apps get wrong.

**Hidden and Recently Deleted are permanent blind spots.** An Apple engineer on the developer forums (thread 719540): *"Beginning with iOS 16, users can require authentication to view the hidden album, and the user setting is YES by default. When YES, the system doesn't return hidden assets even if the `includeHiddenAssets` fetch option is YES."* There is **no API whatsoever** to fetch Recently Deleted. `isHidden` on `PHAsset` still exists and `PHAssetChangeRequest.isHidden` is still writable — you can hide an asset, you just cannot enumerate hidden content. The engineer's recommended workaround is `PhotosPicker`: the user can hand over a hidden asset explicitly through the out-of-process picker.

⚠️ **Trap (marketing/legal):** any "we back up / index your **entire** library" claim is **false on iOS** and must not be made. Expect support tickets asking why your photo count differs from Apple's.

**`PHAssetExtendedMetadata` (iOS 27 BETA — iOS/iPadOS/Catalyst/macOS/tvOS/visionOS 27.0).** *"Represents other asset attributes that are not included when fetching [PHAsset] directly."* Exactly three properties: `caption: String?`, `keywords: [String]`, `originalFileName: String?`. Reached via `PHAsset.extendedMetadata`, or bulk-prefetched with `PHFetchOptions.prefetchAssetExtendedMetadata` — Apple: *"By default these properties are fetched on demand. They can be prefetched by toggling `PHFetchOptions.prefetchAssetExtendedMetadata`."* This is the **first-ever read access to the user's Photos captions and keywords**. It is BETA; it cannot be a launch dependency on iOS 26.

⚠️ **Trap:** even in iOS 27, **keywords and captions are not predicate keys**. You can read them and write them (12.7), but you **cannot search on them via `PHFetchOptions`**. Any tag you write into Apple Photos is for the user's benefit inside Apple's app — it does not become queryable through PhotoKit. That materially limits the "write our AI tags back and then search them" idea. (*Unverified:* whether keywords/captions written via PhotoKit sync through iCloud Photos to macOS Photos keywords and other devices. Highly likely; untested. Do not promise cross-device tagging without testing.)

---

### 12.5 Getting pixels — `PHImageManager`, `PHCachingImageManager`, `PHImageRequestOptions`

`PHImageManager.default()`: `requestImage(for:targetSize:contentMode:options:resultHandler:)`, `requestImageDataAndOrientation(for:options:resultHandler:)` (*"the largest represented image as data bytes and EXIF orientation"*), `requestLivePhoto(...)`, `requestAVAsset(forVideo:...)`, `requestPlayerItem(forVideo:...)`, `requestExportSession(forVideo:...)`, `cancelImageRequest(_:)`. Constant: `PHImageManagerMaximumSize`. `PHCachingImageManager` adds `startCachingImages(for:targetSize:contentMode:options:)`, `stopCachingImages(...)`, `stopCachingImagesForAllAssets()`.

`PHImageRequestOptions`: `isSynchronous`, `version` (`.current` = all edits applied / `.unadjusted` = no adjustments / `.original` = highest-fidelity original), `deliveryMode` (`.opportunistic` / `.highQualityFormat` / `.fastFormat`), `resizeMode` (`.none` / `.fast` / `.exact`), `normalizedCropRect`, `isNetworkAccessAllowed`, `progressHandler`, `allowSecondaryDegradedImage`, `preferHDR` (iOS 17.0+ — *"Request HDR image data if available (such as PQ/HLG formats)"*), `targetHDRHeadroom` (iOS 17.0+).

⚠️ **Trap (multi-callback):** `.opportunistic` delivery fires the result handler **multiple times** — a degraded thumbnail first, then the real image. Check `PHImageResultIsDegradedKey` or you get flicker and duplicated downstream work.

⚠️ **Trap (the silent-skip catastrophe):** `isNetworkAccessAllowed = false` yields **nothing** for cloud-only assets, with `PHImageResultIsInCloudKey = true` in the info dict and no error. A naive indexer will silently skip the entire library of any user on Optimize iPhone Storage — an invisible, catastrophic bug class. Guard against it explicitly.

`PHCachingImageManager` is **required** for a smooth grid at library scale — batch-prefetch around the visible window. For ML indexing, request a fixed small `targetSize` with `.highQualityFormat` + `.exact` resize to get deterministic model input.

---

### 12.6 Original bytes and EXIF — `PHAssetResource` / `PHAssetResourceManager`

`PHAssetResource.assetResources(for: PHAsset) -> [PHAssetResource]` (also an overload for `PHLivePhoto`).
