Each resource: `type` (`PHAssetResourceType`: `.photo`, `.video`, `.audio`, `.alternatePhoto`, `.fullSizePhoto`, `.fullSizeVideo`, `.adjustmentBasePhoto`, `.adjustmentData`, `.pairedVideo`, `.fullSizePairedVideo`, `.adjustmentBasePairedVideo`, `.adjustmentBaseVideo`), `contentType` (`UTType`), `originalFilename`, `assetLocalIdentifier`, `pixelWidth`, `pixelHeight`, `dataSize`. `PHAssetResourceManager.default()`: `requestData(for:options:dataReceivedHandler:completionHandler:)` (streams chunks), `writeData(for:toFile:options:completionHandler:)`, `cancelDataRequest(_:)`, `exportedAssetID(for:)`. `PHAssetResourceRequestOptions` has `isNetworkAccessAllowed` + `progressHandler`. Available iOS 9.0+. iOS 27 BETA adds the type method `PHAssetResource.assetResource(forUploadJob:)`.

This is **the only path** to: (a) true original unmodified bytes, (b) full EXIF/camera metadata (parse with `CGImageSourceCopyPropertiesAtIndex`), (c) the RAW component of a RAW+JPEG pair, (d) the paired video of a Live Photo. **Any backup/upload path must be resource-based, not `requestImage`-based.**

⚠️ **Trap (deprecated property):** `PHAssetResource.uniformTypeIdentifier` is **DEPRECATED** — use `contentType` (`UTType`). Apple additionally notes in the background-upload guide that `resource` *"is deprecated in iOS 27 and unavailable in macOS and Mac Catalyst. Use `assetResource(forUploadJob:)` to fetch the associated asset resource."*

⚠️ **Trap (accounting):** one "photo" can be **4+ resources** (RAW+JPEG, Live Photo pairs, edited + adjustment-base). A dedupe/backup ledger that models 1 asset = 1 file will double-count and blow up users' storage quotas. Also, `dataSize` may be nil until download completes, so total-bytes progress UI is unreliable for cloud-only libraries.

---

### 12.7 Writing back — `PHAssetChangeRequest` and `PHAssetCreationRequest`

All mutations happen inside `PHPhotoLibrary.shared().performChanges { }` (or `performChangesAndWait`), applied atomically, with observers notified. Writes require `.readWrite`, never `.addOnly`.

**Shipping today (iOS 8.0+ core):**

| Operation | API |
|---|---|
| Create from image/video | `creationRequestForAsset(from: UIImage)`, `creationRequestForAssetFromImage(atFileURL:)`, `creationRequestForAssetFromVideo(atFileURL:)`, `placeholderForCreatedAsset` |
| Delete | `PHAssetChangeRequest.deleteAssets(_:)` — **always shows a system confirmation prompt** |
| Mutate | `PHAssetChangeRequest(for: asset)` → `creationDate`, `location`, `isFavorite`, `isHidden`, `contentEditingOutput`, `revertAssetContentToOriginal()` |

⚠️ **Trap (deletion always prompts):** there is **no silent delete, ever**. This is by design. But it means "clean up 3,000 duplicates" must be **one** `deleteAssets(_:)` call with the full array to produce **one** prompt — not 3,000 calls.

**iOS 27 BETA additions to `PHAssetChangeRequest`** — every one of these is real and correctly beta-flagged on Apple's page:

| Symbol | Notes |
|---|---|
| `caption` | `String?`; *"Set to nil or an empty string to clear"* |
| `rating` | `PHAsset.Rating`. ⚠️ **Unverified:** the enum's cases could not be retrieved (Apple doc path 404s). Whether it is 0–5 stars or a favorite/reject tri-state is **unknown** — verify in Xcode 27 headers before designing any UI around it. |
| `addKeyword(_:)` / `removeKeyword(_:)` | write keywords into the system library |
| `setLivePhotoVideoPlaybackEnabled(_:)` | *"Disable or enable the video part of a Live Photo so it just appears as a still image"* |
| `revertAssetContent(to: PHAsset.OriginalResourceChoice)` | |

This is the largest write-side expansion in a decade: AI-generated captions and tags can live inside the user's real Apple Photos library. Design your schema for it now, behind `#available` checks — but see the 12.4 trap: what you write is **not** queryable via `PHFetchOptions`.

**`PHAssetCreationRequest` (iOS 9.0+)** — `forAsset()`, `addResource(with type: PHAssetResourceType, data: Data, options:)`, `addResource(with:fileURL:options:)`, `supportsAssetResourceTypes(_:)` (preflight a resource-type combination). `PHAssetResourceCreationOptions` carries `originalFilename`, `contentType` (`UTType`), `shouldMoveFile`, and the **deprecated** `uniformTypeIdentifier`. iOS 27 BETA adds `originalResourceChoice` — **on `PHAssetCreationRequest` itself**, not on `PHAssetResourceCreationOptions`.

This is the correct API for **restoring a backup**: it constructs a multi-resource asset (a real Live Photo = `.photo` + `.pairedVideo`; a real RAW+JPEG pair), preserving originals, pairing, and filename — unlike `creationRequestForAsset(from: UIImage)`, which flattens everything to a single still. Works under `.addOnly`. Under `.limited`, created assets are auto-added to the user's selection.

⚠️ **Trap:** `shouldMoveFile = true` **moves** your temp file rather than copying it. Getting the exact resource-type combination right for Live Photos / RAW is fiddly — call `supportsAssetResourceTypes(_:)` first.

---

### 12.8 Non-destructive editing and living inside Apple Photos

**In-library editing (iOS 8.0+, fully available, and badly underused).** `asset.requestContentEditingInput(with:completionHandler:)` → `PHContentEditingInput` (`displaySizeImage`, `fullSizeImageURL`, `fullSizeImageOrientation`, `audiovisualAsset`, `livePhoto`, `adjustmentData`, media type/subtypes, `creationDate`, `location`, `contentType`). Build a `PHContentEditingOutput(contentEditingInput:)`, write rendered bytes to `renderedContentURL`, attach a `PHAdjustmentData(formatIdentifier:formatVersion:data:)`, assign to `PHAssetChangeRequest.contentEditingOutput` inside `performChanges`. `PHContentEditingInputRequestOptions.canHandleAdjustmentData` is a closure where you inspect existing adjustment data and declare whether you can reopen it. `revertAssetContentToOriginal()` undoes everything. Live Photo editing via `PHLivePhotoEditingContext` (iOS 10.0+): `frameProcessor` block, `audioVolume`, `saveLivePhoto(to:options:)`, `prepareLivePhotoForPlayback(...)`.

Photos stores the **original** + your adjustment blob + the rendered result. Because `formatIdentifier`/`formatVersion` round-trip, **your app (and only your app) can reopen and re-edit its own adjustments**; other apps see a baked render they can revert but not re-edit. `PHAdjustmentData.data` is an **opaque blob you define** — serialize your entire edit graph into it. If the user subsequently edits in Apple Photos, your adjustment data is superseded and `canHandleAdjustmentData` returns false.

**Photo Editing Extensions (`PHContentEditingController`, PhotosUI, iOS 8.0+ / Catalyst 14.0+ / macOS 10.11+ / visionOS 1.0+).** Apple: *"You can incorporate your app's features directly into the Photos app… A photo-editing app extension can enable people to edit media, apply your app's filter effects, build slideshows, books, or custom content, such as a collage, right in Photos app using code that you supply."* Protocol members: `canHandle(_ adjustmentData:)`, `startContentEditing(with:placeholderImage:)`, `finishContentEditing(completionHandler:)`, `cancelContentEditing()`, `shouldShowCancelConfirmation`. Installed automatically with the host app; Photos hosts your view controller inside its own editing UI and you return a `PHContentEditingOutput`.

This is a **legitimate, Apple-sanctioned beachhead inside the Photos app** — a free discovery channel most competitors ignore. Costs: extensions are memory-constrained separate processes, so sharing ML models and your index requires an **App Group**; and users discover it only via Edit → (…) in Photos, which is not prominent.

---

### 12.9 Change tracking — live observers and persistent change history

**Live (foreground) — `PHPhotoLibraryChangeObserver`, iOS 8.0+.** Register via `PHPhotoLibrary.shared().register(observer:)`; receive `photoLibraryDidChange(_ changeInstance: PHChange)`. From `PHChange`: `changeDetails(for: PHObject)` → `PHObjectChangeDetails` (`objectWasDeleted`, `objectBeforeChanges`/`objectAfterChanges`, `assetContentChanged`); `changeDetails(for: PHFetchResult)` → `PHFetchResultChangeDetails` (`fetchResultBeforeChanges`/`AfterChanges`, `hasIncrementalChanges`, `removedIndexes`, `insertedIndexes`, `changedIndexes`, `enumerateMoves(_:)`, `hasMoves`). Index-level deltas require `PHFetchOptions.wantsIncrementalChangeDetails`. Deltas map 1:1 onto `UICollectionView` batch updates. Also `PHPhotoLibraryAvailabilityObserver` + `unavailabilityReason` (iOS 13.0+) for library-unavailable states. This observer **also fires when the user changes their limited-library selection** — it is the correct listener for that.

⚠️ **Trap:** callbacks arrive on an **arbitrary background queue** — hop to main before touching UI. And `hasIncrementalChanges` can be `false`, meaning full reload required; forgetting to handle that produces index-mismatch crashes.

**Across launches — persistent change history, iOS 16.0+ (SHIPPING).** `PHPhotoLibrary.currentChangeToken` (`PHPersistentChangeToken`, serializable) and `func fetchPersistentChanges(since token: PHPersistentChangeToken) throws -> PHPersistentChangeFetchResult`, enumerable over a very large set of change records, each yielding inserted/updated/deleted `localIdentifier`s. Persist the token; on next launch (or in a background task/extension) ask "what changed since?" instead of re-enumerating 100k assets. iOS 27 BETA adds a **push-based** counterpart: `PHPhotoLibraryPersistentChangesObserver` (`photoLibraryPersistentChangesDidUpdate(_:)`, with `register(_:)` / `unregisterPersistentChangesObserver(_:)`).

⚠️ **Trap (token expiry):** `fetchPersistentChanges(since:)` throws **`PHPhotosError.persistentChangeTokenExpired`** when the system has pruned history past your saved token. You must discard the token and do a full resync — so a resilient, resumable full-scan path is mandatory anyway. Pre-iOS-27 there is **no push notification** for persistent changes; you poll on launch or background wake.

This is the single most important API for a large-library product's performance story. Persist the token in an **App Group** so the background upload extension and the app share sync state — Apple's own background-upload article recommends exactly this.

---

### 12.10 ★ Background Resource Upload Extension — first-class background photo backup (SHIPPING, iOS 26.1)

The headline capability, and it is available on shipping iOS **today**. Apple: *"PhotoKit's Background Resource Upload extension enables apps to deliver seamless cloud backup experiences. The system manages uploads on your app's behalf, processing them in the background even when people switch to other apps or lock their devices. The system calls your extension to process uploads when conditions allow, scheduling work based on factors such as network availability, power state, and device activity."*

This is the first time Apple has given third parties a first-class background photo-backup pipeline — no silent pushes, no background-fetch abuse, no location-tracking hacks. It is barely adopted.

| Symbol | Availability |
|---|---|
| `PHBackgroundResourceUploadExtension` | **iOS 26.1 / iPadOS 26.1 — SHIPPING**; DEPRECATED as of 27.0 |
| `PHBackgroundResourceUploadJobExtension` (async successor) | iOS / iPadOS / Mac Catalyst / macOS 27.0 — **BETA** |
| `PHAssetResourceUploadJob` | iOS 26.1 shipping; Catalyst/macOS 27.0 beta |
| `PHAssetResourceUploadJobChangeRequest` | iOS 26.1 shipping; Catalyst/macOS 27.0 beta |
| `PHAssetResource.assetResource(forUploadJob:)` | iOS 27.0 BETA |

⚠️ **Trap (protocol method names differ by OS):** the **shipping iOS 26.1** `PHBackgroundResourceUploadExtension` uses **`process()`** and **`notifyTermination()`**. The iOS 27 beta `PHBackgroundResourceUploadJobExtension` uses **`processJobs() async -> PHBackgroundResourceUploadProcessingResult`** (`.completed` / `.processing` / `.failure`) and **`willTerminate()`**. If you ship on 26.1 today you implement the former. Plan to dual-path.

**Enabling it:** `PHPhotoLibrary.setUploadJobExtensionEnabled(true)` / `uploadJobExtensionEnabled`. Apple: *"Your app must have full library access before enabling the extension… verify the status is `.authorized`."* ⚠️ **Trap:** this is **dead under `.limited`**. (The docs do not explicitly state limited-mode behavior for the extension itself; full access for the host app is explicitly required.)

**Target configuration — load-bearing and easy to miss.** Use Xcode's **Generic Extension** template. In the extension's Info.plist: `EXAppExtensionAttributes` → `EXExtensionPointIdentifier` = **`com.apple.photos.background-upload`**. Plus a **top-level String key `BackgroundUploadURLBase`** (e.g. `https://api.example.com`). Apple: *"The system requires this key for network access validation."* ⚠️ **Trap: without these, your extension is simply never called** — no error, no callback.

**Server-side contract — a hard backend blocker, not an app detail.** The system implements the draft **IETF Resumable Uploads for HTTP** protocol. Your server **must**:
1. Answer an `OPTIONS` preflight with `200 OK` plus an **`Upload-Limit`** header (or `501 Not Implemented` if resumption is unsupported), **and**
2. Emit a **`104 (Upload Resumption Supported)`** informational response with a **`Location`** header during the request-body upload.

Apple: *"Your API must include both the OPTIONS preflight check and the 104 informational response."* The 104 informational response is described as *"the authoritative signal that the server supports resumable uploads."* If your backend team does not implement both, the feature does not work.

**Job lifecycle.** `PHAssetResourceUploadJobChangeRequest`: `creationRequestForJob(destination:resource:)`, `creationRequestForDownloadJob(resource:)`, `acknowledge()`, `retry(destination:)`, `cancel()`, `placeholderForCreatedAssetResourceUploadJob`. `PHAssetResourceUploadJob` exposes `type`, `destination`, `state`, `error`, `responseHeaderFields`, `jobLimit`, and `fetchJobs(action:options:)` with actions `.retry` / `.acknowledge` / `.process` / `.cancel`. `PHAssetResourceUploadJob.State`: `.registered`, `.pending`, `.succeeded`, `.failed`, `.cancelled` — **cancellation is only legal in `.registered` or `.pending`**.

⚠️ **Trap (inflight cap):** `jobLimit` caps inflight jobs; exceeding it makes `performChanges` throw **`limitExceeded`**. You must call `acknowledge()` on completed jobs to free capacity. Return `.processing` to pause. *Unverified:* Apple does not document the actual numeric cap — measure it on-device.

**Download-only jobs.** `creationRequestForDownloadJob(resource:)` with `PHAssetResourceUploadJob.Type.downloadOnly` is a system-scheduled job that **forces an iCloud-only resource local in the background**. This is a materially better answer to "which of my user's photos are actually on this device?" than per-request `PHImageResultIsInCloudKey`, and it enables local-access-first workflows. ⚠️ **Trap:** the system may purge downloaded resources under disk pressure — consume them promptly.

**Other constraints:** the system may terminate the extension at any time (handle termination, design for interruption at any point). **Not available in Simulator** — Apple: *"In iOS, this feature isn't available in Simulator; test on a physical device."* The extension needs an App Group + a persisted `PHPersistentChangeToken` to know what is new.

---

### 12.11 Background compute — `BGContinuedProcessingTask` and friends

There is **no general "scan the photo library in the background" entitlement**. Three options:

| Task type | Since | Character |
|---|---|---|
| `BGAppRefreshTask` | iOS 13.0 | Short, opportunistic |
| `BGProcessingTask` | iOS 13.0 | Minutes-long, system-scheduled, typically charging + idle; good for overnight ML indexing; scheduling is entirely at the system's discretion and notoriously unreliable for time-sensitive work |
| **`BGContinuedProcessingTask`** | **iOS 26.0 / iPadOS 26.0 — SHIPPING** | *"A task that starts in the foreground and can continue running in the background as needed."* |

`BGContinuedProcessingTask` is the right primitive for full-library ML indexing. It **must be triggered by an explicit user action**. Apple: *"The system displays the progress of this task in a Live Activity and a person can cancel it through the interface if they wish"* and *"Your implementation needs to report progress using the `ProgressReporting` protocol… The system prioritizes the termination of tasks that reflect minimal or no progress, when resources become constrained."* The class also exposes `title`, `subtitle`, and `updateTitle(_:subtitle:)` to drive the Live Activity — use them. Register with `BGTaskScheduler.shared.register(forTaskWithIdentifier:)` + `.submit(request)`; continued tasks need a unique per-job identifier prefixed with the bundle ID. Submission strategy: `.queue` (default) or `.fail`.

**GPU / Core ML in the background** requires the **Background GPU Access** capability — entitlement `com.apple.developer.background-tasks.continued-processing.gpu`. (*This exact entitlement string is high-confidence but was not re-verified against Apple's page in the source pass — confirm before filing.*) With it, heavy Core Image / Vision / Accelerate / Core ML work continues in the background.

**Recommended architecture:** user taps `Index my library` → `BGContinuedProcessingTask` with background GPU → your Core ML face/SigLIP embedders run on the ANE/GPU with a system Live Activity showing honest, monotonic progress, surviving the user leaving the app. This is dramatically better UX than every "keep the app open while we scan" competitor, and almost nobody has shipped it.

⚠️ **Trap:** if the user swipes the app away in the app switcher, the task is **cancelled with no notification**. And progress must be honest and monotonic, or the system deprioritizes you and the user cancels.

---

### 12.12 The adjacent frameworks — Vision, Core ML, SensitiveContentAnalysis, Visual Intelligence

**Vision — face detection with zero identity.** Modern Swift API (iOS 18.0+): `DetectFaceRectanglesRequest`, `DetectFaceLandmarksRequest`, `DetectFaceCaptureQualityRequest` → `FaceObservation`, exposing `boundingBox` (`NormalizedRect`), `roll`, `pitch`, `yaw`, `captureQuality` (`FaceObservation.CaptureQuality`), and `landmarks` (`FaceObservation.Landmarks2D`: `faceContour`, `leftEye`, `rightEye`, `leftPupil`, `rightPupil`, `leftEyebrow`, `rightEyebrow`, `nose`, `noseCrest`, `medianLine`, `innerLips`, `outerLips`, `allPoints`). `FaceObservation` availability: iOS 18.0 / iPadOS 18.0 / macOS 15.0 / tvOS 18.0 / visionOS 2.0 / **watchOS 27.0 BETA**. Legacy `VNDetectFaceRectanglesRequest` / `VNDetectFaceLandmarksRequest` / `VNDetectFaceCaptureQualityRequest` / `VNFaceObservation` go back to iOS 11.0 — use those below iOS 18. On-device, ANE-accelerated, revisioned (`supportedRevisions`) for reproducibility.

⚠️ **Trap (the defining gap):** `FaceObservation` contains **no descriptor, no embedding, no person ID, no clustering**. There is no `VNFaceprint`. Vision will never tell you that two faces are the same person. Every third-party face app must bring its own recognizer.

**Vision — `GenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest`** (Swift iOS 18.0+; legacy `VNGenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest` / `VNFeaturePrintObservation.computeDistance(_:to:)` since iOS 13.0). Produces `FeaturePrintObservation` with `data`, `elementCount`, `elementType`, and a built-in `distance(to:)`. Configurable `cropAndScaleAction` and `revision`. **Useful for:** near-duplicate detection, burst/series grouping, "more like this", visual-similarity clustering — free, zero model download, zero binary size. **Not useful for:** text→image search (there is **no Apple text encoder** — it is image-to-image only), and it is **not** a face embedding (a whole-image descriptor; feature-printing a face crop is a weak proxy that will not survive age gaps or lighting changes).

⚠️ **Trap:** feature prints are opaque and revisioned. Persist the `revision` alongside every stored vector or plan to re-index — a persisted index can silently become incomparable after an OS update. (*Apple does not explicitly document cross-revision comparability; treat non-comparability as the safe assumption.*)

**Vision — the free raw material for semantic search.** `ClassifyImageRequest` → `ClassificationObservation`, with `supportedIdentifiers` enumerating the **fixed, closed** label taxonomy (the identifier count is *unverified*). `RecognizeTextRequest` → `RecognizedTextObservation` (accurate/fast levels, language correction, custom words; the commonly cited "30+ languages" figure is *unverified*). `RecognizeDocumentsRequest` (iOS 26 — structured document/table understanding). `CalculateImageAestheticsScoresRequest` → `ImageAestheticsScoresObservation` (*"indicates whether an image contains memorable or exciting content"*; overall score plus a utility/screenshot-ish flag). `GenerateAttentionBasedSaliencyImageRequest` / `GenerateObjectnessBasedSaliencyImageRequest` (free smart-crop / thumbnail framing). `DetectLensSmudgeRequest` (iOS 26). `DetectBarcodesRequest`. `RecognizeAnimalsRequest` (cats/dogs). `DetectHumanRectanglesRequest`. `CoreMLRequest` for your own models.

⚠️ **Trap:** `ClassifyImageRequest`'s vocabulary is **CLOSED**. It cannot answer "photos of my daughter blowing out birthday candles." Open-vocabulary text→image search still requires your own CLIP/SigLIP model. The right build is a hybrid index: Vision OCR + Vision labels + Vision aesthetics + Vision feature prints (dupes) + your own SigLIP embeddings + PhotoKit structural metadata.

**Vision — segmentation and subject lifting.** `GeneratePersonSegmentationRequest` (iOS 15+ via legacy VN), `GeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest` (per-person instances, iOS 18.0+), `GenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest` (*"an instance mask of noticeable objects to separate from the background"* = subject lifting, iOS 18.0+) → `InstanceMaskObservation`. VisionKit supplies the user-facing UI: `ImageAnalyzer` (iOS 16.0+), `ImageAnalysisInteraction` (`.imageSubject`, subject lifting, Live Text), `ImageAnalysisOverlayView`.

New at WWDC 2026: **`GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest` (iOS 27.0 BETA)** — *"A request that generates a segmentation mask from points, a rectangle, or a scribble."* Three initializers: `init(seedPoint:_:)`, `init(seedBox:_:)`, `init(seedScribbleBuffer:_:)`. Refinable with **both** `addIncludedPoint(_:)` **and** `addExcludedPoint(_:)`. Normalized coordinates (0–1, origin lower-left). Requires an on-device model download at runtime via `DownloadableAssetsRequest`.

⚠️ **Trap:** there is **no lasso seed** — point, box, scribble only. Apple documents a hard limit: *"The request supports a maximum of **13 points** when seeded with a point or scribble, or **11 points** when seeded with a box."* (A widely-repeated "lasso stroke width must be ≥1% of image width" rule is **unverified** — no such statement was found in Apple's docs.) The runtime model download means first-use latency, storage cost, and an offline failure path. Instance masks are compute-heavy — batch them in a `BGContinuedProcessingTask` with GPU access, never inline.

**Core ML + Apple Neural Engine.** `MLModel` with `MLModelConfiguration.computeUnits`: `MLComputeUnits.all` (*"allow the model to use all compute units available, including the neural engine"*), `.cpuAndNeuralEngine`, `.cpuAndGPU`, `.cpuOnly` (iOS 12.0+). Vision integrates custom models via `CoreMLRequest`. The ANE is not directly programmable — you get it by making your model ANE-friendly. ⚠️ **Trap:** ANE support is op-dependent and **silently falls back** to GPU/CPU. Profile; do not assume.

*Unverified (iOS 27 beta, WWDC 2026):* claims that the Foundation Models framework now accepts image inputs as prompt Attachments, supports image-based tool calling with `ImageReference` arguments, and that Vision ships `BarcodeReaderTool` and `OCRTool` — these could not be confirmed against Apple's symbol pages and should not be planned against until checked. Note Foundation Models is Apple-Intelligence-gated (device + region + user opt-in) regardless, so it can never be a hard dependency.

**SensitiveContentAnalysis (SCA) — a real primitive, booby-trapped.** `SCSensitivityAnalyzer` with `analyzeImage(_:completionHandler:)`, `analyzeImage(at: URL, ...)`, `videoAnalysis(forFileAt:)`, and `SCVideoStreamAnalyzer` for live streams. Returns `SCSensitivityAnalysis`: `isSensitive: Bool`, `shouldIndicateSensitivity`, `shouldInterruptVideo`, `shouldMuteAudio` — plus `detectedTypes` (**iOS 27 BETA**). Availability: iOS 17.0 / iPadOS 17.0 / Mac Catalyst 17.0 / macOS 14.0 / visionOS 2.0 — **SHIPPING**. Policy enum: `SCSensitivityAnalysisPolicy` = `.disabled` / `.simpleInterventions` / `.descriptiveInterventions`. 100% on-device.

**iOS 27 BETA:** `SCSensitivityAnalysis.ContentType` has exactly two members — **`.sexuallyExplicit`** (*"nudity or sexually explicit material"*) and **`.goreOrViolence`** (*"graphic violence or gore"*). Previously the framework was nudity-only; this broadening is genuine.

⚠️ **Trap (the silent-disable):** Apple's doc for `.disabled` states the system disables analysis when **any** of: (1) *"The app lacks the necessary [`com.apple.developer.sensitivecontentanalysis.client`] entitlement."* (2) *"Neither the Sensitive Content Warning user preference nor the Communication Safety parental control in Screen Time are active."* (3) *"The person disables the Sensitive Content Warnings toggle in your app's Settings."* And: *"The framework fails to return positive results for apps that lack this entitlement in its code signature."* **Most users never enable Sensitive Content Warning.** For those users SCA returns nothing, with **no error and no signal** — an app that trusts SCA alone will silently pass explicit content through.

Therefore: **always check `analyzer.analysisPolicy != .disabled` before every use**, keep your own calibrated model as the primary gate, and treat SCA as an optional high-precision booster. SCA also exposes **no confidence score** — just a Bool plus three intervention Booleans — so there is nothing to threshold or calibrate. Separately, the entitlement reportedly requires an Apple request/approval and is unavailable to free and Enterprise accounts (*this eligibility restriction and the exact process/timeline are unverified* — but treat it as a long-lead item and start early). Free consolation prize with **no entitlement at all**: `PHPickerCapabilities.sensitivityAnalysisIntervention` makes the system picker blur nudity in your import flow.

**Visual Intelligence App Intents — you are a PROVIDER, never a CONSUMER.** The user points the camera or takes a screenshot; the system hands **your** app a pixel buffer; you return matching entities that appear in the Visual Intelligence UI. Apps can also read what Visual Intelligence writes into system stores (EventKit, Contacts, HealthKit). It is Apple-Intelligence-gated and purely user-initiated.

⚠️ **Trap:** this looks like a door into Apple's semantic index. It is not. The data flow is **strictly unidirectional** — you receive only pixel buffers the user explicitly captured and chose to share. There is **no background access, no automatic scanning of device content, and no way to query the user's photo library semantically**. This is corroborated independently by the 12-key `PHFetchOptions` predicate ceiling. Treat it as a **distribution/discovery channel**, never a data source. (*Unverified:* the specific API names attributed to it — `IntentValueQuery` with `values(for input: SemanticContentDescriptor)`, `input.pixelBuffer` as `CVReadOnlyPixelBuffer`, `@UnionValue`, `OpenIntent`, `@AppIntent(schema: .visualIntelligence.semanticContentSearch)`, and the WWDC 2026 session number — could not be confirmed. Do not rely on these symbol names without checking.)

---

### 12.13 Live Photos, iCloud identifiers, and library availability

**Live Photos.** A Live Photo is a **multi-resource asset** (`.photo` + `.pairedVideo`); `PHAssetResource.assetResources(for: livePhoto)` exposes both. Display: `PHLivePhoto` (`request(withResourceFileURLs:placeholderImage:targetSize:contentMode:resultHandler:)`) and `PHLivePhotoView` (iOS 9.1+: `livePhoto`, `playbackGestureRecognizer`, `isMuted`, `audioVolume`, `startPlayback(with:)`, `stopPlayback()`, `PHLivePhotoViewDelegate`) — Apple: *"Provide the same interactive playback of Live Photos as in the iOS Photos app."* Fetch via `PHImageManager.requestLivePhoto(for:targetSize:contentMode:options:resultHandler:)` with `PHLivePhotoRequestOptions`. Detect via `mediaSubtypes.contains(.photoLive)` or `playbackStyle == .imageAnimated`. Capture via AVFoundation (`AVCapturePhotoOutput.isLivePhotoCaptureSupported` / `isLivePhotoCaptureEnabled` with a movie URL in `AVCapturePhotoSettings` — *these exact property names were asserted from general AVFoundation knowledge and not re-fetched; confidence high, but re-check*). Edit via `PHLivePhotoEditingContext` (iOS 10.0+). iOS 27 BETA: `PHAssetChangeRequest.setLivePhotoVideoPlaybackEnabled(_:)`.

⚠️ **Trap:** naive backup implementations flatten Live Photos to stills and destroy the motion. Use `PHAssetResource` + `PHAssetCreationRequest` to preserve the pair. Also, `PHLivePhotoView` needs a real `PHLivePhoto` object — you cannot fake one from a still + video without going through `PHLivePhoto.request(...)`.

**iCloud identifiers.** `PHPhotoLibrary.cloudIdentifierMappings(forLocalIdentifiers:) -> [String: Result<PHCloudIdentifier, Error>]` and `localIdentifierMappings(for: [PHCloudIdentifier]) -> [PHCloudIdentifier: Result<String, Error>]` (iOS 15.0+; the older non-`Result` variants are deprecated, as is `PHLocalIdentifierNotFound`). `PHPhotoLibraryAvailabilityObserver` + `unavailabilityReason` (iOS 13.0+) covers library-not-yet-loaded states.

⚠️ **Trap (device migration):** `localIdentifier` is **device-scoped and does not survive device migration**. If your index/backup/person-clusters key on `localIdentifier` alone, everything breaks when the user gets a new iPhone. Store the `PHCloudIdentifier` alongside it. The mapping is a batch call that can be slow and can fail per-item (hence the `Result` type), and it is only meaningful for users with iCloud Photos enabled.

**Detecting iCloud sync failures.** The deprecated `PHAsset.isSyncFailureHidden` plus the `smartAlbumUnableToUpload` smart album are the documented surface for finding assets that failed to sync to iCloud — a real edge case for any library-indexing app.

---

### 12.14 React Native reality check

`expo-media-library` is the standard RN bridge. Reachable from JS today: `getPermissionsAsync` / `requestPermissionsAsync` with `accessPrivileges: 'all' | 'limited' | 'none'`, `presentPermissionsPicker` (the limited-library picker; current, not deprecated), and `addListener` / `removeAllListeners` for library change events. Assets are addressed by `ph://` URIs wrapping the `PHAsset` `localIdentifier`.

A large part of the functional surface is now **deprecated and moved to `expo-media-library/legacy`**, with a new class-based API replacing it: `getAssetsAsync` → *"Use the `Query` class or import this method from expo-media-library/legacy"*; `getAssetInfoAsync` → `asset.getInfo()`; `createAssetAsync` / `saveToLibraryAsync` → `Asset.create()`; `createAlbumAsync` → `Album.create()`; `getAlbumsAsync` → `Album.getAll()`; `addAssetsToAlbumAsync` → `album.add()`; `deleteAssetsAsync` → `asset.delete()` / `Asset.delete()`. The legacy functions remain importable. **This is a migration cost, not a cliff** — do not scope it as an abandonment risk.

⚠️ **Trap (the scoping error that costs an order of magnitude):** **every differentiating capability in this section requires native Swift.** Not reachable from JS: `PHPickerViewController` (including the iOS 27 `searchText` / `metadataOptions`), `PHAssetChangeRequest` caption/keywords/rating, `PHContentEditingInput`/`Output` + `PHAdjustmentData`, Photo Editing Extensions, persistent change tokens, `PHCloudIdentifier`, the Background Resource Upload Extension, `BGContinuedProcessingTask`, Vision, Core ML / ANE, and SensitiveContentAnalysis. Extensions (upload, photo-editing) are separate native targets that RN **cannot host at all**, and they must share state with the app via an App Group. React Native is a viable **UI** choice; the photo engine must be a first-class native Swift layer exposed via the Expo Modules API / TurboModules.

---

### 12.15 What a third-party app can and cannot do

| Capability | Available to 3rd parties? | Mechanism / why not |
|---|---|---|
| Enumerate the library, read structural metadata | **Yes** | `PHAsset` + `PHFetchOptions`; filtered to the allowlist under `.limited` |
| Fetch display pixels at any size | **Yes** | `PHImageManager` / `PHCachingImageManager` |
| Fetch true original bytes + full EXIF | **Yes** | `PHAssetResource` + `PHAssetResourceManager` — the **only** path; EXIF is not on `PHAsset` |
| Observe live changes while foregrounded | **Yes** | `PHPhotoLibraryChangeObserver` (iOS 8+) |
| Incremental sync across launches | **Yes** | `PHPersistentChangeToken` + `fetchPersistentChanges(since:)` (iOS 16+); push-based observer is iOS 27 BETA |
| Create assets (incl. multi-resource Live Photo / RAW) | **Yes** | `PHAssetCreationRequest`; works under `.addOnly` |
| Favorite / hide / set date / set location | **Yes** | `PHAssetChangeRequest` inside `performChanges` (requires `.readWrite`) |
| Delete assets **silently** | **No** | `deleteAssets(_:)` **always** shows a system confirmation. Batch into one call for one prompt |
| Create or fetch **user albums** under `.limited` | **No** | Apple: *"You can't create or fetch user albums."* Full access only |
| Read **Hidden** album contents | **No (effectively)** | Face-ID-gated since iOS 16; system does not return hidden assets **even with `includeHiddenAssets = true`**. Only workaround: user hands one over via `PhotosPicker` |
| Read **Recently Deleted** | **No** | No API exists, at any access level |
| Non-destructive editing that lives in the system library | **Yes** | `PHContentEditingInput`/`Output` + `PHAdjustmentData` (opaque blob you define); revertable by the user in Apple Photos |
| Put your UI **inside** the Apple Photos app | **Yes** | Photo Editing Extension (`PHContentEditingController`) — an underused distribution beachhead |
| Background upload of photos to your own server, app closed + device locked | **Yes — SHIPPING iOS 26.1** | `PHBackgroundResourceUploadExtension`. Requires `.authorized`, a Generic Extension target with `EXExtensionPointIdentifier = com.apple.photos.background-upload`, `BackgroundUploadURLBase`, and a server speaking OPTIONS-preflight + `104` resumable uploads. Not in Simulator |
| Background full-library ML indexing with GPU/ANE | **Yes — SHIPPING iOS 26.0** | `BGContinuedProcessingTask` + Background GPU Access entitlement; must be user-initiated; shows a cancellable Live Activity |
| Face **detection** (bbox, 76-point landmarks, roll/pitch/yaw, capture quality) | **Yes** | Vision `DetectFaceRectanglesRequest` / `DetectFaceLandmarksRequest` / `DetectFaceCaptureQualityRequest` — free, on-device, ANE |
| Face **identity / embedding / "who is this"** | **NO — hard sealed** | `FaceObservation` has no descriptor. No `PHPerson`. No People/Pets album subtype. No face-tag predicate key. Apple DTS: *"there is not an API to access people data in PhotoKit"* — and *"Even using private APIs, access to that info is denied to third party apps."* |
| Read Apple's **Memories** | **NO** | No `PHMemory` type; no collection type/subtype. `PHAssetCollectionType.moment` is deprecated |
| Query Apple's **semantic index** (scenes, objects, OCR, people) | **NO** | `PHFetchOptions` predicates accept exactly 12 structural keys. No semantic key exists. Visual Intelligence is provider-only |
| Whole-image similarity / near-dupe detection | **Yes** | Vision `GenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest` + `distance(to:)`. Image-to-image only — **no text encoder** |
| Open-vocabulary text→image search | **No (from Apple)** | `ClassifyImageRequest` is a **closed** taxonomy. You must ship your own CLIP/SigLIP Core ML model |
| Seed a query into **Apple's own** picker search | **iOS 27 BETA only** | `PHPickerConfiguration.searchText: PHPickerSearchText?` — zero permission, but user-confirmed and foreground-only |
| Read the user's captions / keywords | **iOS 27 BETA only** | `PHAssetExtendedMetadata` (`caption`, `keywords`, `originalFileName`) |
| Write captions / keywords / star ratings back into Photos | **iOS 27 BETA only** | `PHAssetChangeRequest.caption` / `addKeyword(_:)` / `removeKeyword(_:)` / `rating`. ⚠️ Written keywords are **not** predicate-queryable |
| On-device nudity / gore detection | **Conditionally** | SensitiveContentAnalysis — needs `com.apple.developer.sensitivecontentanalysis.client`, **and** silently returns nothing unless the user enabled Sensitive Content Warning. Bool only, no score |
| Blur sensitive content in the import picker | **Yes, free, no entitlement** | `PHPickerCapabilities.sensitivityAnalysisIntervention` |
| Know cheaply whether an asset is local vs. iCloud-only | **Partially** | No precomputed flag. Per-request `PHImageResultIsInCloudKey`, or (iOS 26.1+) a system-scheduled `creationRequestForDownloadJob(resource:)` download-only job |
| Detect assets that **failed** to sync to iCloud | **Yes** | Deprecated `PHAsset.isSyncFailureHidden` + the `smartAlbumUnableToUpload` smart album |
| Any of the above from React Native/JS | **Mostly no** | `expo-media-library` covers permissions, listing, basic albums, change listeners. Everything differentiating needs a native Swift module or extension target |

---

### 12.16 Where Apple is weak — our opening

- **The intelligence layer is sealed to *everyone*, which makes it greenfield, not a moat.** No competitor has `PHPerson`, Memories, or the semantic index either. Recognition quality, clustering, calibration, and cross-age matching are won by whoever builds the best on-device models and decision layer — Apple's advantage here is distribution, not an API that we lack and rivals have.
- **Apple's People album is a black box with no user controls we cannot beat.** Because we build identity ourselves, we can expose what Apple never will: confidence scores, calibration, explicit manual merge/split, cross-age linking, and per-cluster quality diagnostics. Apple exposes a name and nothing else.
- **The Background Resource Upload Extension (shipping since iOS 26.1) is almost entirely unadopted.** Every incumbent photo-backup app still resorts to silent pushes, background fetch, or location-tracking hacks to keep uploading. Apple has now shipped a first-class, system-scheduled, battery-aware, resumable background upload pipeline that works with the app closed and the phone locked — and the cost of entry is a backend that speaks OPTIONS-preflight + `104 Upload Resumption Supported`. That is a category-defining unlock available on shipping iOS **today**.
- **`BGContinuedProcessingTask` (iOS 26.0) kills the "keep the app open while we scan" experience.** With the Background GPU Access entitlement, a full-library ML index runs on the ANE/GPU behind a system Live Activity while the user does something else. Almost nobody has shipped this. Every competitor's first-run indexing is a hostage situation.
- **`Moment` grouping is deprecated and gone from the API.** Apple's own date/location event grouping is no longer exposed, so *nobody* gets it for free — our event clusterer competes only against whatever each rival built, and we can beat Apple's own grouping visibly.
- **Two-way metadata is about to open (iOS 27) and nobody is designing for it.** `PHAssetExtendedMetadata` + `PHAssetChangeRequest.caption`/`addKeyword`/`rating` means AI-generated captions and tags can round-trip into the user's real Apple Photos library, visible even inside Apple's app. Design the schema now, ship it behind `#available` in the fall. Caveat: written keywords are not predicate-queryable, so the payoff is user-visible value inside Photos, not a search shortcut for us.
- **The Photo Editing Extension is a free, permanent placement inside the Apple Photos app** that virtually every competitor ignores. One signature capability surfaced there (e.g. person-aware enhance) is a persistent ad for the app in Apple's own UI, at zero acquisition cost.
- **Apple's own APIs quietly break the naive implementations everyone ships.** The deprecated `authorizationStatus()` returning `.authorized` under limited access; `.opportunistic` firing the result handler twice; `isNetworkAccessAllowed = false` silently skipping every cloud-only asset; Live Photos flattened to stills on backup; indexes keyed on `localIdentifier` that die at device migration. Each of these is a competitor bug we can simply not have.
- **Structural limits we must be honest about, and can turn into trust:** Hidden and Recently Deleted are invisible to **every** third-party app; deletion always prompts; albums vanish under `.limited`. Publishing an explicit "Hidden and Recently Deleted are not accessible to any third-party app — here's why" note converts an Apple limitation into a credibility signal and pre-empts the "why is your photo count different from Apple's?" support ticket.
- **Everything above requires native Swift.** The competitive field is narrowed by the fact that RN-first teams structurally cannot reach any of it — extensions cannot be hosted in JS at all.

---
## 13. Performance, Craft & Where Photos Actually Fails

This section is about two things that are really one thing: *why* Apple Photos feels fast and continuous on a 100,000-asset library, and *where* that same app is structurally, documentably broken. The single most important thing an implementer must understand is that **Photos' speed is an indexing-and-derivative architecture, not a rendering trick** — a metadata catalog plus a pyramid of pre-baked thumbnails means the grid never decodes an original image; every craft flourish (progressive sharpen, interruptible zoom transitions, prefetch-ahead-of-scroll) is layered on top of that. The corollary, and the reason this section is worth its length: **Apple's weakness is not speed, it is the decision/curation layer** — face clustering, duplicate detection, search recall, export fidelity, and sync observability are all demonstrably poor, and most of them are wide open to a third party.

Baseline for everything below: **iOS 26.5.2** is the current shipping public release (29 Jun 2026). **iOS 26.6 is in developer beta.** **iOS 27 was announced at WWDC 2026 (June 2026)**, with developer beta 1 the same day and the **public beta on 13 July 2026**; it ships in the fall (~Sept 2026). Nothing labeled iOS 27 in this document is shippable today.

---

### 13.1 The architecture underneath the speed: catalog + derivative pyramid

Apple treats the photo library as a **database problem, not an image problem.**

**The catalog.** All asset metadata lives in a SQLite/Core Data store at `/private/var/mobile/Media/PhotoData/Photos.sqlite`. Confirmed structure (from forensic literature — Apple has never documented this):

| Table | Role |
|---|---|
| `ZASSET` / `ZGENERICASSET` | one row per photo/video: `ZDATECREATED`, `ZADDEDDATE`, `ZDIRECTORY`/`ZFILENAME` pointing into `DCIM/1xxAPPLE`, pixel dimensions, video duration |
| `ZGENERICALBUM` | albums; carries `ZTITLE` plus **denormalized** `ZCACHEDPHOTOSCOUNT` / `ZCACHEDVIDEOSCOUNT` so an album count never needs a `COUNT(*)` |
| `Z_##ASSETS` | the album↔asset many-to-many join table. **The `##` varies per device** (one analyst's device: `Z_23ASSETS`); the number maps to the Album entity in `Z_PRIMARYKEY` |
| `ZADDITIONALASSETATTRIBUTES` | extended per-asset attributes |
| `ZINTERNALRESOURCE` | one row per *derivative*, with a recipe ID, storage path, and `ZLOCALAVAILABILITY` / `ZREMOTEAVAILABILITY` flags |

⚠️ **Trap: the "~70 tables" figure is stale.** The often-quoted "nearly 70 tables in this beast" comes from an **iOS 12.1.2 / iPhone 8** forensic analysis. The schema has grown substantially and shifts *every* release — the same forensic researchers publish materially different query sets for iOS 14, 15, 16 and 17. Treat table/column names as illustrative of the **architecture**, never as current ground truth.

⚠️ **Trap: "the grid renders entirely from the catalog + pre-baked thumbnails; originals are never touched during scroll" is an inference, not a documented fact.** It is a very reasonable architectural bet — and it is the right thing for *you* to build — but Apple has never published Photos' internal render path. Do not cite it as an Apple statement. `[unverified]`

**The derivative pyramid.** Every asset has multiple pre-rendered representations, each a `ZINTERNALRESOURCE` row keyed by a "recipe ID". The confirmed recipe table (The Forensic Scooter, 3 Dec 2022 — **pre-dates iOS 18/26, treat as architectural illustration**):

| Recipe ID | Derivative | Path |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | Original / optimized full-size | device root, `DCIM/` |
| `65739` | Large JPG thumbnail | `/PhotoData/Metadata/` |
| `65741` | Assorted asset types (LPL, CPL, Cloud Sharing) | `/Metadata/`, `/CPLAssets/`, `/PhotoCloudSharingData/`, `/Mutations/`, `/UBF/scopes/syndication/` |
| `65743` | **Photo thumbnail** written as `5003.JPG` / `5005.JPG` | `/PhotoData/Thumbnails/V2/<DCIM path>/` |
| `65749` | Video keyframe | `/PhotoData/Thumbnails/VideoKeyFrames/` |
| `65938` | Photo *with adjustment* (edited) | `/Mutations/` |
| `131072` | Video *with adjustment* | `/Mutations/` |
| `131079` | `IMG_####.medium.MP4` derivative | — |
| `131081` | **Video thumbnail** written as `5003.JPG` / `5005.JPG` | `/PhotoData/Thumbnails/V2/` |
| `131272` | Live Photo *with adjustment* | — |
| `131275` | Live Photo MOV | `/PhotoData/Metadata/` |
| `131277` | Live Photo synced via iCloud | — |
| `131475` | Dolby Vision HDR `.medium-hdr.MOV` | — |
| `327683` | Third-party app thumbnail | — |
| `627687` | Wallpaper asset | `/Caches/Compute/` |

Legacy `.ithmb` thumbnail bundles also persist under `/var/mobile/Media/PhotoData/Thumbnails/`.

Two things to note. First, **`131081` proves videos get the same V2 thumbnail pyramid photos do** — a common misconception is that a video's only derivative is its keyframe. It is not. Second, the widely repeated **"`5003.JPG` is ~256×384 px" figure is low-confidence** — it appears in a single Apple Community thread and forensic forum posts, and is *not* in the recipe reference guide, which gives no pixel dimensions. `[unverified]` Design your own tiers empirically.

**The copyable idea, stated plainly:** never decode an original to draw a grid cell. On ingest, bake at minimum a grid tier (~256 px), a one-up tier (~screen width), and keep the original. Thumbnails survive the deletion of their originals in Apple's implementation (a forensic recovery vector and a privacy wart — but also why the grid keeps painting while iCloud is still fetching).

---

### 13.2 PhotoKit's performance primitives — the APIs that make a grid feel Apple-grade

These are all **fully available to third parties**, and most third-party photo grids feel worse than Photos purely because they skip them.

**`PHFetchResult` — the lazy, batched, thread-safe result set.** Apple, verbatim: *"Unlike an NSArray object, a PHFetchResult object dynamically loads its contents from the Photos library as needed, providing optimal performance even when handling a large number of results."* And: *"A fetch result caches its contents, keeping a batch of objects around the most recently accessed index. Because objects outside of the batch are no longer cached, accessing these objects results in refetching those objects."* And: *"A fetch result provides thread-safe access to its contents. After a fetch, the fetch result's count value is constant … and all objects in the fetch result keep the same `localIdentifier` value. (To get updated content for a fetch, register a change observer with the shared PHPhotoLibrary object.)"* iOS 8.0+.

The result: O(1) count, stable indices for the collection view, and a materialization window that follows the scroll. This is the model to imitate for a custom store: a windowed cursor over a sorted index with a constant count.

⚠️ **Trap: the batch cache is a correctness hazard for whole-library passes.** Values read from far-away indices get evicted and refetched. An app doing a full-library sweep (indexing, hashing, migration) will silently pay refetch costs and can read stale objects.

**`PHPhotoLibraryChangeObserver` / `PHChange` / `PHFetchResultChangeDetails` — the diff channel.** `PHFetchResultChangeDetails` exposes `hasIncrementalChanges`, `removedIndexes`, `insertedIndexes`, `changedIndexes`, and `enumerateMoves` — precisely the diff you feed to `performBatchUpdates` so the grid *animates* rather than reloads. **A competitor that reloads its whole collection view on every library change will hitch on every camera capture.** This is the single biggest omission in most third-party photo grids.

**`PHCachingImageManager` — preheat ahead of the scroll.** Apple: *"An object that facilitates retrieving or generating preview thumbnails, optimized for batch preloading large numbers of assets"* … *"a caching image manager can prepare asset images in the background in order to eliminate delays when you later request individual images."* API surface: `startCachingImages(for:targetSize:contentMode:options:)`, `stopCachingImages(...)`, `stopCachingImagesForAllAssets()`. iOS 8.0+.

⚠️ **Trap: `allowsCachingHighQualityImages` defaults to `true`, and it is now deprecated.** Apple's own doc text: *"If true (the default), the image manager prepares images at high quality. This option produces better images, at a high performance cost. For faster performance when preparing large numbers of images — such as while the user is scrolling quickly through a collection of thumbnails — set this property to false."* Most third-party grids stutter because they never flip it. Because the property is deprecated, **do not build your fast-scroll strategy on it** — get the same effect through `deliveryMode`/`resizeMode` and request sizing.

Apple engineers' guidance from the **WWDC25 Camera & Photos Group Lab** (10 June 2025), which is the most current first-party statement on this:
- prefetch **before and after** the visible range in a grid; prefetch **left and right** in one-up;
- `PHImageRequestOptions.deliveryMode = .fastFormat`, `resizeMode = .fast`; `PHVideoRequestOptions.deliveryMode = .fastFormat`;
- do pre-caching **on a background thread**;
- **request a slightly smaller image than the display size** (e.g. 300×300 for a 400×400 cell) — Apple says it does this internally and the quality loss is imperceptible;
- *"specify the size you need for the grid size… optimizations are done to deliver that size based on intermediates on disk"* — i.e. **requesting a size near an existing intermediate is dramatically faster than requesting an arbitrary size.**

⚠️ **Trap: naive caching kills you.** A documented developer-forum failure mode: caching the whole library at max resolution produces blurry images, frozen scrolling, and unbounded memory growth until a jetsam kill. The prefetch window must be bounded and must move with the scroll (`UICollectionViewDataSourcePrefetching` or equivalent).

**Progressive / opportunistic delivery — the "blurry-then-sharp" trick.** `PHImageRequestOptions.deliveryMode` has exactly three values, verbatim from Apple:

| Value | Apple's semantics |
|---|---|
| `.opportunistic` | *"Photos automatically provides one or more results in order to balance image quality and responsiveness."* **The default. Your result handler is called multiple times** — a fast degraded placeholder first, higher quality later. |
| `.highQualityFormat` | *"Photos provides only the highest-quality image available, regardless of how much time it takes to load."* |
| `.fastFormat` | *"Photos provides only a fast-loading image, possibly sacrificing image quality."* |

The degraded intermediate is flagged in the result info dict by **`PHImageResultIsDegradedKey`**: *"If true, the result parameter of your resultHandler block contains a low-quality image because Photos could not yet provide a higher-quality image."*

`resizeMode`, verbatim: `.none` — *"Photos does not resize the image asset"*; `.fast` — *"Photos efficiently resizes the image to a size similar to, or slightly larger than, the target size"*; `.exact` — *"Photos resizes the image to match the target size exactly."* (The common gloss that `.fast` "hands you an existing intermediate" is *interpretation*, not Apple's text — though the WWDC25 lab answer supports it.)

**This is why Photos never shows an empty cell.** Something is painted within one frame, then upgraded. The pattern to copy: always render *something* synchronously (tiny embedded thumb, dominant-colour or blurhash placeholder), upgrade asynchronously, never let a cell be blank.

**iCloud-backed requests — the API contract every app hits.** Because **Optimize iPhone Storage is on by default** (§13.9), full-size assets are frequently *not on disk*. The contract:
- a request without `isNetworkAccessAllowed = true` returns **nil** with **`PHImageResultIsInCloudKey`** set — *"If true, no image was provided, because the asset data must be downloaded from iCloud"*;
- with it set, you must drive a `progressHandler` UI over a network download.

This lets you distinguish **"not decoded yet"** from **"not on this device"** and show different UI (progressive sharpen vs. download progress). **Most third-party apps don't, and that alone is a differentiator.**

**Request-lifecycle hygiene** (frequently skipped, determines whether a fast fling leaves dozens of stale decodes queued behind the visible cells): `PHImageManagerMaximumSize`, `PHImageRequestOptions.isSynchronous`, `PHVideoRequestOptions` / `PHLivePhoto` request paths, and **`cancelImageRequest`**.

---

### 13.3 Decode and memory: downsample, don't scale

Apple's canonical guidance is **WWDC 2018 session 219, "Image and Graphics Best Practices"**. The core fact, verbatim: *"the size of this buffer in memory is proportional to the size of the image that it contains"* and the allocation *"is proportional to the size of the input image. Not necessarily the size of the image view that's actually rendered in the frame buffer."*

The arithmetic an implementer should internalize: a 12 MP photo decodes to roughly 4032×3024×4 bytes ≈ **48 MB of RAM**, regardless of a 2 MB HEIC on disk. *(Note: this specific 48 MB figure is derived arithmetic — Apple's on-stage demo used a 3000×2000 photo and showed 31.5 MB → 18.4 MB total app memory after downsampling. The arithmetic is correct; don't attribute the number to Apple.)*

The fix is **downsampling at decode time via ImageIO**:

```
CGImageSourceCreateWithURL(url, [kCGImageSourceShouldCache: false])   // defer decode
CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex(src, 0, [
    kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailFromImageAlways: true,
    kCGImageSourceThumbnailMaxPixelSize: <target px>,
    kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailWithTransform: true,
    kCGImageSourceShouldCacheImmediately: true                        // pay the CPU cost NOW, on a background queue
])
```

Two orthogonal levers, both essential: **(a)** never hold a full-resolution decoded buffer for a thumbnail; **(b)** control *when* the decode CPU cost is paid. Apple on `kCGImageSourceShouldCache`: *"Don't go ahead and decode this image immediately."* On `kCGImageSourceShouldCacheImmediately`: *"when I ask you to create the thumbnail that's the exact moment you should create the decoded image buffer for me. So we have exact control over when we take that CPU hit for decoding."* Pair with prefetching: *"prefetching allows the collection view to inform the data source that it will need a cell in the near future, allowing work to start early and spread CPU usage out over time."*

⚠️ **Trap:** this is *the* classic third-party photo-app failure — memory growth → jetsam kill on large libraries. If you render from raw files rather than PhotoKit derivatives, this mechanism is mandatory, not optional.

---

### 13.4 The measurable craft bar: hitches, not FPS

Apple does not talk about average FPS, because a single 300 ms stall ruins the feel while leaving average FPS respectable. Apple's vocabulary, verbatim from the Tech Talk *"Explore UI animation hitches and the render loop"* (Tech Talk 10855):

- **"A hitch is any time a frame appears on screen later than expected."**
- **"Hitch time ratio is the total hitch time in an interval divided by its duration"** — measured in **hitch-ms per second**.
- Frame budget: **16.67 ms at 60 Hz**, **8.33 ms at 120 Hz ProMotion**.

**Apple's published acceptance thresholds — this is the bar to ship against, and it belongs in your CI:**

| Hitch time ratio | Apple's verdict |
|---|---|
| 0 ms/s | the goal |
| < 5 ms/s | good — mostly unnoticeable |
| 5–10 ms/s | the user is going to notice some interruptions |
| > 10 ms/s | greatly impacting UX |

The render loop has distinct phases (app → commit → render server → display). Hitches attribute to the **commit phase** (layout, decode, main-thread work) or the **render phase** (offscreen passes, blending, rasterization). Apple ships a Tech Talk per phase: *"Find and fix hitches in the commit phase"* (10856), *"Demystify and eliminate hitches in the render phase"* (10857). Tooling: **Instruments' Animation Hitches template** and **`XCTOSSignpostMetric`** (scroll-deceleration and drag hitch metrics) — which makes a hitch-time-ratio budget a legitimate **CI gate**.

⚠️ **Trap #1 — ProMotion is NOT lineup-wide.** iPhone 13 Pro and later Pro models have 120 Hz ProMotion; iPhone 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max and iPhone Air (Sept 2025) all got it — **but the iPhone 17e (March 2026) ships a 60 Hz display with no ProMotion.** It is Apple's only new-release iPhone still at 60 Hz. Do not assume the 8.33 ms budget applies everywhere.

⚠️ **Trap #2 — `CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone`.** Since iOS 15, **third-party apps on ProMotion iPhones are capped at 60 fps** for Core Animation / UIKit animation *unless* you set `CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone` to `true` in Info.plist **and** configure `preferredFrameRateRange`. Reading "8.33 ms budget" and assuming your app gets 120 Hz for free is wrong. Apple's own apps do not have this cap.

⚠️ **Trap #3 — Photos itself is not immune.** Users report scroll stutter during background photo indexing/analysis after an update or a large import, resolving *"within a few hours or sometimes after a day or two if the photo library is very large."* Apple Community threads document Photos analyzing indefinitely on large libraries.

---

### 13.5 Grid navigation, zoom levels, and the iOS 26 chrome

**Zoom.** From the live iOS 26 iPhone User Guide, verbatim: *"While you're viewing the library, pinch the screen to zoom in or out."* Discrete, nameable levels also exist as menu commands:

| Command | Apple's description |
|---|---|
| `Zoom In` | *"Enlarge the size of the photo and video thumbnails"* |
| `Zoom Out` | *"Reduce the size of the photo and video thumbnails, to see more at the same time"* |
| `Aspect Ration Grid` **[sic — Apple's own typo]** | *"View each photo or video thumbnail in the dimension it was captured in"* |
| `Square Photo Grid` | *"To return to square thumbnails"* |

⚠️ **Trap: the entry point on iPhone is NOT the `…` More button.** Apple's **iPhone** guide says: *"Tap the **Sort and Filter** button. Tap **View Options**…"* The `…` More-button phrasing is **iPadOS**. An implementer copying the `…` affordance is copying the wrong control.

The same **`View Options`** menu also toggles visibility of **`Screenshots`**, **`Shared Library Badge`**, **`Shared with You`**, and **`From My Mac`**. (The Sort and Filter page itself documents only Screenshots / From My Mac / Shared with You.)

**Time navigation.** Apple: *"Swipe down to browse photos, then tap **Years** or **Months** to go to a specific time in your library."*

**iOS 26 chrome.** The restored navigation is a **Liquid Glass tab bar with exactly two tabs — `Library` and `Collections` — plus a search button**; the tab bar expands into a navigation bar exposing **Months / Years**. Per MacStories: *"when scrolling the grid, the tab bar will morph into Liquid Glass segmented controls for the Years, Months, and All views, joined by a convenient search button."*

⚠️ **Trap: do not benchmark against the pre-iOS-18 "Years / Months / Days / All segmented control" mental model.** That chrome is gone. iOS 26's structure is the two-tab Liquid Glass bar described above.

**The transferable design decision:** zoom is *both* a continuous gesture *and* a discrete, nameable, undoable menu command — discoverability and accessibility without giving up the gesture. Also worth copying: the `Aspect Ratio Grid` / `Square Photo Grid` toggle. Square grids are faster (uniform cell size ⇒ trivial layout) but photographers hate the crop; letting the user choose costs one layout pass.

---

### 13.6 The shared-element zoom transition (and its interruptibility)

The "tap a cell, it becomes the photo" morph. **Since iOS 18 this is first-party public API**, not a bespoke animation:

| Stack | API |
|---|---|
| SwiftUI | `.navigationTransition(.zoom(sourceID:in:))` on the destination + `.matchedTransitionSource(id:in:)` on the source cell. iOS 18.0+ / iPadOS 18.0+ / macOS 15+ / tvOS 18+ / visionOS 2+ / watchOS 11+ |
| UIKit | `viewController.preferredTransition = .zoom(options:sourceViewProvider:)`. iOS 18+ |

Apple describes it as morphing *"a source cell into the incoming view"*, increasing *"a sense of continuity"*. It works for `NavigationLink`, sheets, and `fullScreenCover`.

**The key craft property, from WWDC24 session 10145: the zoom transition is *continuously interactive*** — *"users can grab and drag the zooming view from the beginning or during the transition"* — and it preserves gesture velocity into the animation. Dismissal is a swipe on the zooming view itself.

Implementation subtleties Apple calls out:
- The UIKit closure must capture a **stable identifier, not the view itself**, because collection-view cells are recycled; you resolve the current source view *through the context* at transition time.
- **A push cannot be cancelled mid-flight.** If a pop gesture starts during a push, the push completes immediately and then the pop begins — and the full `viewWillAppear` → `isAppearing` → `viewDidAppear` cycle is still guaranteed.

⚠️ **Trap:** the claim that Photos' own one-up presentation uses *this exact mechanism* is **unverified** — Apple has never said so. Also, there is a **documented iOS 26 regression** on the SwiftUI zoom transition in Apple's own developer forums (source view disappearing, flicker, misaligned geometry), plus older navigation-title animation glitches. Budget test time.

**Bottom line for a competitor:** you can get Apple-grade continuity **for free**, and there is no excuse for a cross-fade. On a non-native stack (web/Electron/RN), the equivalent is a FLIP/shared-element transform driven by *the same gesture recognizer that owns the dismiss*, so velocity is never lost at the handoff.

---

### 13.7 One-up (detail view) gesture vocabulary — exact iOS 26 behaviors

Verbatim from the live iOS 26 guide:

| Gesture | Apple's copy |
|---|---|
| Tap a thumbnail | opens the photo full screen |
| Swipe left/right on the photo | *"Swipe left or right on the photo to keep browsing"* |
| Swipe the filmstrip below the photo | *"…or swipe the thumbnails below the photo to quickly jump forward or back"* |
| Tap the photo | *"To focus on the photo you're viewing, tap it to hide the controls onscreen. Tap it again to show the controls."* |
| Swipe up, or tap the Info button | opens photo/video information |
| Swipe down, or tap the Info button again | *"Swipe down or tap the Info button to close."* (closes the **info panel**) |
| Tap the **`Back`** button | *"Tap the Back button to close the photo and return to the library or collection."* |
| Video scrubbing | *"you can pause the video, or drag the **white bar** to go forward or back in the video"* |
| **`Spatial Scene`** button (new in iOS 26) | *"Tap [the button], then move your iPhone in your hand to view the photo with a 3D effect (available on **iPhone 12 or later**)."* |

⚠️ **Trap: there is no documented "close button" and no documented swipe-down-to-dismiss.** Apple's iOS 26 guide documents dismissal **only** via the `Back` button. Swipe-down-to-dismiss may exist in the app, but it is not in Apple's copy — mark it **unverified** and do not ship the vocabulary "close button".

The layering is worth studying: **three independent scrub surfaces** (page swipe, filmstrip, and — for video — the timeline bar), plus a modeless chrome toggle, plus a vertical axis dedicated entirely to metadata (up = info, down = close info). The vertical gesture is disambiguated by **direction**, not by a mode.

**Historical lesson:** iOS 18 removed/regressed the one-up filmstrip scrubber and users noticed immediately (*"Why did they get rid of the preview scrubber at the bottom?"*), alongside complaints that *"Photos keep going full screen then back to preview regardless of how I hold the phone."* **The scrubber is back in iOS 26.** The filmstrip is load-bearing; removing it was a documented mistake.

---

### 13.8 Selection, scrubbing, haptics — what is real and what is not

This is the area where the folklore is thickest. Be careful.

**Drag-select — CONFIRMED.** In Photos, tap **`Select`**, then press and drag across photos to sweep-select a run of items (present since iOS 9). The system-wide **two-finger drag multi-select** gesture for table/collection views (iOS 13+) also applies. A sweep should be a **range operation over your index**, not per-cell hit testing — that is why it stays smooth across hundreds of items.

⚠️ **Trap — REFUTED folklore: Photos does NOT enter selection mode via long-press.** Apple's guide has you tap the **`Select`** button. The "haptic tap then visual lift" that people describe is the **UIKit drag-and-drop lift gesture** — a *different* interaction which in Photos initiates a drag of the photo, not a selection. Do not conflate them.

**Scroll-indicator scrubbing — system behavior confirmed, presence in Photos unverified.** iOS 13+ system-wide behavior: touch and hold the scroll indicator, *"you'll get a haptic click to let you know you have grabbed it, and the bar will grow a little bigger"*, then drag to fly through content. **However: there is no Apple source stating the Photos library grid exposes scroll-indicator scrubbing.** `[unverified]` Likewise, the claim that you can drag horizontally across a Years/Months tile to scrub its representative thumbnail is **unsourced in any iOS version** and iOS 18/26 rebuilt that navigation. `[unverified — do not build against it]`

**Haptics — the weakest area in the entire corpus.** No primary Apple source enumerates Photos' haptic vocabulary (zoom-level snaps, end-of-library bounce, Live Photo long-press, scrubber detents). Only two haptics are even secondary-sourced: the scroll-indicator grab and the drag-lift. **Audit a real device rather than trust any list.** `[unverified]`

The one principle that *is* transferable and worth keeping: **haptic confirmation should fire at the moment of MODE CHANGE, and should precede the visual change** — so the hand learns the interface faster than the eye. Haptic-on-grab is the cheapest, highest-value haptic in a photo app.

**Scroll physics.** Rubber-band overscroll with a resistance curve, momentum/deceleration, and directional lock are real UIKit `UIScrollView` behaviors — **but Apple publishes no resistance curve or deceleration constants, and nothing ties them specifically to Photos' grid.** `[unverified that Photos' grid is a plain UICollectionView/UIScrollView; iOS 26's Liquid Glass may involve custom presentation layers]` The engineering consequence is blunt: **on UIKit/SwiftUI you get this free; on any non-native stack it is a from-scratch project, and a web/Electron/RN photo grid that does not nail overscroll and momentum will feel wrong no matter how fast it is.**

**Bulk-operation weakness.** There is reportedly **no true `Select All` in the Library grid** (only within albums/groupings), so bulk operations on a large library require the drag-sweep — and users report having to scroll to the bottom first so cells are loaded before a full sweep works. Deleting many thousands of items at once is reported as slow and unstable; the common advice is to batch. `[both supported only by SEO-grade blogs and scattered forum posts — directionally right, verify on device before quoting]` **Recently Deleted** holds items for **30 days** and they still consume storage — which users repeatedly misread as "deleting didn't free space".

---

### 13.9 Libraries that don't fit the device: Optimize iPhone Storage

Path: **Settings → [name] → iCloud → Photos → `Sync this iPhone`**, then **`Optimize iPhone Storage`** or **`Download and Keep Originals`**.

Apple's iOS 26 guide, verbatim: *"When **Optimize iPhone Storage** is turned on, all your full-resolution photos and videos are stored in iCloud in their original formats, with storage-saving versions kept on your iPhone. **Optimize iPhone Storage is turned on by default**, but you can turn it off."*

**The eviction policy is an LRU, and Apple says so explicitly:** *"Your library also optimizes when you need space, **starting with photos and videos you access least**, and you can download originals over Wi-Fi or cellular."*

Consequences an implementer must design for:
1. **The thumbnail pyramid always stays local** — the grid is fully browsable offline even when almost no originals are on device.
2. **Opening a photo can trigger an on-demand full-res fetch** — surfaced to developers as `PHImageResultIsInCloudKey` + `isNetworkAccessAllowed` + `progressHandler` (§13.2).
3. Uploads can be **paused for one day** (Photos → Collections → profile button → **`Pause`**).
4. Deleted items live in **`Recently Deleted`** for **30 days**.

**iOS 26's in-app sync-status vocabulary** (Photos → Collections → account icon, top-right) — worth copying wholesale, since it is Apple's entire answer to "is my library safe?":

| Indicator | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Partially filled **blue** circle around the account icon | photos are actively uploading |
| Partially filled **gray** outline | uploads paused |
| **Yellow badge** | iCloud syncing is paused |
| **Yellow warning** icon | iCloud storage almost full |
| **Red exclamation mark** | iCloud storage full |
| **Blue badge** | notifications from a shared library/album |

Also: *"the last time your iPhone synced with iCloud appears below the account profile."*

**System requirements (corrected — the commonly cited numbers are stale):**

| Feature | Requirement (Apple's live system-requirements page) |
|---|---|
| iCloud Photos | **iOS 11**, macOS High Sierra 10.13, Windows 10 + iCloud for Windows 10 or later, tvOS 11 |
| iCloud Shared Photo Library | **iOS/iPadOS 16.1**, macOS Ventura 13, Windows 10 + iCloud for Windows 14, tvOS 16 |

⚠️ **Trap:** the frequently-repeated "iCloud Photos requires iOS 8.3 / iPadOS 13.1 / macOS 10.10.3 / iCloud for Windows 7.x" is **REFUTED** — those are ~2015-era numbers from an older version of Apple's page.

⚠️ **Unresolved contradiction in Apple's own docs:** the iOS 26 User Guide says *"Optimize iPhone Storage is turned on by default"*, while Apple support article 105061 says *"By default, your photos and videos are stored on your device in their original, high-resolution version."* The likely reconciliation is that Optimize is default **once iCloud Photos is enabled** — but this is unconfirmed. Do not rely on either statement without device verification.

---

### 13.10 iOS 27's performance claim (BETA — not shippable today)

apple.com/os/ios advertises for **iOS 27** (announced WWDC 2026, public beta 13 Jul 2026, **ships fall 2026**):

| Claim | Apple's test configuration (footnote) |
|---|---|
| App launches **"up to 30% faster"** | footnote 8: **iPhone 11 Pro Max**, iOS 26.4.2 vs prerelease iOS 27, *"measured after many cycles of device usage"* |
| **"new photos load in your Photos library up to 70% faster"** | footnote 9: *"Testing conducted by Apple in April and May 2026 using **iPhone 15** with iOS 26.4.2 and prerelease iOS 27. Photos app tested using a **50,000-asset library**, and taking additional individual photos with Camera app."* |
| AirDrop **"up to 80% faster"** | footnote 10: **iPhone 16 Plus**, *"multiple photos totaling 30MB… while not associated with a Wi-Fi network"* |

⚠️ **Trap: the 70% figure is NOT "the grid got 70% faster."** Read the footnote: it is about how fast a **newly captured photo appears in the library** — the ingest path (capture → catalog → derivative → grid), not scroll performance. Anyone quoting it as scroll speed is misleading you.

What it tells you: **Apple believes its remaining Photos latency is on the write/ingest path on a large catalog.** If Apple is spending its 2026 perf budget there, your ingest path is almost certainly far worse. Treat it as a named risk area.

**Adopt Apple's test rig as your own: a 50,000-asset library on an iPhone-15-class device.** It is the only trustworthy scale datapoint in the corpus. (Popular blog thresholds like "Photos gets sluggish by 30,000 photos / stutters by 75,000" come from low-quality SEO sources and should **not** be used.)

---

### 13.11 Where Photos actually fails — the documented catalogue

#### 13.11.1 The iOS 18 redesign backlash — and Apple's on-the-record retreat

The best-documented UX failure in the app's history. iOS 18 (Sept 2024) **collapsed the tab bar into a single continuously scrolling page**. Complaints: cluttered single-page IA; can't find anything in a large library; redundant auto-generated collections; removal of the Library/Albums tabs; Favorites and People buried; photos no longer opening full-screen by default; gesture collisions (a back-swipe switching `All` → `Months` — *"VERY frustrating"*).

⚠️ **Trap — the most commonly repeated fact about iOS 18 Photos is FALSE: the Carousel never shipped.** Apple **removed the Carousel of daily highlights during the beta cycle — in iOS 18 developer beta 5 (5 August 2024)**, ~6 weeks before release. It also **reverted pinch-to-zoom to iOS 17 behavior in beta 3 (July 2024)** and made the `Select` button always visible. The tab-bar removal *did* ship; the Carousel did not.

The retreat, on the record:
1. **11 Aug 2024** — Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports Apple deemed the redesign *"probably a little too bold and potentially confusing"*, removed the Carousel mid-beta, *"tweaked the photo grid to be more user-friendly and pushed albums higher up"*, and *"moved saved content back into the main photo grid."*
2. **Nov 2024** — users still divided two months post-launch (MacRumors).
3. **WWDC 2025** — Craig Federighi, on stage: **"Many of you missed using tabs in the Photos app. Photos now features separate tabs for Library and for Collections."** iOS 26 restored the tab bar in Liquid Glass.

**Still-open gaps after the iOS 26 fix:** you can collapse Collections but you **cannot exclude collection types** you never want; iCloud sync status now takes several taps (it used to sit at the bottom of the Library); the single-scroll view's quick access to Screenshots/Videos is gone; MacStories mourns the loss of Recent Days highlights and wants an optional setting to have both layouts. **A paid third-party app — Photon Library ($5, Sept 2024) — exists solely to restore the pre-iOS-18 feel. That is direct, priced evidence of willingness to pay.**

#### 13.11.2 People & Pets — misidentification with no correction primitives

Exact iOS 26 UI vocabulary (from *"Find and name people and pets in Photos on iPhone"*): the **`People & Pets`** collection; **`Name This Person`** / **`Name This Pet`**; **`Edit Name and Photos`**; **`Add People`** (*"tap Add People at the bottom of the People & Pets collection to see more faces"*); **`Favorite`** / **`Unfavorite`**; **`Sort by Name`** / **`Sort by Custom Order`**; **`Hide [name]`** / **`Don't Feature [name]`**; **`All Photos`**; **`Make Key Photo`**; **`Don't Feature This Person`**. For misidentification: *"Tap **`This is Not [name]`**, then tap **`Rename This Person`** or **`Rename This Pet`**."*

From the *separate* page *"Hide people, memories, and holidays in Photos on iPhone"*: **`Feature This Person Less`**, **`Never Feature This Person`**, **`Confirm`**, **`Show Featured Content`**, **`Show Holiday Events`**. Reset path: **Collections → tap your account icon → `Reset People & Pets Suggestions`** (alternatively **Settings > Apps > Photos > `Reset Suggested Memories` / `Reset People & Pets Suggestions`**).

**Read the gap carefully.** Apple's own iOS 26 documentation for fixing incorrect names offers **only renaming**. There is **no documented un-merge**, **no documented way to remove a single wrongly-attributed photo** from a person cluster within the People & Pets flow, and **no way to correct a bad face rectangle**. The model's clustering errors are, for most users, **one-way doors**.

⚠️ **Verify on device:** an older `Not This Person` selection-based removal flow existed in earlier iOS versions and users still hunt for it. It could **not** be established when — or whether — it was cut; it may still exist undocumented in the People album's Select → `…` menu. This materially changes the size of the opportunity. `[unverified]`

Documented, years-deep, still open:
- Two different people silently merged into one group *"mixing thousands of photos"*, with no merge warning.
- Users unable to unlink one wrong face.
- Face boxes highlighting *"a random part of the photo with no face in it."*
- Wrong people attached to a photo, so searching for person X returns photos X isn't in.
- **Worst: after manually re-tagging, the software undoes the tags and re-merges the same people a few minutes later.**
- The community's only reliable "fix" is nuclear: delete every People album until Photos resets the entire faces database and starts over.
- **Cross-age is a known weak point** (a child's face across years).
- Because *"When you use iCloud Photos, People & Pets is kept up to date on all your devices"* — **a bad merge propagates everywhere.**

*(Note: "pets = dogs and cats only" is press folklore — Apple's docs never scope the species. `[unverified]`)*

#### 13.11.3 Search — a recall failure, not a precision failure

Baseline (non-Apple-Intelligence) search accepts exactly these dimensions, verbatim from Apple's bullet list: **Date** (month or year); **Place** (city or state); **Business names** (museums, for example); **Category** (beach or sunset, for example); **Events** (sports games or concerts, for example); **a person identified in the People & Pets collection**; **Text** (an email address or phone number, for example); **Caption**. Tip: *"You can narrow your search by including a media type in the search field, such as **Video** or **Portrait**."* There is also a **`Shared by`** flow for shared-library contributors.

*(Apple's label is **`Text`**, not "Live Text".)*

**Natural-language / semantic search is gated:**

| Gate | Detail |
|---|---|
| Hardware | **Apple Intelligence only** — iPhone 15 Pro / 15 Pro Max, plus **every** iPhone 16 and 17 model (incl. 16e, 17e, iPhone Air). Floor: **A17 Pro + 8 GB RAM** |
| Maturity | Apple's own words: **"available in beta"** |
