| Languages | **16**: English, Danish, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese |
| Extra capability | also searches **"key moments" inside video clips** and can jump to a segment |

**The quantified gap** (Mac Power Users forum, March 2023 — **one user's library, pre-Apple-Intelligence, three years old; anecdotal, not a benchmark**): *"X-ray"* → Google Photos **1,100** results vs Apple Photos **44**. *"Irish setter"* (their dog) → Google Photos **770** vs Apple Photos **0**. Another user: Apple's search is *"unusable… It misses nearly every time."* Users also report natural-language queries returning nothing (*"Charlie wearing red"* → no results; *"Bella on the beach"* → ~a dozen out of hundreds). ⚠️ **Treat these numbers as directional, not authoritative** — no rigorous head-to-head has been published since Apple Intelligence shipped.

Structural search complaints that *are* durable: the index never finishes (*"Photos is endlessly analyzing the library"*); **no index-progress UI**; **no force-reindex**; **no way to inspect why a photo didn't match**; **no boolean/structured queries**; **no saved searches**.

#### 13.11.4 Memories — quality, and emotional harm

Memories are auto-generated movies/collections. iOS 26 adds an Apple Intelligence **`Create`** flow: **Collections → Memories → `Create` → type a description → `Done`**. Apple, verbatim: *"To create a memory movie, you just type a description, and Apple Intelligence finds the best photos and videos, crafts a storyline with unique chapters and a narrative arc, and sets it to music."* (Gated: Apple Intelligence hardware + the 16 languages, beta.)

**The only user controls are blunt and almost entirely negative:** `Feature This Person Less`, `Never Feature This Person`, `Show Featured Content` (off), `Show Holiday Events` (off), `Reset People & Pets Suggestions`, and hiding individual memories. **Apple's guide describes no way to tell Memories "never surface photos from this date range / this location / this album."**

**The harm is documented and repeated:** memories of a deceased loved one appearing unexpectedly (*"very disturbing"*); photos of exes resurfacing; and the fact that **memory *creation* cannot be turned off** — only slowed or hidden. 2025 press coverage frames the feature as having *"emotionally terrorized"* users. Combined with People misidentification, **a wrongly-clustered person can put a stranger's face into your "family" memory.**

#### 13.11.5 Duplicates — slow, uncorrectable, and undocumented

Path (verbatim): *"Tap **Collections**. Tap **Utilities**, then tap **Duplicates**. Tap **`Merge`** to combine a set of duplicates, then tap **`Merge [number] Items`**."* And: *"If you don't have any duplicate photos or videos in your library, the Duplicates collection doesn't appear."* (iOS 16+; iOS 26 relocates it under Collections → Utilities.)

⚠️ **Trap: "exact-match only" is UNVERIFIED.** Apple has **never documented the matching algorithm.** The widely repeated characterization — that items must match pixel-for-pixel (size, metadata, format), that two shots a fraction of a second apart are "similar" not duplicate, and that similar photos never appear in the collection — comes from user reports and third-party writeups, not from Apple. `[unverified — do not cite as fact]`

What **is** documented by users, consistently:
- **Near-duplicates are never found** (hundreds of true duplicates missed in libraries of thousands).
- **Detection can take days**, runs as an opportunistic background task, and has **no progress indicator**.
- **There is no way to mark a pair as NOT duplicates**, and **no threshold control**. The only user workaround to un-suggest a pair is to **apply a tiny edit to one of them** so they stop matching.

#### 13.11.6 No Smart Albums, no keywords/tags, no bulk metadata edit — ⚠️ **THIS GAP IS EXPIRING**

What iOS 26 has: folders and albums (**Collections → Albums → `New Album` / `New Folder`**), and a real filter set — **`Filter`**: Photos, Videos, Favorites, Edited, **`Not in an Album`** (*"such as Videos, Favorites, or Not in an Album"*; `All Items` resets filters); **`Sort by Recently Added`** (*"Photos and videos you added most recently appear at the bottom of the library"*) / **`Sort by Date Captured`**.

What iOS 26 does **not** have:
- **Smart Albums** (rule-based saved queries) — **macOS-Photos-only. Smart Albums created on a Mac do not appear on iPhone or iPad at all**; only standard albums sync.
- **Keywords/tags** — creatable/editable **only on macOS**; on iOS they are invisible in the UI, and their sole iOS manifestation is that keyword text becomes *searchable*.
- **Bulk metadata editing**, with one exception: the only user-authored metadata on iOS is the per-photo **`Caption`** field (info sheet), which **cannot be applied in bulk**.

**The one bulk exception (confirmed verbatim):** *"To change the date, time, or location of a batch of photos, tap `Select`, tap the thumbnails you want to change, then follow the steps above."* Labels: **`Adjust Date & Time`**, **`Adjust Location`**, **`Add a location`**, **`Revert`**.

⚠️ **Trap — TIME-EXPIRED CLAIM.** **iOS 27 (public beta 13 Jul 2026, ships this fall) ADDS keywords to photos and videos, plus 1–5 star ratings and filter-by-rating, plus a `Show Selected` option for batch metadata editing.** Telling an implementer that "Apple has no keyword/tag system" as a *durable* competitive gap will be **actively wrong within ~8 weeks.** Smart Albums on iOS remain unannounced.

#### 13.11.7 Export fidelity — the hardest, most quantifiable loss

Three distinct fidelity leaks, all from Apple's own documentation.

**(1) On-device export is edit-destroying by design.** iOS 26 guide, verbatim: *"Note: For photos and videos that have been edited, **the unmodified original version will be exported**."* The button is literally labeled **`Export Unmodified Original`** (*"Tap the Share button, then tap Export Unmodified Original"*). Edge case worth knowing: *"Photos and videos in the **Hidden** album won't be transferred if the album is locked"* — you must turn off Use Face ID / Use Touch ID / Use Passcode under **Settings > Apps > Photos**.

**(2) Shared Albums brutally downscale.** From Apple's Shared Album limits page (published 27 Feb 2025):

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Photo resolution | **reduced to 2048 pixels on the long edge** (panoramas up to **5400 px** wide) |
| Video | *"Videos can be up to **fifteen minutes** in length and are delivered at up to **720p** resolution"* |
| Spatial media | **not supported** — *"Shared Albums do not support spatial photo or video"* |
| Items per album | **5,000** (photos + videos combined) |
| Albums you can share (as owner) | **200** |
| Albums you can subscribe to | **200** *(a separate limit from the above)* |
| Subscribers per album | **100** |
| Contribution rate | **1,000/hour**, **10,000/day** per contributor |
| Comments | 200 per item; 1,024 chars per comment |
| Invites | 200/day |
| GIFs | ≤ 100 MB |

**The 2048 px ceiling is the most damning number in this section: Apple's own primary sharing surface throws away roughly 95% of a 48 MP photo's pixels.** iOS 27 fixes exactly this — apple.com/os/ios lists *"iCloud Shared Albums with full-resolution sharing support"* — which is an admission it was broken. **(Beta, fall 2026.)**

**(3) Format conversion on transfer.** Settings → Photos → **Transfer to Mac or PC** → **`Automatic`** (transcodes HEIC→JPEG / HEVC→H.264 on the fly) vs **`Keep Originals`** (hands over the HEIC/HEVC). ⚠️ `[The setting exists and behaves as described, but no Apple support page documenting it could be found — sources are Apple Community threads and press. Low confidence on Apple sourcing.]`

**User-reported consequences:** 4K clips recompressed after an in-Photos edit (~150 MB / 40 Mbps → ~50 MB / 13 Mbps); 65 MB 4K clips shrinking to ~a quarter when dragged to Files; iCloud downloads arriving as compressed `.mp4` instead of the original `.mov`; HEIC→JPEG round-trips creating **phantom duplicates that Photos then fails to recognize as duplicates**, generating manual cleanup work. **Users cannot get an edited photo off the phone at full fidelity via the built-in export.**

#### 13.11.8 No selective sync; Shared Photo Library feels destructive

**iCloud Photos is all-or-nothing.** The whole library syncs, or none of it. There is **no per-album, per-person, or per-date selective sync**; the only lever is Optimize Storage, which is **automatic and LRU-driven, not user-directed**. *(The framing "Apple's design intent is that all libraries are identical across devices" is a characterization, not an Apple statement.)*

**iCloud Shared Photo Library** (iOS 16.1+) is the closest thing to a partition, and its edges are sharp — Apple states them plainly:
- *"share photos and videos with **up to five** friends or family members"* (**6 total**);
- *"**You can belong to one shared library at a time.**"*;
- *"the photos and videos that you contribute **move from your personal library to the shared library**, and **all members of the library can view, edit, and delete them**."*
- **There is no read-only participant role.**
- Content added to it is **invisible on OS versions older than iOS/iPadOS 16.1 / macOS 13 / tvOS 16.**

**Shared Albums** (the older mechanism) don't move anything and don't count against iCloud storage — but they're the ones capped at **2048 px** (§13.11.7).

Perennial user complaint: *"When iCloud Photos is enabled, it's for syncing all or nothing — you don't get to pick and choose."* A user with a 200 GB library and a 128 GB phone **has no way to say "keep my kids' album local, evict the rest."**

⚠️ **Partially eroding in iOS 27 (beta):** Apple is adding a **`Sync Immediately`** option to prioritize specific uploads — the **first user-directed lever over sync order.**

#### 13.11.9 Sync anxiety — the trust wedge

Three classes of documented failure.

1. **Indefinite stalls.** A real MacRumors thread titled *"Photos 'Syncing 2 items...' indefinitely since iOS 26.2"* states the problem exactly: there is *"seemingly no way to find out which 2 files are stuck without manually inspecting the status of 132,000 photos."* Apple Community threads report *"iCloud photos stuck on updating."*
2. **Silent partial sync.** Photos visible on one device, absent on another; albums where ~50 of 65 images sync and re-syncing gives inconsistent results. ⚠️ *The commonly-cited "worse above ~50,000 assets" threshold and the "notably with HEIC captures and edited Live Photos" correlation are **anecdotal forum reports, not established failure modes.** One user reported a stuck item that was "a live image that had been edited" — a single data point, not a pattern.* `[unverified]`
3. **The precedent that broke trust.** **iOS 17.5 (May 2024) resurrected photos users had deleted years earlier.** Apple's own explanation: *"a rare issue where photos that experienced database corruption could reappear in the Photos library even if they were deleted."* Apple's expanded explanation blamed a **corrupted database entry on the device file system** (not iCloud Photos), propagated via **local backup restore / device-to-device transfer**. **iOS 17.5.1 (20 May 2024) fixed the cause but did NOT re-delete the resurfaced photos** — users had to delete them by hand, again.

The user-visible surface for all of this is thin: a partially-filled ring around the account icon, and a `Pause` that lasts one day. **Users cannot answer the only question that matters — "are all my photos actually safe?" — and Apple's UI gives them no way to prove it.** Analyst guidance is literally to keep a redundant, non-Apple backup.

#### 13.11.10 Video is a second-class citizen

Confirmed:
- **Shared Albums cap videos at 15 minutes and 720p** (verbatim from Apple).
- The one-up video control is a **single white bar** — *"drag the white bar to go forward or back in the video"* is the **only** scrub affordance Apple documents.
- **`Export Unmodified Original` applies to videos too** — an edited video exports as its unedited original.
- **iOS 27 (beta) adds saving a video frame as a photo**: *"You can now save a frame of a video as an individual photo."* An admission of a long-standing gap.
- Apple Intelligence search can find **"key moments"** in video clips — but only on gated hardware.

⚠️ **Trap — REFUTED: video keyframes are NOT a video's only derivative.** Recipe **`131081`** is a *video thumbnail* written as `5003.JPG` / `5005.JPG` under `/PhotoData/Thumbnails/V2/` — i.e. **videos get the same V2 thumbnail pyramid photos do** — plus `131079` (medium MP4) and `131072` (video with adjustment). The `65749` VideoKeyFrames resource is one of several.

⚠️ **Unverified sub-claims — do not assert these:** "no frame-accurate stepping", "no bulk video export", "bitrate/codec/fps are not shown". No source was found either way. `[unverified]`

User-reported: 4K clips silently recompressed on edit (40 Mbps → 13 Mbps) and on transfer to Files; iCloud downloads returning compressed `.mp4` instead of the original `.mov`; *"videos get compressed when moving from Photos."*

---

### 13.12 What a third-party app can and cannot do

**The two access modes.**

- **`PHPickerViewController`** (iOS 14+) — Apple: *"a new picker that replaces UIImagePickerController. Its user interface matches that of the Photos app, supports search and multiple selection of photos and videos, and provides fluid zooming of content. Because the system manages its life cycle in a **separate process**, it's **private by default**. The user doesn't need to explicitly authorize your app."* Runs out-of-process over XPC; **no usage description required, no permission prompt shown.** The photo-library portion of `UIImagePickerController` is deprecated in its favor.
- **Full PhotoKit** — requires `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription` (or `NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription` for add-only). *"Attempting to access the Photos library without a valid usage description causes your app to crash."* `PHAuthorizationStatus`: `notDetermined` / `restricted` / `denied` / `authorized` / **`limited`** (iOS 14+). `PHAccessLevel`: `.addOnly` / `.readWrite`.

⚠️ **Trap: `.limited` access is a crippled photo manager.** In limited mode: you see **only the user's selected assets**; **user albums cannot be fetched or created**; **there is no access to cloud shared assets or albums**; new assets your app creates are auto-added to the selection. **You must ask for full `.readWrite` access, and you must earn it** — and the permission ask is your single biggest funnel drop (*"In nearly all cases, users do not want to give third parties access to their entire library"*). The counter is a fully on-device, verifiably offline story — no network entitlement, visible "nothing leaves your phone" proof — which is precisely the ground on which Apple normally wins.

Also structural: `PHAsset` / `PHAssetCollection` / `PHCollectionList` are **immutable**. Mutations happen only inside a `PHPhotoLibrary.performChanges` block and are observed via `PHPhotoLibraryChangeObserver`.

| Capability | Available to 3rd parties? | Mechanism / why not |
|---|---|---|
| Read `Photos.sqlite` directly | **No** | Sandboxed. Use `PHFetchResult` over PhotoKit — itself lazy, batched, thread-safe. A custom library must build and reconcile its own catalog. |
| Read Apple's baked derivatives directly | **No (not the files)** | But `PHImageManager` / `PHCachingImageManager` **serve exactly those intermediates**. Requesting a size near an existing intermediate is dramatically faster than an arbitrary size. |
| Batch prefetch/preheat thumbnails | **Yes** | `PHCachingImageManager.startCachingImages(for:targetSize:contentMode:options:)`. Highest-leverage PhotoKit API for scroll performance. |
| Progressive blurry→sharp delivery | **Yes** | `PHImageRequestOptions.deliveryMode = .opportunistic` + `PHImageResultIsDegradedKey`. |
| Distinguish "on device" vs "in iCloud" | **Yes** | `PHImageResultIsInCloudKey`, `isNetworkAccessAllowed`, `progressHandler`, `PHAssetResource` availability. **Most apps don't do this — it's a free differentiator.** |
| Animate incremental library changes | **Yes** | `PHPhotoLibraryChangeObserver` + `PHChange` + `PHFetchResultChangeDetails` (`hasIncrementalChanges`, `insertedIndexes`, `removedIndexes`, `changedIndexes`, `enumerateMoves`) → `performBatchUpdates`. |
| Apple-grade shared-element open/close | **Yes** | SwiftUI `.navigationTransition(.zoom(sourceID:in:))` + `.matchedTransitionSource(id:in:)`; UIKit `preferredTransition = .zoom(...)`. iOS 18+. **Continuously interactive, free.** |
| Downsample-on-decode / control decode timing | **Yes** | ImageIO: `kCGImageSourceShouldCache`, `kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex`, `kCGImageSourceThumbnailMaxPixelSize`, `kCGImageSourceShouldCacheImmediately`. |
| Measure hitches / gate scroll perf in CI | **Yes** | Instruments Animation Hitches template, `XCTOSSignpostMetric`, MetricKit. Apple's bar: **<5 ms/s hitch time ratio**. |
| Render at 120 Hz on ProMotion | **Yes — but not by default** | ⚠️ Requires `CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone = true` in Info.plist **and** `preferredFrameRateRange`. Otherwise iOS caps third-party apps at 60 fps. |
| Read Apple's **People / faces** graph | **NO — hard wall** | *"There is not an API to access people data in PhotoKit as of now"* (Apple Developer Forums). Apple stores face **rectangles** in EXIF under an `IIO` prefix (coordinates, width, height, type, confidence) but **not the person's name**. |
| Read/write/suppress **Memories** | **NO** | No PhotoKit API exposes Memories at all. |
| Access Apple's **search index / semantic embeddings** | **NO** | Not exposed in any form. |
| Create **Smart Albums** | **NO** | `PHAssetChangeRequest` can set favorite/hidden and create/modify user albums and folders (`PHCollectionList`) — but cannot create Smart Albums, and exposes **no keyword/tag field**. |
| Participate in **Optimize Storage** eviction / pre-warm iCloud originals at scale | **NO** | Apple-internal policy. |
| Access **cloud shared assets/albums** under `.limited` access | **NO** | Limited-library restriction. |
| Get the **true original bytes + adjustment data** | **YES** | `PHAssetResource` + `PHAssetResourceManager`; `PHContentEditingInput` gives you the render pipeline. **You can therefore export a full-fidelity rendered-with-edits file — which Apple's own on-device export path does not do.** |
| Build your own **face graph** | **YES** | Vision (`VNDetectFaceRectanglesRequest`, faceprint-class APIs) + Core ML, entirely on-device. Apple's refusal to expose People **also frees you** to build it your way. |
| Build your own **semantic search** | **YES** | Vision (classification, text recognition, face/animal detection) + Core ML / on-device CLIP-class embeddings + your own inverted index. |
| Build **near-duplicate detection** | **YES — wide open** | pHash/dHash, burst-group detection, embedding-space clustering. Adjustable threshold, "keep the sharpest/largest/newest", "mark as NOT duplicate" persistence, preview-diff before merge — all trivially implementable. |
| Real video handling | **YES** | AVFoundation: `AVAssetImageGenerator` for frame-accurate scrubbing and frame export, full codec/bitrate metadata, **passthrough export with no recompression**. |
| Own sync topology inside Apple's library | **NO** | You cannot create a sync topology inside iCloud Photos. **But with your own backend you can offer what Apple structurally cannot** (below). |
| Scroll physics (rubber-band, momentum, directional lock) | **Free on UIKit/SwiftUI** | `UIScrollView` gives it away. ⚠️ On web/Electron/RN this is a **from-scratch engineering project**, and getting it wrong makes the app feel wrong regardless of speed. |
| Haptic-on-grab / mode-change haptics | **Yes** | `UIImpactFeedbackGenerator` / CoreHaptics. Fire the haptic at the **mode change**, **before** the visual change. |

---

### 13.13 Where Apple is weak — our opening

**Ranked by size of opening.**

1. **People correction is the single largest product opening in the domain.** Apple's iOS 26 docs offer *only rename* for a misidentified person: no un-merge, no per-photo rejection, no bounding-box correction, no threshold. Users report merged strangers *"mixing thousands of photos"*, face boxes on regions with no face, and re-merges that **silently undo manual corrections minutes later**. The community's only reliable remedy is to delete every People album and let the faces DB rebuild. **PhotoKit exposes no People API — which cuts both ways: you can't read Apple's graph, and you are completely free to build a better one with Vision + Core ML** and ship every correction primitive Apple refuses: un-merge, split cluster, reject a single photo, tune the threshold, fix the rectangle, merge across time gaps. Cross-age (a child across years) is Apple's known weak point.

2. **Semantic search on non-Apple-Intelligence hardware.** Apple's natural-language search is **hardware-gated (A17 Pro + 8 GB RAM: iPhone 15 Pro/Pro Max and all iPhone 16/17 models), explicitly beta, and limited to 16 languages.** Everyone on older hardware gets the old, weak search — a documented complaint: *"I have iPhone 12 mini and promised AI based search does not work here… it's dumb as it always was."* **A competing app that ships good on-device semantic search to an iPhone 12 immediately beats Apple on that device.** That is a concrete, addressable market. (Recall, not precision, is the failure: the widely-cited — though anecdotal and pre-AI — user test showed *"X-ray"* returning 1,100 results in Google Photos vs 44 in Apple Photos, and *"Irish setter"* 770 vs 0.)

3. **Export fidelity — trivially winnable.** Apple's on-device export button is literally labeled **`Export Unmodified Original`**: **edits are discarded.** Shared Albums downscale photos to **2048 px long edge** and videos to **720p / 15 min**. Meanwhile `PHAssetResource` + `PHContentEditingInput` let a third party export a **full-fidelity, rendered-with-edits** file. This is the lowest-hanging fruit in the entire atlas. *(Caveat: iOS 27 adds full-resolution Shared Albums — the sharing half of this gap closes this fall. The `Export Unmodified Original` behavior has no announced fix.)*

4. **Duplicates.** No "not a duplicate", no threshold, no progress indicator, detection that can take **days**, and near-duplicates that are simply never found. The only user workaround to un-suggest a pair is to **apply a tiny edit to one photo so it stops matching.** Perceptual hashing and embedding-space clustering are undergraduate-level work. Ship: adjustable similarity threshold, burst collapsing, "keep the sharpest/largest/newest" auto-pick, **persistent "not a duplicate"**, and a preview-diff before merge.

5. **Sync observability — the trust wedge.** Apple offers a partially-filled ring and a `Pause` that lasts a day. It cannot tell a user *which* items are stuck: a real MacRumors thread (*"Syncing 2 items... indefinitely since iOS 26.2"*) notes there is *"seemingly no way to find out which 2 files are stuck without manually inspecting the status of 132,000 photos."* And the trust precedent is brutal — **iOS 17.5 (May 2024) resurrected years-old deleted photos due to database corruption, and iOS 17.5.1 fixed the cause but never re-deleted them.** A competitor can win on **observability alone**: a per-asset sync ledger (this file, this hash, uploaded at this time, verified by this checksum), an explicit "N items failed — here they are — retry" list, content-addressed integrity checks, and a verifiable *"your library is fully backed up"* assertion. **Apple offers none of this.**

6. **Selective sync.** iCloud Photos is all-or-nothing; Optimize Storage evicts on an LRU Apple states outright (*"starting with photos and videos you access least"*) with **zero user control over what stays local — no "pin this album offline."** iCloud Shared Photo Library caps at **6 people**, you can belong to **only one**, contributed photos **move out of your personal library**, and **every member can delete them** — no read-only role. With your own backend: pin-album-offline, sync-only-these-people, per-device library subsets, read-only collaborators, >6 participants. *(iOS 27 adds a `Sync Immediately` prioritization option — a partial erosion, not a fix.)*

7. **Memories consent.** Memory *creation* cannot be turned off, only slowed or hidden; the controls are purely negative (`Feature This Person Less`, `Never Feature This Person`, `Show Featured Content` off). Documented harm: deceased loved ones and exes resurfacing unexpectedly; 2025 press said the feature *"emotionally terrorized"* users. **Build a consent-first memory engine:** opt-in per person/date/place, an explicit "don't resurface" blocklist, preview-before-notify.

8. **Video.** Recompression on edit and export; 720p/15-min shared-album ceiling; a single white scrub bar as the only documented scrub affordance. **AVFoundation gives a third party everything Apple withholds from its own UI**: frame-accurate scrubbing and frame export (`AVAssetImageGenerator`), full codec/bitrate metadata, and **passthrough export with no recompression**. *(iOS 27 finally adds "save a frame of a video as a photo" — an admission of the gap.)*

9. **Organization, with an expiry date.** No Smart Albums on iOS at all (Mac-only, and **Mac-created Smart Albums do not appear on iPhone**); no bulk metadata editing except date/time/location. ⚠️ **But iOS 27 adds keywords, 1–5 star ratings, filter-by-rating and `Show Selected` batch editing — so "Apple has no tags" stops being true this fall.** The **durable** gap is Smart Albums / saved rule-based queries on iPhone, hierarchical tags, and tag-driven smart albums that actually appear on the phone.

10. **IA regressions people paid to undo.** After the iOS 18 backlash and the iOS 26 tab restoration, still-open gaps: **you can collapse Collections but cannot exclude collection types you never want**; iCloud sync status now takes several taps; quick access to Screenshots/Videos is gone; Recent Days highlights are gone with no option to bring them back. **A paid third-party app (Photon Library, $5, Sept 2024) exists solely to restore the pre-iOS-18 feel** — priced, shipped evidence that users will pay to fix Apple's Photos IA.

**And the one thing you must not get wrong:** all of the above is worthless if the grid hitches. Apple's own bar is **< 5 ms/s hitch time ratio** on a **50,000-asset library**. Clear that first.
## 14. Competitive Landscape — The Real Bar

The field that matters is not "photo apps" in general — it is the small set of products that have already solved one or two of the four axes we need to hold simultaneously: **privacy/custody, search quality, sync reliability, and power features**. Ente holds privacy + on-device search. Immich holds search + power features. Google Photos holds search. Mylio holds the sync architecture. **Nobody holds all four**, and the reason is structural: whoever owns the compute owns the pixels. Our desktop-as-compute-node topology is the only one that gets server-class compute without surrendering custody, because the "server" is the user's own Mac on their own LAN.

The single most important thing to take from this section: **Ente already proved that the winning move is to sync the *derived intelligence* (embeddings, face clusters), not just the pixels** — index once on the fast machine, and every other device gets face recognition and semantic search for free. That idea maps 1:1 onto our architecture. Everything else here is either a vocabulary to steal (Mylio), a taxonomy to copy (Immich), or a failure to avoid (Google's Ask Photos retreat; every competitor's iOS background-backup story).

**Version baseline.** All comparisons are against **iOS/iPadOS 26.x — specifically iOS 26.5.2, the current shipping release as of 2026-07-14**. iOS 26.6 is in developer beta (5th beta seeded ~2026-07-13). iOS 27 is the next major release, expected ~fall 2026; press reports say its Photos adds Spatial Reframing, image expansion/straightening, and an improved Clean Up for larger distractions — **treat all iOS 27 Photos claims as unreleased and press-sourced; do not build against them.**

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The exact point-release string (26.5.2) is press-sourced (Macworld/MacRumors/Forbes), not fetched from developer.apple.com. Do not hard-code it; re-check before relying on it in a compatibility gate.

---

### 14.1 Ente — the closest thing to our thesis that already ships

Ente is an E2E-encrypted, open-source, self-hostable photo service whose entire intelligence layer runs **on-device**. It is simultaneously our closest competitor and our best blueprint.

**On-device ML stack (all via ONNX Runtime):**

| Stage | Model / method | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Face detection | **YOLO5Face** (small variant) + Non-Max Suppression | Ente's own docs spell it **YOLO5Face** — use their spelling when citing them |
| Face alignment | Custom **similarity-transformation** step | Neutralizes positional noise before embedding |
| Face embedding | **MobileFaceNet** | Also records quality metrics (blurriness, positioning) |
| Face clustering | Custom **"linear incremental clustering"** | Groups faces chronologically, folds in face-quality metrics |
| Semantic search | **Apple's MobileCLIP** (dual image/text encoders → shared embedding space) | Ente's docs say "Apple's MobileCLIP" with **no version number** |
| Runtime | **ONNX format + ONNX Runtime** | ONNX Runtime has a CoreML execution provider on iOS |

Query path for Magic Search: encode the text prompt with the text encoder on-device → pull **all** image embeddings from the local DB → rank by cosine similarity. Ente documents that "once your photos have been indexed, both face recognition and magic search work completely offline." Temperature, battery, and connectivity safeguards throttle indexing. **ML is OFF by default** and must be enabled at Settings > Machine learning.

**The killer idea — E2E-encrypted sync of DERIVED indexes.** Ente does not merely sync photos; it syncs the *products of local inference*:
- Image and face embeddings are **compressed losslessly and encrypted with the file key**, then sent to object storage.
- **"Person" entities** (the cluster→name mapping) are compressed, encrypted, and stored in the central DB.
- Once *one* device has indexed a photo, every other device gets the index without re-running the models. Ente calls this "a unique approach… to take away common friction points of on-device ML," and states results are "exactly the same across platforms."
- Two independent toggles: **Machine learning** and **Local indexing**. Mobile path: Settings > Machine learning. Desktop path: Settings > Preferences > Machine learning.
- **"ML Lite"** is a real named mode for older/low-RAM devices: it *does not index locally* but *can still use existing (synced) results*.

**Face-curation UX vocabulary (worth copying wholesale):** "Add a name" banner on unnamed groups; **merge by tapping the existing name from the list** (not retyping); **de-merge** via *Review suggestions > History icon > minus icon*; **remove a wrongly-attributed face** via *open person > three-dots overflow > Edit > long-press the wrong photos > Remove*; **Ignore person** on unnamed groupings (restorable via *file info > tap face thumbnail > "Show person"*); **long-press > "Use as cover."** And the one that matters most to us: a **mixed grouping** option for **babies and toddlers**, because "faces change rapidly at that age" — it re-evaluates the cluster with stricter settings.

**Surface availability (corrected — the researcher's original table was wrong):**

| Surface | Mobile (iOS/Android) | Desktop (Mac/Win/Linux) | Web (photos.ente.com) |
|---|---|---|---|
| ML indexing | Yes | Yes | **No ML at all** |
| Magic Search | Yes | Yes | No (metadata search only) |
| View people | Yes | Yes | No |
| **Name + merge persons** | Yes | **Yes** | No |
| Remove face from cluster | Yes | **No** | No |
| "Use as cover" | Yes | **No** | No |
| Mixed grouping (babies) | Yes | **No** | No |

> ⚠️ **Trap:** A widely-repeated claim is that Ente desktop is "view-only" for People. **That is false.** Desktop supports viewing, **naming, and merging**. What desktop lacks is remove-face, "Use as cover," and the mixed-grouping re-evaluation. The real critique is narrower but still true: *the device that indexes fastest is not the device that can do the finest-grained correction.* We should make full cluster curation available on **every** surface.

**Other Ente surfaces:** date search, filename search, description/caption search, album search, **settings search** ("Find settings by searching for their names"), **Map view**, **Location tags** (user-defined custom named places — an inversion of Apple's opaque reverse-geocoding), **Memories** (same date across years), **Memory Lane** (a timeline of *one person* across years), **People**, **Places**.

**Commercial/privacy model:** E2EE with **XChaCha20/XSalsa20 + Poly1305 + Argon2id**; encrypted on-device before upload. Open-source apps on iOS, Android, web, desktop. Self-hostable — the Go server is called **"museum"**, one `docker compose up`. Free plan: **10 GB permanently**, unlimited devices, and it includes map view, face recognition, magic search, shared albums, public links, and background sync. Paid tiers 50 GB → multi-TB. **Family plan: invite 5 (6 total)**, each member gets a private space, admin sets per-member storage caps via the edit icon in the Members List, **storage is shared, not stacked**.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** "The only free-tier restriction is no family plan" is *not quite true* — Ente also deletes a free account with no paid subscription after **12 consecutive months of inactivity** (with prior email warnings). Do not repeat the "only restriction" line in comparison material.

**Ente's published weaknesses = our opening:**
- Mobile indexing is **slow** on large libraries; no progress notifications.
- Face detection/grouping quality is criticized as "pretty lacking," with misrecognitions discouraging users from sharing people-albums. (Note: these complaints come from **forums and comparison blogs, not from Ente** — they are real signals but not rigorously measured. Benchmark Ente's clustering against our pipeline before making any competitive claim.)
- On 4–6 GB-RAM phones, indexing degrades app performance — **Ente's own advice is to disable local indexing on mobile and let the desktop do it.** That is literally our architecture, arrived at by them as a workaround rather than a design.
- Magic Search requires **downloading originals to the device to index** — heavy on cellular; Ente recommends Wi-Fi.
- **No OCR / Live-Text-grade instant text extraction** while viewing a photo. Users have explicitly asked for an Apple-Live-Text equivalent.
- **No pet recognition** documented.

**The strategic trap Ente accepts:** because their server cannot read pixels, there is **no server-side ML upgrade path by design**. Our desktop-node model escapes exactly this trap.

---

### 14.2 Immich — the reference architecture for server + mobile client

Immich is the self-hosted incumbent and the closest structural prior art to our desktop-compute-node design.

**Architecture:** A **NestJS** API/web server, a **separate Python FastAPI machine-learning service**, **PostgreSQL + the VectorChord extension** (pgvector-family) for vectors, **Valkey** (Redis-compatible) for cache/queues, a **Flutter** mobile client, and a **SvelteKit** web client. **v3.0.0 released July 1, 2026.**

Isolating the ML service from the API server is the key structural decision: the heavy model process can crash, restart, or move to a GPU box without taking the library server down. Note that the ML service is the **single ML chokepoint** — it hosts not just CLIP but also **face detection (InsightFace)**, **OCR (RapidOCR)**, and **duplicate detection** — which is precisely why it can be GPU-scaled independently.

> **Important, do not misreport:** **Immich does NOT run ML on the mobile device.** Its CLIP/SigLIP embeddings, face detection, and OCR all run **server-side** in the Python ML service. The Flutter client is a thin consumer. Anyone claiming Immich does on-device mobile ML is wrong.

**Smart Search — user-swappable models.** Paste a model name into *Administration > Settings > Machine Learning Settings > Smart Search*, save, then go to **Job Status** and click **"All"** next to Smart Search to re-embed the library. Naming convention: `ViT-[SIZE]-[VARIANT]__[TRAINING_DATA]` — e.g. `ViT-B-16-SigLIP__webli`, `ViT-L-14__laion2b-s32b-b82k`, `RN50__openai`.

Two documented multilingual families with **different semantics**:
- **`nllb`** models expect the query **in the language set in user settings** — best for a single-language user.
- **`xlm`** and **`siglip2`** models understand the query **regardless of the language setting** — best for language-switchers.

Hardware-acceleration backends: **CUDA** (NVIDIA, compute 5.2+), **ROCm** (AMD), **OpenVINO** (Intel Iris Xe/Arc), **ARM NN** (Mali), **RKNN** (Rockchip RK3566/3568/3576/3588). **CoreML is NOT among the supported backends.** Docs warn some models are incompatible with some backends (e.g. "search latency isn't improved by ARM NN due to model compatibility issues"), and bigger models mean better results but slower inference and more server RAM — an unmanaged tradeoff dumped on the user.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Immich's **default** Smart Search model is **not named in the official docs** — they only say "the default search model is fast." A community discussion says ViT-B/32; `ViT-B-16-SigLIP__webli` appears in the docs **only as an example** of how to change models. **Do not quote a default model name as fact.**

**Search filter taxonomy — the most complete in the category, and a good spec to copy wholesale:** People (recognized faces) · Contextual/content (CLIP) · File name or extension · Full path or folder (searching "Projects" matches `/John/Projects/3D_Printing/...`) · Description · **OCR — text appearing in images** · Locations (geocoded) · Tags · Camera make/model/lens · Time frame · Media type · Display options (archive / favorites / albums) · **Star rating**. A separate **Duplicates Utility** handles dedupe. Server-side OCR *search* predates v3.0.0; what v3.0.0 added on **mobile** is interactive OCR text **highlighting, selection, and copying** in the asset viewer.

**Mobile backup mechanics:** pick which device albums to back up; **double-tapping an album EXCLUDES it** (explicitly necessary because on iOS one asset can live in several albums). One-way "sync/mirror device albums to server albums." **"Reorganize into album"** backfills already-uploaded assets. Uploads are **Wi-Fi-only by default** (configurable). **Dedupe is by checksum**, computed at album-selection time, so an asset already on the server via CLI, web, or another device is not re-uploaded.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Immich's checksum dedupe is **per-library and exists only for UPLOAD libraries** — external libraries are **not** deduped against uploads. If you copy the model, do not assume it gives you global dedupe.

**The iOS backup failure mode.** The foreground uploader runs while the app is open; the background worker only starts once the app is backgrounded, and **"foreground and background backup are separate mechanisms that do not hand off."** Android got a new **periodic task scheduler** in v3.0.0 that respects Android background-execution limits, warns when battery optimization will break backups, offers charging-only mode, and a configurable minimum delay between capture and upload. iOS requires **Background App Refresh** and Low Power Mode off; v3.0.0 now runs sync and upload tasks **in parallel** during the short iOS background window. Also on iOS: **iCloud assets in local albums must be materialized and temporarily cached during hashing/upload**, which can require a lot of free space on a large library.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The much-quoted line *"iOS app stops uploading photos when app is closed (no reliable background sync)"* is **not from Immich's documentation** — it reads like a GitHub issue title and should not be cited as an Immich statement. What Immich's FAQ actually says is: *"On iOS… the operating system determines if a particular app can invoke background tasks based on multiple factors, most of which the Immich app has no control over."* **Immich absolutely does attempt background upload; it is unreliable, not absent.**

**Workflows (v3.0.0, preview, web-only).** A library-automation engine at **Utilities > Workflows**: chain a **trigger** with a sequence of **steps** made of **Filters** (conditions) and **Actions** (effects). **Drag-and-drop visual builder OR a JSON editor.** Ships with **premade templates**. Workflows are shareable as text/JSON via a copy button or a **"Show schema"** context-menu item. Explicitly in preview; the team is soliciting feedback on which triggers and actions to add.

**External Libraries.** Track assets that live outside Immich's upload directory — they appear in the timeline, on the map, in albums, with full functionality, without being copied. Multiple **import paths** per library, scanned **recursively**; *"If a file is in multiple import paths, it will only be added once."* Read-only is enforced at the Docker volume level (`:ro`), which blocks deletion via the UI and blocks XMP sidecar writes. **Exclusion patterns are globs**: `**/*.tif`, `**/Raw/**`; special chars need escaping (`**/\@eaDir/**` for Synology). Files deleted from disk go to trash on rescan and are purged after **30 days**. Experimental **automatic file watching** exists but Immich's own docs say: *"If your photos are on a network drive, automatic file watching likely won't work… you will have to rely on a periodic library refresh."* Watching is flagged experimental, can hang startup, and `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` limits bite on large libraries.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** **Do not build a LAN import story on FSEvents/inotify over SMB/NFS.** Immich confirms it fails. Use content-addressed **periodic rescan with checksums**.

**Sharing.** **Partner sharing is explicitly one-way** — to see your partner's assets they must also share with you (a deliberate consent design; symmetric sharing must be set up twice). Partner-shared photos can be merged into your main timeline, toggleable per-partner. **Album roles**: **editor** (read-write) or **viewer** (read-only). **Public links** for an album or an ad-hoc selection, with **expiration date, password protection, a custom slug, and an allow/disallow-downloads option.**

Immich documents an honest limitation: *"Partner sharing may result in displaying duplicate assets on the main timeline, as duplicates are only detected on a per-user basis."* **Cross-user dedupe in a merged timeline is a real, unsolved problem.**

**Other v3.0.0 items (July 1, 2026):** **mobile non-destructive editing** (same editor as web — crop, rotate, adjust — start on mobile, refine on web, implying the edit recipe is a *synced object*, not baked pixels); **HLS / real-time video transcoding** (preview, **web-only**, mobile in development, GPU recommended); **integrity checks** (untracked files, missing files, checksum mismatches — surfaced on a **Maintenance page** and **schedulable**, e.g. nightly); slideshow; upload straight to an album from the asset sheet; adjustable image quality when sharing; browse recently-added by import date; Android "Open with" gallery integration; custom web video player; timeline rendering optimizations.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The new v3.0.0 mobile editor **DROPPED** capabilities that existed before: **recoloring, Live Photo editing, and editing of local (not-yet-uploaded) assets**. v3.0.0 also carries **numerous breaking API changes and env-var deprecations** that strand third-party integrations. A "rewrite the editor" migration is a real regression risk — plan for feature parity, not just a new UI.

**Immich's trust problem:** the README carries a prominent **"⚠️ Always follow 3-2-1 backup plan"** warning — Immich explicitly does *not* position itself as a backup solution, which erodes trust for the core use case. And metadata added *inside* Immich (albums, descriptions) is **not written back to the file**: *"that metadata is only stored inside Immich and will not be persisted to the external asset file."* That is a lock-in smell users notice.

---

### 14.3 Mylio Photos — the direct blueprint for LAN sync without a cloud

Mylio's defining feature is **peer-to-peer device-to-device sync**: *"Peer-to-peer connections do not rely on an external platform like the Cloud to transfer files. Instead, your devices can talk to each other directly over a network."* Full speed on a LAN; also works over the internet if devices can reach each other.

**The three requirements** (all of which we must replicate or improve on):
1. All devices logged into the same Mylio account.
2. All devices on the same network **or** mutually reachable over the internet.
3. All devices running the Mylio Photos+ app — **and on mobile the app must be in the FOREGROUND.**

> ⚠️ **Trap — and this is the single most instructive failure in the entire landscape:** **Mylio's own support docs state that background syncing is not available on mobile and the app "must be running in the foreground on mobile devices for syncing to occur."** The phone only syncs while you are staring at it. Settings expose a **Background Launch** toggle (launch Mylio in the background when logged in) and **Prevent sleep when active** (don't sleep while importing/syncing) — telling us they are *fighting the OS with workarounds*. An **Unlimited Syncing** toggle governs cellular: when off, cellular is limited to fetching previews and on-demand originals, with minimal background syncing.

**The representation ladder — adopt this data model almost verbatim:**

| Tier | Size | Editable? | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Original** | 100% | Fully — best for editing and export | The master file at native resolution |
| **Optimized** | **< 5%** of Original (Mylio says "<5%", *not* "approximately 5%") | **Yes — "remain fully editable"** | A medium-quality version. **This is the subtle, essential bit: a phone can do real work without ever pulling a 50 MB RAW.** |
| **Thumbnail** | "minimal storage" (< 1% per the researcher; Mylio's glossary says "minimal") | **No — does not support editing** | Library reference / browsing |

The **Catalog** is *"the database file that stores information about your Mylio Photos Library, including metadata and sync data. Each device running Mylio Photos maintains its own copy of the Catalog."* Edits, keywords, labels, and locations are written to **XMP sidecar files**. Because the Catalog + thumbnails sync to **every** device, a 64 GB phone can meaningfully "contain" a 4 TB library: it holds the catalog and thumbnails, some optimized copies, and reaches for originals on demand.

**Device Sync Policy presets — the best storage-policy vocabulary in the industry:**

| Preset | What it stores on that device |
|---|---|
| **Catalog Only** | Only low-resolution thumbnails and metadata; minimal storage |
| **Everything** | A full copy of the entire library — all original-quality photos, videos, and documents |
| **Highest Rated** | "Your top-rated media in original quality only" |
| **Optimized Images** | Optimized versions of all photos; videos and documents on demand |
| **Photos Only** | Original-quality photos; no videos/documents locally |
| **SpaceSaver** | "Optimizes available space by storing as many optimized-quality photos as possible alongside thumbnails and metadata" — docs describe it as "ideal for general use on devices with limited storage" |
| **Travel Backup** | Catalog Only base **+ originals from the past three months**; older on demand |
| **Vault** | A complete, original-quality copy of the entire library. **Mylio recommends running at least two Vaults for redundancy.** |

> ⚠️ **Trap:** Two commonly-repeated Mylio "facts" do **not** hold up.
> 1. **SpaceSaver being "the default" is low-confidence** — Mylio's docs describe it as *ideal for general use*, not as the default. Don't state it as fact.
> 2. **"Highest Rated = 4–5 star / Pick-flagged"** is *not* in Mylio's docs — they say only "your top-rated media in original quality only."

**Sync on Demand + Tap to Sync.** **Sync on Demand** (toggled at *More Menu > Settings > Sync*) lets a device that only holds thumbnails temporarily fetch a higher-resolution **optimized** image from a peer — your primary computer, an external drive, a cloud service, or Mylio Drive — in order to edit or share it. The documented offline fallback is **Tap to Sync**: *"If you anticipate being away from access to a device with optimized images or without an internet connection, consider using Tap to Sync to sync specific folders ahead of time."* Tap to Sync is richer than it sounds: once enabled, **each folder shows a T/P/O/A/٭ badge you tap to change that folder's sync policy on the current device.** Applying a new device preset over legacy per-folder policies surfaces an asterisk and a **"Clear Legacy Folder Policies"** escape hatch — a documented mess that warns us about **letting two policy layers fight.**

**Observability.** Mylio's **Sync Panel** exists at *Info Panel > Sync tab* and shows **connected devices and current sync activity**. Separately, a **Storage Panel** carries the colored storage bars.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** A widely-circulated spec of Mylio's Sync Panel — *per-tier × per-device green/yellow/gray bars, live upload/download speeds, a numeric "files waiting to sync" count, a Vault shield badge, a Preview-Device circle badge, and an explicit "Original Status" view* — **is not what Mylio actually ships.** It is a good design proposal, but it is **not observed prior art.** If you build it, build it as *our* design; do not tell anyone Mylio already did it.

**The "no cloud" purity framing is also softer than advertised:** current Mylio Photos+ subscriptions **bundle "Mylio Drive" cloud storage for OPTIMIZED copies**, and Sync on Demand explicitly lists a cloud service / Mylio Drive as one of the sources it can pull optimized images from. **Cloud is optional in Mylio, not absent.**

> ⚠️ **Trap:** **Mylio's price is unverifiable.** Sources disagree wildly ($9.99/mo, $99/yr, $119/yr, $240/yr, $20/mo/user) and no authoritative current price page could be sourced. **Do not quote a Mylio price to anyone**, including in competitive marketing.

Mylio's other well-known weakness: the concept is powerful but **the UI is notoriously dense; the learning curve is its most-cited flaw.**

### 14.4 Google Photos — the search bar to clear, and a very public retreat

**Ask Photos (Gemini conversational search).** Natural-language, multi-turn search over your library: *"What did I eat on my trip to Barcelona?"*, *"Photos that'd make great phone backgrounds"*, *"What are all the cities I visited last year?"*, *"Photos of me over time."* When opted in, **the Search tab is renamed "Ask."** Voice input via a microphone icon (voice recordings are not stored). Responses show progress states — **"Thinking," "Searching," "Reviewing"** — and results split into a **"Best match"** section (tap the preview's plus sign for all) plus reverse-chronological results below. Thumbs up/down feedback with optional detail.

Runs on **Gemini models, cloud-side**, and works **only on photos that are backed up**.

**Gating (heavy):** 18+ · located in a launched region · a supported language · **Face Groups enabled with your own face selected** · **location estimates enabled** · photos backed up. Labeled "an experimental feature from Google Labs" that "may give unexpected or inaccurate results." Available on Android, iOS, and web for eligible users.

> **The most important gating detail:** Ask Photos is **blocked at US STATE level — it is missing in Illinois and Texas**, reportedly because Google's face grouping does not satisfy those states' **biometric-privacy laws**. This is direct evidence that **face-grouping consent law is the gating dependency for any conversational-photos feature.** Anyone shipping face recognition in the US needs to know this before it becomes a legal surprise.

**The retreat — the most valuable single data point in this section.** Google PM Jamie Aspinall publicly acknowledged Ask Photos "wasn't meeting quality and performance standards" and the rollout was **paused (summer 2025)**. Users complained it "still failed to find some of their photos," was "less accurate than before," and slower. **On March 10, 2026, Google shipped a toggle on the Search screen to turn Ask Photos OFF and get classic results back.** Google also folded classic search back in: classic results now appear **immediately** while *"Gemini models continue to work in the background to narrow down the results set."*

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The exact UI label of that March 2026 toggle **could not be sourced.** Do not invent one.

**What Google's retreat proves — the architecture to copy:** run the **fast deterministic retrieval first, render immediately**, then let the slow model refine **in place**. Results must be instant for simple queries ("beach", "dog"), must **never be worse than lexical/classic search**, and must **degrade gracefully**. **Never block a one-word query on an LLM.** And **build the escape hatch** — a toggle back to classic — from day one.

**Gemini privacy hub — the marketing gift.** Google documents that it processes: your photos, videos, **face group labels/names**, location data, and account info. It explicitly makes inferences — *"guessing the age and locations of your top face groups."* The face-group data Ask Photos consumes also includes user-supplied facts from a **"Remember List"** — e.g. a person's **birth month/year or gender** — i.e. **Google ships a user-editable personal-context memory attached to people.** (That is a genuinely good feature idea *and* a privacy liability, depending on where it runs.)

Human review: *"Human reviewers don't review Ask Photos responses, unless you give feedback, or in rare cases to address abuse or harm"*; before human review, queries are disconnected from the account and sensitive content is removed. Opt-out path: **Settings > Preferences > Gemini features in Photos > "Your Ask Photos Activity."** Documented criticism: **no E2EE; Google can read backed-up photos including Locked Folder content**; "a Google One subscription only gives users more storage — not stronger boundaries around their data."

**Magic Editor / Magic Eraser / Reimagine / Auto Frame / Photo Unblur.** In the editor, **tap, circle, or brush** an area and you get **Erase**, **Move**, and **Reimagine**. **Reimagine** = generative fill from a text prompt. **Magic Eraser** removes photobombers/distractions. **Auto Frame** (generative outpainting/recompose) lives **inside the Crop interface in the Actions toolbar**. **Photo Unblur** sharpens blurry shots. All cloud-executed. The **"circle the thing you want to change"** gesture is the standout interaction — it collapses selection and intent into one motion.

> ⚠️ **Trap — this one will burn you if you get it wrong:** The "free to all Android + iOS users, rolling out starting **May 15**, free users get **10 Magic Editor saves per month**, beyond that requires a Pixel or Premium Google One" announcement is from **Google's blog post of April 10, 2024 — it is two years old, not a 2026 development.** "Premium Google One" means the **2 TB-and-above** tiers specifically. There are also **minimum device requirements**: **≥3 GB RAM and Android 8.0 / iOS 15 or higher** (or Chromebook Plus, ChromeOS 118+). Do not present this as current news.

Also worth stealing and almost universally overlooked: the Google Photos **editor was redesigned in mid-2025** with a bottom carousel — **Auto, Actions, Markup, Filters, Lighting, Color** — plus an **in-editor SEARCH BAR for finding an AI tool by name.** Search-inside-the-editor is arguably the most stealable thing on this surface.

**The contextual "Ask" button in the single-image viewer.** A per-photo **Ask** affordance turns one photo into the start of a Gemini conversation — ask about its content or location, or **request edits in natural language** ("describe the edits you want and watch the changes appear in seconds"). It also **transcribes text from screenshots and handwritten notes and can reformat it** (e.g. a photographed recipe into a grocery list) — i.e. it is an **OCR-to-structured-output surface**, not only an editing surface. Rolling out to eligible users on **Android and iOS in the U.S.** *(The exact button label — e.g. "Help me edit" — could not be confirmed; treat labels as unverified.)*

This is the concrete shape of a "private Ask Photos": **not a search box — an object-level conversation.**

**Free-form organization.** Navigation is a **floating pill bar** with three destinations — **Photos**, **Collections**, **Create** — plus a **circular floating element** for search / Ask Photos. **Collections** (renamed from "Library," announced **Aug 2024**) is the filing cabinet: online albums, local folders, and categorized documents in one place. Documented Collections contents: **Favorites, Albums, Documents, Archive, Locked Folder, People & Pets, Places, Videos, and "Recently added."** **Photo stacks** automatically group duplicates and near-identical shots (backed-up photos only; manual stacking also supported). Albums are pointers, not moves — a photo can be in many albums with no file duplication.

The **floating pill bar shipped on iOS in February 2026** and only reached Android widely in **July 2026 (Photos v7.82)** — **Google now ships some UI to iOS FIRST.** (Amazon did the same thing in May 2026; see 14.7. This is now an industry pattern, not a Google quirk.)

> ⚠️ **Trap #1 (REFUTED claim):** "As of 2026, Locked Folder content backs up to the cloud (originally it did not)" is **wrong by ~2.5 years.** Google announced **Locked Folder cloud backup on August 29, 2023**, together with Locked Folder coming to iOS and the web. Getting this wrong would badly misprice how novel the capability is. The *design* lesson still stands: **any "private/hidden" vault we build MUST be included in backup/sync from day one** — Locked Folder originally had no backup, and a broken phone meant permanent loss. But note Google's version is now the worst of both worlds: **backed up, and still readable by Google.**
>
> ⚠️ **Trap #2 (UNVERIFIED):** The specific quick-access pill set "**Favorites, Trash, Screenshots, Archive** rotating based on what you use most" is **unsourced.** Use the documented Collections contents list above instead.

**Backup quality tiers** (the cloud analogue of Mylio's ladder):

| Tier | Photos | Video |
|---|---|---|
| **Original quality** | Full res, counts fully against quota | Full res |
| **Storage saver** | Anything above **16 MP** resized to 16 MP | **Anything above 1080p resized to 1080p** (commonly omitted!) |
| **Express** | ~**3 MP** | **480p** |

Retroactive conversion is real and has an exact path: **Settings > Manage storage > "Recover storage" > "Convert existing photos & videos to Storage saver."** Two documented constraints: **you can only recover storage once a day**, and **it does not change the quality of future uploads.** Google's help page also states that **changing from Express back to Storage saver or Original causes a re-upload of existing photos/videos from the device.** iOS settings path: *Google Photos → profile icon (top-right) → Photos settings → Backup → Preferences → Photo and video quality.*

> ⚠️ **Trap:** "Original quality is the default" is supported only by **secondary sources** — Google's own help page does not state a default. **Mark low-confidence.**

**OCR / text-in-image search.** Google indexes text inside images and lets you search it — signs, receipts, documents, screenshots, and (imperfectly) handwriting. Handwriting works only when neat; printed/typed text is materially more reliable. The interactive extraction layer is **Google Lens**; the user-facing action label is **"Copy text from image."** Long-standing complaint: **Google's OCR historically did not retroactively apply to older photos** in a library.

### 14.5 PhotoPrism — the anti-pattern that defines the market gap

**No native iOS or Android app.** PhotoPrism's own docs: *"PhotoPrism currently does not include a native app that can be installed through an app store."* The mobile experience is a **Progressive Web App** (open in Safari/Chrome → "Add to Home Screen"; installing requires **HTTPS on a dedicated domain**). Phone backup is **delegated**: **WebDAV** for direct file operations, with **PhotoSync** (a third-party app) as the recommended iOS/Android backup client.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The jab that PhotoPrism "can't even try" at background backup is **rhetoric, not fact.** PhotoPrism's docs specifically say **PhotoSync can "securely backup iOS and Android phones IN THE BACKGROUND."** The delegated path *does* attempt background upload. The real cost is that users must run a **second, separate, paid app** to get photos in — and the PWA itself cannot observe the photo library, cannot pair Live Photos, and gets storage-evicted by iOS.

**ML stack.** TensorFlow runs locally **on CPU (no GPU required)** for automatic object/scene **labels** plus **facial recognition** ("lets you find pictures of your family and friends"); faces are grouped by similarity for you to match to people. Supports **custom TensorFlow models**. Newer releases integrate directly with **Ollama** and **OpenAI** to generate **captions and labels** — a VLM as a *bulk metadata generator*, with **Ollama meaning it can run fully local/on-prem**.

**Organization/library features.** Top-notch RAW support across camera makes/models. **FFmpeg**-based on-demand video transcoding to MPEG-4 AVC. **Places** — six high-resolution interactive maps with reverse geocoding. **Moments** — browse by temporal grouping. **Duplicate detection** (exact duplicates skipped at index) and **automatic stacking by identifier / filename / time-location** — a clean, cheap heuristic for RAW+JPEG pairs and burst runs **that needs no perceptual hashing.** **Private** and **Archive** states hide content from search results. Album sharing via **secret links** with optional expiration.

> ⚠️ **Trap (paywall corrections):** The **AI caption generation via Ollama/OpenAI** and **AI custom-label generation** are **Plus/Pro membership-gated** — as are security hardening, session monitoring, 2FA/app passwords, custom rate limits, and **SSO (OpenID Connect)**. **NSFW detection is also membership-gated** (directly relevant to our Safe Mode work). And the **roles claim is wrong as usually stated**: the full five-role model (Super Admin, Admin, User, Viewer, Guest) **plus the admin web UI for user management is a Plus/Pro capability** — the free Community edition's role support is limited to **Super Admin / Admin / Guest**. Do not tell anyone fine-grained multi-user roles are free in PhotoPrism.

**Why this matters to us:** PhotoPrism has arguably the strongest **server-side** organization/AI feature set of the self-hosted trio, and it **still loses to Immich because it has no real mobile client.** **Mobile-native + reliable background backup is the moat — not the model.**

### 14.6 Synology Photos — rule-driven albums, on mobile, today

All recognition runs **on the NAS**. Auto-generated albums grouped by facial recognition, geolocation, tags, file types, and upload date. The **six auto-albums** are: **People, Subjects, Places, Tags, Videos, Recently Added.** **Subject** (object) recognition lets users remove wrongly-recognized photos and hide subject categories. **People** albums support naming and merging.

**The standout feature is conditional albums:** set conditions at album-creation time — **featured person, object, location, even the camera lens used** — and the album auto-populates. **This is essentially Apple's Mac-only Smart Albums, but on mobile, and driven by ML outputs.** Neither Apple's iOS Photos nor Google Photos offers this.

Synology also exposes a far richer EXIF predicate surface than it gets credit for — **Quick Filters** on: **File type · Date taken · People · Geolocation · Tag · Rating · Camera · Lens · Focal length · Exposure time · Aperture · ISO.**

**Gating.** Object recognition requires **Synology Photos 1.5.0+ and DSM 7.2+**. Face and object recognition are *"only supported on certain models"* — Synology maintains a KB listing which NAS models qualify. *(The specific model list could not be verified — the gating itself is confirmed by Synology's own spec page.)* **This is a nasty capability cliff: recognition silently unavailable on cheaper hardware.** Also: GIF, WebP, and 360° photos can't be manually face-tagged; HEIC/HEIF and many video formats need Synology Image Assistant / Advanced Media Extensions.

**Mobile.** Requires **iOS 16.0+ / Android 10+**. Supports timeline and folder browsing with **offline access to previously viewed photos**, **photo stacking** (Timeline and Album views), map-based **Places** albums, and slideshows with **Chromecast/AirPlay casting** (AirPlay iOS only).

**Backup and deletion mechanics worth copying:**
- **Customizable backup destination path** — *with the iOS caveat that default backup folders are named generically ("iPhone"/"iPad") because of Apple's privacy restrictions on device names.*
- **Free Up Space** (path: **More > Free Up Space**) — selective local deletion to reclaim phone storage.
- **Delete-scope disambiguation**: when deleting in the app you choose the scope — **delete on both NAS and phone, or NAS only.** iOS additionally requires local-deletion permission. **Every photo app that mirrors a phone eventually faces "did you mean delete from phone, from library, or both?" — Synology handles it explicitly. Copy this.**

> ⚠️ **Trap:** The commonly-cited Free-Up-Space filter list — "time range, file size, and **device**" — is **wrong.** Synology documents the filters as **time range, file size, FOLDER (Android), and FAVORITES (iOS)**. **The filters are platform-asymmetric** — exactly the kind of detail an implementer copies incorrectly.
>
> ⚠️ **Trap:** The claim that "Synology tells iOS users to plug in a charger and enable notifications" for backup **could not be sourced.** Do not cite it.

### 14.7 Amazon Photos — the commercial idea, not the technical one

**Prime members get unlimited full-resolution photo storage plus 5 GB of video storage.** **Family Vault**: a Prime member invites **up to 5 others**, and **each invited member receives the same unlimited-photos + 5 GB video benefit at no extra cost** (only the creator needs Prime); everyone can contribute to / view / download from the shared vault. **Groups**: share full-res photos/videos or entire albums with **up to 50 people** — but Groups confer **no free storage**.

**Family Vault is the sharpest commercial idea in the space:** the value to the *inviter* is a shared family library; the value to the *invitee* is free unlimited personal storage. **The sharing feature IS the acquisition channel.** (Ente's family plan has the same shape — a shared space where each member also keeps a private space. That is clearly the right family model.)

**Search:** cloud-side natural-language search ("beach sunset last summer", "kids playing in the snow") plus face, place, and object recognition. Generally rated a tier below Google in accuracy.

**The May 5, 2026 redesign — shipped on iOS FIRST, with Android "coming soon."** It replaced the static grid with a **curated Memories CAROUSEL at the top of the screen**, surfaced **"On This Day"** inside that carousel, added a **floating navigation bar** (the same convergent pattern as Google Photos), and added **Alexa controls.**

**The tell:** the **5 GB video cap** is very low for modern 4K/ProRes. Unlimited photos is a loss-leader; **video is where the cost is.** For a local-first product, "unlimited" is free for us — say so loudly. Amazon's incentive is Prime retention, not photo-app excellence, so the app has historically been under-invested.

### 14.8 Adobe Lightroom mobile — the pro-editing bar, and two sleeper UX ideas

**Generative and repair tools:** **Generative Remove** (Adobe Firefly) — remove road signs, power lines, complex objects with realistic generative fill; available on **Lightroom for mobile (iOS and Android)**. **Distraction Removal**, including **People Distraction Removal**. **Reflection Removal** — eliminate window/glass reflections. **Denoise**, **Raw Details**, and **Super Resolution** now live under a **Detail** section in the Edit panel, are **non-destructive**, and no longer force a separate DNG.

**Selection craft worth stealing:** with the **Detect objects** tool you *"loosely circle or scribble over the object… Lightroom will automatically detect the object, shadow or reflection around it, and mask it."* **Automatically extending a selection to include an object's shadow or reflection** is a small touch that reads as craft.

**Sleeper idea #1 — "AI Edit Status."** A dedicated button (present across Camera Raw, Lightroom desktop, Lightroom Classic, **Lightroom mobile**, and web) that **lists which AI tools were applied**, shows a **dotted yellow highlight when settings need updating**, and updates them **in a recommended top-down order ("Update All")**. It exists precisely because generative edits are **slow, expensive, non-deterministic, and version-dependent** — so they get an **explicit lifecycle surface (pending / applied / stale / re-syncable)** instead of pretending they're instant slider adjustments. **Any local generative feature we ship needs exactly this.** Note also that Adobe's newest generative features **consume generative credits** — the lifecycle UI and the metering are coupled.

**June 2026 addition worth noting:** **Reflection Removal now isolates reflections into a SEPARATE LAYER with opacity control** rather than merely hiding them — a genuinely good "reversible AI edit" pattern.

**Sleeper idea #2 — Assisted Culling with Face View.** Generally available as of 2026. Lightroom evaluates a shoot and proposes which frames to keep or reject based on focus, eye-open state, and similarity. **Face View** *"isolates each person in a photo and analyzes Eyes Open and Eye Sharpness"* — the two per-face scores are named **"Eyes open"** and **"Eyes sharpness"**, surfaced in a **Faces panel inside Assisted Culling Info.** **The model shows its work rather than handing down a verdict.** *(The "improved for shallow depth-of-field" claim is press-sourced, not from a dedicated Adobe doc — historically it over-rejected intentional background blur.)*

**Culling is the single most tedious job in photography and neither Apple nor Google does it.** The lesson from Lightroom's DoF over-rejection history: **a culling model MUST be conservative, reversible, and must never delete.**

**Lightroom's structural weakness:** subscription-gated; heavy cloud dependency for the best tools; and **Lightroom's cloud sync is separate from the OS photo library**, so it is a parallel silo rather than an enhancement of Photos. *(The free-vs-premium split for each individual tool is not fully verified — Adobe's mobile "What's new" and "Premium features" pages did not resolve.)*

---

### 14.9 Apple's own macOS Photos — the competitor inside the house

Apple documents its **own** biggest iOS organizational gaps. Every one of these is a free win for a third-party iOS app.

**Smart Albums (macOS only).** Created via **File > New Smart Album**, or hold the pointer over **Albums** in the sidebar and click the **Add button (+)** → **New Smart Album**. Each condition has three parts: a **category** menu (default "Photo"; also Title, Date, and more), a **relationship/operator** menu ("is" / "is not"), and a **criteria** menu (default "favorite"). Multiple conditions are joined by a **Match** menu set to **any** or **all**. Criteria include date taken, location, people, keywords, titles, camera, lens, and more.

Apple's guide states the limitation outright: **"Smart Albums that you create on your Mac don't appear in Photos on your iPhone or iPad."**

> ⚠️ **Trap (two label/sourcing corrections):**
> 1. It is the **Add button (+)**, not a "More button," in the Albums sidebar hover menu.
> 2. The non-sync claim is **correct in effect but weakly sourced** — it rests on Apple Support Communities plus the *absence* of any Smart Album UI in Apple's iOS Photos guide. iCloud Photos *does* store Smart Albums and syncs them **Mac→Mac**; they are simply not surfaced on iPhone/iPad, because they cannot be created there and they depend on metadata (titles, keywords) iOS has no UI for. Flag it as **"confirmed by absence + community sources,"** not as an explicit Apple statement.

**Keywords and Titles (macOS only; iOS gets only Caption).** On Mac, Photos supports **Titles**, **Captions**, and **Keywords** (Apple's guide section is literally "Add titles, captions, and more to photos and videos on Mac"). On iPhone/iPad, the **only** user-authored text metadata is **Add a Caption** (Photos → select image → swipe up / Info button → Add a Caption). **iOS exposes no keyword UI and no title UI.**

**The exploitable part is better than it first looks:** **keywords ARE synced to iOS via iCloud and DO surface in iOS search results — they simply cannot be viewed or edited there.** iOS users' keyword data **exists but is unreachable.** Captions sync both ways and display on iPhone/iPad.

**And iOS search cannot scope a field.** Confirmed: *"You can't limit the search for captions in iOS 26, so you get search results that have your search in titles, album names, locations, image text, objects, and so on."* There is **no batch metadata editing on iOS**, and **iPadOS is equally limited** (no keywords, titles, or Smart Albums).

**Multiple libraries, Export Unmodified Original, Export IPTC as XMP (all macOS only).**
- **Multiple libraries**: on Mac you can create additional photo libraries and switch between them (personal vs work) — *"photos don't have to be shared with iPhone and iPad."* **iOS supports exactly one library.**
- **File > Export > Export Unmodified Original** copies exactly what was imported, stripping all edits (crop, noise reduction, sharpening). **iOS has no equivalent.**
- The export dialog offers an **"Export IPTC as XMP"** checkbox that writes an **.xmp sidecar per exported file** carrying location, camera model, title, description, keywords, and copyright. **The useful part is the round-trip property: if the .xmp files stay alongside the images, they are re-imported and the metadata is restored — including into another Photos/iCloud library or a third-party manager.** That is the interoperability escape hatch iOS does not have.

Mac Photos also has more export and print capability and supports **third-party editing extensions**.

---

### 14.10 Cross-cutting — the iOS background-backup ceiling

Every competitor with a mobile client struggles here, and the temptation is to declare it a competitor oversight we can simply out-engineer. **Be careful: the honest version of this thesis is narrower than the marketing version.**

**What is actually confirmed:**
- **Mylio** — the strongest evidence. **Mylio's own support docs state background syncing is not available on mobile and the app "must be running in the foreground on mobile devices for syncing to occur."**
- **Immich** — background upload **is attempted but unreliable**. Immich's FAQ: *"On iOS… the operating system determines if a particular app can invoke background tasks based on multiple factors, most of which the Immich app has no control over."* Foreground and background uploaders **do not hand off**. Docs tell users to enable **Background App Refresh** and disable **Low Power Mode**.
- **PhotoPrism** — has no native app, but **delegates to PhotoSync, which explicitly backs up iOS in the background.**

**What is NOT confirmed and must not be repeated:**
> ⚠️ **Trap:** The quote *"iOS app stops uploading photos when app is closed (no reliable background sync)"* is **not from Immich's documentation** — it reads like a GitHub issue title. Citing it as an Immich doc statement is exactly the failure mode to avoid.
>
> ⚠️ **Trap:** *"Synology tells users to plug in a charger and enable notifications"* — **could not be sourced.**
>
> ⚠️ **Trap:** *"PhotoPrism can't even try"* — **false.** See PhotoSync above.

**The honest net.** The real constraint is **iOS's BGTaskScheduler budget, which throttles every third-party client equally.** It is an **OS-imposed ceiling, not a competitor oversight.** A first-party-quality background pipeline **is** a genuine differentiator — but you cannot simply out-engineer the OS, and promising you can is how you end up with the same angry forum threads.

**The primitives that actually work** (and what every competitor gets wrong is treating iOS backup as "an upload loop that needs to keep running"):

| Need | Correct iOS primitive |
|---|---|
| Detect new/changed assets | **PHPhotoLibraryChangeObserver** (library deltas) |
| Transfers that survive app termination | **URLSession with a background configuration** — transfers continue after termination; the app is relaunched on completion |
| Cheap periodic delta sweeps | **BGAppRefreshTask** |
| Long indexing/hashing work | **BGProcessingTask** (can require charging) |
| Idempotency across retries/duplicated transfers | **Checksum dedupe** (Immich already does this — copy it) |
| Peer discovery on LAN | **Network.framework / Bonjour** (NWListener / NWBrowser) |
| Originals, not renders | **PHAssetResource** |
| Rule-based albums | **PHFetchOptions + NSPredicate** over creationDate, mediaType, mediaSubtypes, isFavorite, burst, location |
| Non-destructive edit recipes | **PHAdjustmentData** |
| On-device OCR | **Vision — VNRecognizeTextRequest** (accurate, includes handwriting; Live Text is instant in the viewer) |
| Our ML | **ONNX Runtime (CoreML execution provider) / CoreML** — our existing FR + SigLIP engines |

Also required regardless of primitives: **resumable/chunked uploads** so a killed task loses nothing, and **Live Photo / HEIC pairing** so the asset arrives whole.

**And the part everyone under-invests in: the honest progress surface.** The aggregate complaint across every competitor is not "it failed" — it is **"it failed silently."** Infinite spinners with no progress numbers. Repeated "enable Background App Refresh" prompts when it *is* already enabled. Sync permanently stuck, requiring a force-quit. **Numeric, honest, per-tier progress is itself the feature.**

---

### 14.11 What each does better than Apple Photos

| Product | What it beats Apple at | How (mechanism) | Worth stealing? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Ente** | Cross-device ML without re-indexing | Embeddings + face-cluster "person" entities compressed, **encrypted with the file key**, synced E2EE; index once, use everywhere | **YES — this is the single best idea in the category.** Directly maps to our desktop-node model |
| **Ente** | Humane people-curation vocabulary | Add-name banner, merge-by-tapping-existing-name, de-merge via Review suggestions > History > minus, Ignore person, Use as cover, **mixed grouping for babies/toddlers** | **YES.** The babies case is *literally our cross-age FR differentiator* |
