| **Ente** | Offline semantic search with no account | MobileCLIP text encoder on-device → cosine similarity over local embeddings; works airplane-mode after indexing | **YES** — but our bar is sub-second latency; Ente's is slow |
| **Ente** | Portable, private *and* free-tier-usable | 10 GB free incl. FR + magic search + background sync; XChaCha20; self-hostable ("museum", one `docker compose up`) | Business-model reference, not a feature |
| **Immich** | Search filter taxonomy | People + CLIP + filename/ext + full path/folder + description + **OCR** + location + tags + camera/lens + timeframe + media type + display options + **star rating**, in one panel | **YES — copy the taxonomy wholesale.** iOS Photos cannot even scope a query to captions |
| **Immich** | Model swappability + explicit re-embed | `ViT-[SIZE]-[VARIANT]__[TRAINING_DATA]`; change model in Admin settings → **Job Status > "All"** to re-embed | **YES.** Forces good hygiene: **tag every embedding with model identity + version** |
| **Immich** | Library automation | **Workflows** (Utilities > Workflows): trigger → steps of Filters + Actions; **visual builder OR JSON editor**; premade templates; shareable JSON via "Show schema" | **YES.** Maps 1:1 onto our ~245-command backend; the JSON doubles as the agent contract |
| **Immich** | Trust surfaces | **Integrity checks** (untracked / missing / checksum-mismatch) on a schedulable Maintenance page; **checksum dedupe** across CLI/web/devices | **YES.** No consumer photo app offers this |
| **Immich** | In-place external libraries | Multiple recursive import paths, glob excludes, read-only via `:ro`, trash-on-missing, 30-day purge | **YES** (we already have referenced-import + excludes) |
| **Immich** | Sharing granularity | Editor/viewer album roles; public links with **expiry + password + custom slug + allow/disallow downloads**; explicitly one-way partner sharing | Yes, selectively |
| **Mylio** | Local-only multi-device sync | Peer-to-peer over LAN, identity-scoped device mesh, no third-party custody; optional encrypted **Mylio Drive** relay | **YES — the core architectural precedent** |
| **Mylio** | Storage-policy legibility | **Original / Optimized (<5%, still fully editable) / Thumbnail** ladder + always-synced **Catalog** (thumbs + XMP) + named device presets (Vault, SpaceSaver, Travel Backup, Catalog Only, Highest Rated, Everything, Photos Only, Optimized Images) | **YES — steal the ladder AND the preset names.** Best answer in the industry to "how do I express storage policy to a human" |
| **Mylio** | Reaching for what you don't have | **Sync on Demand** (fetch an optimized copy from a peer) + **Tap to Sync** (pre-download folders before going offline; per-folder **T/P/O/A/٭** badges) | **YES** |
| **Mylio** | Metadata portability | Edits/keywords/labels/locations written to **XMP sidecars** | **YES** — solves the lock-in problem Immich has |
| **Google Photos** | Search quality and conversational search | Cloud Gemini over backed-up photos; "Best match" + reverse-chron; Thinking/Searching/Reviewing states | Steal the **shape**, not the architecture — and steal the **retreat lesson** (fast results first, model refines in background) |
| **Google Photos** | Generative editing on mobile | Tap/circle/brush → **Erase / Move / Reimagine**; **Auto Frame** inside Crop; **Photo Unblur**; editor bottom carousel + **in-editor search bar for AI tools** | **YES: "circle to select"** and **"search for a tool by name inside the editor"** |
| **Google Photos** | Object-level conversation | Per-photo **"Ask"** button: answers questions, performs edits, **transcribes screenshots/handwriting and reformats it** (recipe → grocery list) | **YES — this is the concrete shape of a private "Ask Photos"** |
| **Google Photos** | Near-duplicate cleanliness | **Photo stacks** auto-collapse burst/near-identical runs | **YES.** Highest-ROI cleanliness feature in the category |
| **Google Photos** | Representation tiering | Original / Storage saver (>16 MP → 16 MP; **>1080p video → 1080p**) / Express (~3 MP, 480p) | Confirms Mylio's ladder from a second direction |
| **Google Photos** | Personal context memory | **"Remember List"** — user-supplied facts about a person (birth month/year, gender) feeding search | Good idea; **must run locally for us** |
| **PhotoPrism** | Bulk semantic metadata | **Ollama/OpenAI captioning** — a VLM as a bulk caption generator; captions then feed ordinary lexical search | **YES.** Auditable, editable, XMP-exportable, degrades gracefully, and better for multi-hop "Ask" reasoning than raw embeddings. (Note: Plus/Pro-gated in PhotoPrism) |
| **PhotoPrism** | Cheap stacking | Automatic stacking by **identifier / filename / time-location** — no perceptual hashing needed | **YES** — do this before reaching for pHash |
| **Synology** | **Rule-driven albums on MOBILE** | **Conditional albums**: featured person, object, location, **camera lens** — auto-populating | **YES — this is Apple's Mac-only Smart Albums, on the phone.** Ship it |
| **Synology** | EXIF predicate surface | Quick Filters: file type, date taken, people, geolocation, tag, rating, camera, lens, focal length, exposure time, aperture, ISO | **YES** |
| **Synology** | Delete-scope honesty | Explicit prompt: delete on **both NAS + phone**, or **NAS only** | **YES.** Every mirroring app needs this |
| **Synology** | Controllable space reclamation | **More > Free Up Space** filtered by time range, file size, folder (Android) / favorites (iOS) | **YES** — far better than Apple's opaque "Optimize iPhone Storage" |
| **Amazon Photos** | Family virality | **Family Vault**: invite 5, **each invitee also gets their own unlimited personal photo storage**; Groups up to 50 (no storage) | Steal the **shape** (shared space + private space per member) |
| **Lightroom** | Generative-edit lifecycle | **AI Edit Status**: lists applied AI tools, dotted-yellow "needs updating," recommended top-down "Update All" | **YES — mandatory for any local generative feature** |
| **Lightroom** | Explainable culling | **Assisted Culling** + **Face View**: per-person **"Eyes open"** and **"Eyes sharpness"** scores in a Faces panel | **YES — same shape as our Safe Mode pluggable-explainer framework** |
| **Lightroom** | Selection craft | **Detect objects** auto-extends the mask to the object's **shadow or reflection**; Reflection Removal isolates reflections into a **separate layer with opacity control** | Yes — reads as craft; the layer approach is the right "reversible AI edit" pattern |
| **Apple's own macOS Photos** | Everything iOS lacks | Smart Albums · Titles + Keywords · multiple libraries · Export Unmodified Original · **Export IPTC as XMP** (round-trips back in) · third-party editing extensions | **YES — every one is a free win on iPhone**, and Apple documents the gap itself |

---

### 14.12 Prior art directly relevant to our architecture

**From Ente — take the derived-index sync; fix the curation asymmetry and the speed.**

What they got right, and we should copy structurally: **the unit of sync is not the pixel, it is the index.** Encrypt embeddings with the per-file key, encrypt cluster→name "person" entities, ship both. Index once on the machine that is fast and plugged in; every other device inherits face recognition and semantic search for free. This removes the #1 cost of on-device ML (battery/time) while keeping the #1 benefit (privacy). **Treat the embedding + cluster payload as a first-class, versioned sync object with a model-version tag** — so a model upgrade triggers an explicit reindex rather than silent embedding-space corruption. (Immich's `Job Status > "All" > re-embed` is the user-facing shape of that operation; make it visible, not a hidden migration.)

What they got wrong, and what it cost them:
- **The device that indexes fastest is not the device that can do the finest-grained correction.** Ente's desktop can view, name, and merge — but cannot remove a face from a cluster, set a cover, or run the mixed-grouping re-evaluation. Those are mobile-only. So the user does the heavy compute on the Mac and then has to pick up their phone to fix a bad merge. **Ship full cluster curation on every surface.** For us that means the desktop Electron app must be able to do everything the RN phone app can.
- **Slow indexing with no progress notifications** is their loudest complaint, compounded by needing to **download originals to the device to index**. In our topology the desktop already *has* the originals — this problem should not exist for us, and if it does, we built it wrong.
- **Ente's own advice is "disable local indexing on mobile and let the desktop do it."** That is our architecture, arrived at as a workaround. We should ship it as the *design*, with the phone doing zero heavy inference by default and the desktop node advertised as the compute.
- **Their clustering quality is the top ML gripe** — but the complaints are forum-sourced, not measured. **Benchmark our clustering against Ente's before making any competitive claim.** And note their honest admission: *"no clustering ground truth exists; effectiveness varies by library."*
- **They accepted a trap we don't have to:** because their server cannot read pixels, there is **no server-side ML upgrade path by design.** Our "server" is the user's own Mac — **we get server-class compute AND local custody.** That is the positioning wedge.

**Cross-age is the wedge inside the wedge.** Ente ships a **mixed grouping** mode specifically because *"faces change rapidly at that age"* for babies and toddlers — and it is a stricter-settings re-evaluation, i.e. a workaround, not a model. We have actual cross-age FR (`crossage_fr/match/age_gap.py`). Ship a first-class **"this person as a child"** merge affordance and a **Memory Lane**-style *one person across years* timeline (Ente's own name for the feature), and we beat Ente, Apple, and Google on the emotionally highest-value cluster in anyone's library: their own kids. **That timeline is the demo that sells cross-age recognition.**

**From Immich — take the taxonomy, the automation, and the trust surfaces; do not repeat the trust failures.**

- **Isolate the model process from the app process behind an IPC/HTTP boundary.** Immich's NestJS API ↔ Python FastAPI ML split lets the heavy model process crash, restart, or move to a GPU box without taking the library server down. We already do something like this with our Python backend behind Electron — keep it, and keep the ML service as the single chokepoint (Immich's hosts CLIP *and* InsightFace face detection *and* RapidOCR *and* dedupe, which is exactly why it can be scaled independently).
- **Reindex-after-model-change is a first-class user-facing operation, not a hidden migration.** Ship a visible **Job Status** surface with per-job re-run.
- **Copy the full search filter taxonomy.** It is the most complete in the category and it is a direct indictment of iOS Photos, which cannot scope a query to any field. Combined with our SigLIP engine + Vision OCR + our FR identities, a `caption:` / `tag:` / `person:` / `text:` field-scoped filter panel beats iOS Photos search outright.
- **Copy Workflows.** Triggers → Filters → Actions, with a **visual builder AND a JSON editor**, premade templates, and shareable JSON. It maps directly onto our ~245-command backend, and **the JSON representation doubles as the agent-callable contract** for our MCP surface. A shareable-JSON automation format is also a community moat. Example that only we can offer: *"when a photo is imported AND a named person is detected AND the safety gate says clean → add to album X."*
- **Copy integrity checks** (untracked files / missing files / checksum mismatch, schedulable, on a Maintenance page). It is a trust-building surface no consumer photo app offers, and it directly counters the "⚠️ this is not a backup" anxiety that Immich's own README creates.
- **Copy checksum dedupe** — but **beat their scope.** Immich's dedupe is **per-library and upload-libraries-only**; external libraries are not deduped against uploads, and partner-shared timelines show duplicates because *"duplicates are only detected on a per-user basis."* **Cross-source and cross-user dedupe in a merged view is unsolved.** Solving it (perceptual-hash dedupe across the merged view) is a small, sharp differentiator for couples and families.
- **Write metadata back to the file.** Immich's biggest lock-in smell: *"that metadata is only stored inside Immich and will not be persisted to the external asset file."* Users notice. **XMP sidecar write-back is a trust feature.**
- **Their external-library design is validated — copy it** (multiple recursive import paths, glob excludes, one file in two paths added once, trash-on-missing, 30-day purge). We already have the referenced-import + backend exclude system; Immich confirms the shape.

> ⚠️ **Trap (the one that will silently eat weeks):** **Do not build our LAN import on filesystem watching.** Immich's own docs: *"If your photos are on a network drive, automatic file watching likely won't work… you will have to rely on a periodic library refresh."* Watching is experimental, can hang startup, and `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` breaks on large libraries. **Use content-addressed periodic rescan with checksums.** The same applies to FSEvents over SMB/NFS on macOS.

> ⚠️ **Trap:** **Immich does NOT run ML on the phone.** Its CLIP/SigLIP, face detection, and OCR are all server-side. If you benchmark "Immich mobile ML," you are benchmarking nothing.

**From Mylio — take the vocabulary and the data model; avoid their fatal mobile flaw.**

- **Adopt the representation ladder as first-class:** **Original / Optimized (<5%, still fully editable) / Thumbnail (non-editable, browse-only)**, plus an always-synced **Catalog** (thumbnails + metadata + sync state, one copy per device). **The asset is not one file — it is a ladder of representations**, and a policy decides which rung lives where. Google's Original / Storage saver / Express tiers confirm the same idea from the cloud direction. The critical, easily-missed property: **Optimized copies remain fully editable** — that is what lets a phone do real work without ever pulling a 50 MB RAW.
- **Use XMP sidecars as the metadata transport.** It carries edits, keywords, labels, and locations across devices; it solves Immich's lock-in problem; and it gives instant interop with Lightroom / Capture One / Bridge. Apple's own **"Export IPTC as XMP"** round-trips back into Photos, which proves the format is a real escape hatch, not a gesture.
- **Steal the device-policy preset names.** *Vault* (the always-complete device — our Mac node; **Mylio recommends at least two Vaults for redundancy**), *SpaceSaver* (the phone), *Travel Backup* (catalog + last three months of originals, for the laptop before a trip), *Catalog Only*, *Highest Rated*, *Everything*, *Photos Only*, *Optimized Images*. These are legible, memorable, and map exactly onto our desktop-node + mobile-client topology. And **"Highest Rated" shows how a *quality signal* can drive *storage policy*** — an idea we can extend with our own signals (people you care about, safety-gate status, memories, aesthetic score).
- **Copy Sync on Demand and Tap to Sync.** A thumbnail-only device that can temporarily pull a higher-res copy from a peer, plus an explicit "pre-download this folder before I go offline" affordance, is the correct answer to the phone-with-64GB problem.
- **Do not let two policy layers fight.** Mylio has a documented mess where legacy per-folder policies collide with device presets, requiring an explicit **"Clear Legacy Folder Policies"** escape hatch. Design one authoritative policy resolution order from day one.
- **Close the gap Mylio leaves open:** their docs never clearly state what happens when the source device holding the original is offline (implied: the fetch just fails). **Ship an explicit state: *"unavailable — held on <device> — will fetch when it's back."*** That single state is the difference between a sync product that feels trustworthy and one that feels broken.

> ⚠️ **Trap — Mylio's fatal flaw, and the reason to build our sync on the right iOS primitives:** **Mylio's own docs say background syncing is not available on mobile; the app "must be running in the foreground on mobile devices for syncing to occur."** They shipped a **Background Launch** toggle and a **Prevent sleep when active** toggle — visible evidence of fighting the OS with workarounds rather than using the OS's actual background primitives. **Do not replicate this.** Use Network.framework/Bonjour for discovery, **URLSession background configuration** for transfers that survive termination, **BGAppRefreshTask** for cheap deltas, and **BGProcessingTask** for the indexing/hashing sweep. Sync must make progress while the phone is in a pocket.

> ⚠️ **Trap — do not cite Mylio's "Sync Panel" as prior art for our observability design.** The often-repeated spec (per-tier × per-device green/yellow/gray bars, live queue counts, Vault shield badge, "Original Status" view) **is not what Mylio ships.** Mylio's actual Sync Panel (*Info Panel > Sync tab*) shows connected devices and current sync activity; the **colored bars belong to a separate Storage Panel.** The rich per-tier × per-device design is **our original design** — build it, ship it, and claim it as ours, but never present it as observed prior art. It is still the right thing to build: **observability of sync IS the feature**, and "spinners that spin forever without progress numbers" is the loudest complaint in this entire category.

> ⚠️ **Trap — "no cloud" is a claim Mylio softened and we should not.** Mylio Photos+ now bundles **Mylio Drive** cloud storage for optimized copies, and Sync on Demand lists cloud/Mylio Drive among its fetch sources. **Cloud is optional in Mylio, not absent.** We are the ones who can actually make the no-cloud claim — that is worth guarding, and worth not overclaiming on their behalf. Also: **never quote a Mylio price** (sources disagree wildly: $9.99/mo, $99/yr, $119/yr, $240/yr, $20/mo/user; no authoritative page).

**From Google's retreat — the single most actionable architecture lesson for our "Ask" feature.**

Google built the best conversational photo search in the world, and in **March 2026 shipped a toggle to turn it off.** The mechanism of their fix is the spec:
1. **Render fast, deterministic results FIRST** — classic/lexical results appear immediately.
2. **Let the model refine in the background** and update in place — *"Gemini models continue to work in the background to narrow down the results set."*
3. **Never block a one-word query ("beach", "dog") on an LLM.**
4. **Never be worse than classic search.** If the model has nothing to add, get out of the way.
5. **Build the escape hatch** — a user-visible toggle back to deterministic search — before you ship the model.

And the legal lesson that comes for free: **Ask Photos is unavailable in Illinois and Texas because face grouping does not satisfy those states' biometric-privacy laws.** Face-grouping consent law is a hard gating dependency for any conversational-photos feature in the US. Know this before it surprises you.

**The synthesis.** The four axes are **privacy/custody, search quality, sync reliability, power features.** Ente holds privacy + on-device search but is slow and splits curation across surfaces. Immich holds search + power features but has no E2EE, warns you it isn't a backup, and runs zero ML on the phone. Google holds search but fails privacy — and its own users made it ship a way to turn the AI off. Mylio holds the sync architecture but its phone only syncs while you watch it, its search is weak, and it quietly added a cloud. **Our desktop-node + LAN-mobile topology is the only one that can hold all four at once, because the "server" is the user's own machine: server-class compute without surrendering custody.** Everything in this section is either a component of that thesis or a warning about how the people who tried it before us fell short.
## 15. Settings — Every Toggle That Changes Photos

Apple's Photos behaviour is not configured in one place. In iOS 18+ the old monolithic `Settings > Photos` pane was split across **at least three surfaces** — `Settings > Apps > Photos` (privacy/format/reset rows), `Settings > [your name] > iCloud > Photos` (sync + storage + Shared Albums), and the **Photos app itself** (`Collections` → account button, top-right, for curation controls) — with further Photos-affecting toggles scattered across `Settings > Camera`, `Settings > Privacy & Security`, `Settings > Accessibility > Motion`, `Settings > Screen Time`, and `Settings > General > Screen Capture`. The single most important thing an implementer must know: **almost none of these toggles are readable by a third-party app**, but nearly all of them silently change the *pixels, formats, completeness, and availability* of the assets our pipeline ingests. We therefore cannot read the user's configuration — we must *measure the consequences* per-asset and design every ingest path to be robust to a configuration we cannot see.

Shipping OS at time of writing is **iOS 26.5.2** (26.6 in beta; iOS 27 was announced at WWDC 2026 and ships ~Sept 2026 — nothing in this section depends on iOS 27, and no iOS 27 behaviour should be assumed available).

---

### 15.1 The structural fact: Apple publishes no enumeration of this pane

⚠️ **Trap:** There is **no** "Photos settings" reference topic anywhere in the iOS 26 iPhone User Guide. Apple has never published a page that enumerates the rows of `Settings > Apps > Photos`. The iOS 18 topic *"Customize the Photos app"* (`iph4efb36f5c`) now **302-redirects to the guide's table of contents** when requested at the current `/ios` path, and only resolves at the pinned `/18.0/ios/18.0` path.

Everything presented below as "the Settings > Apps > Photos pane" is a **union of ~10 separate Apple task pages that each happen to mention one row**. Consequences for anyone building on this:

- The row list below **cannot be guaranteed complete**.
- **Row order and section headers are unknown.** Do not reproduce them from memory or from third-party tutorials.
- A physical iOS 26.5.2 device audit (screenshot the pane top-to-bottom) is the only way to close this. Per the corpus, doing so **closes six of ten open uncertainties in about ninety seconds** and is the highest-leverage next action in this domain.

⚠️ **Trap:** Every old tutorial on the internet still says "Settings > Photos". That path no longer exists as written. Any onboarding or help copy we write that says "go to Settings > Photos to turn off Memories" is **wrong on iOS 18+** — that control moved *into the Photos app*.

---

### 15.2 `Settings > Apps > Photos` — row inventory

| Row | Type | Apple-sourced? | What it does | Readable by us? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Use Face ID** / **Use Touch ID** / **Use Passcode** (label varies by device biometric hardware) | Toggle | **Yes** (iOS 26 iPhone User Guide) | Locks **both** the Hidden **and** Recently Deleted collections behind auth. **ON by default.** | No |
| **Show Hidden Album** | Toggle | **Yes** | Removes the Hidden album row from the Photos UI (`Collections > Utilities`). Visibility only — not auth. **ON (visible) by default on iPhone/iPad.** | No |
| **Enhanced Visual Search** | Toggle | **Yes** | Landmark/POI search without geodata; sends an encrypted embedding to Apple. Default state **not stated by Apple**. | No |
| **Reset Suggested Memories** | Action row | **Yes** (Personal Safety guide, pub. March 2026) | Restores Memories curation to original state | No |
| **Reset People & Pets Suggestions** | Action row | **Yes** (same page) | Undoes all accumulated person-suppression signals | No |
| **Keep Originals** | Selectable row (Apple says "*tap* Keep Originals" — a two-option list, not a switch) | **Yes** (support doc 116944, pub. 2025-12-05) | Defeats HEIF→JPEG / HEVC→H.264 transcode on **USB import** | No (and irrelevant to PhotoKit) |
| **Auto-Play Motion** | Toggle | **No — third-party only (MacRumors)** | Autoplay of motion content in the Photos app | No |
| **Loop Videos** | Toggle | **No — third-party only (MacRumors)**; arrived **iOS 18.2** | Loop video playback in the Photos app | No |
| **Show Recently Viewed & Shared** | Toggle | **No — third-party only** (Tom's Guide iOS 18.4 coverage + a Jan-2026 hardening guide, which agree on the label) | Stops Photos recording/showing the Recently Viewed and Recently Shared collections | No |
| **View Full HDR** | Toggle | **UNVERIFIED — no apple.com page contains this string** | Believed: render HDR at full EDR vs tone-mapped SDR. Display-only. | No |
| **Cellular Data** / **Unlimited Updates** | Sub-screen | **UNVERIFIED — "Unlimited Updates" appears on zero apple.com pages** | Believed: cellular sync gating for iCloud Photos. **Probably relocated** to the iCloud pane. | No |

⚠️ **Trap — three widely-repeated claims that are WRONG:**
1. **"Auto-Play Motion and Loop Videos" is not a toggle name.** It is **two separate toggles** — `Auto-Play Motion` and `Loop Videos` — and they are in **Settings > Apps > Photos**, *not* in the Photos app. (The direction of travel is the opposite of what most write-ups claim: these went **to** Settings.) The iOS 17-era label `Auto-Play Videos and Live Photos` is dead and must not appear in current copy — but do **not** replace it with the invented composite string.
2. **The Shared Albums master toggle is NOT in `Settings > Apps > Photos`.** See §15.7.
3. **`SDR (Most Compatible)` is not a Screen Capture label.** See §15.14.

**Rows confirmed *not* in Settings (they live in the Photos app):** `Show Featured Content` and `Show Holiday Events` — both at **Photos app → Collections → tap your account in the top-right corner**. Apple, verbatim, iOS 26 iPhone User Guide: *"Tap Collections. Tap your account in the top-right corner… Turn off Show Featured Content…"* and *"…Turn off Show Holiday Events…"*. The two **Reset** actions are mirrored in *both* places (Settings **and** this in-app account pane).

⚠️ **Trap:** That in-app account pane (`Collections` → account button) is **a whole settings surface Apple has been quietly relocating Photos curation controls into, and it has never been fully enumerated**. Any claim about "where a Photos control lives" is unsafe until that pane is audited on a device.

---

### 15.3 Hidden & Recently Deleted — the lock, the visibility toggle, and the Full Access contradiction

**The lock (`Use Face ID` / `Use Touch ID` / `Use Passcode`).** One toggle governs **two different albums**. Apple, verbatim (iOS 26 iPhone User Guide):

> "The Recently Deleted and Hidden collections are locked by default. You can unlock these collections using Face ID, Touch ID, or your passcode. To change the default setting from locked to unlocked, do the following: Go to the Settings app on your iPhone. Tap Apps, then tap Photos. Turn off Use Face ID, Use Touch ID, or Use Passcode."

- Availability: **iOS 16, iPadOS 16.1, and macOS Ventura and later** (note: iPadOS is **16.1**, not 16). On Apple Vision Pro, **Optic ID** or passcode.
- No per-album granularity. Users routinely do not realise turning it off also unlocks **Recently Deleted**.

**The visibility toggle (`Show Hidden Album`)** is a *different job*: it removes the album row from the Photos UI. Apple, verbatim: *"On an iPhone or iPad, the Hidden album is on and visible by default"* — and the Mac default is the **inverse**: *"The Hidden album is off by default on Mac."* Apple: *"In iOS 14 and later, you can also choose not to show the Hidden album."* Path: *"Open the Settings app, tap Apps, then tap Photos. Scroll down and turn off Show Hidden Album."*

⚠️ **Trap (contradiction between two Apple sources — MUST be resolved on a device before we design our completeness/backup story):**

- **Apple's Photos & Privacy legal page** (`apple.com/legal/privacy/data/en/photos/`, revised **2025-12-12**) states that Full Access *"grants the third-party app access to your photos and videos, **including your hidden photos even if the album is locked**."*
- **Apple's PhotoKit documentation** for `PHAsset.isHidden` states the opposite: since iOS 16 the authentication setting *"is true by default"* and when true *"the system doesn't return hidden assets even if the `includeHiddenAssets` fetch option is true."* `PHAssetCollectionSubtype.smartAlbumAllHidden` independently corroborates the API side: *"When true, the system returns an empty Smart Album."*

**These cannot both be true.** The adversarial verifier's position, which overrides the researcher's, is that the legal page is authoritative on this point and that **the Face ID lock provides ZERO protection against our own app** — i.e. **hidden assets will flow into our ingest and our face index unless we filter them ourselves**. Treat that as the planning assumption *and* run the empirical test before shipping any completeness claim:

> **Device test:** On a device with `Use Face ID` **ON** and a non-empty Hidden album, grant our app **Full Access** and fetch with `includeHiddenAssets = true`. Count the results. Zero ⇒ the API doc is right. Non-zero ⇒ the legal page is right and hidden (often intimate) photos are reaching our NSFW pipeline.

Independently documented escape hatch, regardless of how the above resolves: **`PHPickerViewController`**. `PHAsset.isHidden`'s documentation says explicitly that if you use the picker, *"a user can choose hidden assets to provide to your app."* The picker requires **no permission at all** and runs out-of-process.

⚠️ **Trap:** A **locked** Hidden album and an **empty** Hidden album both present as an empty fetch result. "Zero hidden assets returned" is ambiguous — you cannot infer the toggle state from it.

---

### 15.4 `Settings > Apps > Photos` — Enhanced Visual Search

Apple, verbatim: *"Starting in iOS 18, iPadOS 18, and macOS Sequoia, Enhanced Visual Search lets you search your photo library for landmarks or points of interest in photos or videos — making it easier to find what you're looking for, even if those photos and videos don't have any saved geolocation information."* And: *"Enhanced Visual Search isn't available in all countries or regions."*

**Mechanism** (Apple's own description): on-device ML decides a photo likely contains a landmark and produces *"a low-fidelity mathematical representation of the part of that photo that might contain the landmark, called an **embedding**"*. Only the **encrypted embedding** leaves the device — never image data. Apple matches it against *"a global list of landmarks and places that's too big to fit on your device."* The privacy stack, in Apple's words: **homomorphic encryption** (the server matches without decrypting), **differential privacy** (the device sends fake requests alongside the real one), and an **OHTTP relay** — *"a third-party anonymization network that hides your IP address."* Requests are not stored and not linked to the Apple Account.

- Paths: iOS — `Settings > Apps > Photos` → scroll down → Enhanced Visual Search. macOS — **`Photos > Settings > General`** (not a Settings-app pane).
- Support doc published **2025-09-15**; legal page revised **2025-12-12**.
- **Default state: Apple does not state it anywhere.** The widely-reported "on by default" claim is **not Apple-sourced** — do not put it in a spec. (The iOS 18.x backlash over a network-touching Photos feature enabled without a prompt is real as a *perception*, but the default is unverified against Apple.)
- Calling it "Apple's one cloud-touching Photos search feature" is **editorial, not Apple-stated**. And it is emphatically **not a cloud CLIP index** in the sense our pipeline uses — an encrypted embedding is matched homomorphically against a landmark gazetteer.
- **3rd-party API: none.** No way to read the toggle, invoke the feature, or query Apple's landmark index. Vision framework's on-device classifiers are available to us; the global landmark index is not.

---

### 15.5 The two Reset rows — Memories and People & Pets suppression

Apple, verbatim (Personal Safety User Guide, published **March 2026**):

> "On iPhone or iPad: Go to Settings > Apps > Photos, then tap **Reset Suggested Memories** or **Reset People & Pets Suggestions**. On Mac: Choose Photos > Settings, click General, then click **Reset Suggested Memories** or **Reset Suggested People & Pets**."

⚠️ **Trap (localisation/string reuse):** the Mac label has **different word order** — `Reset Suggested People & Pets` (macOS) vs `Reset People & Pets Suggestions` (iOS). **Do not reuse the iOS string on macOS.**

Both rows are **also** reachable in the Photos app: iOS 26 iPhone User Guide routes users to *"tap Collections, tap your account in the top-right corner, then tap Reset People & Pets Suggestions."* Both surfaces exist simultaneously.

**The negative signals these rows clear** are set from a photo's **More** button → *"Don't Feature a Person"* → **`Feature This Person Less`** or **`Never Feature This Person`** → Confirm. Both of those strings are Apple-confirmed. The Mac memory equivalent is **`Feature Less` → `Feature Fewer Memories Like This`**.

⚠️ **Trap:** the string **`Feature This Day Less` appears on NO Apple page.** Do not ship it.

- **Pain point (and Apple frames it this way itself):** the reset is **all-or-nothing**. You cannot un-suppress one person; you must reset every suggestion you ever gave. Apple documents this under **Personal Safety** — the real-world case is a domestic-abuse survivor who suppressed an abuser and later needs to undo, or who suppressed and cannot verify it took effect.
- **3rd-party API: none.** PhotoKit does not expose Memories at all to third parties, nor the People & Pets suggestion graph, nor the "feature less" negative-preference signals.

---

### 15.6 `Settings > Apps > Photos` — Keep Originals

Apple, verbatim (support doc 116944, published **2025-12-05**):

> "When you import HEIF or HEVC media from an attached iPhone or iPad into Photos, Image Capture, or a PC, the media might be converted to JPEG or H.264. If you don't want it to be converted, open Settings, tap Apps, tap Photos, then scroll down and **tap Keep Originals**."

So **the default behaviour is transcode-on-import**, and `Keep Originals` defeats it. Note Apple says "*tap*" — consistent with a selectable row in a two-option list rather than a switch.

⚠️ **Trap:** the section header **`Transfer to Mac or PC`** and the sibling option **`Automatic`** are the historical labels but appear on **no current apple.com page** (independently searched by both the researcher and the verifier). Treat both as **unverified UI strings**; confirm on a device before putting them in documentation.

- **Scope:** this setting governs only the **USB/PTP import path** used by Image Capture / Photos / the Apple Devices app. It does **not** affect PhotoKit. An app using `PHAssetResourceManager` gets the true original resource regardless.
- **Why it matters anyway:** it is one of the most notorious silent-data-loss traps in the Apple ecosystem — users cable an iPhone to a PC, get JPEGs, and never realise the HEIF original (plus the HDR gain map, plus depth/Portrait data) was transcoded away. **The default is the lossy one.** This is a competitor failure mode we can market against.
- Apple's separate recommendation for Windows compatibility is a *different* lever: `Settings > Camera > Formats > Most Compatible`, which changes **capture** format rather than transfer behaviour.

---

### 15.7 `Settings > [your name] > iCloud > Photos` — Sync, Optimize, Shared Albums

**This is the single most consequential pane on the phone for an app like ours, because it determines whether the original bytes of a photo are physically present on the device.**

Apple, verbatim (iOS 26 guide): *"Go to Settings. Tap your name, then tap iCloud. Tap Photos, then turn on **Sync this iPhone**."* And:

> "When **Optimize iPhone Storage** is turned on, all your full-resolution photos and videos are stored in iCloud in their original formats, with storage-saving versions kept on your iPhone. **Optimize iPhone Storage is turned on by default**, but you can turn it off."

To defeat it: `Settings > [your name] > iCloud > Photos > **Download and Keep Originals**`. (macOS wording differs again: **`Download Originals to this Mac`**.)

**Assume the median user's device does NOT hold full-resolution originals locally.**

**Shared Albums master toggle — location is settled, and it is NOT in the Photos pane.** Two independent Apple pages agree. iOS 26 iPhone User Guide: *"Go to the Settings app on your iPhone. Tap your name, tap iCloud, then tap Photos. Turn on **Shared Albums**."* Apple support article 108314 is more specific: *"On your iPhone or iPad, go to Settings. Tap your name, then tap iCloud. **Under Saved to iCloud**, tap Photos. Scroll down and turn on Shared Albums."* Per-album controls (Add Participants, Subscribers Can Post, Remove Subscriber, Public Website, Notifications) are unambiguously **in the Photos app**, not Settings.

⚠️ **Trap:** Shared-album assets are **not full-resolution** — Apple stores downscaled copies with size limits — and they are **not editable**. Turning the master toggle off **deletes local shared-album content** with little warning.

**Detectability — this is one of the few genuinely readable signals:**

| Signal | API | What you learn |
|---|---|---|
| Is this asset only in iCloud? | `PHImageResultIsInCloudKey` in the image-request result handler — *"If true, no image was provided, because the asset data must be downloaded from iCloud."* | Per-asset consequence of **Optimize iPhone Storage** |
| Will Photos fetch it for me? | `PHImageRequestOptions.isNetworkAccessAllowed` — **default is `false`** | Set `true` or you silently get nothing for optimized assets |
| Download progress | `PHImageRequestOptions.progressHandler` | UI for a long iCloud pull |
| Is this a Shared Album asset? | `PHAsset.sourceType == PHAssetSourceType.typeCloudShared` — *"The asset originates from an iCloud Shared Album"* | Not an original, **not editable**, and (per Apple) does not appear in Moments collections |

⚠️ **Trap (the biggest technical landmine in the whole phone-side ingest):** `isNetworkAccessAllowed` **defaults to `false`**. A naive implementation requests an image for an optimized asset, gets nothing (or a degraded rendition), and ships it into the ML pipeline. Every downstream number — face embeddings, cross-age matches, CLIP vectors, NSFW scores, calibration statistics — is then quietly computed on a **shrunken copy**.

---

### 15.8 `Settings > Privacy & Security > Photos` — the per-app permission pane

This is *the* pane that governs what our app can see. Apple's own framing: *"Go to Settings > Privacy & Security. Tap a category of information… A list appears showing the apps that requested access."* From this pane, a **Limited Access** app shows its selected-photo set, which the user can review and edit **without launching the app**.

The four states are real in the shipping UI: **None**, **Add Photos Only**, **Limited Access**, **Full Access**.

⚠️ **Trap (sourcing):** No apple.com page enumerates those four states **with descriptions**. Do **not** present per-state description strings as Apple-documented. The only Apple prose available uses *different* prompt-side vocabulary — the Photos & Privacy legal page says the user *"may choose to **Allow Full Access**"* and *"can choose to **Limit Access** to your photos and videos."* And, load-bearing for us, that same page says Full Access *"grants the third-party app access to your photos and videos, **including your hidden photos even if the album is locked**"* (see §15.3).

**The API contract — this, not the Settings labels, is what we build against:**

| API | Behaviour / gotcha |
|---|---|
| `PHPhotoLibrary.authorizationStatus(for:)` | Takes a `PHAccessLevel`. ⚠️ **`.limited` is ONLY observable when you pass `.readWrite`.** Limited access does not affect add-only access, so querying with `.addOnly` will **never** return `.limited`. |
| `PHPhotoLibrary.requestAuthorization(for:handler:)` | The request counterpart; same `PHAccessLevel` split (`.addOnly` vs `.readWrite`). |
| `PHAuthorizationStatus` cases | `.notDetermined` / `.restricted` / `.denied` / `.authorized` / `.limited` — handle all five explicitly. |
| `PHAuthorizationStatus.restricted` | Means the user **cannot grant access** — blocked by policy (Screen Time / MDM). **Not** the same as `.denied`. |
| `PHPhotoLibrary.shared().presentLimitedLibraryPicker(from:)` | How a limited-access app asks the user to widen the selection. |
| `PHPhotoLibraryPreventAutomaticLimitedAccessAlert` (Info.plist key) | Suppresses iOS's own recurring limited-library nag so **you** control when to ask. |
| `PHPhotoLibraryChangeObserver` | *"Any changes the user applies to the limited library selection trigger a [change] update."* Register it or a widened selection is missed. |
| `PHPickerViewController` | Requires **no permission at all**; out-of-process. Also the documented route by which a user can hand us **hidden** assets. |
| `PHPhotoLibrary.unavailabilityReason` | For the library-unavailable case. |

⚠️ **Trap:** if you query authorization with `.addOnly` you will misclassify every **Limited Access** user as authorized, then wonder why the library looks tiny.

⚠️ **Trap:** showing a "go to Settings and enable this" prompt to a `.restricted` user is **useless** — they structurally cannot clear it (see §15.13).

---

### 15.9 `Settings > Privacy & Security > Sensitive Content Warning`

The system-wide nudity-detection setting, with per-app sub-toggles for every app that adopts the **SensitiveContentAnalysis** framework. **Uniquely among everything in this section, its state IS readable by us.**

Apple, verbatim: *"When you turn on Sensitive Content Warning, it's turned on automatically for all supported apps, but you can manage access for each app."* And: it *"uses on-device machine learning to analyze photos and videos. Because they're analyzed on your device, Apple doesn't receive an indication that nudity was detected and doesn't get access to the photos or videos."*

⚠️ **Trap — fabricated quotation in circulation:** the sentence *"Over time, as more developers embrace the feature, additional apps will be added."* is **NOT Apple's**. It appears on **neither** Apple support article 105071 (published **March 24, 2026**) **nor** the iOS 26 iPhone User Guide page. It traces to third-party coverage (an AppleInsider iOS 17 tip article). **Never attribute it to Apple.**

- **Path:** `Settings > Privacy & Security > Sensitive Content Warning`.
- **OS coverage:** iOS 17+ / iPadOS 17+ / macOS Sonoma+ / watchOS 10+ / visionOS 2+.
- **What Apple's system actually scans (iPhone):** *"Messages, AirDrop, shared photo albums, Contact Posters in the Phone app and the Contacts app, and FaceTime calls and video messages."*
- ⚠️ **Trap (and it kills a tempting comms defence): Sensitive Content Warning does NOT scan the user's own photo library.** It scans **inbound** content only. There is therefore **no Apple precedent** for what our Safe Mode does (library-wide NSFW classification) — we cannot lean on "Apple does this too" as a design or PR shield.
- The child-account variant is **Communication Safety**, under Screen Time.
- Detected content is blurred behind a warning with Show / safety-resources / block / report-to-Apple options.

**The API — exact names:**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Framework | `SensitiveContentAnalysis` — **iOS 17.0 / macOS 14.0** floor |
| Class | `SCSensitivityAnalyzer` |
| Analysis | `analyzeImage(at:)` / `analyzeImage(_:)`; `videoAnalysis(forFileAt:)` → `hasSensitiveContent()` |
| **Readable policy** | `SCSensitivityAnalyzer.analysisPolicy` → `SCSensitivityAnalysisPolicy`: **`.disabled`**, **`.simpleInterventions`**, **`.descriptiveInterventions`** |
| Apple's guard pattern | `let policy = analyzer.analysisPolicy; if policy == .disabled { return }` |
| Apple's warning | *"This class successfully detects sensitive content only when `analysisPolicy` is a value other than `disabled`."* |
| **Entitlement (request-gated)** | **`com.apple.developer.sensitivecontentanalysis.client`** |

Adopting the framework also **places our app into the per-app list inside `Settings > Privacy & Security > Sensitive Content Warning`** — free, high-trust placement alongside Apple's own apps.

---

### 15.10 `Settings > Apps > Messages > Shared with You`

Apple, verbatim (Personal Safety User Guide): *"On your iPhone or iPad, go to the Settings app > Apps > Messages > Shared with You, then turn off **Automatic Sharing** or turn off Shared with You for a specific app."* The per-app list Apple names: **Music, Apple TV, News, Photos, Podcasts, Safari**.

Per-conversation suppression also exists: open the conversation → tap the contact/group icon → **Info** → turn off **Show in Shared with You**.

⚠️ **Trap:** the off switch for photos flooding into Photos from group chats is under **Messages**, not Photos. Nobody finds it.

- **3rd-party API: none.** Shared with You content cannot be enumerated by a third-party app, and the toggle cannot be read.
- Signal that Apple knows this is a problem: the **iOS 26 Photos app exposes "Shared With You" as a filter in the Library view**, letting users exclude those images from the grid.
- Adjacent Apple-owned marker we *can* use: the **Recently Saved** collection is Apple's own bucket for content saved from Messages, Safari, Mail, and AirDrop.

---

### 15.11 `Settings > Camera` — everything that changes the pixels

#### 15.11.1 Formats

| Control | Apple's words / values | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **High Efficiency** vs **Most Compatible** | *"Open Settings, then tap Camera. Tap Formats, then tap Most Compatible… All new photos and videos will now use JPEG or H.264 format. To return to using the space-saving HEIF and HEVC formats, choose High Efficiency."* | ⚠️ Apple **never uses the word "default"** here. Apple frames Most Compatible as the opt-in for Windows compatibility, which *implies* High Efficiency is the default — but do not quote Apple as saying so. |
| **Photo Mode** | *"Go to Settings > Camera > Formats > Photo Mode, then choose **12 MP** or **24 MP**."* | |
| **48 MP capture** | *"To capture resolution at 48 MP, go to Settings > Camera > Formats, then turn on **Resolution Control** or **ProRAW & Resolution Control** (depending on your model)."* | |
| **Apple ProRAW** | *"On **iPhone 12 Pro and later Pro models with iOS 14.3 or later**, you can take photos in Apple ProRAW."* Enable under **Photo Capture**; then *"Tap ProRAW & Resolution Control and select either 12 MP or 48 MP."* | **DNG** format. **~25 MB** at 12 MP, **~75 MB** at 48 MP. **Cannot be used with Live Photos, Portrait mode, or video.** |
| **Apple ProRes** | *"To use Apple ProRes, you need **iOS 15.1 or later**"* + a supported model — Apple's list runs iPhone 17 Pro Max down to **iPhone 13 Pro** (i.e. iPhone 13 Pro and later Pro models). Enable under **Video Capture**. | ProRes Log / ProRes HDR; 4K120 on 16 Pro / 17 Pro; external USB-C storage supported. |
| In-Camera-app override | Long-press the resolution control to pick **HEIF Max / RAW Max / RAW 12**. | |

#### 15.11.2 Photographic Styles

A capture-time (and, on newer models, re-editable) colour/tone treatment applied to **every photo you take**. Apple: *"Photographic Styles intelligently adjust specific colors in different parts of your photos to create a customized look. The style you select applies automatically to all photos you take, but you can make adjustments in Camera or edits later in the Photos app."* Set/reset via `Settings > Camera > Photographic Styles` → *"select 'Use Standard' or choose a different style."* Also selectable in the Camera app (Styles control, Tone and Warmth sliders). Latest-generation styles include named styles such as **Amber, Rose Gold, Quiet, Ethereal**.

- **Latest-generation (re-editable-after-capture) styles: iPhone 16 and later.** Confirmed.
- ⚠️ **"Default is Standard" is NOT Apple-stated.** Apple's page never states a default. Do not assert it.
- ⚠️ The **iPhone 13+** gate for *original* Photographic Styles is **unsourced** — Apple's iOS 26 page presents a combined supported-models popover, not a clean "13 and later" statement.
- ⚠️ **Trap — Styles are coupled to Formats.** Apple, verbatim: *"On models that support latest generation Photographic Styles, Camera needs to capture photos with **High Efficiency** image capture to edit Photographic Styles later in Photos. To turn on High Efficiency, go to Settings > Camera > Formats, then tap High Efficiency."* A user on **Most Compatible** gets JPEGs with the style **baked in irreversibly**. On iPhone 16+, latest-gen styles are non-destructive metadata on HEIF but **destructive on JPEG** — meaning the same face can present with materially different colour statistics depending on a Formats toggle the user never thinks about.
- **3rd-party API:** the Settings selection is **not readable**. Whether the applied style is recoverable from asset metadata is **unknown** — re-editability implies a recoverable non-destructive parameter set exists, but **there is no public PhotoKit API** for it, and the corpus explicitly **refuses to guess at private metadata keys**. This requires **empirical inspection of a real iPhone 16/17 HEIF capture**.

#### 15.11.3 Preserve Settings

`Settings > Camera > Preserve Settings` — determines which Camera-app settings persist across launches instead of resetting. Apple's list: **Camera Mode** (*"Save the last camera mode you used, such as Portrait or Pano"*), **Photographic Style**, **Creative Controls** (*"Save the last settings you used for a light setting"* — filter / Portrait Lighting / background blur), **Depth Control**, **Macro Control** (*"Preserve the Auto Macro setting"*), **Exposure Adjustment** (iPhone 11+), **Night Mode** (*"Save the Night mode setting rather than reset to Auto"*), **Portrait Zoom** (*"this setting is on by default on supported models"*), **Action Mode**, **ProRAW & Resolution Control**, **Apple ProRes**, and **Live Photo** (*"Save the Live Photo setting. **This setting is on by default.**"*).

⚠️ **Trap (the single most common iPhone camera complaint):** `Preserve Settings > Live Photo` being **ON** means your **last Live Photo choice sticks** — it does **not** mean Live Photos is on. Separately, **Live Photos itself is ON by default in Camera** (*"Live Photos is on by default. You can turn Live Photos off temporarily or permanently"*). This is why "Live Photos keeps turning itself back on" — the fix lives in a sub-pane called *Preserve Settings*, nowhere near the Live Photos control. There is also `Settings > Camera > Indicators > Live Photo` to show a Live Photo indicator.

**Detectable per-asset:** `PHAsset.mediaSubtypes` exposes the **`photoLive`** bit (used as a bitmask); the paired video is retrievable via `PHAssetResource` / `PHLivePhoto`.

#### 15.11.4 Advanced camera settings (all Apple-documented on one iOS 26 page, *"Change advanced camera settings on iPhone"*)

| Row | Apple's words | Default | Model scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Prioritize Faster Shooting** | *"modifies how images are processed—allowing you to capture more photos when you rapidly tap the Shutter button."* | *"Prioritize Faster Shooting is **on by default**."* | general |
| **Lens Correction** | *"adjusts photos taken with the front camera or Ultra Wide camera for more natural-looking results."* | *"Lens Correction is **on by default**."* | "supported models" |
| **Scene Detection** | *"can identify what you're taking a photo of and apply a tailored look."* | *"Scene Detection is **on by default**."* | ⚠️ **iPhone 12 models only.** Apple scopes this explicitly to *"On iPhone 12 models"* — **on iPhone 13 and later this row does not exist.** Treating it as a universal default is wrong. |
| **View Outside the Frame** | *"displays content outside the frame."* | *"View Outside the Frame is **on by default**."* | "supported models" |
| **Lens Cleaning Hints** | *"iPhone detects if your lens is smudged and suggests you clean it."* | — | |
| **Save Captures to Photo Library** | *"Photos you take in the Messages app are automatically saved to your library in the Photos app"* — turn off to stop that. | — | |

Also: **Smart HDR** can be turned off at `Settings > Camera` on iPhone 11 / SE (2nd gen) / 12. **HDR Video** is at `Settings > Camera > Record Video > HDR Video`.

⚠️ **Trap (this one has real ML consequences):** because **Prioritize Faster Shooting is on by default and unreadable**, **per-photo image quality is non-stationary within a single user's library** — burst-captured photos are processed *less*. **There is no flag on the asset telling us a given photo took the reduced-processing path.** Quality must be *measured*, never assumed.

**3rd-party API for the whole Camera pane:** the **settings** are not readable, but the **results** are, per asset — `PHAssetResource.uniformTypeIdentifier` (`public.heic` vs `public.jpeg` vs `com.adobe.raw-image`/DNG; HEVC vs H.264; ProRes) plus `PHAsset.pixelWidth` / `pixelHeight`. We can infer a user's Formats configuration **statistically from their recent captures**. For our own in-app capture, `AVCapturePhotoOutput.isAppleProRAWEnabled` is settable and KVO-observable, gated on `isAppleProRAWSupported`.

---

### 15.12 `Settings > Accessibility > Motion`

Apple, verbatim (iOS 26 guide):

- **Reduce Motion:** *"Turn on. (When off, you'll see more motion, like the fluid morphing effects of Liquid Glass.)"*
- **Auto-Play Video Previews:** *"Turn off. (When on, it allows apps such as the App Store to automatically play video previews.)"*
- **Auto-Play Animated Images:** *"Turn off. (When on, rapid animated images and moving elements such as GIFs in Messages and Safari play automatically.)"*
- **Limit Frame Rate:** *"Turn on. (On models with ProMotion display technology, this limits the maximum frame rate of the display to 60 frames per second.)"*

Other rows on the same iOS 26 pane: **Vehicle Motion Cues**, **Auto-Play Message Effects**, **Prefer Non-Blinking Cursor**. (Related, under Display & Text Size: Dim Flashing Lights, Reduce Bright Effects.)

⚠️ **Trap: only TWO of the four have a public read API.**

| Setting | Public API? |
|---|---|
| Reduce Motion | ✅ `UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled` (iOS 8.0) |
| Auto-Play Video Previews | ✅ `UIAccessibility.isVideoAutoplayEnabled` (iOS 13.0 — abstract literally reads *"whether the Auto-Play Video Previews setting is in an enabled state"*) |
| Auto-Play Animated Images | ❌ **No public `UIAccessibility` property found** |
| Limit Frame Rate | ❌ **No public `UIAccessibility` property found** |

Both readable flags post accessibility-status-changed notifications we can observe.

---

### 15.13 `Settings > Screen Time > Content & Privacy Restrictions` — Photos

An administrator can **freeze the Photos permission for every app**. Path: `Settings > Screen Time > [child's name] > Content & Privacy Restrictions` → (Screen Time passcode) → **Privacy** → **Photos** → **Allow Changes** / **Don't Allow Changes**.

Apple's parental-controls article lists, under *"Prevent changes to privacy settings"*, the exact row: **`Photos: Prevent apps from requesting access to your photos in the Photos app.`** A sibling row is relevant too: **`Media & Apple Music: Prevent apps from accessing your photos, videos, or music library.`**

- Family Sharing dependency confirmed: *"When Family Sharing is set up, and your child's Apple Account is added to the Family Sharing group, you need to turn on Content & Privacy Restrictions."* Apple also notes *"For some settings, you can allow or restrict changes only for your device"* — supporting the local-Screen-Time-passcode path.
- Apple's Intelligence restriction row exists but the exact label is **`Restrict Intelligence & Siri features`**, **not** "Apple Intelligence."
- `Allow built-in apps and features` can hide **Photos/Camera entirely**.
- iOS 26 adds the ability for a child to **request an exception** to a restriction.

**Detectability:** `PHAuthorizationStatus.restricted` is the distinct status meaning *the user cannot grant access* — blocked by policy (parental controls / MDM), **not** by user choice. We can detect `.restricted`; **we cannot detect which restriction caused it.**

---

### 15.14 Adjacent surfaces that change what lands in Photos

**`Settings > General > Screen Capture` (new in iOS 26).** The pane and its **Format** control are confirmed on the iOS 26 guide, under the heading *"Choose SDR or HDR format for screenshots and recordings."* The two options are labelled plainly **`SDR`** and **`HDR`**.

⚠️ **Trap:** the string **`SDR (Most Compatible)` is a fabricated/blended label.** "Most Compatible" is a `Settings > Camera > Formats` string and appears **nowhere** on the Screen Capture page. Apple's actual SDR description: *"This option captures less brightness and color. It's standard for most computer displays and mobile devices. **Screenshots use PNG format, and screen recordings use HEVC (H.265).**"* With **HDR** selected, screenshots are captured in **HEIF** and screen recordings in **HEVC**. Apple's HEIF/HEVC doc confirms the macOS Tahoe 26 analogue: *"if the Capture Format setting in the Screenshot app is set to HDR, screenshots are captured in HEIF format and screen recordings are captured in HEVC format."*

⚠️ **Trap:** on iOS 26, **"screenshot == PNG == SDR" is no longer a safe assumption.** Screenshots remain identifiable via `PHAssetMediaSubtype.photoScreenshot`, and the resource's `uniformTypeIdentifier` tells you PNG vs HEIF.

**Low Data Mode** (`Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data Options`, **and** per-Wi-Fi-network). Apple, verbatim: *"When Low Data Mode is on, iCloud pauses updates and automatic backups, and **turns off iCloud Photos updates**."* It also *"Turns off Background App Refresh."* Apple confirms the per-plan **and** per-network split, and that *"iCloud keeps your Low Data Mode preferences for each Wi-Fi network up to date across all your devices."*

⚠️ **Trap:** Low Data Mode is a **third, independent mechanism** (alongside Optimize iPhone Storage and permission scope) by which the bytes we expect simply are not there — and because it is **per-Wi-Fi-network and iCloud-synced**, it can be silently "on" for a network the user configured months ago on a different device. Apple pauses iCloud Photos **silently**.

Readable for our own traffic: `NWPathMonitor` / `NWPath.isConstrained` (Low Data Mode) and `.isExpensive` (cellular/hotspot); `URLSessionConfiguration.allowsCellularAccess`, `.allowsExpensiveNetworkAccess`, `.allowsConstrainedNetworkAccess`. Background App Refresh state: `UIApplication.backgroundRefreshStatus`.

**`Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > Camera`.** ⚠️ **Unverified:** the verifier could **not find an Apple page tying the Camera location toggle to Photos metadata**. The claim (that denying Camera location access produces a library with no geodata) is plausible and matches observed behaviour, but is **unsourced as written** — mark it unverified in any spec. What **is** solidly true on our side: **`PHAsset.location` is nil** when no location was recorded (or the user stripped it), and users can strip location per-photo via the photo's **More** button → **Adjust Location → No Location**.

---

### 15.15 Detectability matrix — what a third-party app can *actually* read

| Setting / surface | Readable? | How |
|---|---|---|
| Photo-library permission level | ✅ **Yes** | `PHPhotoLibrary.authorizationStatus(for: .readWrite)` — ⚠️ **must** pass `.readWrite` to ever see `.limited` |
| Policy-blocked permission (Screen Time / MDM) | ✅ **Yes** (but not *which* policy) | `PHAuthorizationStatus.restricted` |
| Sensitive Content Warning master + per-app state | ✅ **Yes** | `SCSensitivityAnalyzer.analysisPolicy` (`.disabled` / `.simpleInterventions` / `.descriptiveInterventions`); needs entitlement `com.apple.developer.sensitivecontentanalysis.client` |
| Optimize iPhone Storage | ⚠️ **Inferable per-asset** | `PHImageResultIsInCloudKey` in the request result handler |
| Shared Albums in use | ⚠️ **Inferable per-asset** | `PHAsset.sourceType == .typeCloudShared` |
| Camera Formats config | ⚠️ **Inferable statistically** | `PHAssetResource.uniformTypeIdentifier` + `PHAsset.pixelWidth/pixelHeight` over recent captures |
| Reduce Motion | ✅ **Yes** | `UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled` |
| Auto-Play Video Previews | ✅ **Yes** | `UIAccessibility.isVideoAutoplayEnabled` |
| Low Data Mode (for our own traffic) | ✅ **Yes** | `NWPath.isConstrained` / `allowsConstrainedNetworkAccess` |
| Screenshot format | ⚠️ **Inferable per-asset** | `PHAssetMediaSubtype.photoScreenshot` + resource UTI |
| Geodata present | ⚠️ **Inferable per-asset** | `PHAsset.location` is nil |
| **Everything else** | ❌ **No** | Use Face ID lock, Show Hidden Album, Enhanced Visual Search, Reset rows, Keep Originals, View Full HDR, Cellular Data, Show Recently Viewed & Shared, Auto-Play Motion, Loop Videos, Show Featured Content, Show Holiday Events, Shared with You, Photographic Styles, Preserve Settings, Prioritize Faster Shooting / Lens Correction / Scene Detection / View Outside the Frame, Auto-Play Animated Images, Limit Frame Rate |

Also unreadable **as data**, not just as a toggle: the **Recently Viewed** and **Recently Shared** collections are **not exposed as fetchable `PHAssetCollection`s** to third-party apps — Apple keeps the user's own viewing/sharing history private even from apps with Full Access. (The collections themselves are Apple-confirmed to exist: iOS 26 iPhone User Guide, verbatim — *"You can also find the Recently Saved collection below Utilities along with the Recently Viewed and Recently Shared collections."*)

---

### 15.16 macOS divergences (load-bearing — our desktop node is macOS)

⚠️ **Trap:** shipping iOS strings in a macOS UI would be wrong in **at least three** places.

| Concept | iOS | macOS |
|---|---|---|
| Reset the people graph | **`Reset People & Pets Suggestions`** (`Settings > Apps > Photos`) | **`Reset Suggested People & Pets`** (`Photos > Settings > General`) — different word order |
| Reset memories | `Reset Suggested Memories` | `Reset Suggested Memories` (same string; `Photos > Settings > General`) |
| Enhanced Visual Search | `Settings > Apps > Photos` | **`Photos > Settings > General`** — not a Settings-app pane at all |
| Hidden album | **Visible by default**; toggled via `Settings > Apps > Photos > Show Hidden Album` | **OFF by default**; toggled from the **menu bar**: `View > Show Hidden Photo Album` — not a Settings switch |
| Keep originals from iCloud | `Download and Keep Originals` | **`Download Originals to this Mac`** |
| Memory suppression | `Feature This Person Less` / `Never Feature This Person` | `Feature Less` → **`Feature Fewer Memories Like This`** |
| Screenshot HDR | `Settings > General > Screen Capture > Format` | **Screenshot app** "Capture Format" setting (macOS Tahoe 26) |

Also: `SensitiveContentAnalysis` has a **macOS 14.0** floor and is an Objective-C framework — reaching it from **Electron requires a native-module bridge**. That is a real engineering constraint, not a footnote.

---

### 15.17 Open items that require a physical iOS 26.5.2 device audit

Do **not** guess at these. Do **not** put them in a spec, a support doc, or user-facing copy until someone has opened Settings on a real device.

1. **The full row list, row order, and section headers of `Settings > Apps > Photos`.** Apple publishes no enumeration. (Closes six of the ten uncertainties in ~90 seconds.)
2. **`View Full HDR`** — the string appears on **no apple.com page**. Exact label casing, current location, and default state all unknown. Only Apple Community threads and press.
3. **`Cellular Data` / `Unlimited Updates`** — "Unlimited Updates" appears on **zero** apple.com pages; every source gives the dead pre-iOS-18 path `Settings > Photos > Cellular Data`. Evidence suggests it **relocated** to the iCloud pane along with the other iCloud-Photos controls. ⚠️ **The widely-cited "150 MB per day" cellular throttle figure traces only to forums/blogs. Do NOT repeat it.**
4. **`Transfer to Mac or PC` (section header) and `Automatic` (the option opposite Keep Originals)** — historical labels, unsourceable on current apple.com.
5. **`Show Recently Viewed & Shared`** — toggle label corroborated by two independent non-Apple sources; **on no apple.com page**. The *collections* are Apple-confirmed; the *toggle* is not.
6. **`Auto-Play Motion` and `Loop Videos`** — believed to be two toggles in `Settings > Apps > Photos` (`Loop Videos` added iOS 18.2), but **both labels are third-party-sourced only** (MacRumors).
7. **Whether `Show Featured Content` / `Show Holiday Events` are mirrored into `Settings > Apps > Photos`** in addition to the in-app account pane. Apple documents only the in-app location.
8. **Hidden assets under Full Access** — the Apple-legal-page vs PhotoKit-doc contradiction (§15.3). **Resolve empirically before designing the backup/completeness story.**
9. **Whether the applied Photographic Style is readable from an asset's metadata.** No public PhotoKit API exists; needs empirical inspection of a real iPhone 16/17 HEIF capture. Do not guess at private metadata keys.
10. **The full contents of the in-app Photos account pane** (`Collections` → account, top-right). Never enumerated; Apple is actively relocating controls into it.

---

### 15.18 What this means for us

**A. Ingest correctness — the three independent ways the bytes are not there.** Optimize iPhone Storage (**on by default**), Low Data Mode (per-network, iCloud-synced, silently pauses iCloud Photos), and Limited Access all mean the originals may be absent. Therefore, in the phone-side ingest:

1. **Always set `PHImageRequestOptions.isNetworkAccessAllowed = true`** on the ML/offload path (it defaults to **`false`**), and use **`PHAssetResourceManager`** for true originals.
2. **Always check `PHImageResultIsInCloudKey`** and treat "in cloud" as a **distinct, retryable ingest state** — never as a failure.
3. **Record per-asset provenance** (true original vs optimized rendition vs shared-album downscale) in `workspace_db`, so we can re-embed later and **never mix rendition quality into calibration statistics**. Our detection-pipeline thesis is that the *measurement layer* is the bottleneck; this is exactly where it leaks.
4. Surface an honest **"N photos live only in iCloud — downloading X of N"** progress UI, Wi-Fi-driven and pausable. Apple never shows this.

**B. Permissions.** Query with **`.readWrite`** or we will never observe `.limited` and will misclassify limited users as authorized. Branch **`.restricted`** separately from `.denied` — for `.denied`, deep-link to Settings; for `.restricted`, say plainly *"photo access is blocked by Screen Time or a device-management policy — an administrator has to change this"* and **do not dangle a Settings button**. Set `PHPhotoLibraryPreventAutomaticLimitedAccessAlert = true` and call `presentLimitedLibraryPicker(from:)` at a moment we choose, with our own explanation. Register a `PHPhotoLibraryChangeObserver` so a widened selection is picked up immediately. Ship a genuinely useful **degraded `.limited` mode** (index the selected set; be honest that cross-age matching and library-wide semantic search need the full library) rather than a "grant access to continue" dead end — the dead end is what tanks conversion. Our strongest pre-prompt argument for Full Access is exactly our architecture: **no cloud account; the ML runs on the user's own Mac.**

**C. Hidden assets — a product/ethics decision we must make explicitly.** Per the verifier, **Full Access defeats the Hidden-album lock**: hidden (often intimate) photos will flow into our ingest and our face index **unless we filter them ourselves**. Run the device test in §15.3 first. Whichever way it resolves, we should **decide and state** whether hidden assets enter the NSFW pipeline, the face index, and the backup set. If the API doc turns out to be right instead, then our library counts will **legitimately disagree** with Photos' own count — never present that as a sync error; ship an explicit *"N items are in your locked Hidden album and are not visible to any third-party app"* explainer.

**D. Safe Mode / NSFW — adopt `SensitiveContentAnalysis`.** Request the entitlement **`com.apple.developer.sensitivecontentanalysis.client`**, read `SCSensitivityAnalyzer.analysisPolicy`, and **honour it**: if `.disabled`, do not blur (respect the user's explicit system-level choice); if `.descriptiveInterventions`, show the richer intervention. Layer our hybrid ONNX gate + threshold profiles **on top of**, not instead of, Apple's classifier — it gives us a free, Apple-quality, fully-on-device **second opinion to ensemble against**, and a reference signal for tuning thresholds and measuring false-positive rate against our existing temperature calibration. Adopting also places us in the `Settings > Privacy & Security > Sensitive Content Warning` per-app list — free, high-trust placement. ⚠️ **But note the disanalogy: Apple's system never scans the user's own library.** There is **no Apple precedent** for library-wide NSFW classification. We cannot say "Apple does this too." The privacy framing is entirely on us, and *"app scans your photos for nudity"* is a phrase that ends the product if we get it wrong — lead with **local, on-device/on-your-own-Mac, no cloud.**
On the desktop: `SensitiveContentAnalysis` is macOS 14.0+ Objective-C — budget for an **Electron native-module bridge**.

**E. ML accuracy — measure, never assume.** We cannot read a single capture setting, and several of them systematically shift the input distribution:
- **Prioritize Faster Shooting is ON by default and unreadable** ⇒ per-photo quality is **non-stationary within one library**, with no asset flag to detect it. This is the concrete cause behind our "measurement layer is the bottleneck" thesis, and the reason the quality-gate dead-code bug mattered. Keep a **per-asset quality score** in `workspace_db` and use it to (a) pick the best exemplar per person for cross-age matching and (b) suppress low-confidence NSFW verdicts on visibly degraded frames.
- **Photographic Styles** apply a **library-wide colour shift** (e.g. Ethereal / Amber), which moves skin tones — which moves face-embedding distributions and, most dangerously, **NSFW-classifier scores**, since skin-tone-adjacent features are exactly what those models key on. Detect a library-wide colour-statistics shift at index time and **normalize before embedding**; do not assume neutral sRGB input. A **per-user colour prior** beats a better backbone here.
- **HDR gain maps**: `ingest/safety` and `embed/engine` must make a **deliberate** choice between the tone-mapped SDR base and the HDR-composited image. Feeding an unexpectedly bright HDR composite shifts NSFW and face-detector thresholds. Pin this down explicitly.
- **DNG/ProRAW is not display-referred.** Never feed a linear DNG straight into a CLIP or face model trained on sRGB JPEGs — decode through a proper render (respect the DNG's baseline exposure/tone curve) first, or the embeddings are quietly wrong.
- Ingest must handle, minimum: **HEIF (10-bit, gain map), JPEG, DNG/ProRAW, HEVC, H.264, ProRes**.

**F. Data hygiene — quarantine the junk.** Shared-album assets (`PHAsset.sourceType == .typeCloudShared`) are **downscaled and non-editable** — indexing them as originals produces bad embeddings and corrupts face-quality/calibration statistics. **Screenshots** (`PHAssetMediaSubtype.photoScreenshot`) are pure noise for face/CLIP and skew NSFW calibration (memes, web pages) — and on iOS 26 they may be **HEIF/HDR, not PNG/SDR**. **Shared-with-You / Recently Saved** content injects strangers' faces from group chats. Tag all three at ingest, exclude or down-weight them by default, **exclude them from calibration**, and never let them create new People entries without confirmation. Give the user a visible *"exclude screenshots"* / *"exclude photos I didn't take"* switch — iOS 26's own Photos Library filters (including a **"Shared With You"** filter) are Apple quietly admitting this is a real problem.

**G. Live Photos are the default capture mode**, so a large fraction of any library is Live Photos. Ingest must treat a Live Photo as **still + paired video**: index the **still (key frame)** for face/CLIP/NSFW, and **preserve the paired video byte-exactly** on backup — dropping it is silent data loss users discover a year later. **Opportunity:** because we can read the paired video (`PHAssetResource` / `PHLivePhoto`), we get **multiple views of the same face for free** from the Live Photo's ~3 seconds — a genuine accuracy edge for face recognition and especially cross-age matching, costing only decode time on the desktop node.

**H. LAN sync — be byte-exact, and say so.** Apple's **default** USB-import behaviour **transcodes HEIF/HEVC to JPEG/H.264**. Ours must be **keep-originals always**, with transcoding as an explicit, per-export user choice: pull via `PHAssetResourceManager` and transfer the unmodified resource (HEIF/HEVC/DNG/ProRes), preserving the **gain map, depth map, Live Photo paired video, and adjustment sidecar**. Add an **integrity check** (hash of the on-device `PHAssetResource` vs what landed on the desktop) and **surface it** — that turns a hidden Apple failure mode into a visible trust signal. **Constraint:** ProRAW (~75 MB/photo at 48 MP) and 4K ProRes are huge — the LAN protocol needs per-asset size awareness, resumability, and probably a **"rendered proxy for ML, original for backup"** split, or one ProRes clip stalls a sync.

**I. Transport politeness.** LAN-first sync sidesteps cellular in the common case — **say that, it's a selling point.** Still: default to Wi-Fi-only, honour `allowsConstrainedNetworkAccess = false` under Low Data Mode (Apple's own services do), never offload heavy ML over an expensive path, and — unlike Apple — show a **visible, explained** *"paused: waiting for Wi-Fi — N items queued"* state instead of stalling silently. Since we cannot read Apple's cellular preference, we own our own equivalent and must not try to mirror theirs.

**J. Motion accessibility — a hard requirement that collides with our maximalist UI direction.** Our design language is deliberately bold, vivid, alive. That is the right default — but it **must degrade**. Build **one motion-policy hook** that reads `UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled` **and** `UIAccessibility.isVideoAutoplayEnabled` **plus** our own in-app setting, and route **every** animation, living background, autoplaying Live Photo and video preview through it. Do not sprinkle checks. Provide a **static-but-still-beautiful** fallback (rich colour and depth without movement) — "reduce motion" must not mean "reduce craft." Honour Limit Frame Rate by not fighting for 120 Hz on ProMotion when the user asked for 60 (note: **Limit Frame Rate and Auto-Play Animated Images have no public read API** — we can only honour the two we can read, plus our own setting). Ignoring these is both an accessibility failure and an App Store review risk, and it is cheap now versus retrofitting across seven tabs later.

**K. UX opportunities Apple leaves on the table.**
- **Collapse the two-toggle Hidden design** into one clear model: *Hidden album: Visible / Hidden from view / Locked* — with **per-album granularity** (lock Hidden without locking Recently Deleted), which Apple does not offer.
- **Per-person, reversible suppression.** Apple's Reset rows are **all-or-nothing** and Apple documents them under **Personal Safety**. Give `crossage_fr`'s person entity a first-class, reversible **`suppressed` flag** (not a deletion), an audit trail of what was suppressed and when, per-person restore, **and** a "reset all" escape hatch for parity. Treat suppression as a **safety feature**: make it work **offline and instantly**, never eventually-consistent over LAN sync. Given we do face recognition and cross-age matching, we are *uniquely capable* of resurfacing painful faces — an "excluded people" list is a requirement, not a nice-to-have, and our Memories/Featured equivalent must be opt-out-able **before** it first surfaces content, not after.
- **Viewing history stays local.** If we keep a recently-viewed/recently-shared history, ship the off switch **on day one** and a one-tap "clear viewing history" — and **never let it cross the LAN boundary** to the desktop by default. Apple shipped the feature first and the off switch years later.
- **Ship our own HDR view control** (we cannot read Apple's), and beat it by making it **three-state: Off / Auto / Full**. Our RN viewer **must** make an explicit HDR decision — `UIImageView.preferredImageDynamicRange` (iOS 17+) / `UIImage.DynamicRange`, honouring the asset's `PHAsset.mediaSubtypes & photoHDR` bit. If we naively render SDR while Apple Photos renders full HDR, **our app simply looks worse side-by-side on the same photo** — a first-impression killer.
- **Landmark/semantic search is our single best competitive wedge.** Apple's Enhanced Visual Search is network-touching (encrypted embedding + homomorphic matching + OHTTP relay) and **region-gated** (*"isn't available in all countries or regions"*). Ours runs on the user's own Mac over an E2E-encrypted LAN: strictly local, every region, no server. **Requirement:** the desktop CLIP/semantic index must actually **cover landmarks**, not just objects and scenes — ship a landmark-capable embedding or a local gazetteer, or the claim collapses. This matters most for the users with **no geodata at all**, for whom visual place inference is the only way to answer *"where was this?"*
- **Managed/child devices:** Screen Time can restrict **Intelligence & Siri features**, so Apple's system-intelligence features may be unavailable there while ours — running on the user's own desktop over LAN — still work. Niche, but genuinely differentiating, and it costs nothing to be correct.
## 16. Accessibility

Apple's accessibility story around Photos is four separate surfaces, not one: (1) **Assistive Access ships a genuinely separate, radically simplified Photos app** with its own IA and exactly two supporter-set toggles — a real parity surface, and since iOS/iPadOS 26 a third-party API surface too; (2) **VoiceOver Recognition** (Image Descriptions, Text Recognition, Screen Recognition, Explore Image) is the OS auto-describing photos that apps failed to label — plus Photos' own user-authored per-photo **Image Description** field; (3) a scattered set of **system settings** (Motion, Display & Text Size, Zoom, Voice Control, Guided Access, Per-App Settings) that silently gate how a photo app is allowed to behave; and (4) the **enforcement layer**, which is not App Review.

The single most important thing an implementer must know: **App Store review does not reject apps for being inaccessible — the real gate is the Accessibility Nutrition Labels**, whose bar is "users must be able to complete all of the common tasks of your app using that feature," and whose truthfulness *is* policed under the metadata guideline. And the single most important technical fact: **no React Native list library — not FlashList, not Legend List, not RN's own virtualized-lists — ships any accessibility code at all.** For a virtualized photo grid, 100% of screen-reader semantics is ours to write, including a native Android module.
