### 18.x What this means for us

Our architecture (offline-first React Native phone + E2E-encrypted LAN + Electron/Python macOS desktop as the heavy-compute node, no cloud account) is **not merely a privacy preference — on this platform it is the only technically available path.** There is no public iCloud Photos API. The only ways to reach a user's library are on-device PhotoKit and the local macOS library. That fact should end any internal debate about a server-side shortcut.

**Requirements (must do):**

1. **Windows desktop build is the highest-leverage item in this entire section.** Apple ships a file-sync client and *zero* intelligence on Windows — no faces, no Memories, no search. Our Python ML core (FR, cross-age, CLIP semantic search, NSFW gating) has literally no competitor there. **Ingest must discover the iCloud Photos folder at `C:\Users\<user>\Pictures\iCloud Photos\Photos`.** The OneDrive-displaced variant (`C:\Users\<user>\iCloud Photos\Photos`) is a plausible but **unverified** path — probe for it defensively rather than hardcoding it as fact. **Cold-start on Windows has no `ZPERSON` to bootstrap from — the onboarding flow must not assume Apple labels exist.**
2. **Bootstrap from Apple's face data on the Mac — but scope it correctly.** Import `ZPERSON` named People as pre-labeled enrollment data ("we already know your 42 people" is a killer onboarding moment), use those labels as an **eval benchmark on the user's own library** (the only benchmark that matters), and use Apple's per-face signals as a free prior for our quality gate. ⚠️ **Scope to what actually exists on Photos 5+:** `quality`, roll/pitch/yaw, and the type enums (`age_type`, `gender_type`, `glasses_type`, `facial_hair_type`, `hair_color_type`, `eye_state`, `smile_type`, `face_type`, `manual`). **There is no blur score and no eye/mouth position** on modern libraries. Pin the osxphotos version; handle schema drift across macOS releases; require Full Disk Access in onboarding; state plainly in privacy copy that we read the local library DB and never upload it.
3. **Face/identity write-back to Apple Photos is impossible.** AppleScript cannot touch faces and cannot delete; PhotoKit exposes no person/face writing. Design the Apple-Photos relationship as a **one-way enrichment import**. Do not build UI that implies we can fix the user's Apple People album.
4. **Referenced-mode libraries must work.** If the user unticked "Copy items to the Photos library," the originals live outside the `.photoslibrary` bundle. Our ingest must follow the references (osxphotos gives us referenced-vs-copied state and original paths). Also handle the multi-library case, and know the footgun: **switching libraries turns iCloud Photos and Shared Albums off.**
5. **The watch app must be architected as `desktop ML → phone → WCSession.transferFile → on-watch cache`.** There is no library on the watch. Build our own storage cap and eviction. **Budget paired physical hardware for testing — `transferFile` does not run in the Simulator.**
6. **Nested albums from day one.** Do not bake a flat album list into the RN data model — Apple's Folders (albums-in-folders-in-folders) are Mac-only and don't sync; ours should be hierarchical *and* sync.
7. **Ship a first-class manual face-box editor on mobile.** Apple has proven manual correction is necessary (its own detector misses faces) and then confined the good version to the Mac. A draw-a-box-and-name-it flow on the phone that feeds corrections back to the desktop as human-verified enrollment labels is a double win: better than Apple on the phone, *and* it feeds our cross-age pipeline. **Steal the vocabulary users already know:** "Merge", "Review More Photos", "This is Not [name]", "Make Key Photo", and "feature less often" — the last is an emotional-safety primitive (ex-partners, deceased relatives) we must have.

**Flagship opportunities (ranked):**

1. **Smart Albums that sync.** Apple's most powerful organizational feature is Mac-only and **explicitly does not sync** ("Smart Albums that you create on your Mac don't appear in Photos on your iPhone or iPad"), and cannot be created on iOS at all. We can evaluate criteria on the desktop over *our ML outputs* — `person = Mia AND age-in-photo < 5 AND semantic ≈ "birthday" AND safe` — and mirror the result to the phone over LAN. ⚠️ **Before marketing this as "Apple can't do person-based smart albums," physically check the Smart Album criteria list on a Mac** — Apple documents only examples, and whether a Person criterion exists is **unconfirmed**. The claim that is safe today is the sourced one: **they don't sync.**
2. **Depth/parallax for the whole library, on every platform.** Apple created demand for spatial photos and then withheld the API everywhere except visionOS (`Spatial3DImage.generate()` is visionOS 26.0 only; the iOS 26 Lock Screen effect has no public generation API). Adding **monocular depth estimation to the Python desktop pipeline** and syncing lightweight depth maps to the phone gives us depth-parallax viewing on **the entire library**, on **any photo**, on **iPhone, Mac, and Windows** — where Apple offers no API at all. This is a textbook fit for our offload-heavy-ML-to-desktop architecture. ⚠️ Do **not** justify it with "Apple's Portraits face requires Portrait-mode capture" — that claim is **refuted**; Apple's Portraits face works on ordinary photos of people, dogs, cats, and landscapes.
3. **Person-scoped watch sync.** Apple's watch sync is structurally album-based; there is no person-scoped primitive. "Sync 200 photos of Mia, best-quality-first, refreshed weekly" is something Apple cannot offer. Pair it with a **person-of-the-day photo complication / Smart Stack widget** ("Mia, 3 years ago today") — the closest legal thing to a photo watch face, powered by exactly our FR + cross-age stack. Offer a **size budget (MB)** as well as a count — Apple only offers a "Photos Limit" whose values it doesn't even document.
4. **Apple TV, correctly framed.** The screen saver is closed (no third-party API — plan around it, not for it). But **PhotoKit is available on tvOS 10.0+ and needs no entitlement**, so a native tvOS app *can* render a full-screen ambient "frame mode." Two clean wins over Apple: (a) Apple's tvOS Photos is **default-profile-only** — every other family member is locked out; our tvOS app authenticates over **our LAN sync**, not iCloud profiles, so *anyone's* library works; (b) **tvOS Photos has no search** — CLIP-style semantic search on a TV remote is genuinely novel. ⚠️ **Do not depend on tvOS PhotoKit until a hardware spike establishes what it actually sees** — source over our LAN transport instead, which sidesteps the question entirely. **Sequence:** ship **AirPlay slideshow** from phone/desktop first (a fraction of the cost, no tvOS app, no review), then decide whether a native tvOS app + **Top Shelf carousel** earns its keep. ⚠️ Note the hardware gate on Apple's own Portraits screen saver (Apple TV 4K 2nd gen+) — Apple's "faces on the big screen" is itself gated.
5. **A "TV Frame" system-album exporter.** The tvOS screen-saver source is **album-shaped**. The only way to get our curation onto the most-loved TV surface is to have our engine create and continuously refresh a real album / Shared Album the user points the screen saver at. Legitimate, cheap, and it lands our ML inside Apple's own ambient surface.
6. **A Photos editing extension as a distribution wedge.** `PHContentEditingController` works on **iOS, iPadOS, macOS, Mac Catalyst, and visionOS** from **one extension** (not tvOS). Users of *Apple* Photos would see our capabilities — "Redact faces," "Blur NSFW," "Enhance" — from inside Apple's own app, with zero migration. ⚠️ It is **edit-scoped**: one asset at a time, no library enumeration. It's a marketing/utility surface, not a data pipe. Mac-only bonus: a `PHProjectExtensionController` project could offer "build a face-recognized photo book of Mia, 2019–2026" inside Apple Photos.
7. **visionOS as a halo demo.** `ImagePresentationComponent.Spatial3DImage` + `generate()` gives third parties Apple's own generative capability for free. Apple treats "spatial" as a media *type* (a tab); because we can generate depth for anything, we should treat it as a **viewing mode available on every photo** — which makes a user's entire legacy library immersive. ⚠️ visionOS 26 minimum; Vision Pro hardware needed in the lab; the Simulator limitation on `generate()` is **unverified — confirm on device**. Also **non-destructive by construction** (Apple's own Undo Create Spatial sets that expectation) — sync the *depth decision*, not the heavy rendition, over LAN.

**Do not build:**

- **A custom Apple Watch face.** No API. `CLKWatchFaceLibrary.addWatchFace(at:)` installs only **pre-authored, Xcode-bundled** `.watchface` files, and must be triggered by a user tap on an "Add Apple Watch Face" button. Runtime synthesis of a `.watchface` containing the user's own photos is **undocumented reverse engineering** (WatchFaceDumper) — a prove-or-kill spike at most, never a committed feature. Compounding risk: **ClockKit complications are deprecated in watchOS 10+**; the surrounding framework is in maintenance.
- **A tvOS screen saver.** No API exists.
- **Anything for CarPlay.** No photo/gallery entitlement category exists and none will.
- **Anything for the rumored Apple smart display.** Unshipped, unannounced, no SDK, press-only.
- **Publishing into the visionOS Spatial Gallery.** Editorially curated by Apple; no submission API.
## 19. iPad, Import/Export Fidelity & Automation

This section covers three surfaces that share one property: they are where Apple Photos is *structurally* weakest, and therefore where a competing app has the most room. (1) **iPad** — iPadOS 26 rebuilt both the Photos shell (sidebar + Library/Collections split) and the platform underneath it (a real windowing system, a system menu bar, keyboard/pointer expectations); an app that ships a stretched phone layout reads as unfinished on iPad in the 26 era. (2) **Import/export fidelity** — Apple loses data at four separate boundaries, each with different rules, and *none* of them is labelled in the UI as lossy. (3) **Automation** — Apple publishes an App Intents "Photos" domain that a third-party app can adopt to inherit Siri/Apple-Intelligence vocabulary, and it conspicuously has no schema for search-by-person, search-by-content, or content safety.

The single most important thing to know: **Apple documents that its own transports transcode.** HEIF→JPEG and HEVC→H.264 conversion on AirDrop/Messages/email/USB is Apple's stated behavior, and the only share path that preserves the edit stack ("All Photos Data") works over AirDrop and iCloud links *only*. A hash-verified, byte-exact, full-`PHAssetResource` transfer over our own LAN channel is therefore a fidelity claim Apple cannot make about its own tooling — but it is only true if our sync copies every resource of an asset, not one rendered image.

⚠️ **Trap (version):** `apple.com/os/ipados` now describes **iPadOS 27** (announced WWDC 2026, in beta, GA expected ~Sept 2026 — Spatial Reframing, an Extend tool, enhanced Clean Up, photo/video slideshows with duration + transition + music options, full-resolution iCloud Shared Albums). Current shipping is the 26 line (iOS 26.5.2, 26.6 in beta). Anyone sourcing "current iPad Photos behavior" from that marketing URL will spec against beta APIs. **Use the iPadOS 26 User Guide as shipping truth.**

---

### 19.1 iPadOS 26 Photos: the sidebar shell

iPad Photos in iPadOS 26 is a **sidebar app**: a collapsible sidebar over a Library/Collections split. Apple's "What's new in iPadOS 26" page, verbatim:

> "Photos. An updated design makes it easier to switch between your Library and Collections. You can now customize how Collections appear—reorder them, choose which ones to pin, and select from three display sizes: larger tiles, a denser grid, or a layout that highlights the top row."

Library navigation is via **Years / Months / All** buttons. Apple's iPad guide, verbatim: *"To focus on the images in your library, tap [icon] to close the sidebar, then use the Years, Months, and All buttons to navigate. To show the sidebar again, tap [icon]."*

⚠️ **Trap:** the iPad sidebar is **not** a long-standing pattern. The iPadOS 18 version of the same Apple page describes a single unified scroll — no sidebar, no Library/Collections split, no Years/Months/All ("Below your library, your photos and videos are organized into curated collections like Recent Days, Trips, and People & Pets"). The sidebar was **absent in the immediately preceding release and reintroduced in iPadOS 26**. Do not build a "we already match the long-standing iPad pattern" argument on it — users' muscle memory here is one release old.

Note the idiom split: on **iPhone**, iOS 26 exposes the same content as *"separate tabs for Library and Collections views"* (iOS 26 newsroom). Apple ships genuinely different navigation shells per device idiom rather than one responsive layout.

### 19.2 iPad Photos View Options (verified verbatim labels)

Path: **Photos > [more button] > View Options**. These are Apple's exact strings — copy the vocabulary, not a paraphrase.

| Control | Apple's exact wording | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Zoom In | "Enlarge the size of the photo and video thumbnails: Tap Zoom In." | Bigger thumbnails |
| Zoom Out | "Reduce the size of the photo and video thumbnails, to see more at the same time: Tap Zoom Out." | Denser grid |
| Aspect Ratio Grid | "View each photo or video thumbnail in the dimension it was captured in: Tap Aspect Ratio Grid." | Native aspect thumbnails |
| Square Photo Grid | "To return to square thumbnails, tap Square Photo Grid." | Square thumbnails (default) |
| Screenshots | "Hide screenshots: Tap Screenshots." | Suppress screenshots from the grid |
| Shared Library Badge | "Hide the shared library badge on thumbnails: Tap Shared Library Badge." | Suppress the badge overlay |
| Shared with You | "Hide photos and videos shared with you in Messages: Tap Shared with You." | Suppress Messages-sourced items |
| From My Mac | "Hide photos and videos you manually added from your Mac: Tap From My Mac." | Suppress manually-imported items |

Also: **pinch-to-zoom on the grid works** — *"While you're viewing the library, pinch the screen to zoom in or out."*

Two things to note. First, **"Hide screenshots" is one of the most-wanted Photos behaviors** and Apple buries it two menus deep. Second, **"From My Mac" proves Photos tracks import provenance internally** but exposes exactly one crude toggle over it — no provenance browser, no "where did this photo come from?" answer anywhere in the UI.

### 19.3 iPadOS 26 Collections: reorder, pin, display sizes, library scoping

| Capability | Apple's behavior / exact wording |
|---|---|
| Reorder | "Scroll to the bottom of the screen, tap Reorder, then drag a collection into a new position." |
| Pin | Pinning applies to **collections *and* albums**, grouped under a **"Pinned"** heading. Touch-and-hold gives a **Pin / Unpin** shortcut; there is an **"Any Collection or Album"** picker. |
| Display sizes | What's-new page: "three display sizes: larger tiles, a denser grid, or a layout that highlights the top row." The Browse-Collections guide page separately describes enlarge / reduce / "Show the default display", plus **"Collapse All"** to hide the collection tiles entirely — effectively **3 sizes + a no-image state**. |
| Library scoping | ⚠️ **Not** general "scope to a specific photo library." It appears **only if you're part of an iCloud Shared Photo Library**, and the options are exactly **Both Libraries / Personal Library / Shared Library**. |
| Autoplay | **"Auto-Play Motion and Loop Videos" is ON by default** in Collections. Videos and Live Photos autoplay when you tap Collections; the off-switch lives under the account menu. |

### 19.4 iPadOS 26 windowing — the resilience matrix

iPadOS 26 shipped a new windowing system. Settings path and modes, verbatim: *"Tap Multitasking & Gestures. To turn Windowed Apps on, select Windowed Apps. To turn it off, select Full Screen Apps, or select Stage Manager to multitask another way."* Window behavior: *"Resize a window: Drag the resize handle in the bottom-right corner of the window. Move a window: Drag it from the top."* Familiar close/minimize/resize/tile controls; **Exposé** shows all open windows.

⚠️ **Trap (this is the one that will corrupt your QA matrix): iPadOS 26 did NOT replace Slide Over.** Slide Over was **removed in iPadOS 26.0 and RESTORED in iPadOS 26.2**. Apple's 26.2 release note: *"This update enhances the new windowing system introduced in iPadOS 26 with familiar drag and drop gestures for tiling app windows and creating a Slide Over window,"* with a Multitasking bullet: *"Multitasking gestures to quickly tile windows or place an app in Slide Over by dragging app icons from the Dock."* The current iPad guide documents **Enter Slide Over / Exit Slide Over** as live features. **Slide Over must be in the windowing test matrix.**

⚠️ **Trap (device gating): Windowed Apps is NOT an M-series feature.** Apple lists support on **iPad (8th generation and later), iPad Air (3rd generation and later), iPad mini (5th generation and later), iPad Pro 11-inch (1st generation and later)**. A prior research wave asserted an "M2/M3/M4-only" restriction for external-display window movement — that specific gating is **UNSOURCED**; Apple's external-display page says only "compatible models" and publishes no M-series list. **Do not ship a model check based on it** — it would wrongly exclude most of the installed base.

Also automatable: Shortcuts gained a **"Set Multitasking Mode"** action in the **26.4** cycle (iPadOS and macOS) — the multitasking mode is itself scriptable, which matters for a windowing-resilience test harness.

**Consequence for layout:** windowed apps get **arbitrary continuous widths**. There is no fixed breakpoint set to design against. Multiple windows of the same app require **UISceneDelegate** support.

### 19.5 iPadOS 26 menu bar

iPadOS 26 added a system menu bar and **developers can customize it**. Apple Newsroom (iPadOS 26 press release): *"With a new menu bar, users can access the commands available in an app with a simple swipe down from the top of the display, or by moving their cursor to the top… Additionally, developers can now customize the menu bar in their own apps."*

Apple's support article "Learn iPad keyboard shortcuts" has a section literally headed **"See keyboard shortcuts in the menu bar"**: *"To see a list of shortcuts that you can use with an app, swipe down from the middle of the top edge of the iPad screen, then select a menu."* So Apple actively directs users to the menu bar to *discover* an app's shortcuts — an empty menu bar is a visible, user-facing failure.

- **Mode restriction:** iPad guide — *"To see the menu bar for the active app, you must have Windowed Apps or Stage Manager selected in Settings."* It does not appear in Full Screen Apps mode.
- **API:** **`UIMenuBuilder`** (override `buildMenu(with:)`; update `UIMenuSystem.main`).
- **HIG constraint:** Apple's HIG says the menu bar *"should show all commands from your app, even those without keyboard shortcuts,"* and unavailable commands must stay **visible but disabled — never hidden**.

### 19.6 Keyboard and pointer vocabulary

Every shortcut below is in Apple's published iPad shortcut list, verbatim:

| Shortcut | Apple's description |
|---|---|
| Command-A | "Select all items." |
| Command-X | Cut |
| Command-C | "Copy the selected item to the clipboard." |
| Command-V | "Paste contents of the clipboard." |
| Command-Z | "Undo previous action." |
| Shift-Command-Z | Redo |
| Command-W | "Close a window." |
| Command-M | "Minimize a window." |

Also documented on Apple's list: Globe-F (enter/exit full screen), Command-Tab, Command-Space (Spotlight), Command-Shift-3 (screenshot), Command-Shift-4 (screenshot + open Markup), and window tiling via **Control-Globe-Arrow** and **Control-Shift-Globe-Arrow**.

⚠️ **Trap:** Apple lists **Command-W and Command-M under "Window management"** — they are *system window commands*, not per-app editing commands. Honoring them means **participating in the windowing system** (scenes, window lifecycle), not merely wiring a JS handler.

Pointer/trackpad support has existed since **iPadOS 13.4 (released March 24, 2020)**.

*Unverified:* iPad Photos' **Copy Edits / Paste Edits** via Shift-Command-C / Shift-Command-V is reported by a third-party tutorial and is **not on Apple's shortcut list**. Treat as unverified; confirm on a physical device before relying on it.

### 19.7 Drag and drop

Apple documents the multi-item drag gesture exactly:

> "Touch and hold the first selected item, drag it slightly, and continue holding it. While still holding the first item, tap additional items with another finger. A badge indicates the number of selected items. Drag all of the items together."

Single item: *"Touch and hold the item until it lifts up… Drag it to the other app."* Apple itself flags the common failure: *"(Not all third-party apps support drag and drop.)"*

⚠️ **Trap (vocabulary):** Apple **never calls this a "pile."** "Pile" is not Apple vocabulary and must not appear in our UI copy or specs.

⚠️ **Trap (do not chase a bug that does not exist):** iPadOS 26.2 fixed **drag-and-drop *multitasking*** — dragging *app icons from the Dock* to tile a window or create a Slide Over. It did **not** fix inter-app *content* drag-and-drop. Those are different subsystems. A brief claiming "photo dragging between apps was broken and repaired in 26.2" will send an engineer chasing a bug that was never filed.

**API:** `UIDragInteraction` / `UIDropInteraction` with `NSItemProvider`. **What you put in the `NSItemProvider` determines fidelity** — vend the original file (with its real UTType, e.g. `public.heic`) rather than a re-encoded `UIImage`, or every drag silently strips HEIC/EXIF and any auxiliary data.

### 19.8 Markup and the reed pen (PencilKit)

⚠️ **Trap (a prior wave got this wrong):** the **reed pen is an iPadOS 26 feature, not an iPhone Photos feature.** Apple Newsroom, iPadOS 26 press release (June 9, 2025), verbatim:

> "Available in the tool palette, the new reed pen uses stroke-angle presets to enable a traditional calligraphy experience with Apple Pencil or touch in apps like Notes, Preview, Freeform, and Journal; when using Markup; and in third-party apps using the PencilKit API."

Facts that check out: it lives in the **tool palette**; it works **"with Apple Pencil or touch"** (no Pencil required); **third parties get it free via PencilKit**; Apple names **Notes, Preview, Freeform, Journal** as first-party adopters; it was announced for **iPadOS only**. Apple's iOS 26 newsroom release contains **zero** occurrences of "reed pen", "Apple Pencil", or "Markup".

*Unverified:* whether the reed pen also renders in the PencilKit tool palette on iPhone. Because it ships via PencilKit it plausibly might, but **Apple does not document it there — do not claim iPhone support.** Needs a physical-device audit to confirm.

Markup itself works inside Photos on iPad, with pen/marker/pencil tools, a ruler, a lasso, opacity and line-weight controls, and a Grid/Spectrum/Sliders color picker. **API:** `PKCanvasView` + `PKToolPicker` — adopting them inherits the reed pen and every future Apple tool, including Apple Pencil Pro squeeze/barrel-roll/haptics.

---

### 19.9 Import: the camera-adapter path and its hard limits

Apple's flow: connect a **Lightning to SD Card Camera Reader**, **Lightning to USB 3 Camera Adapter**, **Lightning to USB Camera Adapter**, or **Apple USB-C to SD Card Reader**, then open Photos and go to the import surface. Supported protocols: **Picture Transfer Protocol (PTP)** and **Mass Storage Device protocol**. Supported card types: **SDSC, SDHC, miniSD, microSD, MMC, SDXC**.

**Hard limits, verbatim from Apple:**

> "Flash or USB thumb drives aren't supported for image importing."

> "Apple camera adapters can import only content that was captured by digital cameras. You might not be able to import content that was renamed, edited, or copied to the digital camera or SD card."

That second sentence is the one that bites a migration product: **a card full of files someone copied on will silently fail to import.**

**USB-3 speed gating (confirmed, exact models):** *"If you're using a Lightning to USB 3 Camera Adapter, these iPad models transfer data at USB 3 speeds: iPad Pro 12.9-inch (1st and 2nd generation), iPad Pro 10.5-inch. iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, iPhone 16 Pro, and iPhone 16 Pro Max support USB-3 transfer speeds. All other adapters and iOS devices use USB 2 speeds."*

⚠️ **Trap (copy):** Apple's own vocabulary is **inconsistent across surfaces** — support article 118280 says *"tap the Imports tab"* while the iPad User Guide says *"Tap Import."* Verify the current string on a physical device before writing UI copy that claims to mirror Apple.

**What a third party can and cannot do here.** You **cannot** drive Apple's Photos import UI and you get **no PTP/MTP camera access**. You **can** read a mounted SD card or external volume via **`UIDocumentPickerViewController`** (directory selection, iOS 13+) with security-scoped URLs. That means a third-party importer is in one important respect **less restricted than Apple's**: no "must have been captured by a digital camera" gate, and **USB thumb drives work**, because they mount as volumes in Files.

### 19.10 "Delete After Import" does not exist — the real labels

⚠️ **Trap:** **"Delete After Import" is not an Apple UI string on any surface.** Do not put it in a spec; doing so propagates a fabrication.

| Platform | Real behavior and exact strings |
|---|---|
| iOS / iPadOS (adapter import) | **Post-hoc prompt, not a pre-flight checkbox.** "When the import is complete, you might be asked to Keep or Delete the media on the camera or SD card." / "After the photos and videos have been imported, keep or delete them on the camera, card, iPhone, or iPad." Note **"might"** — it is not guaranteed, and it fires **after** the import. |
| macOS Photos | Has **both**. Pre-flight checkbox: *"If you want to delete photos from the camera after importing them, select the "Delete items" checkbox."* Post-hoc dialog: *"If a message asks whether you want to delete or keep the photos on your camera after they're imported, click **Delete Items** to remove the photos, or click **Keep Items** to keep them on the camera."* Mac also has an "Open Photos" checkbox (auto-open on connect) and a "Stop Import" control. |

The Mac **"Delete items"** checkbox is genuinely dangerous: it deletes from the card before the user can verify the transfer succeeded.

### 19.11 The locked Hidden album trap (two surfaces, both silent)

Apple's Photos User Guide (Mac), "Import from a camera or phone", Note — verbatim:

> "With macOS 15.4 or later, photos and videos in the Hidden album on your iPhone or iPad won't be imported to your Mac if the album is locked. To unlock the Hidden album on your iPhone or iPad, go to the Settings app, tap Apps, tap Photos, then turn off Use Face ID, Use Touch ID, or Use Passcode."

⚠️ **Trap:** this hits a **second** surface most people miss — **direct on-device export to external storage from iPad**: *"Photos and videos in the Hidden album won't be transferred if the album is locked"* (iPad User Guide, Export photos and videos to an external storage device). So a "move everything off my device" flow loses Hidden photos on **both** the Mac-import path **and** the direct-to-SSD path. The user's only feedback is a count mismatch they will probably not notice — and it silently hits precisely the photos they care most about protecting.

(It *is* documented — just buried in a Note. Cite it; don't call it undocumented.)

### 19.12 Share sheet Options — the densest fidelity-loss surface

Path: **Photos > [share] > Options**. Apple's exact text:

| Option | Apple's exact wording |
|---|---|
| Location | "Turn off location data: Turn off Location." |
| Format | "Adjust the file format: Tap **Automatic** for the best file format for the destination, tap **Current** to prevent a file format conversion, or tap **Most Compatible** and files may convert to **JPEG or MOV**." |
| iCloud Link | "Send as iCloud link: Turn on iCloud Link to share a URL to view or download the photos or videos. **iCloud links are available for 30 days.**" |
| All Photos Data | "Send all photo data: Turn on All Photos Data to share the original file with edit history and metadata; the recipient can view and modify the current version (**available with AirDrop and iCloud links only**)." |

Two constraints that shape an entire export architecture:

1. ⚠️ **iCloud links expire after 30 days.** Any hand-off design leaning on iCloud Link has a hard TTL.
2. ⚠️ **"All Photos Data" — the only share path that carries edit history and full metadata — works over AirDrop and iCloud links ONLY.** It is unavailable over Messages, Mail, or any third-party share extension. There is **no way** to hand someone a full-fidelity file with its edit stack over any other channel.

And the silent one, verbatim: *"For devices or services that don't support Live Photos, a Live Photo is shared as a still photo."* Users discover this only when the recipient sees a dead image.

Metadata scope, verbatim: *"Sharing a photo or video includes sharing its associated metadata, such as date and time, location, device, and captions."*

Permanently stripping location from an asset is a **different** flow from the share toggle: open the photo → tap [More] → **"Adjust Location"** → **"No Location."**

### 19.13 Transcoding boundaries — what Apple actually says

Apple's HEIF/HEVC page (published December 5, 2025), verbatim:

> "If sharing this media using other methods, such as AirDrop, Messages, or email, and the receiving device doesn't support the newer media formats, the media **might automatically be shared in a more compatible format, such as JPEG or H.264**."

And the contrast case, in the same breath:

> "If sharing this media via iCloud Photos, the media is preserved in its **original format, resolution, and frame rate**."

Precision: Apple says **"might automatically be shared,"** conditioned on the receiving device not supporting the format. It is **not unconditional**, and **"silently" is a researcher's word, not Apple's** — though there is in fact no UI indication when it happens.

**USB import to Mac/PC**, verbatim: *"When you import HEIF or HEVC media from an attached iPhone or iPad into Photos, Image Capture, or a PC, the media might be converted to JPEG or H.264. If you don't want it to be converted, open Settings, tap Apps, tap Photos, then scroll down and tap **Keep Originals**."*

⚠️ **Trap (string):** the settings-section header **"Transfer to Mac or PC" is NOT sourceable to any Apple-published document.** It appears only in Apple Communities (user-generated) and third-party write-ups. **Cite "Keep Originals," not the section header.** The sibling label **"Automatic"** is likewise **unverified** — widely reported, never spelled out on an Apple page. Confirm both on a physical device before quoting them.

Note also the iOS 18+ Settings path is **Settings > Apps > Photos** (not Settings > Photos).

**The upstream lever everyone forgets:** **Settings > Camera > Formats > "High Efficiency" (HEIF/HEVC) vs "Most Compatible" (JPEG/H.264)**. This is the *capture-time* fix, and it is the one Apple's own transfer article (120267) actually recommends — that article does not mention Keep Originals at all. Apple recommends Most Compatible *"to ensure that photos from your iPhone or iPad have the best compatibility with Windows."*

Also: with iCloud Photos on, *"you must download the original, full resolution versions of your photos to your iPhone or iPad before you import to your PC."*

### 19.14 "Export Unmodified Original" — the inverse fidelity loss

Photos' only direct-to-storage export path on iOS/iPadOS **deliberately throws away edits**. Flow: select photos → [share] → **"Export Unmodified Original"** → choose the device under Locations → Save. Apple's iPad guide, verbatim:

> "Note: For photos and videos that have been edited, the unmodified original version will be exported."

There is **no built-in "export the edited version at full quality to an external drive" path on iOS/iPadOS.** A user who carefully edits 200 photos, exports them to an SD card for a client, hands over 200 *unedited* files — and Apple's only warning is a one-line Note in a support doc.

⚠️ **Trap (label):** the **iPad User Guide uses the singular "Export Unmodified Original"** while **support article 118280 uses the plural "Export Unmodified Originals."** Check which string the shipping build actually shows before quoting it in UI or docs.

### 19.15 Fidelity matrix — only the cells Apple actually states

| Boundary | Codec | Edit stack | Live Photo | Metadata |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **iCloud Photos** | Preserved — "original format, resolution, and frame rate" | Preserved | Preserved | Preserved |
| **AirDrop / Messages / email** (receiver doesn't support format) | "might automatically be shared in a more compatible format, such as JPEG or H.264" | Only via **All Photos Data** — and that is **AirDrop-only** among these three | "For devices or services that don't support Live Photos, a Live Photo is shared as a still photo" | Shared: "date and time, location, device, and captions" |
| **Share > Options > Most Compatible** | "files may convert to JPEG or MOV" | — | Flattened if destination unsupported | Location strippable via the Location toggle |
| **iCloud Link** | — | **All Photos Data** works here | — | **Expires after 30 days** |
| **USB import to Mac/PC/Image Capture** | "might be converted to JPEG or H.264" unless **Keep Originals** is set | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| **Export Unmodified Original** (iOS/iPadOS → external storage) | Original file | **Edits DISCARDED by design** | n/a | n/a |
| **Locked Hidden album** (Mac import, macOS 15.4+; iPad→external storage) | **Not transferred at all** | — | — | — |

⚠️ **Trap (do not fill this cell):** there is **NO Apple source anywhere** stating what happens to **depth maps / Portrait-mode data / HDR gain maps** across any of these boundaries. It is a *plausible inference* from HEIC container structure that a HEIC→JPEG transcode destroys auxiliary images — the *conversion* is sourced, the *consequence* is not. **Do not publish a depth/portrait row in this table.** This requires an empirical physical-device audit to establish. It is exactly the kind of plausible-sounding cell a prior research wave would invent.

### 19.16 PhotoKit authorization — the four-rung ladder

⚠️ **Trap:** the common framing "PHPicker vs. full access" is **wrong** and will produce a broken onboarding. There are **four** rungs:

| Rung | What you get | Permission prompt |
|---|---|---|
| **`PHPickerViewController`** | Out-of-process picker → `PHPickerResult` → `NSItemProvider`. **No enumeration, no change observation, limited metadata.** Can return `PHLivePhoto` objects if configured for Live Photos. Useless for a library app. | **None** — "Apps don't need to request photo library permission when using either class." |
| **Add Photos Only** | Write access only. | Yes |
| **Limited Library** (`PHAuthorizationStatus.limited`) | *"The user authorized this app for limited photo library access"* — a real but **partial** `PHPhotoLibrary` containing a hand-picked subset the user can later revise. | Yes |
| **Full Library** | Enumeration + `PHAssetResourceManager` originals + `PHPhotoLibraryChangeObserver`. | Yes (the "scary" prompt) |

**Availability:** `PHPickerViewController` — iOS 14.0, iPadOS 14.0, Mac Catalyst 14.0, macOS 13.0, visionOS 1.0.

An ingest pipeline that branches only on *authorized/denied* will **silently mis-handle Limited**, which is where a large fraction of privacy-conscious users will land. `PHPickerViewController` also **cannot be subclassed**, and (iOS 17+) its touch events are ignored if its opacity is not fully opaque.

### 19.17 `PHAssetResource` — why one file per asset is the lossy path

Apple's own description: *"Photo assets can contain both JPEG and RAW files representing the same photo. Live Photo assets contain both still photo and video resources. Edited assets contain resources representing content before and after edits, plus a resource for the `PHAdjustmentData` object describing the edit."* Fetch via `PHAssetResourceManager`.

This is the architectural crux: **a single `PHAsset` carries multiple resources.** If a sync copies only one resource per asset, that sync **is** the lossy path — regardless of how good its transport is.

### 19.18 Automation: the App Intents "Photos" domain

Apple publishes app-intent **domains** (Audio, Calendar, Camera, Clock, Files, Mail, Maps, Messages, Notes, Phone, **Photos**, Reminders, System, In-App Search, plus single-purpose Assistant / Visual Intelligence and Shortcuts-only domains). Adopting the Photos domain schemas is how a non-Apple photo app gets the *same vocabulary users already know*.

**Availability (fully enumerated — no iOS 26 gating to worry about): EVERY Photos-domain schema is iOS 18.0 / iPadOS 18.0 / Mac Catalyst 18.0 / macOS 15.0 / visionOS 2.0.**

**Intent schemas (27):**

`addAssetsToAlbum` · `cleanupPhoto` · `copyEdits` · `createAlbum` · `createAssets` · `crop` · `deleteAlbum` · `deleteAssets` · `duplicateAssets` · `editAsset` · `openAlbum` · `openAsset` · `pasteEdits` · `postToSharedAlbum` · `removeAssetsFromAlbum` · `setDepth` · `setExposure` · `setFilter` · `setRotation` · `setSaturation` · `setWarmth` · `straighten` · `toggleDepth` · `toggleSuggestedEdits` · `updateAlbum` · `updateAsset` · `updateRecognizedPerson`

**Entity schemas (3):** `album` · `asset` · `recognizedPerson`
**Enum schemas (4):** `albumType` · `assetType` · `filterType` · `rotationDirection`

⚠️ **Trap:** the **`search` schema is listed by Apple under "Deprecated schemas" — do NOT adopt it.** This is awkward, because search is the single most obvious schema a photo app would wire first. (A researcher also reported `openAsset` as deprecated; the verified enumeration lists `openAsset` among the 27 without a deprecation flag. **Check `openAsset`'s `@available`/deprecation annotation in Xcode before building on it** — this one needs confirmation.)

⚠️ **Trap (API naming):** the current macros are **`@AppIntent(schema:)` / `@AppEntity(schema:)` / `@AppEnum(schema:)`**. The **`@AssistantIntent(schema:)` naming that most third-party blog posts still show is outdated.**

⚠️ **Trap (scope of the payoff):** Apple's own abstract scopes the benefit of *domain adoption* to **"Apple Intelligence and Siri."** Spotlight and Shortcuts exposure come from **App Intents generally**, not from adopting the domain schemas specifically. Don't over-claim domain adoption as a Spotlight strategy.

**Note the domain has no NSFW/content-safety schema, and no person-search or semantic-search schema.** Those features need custom `AppIntent`s, which will not inherit Siri's built-in phrasing.

### 19.19 Shortcuts actions — the vocabulary users already have

| Source | Actions |
|---|---|
| **Apple-sourced, long-standing** | **Find Photos** (in the Find family: Find Photos, Find Reminders, Find Calendar Events, Find Music, Find Health Samples, Find Contacts) · **Get Latest Photos** · **Filter Images** (in the Filter family: Filter Event Attendees, Filter Files, Filter Locations, Filter Articles, Filter Images) |
| **New in the 26 cycle** (Apple's "What's new in Shortcuts for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, and visionOS 26", Photos section — exactly four) | **Rename Album** · **Search Photos** · **Create New Memory** · **Filter Library** |
| **Added 26.4** | **Set Multitasking Mode** (iPadOS and macOS) |
| **Added in the 26 cycle, general** | **Use Model** (Apple Intelligence or ChatGPT) |
| ⚠️ **Third-party sourced only — verify on device** | "Select Photos", "Save to Photo Album", "Create Album" are real and widely used, but could **not** be sourced to an Apple page. Verify the exact strings in the on-device Shortcuts action list. |

Filter parameter grammar (Apple-sourced): predicates read **"Album is Portrait"** / **"Album is not Selfies"**, with **Sort by** + **Order** (e.g. "Smallest First") and a **Limit** / **"Get [x Items]"** control.

**The hole:** Apple's Find Photos filter set is **metadata-only** — album, date, width, is-favorite. There is **no "find photos of a person by name"** filter and **no semantic/content filter**.

### 19.20 Focus filters — Photos has none; we can ship one

Apple's Focus documentation enumerates only **Calendar, Mail, Messages and Safari** as app filters. **Photos is absent.** (Caveat: this is an argument from absence across Apple's Focus docs, not an explicit Apple denial — but it is very likely correct.)

User flow, verbatim: *"Go to Settings > Focus, then tap the Focus you want to add filters to. Scroll down to Focus filters, then tap Add Filter. Tap an app or system filter, then select the information from that app you want to use during the Focus. Tap Add to add the filter to the Focus."*

**API: `SetFocusFilterIntent`** (AppIntents). Availability: **iOS 16.0, iPadOS 16.0, Mac Catalyst 16.0, macOS 13.0, tvOS 16.0, watchOS 9.0 — and visionOS: NOT AVAILABLE.**

⚠️ **Trap (this directly undercuts a cross-device safety-filter pitch):** Apple states — *"Focus filters don't get synced across devices when you have Share Across Devices turned on in Settings > Focus."* **A user who sets a safety filter on iPhone does NOT get it on iPad.** Design for per-device configuration and say so in-app.

### 19.21 Siri — do not over-claim

**There is no Apple support page enumerating Siri's supported photo-search phrasings.** Every specific phrase in circulation ("Show me photos from Cupertino," etc.) traces only to third-party blogs or Apple Communities (user-generated content). An adversarial check attempted to refute this and could not.

What *is* Apple-sourced: adopting the App Intents Photos domain plus **`AppShortcutsProvider`** is the sanctioned path to Siri invocation.

⚠️ **Trap:** this surface is **actively changing** — Apple's June 2026 "Siri AI" newsroom announcement markets cross-app photo retrieval (asking Siri to pull up photos from a recent trip). Treat any Siri-phrasing assumption as a moving target. **Do not hard-code phrasings and do not put specific Siri phrases in a spec** — validate empirically on a device running 26.5.x first. This is precisely the class of detail a prior research wave fabricated.

### 19.22 Inbound paths: Files, AirDrop, Messages

- **Messages auto-save (Apple-sourced, verbatim):** *"Photos and videos shared with you in the Messages app are automatically saved in your photo library. To turn off this feature, go to Settings > Apps > Messages > Shared with You, then turn off Photos."*
- **Files-based import** is the generic document path — `UIDocumentPickerViewController` / security-scoped URLs. iOS 13+ added directory selection, which is also how external volumes are reached.
- ⚠️ **AirDrop codes — new in iPadOS 26.2:** *"an additional layer of verification when using AirDrop with unknown contacts by providing a code on the receiver's device that the sender must enter to complete the transfer."* **Any AirDrop-based ingest flow now has a possible extra interstitial to design for.**

⚠️ **Unverified framing:** the claim that "Files and AirDrop are the two ingest paths a third-party app can fully own" is an **engineering/product assertion, not an Apple-documented fact**. It is plausible (apps can register document types to receive AirDrop and read Files via the document picker) but **nothing on apple.com states it. Do not cite it as sourced.**

---

### 19.23 What this means for us

**iPad shell (its own workstream, not a media query).**
- **REQUIREMENT:** ship an explicit tablet shell — collapsible sidebar + content — with **Library** and **Collections/Memories** as sibling roots, mirroring the vocabulary iPad users now have. A phone tab bar stretched to 1024pt reads as unfinished.
- ⚠️ **RN reality:** there is **no system sidebar primitive in React Native.** `react-native-screens` does not give you a `UISplitViewController`. You need either a custom RN sidebar driven by `useWindowDimensions`/size classes, or a native module wrapping `UISplitViewController` with RN content per column. Scope it as a real line item.
- Do **not** argue "we already match the long-standing iPad pattern" — the sidebar is one release old (absent in iPadOS 18, reintroduced in 26).

**Windowing resilience (hard constraint).**
- **CONSTRAINT:** layout must be **continuously responsive, not breakpoint-snapped.** Windowed apps get arbitrary widths — 320pt one moment, 1366pt the next — and the app **must not unmount our ML/sync state on resize.** Drive column counts from `useWindowDimensions`; never `Platform.isPad` + a static layout.
- **QA matrix must include:** Windowed Apps, Stage Manager, Full Screen Apps, **and Slide Over** (removed in 26.0, restored in 26.2). Use the **Set Multitasking Mode** Shortcuts action (26.4+) to automate mode-switching in the harness.
- **Do NOT gate features on M-series.** Windowed Apps runs on iPad 8th gen+, iPad Air 3rd gen+, iPad mini 5th gen+, iPad Pro 11-inch 1st gen+. Any M2/M3/M4 capability check would wrongly exclude most of the installed base.
- **OPPORTUNITY:** multi-window (library in one window, a Person's photos in another) is genuinely differentiating and Apple Photos handles it poorly — but it requires **`UISceneDelegate`** support, which RN apps often have not adopted. **Decide early**; retrofitting scenes is expensive.

**Menu bar + keyboard (highest polish-per-hour on iPad).**
- **REQUIREMENT:** ship a real menu bar (File / Edit / View / Go / People) with `UIKeyCommand`s wired to our actions. Apple's own support page tells users to look there to discover shortcuts, so an empty menu is a *visible* failure. Per HIG: show **all** commands even without shortcuts; unavailable commands stay **visible but disabled**. Budget a **native RN module around `UIMenuBuilder`** — there is no JS-only path.
- **OPPORTUNITY (high leverage, low cost):** grid keyboard navigation — arrows, Shift-arrow range select, **Command-A**, Space to quicklook, Delete — plus pointer hover states on thumbnails. Third-party photo apps almost universally ignore this, which makes bulk curation on iPad far slower than on a Mac. This is exactly our "iPad as a triage station feeding the desktop compute node" story. Remember **Command-W / Command-M are window-management commands** — honoring them means participating in the windowing system.

**Drag and drop.**
- **REQUIREMENT:** be both a drag **source** (photos out to Mail/Files/Keynote) and a drag **target** (photos in from Files/Safari), and implement Apple's multi-item gesture (touch-and-hold first item, tap more with another finger, badge shows the count). Never call it a "pile" in copy.
- ⚠️ **CONSTRAINT:** vend the **original file with its true UTType** in the `NSItemProvider`. If we vend a decoded bitmap we become exactly the lossy path we are criticizing Apple for. RN has no drag-source API — native module.

**Markup.**
- **Do NOT hand-roll an annotation stack.** Wrap `PKCanvasView` + `PKToolPicker` and inherit the reed pen and every future Apple tool (plus Pencil Pro squeeze/barrel-roll/haptics) for free. Thin native wrapper for RN.
- **Correct any internal doc claiming the reed pen is an iPhone Photos feature** — it is an iPadOS 26 PencilKit feature, and that claim would embarrass us in a spec review.

**Import (our biggest concrete "beats Apple Photos" win).**
- **MAJOR OPPORTUNITY:** build our own Import screen on `UIDocumentPickerViewController` + security-scoped URLs. We can import from **USB thumb drives** and from **renamed/edited/copied files** — both of which Apple's camera-adapter path flatly refuses — and run face/CLIP/NSFW on ingest. This is demonstrable to photographers in 30 seconds. (We still cannot do PTP/MTP camera access; that path is Apple-only.)
- **REQUIREMENT:** implement **verify-then-delete**. Hash each file after copy, and only then offer "Delete N items from card," with an undo window. We own the risk Apple's Mac "Delete items" checkbox avoids by deleting pre-verification. This is a cheap trust win.
- **REQUIREMENT:** never write "Delete After Import" as if it were an Apple string. It is not one.
- **REQUIREMENT:** our migration/import flow must **detect and report an inaccessible-asset count** — "12 items in your locked Hidden album were not imported" — rather than silently skipping. Silent omission in a migration tool is a trust-destroying bug, and it is exactly the failure Apple ships on **two** surfaces (Mac import, iPad→external storage). Note that PhotoKit will similarly not vend hidden assets to us, so we need our **own** private-collection concept rather than depending on Photos' Hidden album.
- **OPPORTUNITY:** our own locked/private collection, backed by our existing crypto, can sync to the desktop **end-to-end encrypted** — something Apple's locked Hidden album explicitly refuses to do.
- **AirDrop ingest:** design for the **AirDrop code interstitial** (iPadOS 26.2+) when receiving from unknown contacts.

**Authorization (design for it, don't discover it).**
- **CONSTRAINT:** we need **full-library authorization**, and we must handle **`PHAuthorizationStatus.limited` explicitly** — a large privacy-conscious segment will land there and an authorized/denied-only branch will silently starve the ML pipeline. Show an honest explanation: nothing leaves the device except to the user's own desktop over E2E LAN. Our privacy story is our best argument for the scary prompt.
- **REQUIREMENT:** register a **`PHPhotoLibraryChangeObserver`** so new camera-roll items are indexed for FR/CLIP incrementally, not by rescanning.
- **CONSTRAINT:** iCloud-optimized assets may be **placeholders** on-device. Ingest MUST handle "original not local" — request the original explicitly and surface a download state rather than silently syncing a low-res proxy.

**Sync fidelity (core to our thesis).**
- **REQUIREMENT (architectural):** LAN sync must enumerate and transfer the **full `PHAssetResource` set per asset** — original, RAW sibling, paired video, `PHAdjustmentData` — not a single rendered image. One resource per asset and *we* are the lossy path.
- **OPPORTUNITY (our most defensible claim):** **byte-exact, hash-verified transfer**, shown as an "Original • verified" badge. Apple explicitly documents that AirDrop/Messages/email/USB *may* transcode; we can guarantee they don't. And because the desktop link is ours, we can offer **"All Photos Data, to any destination"** — full edit history and metadata with **no 30-day expiry** and **no AirDrop-only restriction**.
- **OPPORTUNITY:** a per-asset **fidelity badge** (Original / Transcoded / Flattened). Nobody has this; it's cheap given we already hash for sync; it makes the differentiator legible. Depth and Live Photo frames also give the cross-age matcher more signal than a flattened JPEG.
- ⚠️ **Do not claim** in any doc that HEIC→JPEG destroys depth/HDR gain maps until someone verifies it on a physical device. Apple never says it. The inference is sound; the citation does not exist.

**Export sheet.**
- **REQUIREMENT:** copy Apple's vocabulary so it reads as familiar — **Automatic / Current / Most Compatible**, plus a **Location** toggle.
- **OPPORTUNITY (five-minute UX decision, real capability difference):** offer **Original**, **Edited (rendered)**, and **Original + edit sidecar** as explicit labeled choices. `PHAssetResource` exposes all three. Apple offers exactly one — and picks the surprising one.
- **PRIVACY REQUIREMENT:** strip location **by default** on export, and **never** leak our derived face embeddings or NSFW classifications into exported metadata. Offer strip-GPS / strip-all-EXIF / strip-person-tags / downscale / force-JPEG / flatten-Live-Photo / strip-our-ML-sidecar as first-class options.

**Onboarding.**
- **OPPORTUNITY:** detect the user's **Settings > Camera > Formats** setting (High Efficiency vs Most Compatible) and their **Keep Originals** state, and explain in one screen that our sync never transcodes. "Why are my photos HEIC on my PC" is one of the highest-volume iPhone photo frustrations in existence, and it is caused by exactly these two buried settings.

**Automation.**
- **REQUIREMENT (top of the automation workstream):** adopt the **App Intents Photos domain** schemas. All are available from **iOS/iPadOS 18.0**, so there is no version-gating problem. They map directly to our differentiators — **`updateRecognizedPerson` is literally our face-naming flow.** Use the current **`@AppIntent(schema:)` / `@AppEntity(schema:)` / `@AppEnum(schema:)`** macros, not the outdated `@AssistantIntent(schema:)` naming.
- ⚠️ **Do NOT adopt the `search` schema — Apple deprecates it.** Use the **System and In-App Search** domain for search instead. Confirm `openAsset`'s deprecation status in Xcode before building on it.
- **RN constraint:** App Intents **cannot be expressed in RN.** They must be Swift types in the native iOS target calling into our core. Plan a Swift "IntentsKit" module from the start. Same for `SetFocusFilterIntent` and `UIMenuBuilder`.
- **OPPORTUNITY (sharp and specific — automation primitives Apple structurally does not have):** ship Shortcuts actions for **"Find Photos of Person"** (our FR + cross-age matcher, so it finds them as a child *and* an adult), **"Find Photos Matching Description"** (our CLIP index), and **"Filter Out Sensitive Photos"** (our NSFW classifier). Apple's Find Photos filters are metadata-only — no person-by-name, no semantic content filter. Mirror Apple's naming conventions (Find X / Get Latest X / Filter X / Create X / Rename X) so our actions feel native in the editor.
- **OPPORTUNITY (genuinely novel):** ship a **Focus filter** via `SetFocusFilterIntent` — "When Work Focus is on, hide NSFW-classified and private-album content, and switch to a neutral grid." Apple Photos has none; nobody in the category has this; it needs no cloud; it's a direct payoff on the safety classifier we already have; and it demos in ten seconds. ⚠️ **CONSTRAINT:** Focus filters **do not sync across devices** even with Share Across Devices on — configure per-device and say so in-app rather than letting users believe it followed them. Also **not available on visionOS**, if that's ever on the roadmap.
- **CONSTRAINT ON OUR CLAIMS:** do **not** put specific Siri phrasings in any spec. They are undocumented, the surface is actively changing (Apple's June 2026 Siri AI announcement markets cross-app photo retrieval), and inventing them is the exact failure mode a prior wave committed. Treat Siri as a **funnel**, not a feature — Siri's own photo search is widely distrusted, so a fast, local, obviously-correct in-app search bar is the more valuable investment.

**Provenance (a free differentiator).**
- **OPPORTUNITY:** Photos tracks import provenance internally (that's what "From My Mac" proves) but exposes one crude toggle and no answer to "where did this photo come from?" Make provenance a **first-class, filterable attribute** — Camera / AirDrop / SD card / Desktop sync / Messages — and let users filter *and hide* by it, the way View Options hides Screenshots. Our analogue of "From My Mac" is **"From Desktop"** (LAN-synced items), and combined with our sync, "show me everything that came from my desktop" is a natural, useful filter Apple never built.
- **REQUIREMENT:** ship a **Share Extension** so "AirDrop straight into our app" works. Otherwise every inbound photo detours through Apple Photos and we are a second-class citizen on the user's own device. Extension targets are native-only — build them in Xcode.

**Home surface.**
- **REQUIREMENT:** the home surface must be **user-reorderable and pinnable**. iPadOS 26 set that expectation (reorder, pin, three display sizes + Collapse All); a fixed-order home screen now reads as less capable. Persist the layout so it survives reinstall, and ideally sync it to the desktop over our LAN channel.
- **CONSTRAINT:** honor an **"Auto-Play Motion"** toggle from day one. Apple defaults autoplay ON in Collections; autoplaying video thumbnails *while our on-device ML is running* will visibly tank frame rate and battery. Ship the toggle, and consider defaulting it off on lower-end hardware.
- **OPPORTUNITY:** ship pinch-to-zoom grid density and **"Hide screenshots"** as *discoverable* controls rather than burying them two menus deep, and copy the **Aspect Ratio Grid / Square Photo Grid** pair verbatim — it's the exact vocabulary users already have. ⚠️ In RN the hard part is that pinch-to-rezoom a virtualized grid requires `numColumns` changes **plus scroll-anchor preservation** in FlashList/FlatList, or the user loses their place.

**Items requiring a physical-device audit before they go in any spec or UI copy:**

| Claim | Why it needs a device |
|---|---|
| "Automatic" as the sibling label to "Keep Originals" in Settings > Apps > Photos | Never spelled out on an Apple page |
| The section header "Transfer to Mac or PC" | Appears only in user-generated content and third-party write-ups |
| "Imports tab" vs "Import" | Apple's own surfaces disagree (article 118280 vs iPad User Guide) |
| "Export Unmodified Original" vs "Export Unmodified Originals" | Singular in the iPad guide, plural in article 118280 |
| Copy Edits / Paste Edits = Shift-Command-C / Shift-Command-V | Third-party tutorial only; not on Apple's shortcut list |
| Shortcuts actions "Select Photos", "Save to Photo Album", "Create Album" | Real and widely used, but third-party-sourced only |
| Whether the reed pen appears in PencilKit's palette on **iPhone** | Apple announced it for iPadOS only; do not claim iPhone support |
| What survives a HEIC→JPEG transcode (depth / Portrait / HDR gain map) | Apple documents that the conversion happens, never what is lost |
| `openAsset` deprecation status in the App Intents Photos domain | Reported deprecated by one source, listed without a flag by another — check `@available` in Xcode |
